rule: Internal-to-external: when price hits internal range liquidity (an FVG), expect a reversal toward the external high/low that caused the retracement.
quote: "when price hits this key level, in this case being internal range, a fair value gap, we can expect price to reverse"

rule: External-to-internal: after price reaches or manipulates an external high, expect a retracement back into the range; the internal FVG is the first target.
quote: "But regardless, this fair value gap becomes your first target."

rule: Manipulation ("order pairing") range: the range high/low is the key level, the opposing side of the range is the target.
quote: "the opposing side of the range or swing high being the targets"

rule: No reversal without a swing formation; confirm every universal-model reversal with a swing point.
quote: "the market cannot reverse without a swing formation"

rule: Candle 2 closure = candle 2 closes back inside candle 1's range; then mark EQ of the previous candle and want candle 3's low to hold in the upper half (bullish).
quote: "It is simply when candle 2 closes back inside of candle 1's range."

rule: EQ of the prior candle is a mechanical wick-size gauge: expansion candles have small wicks, reversal candles large ones; trade the small-wick expansion.
quote: "It is a mechanical way to measure wick size."

rule: If candle 3 closes above candle 2's high, mark EQ of candle 3 and seek candle 4 continuation with its low in candle 3's upper half.
quote: "seeking continuation in candle 4 is if we close candle 3 above candle 2's high"

rule: Candle 2 reversal-to-expansion: if candle 1 hits the key level but closes as expansion (no reversal), candle 2 reverses off candle 1's extreme; a small wick lets you trade candle 2 itself.
quote: "If we form a small wick, then we can actually participate in this candle"

rule: Candle 3 closure (no candle 2 closure): cannot be anticipated before candle 3 opens; a strong close is defined as closing over the body of candle 2, then trade candle 4 from EQ of candle 3.
quote: "Once we have a strong candle 3 closure, mechanically defined as closing over the body of candle 2."

rule: When candle 1 hits the range low but does not reverse and candle 2 shows no reversal, do not trade candles 1-3; wait for candle 3 to close above candle 2's body, then trade candle 4.
quote: "So we must wait for the close. If it closes above the body of candle 2, this is what validates us to trade candle 4."

rule: The market also cannot reverse without SMT; combine SMT with swing points for a mechanical system.
quote: "the market cannot reverse without a swing point, but the market can also not reverse without SMT"

rule: Pair SMT within a triad of three correlated markets: DXY/EURUSD/GBPUSD, NQ/ES/YM, GC/XAUEUR/XAUGBP, CL/RB/HO.
quote: "I view correlated markets through a triad that is simply three correlated markets"

rule: SMT at highs/lows: one market takes the (range) low, the other does not; this crack in correlation signals a potential reversal.
quote: "It is where one market manipulates a low or range low where the other one simply does not take that low."

rule: SMT fill: one asset trades into / fills an FVG while the correlated asset leaves its gap open; potential reversal.
quote: "This is where one asset fills in a gap or trades into a gap and the other one leaves it open"

rule: A manipulation-range SMT (failure swing) is only a potential reversal until candle 3 closes above candle 2's body.
quote: "This is what signifies a potential reversal that is not confirmed until we get that candle 3 closure"

rule: Swing-point SMT can sit between candle 1 and candle 2 (trade candle 3 continuation) or between candle 2 and candle 3 on a candle 2 closure.
quote: "here we have swing point SMT between candle 1 and candle 2 on the correlated market"

rule: Two-stage SMT = a first SMT immediately confirmed by a second (e.g. C1-C2 SMT then C2-C3 SMT); a strong reversal signature.
quote: "A two-stage SMT is where we have one stage of SMT and immediately following that is confirmed by a second SMT."

rule: PSP (credited to Trader Day): correlated markets close the same candle in opposite directions; potential reversal.
quote: "It is where between a correlated markets they close in opposite directions."

rule: Two-stage PSP: a C1-C2 SMT confirmed by a PSP, or a PSP confirmed by a later C2-C3 SMT; then trade the following candle in the opposite direction.
quote: "this is our first stage SMT which is confirmed by the PSP creating a two-stage SMT"

rule: Continuation PSP: during expansion toward a target, one asset closes a retracement as a PSP and the other runs that PSP's extreme; it forms no swing point and is used for continuation, not reversal.
quote: "It is simply where one asset retraces back into the range."

rule: Any PSP that opposes the open draw on liquidity after the low/high of day is in is a continuation signal, never a reversal.
quote: "So, any PSP opposing our draw liquidity will not be used as reversal."

rule: If no SMT forms at the key level, a swing-point SMT or a PSP alone can be enough to confirm the universal-model reversal.
quote: "There's no SMT with our key level being a high or low or fair value gap, but we get a precision swing point."

rule: Highest-probability reversal signature: first-stage SMT at the key level, then a PSP, then a crack in correlation at a swing point (SMT + two-stage PSP).
quote: "this is the highest probability reversal signature or confirmation that I use"

rule: An SMT is most significant when its PSP is printed by a time driver (9:00 close holding the equities open, 9:30 open): pair a driver with manipulation.
quote: "So, what makes this SMT so significant is the timing of when this SMT is actually printed."

rule: When the lagging asset that failed to manipulate a high finally catches up and breaks the SMT, that can trigger the reversal; the middle asset breaking it while the weakest diverges is higher probability.
quote: "once the weakest asset actually catches up to that SMT and breaks it, this is when markets can potentially reverse"

rule: Failure swings left by an expansion are not trusted as reversal points until price shows it wants to expand away (e.g. fails to manipulate an internal high and continues through it).
quote: "That's when you can actually trust trading away from failure swings."

rule: Large expansion followed by a choppy, slow retracement is a continuation signature; a V-shaped move off the key level after SMT is a reversal signature.
quote: "Large expansion range followed by a choppy and slow retracement. We know that is a continuous signature."

rule: If a reversal forms before a driver, mark it; the driver (9:30) should then expand away from it, which confirms the HTF draw.
quote: "If we have a reversal prior to a driver we mark that out. What should 930 do?"

rule: When an HTF candle reaches a key level confirmed by SMT, assume its low is in and trade its body; use the fractal model on the LTF for entry.
quote: "So now you can assume that the higher time frame candle's low is put in and trade the body."

rule: Gold triad: use the Forex.com feed for XAU crosses because it opens at 18:00 like GC.
quote: "It actually opens up at 1,800 as well."

rule: Use the checklist only after a daily bias/direction is set; all items must be met before entry.
quote: "Once I have a daily bias or direction, I will use this checklist to make sure all requirements are met before I take an entry."

rule: Step 1 is a stop raid: a low (high) put in and then raided/broken.
quote: "The first thing I focus on is a stop raid. This just means that a low was put in before it was raided or broken."

rule: Step 2 is a market structure shift / displacement: the previous opposite swing broken with aggressive movement.
quote: "This means that a previous high was broken and aggressively moved over."

rule: Step 3 (flexible): price returns into discount (longs) of the displacement range.
quote: "I generally like to see price move back into a discount of this price range here."

rule: Step 4: a PD array in that area; FVG or order block preferred, OTE and breaker also used.
quote: "Generally, I prefer to have a fair value gap or an order block, but I will also use an OTE in this area as well as a breaker block."

rule: Each concept can be an entry model alone, but he blends one to three (e.g. FVG in OTE, box setup in OTE).
quote: "I like to blend one, two, or three of these concepts together for my personal strategy."

rule: Do not go long above the 0.5 of the displacement range; narrow the discount to the OTE.
quote: "I'm not looking to long above this 0.5."

rule: Breaker for a long = the up-close candles before the raid on liquidity; order block = the down-close candle.
quote: "breaker block would be these up close candles here before the raid on liquidity"

rule: Pick the entry by balancing R:R (closer to stop = higher R) against the chance of not getting filled.
quote: "as I move my entry closer to my stop loss, my risk to reward increases. However, the further I go, there is also the possibility that I do not get filled"

rule: Preferred: a FVG nested in an order block inside the OTE, aligned with the box setup.
quote: "I have a fair value gap and this is nested within this order block here."

rule: Stop below the swing low (or order block low); first partial at an intermediate level, then target buy side liquidity; break-even is optional.
quote: "putting my stop on this order block low, partial or move my stop to break even here"

rule: A one-tick run below a low does not count as a stop raid for him.
quote: "we did go a tick below this low, but I do not count that personally"

rule: Displacement without a prior stop raid does not meet his criteria.
quote: "I prefer to have a stop rate prior to the displacement."

rule: Without a lower-timeframe liquidity raid before the move, he is not interested (box setup alone is not A+).
quote: "without a lower timeframe liquidity rate prior to a move, I am not interested in it"

rule: An FVG that sits in premium of the range does not meet the criteria for a long; drop a timeframe and use the discount part.
quote: "It does not because it is in a premium of the range."

rule: Target the initial highs of the morning, then let runners run.
quote: "target the initial highs from the morning, and from there, let runners run"

rule: A deep run back into an initial reversal point that does not take it out makes a failure swing; never trade away from a failure swing.
quote: "Deep runs back into that initial area, creating that failure swing, is an area that we will not trade away from."

rule: Treat a failure swing as an unestablished reversal; true reversals turn, expand and only make shallow retracements.
quote: "What we see this as is an unestablished point of reversal."

rule: The relevant swing is the original extreme that the failure swing ran into; only a later manipulation of that extreme (run, then close back into range) gives a tradeable reversal.
quote: "the only way we're going to trade this higher is if the following day or days returns back down into that relevant low, engages it to manipulate, and then expands back into the range."

rule: A manipulation at a relevant swing is valid only with "valid separation": its own extreme must not form a new failure swing against a daily high/low to the left.
quote: "the low of this manipulation did not create another failure swing to a daily low to the left of it."

rule: When a failure swing appears on one index, check the correlated index; if it shows SMT (divergence) at that level, treat it as a tradeable manipulation, not a failure swing.
quote: "Anytime you see potential failure swings on one pair, your first instinct is to go to that correlated pair and see if you find a divergence"

rule: No clear manipulation back into range at the level means no trade that day in that direction.
quote: "So, we can't trade this to the upside internally on this next day."

rule: Only trade two daily candle types: a small-wick reversal at a relevant swing, or a daily continuation.
quote: "there's only two types of daily candles that you should be trading"

rule: Anticipate a small-wick reversal when the daily candle opens near a relevant swing (only a shallow run is needed to reach it).
quote: "We can anticipate the potential for a small wick reversal to take place when we open a daily candle near a relevant swing."

rule: Demand a small opposing wick on the traded day, because expansion days do not make deep opposing runs.
quote: "expansion days, directional daily candles, do not have time to make deep opposing runs."

rule: Skip a reversal day that needed a large opposing run from the daily open to reach the relevant swing; trade the following continuation day instead.
quote: "we have a large opposing run from the daily open to reach into that relevant swing"

rule: For a continuation day, anchor a 50% fib on the previous daily candle from its close to its opposing extreme (low if bullish, high if bearish); the new day's low (bull) / high (bear) should form beyond that 50% in the trade direction.
quote: "take a 50% fib tool and anchor it in the previous daily candle"

rule: A run through the 50% invalidation makes a large wick / potential failure swing and makes the continuation day uninteresting.
quote: "50% is the area where price should not trade back to."

rule: Do not go from bias straight to entry; insert a confirmation layer (session development + daily profile).
quote: "In between these two steps, we place a confirmation layer"

rule: Trade only the New York session (8:00 onward), for any market.
quote: "Inside of this system, we are only going to be focused on the New York session."

rule: Use the 7h chart for daily profiles: candle 1 = Asia (18:00), 2 = London (01:00), 3 = New York (08:00).
quote: "The first 7-hour candle is Asia session, the second is London, and the third is New York"

rule: Do not trade the 18:00 or 01:00 7h candles; let them print and use them as context.
quote: "we are not going to trade the Asia or London session."

rule: Look for profile alignment in only two places: a small-wick reversal day at a relevant swing, or a continuation day relative to the previous-day invalidation point.
quote: "There's only two places we're looking for daily profiles to form to confirm our bias."

rule: 18:00 reversal profile: if Asia made the intraday low/high and London (01:00) expanded away from it, expect a New York continuation.
quote: "if the 1:00 candle expands away from the 8:00 candle reversal, then seek the 8:00 candle continuation."

rule: If Asia made the low but London stayed ranged, that is not expansion away; expect New York to return to the intraday low and form an 08:00 reversal.
quote: "if the 18 candle formed a low and the 1:00 candle just remained ranged, well then that's not an expansion away."

rule: 01:00 reversal profile: if London runs out the Asia range and closes back inside, expect a New York continuation.
quote: "If the 1:00 candle reverses off the 18 candle range, then seek an 8:00 candle continuation."

rule: 08:00 reversal profile: if Asia and London fail to reverse, require New York to manipulate the intraday high/low, then reverse and expand.
quote: "If the 18 and 1:00 candle fail to establish a reversal, then seek the 8:00 candle reversal."

rule: For 18:00 and 01:00 profiles, 50% of the 01:00 candle (close to opposing swing) is the invalidation New York should not retrace through; the 08:00 profile has no invalidation point.
quote: "The one profile that doesn't have an invalidation point is the 8:00 reversal"

rule: Every entry waits for the 8:00 candle's wick to form, then trades the body.
quote: "Let the wick form and then trade the body."

rule: For a New York reversal, prefer a continuation entry after the reversal over trading the reversal itself.
quote: "Now, it is possible to trade this reversal, but I always prefer to seek a continuation."

rule: Use 7h->15m before 9:30; near or after 9:30 use a lower-timeframe aligned fractal model (1h->5m or 30m->3m).
quote: "if it is closer to 9:30 or after 9:30, that's when I prefer to use a lower time frame fractal model."

rule: With SMT, the stronger asset need not make a new low; its old low becomes the protected low once price closes over the down-close series.
quote: "because of SMT, we don't have to make the new low because the correlated asset or NQ already did that."

rule: A candle-2 closure printed only on the correlated asset can frame the trade on the stronger asset.
quote: "we can treat it like a candle to closure but trading the stronger asset."

rule: Pre-market entries go on the 15m so the stop sits on a swing expected to survive the New York open.
quote: "if I'm taking pre-market entries, I generally prefer the 15-minute time frame."

rule: Build the CISD from the whole series of opposing candles, not a single insignificant candle; stop must cover at least 50% of the down-close candle, ideally ~75%.
quote: "I would just have to have my stop covering 50% of this down close candle or more. I prefer around 75%."

rule: Ignore daily highs/lows older than about 30 daily candles when marking relevant swings.
quote: "anything that's really beyond 30 daily candles, we don't want to consider that"

rule: Protraction study aims to use Asia/London/New York session dynamics to determine where and when the high or low of the day is made.
quote: "to understand the session dynamics of Asia London and New York to ultimately determine where and when the high or the low of the day is made"

rule: A bullish daily candle is open-low-high-close; positioning in the wick of the low aligns you with the daily expansion.
quote: "for every bullish candle we can say that there is an open low high and a close"

rule: Protraction = studying the day's manipulation to infer when, and in which session, expansion occurs.
quote: "protraction is studying the manipulation of the day in hopes of inferring when the expansion can occur"

rule: Classic protraction: London forms the low of the day, then expands higher.
quote: "a classic protraction occurs when London forms the low of the day and then expands higher"

rule: Delayed protraction: the low of the day forms right before / into the New York session.
quote: "a delayed protraction occurs when we get the low of the day forming right before or the New York session"

rule: Judas swing (void profile): Asia and London accumulate, New York manipulates the range, then expansion.
quote: "an Asian and London accumulation followed by a manipulation of the range in New York and then an expansion"

rule: Classic protraction is the best profile to start with; it is a New York continuation profile with the low made between the London open and New York open.
quote: "the low of the day is formed right in between the London open and the New York open"

rule: Classic protraction phases: Asia accumulates, manipulation in or right before London (2:00-5:00 a.m.), expansion in London, retracement in New York, then secondary expansion.
quote: "a manipulation either in the London session or right before the London session 2 a.m. to 5:00 a.m."

rule: Frame the day's low with PD arrays (swing lows, FVGs) that justify it staying intact, paired with market structure and delivery state, to claim which profile is active.
quote: "we're going to use the context of PD arrays like swing lows and fair value gaps"

rule: Delayed protraction is a New York reversal profile: New York reverses the direction of London's move toward the HTF draw on liquidity.
quote: "a delayed protraction sees New York reversing the direction of that London move towards the higher time frame draw on liquidity"

rule: Delayed protraction is often paired with New York news drivers such as 8:30; between 3:00 and 8:30 a.m. price descends/chops into the HTF key level before reversing.
quote: "often times you'll see this paired with news drivers during the New York session such as at 8:30"

rule: Judas swing: when Asia and London fail to manipulate the daily range, expect New York to run Asia and/or London lows (highs) before reversing to the HTF draw on liquidity, often as a V-shaped recovery.
quote: "what we can anticipate is for New York York to run out the lows of Asia Andor London"

rule: The manipulation wick must engage a key level that qualifies it as the high/low of the day; without a meaningful HTF key level engaged, the extreme is not yet in.
quote: "there needs to be a key level that is engaged that can qualify this as the high or the low of the day"

rule: In a Judas swing, an FVG created by the initial run is not expected to support price; fade the initial move.
quote: "we're in fact fading this initial move higher as the form of a Judas swing"

rule: In classic protraction New York does not have to return to the London low; trade New York's retracement into an internal FVG (e.g. 30m / 1h) toward the draw.
quote: "New York does not have to come back into this low this is the low of the day"

rule: The low of the day in a classic protraction is a protected area given the open-low-high-close dynamic; trade in the direction of the draw on liquidity from a PD array.
quote: "understanding that this low of the day is going to be a protected area of price"

rule: Key reversal confluence at the level: SMT with ES plus a CISD (close through the consecutive down-close candles).
quote: "a change in the state of delivery which is a closure through the consecutive series of down closed candles"

rule: Each morning study the prior two sessions to decide classic, delayed or Judas, then combine with the HTF draw on liquidity (bias).
quote: "each morning when I come to the charts what I will first do is I will look back and study the prior two sessions"

rule: He prefers NQ over ES in New York because its volatility offers larger range expansions.
quote: "I'll favor trading NASDAQ over the yes simply because it's more volatile"

rule: GB levels: fib retracement with 0.295, 0.41, 0.705, 0.7475, 0.79 (plus 0 = anchor low, 1 = valid/protected high).
quote: "right down here we have the 295. Okay, the 0 295. We have the 041"

rule: A market structure shift is a body close below the last valid low (or above the last valid high), not an unvalidated low on the right edge.
quote: "Well, the last valid low, we close below. That's our market structure shift."

rule: Mastering market structure matters more than the entry technique.
quote: "as long as you master market structure you are good to go"

rule: Entry 1: after a valid flip at a HTF POI, place a blind limit at the 0.7475 retrace.
quote: "So first entry technique all I'm waiting for is what a retrace up to that 7475"

rule: Entry 1 exits: 0.41/0.295 when the HTF is consolidating; a new high/low when the market is expanding.
quote: "If we're consolidating on a higher time frame, that's when I'm going to look to exit at 041. 295 rather than a new low being"

rule: Expanding markets give shallow retracements, consolidating markets deep ones; the level set covers both.
quote: "in a consolidating market we're going to get those deeper retracements um more so than shallow retracements"

rule: Entry 2: as lower-timeframe structure builds near the extreme, a first close beyond 0.295 is riskier; a close beyond 0.41 (~80% by his estimate) sends the retrace to 0.7475.
quote: "first close above the 0 295 is a little bit riskier."

rule: When price fails to make a new high, the draw is the lows that built the failure swing.
quote: "When price fails to make a new high, what are we expecting the draw in price to be?"

rule: A heavy wick off a key level without a true body close below the wick means the area is supported; wait for the body close.
quote: "I'm waiting for a true body close to happen once we close below this wick right here."

rule: Lower-timeframe POIs (wicks) only matter when aligned with HTF key areas / GB levels.
quote: "You got to have these like lower time frame POIs in alignment with these key areas"

rule: When playing from 0.41 back to 0.7475, require displacement away from 0.41 after the confirmed close before engaging.
quote: "anytime I'm taking an entry off of the 041, playing it back into the 7475, I'm always looking for displacement away from that area."

rule: Require multiple confluences at the level (hourly/4H imbalance, 30m order block / CSS); don't throw limits recklessly.
quote: "you need to have multiple things lined up for your entries."

rule: Avoid executing at the 50% of a whole consolidation range ("no man's land").
quote: "You don't really want to be executing at the 50% of a entire range."

rule: Trading out of the range: after a body close beyond 0.295, price likes to return to 0.41 for a continuation entry.
quote: "you'll see that extreme level closed up above. So that 295 and then what you're going to see is price will like to return back to that 041."

rule: Levels are more sensitive trading back into the range after displacement away than trading out of it.
quote: "they're a lot more sensitive once you get some displacement away, trading back into the range versus trading out of the range."

rule: SMT matters at weak highs/lows (one index takes it, the other does not); ignore inner-range SMT.
quote: "your true focus in regards to SMT is did ES or ENQ fail to take a weak high."

rule: When framing reversals, weight the second continuation break (second new high) over the first flip, which is often fake away from HTF key areas.
quote: "Usually, when I am framing reversals, I would say that second continuation confirmation, that second new high established"

rule: Consolidation above a recent break often sits at the 0.295 (~30% of the range).
quote: "the consolidation above that recent break is going to occur at that 295."

rule: Ideal into-range trade: close below 0.41, decent displacement, retrace to that area, then continuation to 0.7475.
quote: "close below that 041, get decent displacement away from it, retrace back right back to that area"

rule: Retracements are drawn to peak-consolidation (high volume) areas rather than one-sided imbalance candles.
quote: "A lot of times price is going to be attracted to those, you know, very, very peak consolidation areas."

rule: Direct imbalances against your entry mean expect more drawdown; their function is to put in a new extreme.
quote: "you should know the function of these imbalances is what to put in a new low."

rule: Order block / CSS (his definition): needs a recent break-of-structure candle that closed beyond the previous candle's high/low.
quote: "For me to consider an order block, we would have had to had a recent break of a structure candle"

rule: Confirmation alternative to blind limits: wait for a body close back below 0.705, then re-enter at an unmitigated area or limit at 0.705/0.7475.
quote: "And once we get a body close back below that 705"

rule: Prominent swing areas that align with GB levels often get a double tap (first-tap low liquidated) before the rebound.
quote: "a lot of times you're going to see the market refer back and get a double tap."

rule: Aim to place the entry within wicks forming at key levels after a continuous move.
quote: "That's usually my ultimate goal with these kind of trades is I want to place myself within wicks."

rule: Extreme-wick reversal: after an extreme wick (e.g. new hour sweeping prior hourly low) rebalances its 50%, buy stop above that candle, stop below the low.
quote: "We can measure that wick, get the 50% of that right here"

rule: Almost every POI has a responsible candle (last opposing candle before the close through); its 50% is a sensitive continuation level.
quote: "almost every single time there's going to be a responsible candle for the closure of that area."

rule: Discipline: stay level-headed, focus on your own journey, don't rush the process.
quote: "it's important to stay levelheaded, stay focused on yourself and your journey more than anything."

rule: Fund trading from a day job (plus extra work); the day job should cover all bills and savings so losses never touch living money.
quote: "your day job should cover all of your bills, should even cover savings, right? And then you should go get another job or find a side hustle"

rule: With a 1:2 R plan you only need about a one-in-three hit rate, which removes the fear that drives early stop moves.
quote: "let's say you have a one to two R, you only need to be right 34% of the time"

rule: Results come from mindset and execution more than the strategy; even simple retail methods broke even for him.
quote: "it's not the strategy that you use and that it's the mindset that you have and the execution that you're capable of implementing"

rule: Be long below the lows and short above the highs (the smart-money idea that led him to ICT).
quote: "You want to be long and below the lows and shorting above the highs."

rule: Pick concepts you can clearly identify in real time; any ICT model can work with correct psychology and risk management.
quote: "all of it could work if you implement the correct psychology and risk management"

rule: (citing ICT core content month 5) Institutional swing points are either a breaker block or a failure swing; he chose the breaker because its stop hunt is identifiable.
quote: "A breaker block or it's a failure swing. And for me, the reason why I chose a breaker block was because you can identify the stop hunt."

rule: A breaker requires a stop hunt (run above a high or below a low) before you start looking for an entry.
quote: "you need to have that stop hunt. You need to have that run above the high or the run below the low to even begin searching"

rule: Restrict yourself to one pattern in one window (breaker at 9:30) so the yes/no trade decision is simple.
quote: "if you're only looking for a breaker block and you're only looking during 930, it will be very simple to understand if there is or isn't a trade"

rule: (quoting ICT) The breaker is one of the strongest algorithmic entry patterns, especially after liquidity is taken at the opening price.
quote: "the breaker is one of the strongest algorithmic entry patterns, especially if you have taken out liquidity at the opening price"

rule: The "unicorn" is a breaker block with an FVG, a name taken from ICT's market reviews.
quote: "market review after market review from ICT showing breaker blocks with FVGs and calling them unicorns is what created the model"

rule: When the model is not present, do not trade; wait for it.
quote: "When that model is not present, have the patience to wait until it is."

rule: Choose the open that fits your daily life (he uses the 9:30 NY open; 8:30 if work starts at 9) and show up every day.
quote: "you have to figure out what works best for you and your daily life"

rule: Go live only after collecting undeniable evidence that the model works.
quote: "Once I compiled an undeniable amount of evidence showing that this model works, that is when I started using live money."

rule: Do not change the model after a 4-6 trade losing streak; let the probabilities play out.
quote: "Don't create a model and then the first time you go on a five losing streak automatically think you need to change something."

rule: Bias always starts on the daily chart (higher-timeframe order flow).
quote: "the unicorn model for me always begins on the daily. The daily is the higher timeframe order flow."

rule: Daily bias comes from internal vs external liquidity: internal = FVGs, external = swing highs/lows; price at an internal level draws to external.
quote: "Internal liquidity is FVGs. External liquidity is swing highs or swing lows."

rule: Timeframe chain is daily (bias) -> hourly (areas of interest) -> 5m (entry function).
quote: "from the daily, we move to the hourly. That is because of timeframe alignment"

rule: Hourly areas of interest in the bias direction: for bearish bias, bearish FVGs or a swing high (bullish: bullish FVGs or swing lows).
quote: "Since we are bearish from the daily chart, we are looking for bearish FVGs or a swing high."

rule: Only search for an entry once price reaches a higher-timeframe area of interest during the open.
quote: "Since we are at an area of interest, we can begin position searching for our entry function."

rule: Entry function (unicorn): stop hunt, then displacement through the breaker block, with an FVG in the displacement aligned with the breaker.
quote: "First, we would need a stop hunt. Then we would need displacement through the breaker block."

rule: Breaker block = the lowest down-close candle before the up leg that took liquidity (bearish case); if several consecutive down closes, use all of them.
quote: "When the breaker block has consecutive closes in a row, we use all of the consecutive closes."

rule: Displacement through the breaker requires a candle close beyond it; a wick through is not enough.
quote: "We almost displaced through the breaker block, but as you can see, the candle could not close below the level."

rule: Enter with a limit order at the beginning of the breaker block, stop on the other side of the breaker, target 2R.
quote: "We always enter at the beginning of the breaker block. We always put the stop loss on the other side of the breaker block, and then we aim for 2R."

rule: Place entry, stop and 2R take-profit as resting orders up front; the only outcomes are win or loss.
quote: "I am setting a limit order for entry, I am setting a limit stop loss, and I am setting a limit TP at 2R."

rule: No break-even stop, no trailing, no trimming; wait for validation (TP) or invalidation (stop).
quote: "I do not accept break even. I do not trail my position."

rule: Entry location and time are fixed: start of the breaker, during the opening times.
quote: "The entry location is always the same spot. The entry time is always during the opening times."

rule: After a win, stop trading for the day ("play defense") rather than using profit as cushion.
quote: "The individual that thinks he has a cushion to work with is going to go back into the market and lose the profits he just made."

rule: Max one trade per day and two per week, win or lose.
quote: "I only trade two times a week, maximum. I do not take multiple trades in one day."

rule: Risk less than 1% of the account per trade, aiming 1:2 RR.
quote: "For me, it's less than 1% of the account per trade. Aiming for one to two RR."

rule: Stop for a long always goes below the breaker block.
quote: "Stop loss for the position always goes below the breaker block."

rule: The unicorn is a breaker block paired with a fair value gap.
quote: "The unicorn is a breaker block paired with a fair value gap."

rule: Bearish FVG: candle 1's low does not overlap candle 3's high.
quote: "for a bearish fair value gap, the first candlestick's low will not overlap with the third candlestick's high."

rule: Bullish FVG: candle 1's high does not overlap candle 3's low.
quote: "the first candlestick's high does not overlap with the third candlestick's low."

rule: A breaker block is a structural pattern: bearish = high, low, higher high (stops swept), lower low (displacement).
quote: "looking back at it, it is a high, low, higher high, lower low."

rule: Bullish breaker structure: swing low, swing high, lower low sweeping stops, then a higher high displacing through.
quote: "We put in a lower low, sweeping stops below here, and then we put in a higher high and displacing through this area here."

rule: Bearish breaker candle: the lowest / last down-close candle before the move that made the higher high.
quote: "I'm focused on the lowest down close candle prior to the move that went and made this higher high or rated [raided] stops."

rule: Bullish breaker candle: the last up-close candle before the move that made the lower low.
quote: "I'm focused on the last up close or bullish candle prior to the move that made the lower low."

rule: Unicorn model = breaker block with an overlapping FVG created by the displacement through the breaker; the FVG is used for entry.
quote: "The unicorn model is combining a breaker block with an overlapping fair value gap."

rule: Prefer opposite-side equal lows to be taken before the move toward the draw (smooth highs).
quote: "we have equal lows, which I would like to see be taken out prior to a move towards these highs."

rule: Bullish breaker requires a higher high formed with displacement through the up-close candle.
quote: "I want to see if we form a higher high with displacement through this up-close candle."

rule: Stop options: on the swing low (wider) or below the breaker and FVG (tighter, higher R).
quote: "My stop loss can either go on this low,"

rule: Project the manipulation leg and anticipate the 2-2.5 area before a retracement or reversal as added confluence.
quote: "anticipate price reaching for this two to 2.5 area before a retracement or reversal, which is another added confluence here."

rule: Off the New York open, expect price to run the lows left by a slow grind up.
quote: "off the New York open, I'd like to see price drop down to these lows."

rule: If the stop at the swing high is too large, place it just above the breaker.
quote: "My stop on this high is a bit large, reaching for these lows. So I would have it just above the breaker."

rule: If price reaches the target before tagging the entry, do not chase; you were left behind.
quote: "price reaches our target prior to tagging us in, so I would not be interested."

rule: Price may dig deeper into the FVG and breaker; it stays valid while bodies do not close below the mean threshold of the up-close candles.
quote: "it's important to see that the bodies aren't closing below the mean threshold of these up-close candles."

rule: A bullish breaker pattern is a low, high, lower low, then higher high.
quote: "a breaker block is a candlestick pattern in which we form a low, high, lower low, and higher high"

rule: The bullish breaker block is the single or series of up-close candles between the low and the high; expect a reaction there to continue higher.
quote: "we look for the series or single up-close candle here between the low and the high, marking that out, that is our breaker block"

rule: Swings must be confirmed: a lower low only counts once a swing low is put in.
quote: "You can see we've created a lower low, but we want to see when that gets confirmed and put in a swing low."

rule: Bodies respecting the breaker on a retest (even after a wick sweep into it) keeps it valid.
quote: "we sweep this low into the breaker block, the bodies are still respecting"

rule: A bearish breaker needs high, low, higher high, then lower low; the breaker is the single or series of down-close candles.
quote: "I want to see a high, low, higher high, then lower low. From here I can look for the series or single down close candle"

rule: No lower low after the higher high means no breaker.
quote: "So now we're looking for a lower low. You can see that never forms. This does not form a breaker."

rule: Breakers should be paired with displacement, e.g. an FVG overlapping them.
quote: "one thing that is important with breaker blocks is I want to see displacement paired with them"

rule: Unicorn model: a breaker block overlapping an FVG of the same direction.
quote: "The unicorn model is where we have a bearish breaker block aligned with a bearish fair value gap."

rule: Stop goes either beyond the breaker block and its FVG, or at the swing low/high.
quote: "I look to place it either below the bullish breaker block and the fair value gap that is created there, or at the swing low or high"

rule: Entry is either at the start of the FVG (letting price trade into the breaker) or at the breaker within the FVG.
quote: "I can either take an entry at the start of the fair value gap, letting it trade up into the breaker, or I can look to take my entry at the breaker within the fair value gap"

rule: Stop choice has trade-offs; the swing stop's 2R just missed and stopped out while the breaker stop hit 2R; it is the trader's choice.
quote: "there are benefits and drawdowns to each stop loss placement. However, that is up to you to decide what works best for you"

rule: Choose between the earlier breaker entry (to be in the trade) and waiting for the FVG (better R:R); user discretion.
quote: "Do you want to wait for that fair value gap entry to get better risk to reward? Or do you want to be in the trade"

rule: A stop just below the breaker low gives a much nearer 2R than a stop at the swing low.
quote: "If my stop loss was at this low, I would need to have a take profit all the way up here to reach 2R"

rule: Breaker block is marked as the whole candle series including wicks; order block is marked only at the opening price of the series.
quote: "With a breaker block I mark out the whole series of the candles, including the wicks, while with an order block I will just mark out the opening price"

rule: Breaker and order block refer to price near the same level but are different concepts; choice is personal preference.
quote: "They are going to refer to price action at a similar level, however they are different concepts."

rule: In a breaker, the manipulation leg is the leg that made the lower low; project it for targets (e.g. -2 to -2.5).
quote: "This leg down that created the lower low is our manipulation leg and I can project that out"

rule: Targets can be 2R or the projection levels, which gave a 4R trade in the example.
quote: "I could look to target either 2R, which I would have taken right there, or I can look to target these projections right here, giving a 4R trade"

rule: Top-down: an HTF (hourly) unicorn at a sweep low plus a kill zone frames a 5m breaker entry.
quote: "So now we have a breaker block overlapping with a fair value gap or a unicorn model on the hourly chart. And we just entered the London kill zone."

rule: If previous-day lows (equal lows) are not taken and price retraces into the prior range, that is a short opportunity.
quote: "if this is not taken and we retrace back into this previous range, that is an opportunity to short"

rule: A unicorn on the hourly can be entered directly without dropping to a lower timeframe.
quote: "if I did not even want to go to a lower timeframe, I could look to take an entry right here"

rule: Losses are inevitable; a valid unicorn after a sell-side sweep can still stop out.
quote: "Losses are inevitable in trading, and that is why I show this example."

rule: First decide your entry timeframe; it depends on what you watch and what kind of trader you are.
quote: "you have to know which timeframe you want to enter on, whether that is the one minute, five minute, 15 minute."

rule: He uses the 1m and 15s for entries.
quote: "Personally, I use the 1 minute and 15 second the most for my entries."

rule: Know which kill zones you trade and search for the model only within them; he trades New York open.
quote: "The next thing you need to know is which kill zones you enter in and search for these models within those kill zones."

rule: His concept set: displacement/FVGs, order blocks, OTE or discount/premium, SMT, inducement, BPR.
quote: "I will personally be covering displacement or fair value gaps, order blocks, OTE, or discount and premium, smart money techniques, inducement, and BPR."

rule: Have a labelled diagram so you know exactly how you enter, with explicit extra requirements (OTE, premium, SMT, BPR, internal range liquidity).
quote: "ideally you want to be able to have a diagram and be able to label it and know exactly how you want to enter."

rule: Decide what you look for, make a model and stick to it.
quote: "Really, you just have to decide what do you like to look for, what makes the most sense to you, and then make a model and stick to it."

rule: Classic FVG setup: liquidity grab, breaker structure, fair value gap.
quote: "Liquidity grab, breaker structure, fair value gap."

rule: Model 1: liquidity grab, no closes below, aggressive move higher breaking structure, retrace into FVG = long.
quote: "No closes below, aggressive move higher, breaking structure here, and then we get a retracement into a fair value gap, and there is our long entry."

rule: Model 3 = model 1 plus OTE (displacement leg low to high) to ensure solid RR.
quote: "The only difference between model 1 and model 3 in my drawings is that you add an OTE in order to make sure you have solid risk to reward in the trade."

rule: Models 2 and 4 add internal range liquidity being taken before the move.
quote: "the only difference between model 1 and 3 and model 2 and 4 is that there is internal range liquidity being taken before the move"

rule: Entry in OTE with internal range liquidity and an FVG directly to its left.
quote: "Internal range liquidity with a fair value gap sitting right there."

rule: BPR: an aggressive buy met by an aggressive sell (or vice versa), shown by FVGs; their overlap is the BPR.
quote: "BPR, which is really just an aggressive buy met with an aggressive sell, which is shown with fair value gaps"

rule: Bearish BPR: short at the overlap, risk the high or the bodies of that high, target new lows.
quote: "which then you would short, risking this high, worth bodies of that high, targeting new lows."

rule: Bullish BPR: aggressive sell met by aggressive buy; the overlap (pick the smaller gap) is the entry.
quote: "An example of bullish BPR, or balanced price range, would be an aggressive sell met with an aggressive buy."

rule: BPR can be combined with discount/premium or OTE.
quote: "And if you want to combine it with other techniques like discount and premium or OTE, you can definitely do that."

rule: Continuation closure: price sweeps the previous candle's low (high) and closes below (above) it; anticipate continuation.
quote: "When price closes below the previous candle's low, I can anticipate a continuation lower."

rule: Reversal closure: price sweeps the previous candle's low (high) but closes back inside the previous candle's range; anticipate the other direction.
quote: "with a reversal closure, that is when we sweep out the previous candle's low, but we don't close below it."

rule: A candle 2 closure is a reversal closure: sweep of the previous candle's high/low, then close back inside the range.
quote: "a candle 2 closure is focused on when we have a reversal closure or we sweep out that previous candle's high or low and then close back inside the range."

rule: Bullish C2: sweep the previous candle's low, close back above it; bearish C2: sweep the previous high, close back below it.
quote: "price sweeps out the previous candle's low and then closes back above that candle's low, signifying that price has reversed in candle 2"

rule: Only use C2 closures at a higher-timeframe key level; a sweep-and-close-back pattern anywhere is unlikely to work.
quote: "If you just look for every pattern that has a sweep and a closure back in, that is unlikely to work."

rule: Frame C2 with bias and a higher-timeframe POI: fair value gaps and highs/lows.
quote: "You want to define this with bias and a higher time frame point of interest, which I use fair value gaps and highs and lows."

rule: After a C2 closure, anticipate candle 3 to expand in the reversal direction.
quote: "once we have this closure, we can then anticipate candle 3 to have a continuation."

rule: If C3 closes beyond C2's high (low), that is a continuation closure; anticipate C4 to expand too.
quote: "That is a continuation closure. So, we can anticipate price to expand higher as well in candle 4."

rule: If C2 has a large wick, watch its 0.5; C3 should form its wick respecting it, else the swing likely fails.
quote: "If it doesn't respect the 0.5, then it's likely to fail and a swing point is unlikely to form."

rule: After a strong C3 close, mark the whole C3 range and its 50% as the area to hold for a C4 continuation.
quote: "with candle 3, we can do the same as we have a strong closure. I'll mark out the entire candle's range, 50% of that"

rule: Practice: mark every swing point on a daily chart, remove those without a C2 closure, then keep only those at a POI.
quote: "what you'll want to do is just go find swing points. So, find any point in which the market made a turn and go ahead and mark them all out"

rule: A swing point where price never closed back inside the previous candle's range is not a C2 closure.
quote: "this is not a candle to closure as price never closed back below its previous candle's high."

rule: A C2 whose sweep fails to take the relevant high/low (no POI) is not valid for bias.
quote: "we fail to take out this high. So, it is not valid, right? Because I do not have that point of interest."

rule: A POI can come from a much higher timeframe (e.g. an old monthly high).
quote: "you can go to the monthly chart and see we took out a previous high from quite long ago"

rule: Ideally C2 is a reversal, not an expansion; a C2 with a shallow wick that already expanded sets up a weaker C3 (new phase possible).
quote: "ideally we want candle 2 to have a reversal to set up a candle 3 continuation."

rule: Advanced: after a protected swing forms, opposing candles can serve as the POI for a later C2 closure.
quote: "We do form a protected swing. So, I am not looking for price to return to this level."

rule: Bias workflow: find C2 closures on the daily first, then check for a POI, which gives the daily bias.
quote: "you want to find those candle closures first, then see if they have a point of interest, and then that gives you bias"

rule: Confirm a C2 on the aligned lower timeframe with a CISD: find the extreme, mark the series of candles that made it.
quote: "We look for a change in the state of delivery. We're going to find the high. Find the series of candles that made that high"

rule: The bias holds as long as price respects the previous candle's range (EQ area); a high formed in consolidation is hard to trust.
quote: "to continue lower as long as it remains in respect to the previous candle's range."

rule: A lower-timeframe C2 at a POI inside the higher-timeframe move can mark the high of day and give continuation entries.
quote: "we can anticipate this to be where the high a day forms."

rule: Timeframe pairings: daily C2 -> hourly CISD; hourly C2 -> 5-minute CISD; 4H -> 15m.
quote: "if I'm on the daily, I'm going to use the hourly for a change in the state of delivery. If I'm on the hourly, I will use the 5minute."

rule: His indicator marks the C2 closure, the CISD, the EQ area and liquidity targets.
quote: "this is where I will add in my indicator that marks out that candle to closure for me."

rule: Once into candle 5 and 6 a new phase of price may start; be more careful.
quote: "once you get into candle five and six, that's where you can get caught in a new phase of price."

rule: C2 closures often mark market turning points.
quote: "a lot of times a candle 2 closure will mark a turning point in the market"

rule: Continuation closure: price takes the previous candle's low (high) and closes beyond it; expect the next candle to continue with the trend.
quote: "if price takes out that low, for example, and closes below it, that is a continuation closure."

rule: Reversal closure: price sweeps the previous candle's high/low and closes back inside; expect a reversal.
quote: "with a reversal closure, that is when price sweeps out the previous candle's high or low, closes back above it."

rule: In a C2 closure, price reversed in candle 2, so trade candle 3 and candle 4.
quote: "In a candle 2 closure, price reversed in candle 2. So then I could look to trade candle 3 and candle 4."

rule: If price hits a key level without a reversal closure, do not expect a reversal yet; wait for either a C2 closure (sweep and close back) or a C3 closure.
quote: "we hit a key level but price does not have a reversal closure. So I cannot expect price to reverse yet."

rule: Bullish C3 closure: candle 3 does not sweep candle 2's low but closes over candle 2's body (engulfing); expect candle 4 higher.
quote: "a candle 3 closure which is where price does not sweep out the high or the low but then closes over the body of candle 2."

rule: Bearish C3 closure: candle 2 closes over candle 1's high, candle 3 does not take candle 2's high but closes below candle 2's body; expect candle 4 lower.
quote: "candle 3 does not take out the high of candle 2, but closes below the body of candle 2."

rule: After a C3 expansion candle, mark C3's whole range; C4's wick should form in the upper half (bullish) or lower half (bearish).
quote: "I'll use the whole candle's range, the upper half of that. And that is where I want to see the wick of candle 4 form"

rule: A reach into a POI (FVG) without a reversal closure is not a C2; you cannot anticipate an immediate expansion and must gather more information.
quote: "does it have a reversal closure? No. But that means it's not a candle to closure."

rule: When a swing is taken but the candle does not close back inside the previous candle, let another candle print.
quote: "do we have a reversal candle? No, we do not cuz price did not close back inside its previous candle."

rule: A swing point that is neither a C2 nor a C3 closure is ignored.
quote: "it is neither a candle 2 or a candle 3 closure. So I go ahead and remove that from the chart."

rule: A mechanically ideal C2 that just misses the POI (FVG) is not valid.
quote: "although it is a valid candle to closure, an ideal one, it is not valid because it is missing that point of interest."

rule: A mechanically valid C2 that leaves a high very close by is probably not worth taking.
quote: "although it is mechanically valid, does it make sense to leave this high right here? So close? Probably not."

rule: Don't trade away from a level after price already reached the opposing liquidity (equal lows / failure swings).
quote: "it is a candle to closure, but we already reach into these equal lows. So, I wouldn't really be interested in this"

rule: A C3 closure that creates a protected swing is ideal.
quote: "that is a candle three closure and also an ideal one because it creates a protected swing"

rule: Both a POI and a valid closure (C2 or C3) are required; don't pick random swing points.
quote: "if we do not have a point of interest or a valid closure, I'm not just going to choose random swing points. I need both of those."

rule: Execute a 4H C3 on the 15-minute chart; the C3 closing over C2's body at the reversal point is the CISD.
quote: "since we are on the 4hour chart, we would go to the 15-minute chart."

rule: Entry in the next 4H candle at the open or in the upper half of the previous 4H candle, stop on the 15m protected swing, target 2R.
quote: "take any entry in here in the open or in the upper half of this previous 4hour candle. put my stop on a protected swing"

rule: If there is neither a C2 nor a C3 closure, the model does not align even if you anticipate the move.
quote: "I can anticipate things, but my model would not align with it as I do not have a candle 2 or a candle 3 closure."

rule: Without a closure, wait for a close through the series of down-close candles to create a new protected swing, then trade into prior highs.
quote: "once we get a closure through the series of downcloed candles, that's creating a new protected swing"

rule: Use C2 and C3 closures with POIs and context; don't pattern-trade the model.
quote: "I don't want to just randomly choose swing points or pattern trade the model."

rule: C2 and C3 closures are the only two formations in his model.
quote: "these are the only two formations that I look for within my model."

rule: Both closure types always require a higher-timeframe key level.
quote: "First off, we always need a higher time frame key level."

rule: Without a C2 you cannot tell if candle 3 will run candle 2's extreme or reverse, so let candle 3 print first.
quote: "This means I can't really anticipate if candle 3 is going to run out candle 2's low or if it's going to reverse"

rule: Closures + equilibrium (HTF wick location) + lower-timeframe CISD or continuation order blocks is the entire model.
quote: "if you use lower time frame change in the state of delivery or continuation order blocks, you essentially have my entire model."

rule: CISD is price going from bullish to bearish delivery or the reverse.
quote: "the change in state of delivery is when price goes from bullish to bearish or from bearish to bullish."

rule: Bearish CISD occurs when, after price moves up into an HTF PD array or important level, the opening price of the up-close candle (or series) is closed below.
quote: "the change in state of delivery occurs, when the opening price of this up close candle or series of up close candles gets closed below."

rule: After the bearish CISD close, anticipate price to trade lower; mirror for bullish (close over the down-close series after a sell-stop raid).
quote: "After being closed below, I can anticipate price to trade lower."

rule: When price returns to the CISD level after the change, anticipate a reaction in the new direction.
quote: "When price returns, I can anticipate a reaction to trade higher."

rule: With a series of same-direction candles into the level, use the opening price of the FIRST candle of the series as the CISD level.
quote: "when there is more than one up close candle or a series of up close candles, I use the opening price of the first candle."

rule: He generally prefers a lower-timeframe sweep as part of his entry models.
quote: "I generally prefer a lower time frame sweep with my entry models"

rule: The relevant series is the up-close candle(s) that made the new high before the displacement down; a sweep and drop that does not close below them is not yet a CISD.
quote: "what I'm looking for here are the series or single up close candle that made the new high before displacing and closing below."

rule: After a CISD, enter on a retest of the order block with the stop on the high, targeting nearby opposite liquidity (London lows).
quote: "I could be looking for price to retest the order block with my stop on the high."

rule: He prefers a minimum 2R; if the liquidity target gives less, project the manipulation leg and use the -2 standard deviation.
quote: "since this is 1.66R and I generally prefer a minimum of 2R, what can I do?"

rule: A candle series becomes a validated order block once price closes beyond its opening price.
quote: "Which is now validating it as an order block."

rule: Top-down: after an HTF PD array is engaged (daily FVG), look for a CISD on the hourly to confirm the bias.
quote: "ideally we want to see a change in the state of delivery after engaging our higher time frame PD array."

rule: Next day model: a daily candle that reaches into a daily FVG, respects it and closes down implies the next day moves lower, taking the previous day low.
quote: "Using the next day model, we can anticipate price to move lower the next day, taking out previous day low."

rule: Project the manipulation leg (high to low) and target the -2 to -2.5 standard deviation area.
quote: "Then we can look for the negative 2 to negative 2.5 area for a target."

rule: When bearish, a run of an old high is an area to look for shorts.
quote: "when we are bearish with price action, a run of an old high is an area to be looking short."

rule: At the 9:30 open, a manipulation up then a close below the up-close series confirms the CISD for a short with stop on the high.
quote: "Here we get that close, validating it as a change in state of delivery."

rule: Entry model sequence: manipulation, then CISD, then order blocks and FVGs delivering price to projections.
quote: "what I focus on is a manipulation, then a change in state of delivery, and then I focus on order blocks and fair value gaps to deliver price to projections."

rule: First entry: at the CISD or on its order-block retest, stop on the manipulation extreme that swept.
quote: "looking to enter here at the change of the state of delivery or when it retests the order block, my stop on the manipulation high, which swept."

rule: If the first entry is missed, newly formed and closed-through up-close series become further order blocks for re-entry.
quote: "if I was going to miss the first entry, I'd be looking for another entry here."

rule: For shorts, only take entries within the premium of the dealing range.
quote: "I'm only going to be looking for entries within a premium of this dealing range here."

rule: A move into the -2 to -2.5 projection and below lows can itself become the manipulation for a reversal, confirmed by closing over the down-close series.
quote: "if this is going to become manipulation, I'd want to see a change in the state of delivery or price close over the series of down close candles here."

rule: Use liquidity sitting in the projection zone (e.g. an old high in the -2 to -2.5) as the first target.
quote: "What do we have resting in the negative 2 to negative 2.5? We have an old high. So that will be my first target."

rule: Box setup: mark the accumulation range, its highest body (the box line) and the manipulation; normal entry is a retest of the box line, targets from projecting the manipulation leg.
quote: "we'll also mark out the highest body in that accumulation as that is the box setup"

rule: For confirmation in the box setup, wait for an order-block formation / CISD on the retest instead of entering immediately.
quote: "instead of immediately taking an entry, I'm looking for a formation of an order block or a change in the state of delivery right here."

rule: With a CISD-confirmed box entry, the stop can go either at the CISD swing (if a sweep occurred) or at the manipulation extreme.
quote: "I can either put my stop here or up here. In this case, I'm comfortable putting my stop here as we had a sweep."

rule: A target where an FVG lines up with a standard deviation level is preferred confluence.
quote: "looking for a previous high here, or this fair value gap that lines up with the first standard deviation."

rule: Dealing range: zoom in where price is and take the nearest high and low.
quote: "The easiest way to do this is zoom your screen in and look exactly where price is at. Where is a high and a low? It's as simple as that."

rule: Draw a Fib from the dealing range high to low to get premium/discount.
quote: "So then if you take a FIB from high to low of that, that's your dealing range."

rule: External liquidity on a zoomed-in range becomes internal liquidity when zoomed out; do not get caught up in labels.
quote: "as you zoom out, that external liquidity becomes internal liquidity. So don't get too caught up in that"

rule: Multiple nested dealing ranges exist; what matters is where price is trading and what you are looking for.
quote: "you can have multiple dealing ranges like that. But it's important to just notice where is price trading?"

rule: A dealing range that price is already above is not valid; zoom out to the high and low that contain price.
quote: "these dealing ranges right here. Aren't really valid, right? Because price is higher than that."

rule: Displacement range: an aggressive price move over structure.
quote: "Displacement ranges are aggressive price action moves over structure"

rule: Before going long, want a retracement into a discount of the displacement range.
quote: "ideally, you want to see a retracement into a discount before going long"

rule: After the displacement leg extends, either expect a reach for the high or a retracement into the new leg's discount.
quote: "ideally, you'd want to see either a reach for the high or retracement back down"

rule: Anchor the displacement Fib at the low that started the displacement and broke structure, and trail it up with each new high.
quote: "I take the low that started this displacement range, which broke the structure"

rule: For longs, require discount of both the dealing range and the displacement range.
quote: "discount of the displacement range, discount of the dealing range. This is where you want to be looking too long [to go long]"

rule: In premium of the dealing range, look for shorts, not longs.
quote: "now you can see we're in a premium of this dealing range. So if you were looking for short opportunities, this is where you'd want to be looking"

rule: The ideal retracement goes into discount and OTE.
quote: "Where do we want to see this move? Into a discount and ideally OTE."

rule: Look for PD arrays (e.g. an order block) inside the discount/OTE zone.
quote: "ideally you want to search for PD arrays within these points of interest"

rule: Candles not closing through the order block confirms respect.
quote: "you can see how the candles do not close in respect to this order block, and we get our move higher"

rule: If the first entry is missed, look for a second entry in discount of the new displacement range and the dealing range (e.g. 0.62 plus an order block).
quote: "You would want to see if you can get another entry in a discount of the dealing range and a discount of this displacement range."

rule: CISD is the order-block formation that appears when trend changes.
quote: "The change in the state of delivery is the order block formation that forms when trend changes."

rule: CISD = price reaches an important level (sweeps a low/high or taps an FVG) and then closes through the series of candles that reached into it.
quote: "What defines a change in the state of delivery is price reaching into an important level sweeping out a low or reaching into a fair value gap and then closing through the series of candles that wretch into that important level."

rule: On an HTF candle-2 or candle-3 closure, check inside that HTF candle on the paired LTF for a CISD.
quote: "when I have a candle 2 or a candle 3 closure on the higher time frame, I'm going to look inside that higher time frame candle and make sure it has a change in the state of delivery."

rule: Without the LTF CISD, do not treat the HTF closure as a trend shift; wait for the CISD or skip the setup.
quote: "Going to wait for that change in the state of delivery to occur or I'm going to ignore the setup."

rule: CISD check procedure: find the extreme, find the series of candles that made it, ask whether price closed through that level.
quote: "I find the high. I find the series of candles that made that high. Did we close below that level? No."

rule: An LTF CISD without an HTF candle-2/3 closure is not a setup.
quote: "So, even though we have a change in the state of delivery, it does not mean anything to me unless it is paired with a higher time frame candle closure."

rule: Candle-3 closure (no candle 2): candle 3 closes beyond the opening price of candle 2; then check the LTF CISD and look for continuation in candle 4.
quote: "We have a candle 3 closure because we don't have a candle 2 and then candle 3 closes below the opening price in candle 2."

rule: A candle-3 closure whose LTF fails to close through the level is just forming a consolidation.
quote: "we fail to close below this level. And now we are just forming a consolidation."

rule: If candle 3 never closes beyond candle 2's open, it is not a candle-3 closure and any LTF CISD is ignored.
quote: "This is not a valid candle 3 closure because price never closes below the opening price in candle 2."

rule: The "series" can be a single candle.
quote: "find the series of candles that made it. In this case, it's one."

rule: Monthly closures are confirmed with a daily CISD (fractal: any timeframe pair).
quote: "So, you can see it's a fractal concept."

rule: His indicator prints the remaining logic (T-spot, EQ) only once both requirements are met.
quote: "Since we have two of those requirements met, then it will print out the rest of the logic, right?"

rule: Waiting for both the HTF closure and the LTF CISD avoids losses where the HTF swing gets taken.
quote: "So by waiting for the closure through or having both parts of the fractal model, the candle closure and the swing point confirmation or the change in the state of delivery, I saved myself from taking losses that look like this."

rule: A failed CISD usually produces a consolidation that sweeps one side then trades to the other.
quote: "Usually when we fail to form a change in the state of delivery, we're going to consolidate, form a consolidation, and then take out one side of the range and trade to the other."

rule: If a continuation forms and its protected swing is then taken, the trend is weak / consolidating.
quote: "We take out that protected swing. That means this trend is not looking that great."

rule: Not every close-over is a good CISD: if the HTF candle consolidated for about half its duration before closing over, treat it as consolidation.
quote: "Just because it does have a closure over, doesn't mean it's a good closure over. If it consolidates for half of the candle and then closes over, it's usually just a consolidation."

rule: The ideal CISD is a V-shaped reversal from the sweep.
quote: "You want to see that nice V-shaped reversal or Vshape paired with the change in the state of delivery."

rule: After a valid closure + CISD, enter on a continuation order block at a POI, not on the first touch.
quote: "I just want to be looking for a continuation order block."

rule: A POI touch with a candle closure but no continuation is not an entry; wait for the next swing to produce one.
quote: "We reach in, we have a candle closure, but do we form a continuation? No."

rule: Expect the move once a protected swing forms inside the HTF candle.
quote: "as we formed a protected swing inside this higher time frame candle."

rule: Daily bearish order block = price reaches into an FVG, displaces and closes below the series of up-close candles; look for price to return into it to target sell-side liquidity.
quote: "displacing and closing below the series of up close candles here so that is my order block"

rule: With no red-folder news Mon-Wed, his interest lies on the first red-folder news day, after the 8:30 release.
quote: "Thursday is our first red folder News day of the week so this is where my interest lies post 8:30"

rule: A lower high next to a prior high is a failure swing / low-resistance liquidity.
quote: "this creates a failure swing or low resistance liquidity"

rule: When trading lower, want high-resistance liquidity on the highs and target low-resistance liquidity.
quote: "ideally when we are trading L lower I want to have high resistance liquidity on the highs and Target low resistance liquidity"

rule: Want the news to manipulate price up into the highs first, then trade down.
quote: "ideally I want to see price reach up or manipulate up to then go down"

rule: In the market maker sell model, previous day low is the original consolidation and the draw on liquidity.
quote: "that is our previous day low so I'll mark that out and that is our original consolidation in this market maker sell model"

rule: Wait for price to reach back into a premium of the range before shorting; measure the range ignoring the CPI wick.
quote: "I'm ignoring the wick here because it's just CPI manipulation"

rule: For the short, want an intermediate-term high put in within the premium of the range.
quote: "I want to see an intermediate term High put in here in the premium of the range"

rule: Pair the entry with a bullish order block from the buy side of the curve, used as a mitigation block on the sell side.
quote: "I'm looking for a bullish order block on the buy side of the curve to use on the sell side of the curve"

rule: An intermediate-term high is a high higher than the short-term highs on both sides; stop goes on it.
quote: "if I have a short-term High here a short-term High here and this high is higher than both of those that is an intermediate term High"

rule: Do not short into failure swings on the highs; require a sweep first.
quote: "I'm not interested to take an entry here because I have failure swings on the high if I'm going to be taking a short entry I want to see a sweep"

rule: Entry: FVG overlapping the mitigation block, stop on the likely intermediate-term high, target previous day low.
quote: "look to take my entry on the fair value Gap overlapping with the mitigation block My Stop on this intermediate term high"

rule: He took 2R at previous day low rather than 3R to the total draw on liquidity.
quote: "I could be looking for my total draw on liquidity down here for 3 R but I personally just went for 2 R"

rule: Keep the stop at the high where the trade is invalidated.
quote: "I want to keep my stop on this high because this is where it is invalidated"

rule: Do not move the stop to break-even; break-even is not the invalidation, and doing so here would have stopped him out before the run.
quote: "my trade is not invalidated at break even"

rule: Find the range first: swing high to swing low, the most prominent range in the area.
quote: "I look for a swing high to a swing low, or essentially the most prominent range in this area"

rule: Draw a Gann box or fib from high to low; 0.5 is equilibrium.
quote: "we can see where our equilibrium rests right here with the 0.5 fib"

rule: Above 0.5 = premium; below 0.5 = discount.
quote: "Anything above the 0.5 fib is considered at a premium, and anything below the 0.5 fib is considered at a discount."

rule: There are multiple ranges within ranges; each new swing creates a new range.
quote: "There are multiple ranges within ranges."

rule: Discount/premium is used because it shows where R:R is more favorable; entering at equilibrium with stop/target at the extremes is 1R.
quote: "The main reason to be using discount and premium is because it shows where risk to reward is more favorable."

rule: Shorts: PD arrays in premium; longs: PD arrays in discount.
quote: "if I am looking for a short position, I'm looking for PD arrays in a premium to get short"

rule: Ranges expand: move the range extreme with price until a swing high (low) is put in.
quote: "one thing with ranges is they are expanding. So if price moves higher, we're going to track that with our equilibrium range"

rule: After a new low makes a new range, look for price to reach into premium of the previous range.
quote: "we would want to see price reach into a premium of the previous range"

rule: Reversal model inside a range: sweep a lower-timeframe low, break structure up, then use the displacement range's discount.
quote: "we swept this lower timeframe low. We broke structure up."

rule: Before longs in discount, want a raid of the previous day low (or some setup) and a close back in.
quote: "If I'm going to be looking for longs and a discount, I want to see some sort of raid on previous day low or some sort of setup."

rule: Add an OTE inside the discount of the lower-timeframe displacement range for entry; it improves R (3.43R vs 1.6R at equilibrium).
quote: "by entering at a OTE, my risk to reward is 3.43 there, versus 1.6 at an equilibrium"

rule: No candle closes below the OTE = it is being respected.
quote: "it's important to notice how there are no candle closes below there, right? It's respecting it."

rule: Finding the draw on liquidity is how he sets the bias for the day.
quote: "This is essentially what I do each morning in order to determine my bias for the day."

rule: Entering on 5m and lower, find the draw on the daily, 4H and 1h.
quote: "I'm entering on the 5 minute and lower timeframes, so I'm using the daily, 4 hour, and 1 hour as the timeframes where I find my draw."

rule: Entering on the 1h, look to the weekly and monthly for the draw.
quote: "if I was to be entering on the 1 hour chart, I would most likely be looking up to the weekly and monthly for a draw on liquidity."

rule: Determine where price is likely to reach, then use lower timeframes for entry and risk toward that HTF target.
quote: "if I can determine where the market is likely to draw to or reach for, then I can use the lower timeframes to gain an entry and manage my risk"

rule: External draws: old highs and lows, equal highs and lows; internal draws: FVGs and order blocks.
quote: "I search for external liquidity, such as old highs and old lows, equal highs and equal lows, and then internal liquidity."

rule: Volume imbalances and gaps are occasional internal draws.
quote: "I will also throw in the occasional volume imbalance or gap in price."

rule: Also note where price fails to displace over highs/lows and where it is displacing to.
quote: "I will also search for where price fails to displace over lows and highs, as well as where price is displacing to."

rule: Follow the displacement; it is generally right.
quote: "If I follow the displacement, it is generally right."

rule: After a low is taken, ask: displace back into the range (bullish) or keep falling?
quote: "Do we displace back up into the range, pushing a bullish narrative, or do we continue to fall down?"

rule: Do not switch bullish until there is displacement up.
quote: "Now, I won't switch to being bullish until we get displacement up."

rule: After displacement up, the draw is the nearby high and the FVG above.
quote: "When we do get displacement up, where are we likely to be headed? Well, we have this high right here and this fair value gap right here."

rule: Price can draw from the OTE of one range to the OTE of another; the FVG plus previous low is the internal draw.
quote: "If we are going to go from an OTE of this range back to an OTE of this range, what do we have here? A fair value gap as well as a previous low."

rule: If price does not displace below a low or slice through an FVG, expect a move higher.
quote: "If we don't displace below this low, or slice through this fair value gap, I'd want to see a move higher"

rule: Equal highs left behind are a target for later.
quote: "we just left this high, so that will be a target for later, as equal highs"

rule: Drawing higher without displacement means the high is not being targeted; check what array price respects instead.
quote: "we're drawing up higher, but we're not displacing, right? So this high isn't being targeted."

rule: After taking a low without displacing back up, expect lower.
quote: "after taking this low, we don't displace back up. That means we're likely to go lower."

rule: Not displacing below a low means price is likely to reach for old highs.
quote: "since we didn't displace below this low, we're likely to reach for old highs."

rule: Displacing above a high (vs only taking it) makes the next old high the target.
quote: "we displace above this high, right? So with that in mind, I would be targeting this old high up here."

rule: A respected daily OB mean threshold plus a daily FVG with 4H and 1h FVGs nested inside frames the HTF level.
quote: "you can see we have a 4-hour fair value gap nested within this daily fair value gap."

rule: Before RTH open, an 8:00 sweep of internal lows into an FVG with SMT vs NASDAQ points to the range above.
quote: "running these internal lows and actually creating an SMT with the NASDAQ. With that in mind, we are likely targeting up into this range."

rule: Entry on the 1m order block, stop on the low, target slightly before the draw on liquidity.
quote: "I took my entry right here with a stop on this low targeting 39.50 or just slightly before that draw on liquidity."

rule: Knowing the HTF draw keeps lower-timeframe noise from scaring you out of a position.
quote: "knowing so, I didn't let the lower timeframe scare me out of a position and was able to take a trade."

rule: If the nearest daily POI is unconvincing, look further left for one that prior bodies and wicks respected (here a volume imbalance).
