quote: "The prior days bodies and wicks respected both of these levels, and so I felt comfortable still using it."

rule: Watch the correlated index (NQ) filling its own daily FVG as a cue for the ES reversal.
quote: "the important thing I wanted to look for was when NQ was going to fill this fair value gap here"

rule: A 4h SMT where NQ takes a high and ES fails supports the short bias.
quote: "ES failed to take this high here, while NQ did take this high."

rule: Most of his analysis is on the hourly; daily POI plus SMT at the high gives a draw lower to the first BPR and equal lows.
quote: "going down to the hour is where I did most of my analysis"

rule: Candle bodies respecting an area in choppy price action validates it as a level.
quote: "what I noticed with the choppy price action, is how the bodies of these candles respected this area right here"

rule: If price slices through a BPR without a reaction, expect the next liquidity (equal lows) to be taken.
quote: "If we slice through this, I'd want to see these equal lows taken."

rule: After the equal lows are taken, the next PD array becomes the target.
quote: "After these lows were taken, the next PD array that draws my eyes is this BPR down here."

rule: After intraday targets are hit, go back to the daily to re-evaluate the final target (daily FVG).
quote: "after this was taken, I went back out to the daily to reevaluate, and I noticed this daily fair value gap here"

rule: C2U is POI-based: entries do not need a daily bias (optional pairing).
quote: "I don't specifically rely on a daily bias in order to enter a trade now you can pair it with a daily bias if you'd like"

rule: TTrades' view (relayed by the guest): you do not have to trade with a daily bias; find a model that works without one.
quote: "if you don't want to to trade with a daily bias then don't trade with a daily bias nothing says that you have to trade with a daily bias"

rule: Premise: price cannot reverse without a swing point, and the unicorn is ICT's strongest reversal pattern, so join a unicorn to a swing point.
quote: "price cannot reverse without creating a swing point"

rule: Mark hourly swing points that reach into a POI: swing high/low, opposing range candles, FVGs, previous day / session / week high or low.
quote: "I looked where those hourly swing points would reach into a point of Interest"

rule: Inside the wick of an hourly swing-point candle at a POI, look on the 5m for a unicorn.
quote: "inside of those wicks there would be 5 minute unicorns that would form"

rule: Only take unicorns that form in about 10-12 candles or fewer; slow ones are swing points mixed with consolidation.
quote: "I want to see a unicorn form quickly and concisely within that 10 to 12 candle range or even less than that"

rule: Use the 7-hour candle (AM Trades' expansion model) as the daily profile; the 1:00-8:00 a.m. candle is the London candle.
quote: "he uses the 7h hour candle as the daily profile it's a much simpler version of viewing the daily profiles"

rule: Check ADR used: the target should be reachable without exceeding the 6-month ADR; if ADR is already exceeded, expect a reversal.
quote: "so it makes sense to me that price can easily reach down there without having to go past the average daily range"

rule: After a London reversal, price should respect 50% of the previous 7-hour candle (50% of the wick when the wick is large).
quote: "since this was a London reversal we want to see that 50% of the previous candle"

rule: Deviation from TTFM: enter when the unicorn forms inside C2, using it as confirmation that C2 will close valid; do not wait for the closure / candle 3.
quote: "I don't wait for a valid C2 closure and take the trade in in Candle 3 if the Unicorn forms in C 2"

rule: Stacked POIs (e.g. 50% wick, hourly opposing candles, hourly IFVG, earlier unicorn) add confluence.
quote: "we have have four different points of interest stacked on top of each other"

rule: If Asia makes the high and London does not continue lower, expect a New York reversal.
quote: "if Asia makes the high and London doesn't continue lower more than likely we're going to have a New York reversal"

rule: Favourite pattern: bullish, an hourly swing point resting just above a bullish hourly FVG; bearish, just below a bearish FVG; price sweeps into them and reacts.
quote: "if you're bullish you want to see an hourly swing Point sitting just above the fair value Gap"

rule: A T-spot only forms after C2 closes, so no T-spot entry is available while C2 is still open; the unicorn inside C2 is.
quote: "because the t-pot doesn't form until the C2 candle has closed um there was no actually entry off the t-spot"

rule: Target the "low hanging fruit" (e.g. Asia high, NY open, London low); as a funded trader take 2-2.5R and stop.
quote: "as a funded Trader all I'm trying to do is just grab my two to two and a half R and call it a day"

rule: A daily C2 T-spot is an open-ended POI: no other POI is needed, until an hourly closure past it.
quote: "I love the daily te- spot because it's an open-ended point of Interest"

rule: C2U is fractal: 15m C2 + 1m unicorn, 1h C2 + 5m unicorn, 4H C2 + 15m unicorn.
quote: "you would pair a 15minute C2 with a 1 minute unicorn a 1H hour C2 with a 5 minute unicorn"

rule: In the London session this model will mostly trade the reversal.
quote: "if you do want to trade this model in London more than likely you will be trading the reversal"

rule: 4H variant: the 6 a.m. 4H candle is C2 at a POI, a 15m unicorn forms inside it, and you trade the 10:00 open high (short) / open low (long).
quote: "I want the C2 candle to be the 6 a.m. candle what I'm trying to take advantage of is that 10:00 open"

rule: Some trades are losses or long "marathon" holds with drawdown and a second entry.
quote: "some of them are going to wind up being losses and some of them are going to wind up being Marathon trades"

rule: Each day is classified as either a reversal or a continuation.
quote: "This is based off the fact that I'm either going to be looking for a reversal or for a continuation."

rule: Reversals are always framed off the previous day's high or previous day's low.
quote: "If I'm looking for a reversal, I'm always going to frame that reversal off of previous day's high or previous day's low."

rule: Bearish reversal after a bullish close near the high: next day opens, trades into PDH, forms the reversal, target back into the range (EQ) or PDL.
quote: "I'd be looking for the next day to open, trade into previous day high, have a reversal formed"

rule: Bullish continuation: price opens, trades lower first, respects the previous day's EQ, then trades up and through PDH.
quote: "I'll look for price to open, trade lower first, respect the EQ of that previous day's range, and then trade up and through that previous day's high."

rule: A shallow wick at the reversal level supports expansion, so the reversal day itself can be traded; a large wick means wait for candle 3 (the following candle).
quote: "a shallow wick supports expansion lower. So, we can trade this lower in the reversal day."

rule: Over PDH/PDL, require a lower-timeframe CISD to confirm the daily wick before trading back into the range.
quote: "we're going to want to see a lower time frame change in the state of delivery to confirm the wick of this daily candle"

rule: CISD timeframe by session: hourly or 30m early in the day (Asia/London), 5m or 15m in New York (per page and 06:53-07:08; the 01:43 sentence is ambiguous).
quote: "Either a change in the state of delivery on the hourly time frame if earlier in the day or if into New York"

rule: In a continuation, a CISD intraday confirms the HTF wick, then trade the body of the HTF candle.
quote: "we have a change in the state of delivery, which confirms this higher time frame wick. And then we can trade the body"

rule: Mark only three things each day: previous day EQ, PDH and PDL (the relevant extreme for the bias).
quote: "we're just going to mark out the EQ as well as our previous day high and previous day low"

rule: "Respecting EQ" means no closures beyond EQ on the paired LTF (hourly for the daily); a close beyond is not fatal, just less probable.
quote: "I don't want to see a closure below that EQ level. Not that it can't reverse and expand, it's just less probable."

rule: Respecting EQ does not require touching it: the retracement extreme can form short of EQ at a POI.
quote: "price can form its high below that level. It doesn't need to go up and touch it."

rule: Do not guess which FVG below/above EQ will react; wait for a swing / new protected swing to form there, and drop FVGs price ignores.
quote: "Instead of trying to guess which one will have a reaction, I'm going to wait for a swing to form in that area"

rule: How far beyond the previous day's extreme a continuation runs depends on wick size: large wick -> little range beyond; small wick -> expansion.
quote: "With a large wick, I'm not expecting much of a range beyond this level. But with a small wick, we can get an expansion."

rule: Open-low first is bullish; open-high first is bearish.
quote: "When price opens and makes a low first, that is bullish. When price opens it and makes a high first that is bearish."

rule: A protected swing is only protected until price hits liquidity; a common pattern is take liquidity, sweep the protected swing, then the true move.
quote: "this swing is only protected until it hits liquidity"

rule: Do not pattern-trade the framework; align it with a higher-timeframe bias.
quote: "I'm not just going to pattern trade this. I want to actually align it with a bias."

rule: With a bullish HTF bias, a bearish CISD off PDH can be a retracement, not a reversal; wait for the lower wick and a bullish CISD to trade higher.
quote: "this can be still part of a retracement, not a full-on reversal"

rule: On an hourly candle-2 closure, enter on the open of candle 3, or drop to the 5m to trade a 5m continuation inside candle 3.
quote: "This is where I could take an entry on the open of candle 3 to trade it higher"

rule: The framework is fractal: on lower timeframes replace PDH with the previous candle's high (e.g. the 10 a.m. hourly high, executed on the 5m).
quote: "instead of previous day high, it's going to be a previous candle's high"

rule: Ideally the reversal candle's high forms early in the candle with a small wick, confirmed by a CISD, not by a mere close.
quote: "ideally, we want this candle's high to form early into the candle and have a small wick"

rule: He does not like framing reversals / candle 2s below the 4H; focus reversal candles on the daily or 4H.
quote: "I don't prefer to go below the 4hour time frame as it just becomes a bit more difficult"

rule: Timeframe pairs: daily with hourly, 4H with 15m.
quote: "with the 4hour, what do we pair it with? The 15-minut time frame."

rule: To trade away from a consolidation, require the consolidation's previous high (low) to be run first; consolidation is identified by the inability to close and form a protected swing.
quote: "We want to see the previous high ran out to then trade it lower."

rule: When trading a candle 2 he prefers SMT paired with it.
quote: "If I'm going to be trading a candle too, I do prefer to have SMT paired with it."

rule: In candle 3 continuation, the POI in the T-spot is an FVG or a high to be taken out.
quote: "A fair value gap or a high to be taken out."

rule: During Asia / early in the day he prefers executing on the higher timeframe rather than dropping to the lower timeframes.
quote: "since this is during Asia session or early onto the day, this is when I prefer not to go down to the lower time frames"

rule: Fib settings: only 0.5 (0 and 1 usually removed).
quote: "I'm going to use a simple Fibonacci with a 0.5 and a 1 marked out and generally I remove the zero and one and just have the 0.5"

rule: Measure EQ from wick high to wick low, never bodies (bodies are for CISD and order blocks).
quote: "I'm always going to measure the candles from Wick High to Wick low and then Mark out the equilibrium"

rule: In an expansion phase price rarely retraces into discount or premium, which is why he uses EQ opposite to ICT.
quote: "if price is in an expansion phase which is the phase that I trade price rarely goes in retraces to a discount or to a premium"

rule: In expansions, the upper half of the range must be respected to trade higher and the lower half to trade lower.
quote: "I'm looking for the upper half to respect for price to trade higher and the lower half to respect for price to trade lower"

rule: If the expected half is not respected, flip bias and anticipate the other side of the range being taken.
quote: "if these do not respect I then can flip my bias and anticipate the low of the range being taken"

rule: Match PD arrays inside the respected half, e.g. an FVG in the upper half above a protected low.
quote: "I have a fair value Gap in the upper half of this range above the protected low"

rule: Confirm the reaction at the PD array with a CISD before expecting continuation.
quote: "that is where we get a reaction a change in the state of delivery and then we continue to expand"

rule: A protected low forms when price reaches into an FVG and closes through the down-close candles.
quote: "our protected low right here as this has wretch [reached] into a fair value Gap Clos through the down Clos candles"

rule: If an FVG in the respected half is not respected, ignore it and look to the next PD array (e.g. opposing candles).
quote: "is this fair value Gap respected no it is not so I pretty much ignore it"

rule: For indices he generally anticipates the expansion in the New York session.
quote: "the New York session where I generally anticipate expansion for the indices"

rule: Each day, focus on finding the invalidation and the PD arrays expected to support in the respected half.
quote: "going into each day I mainly focused on finding an invalidation for that day and the PD arrays that I anticipate to support"

rule: Daily if-then: if EQ is respected, trade through previous day low (bearish case); if not, trade to the failure swings on the high.
quote: "if the EQ is respected then we can trade lower through previous day low"

rule: An aggressive intraday move does not change the plan while the daily EQ holds.
quote: "since we are respecting the equilibrium of this daily candle I can then expect these lows to get taken"

rule: When there is no PD array in the respected half, allow price slightly past EQ into the hourly structure (e.g. FVG).
quote: "this is where I will allow it to trade a little bit higher than I normally would because of the structure on the hourly time frame"

rule: If price gaps and has already expanded, wait for the next daily closure.
quote: "my whole thought process is wait for the next daily closure as this range has already expanded"

rule: When unsure whether a low will be swept or respected, let the daily profile confirm/invalidate; then look for CISD or order block formation.
quote: "I just let the daily profile confirm or invalidate my thought process"

rule: Without a close through the down-close candles that made the low, there is no bullish setup.
quote: "without that confirmation there is no bullish setup there"

rule: Taking out a previous high already can set up a deeper retracement.
quote: "we have already taken out this previous High here which can set up a deeper retracement"

rule: For a candle with a very large wick, use 0.5 of the wick instead of the whole candle.
quote: "it doesn't really make sense to use the EQ of the whole candle"

rule: Positional entry: short at the opposing candle/order block at EQ, stop over the protected high, target other side of range or 2R.
quote: "that is where I could take a short with my stop over this high and then looking for the other side of the range or two R"

rule: Do not trust an order block that sits inside a consolidation; use the range high as the POI and look for a sweep or SMT.
quote: "I don't trust this as an order block because it is just in a consolidation"

rule: During expansion, up-close candles and EQ are respected; no deep retracements into premium to sell.
quote: "we're not going to get those deep retracements into premium to look to sell"

rule: Trading lower first usually means price returns to at least the opening price.
quote: "we trade lower first which usually means we're going to return to the opening price at least"

rule: After about 3 days/candles of expansion into lows/liquidity, avoid trading and wait for new closures (new phase likely).
quote: "at this point we have 3 days of expansion into lows this is where I'm going to avoid"

rule: A close above 0.5 of a candle's range is generally viewed as a reversal.
quote: "we're closing above 0.5 of this candle's range which is generally when I view it as a reversal"

rule: The concept is fractal; he prefers daily, 4H and hourly candles because 5m is too much to analyse.
quote: "I prefer the daily 4H hour hourly candles because that just gives me enough time to analyze it"

rule: Only pick between EURUSD and GBPUSD when the dollar is not consolidating (it has a directional bias).
quote: "So if the dollar is not consolidating, that is when we're going to look to trade euro or GBP."

rule: Read EURGBP as a fraction: bullish trend = EUR stronger, GBP weaker.
quote: "if that is in a bullish trend, what does that tell me? Well, if you remember back to our fractions video, it means that the euro is stronger and the GBP is weaker."

rule: With EURGBP bullish: long EURUSD if longing (dollar bearish); short GBPUSD if shorting (dollar bullish).
quote: "So, if I'm going to want to long something, then I want to long EuroUSD since it is stronger. And I'd want to short GBPUSD since it is weaker."

rule: With EURGBP bearish (EUR weaker, GBP stronger): dollar bearish -> long GBPUSD; dollar bullish -> short EURUSD.
quote: "Well, that means euro is weaker and GBP is stronger. So, if the dollar is bearish, I want to then long the stronger asset."

rule: Pair the strong currency against the weak currency to get the cleanest trend.
quote: "pairing a strong currency with a weak currency gives you a nice bullish trend."

rule: Equivalent wording: a bearish EURGBP move means EUR is the more bearish; a bullish EURGBP move means GBP is the more bearish.
quote: "if we have a bearish move on EuroGBP, it means Euro is more bearish."

rule: Normally read EURGBP direction from daily closures; drop to the hourly (FVG, protected swing, hourly CISD) when the daily is ambiguous.
quote: "Generally, we can just look at the daily closures, but it's not always so perfect."

rule: On the chosen pair, if there are failure swings at the entry side, wait for them to be taken before entering.
quote: "we would want to wait for those failure swings to be taken out before we could look to get on side with a trade"

rule: A daily candle-2 closure out of an FVG that also creates a protected swing is the ideal (strongly directional) EURGBP signal.
quote: "We have a candle 2 closure out of a fair value gap and it's also an ideal candle 2 closure because it's creating a protected swing at the same time."

rule: Confluence: compare EURUSD and GBPUSD daily closures and structure; the one closing through its series of candles is the weaker / stronger one.
quote: "Comparing Euro and GBP, you can just look at the candle closures as well as the structure."

rule: If the traded pair is in a hourly consolidation but the dollar ran its consolidation extreme, use that SMT on the weaker asset and require a continuation through the level.
quote: "So we can then use that SMT on the weaker asset and we can look to trade away from this as long as we get a continuation through this area."

rule: Relative strength picks the asset; entries come from phases of price / the fractal model.
quote: "Now this is where you can blend in the phases of price the fractal model to get on side with this move."

rule: An engulfing EURGBP daily candle that took out a high still counts as bullish unless the hourly shows a reversal off that high.
quote: "And yes, it did take out this high, but it is engulfing."

rule: Choosing the wrong asset can make a correct idea fail or miss the expansion.
quote: "You could be completely right on a trade idea, but if you trade the wrong asset, you're going to be caught off sides or not catching an expansion."

rule: A bearish EURGBP candle is expected to continue while price respects 0.5 of its range.
quote: "we can anticipate this to continue lower as long as it remains in respect to 0.5 of this range."

rule: Verify with individual daily closes: the pair with the bearish close (EURUSD) is the short; the other closed bullish.
quote: "You can see on EuroUSD, we get a nice bearish closure, while GBPUSD, we don't get that bearish closure."

rule: On the lower timeframe, expect the daily wick to form at a sweep of the consolidation high, then a continuation lower.
quote: "this is where we'd want to see that wick of the daily candle form if it's going to form."

rule: Intraday the weaker pair breaks its low earlier (EUR at 8:00 vs GBP at 9:00) and stays farther from its prior high.
quote: "you can see at 8:00 a.m. we run out this low. Well, we're not running out this low till 9:00 a.m."

rule: First mark HTF (here 15m) points of interest: lows, highs, imbalances.
quote: "the first thing we're going to do is mark out our point of interest on our higher timeframe"

rule: When the context is unconvincing (aggressive up met by aggressive down at the low of the range), wait for a Judas swing before shorting.
quote: "I'd want to see some sort of Judas swing up before going short"

rule: Bias = waiting for POIs to be reached, then looking for lower-timeframe setups.
quote: "Our bias is waiting for areas or points of interest and then look for lower time frame setups."

rule: At a POI, drop to a lower timeframe (e.g. 1m); no structure break and no closes through = no short.
quote: "We never really broke structure in order to get short."

rule: A move down that is immediately reversed more aggressively upward is not a setup.
quote: "it's immediately back up and way more aggressive to the upside"

rule: Do not enter automatically at the POI; wait for an LTF setup to reduce risk because price could go higher.
quote: "Yes, it could go higher, and that's why we don't automatically enter here."

rule: The LTF setup needs displacement with big fair value gaps; a tiny FVG on a weak range is optional at best.
quote: "We want to see displacement down, right? Big fair value gaps."

rule: Entry on the FVG or the order block; risk on the high; first targets internal range liquidity / OTE of the leg, larger targets the lows or equal lows.
quote: "Put your risk on this high and then your immediate target would either be internal range liquidity, OTE of this area."

rule: Do not chase a missed entry; wait for the next FVG retrace and refine it to the order block (opening of the up-close series before the drop).
quote: "if you miss this entry and you're like, oh, I want to chase, why chase? We have another fair value gap in here."

rule: Confirm the refined entry sits in the OTE of the leg.
quote: "if you double check with your OTE you can see that's right in an OTE as well"

rule: On the sell side of the curve, premium PD arrays (bearish order blocks) should resist price; each is another add opportunity.
quote: "when we are on the sell side of the curve here, you will want, you want the premium PD arrays, right, to resist price"

rule: Keep selling until there is an aggressive move up; a break of a high without displacement does not end the downtrend.
quote: "No displacement, and it immediately sells back off."

rule: While the trend holds, look for secondary/later entries (e.g. lunchtime: small high raided, aggressive down, FVG sell).
quote: "You can look for secondary entries or later entries."

rule: Partials optional (e.g. take 2R off).
quote: "obviously you can take partials or trade how you want if you just want to take off the 2R"

rule: Price cannot reverse without forming a swing point (swing low for bearish→bullish, swing high for bullish→bearish).
quote: "the foundation of the fractal model is based off the idea that price cannot reverse without a swing point."

rule: Candle 2 is always the swing high/low; candle 1 is before it, candle 3 and 4 follow; candle 4 is always a continuation if the trend is correct.
quote: "Candle 2 will always be the swing low or swing high."

rule: Without a daily bias, do not drop to the hourly timeframe.
quote: "If I do not have a daily bias I do not drop down to the hourly time frame."

rule: Daily close below the previous day low → expect continuation lower; failure to close below it → expect reversal and bullish; mirror for previous day high.
quote: "if price closes below its previous day low, I'm expecting a continuation lower."

rule: Ideally find a daily closure where price reverses (swing point) and trade the continuation that follows.
quote: "I want to find a closure where price reverses and look to trade the continuation following."

rule: On the hourly, confirm a CISD at the daily candle 2 in the direction of the swing (bullish swing → bullish CISD).
quote: "go to that candle 2 or the swing point on the daily and make sure we have a change in the state of delivery there."

rule: Entries require both the daily closure and the hourly CISD.
quote: "Once I have both the closure and the change in the state of delivery, then I can look for entries."

rule: Entries should occur in the upper or lower half of the previous day's range (discount for longs, premium for shorts) and at a POI where the next day forms its wick.
quote: "I want to see them in the upper half or lower half of the previous day's range and then at a point of interest."

rule: At the POI, wait for an hourly candle closure that runs beyond the previous candle and closes back in (reversal).
quote: "once I've identified a point of interest, I'm going to wait for a candle closure similar to what we did on the daily chart."

rule: Then on the 5m, a CISD confirms the hourly reversal; trade continuations in hourly candle 3.
quote: "Look for a change in the state of delivery to confirm that reversal."

rule: When the hourly closes through the POI against bias, either invalidate the bias or keep it and lower the target (large wick) instead of expecting expansion toward the daily open.
quote: "I can either invalidate my bias and not continue to look short or I can see that we're making quite a large wick"

rule: Ideal candle 3 for a short: opens, makes a high first, then trades lower (inverse for longs); trading the wrong side first is a warning.
quote: "it's most ideal to have it open, make a high, get inside and trade it lower."

rule: In a consolidation with bullish bias, want the consolidation lows run, then a bullish candle closure, then the LTF entry.
quote: "We want to see lows ran out in the consolidation to trade it higher."

rule: Expansion met with expansion is a reversal.
quote: "So expansion met with expansion is a reversal."

rule: No 5m entry until the 5m closes over the series of opposite-close candles (CISD); part of the checklist.
quote: "I have to wait for that to occur before I can take an entry. That's part of my checklist."

rule: Stop on the protected low (e.g. the low out of a fair value gap); target 2R or the -1 standard deviation of the manipulation leg.
quote: "Or I can look for those standard deviations, right? Which is a negative one standard deviation from this manipulation leg."

rule: A sweep that closes back inside but as a bearish candle is not a bullish candle closure; wait for displacement up or another sweep.
quote: "Yes, it closed back inside its previous range, but this is a bearish candle."

rule: Do not trust LTF lows that did not reach a POI; wait for more confirmation or for a sweep then a continuation entry.
quote: "Do I trust any of these lows? No. Because none of them reach into a point of interest."

rule: Best R:R comes from a lower-timeframe entry with a higher-timeframe target (e.g. hourly / previous day high instead of 5m highs: 5.63R vs 2R).
quote: "the best way to get high risk-to-reward trades is to take a lower time frame entry and just use a higher time frame target."

rule: Even a few daily candles (sweep and close back in, engulfing) give enough context; don't overthink the daily chart.
quote: "a lot of people overthink the daily chart."

rule: After the first target (previous day low) is taken, a reversal would show as displacement back into the range (ignore if against bias); a shallow retrace into an FVG then continuation is tradable.
quote: "I want to see does price displace back into the range, right?"

rule: Stop can sit above the LTF high if price should not trade above 50% of the opposing candles, or allow extra room for a sweep.
quote: "I don't want to see price trade above 50% of these opposing candles. That's why I can trust this high."

rule: An hourly candle that closes below its previous allows the next candle to expand as well.
quote: "it closed below the previous which allows this next candle to expand as well."

rule: Minimum target 2R; with 2R, a win rate over about 34% is breakeven or profitable.
quote: "For my system, I'm looking for a minimum of 2R"

rule: Consolidation can only be followed by expansion; never treat a consolidation as the start of a reversal or a retracement.
quote: "Price never goes from a consolidation to a reversal. And price never goes from a consolidation to retracement."

rule: Every phase of price begins and ends with an expansion; expansion can be followed by retracement, reversal or consolidation.
quote: "Every phase starts and ends with expansion. So this is very important to know"

rule: Continuation signature: expansion then consolidation, or expansion then retracement, means price must expand again in the same direction.
quote: "So if price expands, consolidates, then we must expand again"

rule: To trade out of a consolidation without a low being manipulated, require a failed manipulation of the consolidation high: price engages the high, prints opposing candles and closes back through it.
quote: "we have to fail to manipulate the consolidation high which is simply when price engages the high creates opposing candles and closes back through it"

rule: The higher-timeframe signature of consolidation is an inside bar; leave it ideally by manipulating the consolidation low (bullish) then expanding.
quote: "higher time frame signature for consolidation? It's an inside bar."

rule: Expect a new phase (reversal, consolidation or retracement) after three consecutive expansion candles or one large expansion candle into an objective, on any timeframe.
quote: "we can also anticipate a new phase of price after 3 days of expansion or even after one day of a large expansion into an objective"

rule: Manipulation (a swept high/low or protected swing) is the trigger for expansion; when price retraces into an internal range, wait for manipulation before trading away.
quote: "So manipulation is like the trigger for expansion essentially"

rule: Only trade expansion phases; never trade consolidation or retracement phases.
quote: "We don't want to trade consolidation. We don't want to trade retracement. We always want to be trading expansion"

rule: Always pair a manipulation (and any key level) with an SMT on a correlated asset.
quote: "And we're always pairing a manipulation with an SMT"

rule: Do not trade away from failure swings (stacked, near-equal prior highs/lows left by a retracement); they are targets, not reversal points.
quote: none

rule: Reversal signature = expansion into a level and expansion away (V-shape), confirmed by a CISD (IFVG also acceptable).
quote: "Now the way we confirm it is with a CSD. That's confirms the reversal."

rule: If price consolidates at the intended reversal level instead of reversing, use the consolidation high/low as the new reversal point (AMD reversal).
quote: "We're going to revert to the consolidation high as the reversal point. So this would be AMD reversal"

rule: Use FVGs and order blocks mainly after a manipulation; expect them to support expansion away from it.
quote: "So really the best way in my opinion to use fair value gaps or order blocks is after manipulation"

rule: C2 closure: candle 2 that cannot displace through the previous candle's low signals reversal and candle 3 expansion.
quote: "candle 2 can't displace through the previous candle's low, right? This gives us insight that this is a reversal and candle 3 will expand away"

rule: A swing formation or strong close in candle 3 lets you expect candle 4 expansion.
quote: "once you have a swing formation or a strong close in candle 3, we can expect a candle 4 expansion"

rule: Guest variant: a visible HTF C2 closure is not required if C2 shows a lower-timeframe reversal or candle 3 confirms it with a CISD; he uses this only on 1D and 4H.
quote: "one thing about my model is I do not require um a candle 2 closure"

rule: Guest variant: if candle 1 hits the key level but closes as an expansion candle, treat candle 1's low as the reversal point and trade the next candle if it has a small wick.
quote: "if candle one hits a key level but doesn't reverse that I can revert to candle one's low to print that reversal"

rule: EQ filter: after a C2 closure or long reversing wick, the next candle should form its low in the upper half (above 50%) of that candle/wick range; breaking EQ means a large wick that does not support expansion.
quote: "We want the low to form in the upper half of this candle's range"

rule: A bullish daily candle ideally opens low first, forms its small wick early (for indices, before the drivers) and closes near its high; bearish is the mirror.
quote: "a bullish candle ideally opens low first creating a small wick that supports expansion"

rule: Do not trade a low or high of day that forms after about 10:30 (NY).
quote: "I will say I will not trade a low of day or high of day if it's formed after um probably around 10:30"

rule: If the day forms a large opposing wick (reversal candle), do not expect it to expand past the open; cut targets to the daily range, i.e. current-day session highs/lows.
quote: "we simply just adjust our targets because if we have this large wick then we know it can't it's not likely to splice past the opening price"

rule: Futures traders watch the 4H candles opening at 2 AM, 6 AM and 10 AM (NY); forex the 1 AM / 5 AM / 9 AM candles (slide).
quote: "future traders we want to be paying attention to the 2 a.m. candle, the 6 a.m. candle, and the 10 a.m. candle"

rule: If-then chain: Asia consolidates/retraces -> London (2 AM) manipulates; 2 AM manipulation -> 6 AM continuation; 6 AM manipulation -> 10 AM continuation; 10 AM manipulation -> 14:00 continuation.
quote: none

rule: If the 4H candle you are inside does not support expansion (large wick), wait for the next 4H candle open.
quote: "If the 4hour candle doesn't support expansion that you're trading within, then you simply wait for a new candle open"

rule: Driver pairing: a reversal before a driver (8:30 news, 9:30 open) means the driver continues it; no reversal before the driver means the driver should make the reversal at a key level.
quote: "If a reversal is put in prior to a driver, then the driver should continue"

rule: If the driver fails to reverse from the key level, the daily profile is invalidated (no later random time is expected to reverse).
quote: "If the driver fails to reverse from that key level, then it is an invalidation to the daily range or daily profile"

rule: An 8:30 red-folder manipulation implies a 9:30 or 10:00 continuation; a 9:30 manipulation implies a 10 AM continuation (9:30 driver applies to indices only).
quote: "if we have an 8:30 red folder manipulation then we can anticipate a 9:30 or 10:00 continuation"

rule: Reversal (large-wick) candles are tradable only on the daily; never trade a 4H reversal candle, only 4H reversal-into-expansion candles with small wicks.
quote: "we don't trade reversal candles on the 4hour chart"

rule: A 6 AM low of day is tradable only if the 6 AM 4H candle is a reversal-into-expansion candle; otherwise trade the 10 AM continuation.
quote: "just because 6 a.m. forms the low of the day doesn't mean we can trade it always"

rule: Prefer the 6 AM NY reversal over a 10 AM reversal because it can be paired with a driver; 10 AM reversal only with 10 AM news.
quote: "ideally it's the 6 a.m. New York reversal because you can pair a reversal with a driver"

rule: Model goal: align three expansion candles (daily, 4H, then 1H/30m/15m) away from the same key level toward the same draw on liquidity.
quote: "So, the whole goal of my model is to align expansion candles"

rule: A divergence is a fake SMT when the strongest asset fails to reverse; in a true SMT both assets expand away, and the lagging asset will catch up and take the level.
quote: "in a true SMT or reversal, both assets expand away"

rule: Expect a "strength switch" at most SMTs: the weaker asset becomes momentarily stronger so it can catch up; assets constantly switch strength to stay correlated.
quote: "So assets constantly are switching strength to become correlated"

rule: Not every SMT, key level or C2 closure is a trade; taking them all is pattern trading. Inside C2, require the lower-timeframe reversal signature.
quote: "SMTs are not SMTs are are to be traded. Not all key levels are to be traded. Not all C2 closures to be traded. That would be pattern trading."

rule: Do not take a CISD entry inside a 4H candle that does not support expansion; wait for the next 4H candle (example: 6 AM large wick -> wait for 10 AM).
quote: "Can we tra can we trade the CSD? The answer is no, right? Because this candle doesn't support expansion."

rule: A failure swing is a swing high followed by a lower high (or low with a higher low) before reversing, without sweeping the first.
quote: "what a failure swing is, is when we have a swing high, and then we make a lower high relative to that before reversing."

rule: Low resistance liquidity is a failure swing.
quote: "low resistance liquidity is just a failure swing."

rule: High resistance liquidity: liquidity is swept first (higher high / lower low) before the reversal.
quote: "It is where we first sweep that liquidity before the reversal."

rule: Target low resistance liquidity; keep high resistance liquidity behind the stop.
quote: "I want to be targeting low resistance liquidity and having high resistance liquidity for my stop loss or on my side of the curve."

rule: After a sweep (HRL) and a market structure shift / CISD, enter on the FVG or order block toward the LRL.
quote: "here we get the market structure shift or the change in the state of delivery. Now here I could look for an entry on the fair value gap or the order block."

rule: Equal / stacked highs and higher-timeframe failure swings are the first thing to spot as the draw.
quote: "the first thing that stands out are all these highs resting above here."

rule: For a change in state of delivery after taking equal lows, price should go from that low to take the failure swings.
quote: "if we're going to change the state of delivery, I'd like to see price go from this low to take out these failure swings."

rule: Previous days' lows that were never taken (failure swings on a lower timeframe) are LRL.
quote: "we have all these lows or previous days lows, which have not been taken out."

rule: Map failure swings and HRL on the daily to add to bias.
quote: "a lot of times what I like to do on the daily chart is just see where do we have failure swings and where do we have high resistance liquidity"

rule: A daily sweep becomes HRL once the next day closes back inside the range.
quote: "now we get the sweep and the closure back inside the range. So here is our high resistance liquidity."

rule: HRL on the lows plus failure swings on the highs supports long setups (and vice versa).
quote: "if I have high resistance liquidity on the lows and failure swings on the highs, I can use this to add to my bias for long setups."

rule: After a high is taken with failure swings on the low, ideally the high is not retaken before the low runs.
quote: "So ideally, this high does not get taken before running this low."

rule: To target a high cluster, first want a sweep (HRL) of a low; if it is the previous day low, expect it to hold.
quote: "if we're going to be targeting this high, I want to see a sweep or high resistance liquidity."

rule: A daily candle that takes PDL and closes above 50% of its wick -> next day higher toward the lined-up highs / FVG.
quote: "And where does it close? Above 50% of this wick."

rule: Use SMT to pick the weaker index for the trade (ES failed to make the high NQ made).
quote: "since ES formed an SMT here and is weaker, we're going to hop into that chart"

rule: An order block forms when price reaches an important level and then closes beyond the candle(s).
quote: "it reached into an important level, then price closed above, creating an order block."

rule: LRL resting just above an order block is likely run into the order block; its mean threshold gives the reaction.
quote: "We run all these low resistance lows into the order block. You can see the mean threshold of this creates a reaction."

rule: After sweeping lows, stacked lower highs become the target.
quote: "we have a series of lower highs all stacked up. We just swept out all these lows. Where is price likely to go?"

rule: A close over a series of down-close candles validates them as an order block.
quote: "we get a closure over this series of downclosed candles here, validating it as an order block."

rule: If an order block is not in discount, use its mean threshold or wait for a second entry.
quote: "it doesn't really make sense to look for an entry off this order block here. So then I will use the mean threshold."

rule: Entry at the order block, stop on the HRL, take profit at the highs (failure swings).
quote: "I'd look to take my entry right here, my stop on the high resistance liquidity, and then looking to take off at the highs."

rule: Do not trust a low for invalidation unless price closed over its level or it was swept (HRL).
quote: "price never came and closed over this level, right? So I'm not using that as a valid low for invalidation."

rule: Mean thresholds of order blocks / propulsion blocks should be respected in a valid trend.
quote: "Here we close over, creating this propulsion block."

rule: Higher timeframes are relative to your entry timeframe; he enters on 1m/15s and uses 15m, 1h and 4H for POIs.
quote: "I use the one minute and 15 second for my entries and I'll watch the 15 minute, hour and four hour as my points of interest."

rule: POIs to watch: highs and lows (equal, session, daily), FVGs, order blocks, an FVG fill.
quote: "So it can be equal highs and lows, session highs and lows, daily highs and lows, fair value gaps, order blocks, or when a fair value gap fills."

rule: Also OTE of a range and internal range liquidity (often together with OTE).
quote: "Internal range liquidity of a range, which can also go along with OTE."

rule: Only go to the lower timeframe for an entry model when at a POI; do not search all the time.
quote: "when you should go down to a lower timeframe to search for an entry model, because you don't want to just be searching all the time."

rule: For highs and lows, track which have been taken and which are likely to be taken.
quote: "what you want to look for here are which highs have been taken and which highs are likely to be taken."

rule: Lows only slightly moved over without a convincing move are a magnet; after they are taken, look for a long toward equal highs.
quote: "So these lows are a target or essentially a magnet for price. So price should go drop below those lows."

rule: Watch the lower timeframe for entries after highs and lows are run.
quote: "But just watch lower timeframes on here and you can possibly get entries after you run highs and lows."

rule: After a high is broken, the question of continuation vs reversal is where to look at FVGs.
quote: "So right here, we break through a high. Are we going to continue higher or drop back down? And that is where you look for fair value gaps."

rule: Retracement targets: an OTE of the current range or where the FVG fills (which may be an OB).
quote: "either an OTE of this range currently, right? So down into this OTE, or where this fair value gap fills, right? Which is also this order block"

rule: In a bearish trend a long at a POI is a retracement; target the OTE of the range, expect lower eventually.
quote: "But you have to realize that we're in a bearish trend here, so it's likely that we couldn't displace over this high."

rule: A reach into the premium of a down displacement leg, short of the OTE, can still be the turn.
quote: "We don't quite get to an OTE, but if you can see. We do reach into a premium of this displacement leg down."

rule: After an aggressive move down and a retrace into premium, the obvious target is the lows.
quote: "Aggressive move down, reaches back up into a premium, you're likely to see these lows, right?"

rule: After a low is run, watch the lower timeframe for an entry model the other way.
quote: "Now what happens after you run a low? You can be watching right action on a lower timeframe to see if there's some sort of entry model in the other direction"

rule: Once the displacement high is in, look for FVGs in a discount or OTE: rinse and repeat.
quote: "Just rinsing and repeating, fair value gaps and a discount or OTE."

rule: After an aggressive move expect a relief bounce; a counter-trend scalp needs a lower timeframe model.
quote: "I would expect some sort of Relief bounce here, back up into this area, right? So you could be watching lower timeframe in here for a possible counter trend scalp"

rule: Never just enter at a POI; get a confirmed entry.
quote: "You don't just enter, you get a confirmed entry."

rule: After a low is taken and longs are considered, target internal range liquidity first, before the highs.
quote: "Where would you first want to target? Internal range liquidity before highs, right?"

rule: Using bodies instead of wicks for the OTE / OB moves the level slightly.
quote: "if you use the bodies, it's going to be a little bit higher up, but you get the point."

rule: After a high runs, expect a retrace to around an OTE (BPR / FVGs) before continuing.
quote: "After we run this high, what would I expect price to do? Retrace back to somewhat of an OTE before continuing higher"

rule: A true trend is the condition where candles on all timeframes are aligned in the same direction.
quote: "when a true trend occurs, all candles are aligned in the same direction"

rule: A candle supports expansion when it has a small wick and a large body; a large wick / large opposing run means it does not.
quote: "Candles that support expansion will have a small wick and a large body."

rule: Bullish expansion: price opens, forms a small wick early in the candle, then trends higher for the rest of the candle; a long early opposing run makes it return toward its open or current high instead.
quote: none

rule: Require at least two aligned expansion candles (e.g. daily + 4H) before trading a 15m setup.
quote: "I generally prefer to have at a minimum two expansion candles aligned"

rule: For a 5m/3m entry, prefer three aligned timeframes: daily, 4H and 1H (or 30m).
quote: none

rule: Do not trade inside a 4H candle 2 with a large wick; let C2 close and trade candle 3 once it forms its small wick (protected swing).
quote: "Letting this candle 2 close, then I can look to trade the expansion in candle three once it forms a small wick."

rule: The wick of the higher-timeframe candle is formed by a protected swing on the lower timeframe; after it forms, trend can occur.
quote: none

rule: Easiest scenario: align a higher-timeframe bias with a candle 3 and take a continuation entry; reversals can be aligned the same way but are harder to anticipate.
quote: none

rule: If the 4H candle opens and trades against the bias first (large opposing run), wait for the next 4H open before getting on side.
quote: none

rule: Simplest method: trade candle 3 on multiple timeframes (daily C3, 4H C3) with a continuation order block inside them.
quote: "The most simple way will be to trade a candle 3 on multiple time frames."

rule: A 4H C2 closure (V-shaped reversal) whose candle has a large wick is not traded in the reversal candle; wait for the next candle.
quote: none

rule: Bearish daily small wick: price opens, makes no relevant low, makes a high and a CISD, so the day can trend lower.
quote: none

rule: Entry after price sweeps a high into an FVG (POI) and forms a continuation: stop above the protected swing, target 2R.
quote: none

rule: Expansion candles are expected to close near their extreme; a pullback inside them is a retracement, not a reversal.
quote: none

rule: Find where higher-timeframe candles all support expansion in one direction, then align structure (protected swings, continuation order blocks) with it.
quote: "where higher time frame candles all support expansion in the same direction. Then I'm going to align structure with that"

rule: On the 5m, skip an hourly reversal candle; the next hourly candle (C3) supports expansion. Daily C3 + 4H C3 + 1H C3 is a trend by definition.
quote: "Here we have a daily candle 3, a 4hour candle 3, and an hourly candle 3."

rule: If the daily has a large opposing run, do not expect daily expansion; target the daily open or the intraday highs.
quote: none

rule: When neither 4H nor 1H supports expansion, wait for the new 4H and 1H candles at 10 AM instead of picking the bottom.
quote: none

rule: An hourly C2 closure paired with a CISD gives the long; candle 3s across timeframes carry it.
quote: none

rule: If the trading candle's profile opposes the daily (open-high-low instead of the bullish open-low-high-close), take more conservative targets.
quote: "this one is opposing the daily candle as it is not open low, high close, it's open, high, low. So we do want to take more conservative targets"

rule: A good lower-timeframe structure that is not aligned with the higher-timeframe trend is unlikely to work.
quote: "you can have a great lower time frame structure, but if it's not aligned with the higher time frame trend, it's unlikely to work out."

rule: FVG: three-candle pattern where the wicks of candle 1 and candle 3 do not overlap.
quote: "A fair value gap is a three candlestick pattern 1 2 3 in which the wick of candle one and the wick of candle three do not overlap"

rule: IFVG: an FVG that is not respected and is swiftly closed over; resistance becomes support and vice versa.
quote: "an inversion fair value gap is when this fair value gap is not respected and swiftly closed over"

rule: The common mistake is pattern trading sweep + inversion without HTF context or swing-point understanding.
quote: "they fail to look at the higher time frames. They do not understand swing points and they are simply trading a pattern"

rule: Trade inversions only in an HTF candle 2 that supports expansion (small wick) after sweeping candle 1's extreme.
quote: "you want to wait for a candle that supports expansion lower"

rule: Valid IFVG setup in the fractal model: sweep of candle 1's high or low, small wick, then the inversion.
quote: "I will be looking for a sweep of candle 1's high or low, a small wick, and then an inversion"

rule: Extra confluence: SMT between candle 1's and candle 2's highs (or lows).
quote: "look for an SMT between candle 1's high and candle 2's high"

rule: An inversion without a sweep of the previous HTF candle's extreme is not a reversal setup (just consolidation).
quote: "we want a sweep of this previous high in order to be looking for a short setup"

rule: A candle with no wick on the opposing side can serve as a draw on liquidity; wait for the next candle open.
quote: "So, this can be used as a drawn liquidity, but we would want to wait for a new candle open."

rule: An inversion plus CISD above the previous 4h high after a short-term high sweep, with failure swings below, is a high-context setup.
quote: "we have an inversion and a change in the state of delivery, which means it is valid to be looking for a move lower"

rule: When several FVGs sit in the leg, treat them as one big FVG; the inversion needs a close through the whole cluster.
quote: "I want to use all of those fair value gaps and treat it like one big fair value gap"

rule: No V-shaped reversal means consolidation; avoid it even if it might work, and wait for another run of the lows.
quote: "when we fail to have a nice V-shaped reversal, this is where I want to avoid price"

rule: In a bearish consolidation, wait for the consolidation lows to be taken before trading to the highs.
quote: "I want to wait for the consolidation lows to be taken out before I look to trade to the highs"

rule: If the HTF candle opened, traded the other way first and expanded (large opposing run), expect only a reversal candle back toward its open, not expansion.
quote: "if we are going to form a reversal, I'm not expecting it to be an expansion candle"

rule: With a large opposing run, wait for the next HTF candle open to enter (stop allowed into the FVG, target other side of range or 2R) or for a continuation.
quote: "when we have a large opposing run generally that expansion is going to wait for the next higher time frame candle"

rule: An inversion can be used in place of a CISD for continuation entries.
quote: "an inversion in place of a change in the state of delivery that is something you can do"

rule: After three days of expansion, do not trade the same direction; look for a reversal (off previous day high).
quote: "After 3 days of expansion, I don't want to trade in the same direction."

rule: Pair the 4h with the 15m (or 1h with 5m) and use LTF inversions inside that fractal model.
quote: "with the 4hour chart, we can go down to the 15-minute chart to look for our fractal model"

rule: A sell-off that is not V-shaped is hard to trust; wait for a new high / new candle 2 before using an inversion.
quote: "If this sells down, you want to see a consolidation or retracement. That's a V-shaped reversal."

rule: Using the series of FVGs (not just one) as the CISD level saved a loss when price failed to close through both.
quote: "that's why I would use the series of fair value gaps and not just one"

rule: One rejection at the inversion level is fine if price quickly closes back through; repeated failure and consolidation requires a new high first.
quote: "if it rejects it once, that's fine as long as we quickly close back below it"

rule: Stay in respect of roughly 50% of the HTF candle while seeking the inversion.
quote: "We're still in respect to around 50% of this higher time frame candle."

rule: Stop on the swing point / high, target 2R toward the low end of the range; be mindful of tight stops.
quote: "take an entry and put our stop on that swing point or on the high and then look for 2R"

rule: Summary: trade inversions in an HTF expansion candle with a small wick; with a large wick expansion usually happens in candle 3; want a V-shaped reversal and ideally SMT.
quote: "if you're looking to trade inversions, you want to be doing that in a higher time frame expansion candle"

rule: Define a consolidation by marking a high and a low; price stays inside without taking either for a period of time.
quote: "A consolidation is when price remains internal to a high and a low."

rule: Expect consolidation after a large range (expansion) or when price hits a higher timeframe level.
quote: "we can expect it after a large range or when price hits a higher time frame level"

rule: Do not trade inside the consolidation range; wait for price to manipulate (take out) one side.
quote: "I don't want to trade within this range because that is where I'm going to try to guess"

rule: Bullish: want the range low run, then trade higher (power of three: accumulation, manipulation, distribution); bearish is the mirror.
quote: "if I am bullish, ideally I want to see price run out the low, but then I can look to trade it higher"

rule: The only exception to needing a run of the range high/low is SMT: if the correlated asset runs it, treat it as run.
quote: "the only time we don't need price to run out the high or the low is if we have SMT"

rule: With SMT (e.g. ES runs the low, NQ does not), treat the NQ low as protected once price closes over.
quote: "I can treat this as a protected low once closed over because ES ran out the low"

rule: He participates in two consolidation types only: continuation and reversal.
quote: "there are two types of consolidations that I will look to participate in and that will be a continuation or a reversal"

rule: Continuation: with an open draw on liquidity and no HTF level hit, expect price to continue after the consolidation.
quote: "with an open drawn liquidity or an objective sitting above this I can anticipate price to continue"

rule: After the manipulation he often prefers waiting for the continuation: a closure through the level (CISD) rather than catching the low.
quote: "a lot of times I prefer to wait for a continuation because what if we don't form a low here and we just trade lower?"

rule: Reversal: if the consolidation sits at a HTF objective/level, wait for its highs (or lows) to be run, then a CISD, then trade the other way.
quote: "We have hit a higher time frame objective or higher time frame level in which I'm anticipating a reversal to form."

rule: The PD array paired with consolidation is discount/premium around the range equilibrium; a deviation from the range can be traded back to EQ.
quote: "if price deviates from this range, I can look to trade back into the equilibrium"

rule: An expansion that retraces into an FVG but fails to close over the level is unconfirmed and becomes a consolidation.
quote: "it would have closed over this level with a failure to do so. We are then consolidating."

rule: If price pokes outside the marked range but fails to trade out of it, readjust the range high/low; it is still consolidating.
quote: "Is price remaining internal to these? No. But it is failing to trade out of it, right? So, it is still consolidating."

rule: A protected swing forms on the closure through the series of down-close (up-close) candles that traded into the important level.
quote: "wait for that protected swing to form on this time frame which would be a closure through the series of down close candles"

rule: If there is no FVG or swept low as the important level, use 0.5 of the opposing candle as the level.
quote: "That is when I can use 0.5 of this opposing candle here."

rule: The trend occurs after the manipulation, so wait for it before participating.
quote: "Wait for that manipulation, then look to participate, right? Because that is when the trend is going to occur after that manipulation."

rule: If price disrespects the EQ of a CISD leg, that swing point is likely to fail and becomes the draw on liquidity.
quote: "if this EQ is going to fail, that means this swing point is going to fail, which can make it our draw on liquidity"

rule: Without a strong bias, do not enter at the swept low; wait for the closure through the down-close candles to confirm the low.
quote: "So I can then wait for a closure through the series of down close candles into this level, which then confirms the low"

rule: After a breakout close over range highs, want a retracement or continuation, not an aggressive move back into the range.
quote: "Do we want to see price aggressively move back into the range? No. Because then we're likely to trade lower."

rule: The fractal model does not try to catch the lows; it lets a low form and trades the continuation.
quote: "with my fractal model, I'm not looking to catch these lows in here, right? I'm waiting for the continuation entries."

rule: Core loop: consolidation, wait for the manipulation, trade the expansion.
quote: "consolidation, wait for the manipulation, trade the expansion"

rule: For a bullish reversal day, use previous day highs/lows as the levels price reverses from.
quote: "I'm going to be looking for relevant levels for price to reverse off of, which would be previous days highs and lows"

rule: A London reversal off PDL with a small wick allows anticipating a New York continuation.
quote: "if we have a London reversal, we could anticipate what? a New York continuation higher"

rule: When bearish after a daily sweep + CISD, he does not need to catch the session high; he prefers to trade the continuation.
quote: "Do I need to catch this high to trade it lower? No. Could I anticipate a reversal? Yes. But I prefer to trade continuations"

rule: Expansion = a one-sided trending move with very shallow moves against the trend.
quote: "expansion is when we have a one-sided trending move"

rule: Shallow counter-moves are the signature of expansion; do not expect a deep retrace into discount before continuation.
quote: "we have very shallow moves against the trend and that is the signature of expansion"

rule: Expect expansion after a consolidation or after a retracement.
quote: "I expect expansion to occur after a consolidation or after a retracement"

rule: Price cycles between large ranges and small ranges; use that to anticipate the next phase.
quote: "I'm expecting the market to cycle between large ranges and small ranges"

rule: In expansion, do not wait for price to return to discount to get long.
quote: "I'm not wanting to look for price to trade back into a discount to get long"

rule: In a bullish trend, down-close candles support price higher (up-close candles in a bearish trend).
quote: "if I'm in a bullish trend, down close candles to support price higher"

rule: Entry logic: price reaches into a PD array, closes over the down-close candles, creating a protected swing whose low should hold; trade higher off it.
quote: none

rule: For longs in expansion, look in the upper half of the higher-timeframe candle (per his EQ video).
quote: "I'm looking in the upper half of a higher time frame candle"

rule: Look for intraday expansion after the higher timeframe sets up a reversal (e.g. daily sweep + close back inside + CISD).
quote: "after we have a reversal on the daily chart, that's generally when I have expansion"

rule: If the trend is to continue, the latest protected swing low must not be taken; track each new protected swing as it forms.
quote: "if this trend is going to continue higher, I don't want to see this low taken"

rule: A protected swing only forms once price closes over the opposing candle(s); no close over = no new protected swing.
quote: none

rule: After about 3 days of expansion, expect a retracement, reversal or opposing move.
quote: "after we have 3 days of expansion, this is generally when it can set up some sort of retracement or reversal"

rule: A reversal after expansion is expected off previous day highs/lows; check whether price breaks out through the PDH or reverses.
quote: "it could occur off previous day highs"

rule: In a consolidation inside a trend, continuation = manipulation of the high (in a downtrend); reversal = manipulation of the low.
quote: "if we're going to continue this trend, we want to see a manipulation of the high"

rule: Avoid entering right after an expansion, because a new phase of price delivery often follows.
quote: "I don't really want to enter a trade right after an expansion because that's when we can get a new phase of price delivery"

rule: Three days of expansion into an objective: do not expect more expansion; let another day form and expect consolidation, retracement or reversal.
quote: "We have 3 days of expansion into an objective"

rule: In a consolidation, mark the range high and low and anticipate price trading to one of them for a setup.
quote: "what do we mark out in a consolidation? The high and the low of the range"

rule: He applies phases of price on the daily because that is how he pairs it with closures, then executes on the hourly.
quote: "I like to use it on the daily chart because that's how I pair it with closures"

rule: A London-session low confirmed by closing over the level sets up an anticipated New York continuation.
quote: "So a London reversal if we close over this level"

rule: With a bullish bias, do not look for longs in a consolidation until its low is swept.
quote: "if I have a bullish bias, we don't sweep out this low, there's no reason for me to be looking to get long"

rule: After expansions, anticipate a smaller range next (even after two large days).
quote: "after expansions, we can anticipate a smaller range"

rule: A reversal is expected where the PDH meets a FVG; confirm with an hourly CISD before trading lower.
quote: "If we are going to form a reversal, where are we going to form a reversal? On that previous day high in the fair value gap"

rule: Phases of price are fractal: 1D/1h is his main pair, but it works for 1h/5m or 1M/1D via time frame alignment.
quote: "you can also do this on the hourly and the 5-minut or the monthly and the daily time frame"

rule: A retracement is a slow, shallow move against the trend between two expansions (the opposite of an expansion).
quote: "We want to see a slow shallow move opposing the trend."

rule: A healthy retracement leaves failure swings on the opposite extreme (highs in a bull trend), which become the target once the retracement low forms.
quote: "that is a common signature that you want to see with a retracement is the formation of failure swings."

rule: Anticipate the retracement low (bull) / high (bear) inside a fair value gap left by the expansion.
quote: "So, I'm anticipating a low to form in a fair value gap."

rule: Entry option A: inside the FVG, take a candle-2 closure or a lower-timeframe fractal entry model.
quote: "You can one mark out a fair value gap and look for a candle closure or a lower time frame entry model within here."

rule: Entry option B: wait for a protected swing (close over the series of down-close candles) out of the FVG, then trade the continuation on the same timeframe.
quote: "Or I can let a protected swing form out of this area."

rule: After an expected expansion day, a fast move back against it is a reversal, not a retracement.
quote: "Do we want to see expansion back lower? No, that is a reversal."

rule: Wicks may dig deeper than the FVG; judge respect of the gap by candle bodies.
quote: "Yes, it digs a bit deeper, but you can see how the bodies respect."

rule: For a continuation, expect one of two phases: a consolidation whose low gets swept, or a slow shallow retracement.
quote: "Consolidation sweeps the low to trade higher or we're going to have a slow shallow move and then trade it higher."

rule: Judge retracement character by time vs range: in his example 9 hours of retracement covered the range of about 3 hours of expansion.
quote: "9 hours worth of candles took up the range of about three hours of expansion."

rule: Expansion = aggressive, fast, large range; retracement = slow, shallow, small range.
quote: "Expansion is aggressive, fast and large range. Retracement is slow and shallow in a small range."

rule: Phases of price are primarily read on daily and hourly, but are fractal and apply to lower timeframes.
quote: "I mainly focus on the daily and hourly for my phases of price, but it does also apply to the lower time frames."

rule: If highs at the expected wick zone are failure swings, require them to be run out before shorting; no run, no short.
quote: "Now for me, I view all these highs as failure swings. So I would want those ran out before looking for a short."

rule: After aggressive expansion, expect very shallow retracements or none at all (so a deep-FVG entry may never come).
quote: "we have aggressive expansion, which we're going to either get very shallow retracements or no retracements at all."

rule: Once a close beyond the opposing candles forms a protected swing, its violation ends the trend.
quote: "Protected swing now. So now if this gets violated, this trend is over."

rule: Retracements should resolve quickly; if price starts a retracement but fails to confirm (no close through) and hangs around, reclassify it as a consolidation.
quote: "another thing you want to see with retracements is you want to see them be quick."

rule: A shallow tap of an FVG is not enough for him; he prefers a consolidation low swept to get "a wick I trust".
quote: "We do have a shallow reach into it. I personally don't really trust that. I'd like to see a consolidation low swept out."

rule: Do not buy the FVG touch itself; wait for a close over the down-close candle, then enter on the close or the retest.
quote: "I'm not trying to long this right away. I want to wait for what? A closure over the down close candle."

rule: When the entry candle has no wick, put the stop on the wick of the swing rather than on the body; target 2R toward failure swings on the left.
quote: "So, at least on the the wick or a little bit higher. And then look for 2, right?"

rule: Anticipating a move is not enough; without the required sweep / FVG retracement you skip it, even if it runs.
quote: "So you could miss this entire move even though you anticipated it."

rule: The monthly high in his example formed via a retracement into a prior FVG followed by a close back below.
quote: "You can see how that monthly high is formed by a retracement into a fair value gap."

rule: If the correlated index already swept the consolidation low, the SMT substitutes for the sweep and longs are valid.
quote: "ES has taken out that low. So, we can consider that an SMT and then it is valid to look for long setups."

rule: Trail the stop to each new protected swing as the trend makes new ones.
quote: "I have a new spot for my stop loss to trail to."

rule: After expanding through a high, decide among three outcomes by closes: aggressive displacement back into range (reversal), consolidation (wait for a sweep of the opposite side), or retracement into an FVG (then continuation).
quote: "are we going to aggressively displace back into the range, forming a reversal to trade lower"

rule: A retrace back into the prior range during an expansion is unwanted; it reclassifies the leg as a consolidation, which needs a sweep of the low (bull) or high (bear).
quote: "You don't really want to see that in expansion. You want to see it just trade higher."

rule: Expansion met by an opposing expansion is a reversal; the current protected low is then likely unsafe and becomes the draw on liquidity.
quote: "Our protected low is likely not safe and becomes the draw on liquidity."

rule: Summary mapping: consolidation -> wait for a manipulation; retracement -> wait for a protected swing, then trade the continuation.
quote: "If I see a consolidation, I know I want to see a manipulation. If I see a retracement, I want to see a protected swing and then I can trade it higher."

rule: A reversal is expansion met with expansion (an opposing expansion right after an expansion).
quote: "A reversal is when we have expansion met with expansion. And that is what forms a reversal."

rule: Continuation signatures are expansion → retracement → expansion, or expansion → consolidation → manipulation → expansion.
quote: "where we had expansion and a retracement to continue lower with a new expansion or expansion consolidation manipulating the high to continue lower."

rule: After a reversal, don't fight the new expansion; look for continuations in its direction.
quote: "We're not wanting to fight that expansion. So we're looking for continuations higher following a reversal."

rule: Reversals should form at a point of interest: an old high/low or a swing high/low.
quote: "We want to see a reversal form at a point of interest."

rule: When price expands into a swing high/low, check which phase follows: consolidation, retracement (continuation), or opposing expansion (reversal forming the HTF wick).
quote: "do we get a consolidation, do we get a retracement to continue higher or do we have expansion met with expansion forming that higher time frame wick"

rule: Trade reversals by viewing the lower timeframe at the old/swing high: the CISD there forms the higher-timeframe reversal.
quote: "I'm going to want to watch price on the lower time frames to look for reversals."

rule: You don't have to catch the extreme; trade the continuation after the reversal from a protected swing.
quote: "I don't have to catch the high to trade a reversal."

rule: Don't pick random highs/lows to reverse from; use relevant swings, most easily previous day and previous week highs and lows.
quote: "you don't want to choose a random high and low for price to reverse off of. You want to find those relevant swings in the market."

rule: A reversal off a random high that leaves failure swing highs above is not trusted, even if the structure looks good.
quote: "does it make sense for price to reverse off of a random high right here? Not really."

rule: When the phase is unclear, let another candle close; closures give new data.
quote: "So, if I don't know what's going on, I can just let another candle close."

rule: Displacement back into the range after an expansion is neither retracement nor consolidation; it is the opposing expansion (reversal).
quote: "Is this a retracement? No, it is displacing back into the range."

rule: A candle that only leaves an FVG doesn't decide the phase (could be retracement, consolidation or reversal); wait for the next candle.
quote: "It could still be a retracement. It could be consolidation. It could be a reversal. I need to let another candle print."

rule: After an expansion-met-with-expansion reversal, want price to expand directly, retrace a little, or consolidate and sweep the high, then continue.
quote: "I'd want to see either price just expand lower or have a little retracement to continue lower or a consolidation to sweep the high"

rule: Ideal reversal structure: expansion into a low that sweeps lows, displacement back in, and a close over the series of down-close candles (V-shape + CISD); it traps early longs and breakout shorts.
quote: "So you can see how we blend those V-shaped reversals with the change in the state of delivery."

rule: HTF reversal candle with a large wick = expansion met with expansion on the LTF; the model trades the continuation after it.
quote: "When we have expansion met with expansion forming a higher time frame wick, we look into the lower time frames here."

rule: Only trade against the trend after price hits a relevant high/low (target) where a retracement or reversal can be anticipated.
quote: "when can I look to trade opposing the trend? And that would be when you can anticipate a retracement or a reversal."

rule: Expansion shows as fair value gaps being created.
quote: "You can say that we expand when we create fair value gaps."

rule: After a relevant high is taken and a CISD forms, target back into the range: through the daily open, internal liquidity such as an FVG.
quote: "So now this is where I could anticipate price to trade back into the range, right?"

rule: After a reversal, a further opposing expansion (instead of retracement/consolidation) means the low is likely to fail.
quote: "We don't want to see price what? meet it with more expansion lower because then this low is likely to fail."

rule: Use the relevant low (not one that leaves a nearer low behind) as the POI for the retracement.
quote: "Does it make sense for price to reach into this low, leave this one right here, and then go higher? No, it doesn't."

rule: Retracement ends with a new CISD, which starts the next expansion.
quote: "When is price going to expand again? When we get a new change in the state of delivery."

rule: For the CISD, use the series of candles from the swing high that created the swing low (the swing that matters).
quote: "the reason for that is that is the swing high that created this swing low."

rule: A reversal that does not respect the EQ (50%) of its wick is likely to fail.
quote: "We're not respecting the EQ of this wick. This is likely to fail."

rule: Best reversals pair a daily candle closure with an LTF CISD and the phases of price; an LTF reversal without a daily swing point is weaker.
quote: "Now, we are pairing this with a change in the state of delivery and the phases of price."

rule: A slow move back (8 candles to retrace 2/3 of a 3-candle move) is not aggressive expansion; read it as retracement.
quote: "Takes three candles to get all of this range here. And it takes what? Eight candles to just go back up."

rule: A short-term low is a swing low: a low with a higher low on each side; a short-term high is a high with a lower high on each side.
quote: "a short term low is when we form a swing low. So a low with a higher low on each side of it."

rule: An intermediate-term low is a short-term low with a higher short-term low to its left and right (mirror for highs).
quote: "when we have a short term low with a higher short term low on the right and left of it, this then becomes an intermediate term low."

rule: A rebalanced intermediate-term low/high forms when price trades into a fair value gap and away.
quote: "There's also a rebalanced intermediate term high and low, and that is when price rebalances a fair value gap."

rule: A long-term low is the low formed off the reaction to a higher-timeframe level.
quote: "A long term low is the low that is formed off the reaction of the higher time frame level."

rule: Drop from a 15m buy-side sweep to the 1m to read the swing hierarchy for the move to the 15m lows.
quote: "So we are on a 15 minute chart, we sweep a high, so let's drop down to the one minute chart."

rule: A long-term high is validated only once a short-term high forms on its other (right) side.
quote: "if we're going to form and validate this as a long term high, I'm waiting for a short term high on the other side."

rule: Once the long-term high is in, anticipate it to remain intact and price to trade to the opposite draw.
quote: "I'm anticipating this to become a long-term high, remain intact, and for price to trade to these lows."

rule: An intermediate-term high forms when price sweeps a short-term high and then puts in a short-term high on the other side.
quote: "We need price to sweep a short-term high, and then put in another short-term high on the other side."

rule: The swept swing is only a short-term high until a lower high forms on its right.
quote: "This is currently just a short term high until we get another lower high on the right side of it."

rule: Breaking a short-term high could be called a structure shift, but he prefers the intermediate-term high to be taken.
quote: "a lot of times I like to look for the intermediate term high to be taken to signify a shift in structure."

rule: A sweep that is only equal lows does not count much; he waits for a real sweep before an intermediate-term low.
quote: "we get a little sweep here, it's more so just equal lows for me, and there we get a sweep."

rule: Price may sweep an intermediate-term low to retrace into discount of the range before moving higher.
quote: "You see price wanted to retrace to a discount to then move higher."

rule: Long-term highs and lows form off higher-timeframe PD arrays / points of interest and are validated by a short-term swing on the right and price trading away.
