quote: "our long-term high and our long-term low are formed off of higher timeframe PD arrays or points of interest."

rule: After the long-term swing, look for an intermediate-term swing on its right.
quote: "Then I am searching for"

rule: Daily discount FVG as the HTF level: drop to the hourly and mark the swing hierarchy as price reacts.
quote: "you can see we have a discount fair value gap resting right here."

rule: Once an intermediate-term low is confirmed in a bullish leg, do not expect it to be violated if price continues higher.
quote: "now I don't anticipate this intermediate term low to be violated if we're going to continue to trade higher."

rule: If a confirmed intermediate-term low is reached, the bullish assumption is wrong.
quote: "I don't anticipate this to be reached unless I am wrong on this assumption we move higher."

rule: London up-close candles that swept Asia highs into a gap are marked as a bearish order block for the NY session.
quote: "we sweep our Asia highs, and we create an up-close candle during London. So marking that out as our order block"

rule: When price returns to the order block, watch for short-term highs and a long-term high to form at that level.
quote: "I want to look for short term highs and eventually a long term high to form at this level."

rule: After the intermediate-term high forms, do not expect price back above it before delivering to the sell-side liquidity.
quote: "I would not expect price to reach back up here before delivering to the original consolidation or sell-side liquidity resting right here."

rule: A retrace into premium (the up-close candles) forming a short-term high is the entry point toward sell-side.
quote: "reach back up into a premium, into these up-close candles, forming a short-term high."

rule: Use advanced market structure for entries when price is choppy and there are no clean FVGs.
quote: "There aren't really any clean fair value gaps for entries and that's when I'll use some advanced market structure to find a short-term high to enter off of."

rule: First check which liquidity was taken last: after sell-side is taken expect distribution higher, after buy-side expect lower.
quote: "if we take liquidity down here, we want to distribute it higher, pick liquidity up here, want to distribute it lower"

rule: Mark swing highs/lows, short-term highs/lows and relative equal highs/lows; stops (liquidity) rest beyond them.
quote: "That's just where people are going to have their stops above. So it is important to notice them because that is where liquidity rests."

rule: A market structure shift with imbalances signals a change in trend: a short-term high broken with displacement leaving an FVG.
quote: "It breaks it with displacement and then an imbalance."

rule: Check premium/discount: after taking sell-side liquidity, distribute into premium; after taking buy-side, into discount.
quote: "Once we take liquidity here, we want to distribute it at a premium."

rule: Read the swing sequence (lower highs/lower lows vs higher highs) to see the trend.
quote: "just lower highs, lower lows, you know, simple swing highs, swing lows, just to see where we're trending"

rule: To set bias, clean the chart down to the closest imbalances and liquidity.
quote: "I kind of clean it up and just look at the closest imbalances and liquidity."

rule: After an MSS up, expect a move back down to grab liquidity (possibly into the FVG) before the higher target is taken.
quote: "I want to see a move back down a little bit to grab liquidity and move higher."

rule: Lower-timeframe bias can be opposite to the daily target until the near liquidity is grabbed; then revert to the daily direction.
quote: "On the one hour timeframe and lower timeframes, I am Bearish until this liquidity is grabbed and then back to being bullish here."

rule: When bearish, look for a false move up that grabs liquidity, then distribution lower.
quote: "I want to see, you know, that false move up to grab liquidity and then distribute it lower"

rule: Bias = the easiest path for liquidity, mostly relative equal highs and lows because stops cluster there.
quote: "I look for just liquidity. Where is the easiest path for it to go?"

rule: ICT-style entries (sweep then distribution) protect you even when the bias is wrong.
quote: "Trading ICT will keep you from, you know, just entering trades you shouldn't be in."

rule: Frame the draw on liquidity / daily bias with previous day high and low as the default reference.
quote: "The easiest way to frame a draw on liquidity or have daily bias is using previous day high and low."

rule: Unless price consolidates, expect it to take PDH, PDL, or both; ask which is more likely.
quote: "we are going to have it either take previous day high, previous day low, or both of these."

rule: When trending up, the draw is PDH; when trending down, the draw is PDL.
quote: "I would expect price to be reaching for previous day high as we are trending upwards."

rule: PDH/PDL are liquidity pools that frame reversals: reach beyond, fail to displace, close back inside -> reversal.
quote: "we reach into this previous day high, we can't displace above it, and price reverses."

rule: After a close back inside the previous range from PDH, the draw becomes PDL (and vice versa).
quote: "since we close back in, I'm expecting price to reach for previous day low."

rule: After a close above PDH, the next easy draw is the new PDH; keep repeating until it fails.
quote: "we have our previous day high and we closed above it. So I would like to see price move higher."

rule: Taking PDH but not closing over it flips the bias short toward PDL.
quote: "We take our previous high, but we can't close over it. We fall back in."

rule: When both PDH and PDL are taken, the decisive factor is which side price closes outside of.
quote: "we swept this low, couldn't close below it, and we actually take previous day high and close outside of it."

rule: After a very large candle expect consolidation; if price does not stay inside, keep the PDH draw.
quote: "expecting some sort of consolidation, but if we don't stay inside I'd want to see previous day high."

rule: The PDH/PDL framework does not work every day.
quote: "Now it won't be like this every day"

rule: Previous week high and low can frame a reversal (then target the other side of the weekly range) or act as the draw.
quote: "And this can be used to frame a reversal, such as so, and then ideally looking for the other side of the weekly range"

rule: After taking the previous week low and coming back inside the range, expect the previous week high.
quote: "And then we come back into the rain. Where would I expect price to go from here? I would expect it to reach for previous week's high."

rule: A Monday sweep of the previous week low with a bullish reversal candle points to the previous week high.
quote: "Monday we swept previous week's low and formed a nice bullish reversal candle."

rule: Swing points (old highs/lows) serve both as draws on liquidity and as points to frame reversals.
quote: "using swing points, I can frame a drawn liquidity off of that."

rule: Failure to displace under a swing low -> bias up; failure to displace over a swing high -> bias down.
quote: "if we have a swing low and price fails to displace under it, my bias can then be up."

rule: Next day model: after a failure to displace below a low (or respecting a PD array), anticipate an open-low-high-close (bullish) next day; mirror for highs.
quote: "when price fails to displace below a low, my next day, I can expect price to move higher."

rule: Sweep of a swing high with a close back in the range -> anticipate open-high-low-close next day.
quote: "when price takes this swing high, closes back in the range, I can anticipate an open high low close or a bearish candle."

rule: An inside candle keeps the prior bias; keep using it until the draw on liquidity is reached.
quote: "This candle stays inside. I can use that bias."

rule: If the previous day's range is not closed outside of, expect the opposite side to be reached.
quote: "We can't close outside our previous day's range, which leads me to believe that we should be reaching lower"

rule: A close outside a swing high means expect higher prices or a wide-range consolidation.
quote: "Price to move higher or consolidate with a large range."

rule: With no clear bias (inside bar), mark the high and low and see which is taken; lean with the trend.
quote: "So inside bar, just having an uptrend, I think it's more likely to reach for this high."

rule: When price keeps closing outside and the near draws are taken, look left for older swing lows / highs.
quote: "Still closing outside, this is when I would need to look left."

rule: Execution: take the daily bias to the hourly, mark midnight open, wait for a stop hunt into a PD array in the session, enter the lower-timeframe FVG.
quote: "I'm going to go ahead and mark out midnight opening price and let's see what happens."

rule: In a bearish London setup, expect the high of the day to be put in during London.
quote: "If you notice the time this is occurring is London. So I would want to see a high of the day put in in London."

rule: A small sweep is a caution sign that price may want to go higher again; wait for what follows.
quote: "Because this isn't a very big sweep, so I'd be a little concerned that it wanted to go up again."

rule: Stop goes on the high that formed the sweep; target fixed 2R or the PDL / swing-point liquidity.
quote: "look to enter the fair value gap, my stop on that high, and then I can either look for a fixed to R"

rule: Daily profiles rest on sessions/kill zones; for this profile use London 2:00-5:00 and New York AM 8:30-12:00 (his extension to 12).
quote: "we're going to focus on London from 2: to 5:00 and then New York a.m. so generally I'm looking at 8:30 to 12"

rule: A London reversal is a classic expansion candle: open, manipulate to make the wick, expand, close.
quote: "a London reversal is basically a classic expansion candle"

rule: Bullish: London drops during 2-5 creating the daily wick, then CISD / MSS; New York continues off London's reversal.
quote: "we'll have our open we will drop down during London or 2 to 5 this is creating the wick of the daily candle"

rule: Bearish mirror: London puts in the high during 2-5, CISD, NY continuation completes the OHLC of the daily candle.
quote: "this London reversal leads into a New York continuation completing the Open high low close of the daily candle"

rule: Use the daily chart for direction (e.g. bullish reversal candle) and target internal liquidity / range EQ.
quote: "we have internal liquidity right here so that will be our first Target however we can trade up to equilibrium of this range"

rule: London reversal confirmation = reach into the previous range then close over the down-close candle (CISD) around 2-5 a.m.
quote: "at 2: to 5 a.m. London reverses and changes the state of delivery"

rule: If bullish after the London reversal, look for a NY continuation higher, refining on the 5m.
quote: "ideally if we are bullish we're looking for a continuation higher during New York"

rule: In NY, a consolidation then manipulation (AMD); a close over the series of down-close candles forms the order block to enter.
quote: "when we get the close over the series of down Clos candles here that will form an order block"

rule: Entry at the order block, stop on the manipulation low, target 2R.
quote: "I can look to take a position here I stop on this low and look to Target 2 R"

rule: Down-close candles into an order block that hold form a propulsion block that gets retested.
quote: "series of down Clos candles into an order block you now have a propulsion block"

rule: If the LTF is messy, go up one timeframe (e.g. 15m → 30m) to find a clear series for the CISD.
quote: "since this is a little bit messy I will go up one time frame to the 30 minute chart"

rule: For a bearish NY continuation, wait for an opposing run / move higher to get on side.
quote: "I'd want to see some sort of opposing run or move higher to get on side with a continuation lower"

rule: Important NY time levels: 8:30 and 9:30 (also 10:00); an 8:30 move against the expected direction is the manipulation.
quote: "what are the important time levels that we are looking for 8:30 9:30"

rule: Enter when price closes below the opposing run's candles (order block); stop on the opposing run; target 2R.
quote: "I will enter a position there my stop on this opposing run and then I'll look to Target 2 R"

rule: If 8:30 manipulates in the expected direction instead, expect a retracement into London's range before the continuation.
quote: "I'd ideally like to see it manipulate up but it manipulates down which gives me a reason to think we get a retracement"

rule: 10:00 a.m. is important because of the 4-hour candle open-high-low-close.
quote: "right at 10:00 a.m. or another important level due to the 4-Hour open high low close"

rule: 8:30 news can manipulate into London's order block before continuing.
quote: "we have 8:30 news which manipulates up into London's order block here and then continues lower"

rule: After a sweep of previous day low and close back inside (bullish reversal candle), look for the next day to trade higher.
quote: "we see a sweep below previous day low a close back inside and what is this this is a bullish reversal candle"

rule: For continuation, the mean threshold of the order block should be respected, with midnight open as support.
quote: "I want to see the mean threshold of this being respected which it is along with midnight open being used as a support level"

rule: He trades the NY session, not London, even when London gives an entry.
quote: "if I was trading London I could look to get ons side with a short position here however I focus on New York session"

rule: Of the kill zones (Asia, London, NY AM, NY PM), he filters to London and NY AM for the indices.
quote: "I will specifically be focusing on London and then New York am for the indices"

rule: A NY reversal day is an OHLC (bearish) or OLHC (bullish) daily candle whose wick forms in New York.
quote: "we'll have an open high low close and then open low high close"

rule: It differs from a London reversal because London never reaches a relevant PD array, so the move extends into NY to form the reversal.
quote: "London never reached a relevant PD aray so when it went open high into London we never reached a PD array to form the reversal"

rule: Sequence: London moves toward the level without reaching it, price keeps retracing into NY, hits the HTF key level, then the CISD, then expansion.
quote: "continue to retrace into New York where we reach that higher time frame key level then we have the change in the state of delivery"

rule: Mark the HTF level (e.g. previous day low = sellside liquidity) and, once reached in NY, wait for a CISD through the series of opposing candles.
quote: "now what am I looking for a change in the state of delivery"

rule: A failed CISD at the level means price will make a new low or at least reach lower into the wick; re-mark the new series of opposing candles.
quote: "we fail to change the state of delivery here which gives me the indication we're going to move lower"

rule: Prefer the CISD whose opposing candles line up with the New York open or another important time.
quote: "you see how that also lines up with New York open or an important time level"

rule: Entry after the close over; stop on the low or, for better risk-to-reward to distant failure swings, at the bottom of the order block.
quote: "doesn't really make sense in terms of risk to reward so I'll put it at the bottom of this order block here"

rule: Plenty of low-resistance liquidity (failure swings) ahead is what produces the aggressive move after the CISD.
quote: "we have a bunch of low resistance liquidity to run through that is how we get that aggressive move"

rule: A London low that only creates more equal lows (no HTF level reached) is a fake CISD that will run the lows again, ideally around the NY open.
quote: "this is going to be a fake change in the state of delivery to then go run the lows again"

rule: In NY, a sweep that cannot close below at the NY open is the opposing move; that NY-open candle becomes the order block once price closes over it.
quote: "New York open would also be the order block that would be formed if we get a close over"

rule: Targets are the failure swings (London and Asia highs); scale partials anywhere as long as above 2R, e.g. at midnight open.
quote: "doesn't really matter where I take partials as long as it's over two R for me"

rule: If the London move never engaged an HTF PD array, the real reversal is the NY one.
quote: "it looked like a London reversal but we never engaged a higher time frame PD array so then it is actually a New York reversal"

rule: Daily context for a bearish day: price respecting the lower half / consequent encroachment of a wick and closing back inside the previous candle's high forms a bearish reversal candle; expect OHLC next day.
quote: "we close back inside the previous candle's high and what do we form a bearish reversal candle"

rule: Check London (2-5 am ET) for a high; if London keeps trading higher instead, expect a NY reversal.
quote: "London right that's what's important between 2 to 5"

rule: An intraday CISD through a series of up-close candles is the same thing as an order block; use a higher timeframe (30m) if the 15m is messy.
quote: "that is our change in the state of delivery intraday or an order block"

rule: Stop on the high or above the order block; target failure swings (example 2.65R).
quote: "with either my stop on this high or above the order block and then targeting this low for 2.65 R"

rule: A re-entry needs 8:30 to make an opposing run that forms a new order block; confluence with midnight and 8:30 strengthens it.
quote: "I'd like to see at at 830 making an opposing run to form a new order block"

rule: An order block built off an order block is a propulsion block.
quote: "that would be our propulsion Block it's an order block built off an order block"

rule: For external-range setups, use the range high and the most recent swing low as the range low.
quote: "we can consider any of these for the range low but I will use the most current swing low here"

rule: In NY, the times to watch are 8:30, 9:30 and 10:00.
quote: "times am I looking at 8:30 9:30 10"

rule: When London's high is swept rather than forming a significant high, keep the bearish bias and expect a NY reversal.
quote: "we actually swept London's High here so I'm anticipating what a New York reversal"

rule: 8:30 manipulation then 9:30 continuation mirrors the London-then-NY relationship.
quote: "8:30 manipulation 9:30 continuation similar to London and New York"

rule: A NY opening run that sweeps highs then reverses is LTF order-block formation.
quote: "New York makes an opposing run up to sweep out some of these highs that's lower time frame order block formation"

rule: A gap between candles on the HTF (e.g. 1h) marks an imbalance that can act as the NY objective.
quote: "there's a gap right what does that mean that means that there is a higher time frame imbalance right here"

rule: A day can be both: London CISD continuation reaches the HTF objective, then NY manipulates into it and reverses, so it is also a NY reversal.
quote: "this is actually a London reversal but then can also be framed as a New York reversal"

rule: Weekly frame: after a failed run on a daily low and a Friday retracement, expect the retracement to reach a daily order block before the low is taken.
quote: "i saw the order block here on the daily time frame and was expecting to move into this before we drop lower"

rule: While expecting a bullish retracement, require swing lows to be taken before a long; no sweep = no trade.
quote: "expecting to be bullish so i want to see some swing lows taken out and then a move higher"

rule: Once price reaches the daily POI, bias flips bearish; a short-term low taken (MSS) alone was not a setup he liked.
quote: "you could look for a trading here when this short term was taken out right market structure shift"

rule: Being deep into an intraday move is fine if the daily chart still has room to the target.
quote: "you might say oh i don't want to get short this far into a move however we look at the daily chart we're only right in here"

rule: 5m entry model: short-term low taken (MSS down), retrace into FVG/order block, sell, stop on the highs.
quote: "market structure shift down a retracement into this fair value gap and order block you'd sell short there with your stop on these highs"

rule: Target the near edge of an HTF (1h) FVG and take the position off at its start rather than being greedy.
quote: "take off your position you know at the start of it that's what i like to do not to be greedy"

rule: After the daily range breaks down, take shorts only.
quote: "we are looking for shorts only since i was bearish after we broke down from that range on the daily chart"

rule: Use SMT (he calls it divergence) between ES and NQ on the 15m to choose the weaker index to short.
quote: "i saw a divergence on the 15-minute chart here so i was looking at mq since it's weaker"

rule: Alternative: ES itself was tradable after it swept the highs and moved lower.
quote: "you could have taken es when it swept these highs up here and then made it move lower"

rule: If the swing-high stop is too much risk, place the stop just above the FVG.
quote: "too much risk for me putting it on the high there so i just put it right above the fair value gap"

rule: Target a liquidity level (NQ 11,850).
quote: "i want 11 850 here because of the liquidity"

rule: Plan the next day the night before from an HTF (1h) order block: expect highs taken first, then equal lows taken.
quote: "i saw this one hour order block here and kind of drew up what i wanted to see"

rule: When the larger timeframe is playing out a 1h order block, any pop can be shorted, but he refines on the 1m.
quote: "since on the larger time frames you're playing this one hour order block you kind of could just take shorts on any pop in here"

rule: 1m entry: low taken, structure shifts down, retrace into FVG or order block, sell; hold for the day's target.
quote: "when it takes this low out here shift structure down retraces back into this fair value gap sell short there"

rule: Only take entries that appear between 10:00 and 11:00 New York (AM silver bullet window).
quote: "The only time I will take entries is if it appears between 10 and 11 AM."

rule: Frame the reversal with the previous hour's high and low, i.e. the 9 AM hourly candle, marked once 10:00 hits.
quote: "in this framework, I'm going to use the previous hours high and low. And in this case, that's the 9am hourly candle."

rule: Wait for price to take one side of the 9 AM range, then look for an entry targeting the opposite side.
quote: "Price to take one side of this range. So in this case, it takes the 9am high. And then I look for a entry to target the 9am low."

rule: The setup trigger is a stop raid above the 9 AM high or below the 9 AM low inside the window; then look for an entry model the other way.
quote: "All I do is sit back and wait for a stop raid to occur below this low or above this high."

rule: If neither side of the 9 AM range is swept within 10:00-11:00, there is no trade that session.
quote: "price never swept the low or the high of this range, so this would be a session where I would not be looking to take a trade."

rule: After the raid, require displacement back the other way before entering; no displacement means wait.
quote: "No displacement down yet."

rule: Entry arrays used: order block, FVG (or its consequent encroachment), breaker, midnight opening price confluence.
quote: "We have a fair value gap there as well and midnight opening price. So what I'll do is I'll look to take a short entry."

rule: Stop goes on the sweep high/low; target is the other side of the previous hour's candle.
quote: "my stop on this high, and where am I targeting the other side of this previous hours candle."

rule: A breaker forms when price closes below the low that made the new high (short) or above the corresponding high (long); enter on the breaker.
quote: "Now I wanna see if we can close below this low that made the new high. Okay, so we do. So what I'm gonna mark out is this breaker block here."

rule: The limit order must fill before 11:00; if it does not, cancel it.
quote: "we cancel our order, because it's outside the 11am window."

rule: Risk 1% per trade in the backtest.
quote: "So click here, hit place order, risking 1%, sell limit."

rule: Move the stop to break-even once the trade reaches 3R.
quote: "what I did in backtesting was once this hits 3R, I will move my stop to break even."

rule: Equal highs touched without running are not counted as a sweep.
quote: "We do touch that high. I don't really consider that a sweep, just equal highs."

rule: A small FVG after a shallow sweep is not enough; he wants more aggressive displacement.
quote: "Not super convincing to me. I want to see a more aggressive displacement down."

rule: Skip setups where the stop would need to sit above nearby equal highs and the price action has no clear displacement.
quote: "There's no clear displacement. And then if I was to enter in here, we have equal highs, and I want my stop up there."

rule: After a sweep he wants it met immediately by aggressive displacement; a mere retracement suggests continuation the sweep's way.
quote: "I'd want to see this met immediately with aggressive displacement higher, or if we just get a retracement, it's likely to go lower."

rule: Prefer a lower-timeframe sweep forming the entry model, not just the raw range sweep.
quote: "I'd like to see a lower timeframe sweep, so the entry model below here, not just this."

rule: Do not enter once price has already almost reached the target; prefer entries on the sell side of the curve, not when price is coming back.
quote: "Generally, once it already reaches almost to that low, I'm not really looking to enter that. I prefer the entry on the sell side of the curve"

rule: If the 10 AM candle already took one side and price does not come back into the range, the opposite side is unlikely.
quote: "Seems the 10 AM candle just took this low, so if we don't come back into the range, not a large possibility of going for that high."

rule: No trade when the structure cannot be read.
quote: "I'm not going to do anything about it because I can't see the structure."

rule: When the target is only about 3R, there is no need to project a fib for the break-even point.
quote: "And that's just at 3R, so no reason to project a FIB."

rule: Before entering on an order block, wait for the third candle to close beyond the swept low (structure) rather than enter early.
quote: "I want to see this third candle close below here before returning to this order block."

rule: Very shallow sweeps without displacement or FVGs are low quality.
quote: "It's very shallow, which not a huge fan of that. No real displacement up, no fair value gaps, just met."

rule: A 45-day, 15-trade backtest is too small; a deeper backtest is needed to judge the model.
quote: "Now it's important to notice I only tested this over 45 days and 15 trades."

rule: For a 1m entry, use a 4H or 1h draw on liquidity: an old high, old low or imbalance.
quote: "With using a one minute entry, I want to look for a four hour or one hour draw on liquidity. Generally, this is an old high or an old low or an imbalance."

rule: 1m framework: a 15m stop raid in the opposite direction of the draw, then a bullish (in-direction) candle close.
quote: "I'm going to be looking for a stop rate on the 15 minute chart. In the opposite direction of my draw on liquidity and then a bullish candle close."

rule: After the 15m raid and close, drop to 1m and look for an FVG entry toward the draw.
quote: "From here, I will drop down to the one minute chart and look for a fair value gap entry targeting that draw on liquidity."

rule: One index taking an hourly low while the other does not is SMT.
quote: "Well, ES took this low out and Q didn't. So that actually creates an SMT."

rule: If the draw is higher, a low should be swept before price reaches for the draw.
quote: "if our draw on liquidity is higher, we want to see a low swept prior to reaching towards that draw on liquidity."

rule: Wait for price to take the 15m low and close back in before dropping to 1m.
quote: "The next thing I want to do is wait for price to take that low and then close back in."

rule: Enter longs at a discount of the post-sweep range.
quote: "Well, I want to be entering at a discount."

rule: Minimum 1:2 R preferred; take partials or profit at nearby equal highs.
quote: "However, I personally prefer a minimum of one to two R"

rule: After an external draw is taken, the next draw can be internal (an FVG): external to internal.
quote: "if we're going to go from external to internal, we have a fair value gap resting here."

rule: A bearish close back below a BISI after sweeping London highs makes it resistance toward the hourly FVG.
quote: "here you can see we have this BISI right here, and we close below it. So now I'd anticipate this area acting as resistance"

rule: Stacked higher lows are low-resistance liquidity that price should run into toward the draw.
quote: "All these higher lows create low resistance liquidity."

rule: 1m entry: FVG after displacement away, stop on the high, target the hourly FVG.
quote: "So here I would look to take an entry, put my stop on this high, and then I'd be looking to target this hourly fair value gap."

rule: For a 5m entry, use a daily or 4H draw on liquidity (old high, old low, inefficiency).
quote: "What if I'm looking to take entries on a five minute chart? Well, with this, I would want to have a daily or four hour drawn liquidity"

rule: 5m framework: hourly stop raid opposite the draw; he does not wait for the candle close back in.
quote: "And in this case, I'm going to do how I trade it and not waiting for this candle close back in."

rule: After the hourly raid, look for a 5m entry model toward the draw.
quote: "Next I'm looking at the five minute chart after rating that hourly low and looking for an entry model targeting that drawn liquidity."

rule: An inversion gap closed over after the hourly sweep plus SMT is a 5m long entry.
quote: "Here you can see we get an inversion gap closing over. So I can look to take an entry here"

rule: Taking profit at failure swings can save sitting through drawdown, at a small cost.
quote: "here's an example of how using failure swings can be beneficial in profit taking."

rule: Mark midnight open on the hourly; for a lower draw, look for an hourly sweep of a high (e.g. in London) first.
quote: "So the first thing I'm going to do is mark out our midnight open. Now, like I said, our drawn liquidity is below us."

rule: If expecting a lower day, be a seller above (or at) the opening price after displacement down.
quote: "ideally, if we're expecting price to draw lower, I want to be a seller above open."

rule: Frame accumulation, manipulation, then expect distribution into New York.
quote: "Manipulation. I'd expect distribution here coming into the New York session."

rule: When trying to catch the daily range, put the stop on the high of the day rather than the local high.
quote: "I could have my stop on this high, but ideally I'd put it on the high a day because I'm anticipating and trying to catch the daily range"

rule: If the first entry is missed, add or catch a later displacement entry.
quote: "So if I miss that entry, I could look to add or catch this entry here."

rule: Bearish day profile: open, high, low, close, getting short above midnight open.
quote: "Anticipating a bearish move, I want to be looking for an open high."

rule: Mark the consequent encroachment of a large daily wick as the POI; no bodies above it confirms respect.
quote: "Now we have this candle here with a large wick, so I'm going to mark out the consequent encroachment of that wick."

rule: If the draw gives under his RR preference (1.14R), project standard deviations for targets.
quote: "that would be 1.14R, which I don't prefer. So then I can use other methods such as a standard deviation projection to give myself targets."

rule: Read higher-timeframe context first: a 15m consolidation range is marked and labelled "bullish" before dropping down.
quote: none (no speech)

rule: On the 1m, the trigger is a sweep of the consolidation's range lows, followed by a sharp move back up.
quote: none (no speech)

rule: Plan the long at a retracement of the sweep-up leg: a Fib drawn from the swept low to the high, with 0.5, 0.62 and 0.79 levels; the entry sits at about 0.62.
quote: none (no speech)

rule: Stop just below the swept low.
quote: none (no speech)

rule: The planned trade is about 3R (TradingView position tool: stop 3.50 pts, target 10.75 pts, R:R 3.07).
quote: none (no speech)

rule: Use a seconds chart (15s) to refine the entry inside the 1m retracement.
quote: none (no speech)

rule: A counter-trend scalp short was taken into the expected retracement before the long; the caption calls it a counter-trend scalp with a bad market fill.
quote: none (no speech)

rule: Scale out with several limit targets (multiple "Target" fills of 1 contract) while keeping a protective stop on the rest.
quote: none (no speech)

rule: A candle that takes neither the previous high nor low is, by definition, consolidating.
quote: "this candle here could not take out the previous candle's high, or buy-side liquidity, or the previous candle's low, or sell-side liquidity."

rule: A candle that takes only one side of the previous range is a one-sided or directional move.
quote: "price takes out sell-side liquidity, but does not take out buy-side liquidity. So this is a one-sided or directional move."

rule: If price is not consolidating, anticipate it moving toward the previous candle's high or low, sometimes both.
quote: "if price is not in a consolidation, I can anticipate price moving towards the previous candle's high or low, or in some cases both."

rule: Know where previous-candle levels are on multiple timeframes (month, week, day, session).
quote: "this is why it is important to know where these levels are located on multiple different timeframes."

rule: Previous month's high and low frame a draw on liquidity or a reversal.
quote: "these levels are used to frame a drawn [draw on] liquidity or a reversal."

rule: Mark monthly high/low and extend them into the next month as previous month's high/low.
quote: "I have marked out our monthly high and low with a solid line and then extended that into the next month."

rule: The same applies to the weekly: a reversal is framed off previous week's low, or previous week's low is the draw.
quote: "a reversal is framed off of previous week's low, and then we end up going to previous week's high"

rule: In a downtrend, after a close below the previous week's low, the previous week's low (continuation) is the more likely draw.
quote: "since we are trending down, I think previous week's low is more likely."

rule: Taking the previous week's low without displacing / closing outside -> anticipate the previous week's high.
quote: "Here we hit previous week's low, fail to displace or close out the range. So then I would anticipate price reaching for previous week's high."

rule: An indecision candle (little displacement) leaves both sides of its range as possible draws.
quote: "Not a lot of displacement or direction. So here, kind of an indecision candle."

rule: A close back in after reaching into an FVG favors the opposite previous-week extreme.
quote: "we did reach over into this fair value gap here. So with that in mind, I'd want to see price reach for previous week's low"

rule: On the daily, previous day high/low frame a reversal or serve as the draw; a small doji gives no certainty.
quote: "it is a very small doji candle, so could reach for either side. I'm not really certain."

rule: After an outside bar (both sides taken), he leans to continuation in the close direction.
quote: "Here we reach for both sides, put in an outside bar. Here I'd like to see a continuation higher to previous day high."

rule: Indices kill zones: Asia 20:00-00:00, London 02:00-05:00, New York AM 08:30-11:00 (NY time).
quote: "Asia, which is 20 to 0, London, which is 2 to 5, and the New York AM session from 8.30 to 11."

rule: Session highs and lows can be used as a draw on liquidity and to frame a reversal.
quote: "the session highs and lows can be used as a draw on liquidity as well as to frame a reversal."

rule: Focus on displacement or lack of displacement beyond session ranges.
quote: "What I'm going to focus on is the displacement or lack of displacement out and around these areas."

rule: Failure to displace beyond one side of the Asia range points to the other side.
quote: "we're failing to displace out of this area, so ideally, this makes me look to the other side of the range."

rule: If a London sweep of the Asia high is to hold, price should displace below the Asia low.
quote: "if this high is going to hold, then I'd want to see price displace below the Asia low."

rule: Project the London manipulation leg and use the 2-2.5 and 4-4.5 standard deviation areas as targets.
quote: "I'm just going to focus on this 2 to 2.5 and this 4 to 4.5 area here."

rule: A level that price displaces back through can act as an inversion level for continuation.
quote: "you can see how it is using it as an inversion level."

rule: Lack of displacement over Asia high plus displacement below Asia low indicates the NY AM direction.
quote: "The lack of displacement over Asia high and then displacement below Asia low is what gave indication for what follows in the New York AM session."

rule: A monthly candle that respects the CE of a monthly FVG and closes points to the previous month's low.
quote: "NASDAQ retched [reached] into a monthly fair value gap and closed, respecting the consequent encroachment of this fair value gap."

rule: SMT: NQ lower high while ES higher high is a crack in correlation supporting the bearish draw.
quote: "NASDAQ made a lower high while ES made a higher high, showing a crack in the correlation."

rule: Before acting on the HTF draw, want a shift on the daily: displacement and a close below the up-close candles, then a retrace.
quote: "we want to see some sort of shift on the daily timeframe."

rule: He does not act before the NY session; Asia and London are only observed.
quote: "I'm not really interested until the New York session, so I'm just observing."

rule: NY AM entry: stop run (London high sweep) plus displacement toward the draw, entry in the OTE of that range, stop on the high, target previous day low.
quote: "ideally we're looking for a stop run and displacement lower to get short and target this low."

rule: Three refinements: 0.5 fib, aligned order blocks/breakers, smaller-timeframe imbalances.
quote: "using a .5 fib, looking for order blocks or breakers that line up with the fair value gap, and then looking on smaller timeframes"

rule: Put a 0.5 fib on the FVG and enter at the midpoint rather than the near edge to reduce risk.
quote: "your entry would be here instead of up here, reducing your risk"

rule: The midpoint entry misses some plays but lets you run a lower win percentage.
quote: "You might not catch every play, but you reduce your risk and it allows you to have a lower win percentage."

rule: Look left of the FVG for an order block or breaker that lines up with it.
quote: "you want to look to your left to see if there's anything"

rule: Bearish order block = series of up-close candles; use its open as the refined entry.
quote: "using the open of that order block, you can refine your entry there"

rule: Inside a large HTF FVG, use smaller-timeframe imbalances / order blocks as a tighter reference (daily FVG → hourly).
quote: "using smaller timeframe imbalances within a larger timeframe imbalance"

rule: A 5m FVG can be refined with a 1m order block open.
quote: "There's this order block right here. So mark that out, use the open of that"

rule: The LTF order block open and the FVG 0.5 often land in a similar place.
quote: "the 0.5 FIB is pretty similar in position"

rule: When a daily FVG is too wide to act on, narrow it with a lower-timeframe (hourly) order block inside it.
quote: "however this is a pretty wide area the way i narrow it down is i go down to the hourly chart"

rule: Weekly plan: expect price to reach the higher-timeframe POI, then become bearish only after a structure shift lower on a larger timeframe.
quote: "once we shifted structure to the downside on a larger time frame i would become bearish again"

rule: At the 8:30 open, look back and mark resting liquidity (swing highs and lows).
quote: "we look at 8 30 open right in here and we look back to see where the liquidity is resting"

rule: When bullish, wait for lows to be taken out, then for an entry that targets the highs.
quote: "we are looking for lows to be taken out and then an entry to be presented to take out those highs"

rule: Refine entries from the 5m FVG to the 1m; after a 1m market structure shift, the new 1m FVG offers a second entry.
quote: none

rule: If an FVG is very large, enter at its 0.5 (midpoint) to cut the risk roughly in half.
quote: "this is a super large fair value gap so what i like to do is take a 0.5 fib cut it in half and then use that as my entry"

rule: At a POI for a reversal, do not short until swing lows are taken (market structure shift); with none taken there is no short.
quote: "none of these were taken out so there's no reason for you to be thinking to go short anywhere in here"

rule: After the structure shift, require displacement and enter in the imbalance it leaves.
quote: none

rule: When two imbalances sit above an entry, enter at the first but place the stop above the candle beyond the second, since price may trade into it.
quote: "take the trade in the first one but expect it to be able to trade up into the second one"

rule: Target unfilled higher-timeframe FVGs (here a 5m FVG) even when the level looks odd on the entry chart.
quote: none

rule: Relative equal highs/lows are targets; near-equal levels count, perfect ties (a double top) are not what he wants.
quote: "when you have relative equal highs they become a target right you don't want perfect ties like a double top"

rule: In a bearish plan at the 8:30 open, ideally see a false move up that takes liquidity before the move down.
quote: "we want to see a false move up grab liquidity and go down"

rule: Use a broadening formation's boundary together with an FVG as confluence for the reversal zone.
quote: none

rule: SMT play: enter long on the asset diverging up (NQ making higher lows while ES makes lower lows) with the stop below its lows.
quote: "since nq is the one diverging up you can just enter long and risk the lows here"

rule: The SMT entry is invalid once the diverging asset's lows are taken.
quote: "because if the lows are taken out that divergence is invalidated"

rule: For a more confirmed SMT entry, wait for a market structure shift and enter its (2m) FVG.
quote: none

rule: A structure break without displacement does not qualify; wait for the low taken with displacement and then the imbalance.
quote: none

rule: Instead of the FVG, the entry can be refined to the 0.5 of the range or the start of the order-block body.
quote: none

rule: Skip the choppy period before a Fed release.
quote: none

rule: Skip late entries whose risk-to-reward to the target is no longer attractive.
quote: none

rule: Sell only above the 0.5 of the swing (premium) and buy only below it (discount).
quote: "going short you want to be selling above this 0.5 right of the swing"

rule: A series of higher lows after a news event is a change in the state of delivery that should flip a bearish bias; a lagging NQ daily also warned.
quote: "what i didn't notice is we were making higher lows after that fed meeting should have seen that change in the state of delivery"

rule: At 8:30 when the news embargo lifts, after displacement and retracement, risk the lows of the move.
quote: none

rule: To join a trend, enter only when price retraces into a discount (bullish).
quote: "if you're going to want to get into a trend you want to enter when it comes back down into a discount"

rule: Internal range liquidity is an FVG; external range liquidity is a swing high or swing low (buy-side / sell-side liquidity).
quote: "Internal range liquidity is just a fair value gap. External range liquidity Is a swing high or a swing low in the form of buy side or sell side liquidity"

rule: The market only reaches for old highs/lows or seeks to rebalance an FVG.
quote: "the market only does two things. It either reaches for old highs or old lows or seeks to rebalance a fair value gap"

rule: After taking ERL, price seeks IRL; after reaching IRL, price reaches for ERL.
quote: "after taking external range liquidity, price will seek internal range liquidity. After reaching internal range liquidity, price will reach for an old high or old low"

rule: A failure to displace below an old low signals a retracement from ERL toward the FVG (IRL).
quote: "You can see we fail to displace below this old low or a swing low right here."

rule: If the FVG is respected, target the ERL in the trend direction; if not respected, target the opposite old high.
quote: "If we aren't going to respect this, then we reach for this old high."

rule: Until an FVG forms after taking ERL, there is no IRL target yet; wait for the next candle.
quote: "Now, we don't have internal yet. We don't have a fair value gap formed."

rule: Failure to displace below the previous bar and closing back inside suggests the next candle reaches higher (daily bias rule).
quote: "we fail to displace. Below the previous bar and close back in. So then I'd be looking for the next candle to reach higher."

rule: Displacement through an FVG (inversion) flips bias.
quote: "we displace over this fair value gap, creating an inversion, so then my bias is up"

rule: After an inversion he prefers a retracement before the target, but it will not always happen.
quote: "it's not always going to be perfect, as you notice here, as we do not get a retracement, and we just continue higher"

rule: IRL/ERL on a weekly chart can give directional bias for the whole week.
quote: "understanding the relationship between internal and external liquidity on a weekly chart can give you directional bias for that whole entire week"

rule: Use the HTF IRL-to-ERL move as bias, then drop to lower timeframes for setups toward that ERL.
quote: "with this providing our bias, we will drop down to the lower timeframes, in this case the 5-minute and the 1-minute, to look for short setups to this old low"

rule: Wait for the start of his session before looking for setups.
quote: "We will wait for the start of my session."

rule: Confirmation entry: let a high form inside the 5m FVG and be respected, then drop to 1m for the entry.
quote: "I will look for a high to be put in in this fair value gap, price to respect it, and then go down to a lower time frame"

rule: On 1m after taking liquidity, enter the order block (last closed candle), stop on the high, target the hourly lows.
quote: "my eyes are on this order block entry right here. So I would be looking for a short setup here, my stop on this high"

rule: Three-timeframe roles: HTF IRL-to-ERL for bias, middle TF for an intermediate-term high, LTF for entry.
quote: "We then used the five minute chart to find an intermediate term high, and then used the one minute chart for an entry."

rule: Plan ahead: after reaching IRL, mark the next ERL that the continued trend would target.
quote: "if we reach into internal range liquidity and continue the trend up, where is our new external range liquidity?"

rule: Old lows on a lower timeframe can be what forms the FVG on the higher timeframe.
quote: "these are old lows on the four hour. But that is what forms the fair value gap on the weekly"

rule: Switching from a sell model to a buy model starts when price changes the state of delivery / shifts structure over a high.
quote: "what I want to look for first is when price changes the state of delivery or shift structure, which would be over this high"

rule: 15m entry: consolidation on the FVG, sweep below, CISD, enter the order block, stop on the swept low.
quote: "Here we get a sweep below, and then we change the state of delivery. So I would be looking for this order block entry right here."

rule: Target the 4h ERL and optionally leave runners to the weekly ERL.
quote: "looking for a target on this external range liquidity on the 4-hour if I want to leap [leave] runners to this old high or the weekly external range liquidity"

rule: IRL-to-ERL framing nests: a 4h market maker buy model inside a weekly one.
quote: "this was a market maker buy model. Within this larger timeframe market maker buy model."

rule: The IRL/ERL relationship works on any timeframe (e.g. NQ 5m after the open range).
quote: "this can be used on any time frame"

rule: Internal liquidity is a fair value gap.
quote: "Internal liquidity is just a fair value gap."

rule: An FVG is a three-candle pattern where the wicks of candle 1 and candle 3 do not overlap.
quote: "It is just a three candlestick pattern, one, two, three, in which the wick of the first candle and the wick of the third candle do not overlap"

rule: External liquidity is swing highs and lows (a high with a lower high on each side; a low with a higher low on each side).
quote: "External liquidity is simply highs and lows."

rule: After a sweep of external liquidity that fails to displace through, expect price to reach back to internal liquidity.
quote: "since price swept and could not displace through this external liquidity, it is likely to reach back where? Internal liquidity."

rule: After internal liquidity is reached and the FVG is respected, expect price to go to external liquidity.
quote: "price moves from external to internal and back to external"

rule: Model: HTF level, then one timeframe lower look for internal/external, then on the LTF require kill zone, stop raid, MSS, FVG, target 2R.
quote: "on the lower timeframe, I will look to make sure I'm in a kill zone. I have a stop rate [stop raid], a market structure shift, a fair value gap, and then I will target to R [2R]."

rule: After a very aggressive close, do not expect an immediate retracement; let a few candles form.
quote: "with this super aggressive close down here I'm not expecting retracement right away so I'll let a few candles form"

rule: Enter at the start of the FVG but put the stop so price can trade into a lower FVG (stop at that FVG candle's low).
quote: "I'm going to take an entry on the start of this fair value gap, but I want to allow it to be able to trade down into this fair value gap"

rule: The model targets a fixed 2R even when a larger R is available; runners are optional.
quote: "Even though I could target 3.16R with a total run to the fair value gap, I'm just going to be looking at 2R, and I could hold the runners if I want to."

rule: Moving the stop to breakeven on runners would have been stopped out before the daily FVG; holding the original stop would have worked.
quote: "If I would have moved my stop to break even on runners, they would have been stopped out before reaching the daily fair value gap."

rule: Stop goes over opposing candles; if the entry timeframe is messy, check one timeframe higher and place the stop above the inversion there.
quote: "I want to have my stop over opposing candles."

rule: A tighter alternative stop is the FVG candle's high (more aggressive than the HTF-inversion stop).
quote: "have my stop on the fair value gap candles high, and then look to target 2R"

rule: Lined-up previous-day lows are low-resistance liquidity and make a target.
quote: "you can see how these previous days lows are all lined up here. And that is low resistance liquidity"

rule: POIs he uses on a reversal day candle: its opening price and the mean threshold of the up-close candle; prefer the one at premium of the range.
quote: "The two spots that I look for like this is the opening price, as well as the mean threshold of this up close candle."

rule: If a timeframe is messy, move up a timeframe to clean it up.
quote: "We can move up a time frame to the 4-hour, and this cleans it up a little."

rule: After an aggressive displacement, do not want it met by displacement back the other way: expansion into expansion likely continues that way.
quote: "if we have expansion into expansion it's likely to go higher"

rule: Entry options after displacement: premium of the range, the FVG consequent encroachment, or let it trade away first.
quote: "I can either look to take an entry either at a premium of this range or at the consequent encroachment of this fair value gap"

rule: Previous candle highs/lows (e.g. previous month's low) are important liquidity levels for HTF versions of the model.
quote: "previous candles high and low are important liquidity levels"

rule: The model scales: daily/hour/5m can be moved to monthly/daily/hourly for swing trades.
quote: "I can move that up to the monthly, daily, and then hourly chart to get an entry for either a swing trade"

rule: Do not trade a retracement against the HTF bias; wait for it to finish and trade the expansion out of it.
quote: "since it is against my higher timeframe bias, I would rather not trade this retracement, wait for the retracement to occur, and then trade the expansion out of this"

rule: Prefer the FVG closer to discount and lining up with the breaker block's bodies.
quote: "it's just closer to a discount of this range, as well as lining up with the bodies of this breaker block here"

rule: A 2R target beyond the nearest high is acceptable when trading with HTF order flow.
quote: "this is a little bit over this high, but that is fine because we are trading with the higher timeframe order flow"

rule: His preferred pairing is daily, hour and 5-minute because it aligns with the daily candle's formation.
quote: "I personally prefer daily, hour, and five minute setups, as it aligns with the formation of the daily candle"

rule: Look for the LTF setup when price reaches internal liquidity during a kill zone (London, New York).
quote: "if price reaches into it during a kill zone, can we frame a trade?"

rule: For intraday bias, treat the 4h and 1h charts as the "daily" timeframe and base trades on them.
quote: "how to use the four hour and one hour chart as your daily timeframe and then base trades off of that"

rule: Intraday bias comes from three things: displacement, structure and imbalances.
quote: "That comes down to displacement, Structure and imbalances, right?"

rule: Once direction is known, drop to lower timeframes for the entry (retrace into OTE that runs liquidity).
quote: "Once you understand where price wants to go, then you can go down to your lower timeframe charts and search for an entry"

rule: Short example: risk the high, target the lows identified as structure.
quote: "Then you can take a short position, risk this high, and you know you want to be targeting down here."

rule: Look for old lows to be run and then displacement up before looking for longs.
quote: "one thing I look for is old lows to be ran, right? And then displacement up."

rule: Long targets: obvious liquidity, or an FVG up in premium.
quote: "where would I want to be targeting? The obvious liquidity, this fair value gap up here in a premium."

rule: Missed first entry: re-enter long at an FVG in discount / OTE targeting equal highs.
quote: "Now we have equal highs, a fair value gap, and a discount, and OTE, targeting those equal highs, you can enter long"

rule: Frame the narrative with Asia and London price action plus the previous session.
quote: "Another way I frame my narrative is based off of London and Asia's price action, as well as previous action"

rule: London running highs into a bearish FVG creates the intermediate-term high; if it holds, bias is bearish toward resting lows.
quote: "We run highs, right, into this fair value gap, create our intermediate term high."

rule: Target trendline / resting liquidity, especially with large FVGs below.
quote: "We have trendline liquidity or just resting liquidity with large fair value gaps below. So you want to be targeting those lows."

rule: After lows are run and displacement up appears, flip bullish and look long.
quote: "Once we get some displacement to the upside, you want to look back long."

rule: Use the previous candle's high and low to frame either a draw on liquidity or a reversal.
quote: "the previous candle's high and low. This can be used to frame a draw on liquidity or a reversal."

rule: Unless price consolidates forever, it must reach for the previous candle's high or low; the side price is moving toward is the likelier draw.
quote: "unless price is going to consolidate in this range forever, it is going to have to reach for the previous candle's high or the previous candle's low."

rule: If price takes the previous candle's high but cannot displace / close above it, anticipate a move back into the range toward the previous candle's low (and the mirror for lows).
quote: "price cannot displace out of this range or above previous candles high. And then we can anticipate price falling back into the range"

rule: A close back inside after taking the previous low frames a reversal, or bias for the next candle to reach the previous high.
quote: "price reaches below the previous candle's low, however, cannot displace out of this range and closes back in."

rule: If a candle takes the previous extreme and closes outside it, look for continuation to the next previous-candle extreme in that direction.
quote: "We get a close over our previous candle, so I'd wanna see this previous candle's high."

rule: An inside bar gives no new direction; default to continuation of the current trend.
quote: "Here, we have an inside bar, so no direction. From here, I'd want to see just a continuation of this trend up"

rule: If a candle sweeps both sides of the previous range, hold no bias and let another candle play out.
quote: "we kinda swept everything in the range, and I don't really have a lot of bias here, so then I let another candle play out."

rule: Bias is not expected to always be right; it supplies a reliable draw on liquidity to be confirmed on lower timeframes.
quote: "I am just trying to find something that will give me a reliable draw on liquidity that I can confirm on the lower timeframes."

rule: The method works on 1h/30m/15m but gets noisier the lower the timeframe; 4H and daily are cleaner.
quote: "It just becomes a little bit more noisy as you go lower."

rule: When price becomes range-bound on a lower timeframe, mark the range high and range low and wait for price to reach one side.
quote: "Here I just mark out the range high and range low and then wait for price to reach one of those sides."

rule: A swing point that price fails to displace through (closes back inside) frames a reversal back into the range.
quote: "if we have a swing point where we fail to displace or close outside the range and come back in, this can be used to frame a reversal higher."

rule: Next candle (next day) model: when a candle fails to displace beyond a swing point, expect the next candle to move back into the range toward the next swing point.
quote: "when a candle fails to displace outside a swing point, we can anticipate price moving higher back into the range on the next candle."

rule: The next candle model also applies when price respects a PD array: expect the next candle to move toward the draw on liquidity.
quote: "when price respects a PD array, I can't [can] anticipate the next candle moving lower to our drawn [draw on] liquidity."

rule: A swing point that formed out of a fair value gap is a likely draw.
quote: "You notice this one came out of a fair value gap, we're likely to reach for this low."

rule: When a closure says one direction but a PD array (FVG / order block) sits in the way, treat it as conflict / indecision and look left before committing.
quote: "We don't close outside of here, so I'd want to say lower, but we do have a fair value gap right here."

rule: In an uptrend, a close below the swing point into a supporting order block is where to consider a next day model higher rather than continuation lower.
quote: "Although we are closing out, we're in an uptrend and now we're being supported by an order block."

rule: Top-down: take the previous 4H high as the draw, then on lower timeframes expect the bullish candle to form open-low-high-close (move down first, then up).
quote: "if we want to see price move higher, we want to see price move down first, right? So we get our open, low, high, close."

rule: Low-risk buy: an LTF order block with an FVG resting on it after displacement; partial at the nearby high, final target the HTF draw.
quote: "So if we wanted to take a low risk buy, we could look to enter right here, and we could partial on this"

rule: A disrespected bearish FVG (close over it) followed by a new bullish FVG gives the later entry.
quote: "this bearish fair value gap here is disrespected, we close over it."

rule: Buying below the HTF candle's open (discount of the candle) across multiple time ranges is ideal.
quote: "buying at a discount of multiple time ranges is ideal."

rule: The 4H candle's expansion often runs past the previous-candle draw before its high and close; distribution is expected up to the candle's close time.
quote: "I can expect distribution throughout this time period before a high and then a close, right?"

rule: Stop for an FVG entry goes at least below the mean threshold of the order block so a return to the order block does not stop you out.
quote: "I would at least need my stop on this low right here, below the mean threshold of this order block."

rule: He requires at least 2R personally; if the draw does not give 2R, the target must be set further.
quote: "I would not be able to put my target right at this high because I need at least two R personally."

rule: The concepts are fractal: used on the weekly the same way as on the 5-minute.
quote: "these concepts are fractal. If I was to use this on the weekly chart, I would use it the same way as I did on the 5-minute chart."

rule: Market structure is highs and lows: short-term, swing, and relative equal highs/lows.
quote: "It simply just comes down to highs and lows, short term highs and lows, swing highs and lows, relative equal highs and lows"

rule: Trends change when lower highs/lows give way to higher lows and higher highs.
quote: "you can see trends change when you get those higher lows and higher highs"

rule: Liquidity (stops) rests above and below highs and lows; once taken, you want price delivered in your bias direction.
quote: "once it is taken, you want to see it distributed higher or lower, something that matches your bias"

rule: In a downtrend, watch the highs for the market structure shift.
quote: "When you are trending down, you want to be looking at the highs for market structure shifts."

rule: A market structure shift is a lower high broken with displacement.
quote: "once you get into here, you can see that this is broken with displacement. So that will be your market structure shift."

rule: Displacement is an energetic move that breaks structure and must create a fair value gap.
quote: "For displacement to occur, you want to see a fair value gap created because that shows that price moved rather quickly through this area."

rule: A fair value gap is a break in price delivery over three candles: a gap between the candle 1 and candle 3 wicks.
quote: "Fair value gap is just a break in price delivery, right?"

rule: After the MSS, draw the FVG it created; that FVG is the entry.
quote: "We draw out your fair value gap and that's your entry."

rule: If one MSS/FVG entry is missed, later MSS + FVG in the same direction toward the target are valid re-entries.
quote: "Even if you miss this one, right?"

rule: Inducement model: run external liquidity, break structure, then run internal range liquidity before the move.
quote: "you run that liquidity, break structure, and you have some sort of internal range liquidity right here that is then ran before a move down."

rule: The 2022-model FVG entry itself induces traders in; their break-even stops are run before the real move.
quote: "People move their stops to break even. It runs those stops before the real move happens."

rule: Bullish version: sweep the low, high breaks structure, a low induces longs, that low is run before the move.
quote: "Put in a high breaking structure. Put in a low that induces people to go long, right? We then run this low."

rule: Label three parts: liquidity grab, break of structure, inducement.
quote: "where would our break of structure be? Right here. Our inducement? Right here. And our liquidity grab is right here."

rule: Prefer a fair value gap at the level where the inducement gets run.
quote: "I do like to see some sort of fair value gap in there."

rule: Longs taken at a FVG leave stops below; those stops are the inducement liquidity.
quote: "when we reach into here, people go long, put their stops below."

rule: After inducement and a displacement break of structure, the deviation from the range is where to look to go long.
quote: "Then you run, you deviate from this range here, right? So this is where you want to be looking to go long."

rule: Relative equal lows formed by the induced move are expected to be taken (in the short example, their stops are run into the FVG first).
quote: "we get a move down making equal lows. So you expect these to be taken, right?"

rule: The inducement is internal range liquidity that is run before the actual move.
quote: "really it's just internal liquidity in a range that is ran before the actual move."

rule: No reversal without a swing point: a reversal is always preceded by the formation of a swing high/low.
quote: "my fractal model relies on the foundational understanding that the market cannot reverse without a swing point"

rule: Use HTF candle closures to judge a likely reversal: a sweep of the previous candle's high then a close back inside its range makes him bearish (target previous-day low).
quote: "price has swept out its previous candle high and then closed back inside the range"

rule: Confirm the HTF bias by dropping one pair down (1D -> 1h) and requiring a CISD: a close through the series of up-close candles that made the high.
quote: "you can see we have closed through the series of up closed candles that have made this high"

rule: Once the CISD closes through, the high that made it is considered protected.
quote: "so I consider this High protected"

rule: After the HTF closure + CISD, trade the following HTF candle's open-high-low-close in the bias direction (for a bearish day: open, high, then lower, close).
quote: "and then I will look to trade the Open high low close in the following candle"

rule: Entry example: on the close of the LTF candle that closes through the down/up-close candle that made the sweep high, stop on the high, target 2R.
quote: "I could put on a position on the close of this candle my stop on the high and looking for 2 R"

rule: The T-spot is the zone inside the next HTF candle where he expects the HTF wick to form; for a short he wants price to trade into the gray box, form a high, then trade lower.
quote: "Mark out a t-spot which is an area that I look for higher time frame Wicks to be formed"

rule: After a bearish HTF close, look for continuation in the following candle (candle 4).
quote: "because we have closed bearish I will then look for a continuation in this following candle"

rule: The model is fractal: the same logic applies on any timeframe pair (1D-1h, 1h-5m, 15m-1m); in Automatic mode the indicator picks the pair from the chart timeframe.
quote: "since my model is fractal hence the name of the fractal model I can apply this on multiple time frames"

rule: Setting a bias (bullish/bearish) hides opposite-direction setups; neutral shows both.
quote: "if I don't have any bias or a neutral bias I can select neutral and it will show me both bearish and bullish setups"

rule: Validity colour code: gray C2 = setup stayed valid through candle 4; red C2 = failed in the first candle after; orange C2 = failed in the second candle after.
quote: "a gray C2 is when the setup has remained valid throughout candle 4 a red C2 is when that setup fails within the first candle"

rule: Time filters (kill zones, up to 3) are applied on whole HTF candles: to include the 8:00 hourly close you must start the filter at 7:00.
quote: "it's going to choose the whole hours candle so this means I would have to wait for the 9:00 a.m. closure"

rule: Time filters only apply at or below the "Apply below" timeframe; a filter set for 30m and below will hide setups on the hourly until adjusted.
quote: "this time filter will only apply on the 30 minute time frame or below for the this given Kill Zone"

rule: Projections (targets) are drawn from the series of bodies of the CISD; defaults are negative standard-deviation levels and custom ones can be appended comma-separated.
quote: "these are currently drawn from the bodies so the series of bodies in the change in the state of delivery"

rule: Formation liquidity marks the previous candle's / previous day's low (for a bearish closure) that has not yet been taken; already-taken lows are not marked.
quote: "I want to see price run out previous candle's lows or previous day's lows"

rule: Vertical open/close time lines separating each HTF candle's OHLC are "very important" to his analysis.
quote: "open close time is going to be those vertical lines which I find very important in my analysis"

rule: Overlap: run a second indicator copy on the lower pair so an HTF T-spot can be refined by an LTF (5m) T-spot; entry either directly with stop at invalidation or after a confirmation setup inside.
quote: "I could either just take an entry here with my stop on an invalidation or look for a confirmation setup"

rule: A counter-HTF LTF setup that prints inside an HTF setup tends to fail right away.
quote: "that did fail right away as it was opposing the higher time frame one"

rule: When price closes over the level you need to hold for continuation, the indicator turns it red and that close is the early warning the continuation is unlikely.
quote: "that closure right there over my level was the early warning that this setup was not likely to continue"

rule: A failed continuation from a bearish setup can itself create the opposite (bullish) candle-2 closure.
quote: "the continuation from this bearish setup has failed and that is what actually creates the bullish candle to closure"

rule: In a bullish setup, a close through the opposing (down-close) candles forms an order block he can enter in, stop on the low, target 2R; after the close over down-close candles he expects that low to hold.
quote: "that would be an order block I could look to take an entry in here my stop on this low and looking for 2 R"

rule: For continuation lower, price should hold / not close over the T-spot area.
quote: "I'd like to see price hold or not close over this t-spot area here"

rule: Consolidation into the session means expect a manipulation of one side before expansion, ideally into formation liquidity in line with projections.
quote: "with a consolidation I'd like to see a manipulation before we get expansion"

rule: A fair value gap is a three-candle pattern where candle 1 and candle 3 wicks do not overlap.
quote: "a fair value gap is a three candlestick pattern, which the first candle's low does not overlap with the third candle's high"

rule: An inversion is when a FVG (e.g. a SIBI) gets closed over / disrespected.
quote: "a SIBI or a bearish fair value gap gets closed over or disrespected."

rule: After an inversion, expect price to retrace into the old gap or just move higher (continue).
quote: "we can expect price to either retrace into this zone or just move higher."

rule: Consequent encroachment is 50% of the FVG (fib from its high to its low).
quote: "The consequent encroachment is a 0.5 or 50% of a fair value gap."

rule: Price respecting the CE -> expect continuation in the gap's direction; violating it -> expect the opposite move.
quote: "if price comes in and respects this area, then I anticipate it to move higher."

rule: For a bearish inversion, watch for a bullish FVG (BISI) to be closed below.
quote: "we want to see a busy or a bullish fair value gap get disrespected."

rule: After the close through, expect a reach back into the zone or continued selling toward the lows.
quote: "we can anticipate price to reach back into this area or continue to sell off to where? These lows down here."

rule: Entry options: market order on the close, or a retest of the inversion with the stop above an opposing candle; target the lows.
quote: "I can look to just market sell this, or I can look for a retest of this inversion, my stop above an opposing candle."

rule: After sweeping external liquidity and closing back inside, the framework flips toward internal liquidity.
quote: "while we sweep external liquidity. And what do we have resting right here? Internal liquidity."

rule: If the inversion entry gives only about 1R, refine the entry to the CE of the old gap.
quote: "that's about 1R, which does not meet my requirements for entry. So how can I adjust my entry?"

rule: When a retracement fails (sweep of highs but no close outside the range), treat it as consolidation and wait for manipulation / external range liquidity.
quote: "with consolidation, I'll be waiting for manipulation or I'm waiting for external range liquidity to be hit."

rule: A close over the CE is only a hint; the inversion requires a close over the whole SIBI.
quote: "we are closing over the consequent encroachment, which gives us a hint, but I want to see a close over the SIBI for it to become an inversion."

rule: On the return into the inversion, stop on the low; target the other side of the range for partials or full; want the CE respected.
quote: "I'll have my stop on this low, and then I'll be looking to target the other side of the range for partials or full take profit."

rule: A sweep then displacement over down-close candles validates an order block, which then supports price.
quote: "We sweep one more time before displacing over, validating this as an order block."

rule: In a trend, opposing FVGs that fail (get inverted) are entries into the trend.
quote: "if price is trending in one direction, those opposing PD arrays that fail are actually opportunities to get into that trend."

rule: In an uptrend, after a higher high, look for the higher low where a SIBI forms and is closed over.
quote: "So if we trade over this, we can anticipate price to retest it or at least go higher."

rule: Old FVGs from the sell side of the curve can support price on the buy side (reaccumulation), and vice versa (redistribution).
quote: "we can use old fair value gaps to look for reaccumulation or redistribution."

rule: Smart money reversal (gold example): close over the SIBI and over the down-close candles, then a short-term low.
quote: "I'd like to see a close over this SIBI and a close over these down close candles."

rule: Once price closes over an old sell-side FVG, it can use it as support to move higher.
quote: "when price closes over this fair value gap, it can then use it as support to move higher."

rule: Only two liquidity pools set the bias/draw: old highs and lows (external) and higher-timeframe (daily/weekly) FVGs (internal).
quote: "the only liquidity pools I use for my buyers [bias] are old highs and lows and then also higher time frame fair value gaps"

rule: Once a higher-timeframe bias exists, wait for daily order flow to confirm the draw on liquidity before acting on it.
quote: "If I have a certain bias, what I want to see is that the daily order flow is confirming the draw on liquidity."

rule: A daily close through equal highs (instead of a sweep that fails to close above) makes it likely price continues to the next higher draw.
quote: "price is closing above the equal highs, which is a really good sign"

rule: When price reaches the HTF objective (liquidity taken into opposing HTF PD arrays), bias becomes neutral and he takes no trades until price shows intent.
quote: "now that we trade into that level, at this point, my bias is neutral"

rule: He uses three daily profiles (expansion, retracement, consolidation); expansion is his favourite for intraday trades because delivery is one-sided.
quote: "i have three daily profiles i use the first one is the expansion profile my favorite profile to look for intraday trades"

rule: Always forecast both the direction and the profile of the next daily candle; look for intraday trades when bias and an expected expansion profile agree.
quote: "I'm pretty much always trying to anticipate what the next daily candle, what profile is the daily candle going to have"

rule: Expect a consolidation profile after price trades into a higher-timeframe level (e.g. takes a HTF high or low).
quote: "And when can we expect a consolidation profile? That's every time we trade into a higher timeframe level."

rule: Expect a consolidation profile after over-extension: several same-direction daily candles, the last ones large versus the average daily expansion.
quote: "the other criteria I use for a consolidation profile is if the previous daily candles have seen an overextension in price"

rule: Expect a consolidation profile when price trades at the EQ of a higher-timeframe range (premium/discount neutral point).
quote: "another criteria to expect a consolidation profile for me is if you are trading at the EQ of a higher timeframe range"

rule: After three consecutive daily candles close in the same direction, avoid trades in that direction on the fourth day (rule of thumb).
quote: "if we have three consecutive daily candles closing the same direction, I try to avoid taking trades in the same direction on the fourth day"

rule: After a large daily expansion, the next day is most likely a retracement against daily order flow or a consolidation; he does not trade it.
quote: "the next day is most likely going to be either a tradesman [retracement] profile against a daily order flow or a consolidation profile"

rule: Daily dealing range = last daily swing low to swing high; above its 0.5 is premium, below is discount.
quote: "So everything above the 0.5 level is the premium, and everything below is the discount, right?"

rule: Bullish order flow = bullish PD arrays respected and bearish PD arrays to the left disrespected into bullish inversions (mirror for bearish).
quote: "in the bullish autoflow [order flow], what you want to see is you want to see bullish PD arrays being respected"

rule: Daily order flow turns bearish when a daily candle closes below a bullish daily FVG; that FVG then becomes a bearish inversion level to sell from toward the next lower FVG / discount.
quote: "I will use this former bullish FVG as a bearish inversion level to look for sales [sells] into this lower FVG"
