rule: Re-evaluate after every daily close: which PD arrays formed, which were disrespected, and what that means for the next day or rest of week.
quote: "Again, every daily close, I check what PD arrays have been formed, what PD arrays have been disrespected"

rule: Use daily closes (open and close), never wicks, to determine bias; wicks only take liquidity from old highs/lows.
quote: "I always only used the daily candle closes to determine my bias. I never used the wicks."

rule: The overlap of a former bullish FVG (now inverted) and a new bearish FVG is a bearish BPR; if bearish, there must be no daily close back above it, and it is the HTF POI for intraday sells.
quote: "So the overlap of those two FVGs creates one bearish balanced price range."

rule: A bullish PD array should not be closed below its mean threshold and should react from its upper half; a bearish one should not close above MT and should reject from its lower half.
quote: "you don't want to see price too [to] close below the mean threshold"

rule: A high-probability order block is the last opposing candle that took liquidity before price closed through a recent swing (break of structure).
quote: "we have take liquidity, we have close below a recent swing low. So we have another high probability daily order block here."

rule: Execution: price trades into the HTF POI during a kill zone (London or New York), sweeps the opposing side, then a lower-timeframe change in order flow gives the entry.
quote: "and then I wait for a lower time frame change in order flow to get into a position."

rule: "Stuck order flow": price between a bullish PD array below and bearish PD arrays above will range until a daily close through one of them (that close is the trigger).
quote: "order flow is stuck between two PTAs [PD arrays], and as long as we are trading between those two PTAs [PD arrays], Price is most likely going to range"

rule: Never look for trades at the EQ of a range; in a range trade only at the extremes.
quote: "If we are trading in a range, as we have here now, I only want to trade at the extremes of the range."

rule: A large daily wick is a BPR on lower timeframes; for a short, refine it into H1 PD arrays in the wick's lower half.
quote: "to me, those large wicks are nothing but a balanced price range"

rule: Expect the day's largest expansion in the kill zone that carries high-impact news (PPI in New York in the example); he does not trade Asia.
quote: "if we see a large expansion to the downside, it's most likely going to happen during the New York kill zone"

rule: Invalidation: a close above the H1 BPR ends the short idea and returns him to a neutral bias.
quote: "If we would get a close above this level here, above the balance price range, I would not longer be interested in looking for sales [sells]"

rule: Around news, place the stop wider (at the EQ of the daily wick) instead of just beyond the H1 POI, because news can wick through.
quote: "I won't put my stop here because we might see a WIC [wick] once news come out so I will use a wider stop"

rule: Several unswept previous-day highs above price make a sell a low-probability environment (resting buy-side may be run first).
quote: "So for me, this would be a low probability environment to look for sales [sells], because we could also see a quick move above those highs here."

rule: Mondays usually form a consolidation or a retracement against daily order flow; always mark the Monday range.
quote: "Mondays usually tend to be either a consolidation profile or a retracement profile against the daily order flow"

rule: Bearish-week template: high of week forms early; price trades above Monday's high, then rejects to the Monday range lows and the HTF target.
quote: "I want to see price trading above Monday's high, and then I want to see a rejection back to the Monday range lows"

rule: For London he times entries on M15 or M5 and reads them exactly like the daily (dealing range, PD arrays, closes); add a position when the next opposing PD array is closed through, and move the first trade to breakeven then.
quote: "So for London I usually use the M15 or the M5 time frame to time my executions."

rule: Swing points determine where liquidity rests.
quote: "the first thing we need to understand is swing points in the market, because this is how we determine where liquidity is resting."

rule: A swing low is a low with a higher low to the left and a higher low to the right; mirror for a swing high.
quote: "we have a high with a lower high on the left and a lower high on the right that makes this a swing high."

rule: Traders who go long place stops at the swing low; shorts place stops at the swing high.
quote: "If someone was to get long in this area here they're likely to put their stop on this swing low."

rule: Sell stops below swing lows = sell-side liquidity; buy stops above swing highs = buy-side liquidity.
quote: "With the sell stops resting below here, we call this sell side liquidity, and with the buy stops resting above here, we call this buy side liquidity."

rule: Smart money pairs orders below lows and above highs.
quote: "Smart Money will look to pair orders below these lows and above these highs."

rule: Once a high is taken, that buy-side is no longer a concern; the next swing high becomes the buy-side.
quote: "price takes out this high. So now I'm not worried about buy side liquidity here."

rule: A swing that fails to take the previous low creates relatively equal lows, treated together as sell-side liquidity.
quote: "Those are now relatively equal lows. And so those are just sell side liquidity together."

rule: Focus on the really obvious highs and lows on the outside of the range.
quote: "I'm going to focus on the really obvious."

rule: Relatively equal highs/lows: two or more swing points very close together or clustered.
quote: "you have two different swing points that are relatively equal or very close together, forming relatively equal highs or lows"

rule: Old highs/lows: a previous high or low where a single swing point stands out.
quote: "These old highs and old lows just refer to a previous high or low where a single swing point stands out like that."

rule: Always mark the previous week's high and low: an easy draw on liquidity or reversal frame.
quote: "it's a pretty easy draw on liquidity for a way to frame a reversal."

rule: Always mark previous day high and low: frame a reversal or use as a draw.
quote: "previous day high and previous day low, I can either frame a reversal."

rule: Always mark session highs and lows (Asia, London); they frame a narrative, a draw or a reversal.
quote: "And these can be used to frame a narrative, a draw or a reversal as well."

rule: Unreached session levels above/below set the NY targets: NY takes London high, Asia high, then trades to London low.
quote: "we take that London session high, reach for midnight, we end up taking that Asia session high as well."

rule: After the session-high sweep and displacement down, a 5m FVG retest with no body closes inside is the setup.
quote: "We do have a five minute fair value gap here. And we reach back into it. A nice respect to that. No body closes even in the fair value gap."

rule: Equal lows from the London session are the target after the NY reversal.
quote: "we still have equal lows from London session sitting right there."

rule: NY can be framed off Asia and London session highs and lows.
quote: "using these liquidity levels, Asia high and low, London session high and low, New York can be framed off of that."

rule: When session highs and lows are already taken, the previous day high/low becomes the next draw.
quote: "we've already taken session highs and lows, but what do we have previous day high and low?"

rule: After a liquidity run on the daily, the opposite side of the range becomes the obvious target; once hit and back in a premium of the range, stop looking for longs.
quote: "after we ran this liquidity, it was obvious to target the other side, which we hit, right? So not really looking for longs anymore on this."

rule: Use premium/discount of the current range: deep in discount favours longs; near equilibrium (middle of the range) he has little bias and doesn't care for trades there.
quote: "We were down here, deep into a discount. Right here, we're pretty close to equilibrium."

rule: A weekly fair value gap can be found by combining daily candles into weekly ones, or by checking the weekly chart directly.
quote: "That would be your weekly fair value gap, just adding those candles to these ones. You can also go down and look at the weekly."

rule: Price continuously supported by down-close candles with non-aggressive pullbacks stays bullish until an aggressive move down appears; compare the speed of moves up vs down.
quote: "When price is continuously supported by down close candles, like it is here, still bullish on this until you want to see an aggressive move down, right?"

rule: No raid, no trade: an intraday setup needs a liquidity run first.
quote: "So liquidity run, right? That is No raid, no trade, right?"

rule: Intraday stack is 15m / 5m / 1m: liquidity run on the 15m, shift of structure with an FVG on the 5m, entry in an FVG (1m if needed); a lower-timeframe shift can still be a pullback on the 15m, and the higher-timeframe reason decides.
quote: "if you just sit on the 15-minute, wait for a run of liquidity, look for a five-minute shift in structure, and then look for an entry into that, that will be your easiest way to kind of trade that."

rule: When shorting, don't use an FVG that sits in a discount; drop to the 1m for an FVG in premium instead.
quote: "that fair value gap is in a Discount and you're looking to short, this is when I would go to the lower timeframes to look for a one-minute, right, fair value gap in there"

rule: Judge a structure shift by speed and distance covered (displacement); a move through structure without an energetic move is not a market structure shift.
quote: "that is no way a market structure shifted to the upside because there's no displacement, right? No energetic move above the market structure."

rule: Intraday session timing: at 8:30 look left for where liquidity rests (equal lows, lows, FVGs) to define targets.
quote: "So, 8.30, right? Look to the left of 8.30. Where is the liquidity resting?"

rule: If you miss the first entry, a re-break of structure with a big FVG gives a secondary entry at the 0.5 fib of that leg.
quote: "use a .5 fib of that, and there's a secondary entry."

rule: Confirmation entry: after liquidity is run, wait for a break/shift of structure, then enter in the upper half (premium) of the displacement range for a short.
quote: "looking at the displacement range, which is from here to here, and then finding some sort of setup in the upper half there, right?"

rule: You are technically invalidated only when the liquidity low behind the move is taken; choose between FVGs by the drawdown you accept and size down for the wider stop so account risk stays the same.
quote: "So if you're going to enter in these positions up here, you have to take a lighter position."

rule: Order block = last up-close candle (or its body) before a down move, where orders load; he mostly uses liquidity and imbalances and uses OBs to narrow an entry inside a larger imbalance or when a single OB precedes a large move.
quote: "I like to use them if there's a single order block and a large move up or a large move down."

rule: Scalping in a trend: go imbalance to imbalance, enter at 50% of the displacement range, risk the low of the imbalance, target the liquidity; after structure shifts, up-close candles should resist price.
quote: "While we still are targeting that liquidity, scalp the imbalance, risk the low of the imbalance."

rule: Daily bias comes from imbalances and liquidity; at minimum, mark out liquidity.
quote: "Looking at imbalances, liquidity, right? So if nothing else, just mark out your liquidity."

rule: SMT: correlated indices (ES/NQ) should make the same structure; when one breaks a short-term low and the other fails, it signals a potential reversal and the failing one is stronger. Look for it on the 15m.
quote: "But I personally like to look for them on the 15-minute timeframes. It's just the easiest to see, right?"

rule: Time matters more than price for entries: a valid confirmation at a bad time of day is still a poor entry.
quote: "It's time and price, not price and time."

rule: Price action is fractal: the same setup (liquidity run, displacement, FVG entry) appears on daily/4H/1H; traders who can't watch low timeframes can use those and set alerts at higher-timeframe POIs.
quote: "So like I'm using the 15-5-1. Why don't you use the day, 4-hour, an hour, right? Because setups appear on the hour, it's just they take longer to play out"

rule: A swing high is three candles: a high, a higher high, then a lower high (opposite for swing lows); a line chart shows structure simply.
quote: "You have one candle with a high right here, a higher high, and then a lower high on the next side to it."

rule: Inducement (IDM): equal lows (or a trendline) run inside the move before the entry FVG adds confidence to the entry.
quote: "Or actually, that's like perfect example of inducement. So that's your IDM. And then you have your fair value gap right here."

rule: Breaker = an order block price ran through and came back to; it then acts from the other side. He rarely uses breakers.
quote: "let's say you had an order block right here and price goes through it and then comes back. That's your breaker, right?"

rule: When ES and NQ both offer the setup, pick the one with the better risk-to-reward (here ES, because it retraced back up further).
quote: "ES made this retracement back up into here, so risk-to-reward-wise, it's just set up a lot better, right?"

rule: Be wary of early-week moves in a heavy news week (GDP, FOMC): they are probably accumulation for the news.
quote: "I know there's a bunch of news, GDP maybe, and FOMC and stuff, so be wary of that because it's probably just gonna, whatever move that is, accumulate for that."

rule: Read the weekly/daily for where price is reaching (liquidity) and keep targeting it until price turns bearish.
quote: "So going back down to a daily timeframe, that is what we should be targeting until we turn bearish or otherwise."

rule: With a bullish HTF read, don't step in front of it; prefer a retracement into a 4H/1H area before going long.
quote: "I don't know why you'd want to step in front of a train here. I would possibly like to see some sort of retracement into this area"

rule: Bias only gives the target; then trade the structure of your session (for New York, read what Asia and London did).
quote: "Bios only gets you so far, and then you can just look at the structure, depending on what sessions you play"

rule: Judge premium/discount by the 50% of the range; the read depends on which range you measure (premium of the small range, equilibrium of the whole range).
quote: "if you look at the 50% line, we're going to show in the premium of this range, but if you go out further, look at this whole range here, we're kind of right at equilibrium"

rule: An ES/NQ divergence where one index takes highs the other fails to take is a bearish warning against a bullish read.
quote: "So ES could not take those highs while NQ did take those highs. So that's one thing to be looking at."

rule: Weekly power of three: the week opens, drops to make its low (usually Monday, Tuesday or Wednesday morning), makes the high, then usually falls back into the range to close.
quote: "So you have your open, you drop down, right? Make your low of the week. Usually it's around Monday, Tuesday, or Morning session Wednesday. And then you go make your high, and then you normally fall back into the range"

rule: Use the 1-minute chart for entries.
quote: "I usually use a one-minute for entries."

rule: Whatever the bias, play the structure: at 8:30 find where liquidity rests and the points of interest, then look for lower-timeframe setups within them.
quote: "So look where 830 is at. Where's liquidity resting or points of interest? And then look for lower timeframe setups within that, right?"

rule: Inducement model: after liquidity is run and a breaker signals reversal, internal range liquidity builds and is run (stopping early entrants) before the real move.
quote: "You put in your internal range liquidity. So this is inducing people to go long. And then before the actual move, you run them out of their position, right?"

rule: A structure break is stronger when the breaking candle closes through with displacement; a weak break risks a quick stop-out.
quote: "It's kind of weak though, right? You would have preferred this second candle to close lower. Showing more displacement."

rule: Don't short in a discount; a counter-trend scalp should target an imbalance in discount or where the higher low is expected, or simply entry into discount if there is no clear target.
quote: "Well, there's no reason to short down here because you're in a discount, right?"

rule: Take profit off structure (FVGs, previous lows/candles, discount imbalances), not fib extensions.
quote: "So target, taking profit, I would base off of structure, right?"

rule: Order block: the down-close candle (or series) before an up move, or up-close before a down move; its high/low should support price.
quote: "So this is your down close candle before the move up, right? That's essentially to keep it simple. So if you mark out the high of that or low of it, this should support price, right?"

rule: Mark liquidity levels (equal highs/lows) on the 15-minute, not the 1-minute.
quote: "So what I would do is I'd recommend the 15-minute chart for liquidity levels and stuff like that, right?"

rule: When several highs/lows qualify as liquidity, prefer the most extreme one.
quote: "So you could mark it out as all three, but I like to use the more extremes most of the time."

rule: Long setup: sell-side is run into a higher-timeframe FVG/order block, a lower-timeframe structure shift follows, and he enters on the retracement into the FVG/breaker; no retracement, no trade.
quote: "And then a retracement down into this fair value gap, this little breaker to go long. Didn't happen, so I didn't trade it."

rule: Equal highs (and lows) are always a target.
quote: "So equal highs are always a target."

rule: Require the retracement to reach 0.5 of the displacement range; if it turns just short of 0.5, skip it.
quote: "This retraced to a 0.5, but it was just off the 0.5, right? So I didn't trade that."

rule: Compare ES and NQ: the same setup can be cleaner on one index (NQ retraced into discount and the FVG while ES did not).
quote: "You can see NQ was a little bit cleaner, in my opinion, just because I like the retracement, but ES was a little stronger."

rule: Risk on an eval: 4% per trade with 2R as the first scale-out.
quote: "So right now I'm doing 4% risk with 2R as my first scale."

rule: Don't look at lower timeframes until a higher-timeframe reason exists (e.g. price retracing into a 5-minute FVG).
quote: "So I would say for the most part, unless you have a higher timeframe reasoning to like be looking for a trade, don't look at lower timeframes, right?"

rule: If the first OTE entry is missed, a break in structure followed by a return to the FVG gives a second optimal entry.
quote: "And then if you miss that, you also have this break-in structure returned to a fair value gap, which is another optimal trade entry there."

rule: In the PM session, mark the morning and lunch liquidity and look for it to be run before the next move.
quote: "normally mark out your liquidity from the morning before lunch and during lunch and look for something of that nature to get ran before you go on."

rule: His model (ICT 2022 mentorship): at the open look for a run of liquidity or a higher-timeframe point of interest, a market structure shift on 5m/1m, then a retracement into discount (longs) or premium (shorts).
quote: "Basically the 2022 mentorship model. When we open up and just look for liquidity, run of liquidity or higher timeframe point of interest, market structure shift on five or one minute or timeframes in between, and then a retracement into a discount or premium."

rule: Take two to three good trades a day, or none.
quote: "good trades, you should, like, two to three, or none."

rule: If you missed the move and it did not retrace, don't chase it: there is no risk-to-reward left.
quote: "So once we, once I missed this morning move and saw it didn't retrace, I knew there's no risk or reward to long it up into here."

rule: Prefer FVGs in areas of liquidity over order blocks; an order block usually has an FVG above it, so entering the FVG lets the order block support price anyway.
quote: "I mostly just focus on fair value gaps in, like, areas of liquidity, right?"

rule: On the 1-minute, a single candle inside a big impulsive move can serve as a reference point (technique credited to Turbo, a third party).
quote: "when you have a big move up and then a single candle that is in there, you can use that as a point of reference."

rule: Breaker: an order block that price blows through instead of respecting; then look for a return to it.
quote: "Let's say instead of price kind of mitigating this right here, it just blew right through it. Then you would look for a return to it, if that makes sense."

rule: Timeframe stack: daily and hourly for bias, hourly for POIs, 15-minute for POIs and liquidity, 5-minute through 1-minute for entry once price reaches the area.
quote: "So I normally go daily and hourly, kind of just give me my idea for like bias, and I'll look for hourly for points of interest, right?"

rule: OTE: measure the displacement range; the reversal should come in discount below 0.5, with 0.62-0.79 the optimal trade entry zone; 0.5 is used for premium/discount on everything.
quote: "I use the 0.5 for everything if you watch my video on premium discount, but OTE is just displacement range, low to high, and your reversal should occur somewhere in a discount"

rule: Directional bias comes from HTF market structure (1H/15m): higher highs and higher lows after a smart money reversal mean bullish until the lows break with displacement.
quote: "So until these lows give with displacement, we're still bullish. That is how I determine bias. It's pretty simple."

rule: Bias only gets you so far; lower-timeframe market structure and execution are what make the trade.
quote: "bias gets you so far, but market structure and lower timeframe, like executions are really what do it, right?"

rule: Don't focus on determining bias; read market structure and don't let a bias stop you taking opportunities.
quote: "Just look at market structure and see what it tells you, right? Don't let bias take you away from opportunities."

rule: SMT divergence (one correlated index takes a high/low, the other fails to) only signals a possible reversal.
quote: "SMT just kind of gives you an indication that there could be a reversal. That's all it really does"

rule: With SMT, normally trade the weaker index, but in practice watch both and take whichever shows the cleaner setup.
quote: "watch both of them. See which one presents a better setup, right?"

rule: For an SMT long, entering the index that did not take the low gives clear invalidation if that low is taken.
quote: "I would just take ES because then you know you're invalidated if this low is taken again."

rule: Short only after the higher-timeframe POI (hourly imbalance) is reached and a lower-timeframe market structure shift with an energetic move prints; enter at the order block.
quote: "So if we got some sort of market structure shift to go lower, I was looking for that."

rule: A reversal needs an energetic (displacing) move; slow price action is not convincing.
quote: "This isn't very convincing price action of a reversal, right? We want to see an energetic move down"

rule: Use the FVG for the entry area and refine with an order block to its left when they line up.
quote: "we have this fair value gap here. And then I look to the left, I see this order block right here, which just kind of refines my entry"

rule: A high-probability order block has a fair value gap above (beyond) it, i.e. price displaced out of it.
quote: "that makes a high probability order block is when you have a fair value gap above it"

rule: Order block with a clean series of bodies: use the whole series and mostly its opening price; with a single candle use the full candle (or top to open).
quote: "If I see a clean series, I'll use all of them and I use the opening price mostly. If I use a single one, I usually use the full."

rule: A series of candles on a lower timeframe aggregates into one candle on a higher timeframe, which is why order blocks are series.
quote: "So it's like your series of candles on lower timeframe, are you going to add up to one candle in a higher timeframe?"

rule: Don't look for longs in premium; in discount look for the pullback/setup in the 0.62-0.79 OTE zone of the leg.
quote: "you don't want a long. When you're in a premium, so that's why don't look for longs up here. Once you get in a discount, you can be looking for longs"

rule: Setups inside a higher-timeframe FVG are valid without a liquidity grab, but you need a higher-timeframe reason to be long or short there.
quote: "It doesn't have to grab liquidity to work out, right? I just say higher timeframe reasoning as some sort of reason to be looking long or short."

rule: On a balance-type day target imbalances rather than the opposing highs/lows.
quote: "on a balance day, something like that, I target imbalances, so I wouldn't be targeting these highs here."

rule: Trade only the New York morning, about 8:30 to 11:00 EST; high-probability setups come down to time of day.
quote: "that's why I only trade the, like, 8.30 to, like, 11-ish time, because that's when I think the higher probability setups occur."

rule: 8:30 matters because the news embargo lifts and volatility enters.
quote: "It's when the news embargo lifts, so that's when the volatility comes in."

rule: For the afternoon, mark 13:00, find resting liquidity and imbalances, and look for the same run-then-lower-timeframe-setup as the morning.
quote: "the way I would do it is mark out $1,300 on your chart. And from there, look back, where is your liquidity resting?"

rule: Find one repeatable, scalable setup and only trade that.
quote: "If you can just do that single setup every time or whatever setup you choose every single time and only do that, it's going to work for you."

rule: With 2:1 reward to risk a 50% win rate is profitable.
quote: "if you trade with a 2 to 1 risk or reward, you can be 50% win rate and be profitable."

rule: Enter on 1m or even 15-second charts, rarely above 5m; recommend 5m/15m swing highs and lows for most traders, 1m only for low-risk entries at a point of interest.
quote: "If I'm looking and I have a point of interest, I'll use the 1-minute to try to catch a low-risk entry, but I would recommend for most people, 5-minute will definitely give you the best results"

rule: Structure trailing: when a swing low is taken you are bearish, when a swing high is taken you are bullish; on the 1m this gets choppy.
quote: "that takes it, now you're bearish, so then you go over here, low or high, right here, now you're bullish."

rule: Front-running before full displacement is possible with a tight stop, but the more convincing entry comes after the aggressive move, at OTE.
quote: "And if you're wrong, this is more convincing right here, this aggressive move down and then your OTE right there."

rule: Weekly plan as a projected path: retrace into the weekly/daily imbalance early in the week (Mon-Wed) to put in a low, then run the highs.
quote: "So I want to see some sort of move down into this area, Monday, Tuesday, possibly Monday, Wednesday morning, put in a low. Go run these highs."

rule: Market maker sell model: original consolidation, smart money reversal with SMT, and target the completion below the original consolidation's low.
quote: "This is your smart money reversal, second consolidation, consolidation, completion. If you know what the market maker sell model is"

rule: Mark higher-timeframe (15m and 1H) points of interest and liquidity first, then drop to a lower timeframe only when price reaches one.
quote: "I just mark out higher timeframes, points of interest, and then when I see something, I go to a lower time frame."

rule: Look for setups after liquidity is taken or after price moves into a fair value gap.
quote: "I look for setups after some liquidity is taken or I move into a fair value gap."

rule: He trades only 8:30-11:00 New York.
quote: "do I only trade between 830 and 11? And the answer for me is yes"

rule: Without a daily bias he still trades lower-timeframe market structure; a bias held against what the chart shows is useless.
quote: "Your bias does you no good if you hold on to it and don't do what the chart tells you."

rule: A liquidity run or higher-timeframe reasoning behind an FVG trade raises the win rate; win rate cannot be judged without the R:R targeted.
quote: "I would say some sort of liquidity run or higher timeframe reasoning will definitely give you a higher win rate and higher success."

rule: A break of structure only counts with displacement; without it, treat the move as a possible liquidity grab and watch whether it wicks out.
quote: "the way I kind of think of it is like a breaker structure, you got to have some sort of displacement, right?"

rule: [guest] A market structure shift needs both displacement and a candle close beyond the structure; a high taken barely and closed above without displacement is not one.
quote: "you want to see one displacement and two closing above or you know below some structure for a change in trend"

rule: [guest] A fair value gap in a move is itself evidence of displacement (energetic, rapid delivery).
quote: "fair value gaps themselves inherently indicate some energetic move"

rule: After a strong news-driven move up, a breakdown is more likely just a higher low; demand displacement down breaking structure before calling it a reversal.
quote: "but the thing about that is it's more than likely just going to put in a higher low, right?"

rule: [guest] On trend days or heavy-news days gauge trend on the 5-minute rather than the 1-minute.
quote: "using, like, the five-minute to kind of gauge trend is a lot better than the lower timeframes."

rule: Scalp entry: an order block with a fair value gap; enter in the FVG and expect a little trade into the order block, or wait for the reaction out and play it the other way.
quote: "Take your entry into the fair value gap, expect it to trade a little bit into the order block, or you kind of wait for the reaction out and then play it the other way."

rule: Order block = the last down-close candle before the move up (last up-close candle before the move down); it is not the same as the fair value gap.
quote: "This is our order block, is the last down close candle here before the move, or up close candle before the move's down."

rule: [guest] Order blocks are only expected to hold when price is working with the higher-timeframe bias.
quote: "they're really only, I guess, valid or should expect to be valid when your higher timeframe, when price is working with your higher timeframe bias."

rule: [guest] OTE is a 62%-79% retracement of a swing; an FVG inside the OTE of a leg gives a premium/discount entry in the direction of the higher-timeframe bias.
quote: "Optimal trade entry, which is defined as retracement between 62% and 79% from the low to the high, or vice versa."

rule: Do not trade the middle of a range: short in the upper (premium/OTE) part, long in the lower (discount) part.
quote: "So that's why you use your OTE and either, you know, look for trades up here in the range to go short or look for trades in this part of the range to go long, right?"

rule: Measure premium/discount on the higher-timeframe displacement leg (bodies or wicks) and look for longs in its OTE area, ideally at an FVG.
quote: "It's the same thing. You get a displacement leg up. Where would you want to look long? OTE area. There's a fair value gap right there."

rule: Liquidity rests at the obvious highs and lows where traders would put their stops.
quote: "Probably on this low, right? So that's where the liquidity is resting."

rule: [guest] Higher-timeframe highs and lows are the more significant liquidity.
quote: "higher timeframes are usually of higher significance, higher timeframe highs and lows."

rule: [guest?] Price runs premium to discount and back, getting there either by going to fair value gaps or by running liquidity (speaker unclear).
quote: "And the way you do that is you either go to fair value gaps or you run liquidity."

rule: Do not trade breakouts; when liquidity is run on one side, look for the trade the other way.
quote: "The whole point of ICT is kind of to do the opposite of a breakout."

rule: SMT: when correlated indices diverge at a high (one makes a higher high, the other a lower high), expect a reversal and short the weaker one.
quote: "And so I'd normally prefer to short the one that's weaker, right? So I would rather short ES here."

rule: After running pre-8:30 liquidity and getting a lower-timeframe setup, expect at least the nearest imbalance to be hit, or the opposite liquidity.
quote: "you expect to see at least an imbalance hit"

rule: Use a 15-5-1 timeframe stack, with 15- or 30-second charts for refined entries; it is fractal.
quote: "Like, I personally use the 15-5-1, and then I'll use like a 15-second, 30-second, depending on what price is doing."

rule: Very low timeframes refine entries but can make you lose sight of higher-timeframe structure.
quote: "So I would say 15 seconds can get you really refined entries, but also if you're too narrowed down on it, you can lose sight of what's actually going on."

rule: For a trend change, want structure shifts to domino 1m -> 5m -> 15m; with a 15-5-1 stack, ideally see the shift on the 5m (intermediate) without waiting so long that the low-risk entry is gone.
quote: "I kind of want to see them domino."

rule: [guest] Use three timeframes (high, intermediate, low; e.g. 15m/5m/1m for a scalper) and require the clearest structure change, with displacement and a close, on the intermediate one.
quote: "ideally, you want to see, I guess, the most confident structure changes on your intermediate timeframe at the least."

rule: [guest] Build bias from the 4H (daily gives little bias), then work the 15m (maybe 1H) as the highest timeframe of the day.
quote: "something like the 4-hour kind of gives me a better idea of what I think an ideal day would look like."

rule: Retracement vs reversal is decided by a structure shift with displacement (big energetic candles breaking structure).
quote: "And the difference between retracement and reversal comes down mostly to shifting structure with displacement, right?"

rule: Strat combination: a 1-2-2 reversal or a 2-2 after a liquidity run, hammers/shooters off highs and lows, always with higher-timeframe reasoning.
quote: "Yeah, I'd say 1-2-2 reversals or just 2-2 after running liquidity. Look for hammers and shooters off highs and lows."

rule: Stop: the short-term low/high beyond the entry or the candle that created the FVG.
quote: "Or short-term high above it where I'm entering, or the candle that made the fair value gap."

rule: After the higher-timeframe liquidity is run and structure breaks in your direction, the swept swing should hold, so a stop beyond it is reasonable.
quote: "once we break structure and continue up, and continuing up, this low should be held. We already ran the liquidity."

rule: [guest] Risk about 1% per trade, max three trades a day, at 2:1 R:R so a day is capped at -3%.
quote: "Just for my account, I usually risk like 1% per trade. And try to take three trades per day."

rule: Size positions on micros so every loss is a fixed dollar amount (his eval: 4% of drawdown, $100) whatever the stop distance.
quote: "So no matter what, if my loss is just around $100, I didn't have a loss."

rule: Trade index options off ES/NQ futures charts because futures carry the overnight structure.
quote: "just because it gives you all the overnight structure that you don't really have with SPY and QQQ charts"

rule: [guest] On sub-1-minute charts a volume spike at a stop hunt of a pivot, followed by a structure break and retrace, can mark a reversal entry; volume is not useful at 5 minutes and above.
quote: "if it takes out some swing low and then the volume comes in and then it breaks structure to the upside and retraces back down then that might be you know some sort of a long opportunity on a smaller time frame"

rule: Backtest/demo with no money before going live (he did about 1.5 months) and do not rush.
quote: "I would definitely say if you're just learning to not kind of rush it and just focus on actually learning."

rule: [guest] A sweep of obvious equal highs is not a short signal by itself; wait for lower-timeframe (hourly) signals of reversal.
quote: "I don't think moving over is technically a short signal."

rule: [guest] Bias comes from weekly bias and the market maker model narrative rather than a separate daily bias.
quote: "I don't really go about daily bias as much. Sometimes I like to look into weekly bias more"

rule: Without a bias model, use daily relative equal highs/lows and fair value gaps as the draws on liquidity.
quote: "just look for things like relative equal highs, fair value gaps, stuff like that, where price is likely to draw to."

rule: [guest] Market structure break = break of an intermediate-term swing point; market structure shift = intraday shift (e.g. 30m high broken after a low is taken).
quote: "Breaks are going to be something more significant, like a taking of an intermediate-term swing point."

rule: [guest] Premium arrays on the higher timeframe produce sell models; discount arrays produce buy models.
quote: "So premium arrays, higher timeframes are going to make sell models. Discount arrays are going to make buy models."

rule: [guest] Wait for price to reach the higher-timeframe point of interest, then look left and drop to the lower timeframe for the model.
quote: "I always say wait for the point of interest and then look left."

rule: [guest] A smart money reversal outside the kill zone is a valid but risky short; the safer play is to wait for distribution, the intermediate-term high and the silver bullet FVG.
quote: "So if you want to play a less risky game, also, it's not in your kill zone, you let it play out."

rule: [guest] A buy-side level already taken (high of day) makes a weaker point of interest.
quote: "But we already took buy side, so that's not going to be as ideal, but still something to note."

rule: [guest] Enter on the silver bullet fair value gap formed at the intermediate-term swing point, stop beyond that swing (a defended stop), partials at significant lows, target the sell-side liquidity.
quote: "Take it right when it goes in there. Stop above that price."

rule: [guest] Prefer the failed swing on the second leg of the market maker model over the first intermediate-term point.
quote: "So I have a preference for that second leg."

rule: [guest] A down-close candle before a run on buy-side liquidity becomes a bearish breaker once price breaks below it; opposite for bullish breakers.
quote: "Down close candles are going to be bearish breakers and the opposite stands true for bullish breakers."

rule: [guest] 15m is the lowest timeframe for higher-timeframe narrative; hourly to daily is the sweet spot even for day trades.
quote: "I think hourly to daily is your sweet spot for sure, even for day trades."

rule: If you cannot watch screens, sit on the 15m chart and only go to a lower timeframe once a point of interest is reached.
quote: "I would just sit like 15-minute chart. When you have a point of interest, then look at your phone and look to a lower timeframe."

rule: Host: take the first partial at nearby liquidity and move the stop to break even, or trail the stop under each new higher low on a 1m/2m chart.
quote: "And you can just trail market structure like that."

rule: [guest] Do not touch the stop until the first target is hit, even if structure shifts; then scale out and move to break even or slightly in profit.
quote: "If structure shifts, I'm not going to change my stop prior to when that first target's hit."

rule: [guest] When bearish, intermediate-term lows should break and intermediate-term highs should stay unviolated; intermediate-term swings form where price trades back into a fair value gap and moves away.
quote: "intermediate term swing points are going to occur when price trades back into a fair value gap."

rule: Do not enter a long at the high of the day/week without a prior run of liquidity; the risk to reward is poor.
quote: "You would want to see some sort of run of liquidity and then move higher before getting one."

rule: Risk a fixed dollar amount every trade and size contracts to the stop distance.
quote: "I did a 50k account and I risked $100 per trade every time, no matter what."

rule: [guest] All points of interest are roughly equal in value; context decides, and higher-timeframe POIs carry more significance.
quote: "Anything higher time frame is going to hold that higher significance."

rule: Host: with NQ making higher highs/lows while the Dow makes lower highs, trade the stronger NQ long on a lower timeframe after a break of structure up.
quote: "And so how I would have personally traded this is I would have went to the NASDAQ on a lower time frame here."

rule: Host: only use very low timeframes (15s) inside a higher-timeframe (5m/15m) point of interest, to reduce risk.
quote: "I'll have my 5-minute, 15-minute point of interest, and from there, then I will go down."

rule: Host: in a ranging market target fair value gaps or the discount of the range rather than the lows.
quote: "When we're rangy, I target a lot of the fair value gaps instead of the lows, right?"

rule: Practise without money (paper/demo) before trading live.
quote: "Definitely practice without money because that allows you to think logically and without emotions."

rule: [guest] First step of any MMXM: identify whether price is on the buy side or the sell side of the curve.
quote: "You want to be able to identify whether you are on the buy side or the sell side of the curve."

rule: [guest] Market Maker Sell Model sequence: original consolidation, push up to a premium array (PDH, HTF FVG, buyside liquidity), smart money reversal, market structure break with displacement, retrace into an OTE fair value gap, break of structure, second distribution leg to sellside liquidity/session lows.
quote: "once you have that market structure break or shift, you look for a retracement into a optimal trade entry, fair value gap"

rule: [guest] Only take shorts when price is above equilibrium (50% of the Fibonacci drawn over the retracement leg), i.e. in premium / OTE.
quote: "I don't take a short unless price is above equilibrium, which is above that is considered premium and below 50% is considered discount."

rule: [guest] The second distribution leg after the break of structure (his 'silver bullet') is the highest-probability entry.
quote: "you're waiting for that second leg of distribution, which is the silver bullet, AKA it's like the highest probability of trade entry."

rule: [guest] After the second entry, trail the first entry's stop into profit to where the second entry's stop is.
quote: "you can trail your first entry's stop loss and profit where the second entry's SL is."

rule: [guest] Original consolidation is often the Asia session range / previous daily low chop (accumulation, relative equal lows or highs).
quote: "previous daily lows and Asia's lows are in a form of chop and consolidation. Like this, we're accumulating price."

rule: [guest] A smart money reversal is only confirmed by the reaction after liquidity is taken (swing lows broken with displacement), and entries should fall within kill zone times.
quote: "You have to consider kill zone times."

rule: Liquidity = the most obvious highs and lows: PDH/PDL, relative equal highs/lows, double tops/bottoms, session and weekly highs/lows, retail support/resistance; don't overthink it.
quote: "It's just kind of, what's the most obvious? Try not to overthink it."

rule: [guest] The model is fractal: it appears on 1m up to daily.
quote: "This same model can be happening on a 1-minute chart, a 2-minute, like a 30-minute, an hourly, a daily."

rule: [guest] On weekly/daily/4H models expect the buy side of the curve to offer two entries before the premium array; on lower timeframes usually one.
quote: "if you are in a higher timeframe, expect like a buy side of the curve to present two opportunities before reaching its premium array."

rule: [guest] After a break of structure, wait for a retrace into equilibrium before selling rather than selling the extension.
quote: "I want to see price retrace into some sort of equilibrium, maybe, who knows, here."

rule: Below both the midnight and 8:30 opens is deep discount (look for buys); above both is deep premium (look for sells / a retrace down).
quote: "If price is above Is above the 830 Open and Midnight Open, you're in a deep premium."

rule: Prefer fair value gaps over order blocks for entries on indices; a breaker can narrow down an oversized FVG.
quote: "sometimes if I have a larger fair value gap, I'll look for some sort of breaker, something like that to narrow it down."

rule: Risk the same fixed amount (around 1%) on every trade and stop when wrong.
quote: "I try to risk the exact same amount in every trade."

rule: [guest] No market structure break after the liquidity run = no sell; price is still on the buy side of the curve.
quote: "So I need a market structure break or a shift."

rule: [guest] Take the first partial at 2R, then move the stop to break-even and leave about 20% for the final target.
quote: "Pretty much move my stop loss to break even and then just leave like 20% on the table for continuation to hit the final TP."

rule: A structure break needs displacement that leaves a fair value gap; a small wick below a low followed by an aggressive move back is a liquidity grab, not a break.
quote: "The displacement has to have, has to create a fair value gap."

rule: Power of three intraday: for longs, the drop below the midnight/8:30 opens is the manipulation to buy before the expansion.
quote: "So that's where you'd want to be eyeing entry, and then you get your range expansion move up to distribute price"

rule: Use SMT between indices: short the weaker index (NQ barely tapped the highs ES ran).
quote: "NASDAQ barely tapped into these highs here. So that's what I was looking to go short on."

rule: No reason to be bullish until structure breaks to the upside; judge direction by which moves are more aggressive (displacement).
quote: "There's no reason to be bullish until we break structure to the upside."

rule: If the high you expect to be protected is taken, the idea is invalidated.
quote: "So then I expected this high to be protected. And then if this got taken, my idea was invalidated."

rule: A market structure shift shows strong FVG candles; moves with only wicks and no FVGs lack aggression and are not a shift.
quote: "No fair value gaps, no aggression."

rule: Weekly power of three for a bearish week: early-week (Mon/Tue) high, then Wed-Fri distribution down (open-high-low-close weekly candle).
quote: "I'd want something like a candle, whatever Monday, a candle to be put in Tuesday, or like a high, and then to continue lower."

rule: Don't be fixed in bias; follow where the displacement is.
quote: "I'm not super biased. I just look at where the displacement is."

rule: [guest] Journal every trade including how you felt and your confluence; compare confident vs skeptical trades.
quote: "I think that's very important to note down how you felt during a trade"

rule: [guest] Cap the daily loss and aim for one trade per session.
quote: "I typically shoot for one trade per session"

rule: Daily bias: where liquidity rests, what has been taken, then displacement and FVGs toward the higher-timeframe draw.
quote: "Basically, you just want to look at where liquidity is resting, what liquidity we've taken"

rule: You need a higher-timeframe narrative (bias) to stop finding setups in both directions; on the sell side of the curve look for shorts, not longs.
quote: "You've got to have higher timeframe narrative."

rule: A counter-trend long is only taken to get a retracement into premium for an optimal entry in the direction of the higher-timeframe bias.
quote: "The reason to be looking for longs in here was because we wanted a retracement after these down days to get an optimal trade short"

rule: Don't skip around timeframes; when day trading use the 15m (and 1h) for points of interest.
quote: "don't skip around too many time frames, focus on, like, 15-minute, stuff like that if you're day trading"

rule: If daily bias is uncertain, trade without one and follow structure (market structure break with displacement).
quote: "I mean, you don't have to have a bias. If your bias is wrong, you should still be okay just focusing on the model."

rule: Only the entry has to form inside the kill zone (8:30-11:00 NY); the stop raid can happen before it, typically London sweeping lows and New York delivering the setup.
quote: "I just focus for my entry to form during a kill zone, right? So a lot of times London will take the Lowe's break structure up."

rule: Repeated ES pattern: London sweeps the lows, structure breaks up, an FVG forms and internal range liquidity is run around 9:30, then price moves up.
quote: "London takes Lowe's here, break structure up, have a fair value gap here, right? Also runs that internal liquidity."

rule: Kill zones are 8:30-11:00 AM EST and 1:30 PM to the close; lunch is optional.
quote: "if you focus on the kill zones, 8.30 a.m., 2.11 EST, and then like 1.30 to close, those would be the kill zones"

rule: Order blocks only work with a narrative; which side of the market-maker curve you are on decides which order blocks matter.
quote: "If you don't have any narrative to it, like it probably won't work, right?"

rule: The order block level is normally the open of the candle; when choosing among candles, use the larger, fuller one.
quote: "For the most part, I use the open and then the wick, but normally just the open for the candle."

rule: Order blocks are a secondary filter: take FVG trades supported by an order block; the main POI is a liquidity run with an aggressive move back, or an FVG.
quote: "I would rather take a fair value gap trade that is supported by an order block, right?"

rule: Bias flips on liquidity: he was bullish wanting a retracement until the equal lows were taken, then bearish.
quote: "I was bullish until these were taken. Once these were taken, bearish."

rule: OTE is measured from the wicks, not the bodies.
quote: "For OTE, do you use body or WIC? I use WIC."

rule: Inducement entry: after lows are run and structure breaks up with an aggressive move, wait for the retracement into the discount of the range that runs internal stops into the OTE and FVG; enter long there, first target the (equal) highs.
quote: "So runs those stops, goes into our OTE, into this fair value gap, fills it. That's your long entry, right? First target, those highs."

rule: Re-anchor the dealing range (fib) to the new high once the old high is taken.
quote: "you would move it up once the range got hit"

rule: Lower-timeframe confirmation entry: only at a POI, drop to 5m / 1m / 15-second for an aggressive move that breaks structure, then enter on a retracement that runs a short-term low.
quote: "I'll just look for an aggressive move up, breaking structure on the lower timeframes, right?"

rule: In the premium of a higher-timeframe range after a liquidity run into an FVG, target discount arrays.
quote: "when you are in a premium up here, you want to target discount arrays"

rule: Weekly power of three: in a bullish week the low should be in by Monday, Tuesday or Wednesday morning (often Tuesday): open, manipulation down, expansion up, close near the highs.
quote: "If you want a bullish week, you want the low put in on a Monday, Tuesday, or Wednesday morning, right?"

rule: He plans only for where price is likely to draw tomorrow / the next couple of days, not the coming month.
quote: "I just care about where we're going tomorrow."

rule: Win rate is meaningless without risk-to-reward and consistent position sizing.
quote: "Win rate doesn't mean anything unless you combine it with, um, your risk to reward. And position sizing, right?"

rule: Usual risk-to-reward is over 2R, moving the stop to break-even at 2R (speaker not certain).
quote: "my usual wrist reward ratio is over 2R. That's where I try to, I go break even at 2R."

rule: Avoid joining a big run late; if you are already green and it feels like chasing, stop trading.
quote: "I don't want to be involved after I already because I feel like I'm chasing even though you know there were entries"

rule: [guest] Use ICT concepts for the overall trade idea and location, then footprint and DOM to time the entry inside the area.
quote: "ICT and the concepts from ICT I would more use as the overarching concepts for Like trades that I'm looking at."

rule: [guest] At the area, enter only when the tape/footprint shows speed picking up or aggressive buying; selling hard with nothing on the tape is a reason not to enter.
quote: "if we're just selling down super hard and the tape shows nothing or no reason to enter, it can be a good deterrent"

rule: [guest] Target equal highs/lows for liquidity and use balance-area levels and volume profile to get entries, instead of precise Fibonacci OTE.
quote: "I don't completely use like Fibonacci and OTE, but a lot of times I'll kind of eyeball it and use volume profile or market profile where I see a level in that fair value gap."

rule: [guest] When price re-enters a balance area (range), target the point of control first and the far edge of the balance area next.
quote: "once we re-enter into that range ... you're going to want to target the point of control"

rule: [guest] Use delta like RSI divergence, but not when the divergence spans too much time; for reversals watch tape speed.
quote: "you don't want to use it if the divergence is too far distant in time"

rule: [guest] Volume-profile ledges are absorption areas: a bounce level, or a pivot if broken because the absorbers get liquidated.
quote: "these ledges where we have a straight-out protrusion of volume is usually an area of absorption"

rule: [guest] Every fair value gap is a low-volume node.
quote: "every fair value gap is really just going to be a low volume node"

rule: [guest] Resting limit orders on the ES DOM matter little because they can be pulled; market activity matters.
quote: "The limit orders and the level two on ES is usually not that important because people can just pull these orders."

rule: [guest] Stop trading right after high-impact news if it is not your type of price action, to avoid FOMO.
quote: "I actually stopped trading right after the news just because it's not my type of price action I love and I knew I was going to feel FOMO"

rule: [guest] Too many concepts cause analysis paralysis; narrow down the setups.
quote: "you need to narrow down the setups"

rule: A higher-timeframe point of interest is required when using very low timeframe (15-second) entries, otherwise you get lost.
quote: "But it's just important you have a higher timeframe point of interest or else you'll kind of get lost."

rule: He trades the 1H and the 15m/5m/1m; ideally structure breaks domino from 1m to 5m to 15m.
quote: "So you wanna see the one minute break structure that leads to a five minute break of structure that leads to a 15 minute break of structure, et cetera."

rule: Use the 15m for the point of interest (liquidity, FVGs, PD arrays) and only look at lower timeframes once price is in it.
quote: "I like to focus on our 15 minute for my point of interest."

rule: Entry criteria: a higher-timeframe liquidity run (a high or low taken), then a 1m confirmation setup to reduce risk.
quote: "I look for a liquidity run, so some sort of higher timeframe. Reason to get short."

rule: Some liquidity level (buy-side or sell-side) must be taken before a trade.
quote: "Yeah, one or the other, or at least some sort of liquidity level."

rule: Before the open, mark points of interest and higher-timeframe liquidity levels: 15m/hourly, Asia, the 8:30 mark, obvious levels to the left, then hourly/daily.
quote: "what I do before my morning is just mark out points of interest and higher timeframe liquidity levels."

rule: Separate a liquidity grab from real displacement with higher-timeframe context: the 5m/15m stays bullish until its intermediate-term low is taken.
quote: "we're still bullish unless this intermediate term low right here is taken."

rule: With large liquidity voids on the hourly, watch the 5m or 1m for setups in the OTE area.
quote: "It's just when I have large areas, large liquidity voids like that, I'll use lower timeframes."

rule: [guest] Use high-timeframe POIs (hourly, daily, weekly, monthly) and drop to 1m or 15-second charts for more precise, lower-risk entries.
quote: "I got into the lower timeframes and ICT in general just as a way to figure out how to get better, more precise entries."

rule: [guest] Premium/discount is measured at the 50% of the larger displacement leg; a weekly FVG above that 50% is a premium POI for shorts.
quote: "So we had the weekly fair value gap in premium above that 50% mark of this larger impulse down."

rule: [guest] Reversal setup: run above previous highs, then rejection with displacement below the previous low (market structure shift), in line with the higher-timeframe bias.
quote: "it's going to be a run above the previous highs and then a rejection with displacement below that previous low to shift us back into going lower lows and lower highs"

rule: [guest] An intermediate-term low is a low that filled a fair value gap (or sits between two short-term lows); a structure shift needs displacement below it.
quote: "And it's intermediate because it filled that fair value gap, right?"

rule: [guest] Enter at the midpoint (preferred) or edge of the 1m FVG left by the displacement.
quote: "You can either short the bottom of the fair value gap or the midpoint of it. Ideally, I'm trying to go for the midpoint more often than not."

rule: [guest] The stop goes above the high left by the displacement, which should not be retaken; that is the widest risk he takes.
quote: "that's going to be the widest risk that I would attempt to put on for my position."

rule: [guest] T1 is the first lower low: take about 20% off and move the stop to breakeven; runners go to the higher-timeframe target (T2).
quote: "So if this is my T1, my T1 is where I'm gonna move stops breakeven."

rule: [guest] Size positions by stop distance (e.g. 10-point risk = 2 ES, 3.5-4 point risk = 4 ES).
quote: "You should be sizing based on your stop loss."

rule: [guest] With 1:10 targets a very low win rate is acceptable; one winner covers many losers.
quote: "Since your risk reward is so, so, so high, your win rate can be Extremely small"

rule: [guest] Weekly power of three / outside bar: after taking last week's high and rejecting, target last week's low.
quote: "So with that, I want to be targeting last week's lows for the power of three."

rule: [guest] If price reaches into the targeted FVG with no displacement or structure break against you, the trend is strong; hold for the lower-timeframe relative equal lows and last week's lows.
quote: "we know it's a really strong trend and we know we can pretty much hold confidently looking for your relative equal lows on the lower timeframe taken out"

rule: [guest] The same model works on yearly/monthly candles with the daily as the entry timeframe.
quote: "That can be traded the exact same way, but instead of using a one-minute time frame, you can use like a daily or something as your one-minute or entry time frame."

rule: [guest] Afternoon session tends to run the highs and continue in the morning's direction after a strong morning trend.
quote: "Afternoon runs highs and then continues in the direction if we have a strong morning trend"

rule: [guest] Volume spikes on the 15-second (or when price moves lower on any timeframe) show large resting orders / demand; context, not an instant reversal signal.
quote: "volume spikes will tell you where there's big resting orders."

rule: [guest] Strat monthly continuity: once a new month starts printing green, don't short against it for a large move; an inside bar is a consolidation.
quote: "the second this one starts coming green, I don't want to be shorting that one"

rule: [guest] A consolidation is a candle inside the previous timeframe candle's high and low.
quote: "And this is defined as a consolidation because it's inside of that previous time frame's highs and lows, which is the definition of a consolidation."

rule: [guest] Previous candles' highs (lows) are pivot targets once a consolidation breaks.
quote: "With the strat, we use previous candle's highs as our pivot target"

rule: [guest] Daily bias: mark relative equal highs and lows; on NFP-type news expect both sides taken; wait for the Judas swing off the open and an aggressive break of structure with closes and an FVG, often around 10:00.
quote: "I want to look for where the relative equal highs are and where the relative equal lows are."

rule: [guest] He normally does not trade afternoon reversals.
quote: "If it comes in the afternoon, normally I don't really trade it, but this one we did."

rule: [guest] A bullish shift needs displacement above the intermediate high, with an FVG on the leg that takes it and closes above it.
quote: "So we know that we want to see this high get displacement above it with a fair value gap on the price leg that were to take it out."

rule: [guest] OTE is drawn on wicks (highs and lows), not bodies; round 'bank levels' can be used.
quote: "on the OTE, I don't really use the bodies. I use the lows and the highs"

rule: [guest] Bias should be dynamic and change during the day as price gives information; don't hold a fixed morning bias.
quote: "Your bias doesn't have to be set in stone in the morning."

rule: [guest] Strat 15m reversal entry: buy the break of the previous candle's high, stop at its low or midpoint.
quote: "trading the break of that previous candle's high and then using either the low of it or like the midpoint of that candle and targeting the exact same area"

rule: [guest] For a very large FVG use its 50% as the POI, or trade the structure (breaker/FVG) inside it, or don't trade inside it at all.
quote: "which when you have a really big one, you totally can use like the 50% mark of it."

rule: [guest] In a range, wait for displacement through the lows (not just a liquidity run) before shorting; then the setup (breaker/FVG) defines entry.
quote: "You want to wait for that displacement and then you don't have to guess where this high ends up."

rule: [guest] A trend has changed when lows are run through with many closes below and no reaction (not a one-candle sweep); after that, use FVGs only as targets.
quote: "you're getting ran through and getting tons of closes below and there's no reactions, right?"

rule: [guest] When a market maker buy model reverses, target the lows of the consolidations that built the move (resting stops), not the inefficiencies.
quote: "We know we're actually targeting the lows and the stop losses left behind, right?"

rule: [guest] 0DTE options: choose a strike that is in the money before the target, pay less than half the intrinsic value at target, take 50% off at +100% and let the rest run.
quote: "The furthest you wanna go is wherever you're gonna be in the money."

rule: [guest] If you miss a strong trend-day open, walk away rather than chase (especially with options).
quote: "So what I would heavily suggest is just walking away."

rule: [guest] Box setup: consolidation, run below its lows, FVGs, retest under the lows, structure shift, then target the highs.
quote: "I just look for the consolidation, run below the lows, and I want to see fair value gaps, retest under the lows, and shifts of structure to take it higher."

rule: [guest] A big initial consolidation, a break and close beyond it, then a small secondary consolidation tends to launch the move (breakout trade); he rarely takes it.
quote: "Breaks above and closing above those highs and really small secondary consolidation that will send it"

rule: [guest] Sizing up depends on full confidence in the strategy, built from small stops and repeated precise entries.
quote: "Adding size, it all comes down to like very much trusting your strategy."

rule: [guest] The market is fractal: the same market-maker buy/sell model (consolidation, legs, SMR, distribution) appears inside a single leg of the higher-timeframe model.
quote: "the market is fractal, so what you see on one time frame, If you drop down to a smaller time frame, you will see the same price occurrences within that model."

rule: [guest] Separate the sponsorship timeframe (where the idea and target come from) from the execution timeframe; find a low-timeframe model inside the high-timeframe model.
quote: "So the first model is the sponsorship. The second model is your execution."

rule: [guest] The sponsoring timeframe sets the target: weekly sponsorship means weekly targets.
quote: "If the weekly is sponsoring this move, weekly sponsorship means weekly target."

rule: [guest] Zooming into the HTF point of interest for a lower-timeframe entry gives the same target with a far smaller stop: higher R and less time in the market.
quote: "Being able to identify points of interest on a higher timeframe and then recreate that model as you get deeper into price will not only allow you much higher R trades"

rule: [guest] An FVG is invalidated by candle closes beyond its defending side; wicks into it and revisits of a partly filled FVG are acceptable.
quote: "So I'm looking for the top of this box. I'm looking for no candle closures above that"

rule: [guest] Stop goes at the swing high/low where the move originated (the shift); an outlying wick high can be used as a more conservative stop.
quote: "So this is the swing high where the move is originating from."

rule: [guest] Don't place the stop at a swing that was just raided; use the next valid swing.
quote: "Because we can't use this one because we just raided this one."

rule: [guest] Unmitigated FVGs (open gaps) are targets because price seeks to rebalance inefficient delivery.
quote: "Fair value gaps are places where price wasn't offered efficiently. Price is going to seek rebalancing that before, you know, leaving."

rule: [guest] Price works through the PD array matrix from one extreme to the other; take targets in order (FVG fill, order block, liquidity pool).
quote: "Price is going to work from one extreme to the other. And in the process, it's going to go through the ladder of PD arrays."

rule: [guest] Use only the PD arrays you see clearly and have journaled data for; don't use every ICT tool.
quote: "You don't need to use everything in ICT's arsenal."

rule: [guest] A breaker is a flipped order block formed after a new swing high/low; a mitigation block lacks the new swing.
quote: "A breaker block creates a new high."

rule: [guest] A 1:1 fixed R needs >50% win rate to break even; he prefers 3R-3.5R and tests R choices on 20-50 logged trades.
quote: "So if you have a sub-50% win rate, it's mathematically impossible to be profitable with a one-to-one R2R system."

rule: [guest] Journal every trade with before/after screenshots and the mechanics present (liquidity taken, MSS, FVG in premium/discount, OTE); it builds confidence to hold and to enter.
quote: "take before and after screenshots of all your trades, log them"

rule: [guest] Define the dealing range from the swing where sell side and buy side were taken; enter in the correct side of equilibrium (premium for shorts, discount for longs).
quote: "Where did we come back above equilibrium? Here. Is this tradable? Yes. Inside your FEG."

rule: [guest] On the execution timeframe, wait for a secondary shift in market structure after liquidity is taken, then enter at the FVG/equilibrium of the new dealing range.
quote: "we've created a secondary shift in market structure after taking sell-side liquidity. So this becomes our dealing range once we have a confirmed swing high in."

rule: [guest] A shift with displacement and FVG can still be a stop run; only the daily bias / draw on liquidity tells you which it is.
quote: "But you're not going to be able to differentiate a stop run against real direction until you learn how to figure your daily bias."

rule: [guest] DXY is the barometer: no index or major longs against a strong dollar; if the dollar disagrees, skip the trade.
quote: "so the dollar is the barometer to everything I do if the dollar disagrees I don't take it"

rule: [guest] SMT (SPY vs NAS, DXY vs majors) is secondary confluence only, never leading.
quote: "Secondary confluence for me."

rule: [guest] Start each week on the weekly chart for the weekly draw, and look for the opposite-side PD arrays that can be raided first (PO3 / market maker buy model).
quote: "Primarily, I always start my week. I always look at the weekly. Because I'm looking at my weekly draw."

rule: [guest] Use 4H/1H PD arrays for the daily bias and daily/4H PD arrays for the weekly bias.
quote: "And I'm looking for PD arrays in the 4-hour, the 1-hour for the daily, and the daily and the 4-hour for the weekly."

rule: [guest] An impulse that never retraced to equilibrium before extending marks the extension as a stop hunt; price always oscillates external to internal liquidity on all timeframes.
quote: "Price for this impulse never came back to equilibrium. So for me, this is a stop hunt."

rule: [guest] You are trading inside every higher-timeframe candle at once; use that to pick direction in a trending market.
quote: "even if you're trading on the 5-minute, you're still trading on the 15-minute, 30-minute, 1-hour, daily, weekly, you're still trading inside that candle."

rule: [guest] Trade only kill zones; it is fine to skip sessions and take 1-2 trades a week.
quote: "You don't need to catch every swing. You don't need to trade every session."

rule: [guest] Real liquidity targets come from the daily and higher timeframes because institutions operate there; lower timeframes show how price delivers to them.
quote: "But the real targets, and this is words of ICT, says they come from the daily and higher"

rule: [guest] Win rate excludes break-evens (he scales in and trails); don't confuse win rate with strike rate.
quote: "So even though if I can say 60% of my Trades aren't losers, which is what win rate is, that doesn't mean I'm hitting my take profit 60% of the time."

rule: [guest] Balanced price ranges (filled FVGs revisited) are more sensitive than plain FVGs.
quote: "But I like BPRs because they tend to be more sensitive than fair value gaps"

rule: Use the 1H and 4H charts as the daily-bias charts; while the intermediate-term high holds, stay bearish.
quote: "So like my daily bias, I normally use my hour and 4-hour as my daily bias charts, right? So when I saw this, Get put in, right? This is your intermediate term high. As long as that's not broken, we're still bearish, right?"

rule: The daily draw can be just an obvious 1H swing low (3693.25 today).
quote: "all it is is this low. That's all that was."

rule: OTE (0.62-0.79) is only a zone to look for an imbalance (FVG/order block); the exact fib level does not matter.
quote: "normally I just use OTE to find some sort of imbalance in that region"

rule: Only take shorts from premium/OTE, not from the lower end of the range, because OTE inherently gives better risk-to-reward.
quote: "OTE just gives you better risk to reward, like inherent, like it just gives you better risk to reward no matter what, because you're not looking for trades in the lower end of a range"

rule: Lower-timeframe model on every timeframe: run of the highs (preferred, not required), break of the low with displacement, then enter at the obvious imbalance (FVG midpoint or breaker), stop on the high, target the lows/internal liquidity.
quote: "this is about what I look for on every timeframe, right? So we want this, Liquidity run of the highs, even on the lower timeframes. It doesn't have to happen, but I prefer it."

rule: A break of structure without displacement does not count; lack of displacement over highs is the cue the move is just a liquidity grab and the trend continues.
quote: "However, there's no displacement over these highs. And that is what kind of gave you the cue that we're going to continue short."

rule: Inducement model: internal range liquidity is run (e.g. by a news pop into a FVG) to form the intermediate-term high; that is where to get short.
quote: "News comes out, pops that high into a fair value gap, puts in your intermediate term high. That's where you want to get short."

rule: Entering on a lower timeframe gives a tighter stop and better R:R for the same target (2.5R vs 1.6R in his example).
quote: "For targeting the same thing, 1.6 risk to reward versus 2.5, right?"

rule: Counter-trend scalps need a lower-timeframe setup in the other direction (break of structure) first; without it there is no reason to go long.
quote: "And there's no reason to go long yet, right? Because you want to wait for that break the structure, which you had none of."

rule: Use breakers only when they are obvious and line up with a fair value gap; otherwise use a lower-timeframe confirmation entry in OTE.
quote: "the only time I really use them is when they're super obvious within a fair value gap"

rule: While trending down, up-close candles (like mitigation blocks) should resist price and give second entries.
quote: "Really, when you're trending, right, or moving down, all these up-close candles, sweet, all these up-close candles should resist price, ultimately, right?"

rule: If you miss the move, stay out rather than chase.
quote: "So usually if I miss something like that, I just stay out of it"

rule: During volatility (news/FOMC) drop to the 15s/5s chart and take low-risk pullbacks rather than market orders.

rule: A previous daily high taken and then closed back inside the range (failure swing) gives a bearish bias for the next day toward the previous day low.

rule: After a deviation from a range, the retest of that deviation should resist price.

rule: After a large range day, expect consolidation, at least during Asia.

rule: [guest] With bullish order flow, a daily reversal wick (rejection block) should have its upper half (50% of the wick) respected.

rule: [guest] A weekly bias is speculation until confirmed: no shorts on Monday in an expected bullish week; wait for a trade above a high that holds the breaker and displaces in the 9:30-10:00 window.

rule: Frame each asset by phases of price delivery and daily closures aligned with the weekly profile; after multiple days of expansion do not trade further in that direction until a new phase (retracement, consolidation or reversal) appears.
quote: "So when I see this move out of a consolidation, right, we have multiple days of expansion, I'm not thinking about trading this to the upside until we enter a new phase of price delivery"

rule: Mark the weekly opening price on every asset; trades are framed relative to it (e.g. trading back to the open after a reversal closure).
quote: "And most importantly, we'll mark out the weekly opening because this is just how I frame trades."

rule: He uses the hourly chart for the weekly profile.
quote: "So here we are on the hourly chart, which is what I use on the weekly profile."

rule: After a reversal closure, price should not trade back above the reversal high (or above 0.5 of the range); a candle that does invalidates the idea.
quote: "I wouldn't want to see price trade above this high, right? Or above 0.5 of this week"

rule: If Monday made the low of the week and price traded higher all week, do not trade long on Friday, which normally caps the weekly range.
quote: "if we made the open low basically on Monday and we trade higher all week, I'm not trying to catch the high like that or trade higher on a Friday when it's normally going to cap the weekly range."

rule: He does not like to short below swept lows; after a low is swept he waits for a swing point to form and trades back into the range from discount of the last impulse leg.
quote: "Interest in trading short below lows, right? That is not ideal for me. So once we're below this low, I am waiting for a swing point to form to try to trade back into the range."

rule: When a daily candle can be framed both ways (reversal vs respecting an order block), take no bias and let another day print.
quote: "So on this day, I have no bias going into Tuesday because I can frame it both ways."

rule: The reversal (CISD) is confirmed by a close through the whole series of opposing candles, which he prefers over a single candle.
quote: "And so you could use this right here. I prefer the whole series. And so then once we close below this, then it is valid for me to look for shorts."

rule: In expansion, each new opposing candle that price closes beyond becomes a level that should not be revisited (trailing invalidation).
quote: "When we make new opposing candles, then we shouldn't return to them."

rule: An opposing candle without a wick does not make a relevant high; on a new day he wants to see open-high-low-close, and a day that just opens and goes lower gives no validation.
quote: "It doesn't really make a relevant high for me, lacking a wick. And when I'm on a new day, I want to see open, high, low, close."

rule: Tuesday high of week, Wednesday and Thursday expansion into a higher-timeframe objective validates looking for a TGIF retracement on Friday.
quote: "And if we have a Tuesday high week, Wednesday expansion, Thursday expansion, we meet our higher timeframe objective, which were these lows, and an imbalance on the higher timeframe. You see how we reach into here. Then what does that validate? It means that I can be looking for a TGIF setup."

rule: SMT with a correlated asset lets him treat the opposing candles as a valid order block; TGIF targets the marked highs or the 0.2-0.3 retracement of the week's range.
quote: "we had an SMT here with gasoline. So that allows me to use these opposing candles as an order block."

rule: He is not a fan of trading away from failure swings; trade toward the side that has failure swings (low resistance liquidity), not into high resistance liquidity.
quote: "I am not a fan of trading away from these failure swings."

rule: A large wick on a daily candle is a weak close; use 0.5 of the wick and expect its lower (or upper) half to hold price in the bias direction.
quote: "Now with the wick like this, that is a week close within the daily candle. And so you can use 0.5 of this wick in looking for the lower half to support price lower."
