rule: His model is built on swing points on the daily chart; without swing points forming he finds it hard to trade.
quote: "my model focuses on swing points on the daily chart, right? That's why I look at closures."

rule: A weekly candle that closes weak and inside the previous week leads him to frame downside early the next week, still taken day by day.
quote: "I'm probably going to be looking to frame some downside in the early next week just because of how we closed the weekly candle, which is fairly weak and inside the previous week's candle, right?"

rule: In a strong trend or expansion price respects 0.5 of the opposing candles; a close beyond that 0.5 and then beyond the opposing candle is a change in state of delivery.
quote: "if price is going to trade higher, it will respect 0.5 of these opposing candles. That's what it will do in a strong trend or expansion."

rule: He prefers price to trade slowly down into the point of interest (e.g. a London reversal) rather than first running the highs; a very large previous range raises the chance of consolidation.
quote: "But normally what I like to see is trade a little bit slower down into this point of interest. This would be something I want to see, like a London reversal, and then trade higher off of that."

rule: Do not trade into high resistance liquidity within the daily profile; he wants failure swings on the target side.
quote: "I don't like to trade into high resistance liquidity like this within the daily profile. I like to have the failure swings there."

rule: A new week that reaches back into the previous range, sweeps a high and closes below is a reversal; respecting the opening price and 0.5 of it supports continuation lower.
quote: "And then we're sweeping out a high and then we close below here. That is what I would consider a reversal. So then if we respect this opening price as well as 0.5 of this, I would anticipate price to trade lower."

rule: OHLC/OLHC of the daily candle is the foundation of the model; he mostly trades the daily candle's open-high-low-close and emphasizes the daily open over the midnight open.
quote: "I am only looking to trade The daily open high low close most of the time. That's my goal."

rule: The model is fractal; he prefers higher timeframes because they fit the economic calendar and make decisions easier.
quote: "my model is fractal, so what I do on the higher timeframes, you can do on the lower timeframes. I just find that the higher timeframes fit better with me within the economic calendar"

rule: SMT is optional confluence, never a requirement for a setup.
quote: "I'm not going to take something because it doesn't have SMT, right? SMT is an added confluence for me"

rule: Do not place limit orders inside fair value gaps; wait for a reaction that validates a new order block and enter with the defined stop, trading with price.
quote: "So I'm less focused on using fair value gaps for entries and more so as defining order blocks. So I will wait for price to Have a reaction here, validate a new order block"

rule: On a New York reversal day with short bias, 8:30 makes the opposing run higher; New York forms the reversal, so anything after 10:00 should be continuation.
quote: "We trade higher. New York is what forms the reversal. So that anything following specifically 10am should be a continuation lower."

rule: Intraday targets in order: consolidation lows, then London lows, then previous day low.
quote: "So although that isn't the London lows, that would be my first target before the previous day lows. There's kind of three targets there."

rule: Trailing the stop to each new opposing candle can be too tight (stopped before the target) but avoids sitting through a reversal.
quote: "And that would be a little bit too tight of a trail, but it also saves you from sitting on that."

rule: He reads premium/discount relative to the reversal: after a bearish reversal price should stay in the lower part; a full retrace back up is no longer bearish.
quote: "If price is going to trade all the way back up here, that isn't bearish for me anymore, right? So that's why I kind of use discount and premium opposite."

rule: Relative equal highs/lows are tradable but a sweep is preferred.
quote: "Sure. It's not really preferred. I prefer to have a sweep."

rule: After an expansion, expect a new phase of price delivery: retracement, reversal or consolidation, and identify which one from the daily closures.
quote: "we were looking for a new phase of price delivery, right? And so if I was looking for a retracement, reversal, or consolidation."

rule: A retracement that will continue must close over the series of opposing (down-close) candles; failing to do so and falling back into the range makes it a consolidation.
quote: "When we fail to do so and we fall back into the range, this is when I view this as a consolidation range."

rule: In a consolidation, have no interest until one side of the range is taken; do not try to predict or trade inside it.
quote: "I have no care what gold does in this range at all until we take out one side of it."

rule: TGIF requires a low (or high) formed Monday/Tuesday, expansion through Thursday, and a weekly objective hit; without the objective hit, do not fade Friday.
quote: "We need expansion or a low formed on Monday, Tuesday, expansion through Thursday. So we have those, right? But we also need to hit a weekly objective, which we never did."

rule: A mitigated order block / CISD level can be reused as long as the draw on liquidity has not been taken.
quote: "And I personally do as long as my drawn liquidity or wherever I'm looking to have price reach for is not taken, right?"

rule: A CISD is defined by closing through the opening price of a series of opposing candles, never a single candle.
quote: "That's how I define opposing candles. I never select one candle. I always will use a series of candles."

rule: A strong Monday close argues against much downside on Tuesday.
quote: "With a Monday strong close like this, I wasn't really anticipating this much downside on Tuesday."

rule: He trades swing points on the daily chart; if price is not near a daily swing high/low he does not catch the move, and after a Monday reversal his opportunity is the Tuesday continuation.
quote: "Within my model, if I'm not in near the highs, I wouldn't catch this, just because I trade swing points on the daily chart."

rule: Avoid trading the day after a very large range day.
quote: "I wouldn't really like to trade it after such a large range day."

rule: He takes zero to four trades a week and does not trade every day.
quote: "Normally I'm taking zero to four trades a week."

rule: He does not trade reversal days; he lets the reversal day form and trades the continuation the next day.
quote: "So I don't trade the reversal day. That's just because continuation is much easier."

rule: When bullish after a sweep, price trading back into the range should respect (get support from) opposing down-close candles; mark them off the body, not the wick.
quote: "if we're going to trade back into the range, then we should respect opposing candles, right, so basically just get support from opposing candles."

rule: The model is fractal (identical on every timeframe); he prefers daily and hourly because they align with the economic calendar, and all his analysis starts on the daily.
quote: "The only difference is I like the daily and the hourly because it aligns with the economic calendar."

rule: Order-block timeframe follows the higher timeframe: daily bias uses hourly order blocks.
quote: "So if I'm using the daily, I'm going to use the hourly for my order blocks."

rule: The only PD array he uses is the order block; the only entry confirmation is a change in state of delivery or an order-block formation.
quote: "Or an order block formation. That's it."

rule: To position in the wick of a bearish daily candle, sell above (or around) the daily opening price; the bias is invalidated if price trades above 50% of the opposing candle's range.
quote: "if price trades above 50% of this range here, I'm not anticipating this to move lower. I'm anticipating it to go take out the highs."

rule: The daily candle opens at 6 p.m. New York; the midnight open is used only as support/resistance.
quote: "Opening price, I use the 6 p.m."

rule: No weekly outlooks: trade day by day, deciding each day only after the previous daily candle prints.
quote: "I personally just trade day by day. So I don't know what I'm going to be doing Wednesday until Tuesday prints."

rule: SMT needs a CISD to confirm it, and SMT is only a confirmation, never the source of bias.
quote: "No, SMT is just a confirmation for me. It does not determine my bias."

rule: Let the low (or high) of the week form; the expansion days after it are far easier to trade than the reversal.
quote: "these days are far easier to trade than the reversal."

rule: Skip Monday about 90-95% of the time; Monday's daily candle carries no weekly information yet.
quote: "Do I always skip Monday? Like 90-95% of the time, yeah."

rule: Enter at market on the close of the confirming candle rather than waiting for a limit retest of the order block, if R:R allows.
quote: "Why would I be greedy over a fill there when I could just take a fill on the close of that candle if it doesn't destroy my risk to reward too much, right?"

rule: Execute on the 5m for indices (15m or 1H for higher-timeframe trades); generally do not go below the 5m.
quote: "I find that the five-minute chart is where things are still clear, but I can get in and lower my risk a little"

rule: Kill zones matter for lower-timeframe executions, not for positional/hourly executions.
quote: "If I'm trading positionally or like an hourly execution, then I don't really care."

rule: In a bearish continuation, price should not retrace into premium; for a bullish continuation he wants a shallow retracement - a deep retracement means a wick is forming against the bias.
quote: "If price for trace is up there, that tells me that we're forming a wick and that this isn't bearish."

rule: Low-resistance conditions come when the daily is set up for an expansion; high resistance comes before very high impact news or after very large ranges with nothing set up.
quote: "Or the main ones are prior to very high impact news events."

rule: Do not trade after three days of expansion: a new phase of price delivery is due and you would be chasing.
quote: "I don't trade after three days of expansion because that's when you get a new phase of price delivery and that's when you're essentially chasing price."

rule: Manage the position only after 2R.
quote: "So I will personally only look to manage my position after 2R."

rule: Enter on the hourly if R:R makes sense, otherwise refine to a lower timeframe.
quote: "I'll use the hourly and I can enter that if it makes sense in terms of my risk to reward. Otherwise, I'll refine that down."

rule: Set and forget once in a trade; watching the screen does not change the market.
quote: "Set and forget. Just don't stare at the screen."

rule: The amount of confirmation to demand inside a higher-timeframe Candle 2 reversal scales inversely with bias/structure quality: strong, clean bias -> reversal entry on the first CISD; less confidence -> continuation order block or SMT; very little -> continuation AND SMT.
quote: "This graph right here, if we have more bias and structure, we can demand less from the market. If we have Less bias in structure, we need to demand more from the market."

rule: Inside a higher-timeframe reversal candle there are two entry types: the first CISD that confirms the wick (reversal entry), and a later continuation (continuation order block).
quote: "The first one being that first change in the state of delivery that confirms the wick. Now the next one would be a continuation following that."

rule: Trade Candle 2 only on candles with a small wick (small opposing run) that allow expansion inside the same candle; if the wick is large, wait for a candle that supports expansion (Candle 3).
quote: "If it has a large wick, we're going to want to wait, as that would be a candle 2 with a large wick, and we'll wait for a candle that supports expansion."

rule: The reversal must form early in the higher-timeframe candle, not midway through it; if it forms midway there is no point trading it - wait for the next candle open and look for a continuation.
quote: "If it doesn't midway through it, there's no point in trading it. You just wait until the new open and then see if you can get a continuation."

rule: The wick should form early and without using a lot of the candle's range; reaching the level early with a CISD leaves enough time and range to expand.
quote: "We want to see pretty early on price reach into it, have a change in the state of delivery, because that leaves it enough time and range."

rule: Core principle: let the wick form, trade the body - only use a high/low as invalidation once you trust that the wick has formed.
quote: "let the wick form you have to be like i trust the wick then you can trade the body"

rule: A high that forms as a consolidation is not trustworthy; do not put the stop on it - either place it higher or wait for a continuation that creates a trustworthy high.
quote: "So if I was going to take an entry here, am I going to put my stop on the high of this 4-hour candle right now? No, because I don't trust it."

rule: For a continuation, wait for the new higher-timeframe candle to form its wick and enter on the continuation inside that new candle so the stop sits at the HTF extreme; entering at the end of the previous candle puts the stop on an internal high.
quote: "It makes no sense to enter right at the end here because you're going to want to wait and then wait for this wick to form."

rule: Preferred Candle 2 reversal context: price expands, consolidates, then sweeps the previous candle's high (external liquidity) and trades back into the range (internal liquidity); he dislikes a slow drift then dump unless it is a New York reversal profile.
quote: "generally when I'm trading a candle 2 reversal, I want to see price expand, consolidate, and then I like the sweep of the high, and then can trade that lower."

rule: For a reversal you want a shallow reach beyond the previous high/low; a gap open beyond the level already creates a large distance and turns it into a gap-fill trade, which he avoids.
quote: "If we're wanting to see a reversal, right, we want to see a shallow reach above the high and then trade it lower, right?"

rule: A Candle 2 needs the opposing liquidity taken first; if price consolidates internally or runs the target-side highs first, there is no way to frame the reversal.
quote: "Consolidating, that's fine, so no way for me to trade away from this low, so you need that taken out as well"

rule: If the reversal only forms after the short-term targets are already taken, it is too late in the day/candle - skip it.
quote: "But the thing is, it already took these targets, right? So you see how it just consolidates? You don't want that."

rule: If the entry-timeframe CISD level sits so far from the swing that it is near the first target, do not enter there - drop one timeframe lower to get a usable CISD.
quote: "The change in the state of delivery is so low that this is essentially where I want to be going break-even over my first target."

rule: Enter shorts only in the upper 50% of the range between the swing you trade from and the first short-term target (lower 50% for longs); past that there is no clear invalidation.
quote: "If you're trying to get short in here, you want to be trying to short in the upper 50% from your target to the swing."

rule: Continuation entries should come from a shallow retracement into a POI (FVG or high); a retracement deep enough to run the high is no longer an expansion retracement.
quote: "We have a fair value gap up there, but you don't want to see price retrace that much."

rule: If price reaches the level but cannot produce a CISD and comes back in, it usually fails and makes a new extreme; wait for the new one with a CISD.
quote: "So when we can't get the change in the state delivery and it comes back in, it usually means it's going to fail and make a new one, right?"

rule: Bias comes from the daily and hourly; setup/entry pairings (H4/M15, H1/M5, M30/M3) are interchangeable as long as every timeframe points the same direction.
quote: "Because the whole goal is you're just aligning these in the same direction."

rule: The model is fractal: a monthly wick is confirmed by a daily CISD, a daily/4H wick by a 15m/hourly CISD, and an hourly wick by a 5m CISD - the same process on all timeframes.
quote: "If I'm looking for this wick to form on the monthly time frame, I'm looking for it to form in this area. So I'm going to look for a daily change in the state of delivery."

rule: Once the higher-timeframe wick is trusted, the draw on liquidity and an ideal Candle 3 closure follow; the indicator then prints the next box where the Candle 3 wick should form.
quote: "So now what do I have? I have a drawn liquidity and I have an ideal candle 3 closure."

rule: A large-wick candle is not expected to expand: look back to its open (daily open or liquidity around it) and otherwise wait for the next candle (Candle 3).
quote: "So if I have a large wick, I'm not expecting price to just go expand, right? So then I'm looking back to the daily open or the liquidity around it"

rule: Ideal bullish daily: open, shallow opposing run, trend higher. If it does a deeper drop first it can still be anticipated, but it is often better to wait for the next candle.
quote: "So really, if you're bullish, you want to see price open, make a shallow run, trend higher. That's the most ideal."

rule: When the daily candle gives no clear information, drop to the 4H: if the 4H candle is a reversal candle, the next 4H candle can expand.
quote: "Really, this daily candle isn't telling us much. So you're just using the 4-hour candle. If this is a reversal candle, the next one can expand."

rule: With very high confidence (clean consolidation, sweep, correct closure, EQ respected) a positional entry without a reversal entry is acceptable, with the stop above 0.5 of the wick.
quote: "I could just say, yo, I'm just gonna enter someone here who might stop above .5 of the wick. It's not gonna get touched if I'm right."

rule: After a reversal off a previous candle's high with a small wick, watch what price does at EQ - support/resistance often forms there (a lower-timeframe low around EQ).
quote: "if you get a reversal off of a previous candle's high with a small wick, you want to see what the EQ does. Because That is where we could find support"

rule: Use only the 18:00 NY daily open; no midnight or other 'true' opens.
quote: "I'm just focused on using the current day open, which is 1800. I don't use midnight."

rule: Do not trade 'macros'; wait for the new candle open (e.g. 10 a.m.), let its wick form, then trade the body.
quote: "Ideally, I'm going to let 10 a.m. open, form its wick, and then trade it away, right?"

rule: In London, do not refine to 1-3m inside pre-move chop; use 15m/30m because the invalidation is the session low or a continuation.
quote: "If you're entering in here, you're not going to want to enter on that three-minute, the five-minute, those lower timeframes, right? Because you can just get wicked out and it just goes and it's still valid"

rule: 2R is a sufficient target; very high R:R examples are not realistic or sustainable.
quote: "2R, that's plenty, man."

rule: A CISD is not the same thing as a market structure shift.
quote: "Does CISD validate a market structure shift? No, it's different."

rule: SMT pairs: GBP with EUR; NZD with AUD; JPY alone; CAD alone; RTY treated as its own asset.
quote: "I know pound and euro go together. Yen is alone. CAD is alone for me."

rule: A candle with no wick (on the side of the level) is expected to get that side taken out.
quote: "Ideally, it comes in, gets taken out, right?"

rule: The indicator's T-spot box (wick-forming zone) is sized by average volatility; projections such as -1 are first targets for large-wick manipulations.
quote: "Now why is it so large? Because it accounts for the average volatility, right?"

rule: After an aggressive bullish daily candle, stay bullish as long as price holds the upper half of that candle and expect a push into the highs above.
quote: "as long as we hold the upper half of this candle, I want to see us push higher into these highs."

rule: Timeframe alignment: you want all timeframes (daily, 4H, 1H) supporting the move; a candle with a small wick supports expansion, a large wick does not, and trading against the 4H candle is harder.
quote: "Generally speaking, if you've watched my timeframe alignment video, we want all timeframes to be green, right?"

rule: When a higher-timeframe candle does not support expansion, mechanically expect a move in your direction only back to that candle's opening price, and wait to see how it closes.
quote: "So you could see if we do get a move higher, mechanically, I'm just looking for it to trade back to its opening price, right? So I want to see generally how this 4-hour closes"

rule: When the 4H does not align, wait for the 10:00 NY 4H open/close instead of chasing the opening move.
quote: "So I'm just kind of waiting because I want to wait for 10 a.m. in this scenario."

rule: Long the strongest asset and short the weakest; to go long, wait for the weakest (or middle) asset to form a reversal off a relevant swing, then trade the strongest.
quote: "If you want to short something, the focus is on YM, right? If you want to long something, you kind of want to wait for YM or ES to form a reversal, and then you trade the stronger asset."

rule: The same idea on the wrong asset fails: identifying the weakest and strongest index decides whether a trade works.
quote: "So you can have the same idea but applied to the wrong strength or wrong asset, it doesn't work out, right?"

rule: Identify asset strength in three steps: SMT, separation or structure, then candle closures (a big bearish closure is weaker than a bullish one).
quote: "SMT, separation or structure, and then candle closures, right?"

rule: An SMT only counts when it forms at a relevant swing: the divergent asset has to run out the relevant low, not just a minor one.
quote: "The only thing I don't like about that is it didn't run out this low, right? So to me, it's not that relevant. I would prefer a run of that low in the reaction."

rule: A reversal forms when a relevant swing is run out; a reversal on the weakest asset is what lets you focus on the strongest.
quote: "Because when we run out a relevant swing, that's when we can form a reversal, which then tells us, okay, if we form a reversal on the weakest asset, then I can focus on the strongest one."

rule: A valid reversal needs expansion into the low followed by an aggressive (V-shape) expansion out; consolidation or retracement at the low signals continuation the other way.
quote: "So if we want to see this trade higher, we need some sort of V-shape reversal, right? Because phase is a price. We have expansion into a low. If we don't get expansion out, right, if we consolidate or retrace, that tells continuation lower"

rule: Define the invalidation of the bias in advance: if the strong asset (NQ) fails to hold its low while the others sweep theirs, the bias is wrong; stay out.
quote: "And we want NQ to hold this low. If we don't, then we just probably fall and my bias is wrong."

rule: Do not rely on a CISD for entry when, by the time it prints, price is already at the target highs; you want to be in lower in the range.
quote: "The reason I won't be focused as much on a change in the state of delivery here is because if we get a change in the state of delivery, we're already at these highs, right?"

rule: Confirmation of a reversal can be any of: engulfing a candle, an inversion (IFVG), or the weak asset closing back over the swept level on the 3m.
quote: "Engulfing a candle. We could see an inversion. You can really use whatever."

rule: Continuations are easier than reversals; when uncertain, wait for a new high/low (structure) and trade the continuation instead of the reversal.
quote: "And you'll see why I always just favor a continuation. If I'm not certain on something, then I just wait, right?"

rule: Opposing FVGs/highs always exist; what invalidates the bias is a reaction at them with a close back beyond the level (for longs, a close below), which marks a retracement to continue, not a reversal.
quote: "So we don't want to see price close below this level if we're bullish, right? And it looks like we're wrong."

rule: Do not trade away from equal lows or a failure swing; the low you trade away from needs separation (and SMT) to be protected.
quote: "For that to work, I would have needed that separation here to then trade higher. Does that make sense? Like, I don't really care to trade away from a failure swing like this."

rule: Daily profile: when the open runs into a high (e.g. previous day high) and reverses without a clean low, expect another low to be swept before the move up; don't treat the first low as protected.
quote: "So a lot of times what I see is when we have a high and then we hit it, we want to come sweep out another low before we go higher."

rule: After a very large range day (~1,000 NQ points), expect a smaller range; continuation is still favored but the profile must confirm it.
quote: "What do you expect after we have a supermassive range? A smaller range, right? Now, we can still get a continuation, right?"

rule: Bias is set day by day within the daily candle, not held for the week; if a reversal forms, look to the opposite target (e.g. previous day low).
quote: "Guys, I go day by day with my bias."

rule: Kill zones are irrelevant; timing comes from the higher-timeframe candles you trade within.
quote: "I don't really care about kill zones. I'm just caring about the higher timeframe candles that I'm trading within."

rule: Most entries come between 08:00 and ~10:30 NY; after 11:00 setups are less interesting.
quote: "the majority of my entries come from 8 a.m. to about 10.30. Once I hit 11, it's less interesting later into the session."

rule: Use the 9:30 open rather than a 'first presented FVG'.
quote: "If you want to use something like that, I would just use 930 open, personally."

rule: Pre-open entries: almost always on a 30m or higher timeframe, only when the daily C2 supports expansion into clear targets (PDH/high), an hourly CISD confirms, all timeframes are green, and there is a protected swing before the open to trade away from.
quote: "Is that confirmed by an hourly change in the state of delivery? It is. ... see how all the timeframes are green here? That's what we were missing this morning."

rule: Stop placement on a pre-open trade: below the protected swing, covering the FVG and its 50%, never just at the open; target 2R or more; if that R:R is poor, wait for after the open.
quote: "You could either put your stock entry at the low, you could enter, but you need to cover this fair value gap and 50% of that, right? And then you can look for 2R or trade that higher"

rule: Do not enter longs above range highs or far from the daily open; be in around the daily open or mid-range before the high is taken, otherwise skip.
quote: "you need to be in around the daily open or midway through its range before this high is taken. Once this high is taken, I'm not interested in it"

rule: Don't take a continuation in a direction whose target has already been hit, and don't trade against your day's bias.
quote: "Got to realize it already hit its target, right? Like I said, I don't care for the downside today because I'm bullish, right?"

rule: Scalping model: when there is little range, the only trade is off a 15m swing point with candle 3/candle 4 aligned with the hourly; skip it if it's messy.
quote: "The only way to trade it is this 15-minute swing point. There's candle 3, candle 4, right? Does that align with the hourly? Yeah, it does, right? So this is the scalping model"

rule: If the specific criteria are not met, there is no trade: being right on direction without a valid entry is fine.
quote: "My idea can be right. It doesn't give me an entry. Great. Who cares?"

rule: Patience is the main skill; when nothing is there, set an alert on the trigger level and stop watching.
quote: "Like normally what I would do is I would just set an alert on this level for YM and then just not watch because I don't really care unless we hit this low."

rule: Plan as two explicit scenarios tied to the weakest asset: it reverses at the low -> long the strongest; it fails -> expect the other assets to go to the same low; favor the one matching your bias.
quote: "We have two scenarios, right? YM reverses, NQ higher. YM doesn't reverse, ES lower, right?"

rule: Avoid consolidating markets (range-bound with highs and lows being run back and forth).
quote: "It's just good consolidation, so I'd rather avoid it personally."

rule: Trading the invalidation of the bias is possible, but not on a day that looks like it will consolidate.
quote: "Can you trade the invalidation of bias? Sure. ... But this is just something where I don't really care to try to trade or flip because this is a day that I could see just consolidating."

rule: He does not use contract SMT (MNQ vs NQ), breaker blocks (rarely) or the London reversal profile for decisions.
quote: "MNQ took out the low contract SMT. That's not something I personally use."

rule: Backtest/trade on the continuous contract with daily settlement turned off.
quote: "I said, you need to have daily settlement turned off."

rule: Do not trade the 08:30 CPI release itself; wait for the release, then look for the move at the 09:30 equity open.
quote: "Obviously I'm not going to be participating in CPI release, but I would be bearish on the initial release at least."

rule: On a news morning, hold off on firming the bias until the release has printed, while keeping the daily-closure lean.
quote: "I'm going to kind of see what the release does before I get too biased."

rule: Treat the 08:30 move as manipulation and expect 09:30 to deliver the move in the bias direction.
quote: "830 is manipulation, so I'm wanting 930 to continue lower, right?"

rule: A quiet release does not change the plan; there is no 'delayed CPI move', the daily bias and draw stay the same.
quote: "No, it just didn't have a CPI move. It's not delayed."

rule: The 09:30 volatility comes from the NYSE equity open (stocks/ETFs start trading), which is why the NY open matters for index futures and not much for currencies.
quote: "Equity's open, NYSE open, exactly. So you have NYSE open, right, at 9.30."

rule: For shorts trade the weakest index (here YM) and for longs the strongest; the easiest target for the weakest asset is the previous day low.
quote: "if I had to focus on one thing, I'm going to choose the weakest asset, and the easiest target is just the previous state low, right?"

rule: Confirm the weak asset's move with the strong asset: the YM short needs NQ to reverse off its high; if the strong asset won't reverse, you are probably wrong.
quote: "If it's not reversing here, that usually means I'm wrong, but we'll see what happens, right?"

rule: Skip the CISD when its level sits at the same place as your short-term target; use other evidence instead (V-shape reversal back into a gap with SMT).
quote: "my change in the state of delivery level or my continuation level is at the same level as what would be a short-term target for me. And so if I wait for this to close, I'm literally at a target."

rule: With a large wick, the next candle should respect 0.5 of that wick; trading much beyond it makes a continuation unlikely and turns it into a reversal-candle scenario.
quote: "this is 50% of that wick, right, this is kind of where it caps it, right? We don't want to see a trade higher than that if this is going to be a continuation of this move."

rule: EQ / 0.5 of the wick tells you whether the wick is small enough for the candle to still expand mechanically.
quote: "That tells you when the wick is small enough to still expand mechanically."

rule: Continuations should be quick; if price spends more than about two candles trying to form one, treat it as consolidation that likely runs the high again.
quote: "we want continuations to be quick. You don't want to see it hang around, then close, right?"

rule: Do not take blind retest entries into a POI; wait for price to form a swing point (or a strong candle 2 close with a small opposing wick) there first.
quote: "I don't want to just, I don't personally want to just retest entries"

rule: Do not flip the daily bias on one lower-timeframe candle; only a relevant level being hit (e.g. PDL) or the strong asset turning weak would change it.
quote: "Like, I don't switch my bias because of one 15-minute candle."

rule: Anticipate one leg of price at a time (one draw), then react; don't predict several legs ahead.
quote: "You are just predicting one leg in price. Then you see what happens. Then you predict, right?"

rule: One shot, one idea: once the target is hit he stops; continuations after the target are less attractive, especially when most of the daily range was used to reach it.
quote: "But we've used a lot of the daily range just to reach this level, right? So it makes me less interested in continuations below that level, right?"

rule: As price approaches the target, trail the stop tightly to the 1-minute bar instead of giving back the move.
quote: "So a lot of times I'll just trail my stop tightly to the 1-minute bar."

rule: Time-based exit: expansion candles (30m/15m) close into their lows/highs, so you can hold to the end of the period (09:45 or 10:00).
quote: "So if you have an expansion candle, generally you can hold till the end of the period and you're gonna be near that low, right?"

rule: 10:00 NY opens new higher-timeframe candles; any new idea forms there.
quote: "So, 10 a.m. is kind of where, if you want to... Get any sort of new idea, it comes at 10 a.m."

rule: Confirm bias by waiting for the HTF candle to form its wick, then trade away from it with a swing point or fractal model, aligning timeframes and finding a protected swing.
quote: "So all it's really about is you're aligning multiple timeframes in one direction and then finding a protected swing."

rule: A+ setup: candle 3 on every timeframe, an open, a reach into a POI (usually an FVG), closure through, enter with the stop at the swing.
quote: "Candle 3 on the daily, candle 3, it's just candle 3 on every time frame."

rule: Asia is traded only on a daily candle 2 closure with a protected swing formed inside C2 before the next candle opens; enter positionally with the stop at that swing.
quote: "The only time I trade during Asia session is when I have a candle 2 closure on the daily."

rule: Timeframe floor by session: 15m minimum for London; go lower only in New York when volatility allows; a 4H swing is entered on the 15m.
quote: "15-minute minimum for, like, London, if I ever watch that. The only time I really go lower is into the New York session when the volatility allows that."

rule: For a candle-2 day the London reversal should form a shallow wick (high of day); if NY runs the London high, the day is consolidation and he is not interested.
quote: "if I'm trading a candle 2, the whole idea is that we form a wick, a shallow wick, and then trade lower. I'm not really interested if price runs out this London."

rule: A reversal expectation is basic: from a high, wait for a lower high to trade.
quote: "Here's a high, I want to wait for a lower high to trade. That's it."

rule: The level to trade away from (invalidation) matters, not the timeframe; the 3m is often cleaner than the 1m.
quote: "But the whole thing, guys, about trading is you want to level the trade away from. You want some sort of invalidation."

rule: When price is messy and the confirming asset isn't cooperating, use a wider stop, e.g. beyond 50% of the 30-second CISD.
quote: "that's when you may have to use a little bit of a wider stop."

rule: After the weak asset reacts at its target, the strong asset can be traded the other way, but take the continuation that forms a protected swing rather than the reversal itself.
quote: "you don't even have to trade the reversal, you wait for the continuation, which is what? That. That forms a protected swing, right?"

rule: For FX, do the analysis on the dollar and pair it with the weakest (or strongest) currency; use only the dollar as the SMT reference for USD pairs.
quote: "If dollar is bullish, you want to pair it with the weakest currency."

rule: Skip markets in consolidation (gold, oil, crypto here); after large ranges expect small ranges; he trades expansion.
quote: "It's not really, like, guys, I try to trade expansion, right?"

rule: Enter turtle-soup style only with all timeframes aligned, at the sweep, with the stop right there.
quote: "You really have to enter with your stop that."

rule: Move to breakeven only after a new protected swing forms and price trades away; too early gets retested out.
quote: "So you don't want to do it too early."

rule: Get entries early in the candle rather than near its close.
quote: "Well you ideally get entries earlier into the candle."

rule: At 2R, a win rate above 50% is good; aim for few trades (one or two a week).
quote: "I just know that at 2R, if I have over a 50% win rate, I'm doing good."

rule: Keep the chart clean: highs/lows, FVGs, opposing candles (his OB) or CISD, protected swings, SMT, HTF opens; no BOS/CHoCH.
quote: "I'll use highs and lows, fair value gap, and then opposing handles."

rule: Psychology fix: stop doing dumb stuff; don't compare yourself with others or with cherry-picked 10R posts.
quote: "Stop comparing yourself to random people on the internet."

rule: Use the instrument's typical daily range (YM ~700-800 points) to choose targets; once most of it is used, pick a near target rather than a deep one.
quote: "If you take a look at our previous expansion candles, right, or just candles in general, they're usually around 700, 800 points on YM, right? So when looking at this day and we already go 500, I'm like, we're pretty exhausted already."

rule: A Friday trade back into the weekly range ('TGIF') needs a relevant level hit first; a large expansion with no relevant level hit is a consolidation day to avoid.
quote: "Just because we have a large expansion and we don't hit a relevant level, it's more so a consolidation setup for me, right?"

rule: At the high of a range, only look to trade back lower; don't long over range highs.
quote: "We're at the range high, and then the only interest to me is trading back lower, right? I don't long over these highs. This is where you get caught."

rule: When trading ranges, trade from the edges of the range back into the range, never in the middle of the range trying to break out.
quote: "if I'm trading ranges, I want to focus around the edges of the range, trading back into the range, right? Edges of the range trading back into the range. I don't want to focus on trading in the middle of the range, trying to exit the range."

rule: In a consolidation range you favour the opposite side, but if the market is still bullish it will often react at the EQ.
quote: "Yes, we favor to the low of the range, but a lot of times if it's going to still remain bullish, it's going to act at the EQ, right?"

rule: Trading against the weekly range on a Friday is only appealing when the day opens with a small wick; otherwise the target is just the daily open and he prefers trading expansion.
quote: "my preference for trading something against the weekly range, so like on Friday, is when we open and we have a small wick, right?"

rule: The 10:00 NY 4H candle is a decision point: for a 4H reversal, the prior 4H should close back inside with a small wick, and the new candle should open, trade into 0.5 of that wick, then expand away.
quote: "we're gonna have a 4-hour candle closure somewhere back in here. It's gonna use 0.5 of the wick, then the next candle will open up. Hit that and then go."

rule: A large wick on the setup candle makes a sweep of the opposing high unlikely to be a clean reversal; he wants a closure with a small wick.
quote: "because if it closes lower, right, I don't want to see it reach all the way up there, that's a large wick. So the only way for it to sweep this high is if it closed higher, small wick."

rule: Trade swing points, not gaps; a gap is just another daily/monthly low.
quote: "I'm looking to trade swing points. So when this closes bearish, I'm looking just for this to be bearish. I don't really care about the gap."

rule: A reversal needs expansion into the level and expansion back out (a V-shape); consolidation candles at a level are not a reversal.
quote: "Now, if we're going to have a reversal formed after this gap, what do you need? ... You need expansion here and then expansion back out. Well, do these candles tell you expansion? No."

rule: A candle that hits a high and prints aggressively lower stays bearish while it respects its EQ, even if it didn't close below its open (not a C2).
quote: "It didn't close below the open, but it's still bearish to me. As long as we respect the EQ on this one, it's still bearish. Make sense?"

rule: Relative strength across indices: YM and NQ sit at opposite ends and ES is in the middle. To short, focus on the weakest; to long, the strongest.
quote: "YM and NQ are kind of always on the opposite ends. So YM is strong, then NQ is weak, ES is in the middle. YM is weak, then NQ is strong, ES is in the middle"

rule: Don't trade the lagging asset; prefer the leading asset or the middle one (e.g. take ES when YM leads).
quote: "generally here, I don't like to trade the lagging asset, so I don't really like trading NQ because it's weak, right? So I generally tend to prefer that middle one or the leading one."

rule: After the 9:30 open, give it about five minutes to clear up before reading direction.
quote: "Well, honestly, I'd give it five minutes to clear up because we do have this high."

rule: Read the phase of price: a slow, shallow pullback after expansion is a retracement, not a reversal. A reversal is expansion up, expansion down, a V-shape. If it's a retracement, expect the next target.
quote: "That is a retracement. That's not a reversal, guys. Think about it. You know what a reversal looks like. Expansion up, expansion down, a V-shape."

rule: Without a bias there's no reason to sit on the 1m chart.
quote: "Why would I go to the one-minute chart when I don't really have a bias or care?"

rule: After a level is swept in a range, require a new continuation before shorting; otherwise you get in and get stopped. Better late than early.
quote: "I would need another continuation just to show we're not reversing here. A lot of people will just enter short and then they get right out."

rule: Better to be late than early.
quote: "I would favor to the downside, but I'd rather be late than early. That's my thing."

rule: If the strongest asset doesn't reverse off its level, it usually goes for the next level, and the other assets should follow toward their highs.
quote: "So if YM is not reversing here, generally speaking, it's going to go for the next level, right? ... If it's going to go for its next level, then ES should also continue towards these highs"

rule: If the daily isn't obvious, don't drop to lower timeframes; it's usually consolidating and you'll get chopped. Wait for the open.
quote: "If the daily is not obvious, going lower is not going to help, because generally speaking, when the daily is not obvious, it's consolidating."

rule: He only trades continuations, not reversals, to avoid getting stopped out of moves.
quote: "And that's why I don't trade reversals, guys. I only look to trade continuations because I don't like getting stopped out of those moves."

rule: Consolidation at the EQ after leaving a range (no reversal) generally means continuation.
quote: "We come up here, are we gonna get a reversal? No, right? It consolidates. Consolidation means continuation, generally speaking."

rule: Don't go too low for targets; focus on daily highs and lows.
quote: "Well, this is another simple trick, guys, is stop going so low for targets. Focus on the daily highs and lows."

rule: After two large expansion days, expect more consolidation conditions and smaller targets.
quote: "You just had two large days, so a lot of times it can set up some more consolidation conditions."

rule: His model only trades candles 3 and 4 of a daily run; by candle 5 he doesn't chase. That keeps him out of a new phase.
quote: "I'm not going to trade dollar after one bullish day, two, three, four, right? This is candle five. Candle two, three, four. If you notice, my model only looks for three and four, right? Because it saves you from a new phase."

rule: Shorting against the daily range only targets the daily open, which is a less attractive trade than trading with expansion.
quote: "Harder to try to short against the daily range. If you're going to short against the daily range, what's your target? Back to the daily open."

rule: Mark relevant highs and lows, not session highs/lows; e.g. a London high may carry no relevance.
quote: "I don't really mark session highs and lows. To be honest, I just mark highs and lows."

rule: He doesn't use intermarket analysis (dollar vs gold, dollar vs indices) or macro/politics on 5m/15m trading.
quote: "I don't use gold versus dollar. And then I definitely am not using Dollar versus indices, personally speaking."

rule: When price is confusing, don't watch it; don't pretend to know.
quote: "When stuff is confusing to me, I just don't watch it. I don't pretend like I know everything."

rule: Taking LTF formations (e.g. a V-shape) without an HTF bias and model (C2 closure + CISD) is pattern trading, and it loses.
quote: "This is where people fall into the problem of their pattern trading. They see some lower timeframe formation. They're like, this looks really good. And then they just try to act on that, right? I don't do that because that's how you lose"

rule: No trade unless the setup has closed through; 'did we even close below? No' is a reason to skip.
quote: "Did we even close below? No. See, you have two reasons to not take this."

rule: Preferred entry timeframes are 5m and 15m; go lower only if needed. If you can't execute on the 1m, don't trade the 1m.
quote: "My favorite time frame are entries. I would say, like, 5-minute, 15-minute. You can go lower if you need."

rule: A very aggressive up-down shape on the lower timeframe can count as the CISD on structure; otherwise use the later close below.
quote: "I would consider their change in the state of delivery there just based on the structure. Otherwise, you would have it here."

rule: On the confirmation timeframe, if the 15m isn't clear, drop to the 5m.
quote: "And so 15-minute, you can look. See how it's not that clear in the 15-minute? That's when you can go to the 5, right?"

rule: Continuation entry: price sweeps a high and closes below, making that swing protected; it should then hold 0.5 of the leg, retrace into a small FVG, and close below again. Enter on that close.
quote: "Sweeps out a high, closes below. So this is the point of interest, closes below, 50% should be respected. Respects that into this little tiny fair value gap. Kind of hard to see. It's like right there. Closes below."

rule: Stop goes over the bodies of the swing.
quote: "But it'd be like this, where you're stopping the bodies, and then to our minimum."

rule: Target depends on conviction: the previous-day low for a full HTF move, the range EQ on a consolidation day, or nearby equal lows / failure swings at ~1.5R when he lacks HTF bias.
quote: "If you think it's going to previous day low, then you have like a really nice trade. But if you're like, hey, we're more on a consolidation ... I'd rather just target around the EQ of this range."

rule: Failure swings that form off a protected low are good targets: price often takes them out and then bounces if still bullish. Not greedy without HTF bias.
quote: "this is a nice protected low, closure, nice protected low, and then these are failure swings from that. So a lot of times price will, if it's going to react, will take out failure swings like this and then go back up"

rule: On a Friday / low-conviction trade, take most of the position off at the first target and hold the rest at breakeven or exit; otherwise partials at 1.5R-2R and hold runners.
quote: "if I was on a Friday taking this, like, I would take off most my position here and then either just hold a little break even or just be done."

rule: True expansion happens when the daily and 4H candles both support expansion in the same direction (timeframe alignment).
quote: "this candle supports expansion, this candle supports expansion, right? So then you get this expansion lower."

rule: Daily-profile target: if the daily has a larger wick, the mechanical target is the daily open; otherwise reach for nearby failure swings.
quote: "Now, looking at the daily profile, we either go to Daily Open, because we have a larger wick, that's mechanical, or if we have failure swings here, you can reach for that"

rule: Target the first failure swing after a V-shape, especially when not trying to be greedy.
quote: "You have a nice V shape and then the first failure swing. Nice V shape, first failure swing. I like targeting those, especially when I'm not trying to be greedy."

rule: Don't go to lower timeframes until you have HTF context; e.g. wait for the 10:00 4H, see the C3 closure aligned with the 4H, then go to 1H and 5m.
quote: "Why would you go down to the lower timeframes, look for an entry until you have a reason to? Like here, you could have sat on the 4-hour or 1-hour chart."

rule: Enter on the close through (don't wait for a retest that may not come), unless the closure candle is so large that the stop is far away; then wait for a new continuation.
quote: "It's a bit different if price closes, like let's say it was this closure. I'm not going to enter this on the breakout with my stop up there, right? Then I would need a new continuation."

rule: Max one trade a day prevents tilt days and caps a bad week at five losses (covered by 2.5 wins at 2R).
quote: "Because if you do only one trade a day, you're not going to go on tilt because you can only allow one trade a day."

rule: A 50% win rate works with 1.5R or more, not at 1:1.
quote: "If you have a 1-1 R, no. If you have a 1.5 R, yes. If you have a 2 R, yes."

rule: He doesn't use PSPs because he mostly trades continuations, not reversals.
quote: "Like a PSP doesn't really help me, for me at least, because I mostly trade continuations."

rule: He prefers a C2 closure to form from a key level, but on the 4H and daily it doesn't always need to.
quote: "Yeah, I prefer to have it form from a key level. 4-hour doesn't always need to, daily doesn't always need to."

rule: His A+ setup: daily candle 3 (after a daily C2 closure), London forms the reversal (the day's wick low), New York continues on a ~15m continuation; trade a continuation inside a larger continuation.
quote: "If I had to choose only one setup to trade forever, it would be this. Candle 3 on the daily, London forms a reversal, New York continuation on like a 15-minute chart, that's it."

rule: The easiest expansion comes when candle 3s align on multiple timeframes, e.g. daily C3 plus a 4H C2 closure that gives a 15m C3.
quote: "when does the easiest expansion aligns? It's like multiple C3s, right?"

rule: Mechanical sequence: point of interest, then a closure over it, which creates a protected swing; you can enter once the protected swing forms.
quote: "What do we look for? Point of interest, then closure over. When it does that, what does that tell us? It tells us that we now have a what? A protected swing."

rule: A forming London low (the wick) plus a continuation is the confirmation; then New York should continue into targets.
quote: "If we have a continuation that forms, we do, right? That's our confirmation that we have formed a London low a day."

rule: Enter around the higher-timeframe candle's opening price: let the wick form, then trade the body. Do not enter after the candle has already expanded or made its average range.
quote: "You can only trade the body of the candle if you're trading around the opening price of the candle"

rule: Do not enter above highs that have already been taken; that is a chase.
quote: "I don't really like entering above the highs, generally speaking, right? That's a chase to me."

rule: A small wick (shallow sweep) sets up a bigger expansion. A large wick makes a big expansion less likely, so pull targets in (e.g. back to daily open / previous day low).
quote: "Because we want a small wick to expand. To make a larger wick, I have to adjust my targets to back to the daily open, previous day low."

rule: Take targets from the daily chart: previous day high/low first. Then use average daily range to judge whether a further daily high is reachable.
quote: "Guys, if you want easy levels, you always get those from the daily chart."

rule: Equal highs (failure swings) make cleaner targets; combine the fractal model setup with them.
quote: "So you have the mechanical fractal model, the setup, right? But then you add that with failure swings, right?"

rule: Rank YM/ES/NQ by relative strength and trade the strongest or the middle one, not the weakest. ES, in the middle, often keeps strength from the start through the continuation.
quote: "ES is the best because it's just in the middle. It's going to have the strength in the beginning and strength continue."

rule: A 4H expansion candle should close near its high/low. If 09:30 does not reverse, hold to the 10:00 4H close as a time-based exit.
quote: "If 9.30 is not going to reverse, it should continue until 10, right? This is what we spoke about before as well, time-based exits, because this is a 4-hour expansion candle"

rule: Once the target level is hit, the idea is complete; stop caring about what price does next.
quote: "Once it hits that level, I do not care."

rule: A candle 2 closure is a candle that sweeps the previous candle's low and closes back above it (bullish), or the mirror for bearish.
quote: "What is a candle 2 closure? It sweeps out its previous low and closes back above it."

rule: A C2 for a continuation inside the daily range does not need a POI; a C2 for a reversal must be at a POI. He teaches 'yes, POI' for simplicity.
quote: "If you're trying to trade it as a reversal, yes, 100%. If you're trading it as a continuation, no."

rule: On a daily continuation the daily profile (London reversal then New York continuation) can stand in for a POI as the extra confirmation.
quote: "sometimes on the continuation, specifically on the daily chart, you don't need a point of interest because of how the daily profile is confirming it"

rule: A reaction off an opposing daily FVG needs a candle closure and change in state of delivery through it. A mechanical close back below is not enough if the price action is slow and shallow (no aggression); use discernment.
quote: "I need to wait for a candle closure and a change in the state of delivery."

rule: The level a continuation must respect is 50% of the opposing candle's bodies (EQ); for a bullish day the low should form in the box above it.
quote: "This is an opposing candle. What area do we want to see be respected from that? 50% of the bodies. Mark out 50% of the bodies. Is it respected? Yes. Then we form a continuation."

rule: Avoid trading candle 4 when candle 2 and candle 3 have both already expanded.
quote: "When to avoid trading candle 4? Well, generally when candle 2 and candle 3 both expand."

rule: Find one A+ setup and take it; if there is none, get off the charts. Pick the cleanest framework among all assets and focus only on it.
quote: "Find one A plus setup. Take that. If nothing, Get off charts. That's literally how I trade."

rule: To stop overtrading, every trade needs a higher-timeframe bias or reason (step one of the model).
quote: "Step one in my model. Get a higher timeframe bias or reason."

rule: Skip consolidating or choppy assets (e.g. gold and silver here) even if a mechanical setup prints. Pattern-matching the model is not the same as a clean framework.
quote: "This is really crappy price action to me. I stay away from this, right? And this is what I mean between pattern trading the model and not, right?"

rule: A doji/reversal closure with no follow-through means a lack of direction; wait rather than pick a side.
quote: "It just has a lack of direction, which means I'm going to just wait on it, right?"

rule: He only trades continuations, never opposing the daily range or picking reversal highs/lows intraday.
quote: "I don't care to oppose the daily range. Like I said, I prefer to trade continuations."

rule: Which session expands depends on the framework: if Asia forms no manipulation, it won't expand; London manipulates, which sets New York up to expand.
quote: "Well, is London set to expand? No, because Asia never formed any manipulation. Well, then London manipulates. Okay, that sets up New York to expand."

rule: For a pre-open entry on the A+ day, the clean entry window was roughly 07:00-08:00 NY on the 15m continuation (or 6-7 AM). Without it, nothing is tradable before the open.
quote: "You either get an entry around here, 7, 8 o'clock, right? Or you're not really getting anything pre-open, right?"

rule: The 09:30 SMT scalp (weaker assets sweep the 09:30 low, 1m entry, stop under it) is possible but not his type of trade.
quote: "you'd have to trade a very quick SMT of 930 being swept by the weaker assets, right? ... But like I said, that's not really my type of trade."

rule: He does not use OTE except in larger ranges; a retrace into the OTE of an intraday leg would make him look short, not long.
quote: "So I don't use OTE, personally speaking. The only time I use OTE is in larger ranges."

rule: Use back-adjusted continuous contracts with settlement-as-close off, so daily candles show the actual close and no rollover gap.
quote: "I have set turned off. I don't like daily settlement. It changes. I want the actual close, not the settlement close."

rule: The whole read used only highs/lows, a fair value gap and opposing candles (CISD); those concepts are enough.
quote: "I used highs and lows. I used a fair value gap. And I used what? Opposing candles or CISD."

rule: Use currency-futures SMT mainly on the daily; differing 4H opening times between instruments aren't worth overthinking.
quote: "currency futures, I mean, I mainly use it for the daily chart, to be honest."

rule: Expansion days can close at their highs, so a runner can be held toward the end of the day after a continuation long.
quote: "Potentially, I can hold a runner towards the end of the day, because if it's an expansion day, it can close into the highs as well"

rule: Even when the move sits high in the range, a new hourly candle open can expand; that is the only reason to consider a late continuation.
quote: "The only reason you could potentially take that is a new candle open, so a new hourly candle can expand, right?"

rule: In a consolidation, if there is no aggressive price action off the high, look for the move to the other side (the low).
quote: "if we didn't get some sort of aggressive price auction off of this high, then we'd be looking for a move to this low."

rule: Once an asset has already hit its target / made a big range, don't trade it; the only trade left is back into the range.
quote: "It's already made a pretty massive range, so this is when you don't want to trade."

rule: Wait for the daily closure to confirm a reversal (with SMT), then look for the continuation into the target.
quote: "We need to wait for this daily close. This daily closure tells us, hey, what price has reversed here with an SMT. We can look for a continuation in this area."

rule: His toolkit is only highs/lows, fair value gaps and CISD, with SMT as confluence — no rejection blocks, breakers, OTE, Fib, breakaway gaps or silver bullet.
quote: "What do I use, though? Highs and lows, fair value gap, right? And then CISD. The confluence I will use is SMT."

rule: If the 4H candle has already expanded before 10:00, wait for the 10:00 candle rather than trading the retracement.
quote: "We've already expanded this 4-hour candle, so it's not really that interesting until 10 a.m."

rule: Estimate average daily range by eyeballing recent daily expansion candles (YM ~700-800) and check the draw on liquidity sits inside it; bigger ranges need high-volatility days like FOMC.
quote: "maybe just around 700, 800 is a good amount for YM. So that's kind of just what I expect."

rule: If the daily move already happened before the open, either don't trade or trade only toward a remaining open draw on liquidity, with lowered expectations.
quote: "the easiest, most simple way is, hey, price has already expanded, I'm just gonna avoid this, right? The second is, is there any open drawn liquidity?"

rule: On a bearish day trade the weakest asset — the one closest to the draw (here YM nearest its PDL).
quote: "the focus would be on YM, since it is weaker, it's closer to that previous day low"

rule: Failure swings without SMT are not trustworthy; you need a swing put in at the high or the move will likely fail.
quote: "I'm not the biggest fan of these failure swings right here unless we have SMT. And we don't, so it's just kind of garbage looking."

rule: The fractal model needs a candle closure first; nothing is of interest until the HTF candle closes and prints its EQ, which must then hold.
quote: "what does the fractal model need? It needs a candle closure first, right? So that's why we're not interested in anything until what? This candle closes."

rule: After an expansion you want a retracement or consolidation, not expansion met with expansion; repeated opposing expansions mean consolidation.
quote: "When you see expansion, you want to see a retracement or a consolidation. You don't really want to see expansion, met with expansion, met with an expansion"

rule: When you don't want the candle-2 high revisited, use 0.5 of the wick as the level that must hold.
quote: "we don't want to see this high hit, we use 0.5 of the wick."

rule: Move to breakeven once price has traded far from the entry with an expansion candle (or a lower-timeframe V-shape reversal).
quote: "if I was in anywhere in here, I would be breakeven at this point because We're so far traded away from it"

rule: The 10:00 continuation should ideally run until about 10:10-10:15.
quote: "This can continue until around 10, 10, 10, 15, right? That'd be ideal."

rule: Take a partial at the previous 4H low; price can react there even if the final target isn't reached.
quote: "Now, this is somewhere where I want to partial. Why is that? Well, that's the previous 4-hour low"

rule: Enter early in the continuation; continuations fail when people enter after the short-term lows are already swept.
quote: "most people fail because they're trying to take an entry here after we already took all these short-term lows"

rule: Once a new protected swing forms, move the stop to it.
quote: "I'm moving my stop loss to here, right? Because this is now protected in my eyes."

rule: Rank relative strength from the daily: close vs open, who took the previous day high (SMT), strongest close vs largest wick; largest wick / weakest close = weakest.
quote: "This one has the strongest close, this one has the largest wick, so it tells me that YM's the weakest"

rule: Trading the move from low in the daily range risks consolidation, so be less greedy with targets; from high in the range you can catch the expansion.
quote: "If you're trading this type of move somewhere up here in the daily range, you can catch an expansion. If you're trading it down here, this is where you get the risk of consolidation"

rule: A lower-timeframe reversal does not by itself cancel the higher-timeframe idea; decide whether the idea is still valid.
quote: "Just because price has a reversal in one minute doesn't mean that you just get rid of your whole idea, right?"

rule: Don't pattern-trade setups; the lower-timeframe model is only valid because HTF analysis put you there (4H expanded -> 10:00 -> 15m swing point -> 1m fractal model).
quote: "the only reason we're down here is because of higher time frame analysis. So that's why you don't try to pattern trade things."

rule: Prefer trading the leading asset; lagging or middle assets tend to chop you up.
quote: "I prefer not to trade the lagging or middle assets because sometimes you just get chopped up. I prefer to just trade the leading one"

rule: Protected swings shouldn't be touched until the target is hit; after the target, price often runs out the first protected swing and then continues — a place he likes to find entries.
quote: "a lot of times we come run out with a first protected swing and then that's where we form the continuation"

rule: Confirm a higher or lower day with either a CISD or a candle closure, then expect it to hold.
quote: "you're either going to use a change in the state of delivery to confirm it, or you're going to use a candle closure"

rule: Framework transfer: take the candle-2 framework from the stronger assets (NQ/ES) and apply it to the weaker asset, treating it like C2 to trade C3/C4.
quote: "I'm transferring the framework from NQ and ES to the weaker asset, so I'm treating this like a candle 2 to trade candle 3 and 4"

rule: If you missed the reversal expansion, wait for a retracement and a new continuation with a new protected swing.
quote: "Generally speaking, you need to wait for a retracement, but then waiting for a new continuation."

rule: When the 1H gives no candle-2 reversal, use the 30m for its swing framework.
quote: "You have 30 minutes going to provide a swing framework, and then you can look at that."

rule: Trade low frequency: one trade a day max.
quote: "I prefer to take a low frequency. I could take one trade a day max."

rule: Order of work: bias from the daily (direction and draw) -> framework -> then choose the stronger/weaker asset; the choice changes daily.
quote: "for me, the directional bias is bearish, right? Then I look. I already have a bias. I can look for a framework, but then I would just look at the assets and determine which one is stronger or weaker"

rule: Pick the setup timeframe from when you expect expansion: wanting the 10:00 move meant 15m (not 30m/1H), with entries on 1m.
quote: "Because I just want to see 10 a.m. expand, I need to use the 15, and that's why we ended up on the 1-minute."

rule: Don't enter above a range high that's already been taken unless there is a new swing / new phase of price.
quote: "we already took out this range high. I don't really like entering above that unless I have a new swing, new phase of price."

rule: A small wick can be enough in context; what matters is that it does not grow into a bigger wick (that would fail the idea).
quote: "Within context, that's enough of a wick. I don't want to see a bigger wick here, otherwise it fails."

rule: If a candle closes below a level, the high above should remain and 50% of it should be respected; he refined the 50% line to a nearby volume imbalance.
quote: "This candle here closed below this level. That tells me this high should remain. If this high should remain, what should be respected? 50% of it."

rule: Visualise higher- and lower-timeframe candles on one chart: expansion, consolidation, manipulation (sweep), distribution.
quote: "So expansion, consolidation, manipulation, distribution."

rule: On a reversal day with a small wick, target the EQ first, then the previous day high.
quote: "if you're trading a reversal day like this, small wick, it's EQ."

rule: Enter around the opening price of higher-timeframe candles; once price is through it, the trade is no longer interesting.
quote: "I want to enter around the opening price of higher timeframe candles. So once you're already through that, it's not that interesting"

rule: For a continuation away from a high: sweep the high, close back below it, then go; if not, you are wrong.
quote: "it needs to sweep this high, close back below this high, right? Back in here, and then it needs to go. Otherwise, I'm just wrong"

rule: If the retracement already formed before 10:00, the 10:00 candle can expand without making a new wick.
quote: "If price has already formed its retracement, it doesn't need to go make another retracement, it can just expand lower."

rule: The candle closure after a pullback tells you whether it's a retracement (continue) or a reversal.
quote: "The candle closure here is going to tell you, hey, is this a reversal to go back up or is this a retracement to go lower?"

rule: If your stops keep getting swept before TP, enter on a higher timeframe (15m or 5m) instead of M1/M3; low-timeframe entries need HTF opening-price knowledge.
quote: "Stay on higher timeframe for entry. So assuming that you're on this, I don't know. You didn't say. Usually staying on a 15-minute for an entry."

rule: On a reversal day, trade it before price reaches the target, never at the EQ afterwards, and don't oppose the reversal day.
quote: "I'm not really interested in entering a reversal day all the way back at the EQ. If I'm trading a reversal day, I'm trading before we reach into this target"

rule: SMT formed before 10:00 is sufficient; you don't need SMT at the 10:00 candle itself.
quote: "There was an SMT prior to 10AM, so you don't necessarily need SMT at the 10AM candle, right?"

rule: When what you want to happen isn't happening, stay away — it's usually consolidation.
quote: "Usually when something that you want to happen isn't happening, it's usually something to stay away from, consolidating."

rule: If the setup is a reversal day with no swing point and you think it's a retracement to continue, wait for the following day's continuation.
quote: "If I'm going to trade something like this, and this is going to be the retracement to continue higher, then I'm waiting for the following day."

rule: Each day you only need the one asset that makes sense; ignore the rest of the basket.
quote: "each day, I have a basket of assets, right? Today, which one could I make sense of? One, YM, nothing else."

rule: Once the target is hit, the read is over; later price action becomes less interesting the further it has already expanded.
quote: "Now once this is hit, I have no idea what's going on anymore"

rule: If the candle 2 you identify as the reversal candle is also the expansion candle, the following candle is lower probability and often starts a new phase; ideally C2 reverses and C3 expands.
quote: "if candle 2, which we're identifying as a reversal candle, also is the expansion candle, it can set up lower probability conditions in the following candle"

rule: To frame a reversal lower you need a sweep of the previous day high or an SMT; without one there is no framework, so let the day pass.
quote: "Generally speaking, if I wanted to trade this back lower, I need a sweep of previous day high or an SMT."

rule: Don't trade against the daily profile; if a day is unclear, wait for the following day's continuation.
quote: "most of this is a bearish day, so you're fighting the daily profile. It's better off to just wait for the following day."

rule: Entry timeframe is irrelevant; what matters is having something (a wick/swing/level) to trade away from.
quote: "I just need to trade away from something."

rule: Do not short when price is far from the 4H open, deep in the hourly run (e.g. candle 6), with no 30m swing; wait for a new 4H candle.
quote: "You're not trading near the open, you're trading below below if you're to short that. 1-hour, candle 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, you're in candle 6, 30-minute. Is there any swing to trade off of? No."

rule: Rank index strength with three tools in order: SMT, candle closures, structure.
quote: "I use SMT, candle closures, and structure."

rule: He does not take raw reversal trades; he waits for a lower high (bearish) or higher low (bullish), i.e. a continuation, which saves losses when the reversal never confirms.
quote: "Basically in the simple point of my model I am waiting for a lower high if bearish and a higher low if bullish."

rule: A reversal sweep with a very large wick is not ideal.
quote: "Another thing is this sweeping out with a large wick is not that ideal."

rule: No retest is needed after a closure; enter when price closes through the level.
quote: "I'm just taking the entry when it closes through."

rule: Expansions have shallow retracements, ideally only into the lower half of the gap. A deep retracement is a reversal (V-shape / higher-timeframe wick), not a retracement.
quote: "Here's the thing about expansion, right? When you have expansion, there's shallow retracements"

rule: If expansion gets bought back up through the gap, it becomes a V-shape reversal the other way.
quote: "If this gets bought back up, this is now a V-shape reversal to the upside."

rule: Entries right off the open: use smaller size with the stop on the small swing and expect to be stopped out.
quote: "I would probably enter lower size because it's off the open"

rule: Use the stronger asset to confirm the weaker one: an inversion of a gap or a reversal on the stronger asset allows the weakest asset to continue.
quote: "So really, I'm using the current strongest asset to tell me what is up on the other ones"

rule: The easiest daily bias is a clean candle 2 closure that looks like a reversal out of a POI; it gives one to two days of expansion.
quote: "Focus on those candle 2 closures that look like a reversal... Clean candle 2 closure out of a point of interest. One day, two day."

rule: If you missed the C2-day/C3-day move, accept it; chasing later or trying to catch the reversal at every gap blows accounts.
quote: "If you missed this, you just have to accept that, right? You're going to lose if you go and try to just chase stuff around here"

rule: A good reversal structure is not tradable without a relevant level to frame it from.
quote: "The problem is this is the good structure for a New York reversal. It's just I don't have a relevant level to frame it off of."

rule: IC-CISD (intra-candle CISD) forms the higher-timeframe wick and must be off a POI; if there is no FVG or high/low, use the CISD itself.
quote: "I have a concept I created called ICCSD, which is intra candle change and state of delivery, right? So that's what forms the wick of the higher timeframe candle."

rule: Stress and slow execution mean the timeframe is too low; move up a timeframe.
quote: "What's the root cause? You're on too low of a time frame."

rule: A daily framework is required; after that any entry timeframe works, including entering on a higher timeframe.
quote: "I need a daily framework. After that, don't really care."

rule: Asia entries are typically H1 and London M15, but any works if there's a higher-timeframe wick to trade away from.
quote: "Asia is more of the H1 entries. London is more of the M50, right?"

rule: Enter only after the higher-timeframe candle's wick has formed; before that you are in drawdown.
quote: "If you trade before the wick has formed, you're in drawdown. So you want to wait for this wick to form."

rule: Use 0.5 of the wick, not OTE, as the level the swing must hold.
quote: "I would use 0.5 of this wick, not the OTE. I don't use that."

rule: Zoom out when lost on the 3m: check the hourly and 4H candles before deciding.
quote: "let's zoom out because, guys, I don't know what's going on if I'm sitting here on a three-minute time frame."

rule: A New York reversal needs a relevant level and should occur at a key time: 9:30 preferred, or 8:30; 10:00 distributes.
quote: "I want those to occur at important time levels, so either 9.30 or 10. I prefer it at 9.30. Well, it can also be 8.30, right? I prefer 8.30 or 9.30 and then 10 can distribute."

rule: If price leaves the relevant levels without hitting them, there is nothing to trade away from.
quote: "But for me, if we leave these levels, I just do not care. I can't trade away from that. And that's just my rules."

rule: Risk per trade = account drawdown / number of losing trades you accept before the account is blown.
quote: "Decide how many trades you want until account is blown, right?"

rule: After an SMT at the expected HTF wick, require the weakest asset to close below the level before calling the wick formed and seeking continuation.
quote: "And so then I would need At least the weakest asset to go and close below here, right? Because then I could say, all right, potentially that this has formed its wick"

rule: No closure means no setup; being right on the idea without the closure is still a pass.
quote: "We haven't got the closure below here, so there's still no setup."

rule: A closure through a level after a consolidation often just sweeps liquidity to go the other way; don't trade lower-timeframe consolidations when the HTF setup is weak.
quote: "you see how we want to see a closure over a level. It fails to do that, kind of consolidates, then it goes and closes through. But a lot of times that's just sweeping out liquidity to go the other way."

rule: Bias strength and required confirmation are inverse: strong bias needs little confirmation, weak bias needs a lot.
quote: "The more my bias increases, the less confirmation I need."

rule: If a setup takes too long to produce a meaningful closure or displacement, it's no longer interesting.
quote: "And now it's taken too long to form any sort of meaningful closure or displacement. So it's just not that interesting."

rule: Once short below the swept short-term low, price should not return to the opening price/gap; if it does, it likely takes the highs.
quote: "If price comes back up to here around this opening price, then it's more than likely just going to take these highs and go back up here"

rule: Trade the expanding (weakest/strongest) asset, not the lagging one.
quote: "I just don't really trade the lagging asset, generally speaking, because it's just so much slower"

rule: A V-shape reversal not off a relevant level is fake to him; don't flip bias on it.
quote: "For me, there's no reason to be bullish because we haven't hit any relevant levels. So this is all fake to me."

rule: Know where you want price to go and don't flip-flop each time price moves against you.
quote: "you just have to know where you want price to go and stop trying to just get flip floppy around"

rule: All he looks for are continuations; an intraday reversal in the direction of the daily candle is still a continuation.
quote: "Guys, you'll realize all I look for is continuations, right?... This is technically a reversal, but it's a continuation. Of the daily range, it's in the direction of the daily candle"

rule: Counter-trend trading only means trading the invalidation of his bias, not retracements against it.
quote: "So the only way I really trade counter trend is I'm trading the invalidation of my bias."

rule: A candle 2 closure only counts if the candle is a reversal candle (opens, makes the low/high, reverses); a C2 closure without that shape is ignored.
