quote: "The whole goal of candle 2 closure, guys, is to have price open, make a low, and reverse, right?"

rule: For a reversal, prefer a sweep of the high over SMT.
quote: "If we're going to reverse, you want to see it sweep that high and then go lower. Or we have SMT there, but you prefer the sweep."

rule: When in a trade and price reaches the consolidation range low, move to break even.
quote: "if it hits the range low, I just go break even because it's either going to fail or it needs to break lower"

rule: Expect a candle 3 after an hourly candle 2 closure only if it is a good closure aligned with higher-timeframe bias.
quote: "That's generally ideal if you get a good candle 2 closure and it aligns with your higher-temper and bias."

rule: Use the daily target that fits the daily range; if one index's target is too far, use another index's target.
quote: "Sure, it could reach there, but that's too much in the daily range, so I'd rather use YM as a target."

rule: Only candle 2 matters; candle 1 is arbitrary, just the candle before C2.
quote: "Well, you never actually focus on C1. You only focus on C2. C1 is just arbitrary. It just is before C2."

rule: With no CISD, he requires a V-shape, and even a V-shape needs a continuation before he trusts it.
quote: "we don't technically have a CISD bullish rate. That's when you have to require a V-shape. So the only reason I can look this way is there's a V-shape. So even with the V-shape though, you need a continuation."

rule: Only take setups that align with the higher-timeframe bias; a valid opposite-direction fractal pattern is ignored.
quote: "is this a valid fractal model pattern? Sure. Does that align with my bias? No. I can only frame to the upside today. And if I'm wrong, I'm wrong, okay?"

rule: Go in with a higher-timeframe bias; never build a trade around an SMT alone.
quote: "You have to stop going into the market. Just looking for SMT and stuff and making a reason to trade. You have to go in with a higher timeframe bias."

rule: Trade the strongest asset in the bias direction (for longs) and never the lagging/weakest one, even if it later catches up.
quote: "I don't trade the lagging asset, so I won't ever be really interested in NQ higher here."

rule: When the weakest asset flips to strongest mid-move, he does not chase it; he prefers trading the strongest asset from the start.
quote: "I don't like to trade the weakest asset when it flips because I'd rather just trade the strongest one right away"

rule: Relative strength among NQ/ES/YM tends to switch at a higher low (or the equivalent swing).
quote: "It normally happens at some sort of higher low. Happens here. That's when it switches."

rule: If relative strength is hard to read, trade ES, the middle asset; it is slower and reflects what is actually happening.
quote: "if you struggle with identifying the relative strength and weakness, just focus on the middle asset or ES, because usually these ones can kind of mess around, do their thing, and ES will just kind of do what actually is happening."

rule: Before entering, ask whether there is a low you trust to trade away from that also gives a sensible stop and R:R; if not, wait.
quote: "Do you have a low that you trust to trade away from? Do you trust this low to trade away from? Personally, I don't."

rule: Do not enter right at 09:30; give it 3-5 minutes. Missing a move is better than getting run out at the open.
quote: "So I need to wait three, five-ish minutes and see, right? Do I, maybe I missed something? Cool, right? That can happen. But I prefer that than just getting ran out right at the open."

rule: No entry without a closure over the level, plus ideally an SMT sweep on the weaker asset; a quick expansion without those is let go.
quote: "for me personally, I couldn't because we never got this closure over this level. It was very close, but I would have preferred some sort of run below here because if I get another SMT right here"

rule: An inside day is not automatically neutral or bearish: read its internal path and whether there was a bearish CISD. Open, trade lower, close up with no bearish CISD is bullish.
quote: "Now, why isn't this bearish to me, right? Because people are saying, hey, it closed inside, why isn't it bearish? Well, you also have to look at the lower timeframes"

rule: After an inside day following a weak close, he does not expect price to leave the range, so targets stay inside it (previous-day high / Monday high).
quote: "because we closed so weak on Monday, I'm not really expecting us to go outside the range. If we look at this individual formation, is this more bearish or bullish? It's more bullish."

rule: After a trend runs out relevant lows on the daily, expect a reaction rather than a further reach for lows.
quote: "Are we gonna go reach for these lows or are we gonna get a reaction, right? And considering we've trended down and we had this previous trend, I'd rather see some sort of reaction."

rule: A candle 2 closure with a large wick should have its 0.5 (EQ) respected for continuation.
quote: "This is a candle 2 closure with a large wick. So we'd respect 0.5 of this, and then we can trade higher."

rule: EQ is measured on the whole candle (wicks included), not just the body.
quote: "Do we use EQ of the whole candle or just the body? Well, the easiest way to learn that is to watch the video or go to the blog, but it's the whole candle."

rule: Relevant swings are judged by visible separation, not a mechanical percentage. Close-together highs/lows count as one; well-separated ones are each relevant targets.
quote: "Well, because there is separation between these two highs, right? It's a big difference if the high would have been like here, right?"

rule: He does not trust failure swings as levels to trade away from.
quote: "I don't really trust those failure swings, so I don't want to see like that."

rule: A level that should have produced the opposing wick but was not respected at all (e.g. a T-spot) often acts as resistance turned support.
quote: "It's like not respected at all because this is the area that would need to form this wick to trade lower, right? You see how that's just not respected at all? A lot of times that is like resistance turned into support."

rule: Trade the expansion, not the consolidation after it.
quote: "It expands, and now it's consolidating. You don't want to trade after the expansion. You want to be trading the expansion."

rule: If a valid continuation setup's target (e.g. the range low) is already taken, require additional confirmation (a further continuation) or ignore it, because a new phase of price may form.
quote: "So that's where we either wait for a continuation to trade it lower, or we just ignore it, right? Because this is where we can form a new phase of price."

rule: A setup whose range target is already hit by the time of the open/10:00 is uninteresting; stand aside in the resulting consolidation.
quote: "If we already hit that by the time it opens, right? It's not that interesting to me. And then I'd probably stay away because it's more of just a consolidation"

rule: The later in the NY session, the less time the daily candle has to trend, so interest in new setups drops.
quote: "as we go progress through the New York session, we get less and less time in the daily candle, right? ... So the further I go on into the New York session, the less I'm interested in price action for me."

rule: Use the open's volatility; do not wait hours for a 4H higher low before acting on the bias.
quote: "Because the open gives you the volatility to just go there. I'm not going to sit here and wait for four hours to say, hey, do we form a higher low to then trade it when the open, that's, it's just too late."

rule: For the 10:00 continuation, the candle should close over the body of the prior candle; ideally read the 4H closure with the lower timeframe in a reversal.
quote: "you just want to see this candle close over the body of this. Ideally, we want to focus on the 4-hour closure, but as long as this lower timeframe is in a reversal."

rule: If candle 3 does not close beyond candle 2's open, it is nothing (no signal).
quote: "About candle 3 closure, what if candle 3 does not close above or below the open on candle 2? Well, then it's nothing."

rule: The fractal model trades C3 off a C2 closure and C4 after a good C3 close, but never candle 5.
quote: "It's just a candle 2 closure trading candle 3. Oh, well, then this close is good. Trade candle 4. My model doesn't trade candle 5."

rule: There is no weekly bias, only a daily bias; a weekly profile is the chain of daily biases built from each prior day's closure.
quote: "weekly profile doesn't have to have a weekly bias, it's a daily bias. ... So weekly profile doesn't mean weekly bias. It's you're using the previous days, what they did to anticipate the next day."

rule: No OTE entries: the model assumes price does not retrace much when expanding, so a deep retrace to OTE is not an entry.
quote: "My whole fractal model is based off the fact that price doesn't retrace a lot when it's expanding. So if price goes all the way back to the OTE, I'm not looking for an entry."

rule: He does not trade reversals or consolidations (fading range breakouts back into the range); only continuation and expansion.
quote: "So really, see, I don't trade reversals, right? But if I was trading a reversal, this would be saying, hey, I can trade this back into the range."

rule: When nothing is aligned (mechanically bearish but not bearish by bias, bullish but no supporting formation), stand aside rather than trade every frame.
quote: "For me, this formation, everything here says bearish, right? But I'm not bearish. So nothing's aligned for me. So that's why I'm not interested in that."

rule: Stop trying to capture every move in the market.
quote: "So you see how it's like, stop trying to capture every move in the market?"

rule: A clean bullish daily candle is open, low, then trade higher into the close; open-low-high-low is not a clean formation to expect expansion from.
quote: "You can see now our daily candle, it's not open, low, trading higher to close, right? It's open, low, high, low, like it's not a clean formation."

rule: A target sweep (e.g. RTY sweeping the highs) is where you take profit if long; if flat, it is not a trigger.
quote: "Well, that would be your long target, right? So if you're long, that's where you take profit. But if you are not in anything, well, then you don't really do anything."

rule: In FX, when the dollar consolidates, pair a weak currency against a strong one; if nothing is clearly weak vs strong, there is no trade.
quote: "I want to find something that is weak versus something that is strong, which is not really anything."

rule: His trading window is about 08:00-10:30 NY; he does not trade London or scalp before FOMC.
quote: "8 a.m. to about 10.30. This is the window I trade."

rule: TTFM can be traded without SMT; SMT is a helper, not a requirement.
quote: "Can you trade TTFM without SMT? The answer is yes."

rule: When TTFM is invalidated, you can trade the other way.
quote: "When GTFM is invalid, trade the other way."

rule: A continuation through a swept high (instead of a reversal) is a phase-of-price outcome to expect, not a failed sweep.
quote: "We run into a high, and instead of forming a reversal, we run into a high and we continue."

rule: The daily profile's previous-day mid matters as EQ in terms of expansion.
quote: "I used that, but it's more about the EQ in terms of expansion."

rule: Score every idea on three entry criteria (enter before targets are hit, before the daily range is made, around the daily open): 3/3 good, 2/3 ok, 1/3 not good, 0/3 low probability.
quote: "If you have three of three met, that's good. Two of three met, okay. One of three, not good. 0-3 meant low problem."

rule: To stop chasing, enter around your timeframe's opens and not after the daily range has been made.
quote: "Enter around the... our time frame opens. Don't enter after daily range."

rule: Prefer longs near the daily open or the 4H candle open, not far above it.
quote: "I prefer to long near the daily open, near the open of the 4-hour candles, right? So somewhere in here, not really here."

rule: Judge the daily range by eye from the last few daily candles. Once most of the typical range is made, new trades in that direction are less appealing.
quote: "But once you get towards the high end of this range, that's when it becomes a little less appealing"

rule: Wait for the weakest asset to form the low; then look for the others to trade higher.
quote: "Wait for the weakest asset to form the low to see the other ones start to trade higher."

rule: When you can't tell whether NQ or YM will be stronger, focus on ES, which usually sits between them and is cleaner.
quote: "if NQ and YM want to whipsaw around, you don't really know what's going on, ES is generally just a more clean"

rule: Don't trade the lagging asset; long the strongest (or short the weakest). Relative strength decides which symbol actually pays.
quote: "I just don't trade the lagging asset because I want to long the strongest one."

rule: He doesn't trade reversals: let a reversal form, then trade the continuation. Don't fade a continuation.
quote: "I don't trade reversals, guys, so I let a reversal form, then I trade a continuation."

rule: Don't flip a multi-timeframe bullish bias just because there are relative equal lows below.
quote: "I'm not gonna just flip that because of some equal lows"

rule: Daily bias: a small wick plus a reversal off the previous-day low (SMT, CISD), followed by a consolidation rather than a reversal, means continuation to the previous-day high.
quote: "we have a small wick with a reversal off previous day low, right? SMT, CISD. So then if it has a small wick, I can look for it to trade to here."

rule: A consolidation after a reversal says continuation, not reversal.
quote: "Now, consolidation doesn't tell me reversal."

rule: If trading toward a high, the new protected swing low must not be taken; let the open form first.
quote: "if we're going to trade towards this high, we don't want to see this low taken. So we have a swing point forming there. You kind of got to let the open form."

rule: In the 4H-15m fractal model, stay with the bias for the whole 06:00-10:00 4H expansion candle. The lower-timeframe expansion should finish before 10:00, so time-box the move (his yellow box).
quote: "I just want to see this before 10 a.m. because the whole idea is this is a four-hour expansion candle, right? Our lower timeframes are expansion candles as well. When does this end? 10 a.m."

rule: Pick the entry from the invalidation (where a stop can go), not from a preset entry timeframe.
quote: "Stop thinking about what time frame my entry needs to be on and start thinking about where could my stop be placed because that tells you"

rule: If a market entry doesn't give the R you want (e.g. 2R to the target), use a limit order lower; for about 1R a market entry is fine.
quote: "So if we want to get 2R to this high, right, where do we have, can we enter on the close there? No, we'd have to adjust it down to limit entry there"

rule: Once the target is hit, the daily range is reached and price has closed into the highs, stop looking for longs. Any further idea must be a reversal framed across the hit level.
quote: "So this is where I'm uninterested in any long setups, right? Because my long ideas played out."

rule: A real liquidity sweep gives a V-shape reaction; a lethargic reaction after a sweep is just part of a consolidation.
quote: "It sweeps and then it's just kind of lethargic versus a V-shape."

rule: A reversal off the previous-day high needs an aggressive V-shape. Without it, expect continuation.
quote: "If you don't form a V-shape off previous day high, then it's just nothing"

rule: Reversal off the previous-day high at a new 4H open: the new 4H sweeps the previous 4H candle and leaves a small wick. Target the previous 4H candle's 0.5 or the lows.
quote: "Previous day high, new 4-hour open, we sweep out the previous candle, small wick, this is when we can trade back to the previous 4-hour EQ, or all the way down here if we want."

rule: When he does trade a reversal, use very small stops and wait for a CISD.
quote: "If I'm ever trading a reversal, I'm trying to get in with very small stops, because I either want to be wrong or right right away."

rule: A short needs a protected swing. Failure swings alone aren't enough, and he wants a shallow sweep rather than a deep one.
quote: "see how we don't make any protected swing? Right? Only a failure swings. Normally I want to see a shallow sweep of that to go lower, but it's a bit deep."

rule: After a sweep, the 0.5 of the CISD must hold. A close back over it is a bad sign for the idea.
quote: "Well, what do we want to see hold in the CISD? 0.5 of it, right?"

rule: Swings must have separation. Two highs left close together without a sweep form a consolidation, not a relevant swing to trade from.
quote: "we either need to sweep this out to form a relevant swing to trade lower, but when we leave highs like this, that just becomes like a consolidation"

rule: SMT is only a confluence to an existing model/framework. Never trade SMT on its own.
quote: "SMT should be a confluence to an already existing model."

rule: An SMT in an FX pair counts when the dollar's own read supplies the framework.
quote: "See how now this SMT makes sense? Because we actually have a framework aligned with it, the dollar, right?"

rule: Continuation order block: after a change in state of delivery, price either reaches into an FVG and closes back over it, or sweeps a low and closes back over. At its simplest it's waiting for a higher low or lower high to use as a protected swing.
quote: "at its basic level, what I do is wait for a higher low and then I trade that or a lower high."

rule: Trade the expansion, not after it. After an expansion, only the reversal scenario (a sweep) is tradable.
quote: "Because you want to trade the expansion, you don't want to trade after the expansion."

rule: At the high of day above the previous-day high after an expansion, a long is chasing; the only frameable idea is a short back into the range.
quote: "We are at the high of the day over previous day's highs after we've already expanded. There's no reason too long here. This is where you would be chasing longs."

rule: Trade only with all three: a bias, a lower-timeframe fractal model aligned with it, and a continuation.
quote: "Do you have a bias? Do you have a lower timeframe fractal model aligned with that? And then do you have a continuation? If you have that, sure."

rule: He doesn't always wait for the C2 close; it depends on bias and framework.
quote: "Not always. Kind of depends on my bias and framework, what I'm expecting."

rule: A close slightly outside the POI is not a C2 closure; it needs more confluence.
quote: "Well, it wouldn't be a C2 closure, but you need some more confluence."

rule: Don't wait for an order-block retest; enter at the OB with the stop beyond it.
quote: "I just enter there with my stop there, right? Like, I don't know if it's going to come back and retest it."

rule: If unsure whether a move is a retracement or a reversal, target a retracement and treat anything extra as a bonus.
quote: "Don't know which it is, you kind of anticipate a retracement, and then any extra is great."

rule: The next relevant low (the 4H low next to the move) is the first target and a likely reaction point.
quote: "That's very relevant low, because where's the lows next to it? Like, this is the next relevant low, so that's why this is important to me."

rule: Don't trade after a huge candle (e.g. a 4H C3 after a monster range). The exception is the 06:00-10:00 4H expansion continuing into the 10:00 candle.
quote: "the only time I would say a huge, massive candle and we can get another one is when this is at 6 a.m. to 10 and then 10 a.m. continues."

rule: Don't short at the lows after the move has happened; the continuation entry was earlier.
quote: "You don't want to trade short at the lows."

rule: Use context (e.g. the previous-day high) for higher-timeframe reversals, not candle patterns alone.
quote: "stop trying to pattern trade it and focus on some context."

rule: Don't trade the middle of a range; trade from the range extremes back in.
quote: "I'd focus on the highs of the range to trade back in"

rule: Skip an asset that has already hit its target for the day (gold, YM today).
quote: "that's not a trade that I want because we already hit a target."

rule: On choppy days don't trade, and cap daily losses at one or two losing trades.
quote: "When you see stuff that's choppy, Get off, don't trade it."

rule: Form no view on tomorrow until today's daily candle closes.
quote: "I don't think about tomorrow until I get the daily close."

rule: Red-folder news at 10:00 usually isn't volatile enough to stop you out unless you're on a very small timeframe.
quote: "It doesn't, it's not volatile enough to normally run you out of a position unless you're on like a super small timeframe."

rule: Crypto: use higher stacks (daily-H4-15m or daily-H1) because the lower timeframes are too volatile.
quote: "I'd focus on, you know, daily H4 and 15 or daily H1"

rule: He doesn't use midnight-open statistics.
quote: "I don't even use midnight open, so it's not anything for me."

rule: Execute a 15m swing continuation on the 3m; the 1m is too noisy. If analysis takes too long, move up a timeframe.
quote: "I just don't really like the one-minute chart. Like, there's just too much going on in the one-minute."

rule: Treat paper trading exactly like real money.
quote: "Read paper like it's real. Otherwise, you're just going to build bad habits"

rule: Easiest daily bias: on the daily chart, a candle 2 or candle 3 closure confirmed by an H1 CISD is your daily bias.
quote: "Is there a candle 2 or candle 3 closure with H1 CISD? If so, that's your daily bias."

rule: After the daily C2/C3 + H1 CISD bias, confirm it with the daily profile; a bias without a confirming daily profile is not traded.
quote: "The next thing, though, is you need to confirm that with the daily profile, right?"

rule: Bullish daily profile: price opens, makes a low, then trades higher. If it opens and expands straight into objectives instead, the profile leans bearish, back to the daily open.
quote: "You want to see price open, make some sort of low and then trade higher, right?"

rule: The daily profile is middle-timeframe structure, the structure of the daily candle; read it on 4H, 1H or 15m (he prefers the hourly).
quote: "So daily profile is middle timeframe structure. The daily profile is the structure of the daily candle."

rule: When there is no established/protected low of the day and price just trades higher into NY, New York is normally bearish back toward the daily open.
quote: "we just trade higher we get some structure like this and in new york it's normally bearish back to the daily open and around that"

rule: A bias alone is not enough: you need lower-timeframe structure aligned with it, i.e. a low (or high) to trade away from.
quote: "That's great to have a bias, but what do I need with a bias? I need lower timeframe structure that aligns with that."

rule: To frame longs you need a sweep of a relevant low or an SMT at it (a sweep on another asset); without one, a bullish bias produces no long setup.
quote: "I need something at this relevant level, which is either a sweep of it or an SMT, which is a sweep on another one."

rule: To frame a reversal lower at the open, price should open, go higher first (into the POI), then go lower. Opening lower first and then higher invalidates it.
quote: "If I'm wanting to frame something as a downside, I want to see price open, go higher first, then go lower. I don't want to see price open, go lower, then go higher, then go lower."

rule: Three entry timing rules: enter before targets are hit, before the daily range is created, and around the daily open.
quote: "Enter before targets hit. Enter before daily range created. Enter around the daily open."

rule: Relative strength: if bullish, trade the strongest asset; if bearish, trade the weakest.
quote: "If you're bullish, you focus on YM. If you're bearish, you focus on NQ, right?"

rule: For a short on the weakest asset to work, the strongest asset must also reverse; if the weakest hits its low and reverses, the others are unlikely to go lower.
quote: "Like, you want to see the strongest asset start to fall, so the weakest asset can fall as well."

rule: Use SMT as confirmation, not to frame trades: price must first displace in the intended direction before the SMT is relevant.
quote: "A lot of people use SMT to just frame things. You want to use SMT as a confirmation, right?"

rule: He does not trust an equal-high SMT.
quote: "I just don't really like the equal high SMT like that because it's not that bad."

rule: Fading the daily candle (especially on day three of an expansion) is a reversal trade and needs more confirmation; he generally avoids it.
quote: "Trying to fade the daily candle on a day three, it's not as great."

rule: When you have no bias or don't know what is going on, don't trade, and zoom out rather than sit on lower timeframes.
quote: "And the one thing I do is when I don't know what's going on on the indices, I don't sit on the lower timeframes, guys. I zoom out because it's not going to help me."

rule: Hold one idea per session and wait for it to occur or invalidate; once invalidated, you are done for that idea.
quote: "I have one idea and I look for that to either occur or to invalidate, right?"

rule: A valid reversal displaces away in a V-shape; the longer price takes to reverse (consolidation, failure swings), the less interesting it gets.
quote: "We want to see like a displacement away, right? We want to see a V shape, right? We don't want to see this and then consolidation, right?"

rule: If price is going to go, it usually goes right away; it does not sit for an hour or two after the open.
quote: "The thing is, if price is gonna go somewhere, it just usually just goes. It doesn't sit here for an hour or two."

rule: A good continuation reaches cleanly over the level and closes; rejecting the level and coming back inside turns it into consolidation.
quote: "You want to see a nice, clean reach over the level? Close. You don't normally want to see price reject that level, come back in and do that because then it becomes a consolidation."

rule: Confirmation of a continuation after a weak reversal is a new lower-timeframe swing (a new LTF high for shorts), rather than gaps or displacement per se.
quote: "Gaps, displacement, for me, it's just I look for a new high, like lower, lower time from high to form."

rule: A lower-timeframe FVG at a low is just that low; price reacting off it without closing below means a LTF low swept to go higher. Require a close below it on your entry timeframe (3m).
quote: "This fair value gap is literally just this low. That's all it is."

rule: After a close below the level, the 50% of that move should hold with no consolidation; each minute without a drop builds failure swings and lowers interest.
quote: "Then you want to see 50% of that hold. So if it already hits this, you want to see that close below. You don't really want to see it consolidate."

rule: For a bear idea into a new 4H candle, price should respect 0.5 of the prior wick; returning above it means bearish is wrong.
quote: "And usually I'm just focused on 0.5 of that wick, 0.5 of that wick."

rule: If you take a reversal, price should not return to the reversal point; he would be at breakeven once it does not follow through.
quote: "So now if I was short on a reversal though, I would be breakeven, right? Because you don't want to see the reversal return back to this point."

rule: Once in a trade with a defined invalidation, ignore lower-timeframe closures; only check the HTF candle the setup is based on (e.g. 4H C3 closure).
quote: "Really, the only thing I'd want to look for is this is based off of a four-hour swing point. This is four-hour candle 3. So I want to see how this candle closes on the four-hour."

rule: Read CISD using both the previous candle's price action and the current candle's; don't box off the prior candle.
quote: "Well, you gotta use both."

rule: Macros are just new higher-timeframe candle opens (10:00 4H/1H/30m); understand HTF opens and closes instead.
quote: "All it is is a new higher timeframe candles."

rule: Ignore DXY when trading indices; the correlation is not reliable lately.
quote: "I could care less what the dollar is doing in terms of taking a trade on the indices."

rule: In FX, pair a bullish currency with a bearish one, not with one that is consolidating; that is where expansion occurs.
quote: "You want to pair them opposite directions because that's what expansion occurs."

rule: In an uptrend, enter either on a sweep of a low or on a retrace into a fair value gap.
quote: "All you're looking for is either a sweep of a low to then trade, or for price to retrace into a fair value gap, oops, to then trade it higher."

rule: A POI that price closes through (e.g. a 1H FVG closed below while sweeping, not aggressively bought back) is not trusted to trade away from; closely spaced lows also need a sweep first.
quote: "Let's say we are truly going to trend today. We would respect this area, right? Makes sense, right? So that means we wouldn't really go close below this gap, right?"

rule: Don't trust the first retracement after price expands away from the open; it can be swept. Wait for a close over and a continuation.
quote: "because when you expand away from the open, right, I don't trust this initial retracement back in, because to me, it's like I can go sweep that."

rule: Don't chase a late continuation at the high of the day: gold's candle 6 move into the high is not worth trading even though the 4H C3 bias is intact.
quote: "This is candle 6, like I said. So yeah, not amazing on gold."

rule: C5 is not normally traded; it depends on whether an open objective remains.
quote: "C5 isn't normally something I trade, it just depends if you have an open objective or not."

rule: A small-wick daily reversal can be traded as candle 2 if you trade C2; otherwise let it close and trade candle 3.
quote: "That would be so if you're trading candle 2, yeah. If not, you let it close and you're still trading candle 3."

rule: Inside a range, big moves usually just draw people in on both sides; don't chase them.
quote: "when we're inside a range like this and you see the market make big moves like this, it usually is just drawing people in, right?"

rule: Not fitting the model is reason enough to skip a breakout; you will miss moves trading mechanically, and that is expected.
quote: "It doesn't mean it can't break out. It just doesn't fit my model to trade that breakout."

rule: Feel the emotion, don't act on it; emotions can't be eliminated, only not acted upon.
quote: "Feel the emotion. Wow, I spelled so bad, right? Don't act on it, right?"

rule: To stop blowing accounts, identify the root cause and fix it: overtrading means max one trade a day, no system means learn a model, oversizing means size correctly.
quote: "Well, if I'm tilting or over-trading, max one trade a day."

rule: For crypto, use higher timeframes; crypto setups sweep both sides before moving and trend less cleanly than indices.
quote: "if you're going to trade it on crypto, you're better off focusing on some higher timeframes, right?"

rule: He trades only the NY AM session and considers about 10:30 past his window.
quote: "I can't trade anything now. It's past my time that I would be anything."

rule: For daily bias with his model, use the daily-hourly (1D-1H) fractal model: when it appears, its direction is your bias for that day.
quote: "So if you want to use my model for daily bias, you just use the daily and hourly model when it appears that's your bias."

rule: Trade continuations in line with the daily candle; an open-high daily candle supports lower prices, so do not take counter-trend longs even if a lower-timeframe model forms.
quote: "Personally, for me, I trade continuations in line with the daily candle. This daily candle is open high, so it supports price lower, right?"

rule: To anticipate a reversal across correlated indices, the strongest asset must reverse (sweep) off a level; then the weaker assets can continue. Without that reversal or an SMT, do not trade away from the level.
quote: "Because it's the strongest asset, so if the strongest asset can reverse, then the weakest assets can get a continuation."

rule: If price never reversed off the intended level, you cannot anticipate the reversal; wait for a continuation to form, after which price should not return there.
quote: "So we can't look for the actual reversal point here. We need to wait for a continuation, because once we form a continuation, we can say, okay, it shouldn't return there, right?"

rule: Judge relative strength between NQ/ES/YM from the most recent hourly candle closures: the asset with the bearish close is weakest; short the weakest (or long the strongest).
quote: "Look at this previous hourly candle close versus this one. Which one is stronger? Which one is weaker? YM is clearly weaker, right? Look at its candle closure. Very bearish."

rule: Pick the asset by lower-timeframe relative strength (the timeframe you execute on), not by which asset has the bearish daily candle; the bias can come from one index and the trade from another.
quote: "You care more about what the lower time frame relative strength and weakness is doing."

rule: Only trade the strongest or the weakest asset; never trade the lagging asset hoping it will follow.
quote: "Personally, I always like to trade the strongest or the weakest. I don't like to trade the one hoping it will follow."

rule: On low-expectation days, protected swings (highs/lows that swept earlier ones) are hard to reach; target the failure swing to the right of the protected swing instead.
quote: "So in that case, if I have lower expectations, right, and I have a protected swing, I'll look at the failure swing to the right of it as a target."

rule: If an asset has already made its average daily range (judged by eye from this month's daily candles), avoid trading it further in that direction.
quote: "So when it already hits that, that's when I kind of want to avoid it."

rule: Do not trade away from a market that failed to reach a relevant level (e.g. no high taken), however good the hourly pattern looks.
quote: "Why? Well, why would I try to short away when it has failed to reach a relevant level?"

rule: A trade must come out of a point of interest, normally a high or a fair value gap (not necessarily a higher-timeframe FVG).
quote: "No, I want it to be out of a point of interest, which is normally a high or a fair value gap."

rule: His candle 2 needs a small wick; he essentially does not trade reversal days (large wick trading back to the open).
quote: "If you go look at how I trade candle 2, I need a small wick. I don't ever trade a reversal day, really. That's a large wick, trading back to the open."

rule: The whole model: a change in the state of delivery, then a continuation in the next higher-timeframe candle, and take that trade.
quote: "I have some sort of change in the state of delivery, and then in this next higher timeframe candle, I'm looking for a continuation, and then I literally take that trade."

rule: Use the highest timeframe pairing that makes sense (4H-15m or 1H-5m).
quote: "But really, I just use the highest time frame I can where it makes sense."

rule: Preferred trading window is the 06:00-10:00 4H candle; if nothing sets up, wait for the 10:00 open.
quote: "No, I actually prefer to trade the 6-10 a.m. 4-hour candle or in that range."

rule: Pre-open decision: if you have an anticipation, trade the open; if not, wait for the open; if the open gives nothing, wait for 10:00.
quote: "if I have an anticipation, I can trade the open. If I don't, I need to wait for the open. I waited for the open today. The open didn't tell me anything, right? It didn't give me what I wanted. So then I have to wait for 10 a.m."

rule: Checklist: for each asset ask whether you understand/can anticipate the daily candle; only if yes go to the lower timeframe for an aligned fractal model, otherwise skip it.
quote: "Daily. Ready? And it'll say, do you understand the daily chart? ... Yes. Cool. Then go lower. Find fractal model aligned with that. And then we repeat it. No, don't go lower. That's literally my checklist."

rule: For FX, check the dollar first; if the dollar is not clean, do not look at the pairs.
quote: "But forex, all I'd look for is a dollar. If the dollar is clean, then I can look at the other ones. Otherwise, I'm not looking at anything, right?"

rule: When the plan's reversal does not happen at the open, keep the plan rather than chasing other assets or switching ideas.
quote: "So instead of chasing stuff around and trying to switch my plan, my plan remained the same."

rule: You cannot form tomorrow's expectation until today's daily candle has closed.
quote: "So has the daily closed? No. So how can I anticipate what's gonna happen tomorrow if the daily candle hasn't closed? I can't."

rule: If timeframes conflict and you are confused, avoid; do not short at the low of the day after a big low was taken, and do not long against a bearish daily candle.
quote: "If you're confused, guys, you just avoid, right?"

rule: Do not fade a bearish expansion daily candle; wait for a new daily candle and then watch the previous-day low reaction or an SMT there.
quote: "Currently, this is a bearish expansion. I don't want to fade that daily candle, so I would be waiting for a new daily candle."

rule: In a consolidation (e.g. a monthly range) favor trading back into the range from its extremes, but only with a fresh daily candle/phase at the level.
quote: "So it's a consolidation. So really you favor trading back into the range."

rule: After the open, a clean fall through the low is wanted; an aggressive bounce off the low means price returns to the range and chops.
quote: "Do not want to see price of a very aggressive move off this low. Like, you want it to ideally just fall through. Otherwise, it's just going to come back in the range and chop around."

rule: A C3 that opens without a wick usually comes from a lower-timeframe protected swing formed before the higher-timeframe candle opened.
quote: "Usually that occurs if you have a lower timeframe protected swing prior to the open of the higher timeframe candle."

rule: When the 4H has already run several candles (C2-C5) in the direction, it is extended and not interesting; entering after price has travelled far is a chase.
quote: "The four hours a bit extended, right? If you look, candle 2, 3, 4, 5. 2, 3, 4, 5, already went lower. It's just not super interesting."

rule: He takes only a couple of trades a week at most and does not trade every day.
quote: "I only take a couple trades a week max."

rule: He ignores news and macro for trading decisions.
quote: "I don't really use macroeconomics and major news events in my trading decisions. I genuinely do not care."

rule: Two SMTs off a high (other indices took it, this one did not) mark that index as the weakest.
quote: "So you can see ES and YM both took out this high, with my indicator showing, right? So you can see the SMT there."

rule: Set an alert at the level you need (here YM's high) instead of watching a market that has not reached it.
quote: "So really, we can probably just set an alert right here. I'm really only interested in anything if YM runs this high."

rule: Daily bias comes from the previous daily closure: after a bearish daily candle 2 closure, ask whether the previous day high or low is more likely, then trade only toward the previous day low.
quote: "The only reason I'm bearish today is we had a bearish closure yesterday. Is it more likely for me to see previous day high or previous day low? To me, previous day low."

rule: Confirm the daily high/low (wick) either with a CISD on the session timeframe (Asia H1; London H1/M30, rarely M15; New York M15/M5) or with an H4/H1 candle 2 closure at a relevant POI, never below H1 for the closure.
quote: "Now, this is going to be on a higher time frame, so it's either going to be an H4 closure or H1 closure. I would not really go below those two, and it's going to be a candle 2 closure. At a relevant POI"

rule: Confirm a daily C2 bias on the hourly with a change in the state of delivery, ideally with SMT.
quote: "Hourly change in the state of delivery, we also have an SMT, right? So I can be looking for a continuation lower in this next day."

rule: With a daily candle 2 closure, the EQ of that candle must be respected for the continuation.
quote: "With a candle 2 closure, what do we want to see be respected? The EQ."

rule: If London has formed the reversal (high/low of day), New York is only a continuation; frame nothing else.
quote: "I have considered that London has formed a reversal, so that means New York, to me, is only a continuation to the downside. I cannot personally frame anything else."

rule: On a London-reversal continuation day, expect 9:30 to drive price (volatility, not manipulation), because the manipulation already happened inside the daily range.
quote: "If we're expecting a continuation, we expect volatility to drive price, not manipulate price. Why don't we expect manipulation? Because we've already manipulated within the daily range."

rule: His favourite setup: daily C3/C4 + London reversal + a 15-minute continuation entry before the NYSE open.
quote: "Daily C3 slash C4, London reversal, and 15 continuation prior to NYSE open. I will do this. That's literally my favorite."

rule: Pre-open continuation entries go on the 15m, not the 5m; the 5m chops you out.
quote: "You can trade a five-minute continuation, sure, but for the most times, pre-open, you want to be at the 15-minute, just because five-minute, you can get chopped up"

rule: Don't take a continuation without an invalidation you can trust; equal highs without SMT are not a trustworthy stop. With SMT, the opposing candles become the stop reference.
quote: "If we had SMT here, right? If it looks like that, what becomes our opposing candles? Now we can use this, right? ... So without an SMT there, I can't trust this high personally within my system"

rule: Separate the idea (anticipation) from the setup: a bias without a sensible stop location is not a trade.
quote: "There's a difference between an idea and having the setup to actually execute on, right?"

rule: If you are uncertain about relative strength between NQ, ES and YM, focus on ES; NQ and YM bounce around, and ES is the most consistent.
quote: "If we're uncertain on relative strength, Focus on ES because YM and NQ are the ones that will bounce around, right? ES will just be in the middle."

rule: Avoid the lagging-asset trade: don't chase the index that has rebounded when another index is already making the move.
quote: "We can see NQ go lower. It's just that'd be a lagging asset trade, and I just don't like the lagging asset"

rule: Time-based exit: a 9:30 expansion usually ends at 10:00, when the 4H/1H/30m candles close; sometimes at 9:45 with a new 15m.
quote: "You guys all got to write 10 a.m. because it's a 4-hour expansion, hourly expansion, 30-minute expansion. It can sometimes be 9.45 that they'll flip around because you have a 15-minute expansion ending"

rule: Enter early in the candle, around the open or in the wick of the HTF candle; entering late in the candle after the move is a chase.
quote: "Ideally, you want to be entering around the open or above the wick. This is early into the candle. We're late into the candle, almost at the end of it"

rule: Don't enter after the move has already happened; it destroys risk to reward.
quote: "Personally, I don't enter after this move down, because then it destroys all risk to reward, like against me."

rule: When bearish, sell around the daily open or in the daily wick, not below the previous day low; prefer to sell before the first target is hit.
quote: "If I'm bearish, I want to be selling around the daily open or in the wick of it. ... I don't want to be selling below previous day low, generally speaking"

rule: Skip assets whose daily target is already reached (gold/silver below the previous day low, oil above its highs); he doesn't long over highs or short under lows.
quote: "Guys, it's a continuation, but here's the thing, it's already below the previous day low. That's why I said I'm not a huge fan of it. ... I'm not afraid, not a fan of longing over the highs."

rule: Shorting under the lows after an expansion into a low sets you up for a new phase of price (consolidation/reversal); short inside the higher-timeframe candles.
quote: "You have price expanding into a low. You can expect some sort of new phase of price. So, like, why would you short here? You should short in the higher time frame candles."

rule: Price phases alternate expansion -> consolidation; a consolidation is usually left at a new higher-timeframe candle, so trade the beginning of a new HTF candle, not its end.
quote: "So consolidation, normally, if it's gonna leave it, it'll be at the new higher time from candle."

rule: When the dollar is mid-range, pair currencies against it (find the weakest/strongest counterpart) to locate the real expansion.
quote: "if the dollar's not really getting super clean movement, you want to pair currencies to find the actual expansion"

rule: A HTF candle that is just a ranged candle gives no edge on its own; wait for the open.
quote: "If you look, this 4-hour candle is just a ranged candle. It could really go either way."

rule: A protected swing that holds is still valid even if price retraces deep into the leg; don't judge it from very low timeframes or stops that are too tight.
quote: "That's protected. Now that's protected. It's still following the trend. So unless you're too low and jamming your stop, that shouldn't have stopped you out."

rule: Use his indicator's daily and hourly boxes for bias: gray box = bearish, green box = bullish.
quote: "So literally all I'd use for bias is I just go to daily and hourly with my indicator. It has a gray box. I look to be bearish in the gray box."

rule: Have only one or two ideas per day; on this day only one direction (downside on indices).
quote: "You guys can notice from my streams, I really only have one to two ideas each day."

rule: A 9:30 non-move on an FOMC day is not a concern; the afternoon news is likely to make the move. Don't trade FOMC or post-FOMC.
quote: "The only thing to note is if 930 doesn't make a move, I don't really care too much because we have FOMC later in the day, which is likely to make the actual move."

rule: Use higher-timeframe candles for timing, not kill zones.
quote: "I don't really use kill zones. I just use higher time frame candles."

rule: Don't sit on the 1-minute guessing; focus on the higher-timeframe context.
quote: "We're not going to go down here and sit on a one-minute and try to just guess things. We're focused on the actual context of stuff."

rule: After an index breaks a daily swing low, project continuation in the other indices to their own draws (ES previous day low, NQ line) rather than chasing the one that broke.
quote: "So clearly YM is dropping through this level. So what's the next level here, right? Which means the other assets we can look for will end or ES into previously low and Q down to here."

rule: A trade idea is anticipation, not knowledge; you never know the next outcome.
quote: "But the thing is in trading, you don't know things for a fact, right? You never know the outcome of your next trade."

rule: Learn the 4H-15m model first; a mentee's 4 months of gold on it gave 48 trades, 63% win rate, 63R, average 1.93R taking 2R targets.
quote: "Four months of 2026 on gold tested the 4-hour and 15-minute model. I understand why you asked beginners to focus on this."

rule: Trade in the direction of the daily candle: a small-wicked daily candle trading higher supports expansion higher and should not be faded.
quote: "I want to trade candles in the direction of their daily timeframe."

rule: The whole model: daily bias, one more timeframe aligned, then a reversal and a continuation in line with both, then enter; kill zones don't matter.
quote: "That's my model right there. That's the whole thing, right? Daily bullish, let's say this is 4-hour, 15-entry."

rule: Have the model first; SMT is only confirmation or confluence, never the basis of a trade.
quote: "I have to have an actual framework first, and then I use SMT to give me confirmation of that, or a confluence."

rule: Once price takes the highs without forming a continuation the other way, the bearish profile is invalidated; with the target already hit and price expanded, there is no framework and he will not buy above the highs.
quote: "Now that we're above the highs, this profile doesn't support expansion lower. It's kind of an invalidation trade."

rule: There is only one CISD per day and it forms the daily wick; if London made it, New York is a continuation.
quote: "Well, you really only have one change in the state of delivery per day. That forms the daily wick."

rule: A CISD is the order block that confirms a shift in trend; later same-direction formations are continuations, not new CISDs.
quote: "That is the OB that confirms a shift in trend."

rule: Protected swings stay protected until the high (the target extreme) is taken; after that, price often runs a protected swing and then continues, often around the EQ.
quote: "These all are protected until when, until this high is taken out."

rule: A swing is protected by a close beyond it, but he discounts a 15m close he doesn't trust ('technically protecting this low, I just don't think it's protected').
quote: "they did close over here, so technically protecting this low, I just don't think it's protected, personally speaking."

rule: The only POIs he uses are fair value gaps, highs and lows.
quote: "POIs to use. Your value gaps, highs, lows. That's it."

rule: If a protected swing exists going into the open he does not want a sweep; without a continuation on any asset he needs one asset to run a low on the open first.
quote: "So I want one of these assets on the open to take out a low. Otherwise, there's zero interest."

rule: A counter-daily reversal can only be framed at a new higher-timeframe candle (the 10:00 4H open) with SMT; 09:30 must manipulate to trade 09:30, otherwise wait for 10:00.
quote: "So we have to wait till 10 a.m. ... 10 a.m. would have to essentially open up for my reversal"

rule: Wait for the 15m closure (09:45 / 10:00) before aligning a fractal model off the open.
quote: "So this 15-minute, we kind of have to wait until 9.45 because this doesn't support expansion."

rule: When looking lower, don't trade the strongest asset, and don't chase the asset that already moved; trade the middle asset that is still in the upper half of the range toward the target.
quote: "You don't trade the strongest asset if you're looking lower."

rule: Dealing range entry: measured from the extreme to the target, short in the upper half and long in the lower half.
quote: "you want to be entering into the upper half short or lower half long"

rule: With a large daily wick, the intraday target for a retracement is back toward the daily open.
quote: "if we have a larger wick, your target's back towards the daily open."

rule: A clean day: trade a daily C3 and a 4H C4 with a protected swing, timeframes aligned for expansion and not already expanded.
quote: "Really, you need to align multiple timeframes together for expansion. Having them not already be expanded and then find a protected swing."

rule: Candle 2 is always the swing point; the only two swing definitions are the C2 closure (sweep and close) and the C3 closure (for engulfing moves), then trade the continuation.
quote: "And so then I figured out candle 2 closure. Then I realized not all of them sweep and then close, some engulf. But then I was like, okay, candle 3 closure."

rule: Only wicks on doji or hammer/shooting-star candles are used as wick POIs (not generic rejection blocks).
quote: "I only use wicks on doji candles or hammer shooter candles."

rule: Enter with the daily bias around the opening price early in the candle, not at the highs after a decent daily range.
quote: "I'm not going to enter long right at the highs, right? Like we took out some highs, we're already at a decent daily range. This is not the area to look along."

rule: Phases of price: manipulation at a range edge leads to expansion, expansion leads to consolidation, retracement leads to expansion.
quote: "In the most simple sense, price either expands or consolidates."

rule: If price does not respect a level it should have reacted from (e.g. a monthly low), treat it as consolidation and trade to the other side of the range.
quote: "So if it's not respecting it, now it's just a consolidation. So trade into the consolidation low, trade higher."

rule: A real continuation shows up early and trends; if it fails to, treat the move as a range and target the opposite end.
quote: "But if we were going to get a continuation, we would have just done it early on and started trending."

rule: If the continuation fails, expect chop.
quote: "If it fails this continuation, then that's just telling you that it's going to chop."

rule: A reversal trade needs more confirmation: let a gap form, then wait for a continuation (new opposing candle) out of it.
quote: "You wait for some sort of continuation in here, right? A new opposing candle, right? But you have to let that gap form."

rule: A new 4H candle (10:00) can bring a different phase of price, especially after a full day of expansion before 10:00.
quote: "New 4-hour candle can be a different phase of price."

rule: After shorting the top, breakeven is fine because a valid continuation should not come back; once a candle closes below, the high is mechanically protected and the stop can sit there.
quote: "Then, mechanically, this should be protected so your stop could be right there."

rule: Entries in line with the daily and 4H can be more aggressive; entries opposing the daily range should be less aggressive.
quote: "Are you going to want to be more aggressive on an entry here that's opposing the daily range, all of that? Probably not as aggressive, right?"

rule: Ideal continuation: in line with the daily candle, in line with another timeframe, a reversal, and a new protected swing.
quote: "In line with the daily candle, in line with another time frame, and then you have a reversal, and it's a new protected swing."

rule: He trades continuations, not reversals; a 4H reversal against the daily range is inherently harder and more likely to get stopped.
quote: "Like, look, you're trading a reversal on the 4-hour against the daily range. Daily is bullish. It's just going to be harder to trade"

rule: Timeframe stacks: daily-4H-15m for Asia/London/NY with a London reversal; daily-1H-5m for a New York reversal or New York manipulation; daily-1H alone is valid.
quote: "I think that this is better for New York reversal, New York manipulation."

rule: Frame exotics (JPY crosses) only when the dollar is consolidating.
quote: "you only look to frame exotics when dollar is consolidating."

rule: Monday is usually an opposing run to the weekly range or consolidation; trade Monday only if Friday reversed.
quote: "The only time I'll trade Monday is if Friday has reversed."

rule: The daily bias concept is fractal and applies to the weekly.
quote: "Yeah, you can. It's fractal."

rule: Bullish closure first, then trade the continuation: for a reversal off a monthly low he waits for today's daily close and needs price to hold the EQ/level the next day.
quote: "I would need today to close, use the EQ, probably this level, need price to hold up this level tomorrow to trade higher."

rule: Discipline plan: one trade a day, 2R or -1R with no management, proper size, follow the rules/model, for a month.
quote: "So limit to one trade a day, 2R or minus 1R. Basically, you're not managing your position at all because that removes the over-managing aspect."

rule: Journaling only helps if you review the journal to find the root causes (tilt, oversizing, revenge, not following model, blow-up days, over-managing).
quote: "You can't just journal and say you don't know the cause. You have to journal and then go review your journal."

rule: Swing trades: the entry timeframe matters little; stop on the daily low still gives good R:R.
quote: "I can just put my stop on the daily low and that's still a really good RR, right?"

rule: Tools he does not use: ICT macros, kill zones, order flow, breakers, rejection blocks, DXY for index correlation, the weekly EQ, RTY, the 1m chart.
quote: "I believe in macroeconomics, but I don't believe in ICT macros. I think those are fake."

rule: Reaction trading (hit a POI at 10:00 and react) is something he avoids; he prefers a clean daily framework.
quote: "The thing is, is like, this type of trading is more reaction trading to me, which I stray away from, generally speaking"

rule: When the index expands away from the open without establishing a low of the day, it usually favors a move back toward the daily open / into the range, not continuation.
quote: "No established low. Usually that favors a move back. It has kind of a low there. Usually it favors a move back towards the daily open, right?"

rule: Intraday, a multi-candle expansion away followed by a reversal in the NY session behaves like the Thursday counter in his weekly profile: favor back into the range.
quote: "We expand away multiple candles. This is like a Thursday, but it's just New York session, forming a reversal, favoring back into the range."

rule: A 1H candle 2 closure plus CISD, with a protected swing forming at the start of the next candle, gives a tradable continuation toward the gap.
quote: "Right, candle 2 closure, CISD. You have a protected swing that forms at the start of this next candle. You can trade this continuation lower."

rule: You will not always have a POI to the left. At highs with nothing to the left, use an average-daily-range estimate as the POI and keep trading the candles in front of you.
quote: "You could probably pull up an average daily range and we're almost at it, so that can be your POI. But you're not going to have a POI at all times."

rule: If Asia and London already expanded and there is no nearby draw on liquidity, do not frame a continuation; favor the retracement or reversal.
quote: "And like right here, it's like you don't have a draw on liquidity. There's nothing to range for. So it's like you favor the retracement. Retracement or reversal."

rule: To trade the stronger correlated asset into its level, first wait for the weakest asset to form a reversal, then trade the stronger one.
quote: "So if your idea is to trade YM here, well, then you just wait until the weakest asset, which is this one, forms a reversal."

rule: Correlated indices like to move together; when one diverges, the one going the other way is usually 'lying' and will follow.
quote: "So if one just continues way down, usually the one that's going the other way is lying and will follow suit."

rule: Be in before the expansion; once the highs have been taken and the day has expanded, you are too late.
quote: "You want to be trading before the expansion, before these highs get taken out, right?"

rule: Once the daily range is already made (expansion reached its typical size), do not enter. Wait for the next day.
quote: "Because when a range gets expanded, I'd rather wait for the following day."

rule: He does not fade the daily candle. After a big directional daily candle, wait for the close and look for a small wick on the next day's candle instead of trading back across the range.
quote: "So I would rather wait for today to close and then look for a small wick on the daily candle tomorrow."

rule: Estimate the daily range from recent expansion candles only (not an ADR average). When the day reaches that size, treat the range as probably capped unless it is an anomaly day.
quote: "So if I get to 150, 160, somewhere in there, right, 140, that's where I'm like, hmm, the daily range might be capped."

rule: A bias can only be invalidated when there is a model on the daily chart. No daily model means no invalidation day.
quote: "you need a model. There is no model today on the daily chart."

rule: Bullish daily bias needs daily-profile confirmation: open, make the low, then rally. A gap-up that just expands is not bullish enough.
quote: "If the daily profile would have opened, made a low, and then was doing this, sure, I can be bullish. But when the daily profile just does this, it's not very bullish to me, right?"

rule: You need a trustworthy low (swing) to trade long away from. Without one, do not favor longs from the daily profile.
quote: "Here, I don't really have any low to trade away from. This is the last kind of low that I would trust."

rule: When price doesn't respect the bias, either do nothing or trade the invalidation of the bias.
quote: "You can either do nothing, or you can trade the invalidation of a bias."

rule: Without a daily bias, look for reactions at points of interest and wait for candle closures, not a pre-open trade.
quote: "So I'm just waiting to see how candles close and react."

rule: If correlated assets are far beyond a level the lagging one is near, prefer to see the lagging one take it rather than trade a reaction there as SMT.
quote: "they're way over it, so, like, I'd more want to see it get taken out than have a reaction."

rule: Choose the index by relative strength: bias first, then a model, then pick the asset using divergence off the open and opposing 4H candle closures (bullish 4H close = stronger, bearish 4H close = weaker).
quote: "Candle closure, yep. Look at the 4-hour close here. Bullish closure, 4-hour close here. Bearish closure. Do you know what I mean? So you use those two things together, that's all it is."

rule: Prefer the leading asset. If bullish, focus on the strongest (YM or ES) and ignore the weakest. If unsure which is stronger, use ES.
quote: "If I'm bullish, I'm focused on YM or ES. This is the weakest one, so I don't look at it."

rule: When the indices point opposite ways and no higher-timeframe bias prefers one path, expect consolidation and stand aside.
quote: "I don't really have a higher timeframe bias that tells me one should be preferred over the other, right? And then that's when consolidation can kind of occur."

rule: For a NY continuation he wants the 9:30 and 9:45 15m candles to expand. He prefers continuations taken as the 9:30 or 10:00 candle expands, not after.
quote: "I just prefer a continuation with 9.30 or 10 expanding, not really after it generally."

rule: If the 4H candle is closing weak, it is not a good setup for continuation.
quote: "The main thing we're looking at, guys, is the 4-hour. If the 4-hour is going to close like this, it's not as nice for continuation."

rule: A swing that takes a long time to form before the opposite high is taken is a consolidation range, not a protected swing.
quote: "By the time it takes out this high, it's more of a consolidation range than an actual protected swing to me."

rule: In a range with a protected low, once internal liquidity is swept and price reaches a fair value gap, favor the other side of the range. After a big bearish daily, use 0.5 of the wick and trade higher if it is respected.
quote: "So usually when you have a range and a protected low, I favor when we have some sort of internal liquidity swept, we're reaching to a fair value gap to favor the upside or to the other side of the range."

rule: If you keep getting stopped out before price goes to your target, move the entry up one timeframe (e.g., 5m to 15m).
quote: "Like if you're on the five minute and you're always getting stopped out, then it goes, go to the 15 minute, take an entry there."

rule: To stop revenge trading, cap yourself at one trade a day, no matter what.
quote: "One trade a day max, no matter what. How can you revenge trade if you're only allowed one trade a day?"

rule: If you enter too early, wait for a continuation instead.
quote: "I always enter my trades too early. What do you suggest? Wait for a continuation."

rule: Always trade with a higher-timeframe context; trading lower-timeframe patterns alone is why traders get lost live.
quote: "You need to go in with some sort of higher timeframe, right?"

rule: The weekly is useful for predicting the daily candle, but intraday he always focuses on the daily candle and its closure.
quote: "Like the weekly is good for predicting the daily candle. I'm always just going to focus on the daily candle."

rule: NY entry timeframes are 3m, 5m and 15m (not 1m). He never trades NY PM and does not use the first presented FVG.
quote: "Doing New York, the New York you can use 3-minute, 5-minute, 15-minute. I don't use the first presented fair value gap."

rule: Session/timeframe pairings: London = H4-15m fractal after the Asia range is taken; 9-to-5 traders = daily-H1 (check hourly) or a 4H-based model (check every 4 hours); swing = fractal model on a higher timeframe; a beginner or someone without an edge = simple 4H-15m.
quote: "I would probably just use H4 15-minute fractal model after Asia range taken out."

rule: The 6 a.m. NY 4H candle is a good time to position before the New York open.
quote: "Is the 6 a.m. 4-hour candle a good time to position before New York Open? Yeah, it is."

rule: In FX, pair a weak dollar with a strong counter-currency to get a trend; use the dollar's read to bias the majors.
quote: "dollar, right, had a weak move and ZD had a strong move. So you pair them together, you get a trend."

rule: Volume profile: never trade the POC; in consolidation trade the range edges back into the range; in expansion use higher-timeframe low-volume nodes as levels.
quote: "So if I was to use volume profile, I'd use it on a higher timeframe and I use low volume nodes mainly."

rule: Build a model by blending concepts into a mechanical entry and removing everything else (he removed breakers, advanced market structure, premium/discount).
quote: "I used to have breaker blocks in there. I would have advanced market structure, discount premium. I removed all of it because I didn't need it, right?"

rule: A 1:1 R:R fractal model works if the win rate is above 50%.
quote: "The only thing 1-1-R means is you just have to get over a 50% win rate, right?"

rule: He prefers short futures trades as a hedge because his long-term portfolio and swings are already long.
quote: "Also, I prefer to futures trade to the downside, just because I already have upside exposure on my long-term portfolio and swings."

rule: He reads each day from the daily closure: most of the time wait for the daily close, then anticipate the next candle.
quote: "most of the time I'm just waiting for the daily closure and then anticipating something."

rule: Do not pick tops: wait for the market to either rip through or form a swing, then trade the continuation.
quote: "Versus I can just wait and see is it going to go rip or is it going to form a swing and then I can trade the continuation, right?"

rule: At 9:30 do not predict; have an HTF idea and wait for the open to either sweep the high or form a lower high, and do not trade until one of the two happens.
quote: "I don't know. I'm not going to trade it until we do one or the other."

rule: Without a clean daily framework, do not trade a candle closure by itself; wait for more framework (no pattern trading).
quote: "I need to wait for more framework."

rule: Use the strongest asset to frame the reversal (its reversal off the high tells you where the others reverse), but execute on the middle asset (ES) when strength keeps flipping, to avoid whipsaws.
quote: "I prefer to just focus on the middle asset here, so that's ES, because then it's not going to have those whipsaws around, right?"

rule: SMT at the previous day high (one index takes it, the others don't) plus a bearish candle closure is enough to enter short.
quote: "The entry logic is, I think it's going lower, and we have an SMT up here, a candle closure. So I just enter."

rule: SMT can be read before the higher-timeframe candle closes.
quote: "It didn't need to close yet to tell me that it had an SMT up here."

rule: An asset can print a candle 2 closure without sweeping the high/low itself if the SMT partner swept it.
quote: "Can you have a candle to closure on an asset that didn't sweep a high or low because of SMT? Yes."

rule: If the lower timeframe is sloppy (3m), go up a timeframe (5m) for the closure; prefer the 15m, but drop to the 5m when waiting for the 15m closure would miss the move.
quote: "The reason I go up a time frame is the three minutes. See how it's sloppy? You just go up a time frame. A lot better there. Really, I probably honestly just prefer the 15."

rule: For a continuation (C4 after a C3 closure) you need only one CISD, from the swing point (in C2); not a CISD in both C2 and C3.
quote: "You don't need a CISD in here and in here. You just need one to confirm the swing low. So it's just in the C2."

rule: A reversal off a swept previous day low needs a V-shape reversal with a CISD (a close back over); an aggressive move that fails to close over means a new low.
quote: "We want to see what? A V-shape reversal with a CISD."

rule: He normally always waits for the second CISD; he skips it only when the reaction off the key level (here the previous high) makes him confident.
quote: "Usually, I normally do, always. Here, I was actually, like, fairly confident in just this working based off the reaction off this previous high."

rule: Target the current daily range low rather than a lower protected swing; protected swings are much harder to reach. Mark ~50% of the bodies as where a low would form if the swing holds.
quote: "this is a protected swing. So it's going to be a lot harder to get to this low than it is to this low or this low, right?"

rule: Once the objective (previous day lows) is hit, exit fully; do not give back the open profit chasing a further low.
quote: "Like, I'd rather just exit here and not be greedy for that."

rule: Do not chase: if you missed the entry before the range breakout, do not enter after price already hit the lows/target.
quote: "if you didn't catch it before the breakout of this range, why would you try to enter short after it already hit these lows?"

rule: Do not trade a C4 that already hit a previous low, especially from a doji without a small wick.
quote: "You just hit candle 4 into a previous low. Why are you trying to trade this candle? It doesn't have a small enough wick to look for it to the upside. It's just a doji candle."

rule: Trade pre-market only with a valid 15m setup and a protected swing you can trust for the stop; otherwise wait for the open.
quote: "Like, here, there's nothing to base my stop off of where, like, oh, I don't think it's gonna run this high or something like that. I don't know, so I gotta wait for the Open."

rule: If the daily is aligned but the 15m structure is against you, wait for the 15m to align.
quote: "I would wait for the 15-minute to align with you."

rule: Candle closures are enough for bias.
quote: "Are candle closures enough for bias? Yes."

rule: You can enter on the reversal (bias) candle itself before the 4H closes; the lower timeframe confirms.
quote: "Well, yeah, I was trading the reversal candle."

rule: Take profit vs trail stop depends on expected price behaviour: trending means trail the stop; reversal/reaction/consolidation means take profit.
quote: "If it's trending, then I would trail stop loss. If I expect some sort of reversal or reaction, I guess, then what would I do? TP, right? So it's not like, hey, this is better than that one. It's all situational."

rule: The entry model (IFVG, 5m, 1m) matters less than the higher-timeframe framework.
quote: "Sure, it matters, but it's really not that important. It's about the higher timeframe framework."

rule: HTF levels are imbalances where a high does not overlap a low; do not buy the level blindly, wait for a reaction there, and if none, move to the next level.
quote: "Buy the low? No. Wait for a reaction. So I got these levels because they're just imbalances, right?"

rule: Expect a 4H/hourly expansion candle to close near its extreme (in the lows for a bearish one), so the move can be held into the candle's later part (here toward 10:00).
quote: "if this is a 4-hour expansion candle, hourly expansion candle, they close in the lows, right?"

rule: Inside/consolidating markets are not interesting; trade once price gets out of the range (oil: buy the lower part of the range; stocks: no exposure while inside the fat range).
quote: "I personally didn't touch this because we're in this fat range, like mainly this range, right? So it was more once we got out of that range, that's when I was interested."

rule: To improve win rate, remove losing trades rather than trying to add winners.
quote: "I wouldn't worry about trying to add winners, it's just, what can you do to remove losing trades?"

rule: On currencies prefer the 4H-15m pairing or higher timeframes (less volatility); stocks on monthly/daily; indices 4H-15m with daily/hourly framing.
quote: "I prefer currencies to use the 4-hour 15 or higher timeframes. That's just less volatility, usually."

rule: News (even NFP) is not a reason to change the plan currently; he ignores orange-folder 10:00 news.
quote: "Honestly, news lately, based off how the market's trading, just doesn't care."

rule: When currency pairing, only pair against the dollar while the dollar is moving: find what is bullish and what is bearish.
quote: "you would want to find what is bullish and what's bearish."

rule: Use a previous candle's range as the trading range.
quote: "I just use a previous candle's range."

rule: Judge whether a reversal low is tradable by its separation from the prior low: NQ's two lows ~400 points apart make a better low than ES's lows sitting close together.
quote: "We have good separation between that low and that low, 400 points, versus on ES. We don't really have that same separation, right? It's quite close, so that's less ideal."

rule: The most relevant low is the one with enough separation that it could have held while price ran the other low; if it breaks, move to the next low further left.
quote: "It has enough separation to here, that this could have remained while that goes there. If it falls through there, then I would just look at that."

rule: A deep run into a low makes the reversal less ideal; he prefers the low to form higher in the range.
quote: "I just wish it didn't go so deep. So it's not as ideal for me. I would have preferred it somewhere up in this range to form a low."

rule: Rank NQ/ES/YM by strength; when the strongest (YM) continues toward its high, the middle asset (ES) is expected to follow as long as it holds its level.
quote: "If YM continues towards this high, then it's most likely just ES as long as it's over this, looking back higher since it's the second strongest."

rule: When strength keeps switching between NQ and YM, focus on ES - the middle asset that follows whatever is real and is usually the cleanest.
quote: "ES is just the cleanest. It's like if you were to focus on something, you just focus on ES."

rule: Do not short the weakest asset at its lows; wait for a stronger asset to reverse and trade that.
quote: "Generally, you want to wait for a stronger asset to reverse."

rule: In a trending lower-timeframe move, trade what is actually trending (the strongest/following asset), not the weakest one.
quote: "Well, NQ's the weakest. You want to focus on what's actually trending."

rule: To trade back across a range in the opposite direction, pick the weakest index because it is closest to the other side.
quote: "If you did want to trade this back across the range, What's weakest? Is NQ, YM, or ES? Well, NQ's the weakest, right? It's closest."

rule: A C2 reversal day should be paired with an hourly change in the state of delivery (CISD) for the entry framework.
quote: "It's a C2 reversal day, so we want that paired with an hourly change in the state of delivery."

rule: After a range high is swept, expect a return to the middle of the range; watch there for a reaction back higher or a fall-through to the other side.
quote: "Normally for this type of move where we sweep out a high in the range we come back to the middle of it then we can see around the middle do we get a reaction to go back higher or if we fall through that to the other side of the range."

rule: A daily close below the level after sweeping the previous month's highs is a valid candle 3 closure, targeting the monthly open and possibly the other side of the range.
quote: "So this is pretty relevant today's closure whether or not we close below this level because if we do then we do have a valid candle 3 closure and we're sweeping out these previous highs which is the previous month's highs"

rule: In a range, once one extreme is taken, favour the opposite extreme; if the other extreme is then taken without a reaction, flip back.
quote: "We took out the range low, or the range high, we go to the range low. Since we took out the range low, then I just naturally favor the range high."

rule: He trades expansions; once a market has already expanded to its target (e.g. EUR past its PDH, YM up at its highs), he avoids it.
quote: "Guys, I like to trade expansions, so if price has already expanded, then I avoid it."

rule: Do not short the low of the day after significant lows have already been taken; favour the side where risk-to-reward makes sense.
quote: "Low of the day after it took out lows. I favor to the upside here because that's where the risk to reward makes sense, right?"

rule: He does not take 1:1 trades; a setup whose invalidation leaves only 1R is skipped.
quote: "That's just not a risk to reward for me, a 1-to-1. I don't trade a 1-to-1, right?"

rule: Without a higher-timeframe framework there is no trade, even if a pattern (continuation, limit for 2-2.5R) is visible; being right on direction is not a reason to trade.
quote: "But that's not a trade that I like to put on because it does, it kind of lacks the proper higher timeframe framework, right? You can be right about the direction on something and not trade it."

rule: He does not pattern trade: a continuation pattern needs a higher-timeframe bias behind it.
quote: "But I don't really just trade a pattern. I need to have a higher timeframe bias for a framework. Does that make sense? I don't pattern trade stuff."

rule: A random HTF FVG plus a candle 2 closure is not the model; you need an idea of what you want price to do first.
quote: "Like you can't just randomly choose a fair value gap and be like, oh, candle 2, closure. There you go. Like you still got to have some idea of what you want to see price do."

rule: You generally need a point of interest for a model to form; on the hourly it matters more than on the 4H because the hourly has ~24 candles a day versus six.
