quote: "You generally need a point of interest, yeah, for a model to form."

rule: In the daily-4H-15m model he prefers the POI to be on both the daily and the 4H, though it is not always so.
quote: "I prefer that it be a point of interest on both, but it doesn't always happen that way."

rule: If the ES open is messy, wait for 09:30 to show something or wait until 10:00 rather than forcing a trade.
quote: "This is very messy on ES, so most likely 9.30 maybe even waiting for 10am just because we'll see."

rule: Avoid trading the following candles right after a run of the previous day low and another low, because that often sets up consolidation and chop.
quote: "You don't generally want to trade just the following because it can set up consolidation, especially after running out the previous day low and that low, right?"

rule: On a lower-timeframe reaction from an FVG, the next candles should respect the upper 50% of the reaction wick and do it quickly, then close over for a candle 2 closure while the stronger index continues.
quote: "Generally here, if it's going to go, you're going to want to see it respect 50% of this wick and kind of do it rather quickly."

rule: Scalp sequence: SMT off the low + V-shape + stronger index continuing; react at the only POI (FVG) with a candle 2 closure, expect C3 to expand and C4 to continue.
quote: "It hits the fair value gap and has what? A candle 2 closure. What do we expect with a candle 3 in a candle 2 closure to go higher and expand? If that closes strong like it does, what do we expect for candle 4 to also continue?"

rule: For a trend to continue, price must not close below the higher-low area, should respect about 50% of the last leg and then close through the high.
quote: "If it wants to continue now, it would need to not close below here. ... So then I would need it to, what? Respect 50% of this, generally speaking, and then push higher from here, right?"

rule: Bias decides between a higher low and continuation versus a shift back into the range; the higher low should form at the marked area, followed by a closure through the high.
quote: "Are we going to get a higher low to make a higher high? Or are we going to shift and come back into the range? That's where bias comes in."

rule: Once a daily target has been hit (NQ), he stops looking for continuation in that direction; a 300-400 point NQ range is a normal day.
quote: "Because, especially on NQ, we already hit our targets on the daily level. That's my target."

rule: Bias flips with location: bearish above in the area of yesterday's idea, bullish once price is below the lows.
quote: "I'm not bearish right here. We're below the lows. That's where I start to become bullish."

rule: He often watches an inversion (IFVG) after a sweep get ripped through rather than treating it as automatically bearish.
quote: "They see this inversion and they just automatically think it's going to be bearish. A lot of times I just like to see that ripped through."

rule: If you miss a reversal day setup, wait for the following day rather than chasing.
quote: "If you don't trade this reversal, you just wait for the following day and look."

rule: Without a fresh swing to trade away from, wait for the next day to form a low/high.
quote: "There's no new swing, so I would probably be waiting for the next day to form some sort of low to trade away from"

rule: For swing trades use the daily and hourly: get on side with an intraday move and hold to daily targets.
quote: "You get on side with some intraday moves, like let's say you have this reversal here, you get on side with this continuation or something in here, you're trading this intraday move and then you're just holding towards daily targets."

rule: Timeframe pairings he names: daily-H4-15m, currently prefers 4H-15m, hourly-5m exists, 15m-1m for scalps, yearly bias via monthly candles; hourly vs 4H framework is personal preference.
quote: "My preferred timeframe, I really like the 4-hour 15 model currently. If I have to go lower, then I will go lower."

rule: He does not mechanically follow the timing-alignment plan once he has a daily bias; he finds highs and lows to trade away from.
quote: "I'm just going to find highs and lows to trade away from and then trade away from them. If you need the mechanical plan, you can do that."

rule: Existing exposure shapes trade choice: with long swings on, he is less inclined to add longs and more inclined to take shorts that hedge.
quote: "I'm more inclined to trade short because it hedges my position."

rule: Know your exit before entering.
quote: "When you go into a trade, you should know where you want to exit."

rule: Higher-timeframe entries are preferred because they are calmer and give fewer chances to make quick mistakes; scalping is useful for reps while learning but risks bad habits.
quote: "It's a lot more chill, less opportunities to make mistakes quickly."

rule: A setup that lacks the daily framework is not A+ even if the intraday structure (e.g. an Asia reversal) is fine.
quote: "There's no, the daily framework is not there for me. Right, so it lacks a daily framework."

rule: Do not force trades on a day with no framework; let the open tell you something or nothing.
quote: "Guys, there's just not much. Like, if you want to force yourself on something, that's fine. That's not how I trade."

rule: On news eve (NFP tomorrow) he judges caution from the day's profile rather than the news itself.
quote: "I mean, I'd also just look at the profile of the day, like it's not great."

rule: In London, trade the continuation rather than a counter-move long setup on the strongest index once it has a clear direction.
quote: "I personally wouldn't trade this long setup. I would trade the continuation if I wanted to."

rule: A consolidation low is harder to reach than a single swing low; price may enter a new phase before returning to it.
quote: "I just think it's gonna be a little bit harder to reach than this low here, because this is just kind of that original consolidation."

rule: For a monthly bias, ask whether price is closer to the previous month's high or low; trade toward the closer one and hold that bias all month until it is taken, then watch the reaction.
quote: "That's your bias, which you can have for the whole month until it takes it. Then we watch the reaction."

rule: Do not short below a low right after a massive expansion; that is not the place to sell.
quote: "I don't want to short below the low after a massive expansion, right? That's not where I want to short."

rule: Do not fade the daily candle/range: if the daily is bearish, only look short.
quote: "If this daily candle is a bearish candle, I generally don't try to look to fade that because usually what happens is it just does that."

rule: Never trade the lagging asset: in a bullish market don't trade the weakest index, in a bearish market don't trade the strongest.
quote: "So if it's bullish, I'm not going to trade the weakest one. If it's bearish, I'm not going to trade the strongest one. I just don't do that."

rule: When the weakest asset is already far extended, trade the middle asset toward its own equivalent level instead.
quote: "NQ is super weak, but it's so far lower that I would prefer the middle asset."

rule: If the leading asset continues through its level instead of reversing there, expect the next weakest asset to reach its own equivalent level.
quote: "I was just looking for the fact that we didn't reverse off of this low here tells me that ES can likely trade into this low, right?"

rule: SMT alone means nothing; you still need a reversal to form in the area. It is a confluence, not a requirement.
quote: "SMT alone doesn't mean anything. We've got to see what happens in this area. Does it form some sort of reversal?"

rule: EQ invalidation: in a continuation, price should respect EQ. A shallow wick through is fine, but a close below EQ on the aligned timeframe with no reclaim is a failure. Expect expansion to the opposite liquidity, often via a retracement to an FVG.
quote: "A shallow wick can support it, but if price closes below the EQ on the aligned timeframe and fails to reclaim it, that's failure."

rule: A valid bullish model (C2 closure, CISD, SMT, expansion) that opens and dumps below EQ instead of forming a small-wick low and expanding is invalidated; trade the invalidation to the opposite liquidity (previous day low).
quote: "In this case, we had a valid bullish model. See how we have a candle 2 closure, change in the state of delivery, SMT, expansion."

rule: 08:30 reversal, 09:30 continuation: on news days the 09:30 move continues the 08:30 reversal.
quote: "Yeah, this is a continuation of 830's reversal. 830 reversal, 930 continuation."

rule: Once the daily range (ADR) is already made, the only extra range comes from 09:30-10:00 volatility; target that window only.
quote: "we already have such a massive daily range on NQ that the only way we add more range to that is with some volatility, which comes at 9.30 to 10."

rule: At the open, drop to the 5m/3m if a 15m setup would form too late; the move will expand within the current 15m candle, so waiting for the 15m close is pointless.
quote: "if this is going to work, it's going to expand within the 15 minutes. So if I wait for a 15-minute closure here, it's like, what am I doing?"

rule: If the higher-timeframe entry doesn't give 2R, drop a timeframe (5m to 3m) to find one that does.
quote: "Yeah, that 5-minute doesn't give 2R. There's a reason I went to the 3-minute."

rule: Entering on the FVG rejection means entering a candle 2 closure and looking for candle 3 to continue.
quote: "If you're entering there, you're basically entering a candle 2 closure, looking for this candle 3 to continue, right?"

rule: After entry, price should not displace back up to your entry/breakeven; a strong reaction back into the area is a warning.
quote: "You don't want to see it come back up to your breakeven, right?"

rule: Stop goes on the swing high of the reaction or above the bodies.
quote: "your stop would either be on the high or above the bodies."

rule: Take profit at the logical level (previous day low), or 2R. Runners exit at 10:00, when the 4H, 1H and 30m expansion candles close; 09:45 is also a TP area.
quote: "This is where I would consider taking my profit because that's the end of a 4-hour expansion, end of a 1-hour expansion, end of a 30-minute expansion."

rule: Expansion candles close into their extremes, so hold a runner to the expansion candle's close (e.g. the 4H close).
quote: "Expansion candles close into their lows. We can look for that wherever it closes at 10 a.m."

rule: Whether a candle is an expansion candle is objective: if price expanded, it counts, regardless of its C-number (C5/C6).
quote: "Expansion candles are objective. Did price expand? Yeah, so that's an expansion candle."

rule: Trade a defined window; once you have traded it (or it has passed) you are done for the day, with no searching for more.
quote: "If I trade it, I'm done. If I don't trade it, I'm done. I don't just sit on here all day trying to search for something."

rule: Keep a single bias and a single line: one target level, one reaction area (here a 5m FVG), one move.
quote: "All right, we come in, we have one bias. We say, this is where we want to see it react. We chose a five-minute gap. We get a reaction there. We have a V-shape reversal."

rule: Before the open with no 15m setup (or no limit entry available up into the area), wait for 09:30 to provide the move.
quote: "So I would prefer to just wait for 9.30 to open up for me."

rule: When lows are being taken, that is where long opportunities set up; you need to see the new phase of price before acting.
quote: "So when we take out lows, that's a spot that sets up long opportunities. I need to see the new phase of price."

rule: To push against the open's move, you need an aggressive reaction and a close through the level.
quote: "But if we're going to push lower, we need an aggressive reaction."

rule: Don't trade a breakout move; wait for it to form a retracement swing and break down, then trade the continuation.
quote: "You have to wait until it kind of actually shows its retracement."

rule: Consolidation at a high is not a reversal; in a range, trade only from a sweep of the range extreme with a candle 2 closure, then candle 3.
quote: "if we're consolidating at a high that's not a reversal"

rule: A range-low run is a valid POI, but bias flips only after the hourly CISD; on the entry timeframe wait for a continuation (sweep) rather than trusting the first reversal.
quote: "Reversal, reversal. I generally want to wait for a continuation. Don't trust that."

rule: A move can be a reversal on the lower timeframe while being a continuation on the higher timeframe; frame it by the HTF.
quote: "It's a reversal, but it's a continuation, so... This is the reversal. On a higher time frame, that's the continuation."

rule: Size the risk by position size, not by shrinking a structurally correct stop.
quote: "You just change your position size. You keep your stop loss."

rule: Risk per trade should be set from how many consecutive losses you can absorb before the account is blown.
quote: "The question you have to answer for yourself is how many trades do you want to take before it's blown up?"

rule: On news days (CPI/NFP/FOMC), don't trade the day prior to the news release; otherwise nothing changes.
quote: "Don't trade the day, that current day prior to the news. Besides that, nothing changes for me."

rule: He enters with market orders, not stop orders.
quote: "I don't really use stop orders to enter. I always just market order."

rule: If you entered before 09:30, sit and let the open either stop you out or run.
quote: "You just sit and let 9.30 either stop you out or just rip."

rule: Every reversal forms a swing point, which is what the fractal model is built on.
quote: "The thing is, market can only reverse, like candlesticks, it makes a swing point if it reverses."

rule: Bitcoin often trends out of failure swings, unlike indices; trade it where the model prints at the level, not inside the following consolidation.
quote: "Bitcoin will do this more often than the indices where it just makes failure swings and then trends out of it."

rule: Trade on Monday if Friday turns out to be a reversal.
quote: "And I will trade on Mondays if there's a Friday reversal."

rule: With no clear bias, don't anticipate: let the open (the 09:30 candles) show the direction and react to price at levels.
quote: "There's a difference between having a bias and not having a bias. You see, I don't really have much of a bias today, so I'm more just trying to react off the price action."

rule: After a massive previous-day range with price in its middle, favour range-bound delivery to the nearer overnight extreme rather than a trend.
quote: "we had such a massive range yesterday, and we're in the middle of it, so I usually favor being range bound, which would just put us to the overnight highs."

rule: Never decide or market-enter before the candle closes; let the closure confirm the idea.
quote: "If you notice, I'm not making decisions early or anticipations until we get a closure, right? Like, why would I just market enter short?"

rule: If a closure is not convincing, there is nothing to do; wait for the next candle on your timeframe.
quote: "if you don't get convinced of anything, there's nothing to do, right? You gotta just wait another three minutes."

rule: Use the 'phases of price' at a relevant level: when price hits it, watch the reaction. Dying back into the range is a reversal; a retracement into a gap with the next candle bought is a continuation.
quote: "If it just dies back into the range, that's a reversal, right? ... Into a gap and gets the next candle to buy up, then it looks like a continuation higher, right? Does that make sense? That's why you just use the phase as a price."

rule: If you expect price to reach a further high, you want it to push straight through an intermediate level, not react there.
quote: "if you want to see price reach for these highs up here, you don't want to see it React at that level, really. You want to see it just push through, right?"

rule: In a 09:30-10:00 trend you should not get deep retracements; deep retracements are not his type of trade.
quote: "Because ideally, if we're going to trend from 9.30 to 10, you don't get deep retracements there, right? You just want to see it go, form a continuation."

rule: Expansion targets should ideally be hit before 10:00 (and preferably 9:30-9:45) when trading the opening expansion candle; slow delivery is a negative.
quote: "So ideally, this hits before 10 a.m., you know? Because that's the whole idea is if you're trading this expansion candle."

rule: When long NQ toward a level, take TP1 when the correlated leader (ES) hits its level, because that creates SMT and price often leaves the level.
quote: "A lot of times I will TP1 if I'm on NQ here because ES hit this level, right? So that creates an SMT."

rule: Without SMT at a range extreme on either HTF or LTF, he is not interested in trading the reversal from it.
quote: "Personally, not that interested in this open for the downside because I'd want some sort of SMT at this range high."

rule: SMT is mostly confluence and a target tool; whether it is 'real' is only known by price reacting at the level.
quote: "I use it for targets sometimes, but you really just got to wait for price to react around that level."

rule: A consolidation (the indicator's green box) is traded by its sweep: for a bullish move, the consolidation low is swept, then price goes higher.
quote: "the main idea is it's green. It's a consolidation. So we sweep the low on the consolidation to go higher."

rule: Trading away from a reversal point needs a new protected swing (higher low or continuation); a close over the consolidation high makes the long mechanically valid.
quote: "If we're trading away from this as a reversal point, we need a higher low or a continuation, right? What are we looking for? A new protected swing."

rule: Mark the relevant swing as the target, not the failure swings next to it, even if sweeping the failure swing is technically valid.
quote: "So I could mark out this level, but it's just a failure swing. This is the relevant swing."

rule: Session timeframe pairings: Asia daily-H1 or H4-M15; London H1-M5 or (preferred) H4-M15; New York AM H4-M15, H1-M5 or M30-M3. Higher volatility allows smaller timeframes.
quote: "New York AM, you can use H4, M15, or H1, M5, or M30, M3. Basically, as volatility increases, volatility increases as you go down this list, you can use smaller timeframes, right?"

rule: Daily bias = a daily C2 or C3 closure paired with an H1 CISD (his model on daily/hourly).
quote: "the easiest way to do it ever to get daily bias is C2 or C3 closure on daily paired with an H1 CISD."

rule: On a reversal day the confirming CISD in the New York session is usually a 15-minute CISD; H1 CISD confirmation applies to C2/C3-closure trades.
quote: "If you're trading a reversal day, it's a bit different. I still would prefer that, but if you're in the New York session, it's usually a 15-minute entry. I mean a 15-minute CISD."

rule: If the daily fractal model (C2/C3 closure) is not present, either don't trade or trade the reversal-day framework.
quote: "I either don't trade or I trade a reversal day. That's really it."

rule: Only trade the first CISD as a reversal when bias conviction is very good.
quote: "When you have very good bias, conviction in a trade, you can trade reversal if you want."

rule: He requires 2R. When price is already close to the objective, only an M1 swing with a candle 2 closure can give 2R; otherwise skip it.
quote: "Otherwise, you don't get risk to reward. And because I trade, I need 2R. It's quite hard to get 2R there."

rule: At 10:00 a new 4H candle opens: use the 15m FVG as the POI, refine it to the 5m swing low it coincides with, and use the 0.5 of that on the 3m; price should not take out that LTF swing low.
quote: "New 4-hour candle, 15-minute, fair value gap. That's the point of interest. We want to see it react. 5-minute, that 15-minute gap is the 5-minute swing low. And you go to the 3-minute. Well, you don't want to see it go below there. You use 0.5 of that."

rule: A high followed by a low on the higher timeframe implies a lower-timeframe swing low; for a continuation, price should not take out that low.
quote: "You see how we have a high here and then a low here? That means on the lower time frame you went up here and came back here. So we don't want to see price go take out this low, right? Because that's a lower time frame swing point."

rule: Kill zones don't matter; what matters is where you are inside the daily/4H/1H candles. Skip if the HTF candle has already expanded; take it when the 1H and 4H (and daily) align toward the same target.
quote: "So I don't really care about kill zones, I just care about the higher timeframe candle, right? So if this is already expanded, I'm like, oh, why would I really care about this?"

rule: Avoid counter-trend trades where the daily opposes the 1H/4H; you want the daily, 4H and 1H aligned in one direction.
quote: "It's counter trend because the daily is nice and bearish, and the 4-hour, right? 4-hour supports it, but see how they're fighting? Ideally, you want these aligned together."

rule: Once the daily target is hit after a good daily range, don't trade the continuation beyond the target and don't fade the move.
quote: "But I don't like to trade below the target at a pretty good daily range, right? And I don't want to fade the move"

rule: Enter before the break of the level; don't chase after price has already broken out.
quote: "I'm not going to enter up here. I enter before we Break. That's how I do."

rule: If the CISD swing (the high that should hold) is taken, the idea is invalidated; trading to the failure afterwards is a separate 'invalidation trade'.
quote: "If this high gets taken, the bearish idea is invalidated because you would want to see it continue. So then when it takes it out, you're just invalidated and that's why it's chop, right? Could you trade it to the failure? Sure, that's an invalidation trade."

rule: A CISD that forms only after several failed attempts and wicks is lower quality; prefer the T-spot gap entry for a continuation.
quote: "I'm not a huge fan of it failing, failing, finally does it, right? And also wicking this."

rule: A level you need respected must not see closures below it or its low taken; a single close below is acceptable only if the next candle is immediately bought back.
quote: "If we close below that level, it's not a good sign in terms of a continuation higher unless the next candle immediately gets bought up."

rule: He becomes bearish only after a high is taken (draw on liquidity reached); until then the bias stays bullish.
quote: "I need us to take out some sort of high to become bearish. Other than that, I'm just bullish."

rule: A trend change is target hit plus a shift in structure (CISD); at a POI with SMT and a CISD, look for the reversal.
quote: "There we go, SMT at the highs, CISD. Setting up some bearish price action. ... I would be looking for a bearish reversal here because we were at a point of interest."

rule: Limit to one trade per day; each trade exposes your psychological weaknesses. Higher-timeframe entries (15m) prevent revenge trading by slowing you down.
quote: "Every time you take a trade, you expose yourself to the market and expose yourself to your weaknesses."

rule: To reduce stop size, enter closer to your invalidation.
quote: "You enter closer to your invalidation."

rule: Use breakeven only when returning to entry would itself invalidate the trade.
quote: "if I don't want to be in a position if it returns to my breakeven so I get an invalidation, then yeah, I would use that."

rule: He stops trading around 11:00 NY and rarely trades the PM session.
quote: "No, not really. That's usually when I just, like, end my day. I'm like, most of my trades would be over or running, right?"

rule: Midweek (Wednesday): let the day form before judging the weekly profile.
quote: "I would let today form if you really want to understand the weekly profile because it could kind of go either way today."

rule: Always start the analysis on the daily chart.
quote: "So I'm always going to start on the daily, guys."

rule: The method is identical across markets (indices, FX, gold, crypto); only the time-of-day material is index-specific. Use CME futures data (e.g. GC1!) and XAUEUR/XAUGBP for gold correlation; he does not use DXY with NQ/ES.
quote: "All of my videos work for everything. It's all the same."

rule: When ES leads the indices (instead of NQ/YM being the extremes), expect less clean delivery and lower expectations.
quote: "So it throws me off a little when it's leading. So normally I just don't have as good of expectations, right?"

rule: A continuation trade from a gap after a candle closure is entered on the new LTF candle's displacement, expecting the swing to hold, targeting about 2R.
quote: "So then it would really be you're just entering short on the displacement. Looking to get 2R, maybe you don't get 2R, unless it retraces"

rule: He does not use kill zones, the midnight open, first-presented FVGs, the DR concept, or DXY correlation for indices.
quote: "Do you like to use midnight? No, I don't use it."

rule: If you keep losing with a setup type (e.g. reversals), find what your losing trades have in common and stop taking that type.
quote: "I'm trading the reversal every time and I keep losing. Well, maybe stop trading the reversal."

rule: After several days of expansion and a PDH sweep with SMT (NQ takes PDH, ES does not), expect consolidation/retracement and take a bearish bias only as far as the overnight session lows.
quote: "NQ ran out previous day high. Well, mainly we have multiple days of expansion, right? ... They're looking for some sort of consolidation or retracement. We take out previous day high. ES does not take out previous day high. So that can give us a bearish bias."

rule: In a range, once the range high is taken (with SMT), target the range low.
quote: "Because I'm just, I'm assuming it's a range, right? Range high, range low, takes out range high, goes to range low."

rule: To short toward a low, focus on the weakest index (NQ here) and watch the strongest (YM) for the reversal formation.
quote: "If I'm wanting to frame something to these overnight lows, I'll probably be focused on NQ. But with that, I'll probably watch YM to see if YM can form a reversal, right?"

rule: Anticipate an SMT at the open on the 15m: the strong index takes its previous 15m high while the weak one does not, then the weak one runs to the draw.
quote: "So I want to see YM take the high, which it did. I want to see it reverse there, and NQ not take out the high, right? ... All right, so you see how we anticipate an SMT forming at the open in the 15-minute chart."

rule: Confirm on the lower timeframe by closure: the 3m must close below the body, ideally below the low; a move back above that body is unwanted.
quote: "Generally, you want to see it will go to three-minute, see the closure. You want to see the three-minute close below here, right? Ideally below this low as well."

rule: Counter-trend ideas (daily bullish, 1H bearish) get conservative targets: aim for the level and watch the reaction, not a big expansion.
quote: "you either have to be way more conservative with your targets, right? Kind of like this, where I'm not looking for this to just expand crazy, right? It's counter trend."

rule: When the weak index takes the low and the others do not, that creates a bullish SMT for the move back higher.
quote: "I just would prefer it to take out the overnight lows, because then that creates a bullish SMT. For these moves higher."

rule: After the reaction at the range low, the easy target is the liquidity around the range EQ (the internal high near 50% of range high to low).
quote: "I'm just saying this is the easy target, because that's your range high to low. It's the EQ, the liquidity right around the EQ."

rule: If an index moves opposite to the others, it is usually the one 'lying' (lagging); the leaders show the real direction.
quote: "If it's lying, usually the one that's moving in the opposite direction is lagging."

rule: Index strength switches during the session; re-check which is strongest/weakest after each move.
quote: "If you notice, this is now weakest. This is in the middle. That's now strongest. They switch strengths."

rule: Always have a higher-timeframe draw on liquidity; never take a bias off a random FVG.
quote: "You should have a higher time frame draw on liquidity. So you have some higher time frame spot you're looking for price to trade to. You shouldn't just use a random FEG or something and be bullish off of it or bearish off of it."

rule: His whole toolkit for reversals/counter-trend: highs, lows, fair value gaps, CISD and SMT, nothing else.
quote: "Highs, lows, fair value gap, CISD, SMT. That's it. No matter what, that's all I use."

rule: An IC-CISD forms from a point of interest: a high, a low or a fair value gap.
quote: "It can form from a point of interest, as I said in the video, which is a high, low, or fair value gap."

rule: What distinguishes his newer CISD concept from the standard fractal is location: the CISD forms at the wick of the higher-timeframe candle.
quote: "It's the location it forms. It forms the wick of the higher time from candle. It's just very specific."

rule: For the 4H-15m model on NQ you must wait for the 10:00 NY candle; if the target low hasn't traded by 10:00, treat it as more consolidation and don't trade.
quote: "you would have to wait for 10 a.m. to properly trade the model and most likely if By 10 a.m. we haven't hit this low, then it's just even more consolidation and you wouldn't want to trade it."

rule: Kill zones don't matter; what matters is being inside the higher-timeframe candle after its wick has formed.
quote: "It doesn't matter where I'm trading as long as I'm inside this higher timeframe candle and it's formed a wick."

rule: Skip a market that already made its move, or a daily that is late in its sequence (candle 5 after 2, 3, 4).
quote: "Previous day high if you want, just not the cleanest daily framework because that's candle 2, 3, 4, you're in candle 5."

rule: He does not trade retracements and does not pick lows; he lets the open develop and joins a trend once it starts.
quote: "I would rather just let it open up and see and then if it starts to trend higher, Try to catch something there. I just don't like picking lows."

rule: A bearish daily idea needs a bearish profile (open-high then trend); an open-low profile doesn't support shorts even if your bias says bearish.
quote: "This isn't a very bearish profile, right? ... It would have needed to go open high and then a trend. That's something I'm interested in. See how you can have an idea that profiles doesn't support?"

rule: For FX, decide the dollar bias first and trade the pair as its inverse.
quote: "What's your bias for dollar, right? Decide your bias for dollar, and then your euro is against that."

rule: A deep retracement into the gap above would be bullish; for a short continuation, price should stay internal (below the EQ).
quote: "I don't really want to see price go all the way up there. That's bullish. I'd prefer it to just kind of remain internal here to go lower, right?"

rule: The day before FOMC (and similar news), expect range-bound price; the cleaner day comes after.
quote: "Yeah, we have FOMC tomorrow, 2 p.m. That's the main thing. And Thursday, I think Thursday will probably be the cleanest day."

rule: When the planned moves are done and there is no new draw on liquidity, do nothing.
quote: "If you don't know, I don't know. That means I don't do anything."

rule: The model is closure-based: make no decision until the candle closes, and don't predict closes from a live candle.
quote: "Stop trying to make predictions off of a candle before it closes, right? What is stopping price from closing and then going the opposite direction 10 seconds later? Nothing."

rule: Traders who struggle with live fluctuation do better on the 15m because there is less noise and it is easier to wait for the close.
quote: "And that's why a lot of people do better when you go to the 15-minute, because guess what? There's less fluctuations in here, and it's easier to be like, oh, I gotta let it close."

rule: Execute on whatever timeframe the setup appears on (1H, 15m, 5m; even the daily).
quote: "Whatever timeframe the setup appears. If that's on the hourly, I'll trade the hourly. If that's on the 15-minute, I'll trade the 15-minute. If it's the 5-minute, I'll trade the 5-minute."

rule: Valid timeframe stacks he names: 1H-5m, 30m-3m, 4H-15m(-1m), plus D-1H and W-D on the indicator.
quote: "Yeah, you can trade the fractal from the 4-hour to 15 to the 1."

rule: The model works on any day, including news days, because it trades swing points and the market cannot reverse without a swing point; it just may not be clean.
quote: "my model focuses on swing points and the market can't reverse without a swing point."

rule: Size positions by fixed dollar risk divided by the stop distance.
quote: "You decide how many dollars you want to risk on a trade, and then you figure out the contract size for your stop loss."

rule: In the New York session he usually has a read; outside it he doesn't know or care, and some days he simply doesn't know.
quote: "during the New York session, I generally have a pretty good idea. The rest of the sessions, I don't really know or care."

rule: A daily profile sitting in the middle of its range (go up, go down, doji around the open) means no bias: don't trade it.
quote: "look at the daily profile on this, and there's just a lack of bias. You're just in the middle of this range"

rule: ICT/SMT are a set of concepts, not a strategy; you have to combine them into a defined model.
quote: "ICT, SMT is just a bunch of concepts. It's not a full strategy."

rule: Mechanical daily bias: wait for a daily candle 2 closure, then check for a CISD on the hourly; if both are present, take that bias for the day.
quote: "The easiest way ever is to just go to the daily and hourly. You're gonna wait for a daily candle 2 closure, right?"

rule: The daily bias is not always right; use the EQ (respect or invalidation of it) to manage it.
quote: "Is it always gonna be correct? No, right? But that's why I have a video on The EQ, how it's respected, or the invalidation of it."

rule: The PDL is the draw only as long as the EQ is respected.
quote: "So most likely looking for previous day low on indices as long as it respects the EQ here."

rule: Practice market structure only inside a higher-timeframe bias (daily candle 2 closure) and only in that direction; lower-timeframe structure without context just chops between bullish and bearish CISDs.
quote: "Don't just randomly go into the lower timeframes, because you just go in here and you're like, all right, marking out market structure, you're going to have a bullish change in the state of delivery, bearish, it's just going to be chopping around, because you need the context, right?"

rule: If the lower timeframe is still bullish against your bearish idea, wait for it to switch; trading before that means you are just wrong.
quote: "Currently it's bullish on the lower time frame, so we kind of have to wait for that to switch, otherwise we're just wrong."

rule: There is nothing to anticipate before 09:30; wait for the open to play out before acting.
quote: "Kind of need the open to play out. There's nothing to anticipate pre-open."

rule: For a bearish opening-drive idea, he wants 09:30 to push straight into the target; if price comes back and invalidates the protected swing, the idea is off and it becomes chop.
quote: "The whole idea for me is if we're going to trade lower, I want to see 930 just push us into that low. When we come back and invalidate this protected swing, that means I'm not interested anymore because it just becomes choppy."

rule: When price breaks back over the protected high of a bearish trend, the trend is over and the market becomes chop; stop trading the idea.
quote: "When ES broke over this high, that tells me that this bearish trend is over. And so, for me, it becomes a chop."

rule: A protected swing is a high that hits a point of interest and closes through the series of candles into that POI (it can be a single candle), forming a continuation; the short stays valid while price respects that high.
quote: "So as long as we remain in respect to this high, it's still valid to the short."

rule: After a move off a POI, the 0.5 of that leg should be respected; if price trades well over the 0.5, you need a new swing and a close back lower to get another continuation, otherwise it is chop.
quote: "Because ideally, when price goes up here, it's this point of interest, closes below here, what area is respected? 0.5 of this to go lower."

rule: Once price forms a new invalidation (lower-timeframe C2 closure and continuation), move the stop to breakeven and hold for the target.
quote: "Now you can be breakeven here, looking for a continuation to previous day low."

rule: Once a trade is moving to target, price ideally should not retrace back up into the high that formed the setup.
quote: "Ideally, when price, if it is to hit this level, it doesn't retrace back up into this high."

rule: In a bearish setup pre-open he prefers a lower high rather than London highs being taken.
quote: "generally speaking, when I see this type of structure, I don't want to see London highs taken, right? I'd prefer a lower high in here."

rule: When NQ/ES/YM are decoupled and switching relative strength, trade ES because it is generally in the middle.
quote: "so I like to take ES, which is generally in the middle."

rule: Ideal opening sequence for a short: the strongest index sweeps its high and reacts, the weakest pushes through its low, and the middle one continues.
quote: "Because I'd ideally want to see NQ, it's currently strongest, reach up, sweep this high, and then some sort of... Continuation move."

rule: Use B-ADJ (back-adjusted) futures so futures highs/lows line up with the ETF (QQQ) and index (NDX).
quote: "I want it to be in comparison to the index and the ETF."

rule: On an FOMC day expect chop before the release, with at most one 09:30 move; he usually does not trade before FOMC unless something is clean, and will not short into a live Trump speech.
quote: "It's probably going to chop if it's a normal FOMC day"

rule: With high-impact news later in the day, do not expect range or a trend breakout beforehand.
quote: "there's just not much expectation for range for today, right? I'm not expecting it to just break out in trend prior to FOMC."

rule: Skip a market that is in a range until it takes out the range high or range low.
quote: "Gold's just in a range, probably won't look at it until it takes out this range high or range low."

rule: If one side of a range is taken and the other is not, the bias is toward the untaken side.
quote: "It gives you a bearish bias, run into there."

rule: Do not trade away from (out of) fresh lows in chop; wait for a reversal candle to close, then expect the expansion the following day.
quote: "If this is a reversal candle, then you can get an actual expansion on the following day."

rule: After a candle 2 closure and candle 3 expansion have played out, he has little interest in the following retracement.
quote: "I just don't really have much interest after the expansion."

rule: He does not use 'run vs sweep' or 'close the body'; at a high/low he reads phases of price: aggressive V-shape reversal, consolidation (continuation or reversal), or retracement then continuation.
quote: "I just use the phase of the price at a high or low."

rule: A displacement through a level followed by a 2-3 candle pullback is a retracement and continuation, not a reversal; a reversal needs price to displace back and close over. Do not decide from one closure.
quote: "I don't just look at one closure and say, oh, that's it."

rule: A breaker is a low, high, lower low, then higher high (bullish) closed through; a high-low-higher high-lower low used as a level without that structure is an order block, not a breaker.
quote: "But that's not a breaker. That's an order block."

rule: A late entry after the move has already run (e.g. an 'elite bearish breaker' after the drop) technically exists but has no risk-to-reward.
quote: "I mean, technically you could. There's no risk or reward in that."

rule: Trade the TTFM setup seen on NQ through QQQ options with an at-the-money strike.
quote: "So really, I'm usually taking an at-the-money strike."

rule: In funded accounts trade the same way as in the eval (minus the risk); do not switch into over-conservative capital preservation. (speaker unclear)
quote: "So you need to trade that eval just like you trade the funded minus the risk."

rule: When adding to a position, move the stop so total risk never exceeds the initial risk. (speaker unclear)
quote: "You're taking on more risk than you initially put on, which is against my plan."

rule: [guest] Limit trading to 09:30-11:30 NY and schedule commitments right after so you have to leave; fewer screen hours means fewer mistakes. (likely Nick; speakers not separable)
quote: "If I limit the amount of time I trade, that gives me a higher probability of, like, not making as many mistakes, right?"

rule: [guest] Premature entry: when waiting for a 5m close through a level, a 1m close through it can be used to enter early with the 5m stop; if the 5m candle then fails to close through, cut for a small loss and wait for confirmation.
quote: "If you don't want to wait for the five-minute to get that close or if it runs without you, you can just take that one-minute premature entry, and if the five-minute confirms that five-minute level, then you just hold on to it. If not, you just close it for a small loss and wait for more confirmation."

rule: [guest] In a strongly one-sided market the counter moves need near-perfect entries; entering mid-range is too late because price runs a low and reverses. (likely Nick)
quote: "you literally have to get like perfect entries because if you catch like the middle of the range on them, it's too late and like it'll just run a low and then just reverse back up."

rule: Use a live headline feed (Walter Bloomberg) during 09:30-11:00 to know when a speaker says something market-moving.
quote: "If you guys ever need alerts, as you guys know, go to Walter Bloomberg."

rule: Do not trade seconds timeframes.
quote: "No, I don't trade the seconds time frames. Don't do that."

rule: Use his checklist video as a pre-trade checklist rather than building one from scratch.
quote: "I would just say follow this video and use it as a checklist."

rule: On a slow day, set alerts at the HTF level that would make a market attractive (e.g. above a bearish daily gap) instead of watching it.
quote: "The best thing to do on gold, if you look at the daily chart, is probably to set like an alert above the bearish gap from June 5th."

rule: After a consolidation, when price runs the range low and reverses, look higher: that is where the risk-to-reward is (and vice versa).
quote: "If we have a consolidation, we run a range low, then we'd want to be looking higher, right? That's where the risk to reward is."

rule: A sweep of the previous day low with a small wick supports expansion higher; the mechanical target is the previous day high.
quote: "We have a sweep of previous day low with a small wick, which supports expansion higher. So what's our target on that mechanically? I have a whole video on it, previous day high."

rule: A new protected swing (higher low) only forms with a closure over; without it, the swing forms the other way.
quote: "Did we form a new protected swing? No, we never got the closure over. So then we form the swing the other way."

rule: For taking highs and reaching targets, trade the strongest correlated asset; if the strongest forms a reversal, trade the reversal on a weaker one.
quote: "So if the strongest asset forms a reversal, you want to look to the weaker ones, right? So either YM or ES."

rule: Among weaker assets for a reversal, prefer the one with the cleaner range (ES today).
quote: "I prefer ES here just because it's a cleaner range, right?"

rule: Do not trade away from equal highs / failure swings on the correlated asset; expect them to be run first.
quote: "But the thing is, is I can't trade that away from those failure swings. It's just not something I do."

rule: SMT alone is not enough: a PDH sweep counts as SMT, but you still need structure that aligns (no failure swings to trade away from).
quote: "I do consider that as an SMT. But the structure doesn't align for anything for me to trade shorts."

rule: Avoid reversals that fade the daily candle (reversal on every timeframe); aggressive setups are preferred only when in line with the daily bias.
quote: "I'm just saying when you're aligning time frames together, it's a lot more preferred if you're trading with the daily candle, right?"

rule: Prefer trading the continuation into a point of interest over guessing whether the POI forms a reversal.
quote: "I prefer the continuation into the point of interest versus trying to just guess if the point of interest forms a reversal."

rule: Enter around (or, if bullish, below) the opening price of the higher-timeframe candle; do not enter after that candle has already expanded.
quote: "If you want to stop chasing trades, enter around the opening price of the higher timeframe candles."

rule: Trade the expansion, not the consolidation after it; once the expansion has happened and targets are hit, probability drops.
quote: "We want to be trading the expansion, not after it."

rule: Default pairing for most traders: daily + hourly fractal for bias, 4H + 15m model for execution.
quote: "using daily and hourly fractal for bias and then using the H4 and 15 model, right?"

rule: A lower-timeframe CISD (15m/30m) still needs the 4H candle to support expansion (small wick or a formed reversal).
quote: "You still need the 4-hour candle to support expansion, whether that's a small wick or the reversal has formed, right?"

rule: On the entry timeframe he looks for a change in state of delivery then a continuation, not a C2/C3 sequence.
quote: "I'm looking for a change in the state of delivery and then a continuation. I'm not looking for a C2 or C3 down here generally."

rule: If the swing you expect to hold is formed before 9:30, expect expansion off the open.
quote: "If we have some sort of swing that I'm expecting to hold prior to 930, I'd expect it to just expand off the open."

rule: Use full ETH data; the overnight session is a core input, so the RTH-only chart is not used.
quote: "for me, a lot of my analysis is built off the fact that the overnight session and what it does, right, that's what I use."

rule: Pre-open he does not go below the 15m chart.
quote: "If you noticed pre-open, right, I'm not going below a 15-minute chart because of this, right?"

rule: Every trade needs a swing / protected swing to trade away from; that is the invalidation and the stop.
quote: "I need to have some sort of low or swing point or protected swing that I can trade away from, right? That's my invalidation, right?"

rule: If you are stopped out and price then goes to your target, move up one or two timeframes.
quote: "It's a very simple fix. Up a time frame or two."

rule: A trade needs a bias, an invalidation and structure; don't take quick level-to-level trades without them.
quote: "You need That's like a bias, right? You need invalidation, then you need structure."

rule: Don't pattern trade candle 2s against the bias; a C2 that points away from the draw on liquidity is expected to fail.
quote: "So one, things just fail, but also don't pattern trade. You need a bias, right?"

rule: Don't move stops to breakeven.
quote: "Don't go break even."

rule: Use a fixed take profit (around 2R) and leave the trade alone; cutting winners early raises the win rate you need (about 34% at 2R vs 50% at 1R).
quote: "have some sort of 2R whatever take profit and you just place the trade and you don't do anything"

rule: Max one trade a day if you revenge trade.
quote: "So how do you simply fix this one trade a day max"

rule: On prop accounts, size so you could take about 10 losses in a row without hitting the drawdown, but large enough that winners reach the profit target.
quote: "position size so you can have, you know, on props, I would say, 10 losers in a row."

rule: Evaluation risk sits on a time-vs-money curve: aggressive ~20%+ of drawdown per trade, middle ~7-10%, conservative ~5% or less.
quote: "Down here, you're probably 5% or below. I'd say probably 5% of drawdown."

rule: A loss is not a bad trade; a bad trade is breaking your rules. Take every trade the model prints and treat it as data collection.
quote: "A loss doesn't equal a bad trade. A bad trade is not following rules, right?"

rule: If your model prints the entry, take it; don't overthink.
quote: "So for me, if everything's there, and price forms an entry, I take the trade."

rule: Build bias by hindsight-testing the daily chart one candle at a time, anticipating the next day mainly from candle 2 / candle 3 closures.
quote: "Go to the daily chart. All you're going to do is go through days like this and you're going to say, okay, could I reasonably anticipate what this day is going to do?"

rule: After a bullish daily closure, the EQ of that candle becomes the candle 2 / candle 3 area to look for the next candle higher.
quote: "I would prefer this to hold up, have a nice bullish daily closure, then we can use the EQ of it as a candle 2 or candle 3 and candle 4 higher, right?"

rule: Once a candle closes over a prior candle, price should not return below 50% of that candle; the swing there is the protected low, and only a lower-timeframe low in that area needs sweeping.
quote: "We close over this candle here. What do we not want to see? We don't want to see price return to below 50% of that, really."

rule: The T-spot is where the wick of the candle should form.
quote: "But what it means is it's where the wick should form, like where the wick should go, you know?"

rule: If you can only trade Asia, use it to enter the daily range positionally near a protected swing on a day expected to expand (C2/C3 closure), with a limit in a gap, stop beyond the swing, daily + hourly.
quote: "I would only be looking to trade it in line with a daily candle of some protected swing."

rule: If you can only trade London, use the 4H-15m model.
quote: "4-hour, 15-minute model."

rule: Use typical daily candle size (ADR) to judge exhaustion: once a candle has made its usual range, expect little further expansion.
quote: "After it goes 100 points, You don't really have too much expectation for it to expand much further."

rule: Equal lows far below price don't matter once the reversal has formed and price is continuing away from them.
quote: "Once it's already formed its reversal and now it's in a continuation higher, not even close to it, I don't really care as much about it."

rule: If the strongest asset consolidates above its previous day high, expect the lagging correlated asset to reach its own previous day high.
quote: "ES is going to want to go to its previous day high. So that's where it could go the rest of the day."

rule: He waits for 9:45 after the open before acting on a reversal idea.
quote: "I'm gonna wait for 9.45, right?"

rule: On a quiet news week, the volatility windows are simply 9:30 and 10:00.
quote: "I mean, I'll just focus on 9.30 and 10. Pretty normal."

rule: Focus on the mini contracts, not micros, for SMT/highs reads.
quote: "I personally focus on the minis when looking for"

rule: Do not short a reversal at 10:00 on the strong asset while the correlated asset has not taken its previous high.
quote: "Did ES take out the previous high? No. See, like, if it did, you could trade 10 a.m. lower"

rule: On an inside day, use only three points of interest: previous day high, previous day EQ and previous day low.
quote: "I'm only going to look for two points of interest or three. Previous day high and previous day EQ. And then if we fail the previous day EQ, we have previous day low."

rule: Bullish inside-day plan: respect of the previous day EQ means trade into the previous day high; if EQ fails, the previous day low is next.
quote: "respects EQ, I'm bullish to previous day high."

rule: A close below the previous day EQ is not automatically an invalidation; it can be a liquidity sweep around the range EQ.
quote: "Just because it closes below the previous day EQ doesn't mean I'm invalidated for sure, right?"

rule: Only trade an invalidation of bias in the opposite direction once you are more advanced.
quote: "you should really only focus on invalidation of bias, like in terms of trading it the other way when you get a little bit more advanced in it"

rule: The bias stays until it is invalidated.
quote: "Why is the bias bullish? Because it's not invalidated me yet."

rule: His model is daily bias, then daily profile, then entry; a bullish bias alone is not a long if the profile/price action doesn't support it (e.g. PDH swept and dying).
quote: "But my model is daily bias, daily profile, entry, right?"

rule: The most ideal setup is an ideal candle 2 closure and then trading candle 3, not C2 with expansion in the same candle.
quote: "The most ideal setup within my model is an ideal candle 2 closure and then trading candle 3."

rule: Before 10:00, trading around the open needs a 30m bias/3m entry fractal because the hourly closes at 10:00; otherwise wait for 10:00 and use the 15m or 5m.
quote: "Otherwise, you wait till 10, and then you can use the 15-minute or the 5-minute."

rule: It is usually better to wait for 10:00 to get a range on what 9:30 does; at 10:00 the 4H, 1H, 30m and 15m all open new candles and price can start a new phase (continuation or reversal).
quote: "What happens at 10? We get a new 4-hour candle. We get a new hourly candle. We get a new 30-minute candle, a new 15-minute candle."

rule: In the morning he wants the opening-drive move from 9:30 to 10:00 to reach for the objective, and the 9:30 low (with SMT) should not be taken.
quote: "normally I want this move to occur from 930 to 10, like it's just like an opening drive movement"

rule: Focus on the strongest asset by relative strength (closest to its target); trade it into its draw first and expect the others to follow.
quote: "but I always try to focus on the strongest asset, right?"

rule: If the strongest index has already taken the target, trade the one that still has it (YM over NQ when NQ already took the level).
quote: "So what makes sense to trade into previous day's highs first, YM or NQ? Well, like, just look at difference versus a difference. The YM, right?"

rule: Don't trade a move unless there is a low you can trust for the stop; if not, wait for new structure.
quote: "can you trust any of these lows in here? No. So like, if I was going to trade it in here, I need my stop somewhere here, which I'm not a huge fan of"

rule: Don't take a reversal entry against higher-timeframe candles that are not yet in line; require a continuation first.
quote: "I'm not going to try to take a reversal entry when it's not really in line with the trend"

rule: Sweeping a high without a close over it usually sends price back into the gap.
quote: "Sweeps out the high, can't get a closure. That usually means back into the gap."

rule: When lower-timeframe structure turns into consolidation, look for a sweep of the low and an aggressive move back up.
quote: "When it becomes a consolidation, what do you look for? Sweep of the low, aggressive move back up"

rule: The most ideal reversal in a gap is a small-wick reversal that sweeps the previous candle's low.
quote: "The most ideal way to form a reversal in this gap is a small wick reversal off of this previous candle's low. So sweep of the low."

rule: If the reversal candle forms a large wick near the end of a 15m candle, wait for the close and the new 15m open where timeframes align.
quote: "So we're at the end of the 15-minute candle, so it's better to just wait for the new open, which all aligns together."

rule: His ideal trading day doesn't have a large daily wick; a large-wick New York reversal day (trading back toward the daily open/PDH) is valid but not ideal and has less range.
quote: "my ideal trade doesn't have a large wick, right?"

rule: Once a higher low holds after the sweep, stay bullish to the high.
quote: "This is a higher low. So as long as this holds, I'm bullish to that high."

rule: Don't fight the daily and 4H candles with a reversal when everything is bullish.
quote: "Stop trying to fight all these candles when everything's bullish, right?"

rule: Against a bullish gold day, shorts are only worth looking at after a new 4H candle sweeps the high.
quote: "The only time you could potentially even look for shorts is new 4-hour candle, sweep of this."

rule: Don't chase late continuations: either capture the continuation or miss it, then wait for a new swing.
quote: "I can't really trade this unless we form a new swing, and I'm not a huge fan of trading at late, right? So I either capture the continuation down here or I miss it."

rule: After a long run of candles (C2 through C6) with only a shallow or equal sweep, wait for a new swing or consolidation, ideally an inside day that gets swept the next day.
quote: "So really, I would prefer this to actually be an inside day or do something and then can sweep it out the next day to then trade higher"

rule: Advanced entry: when the CISD level is too far away for the RR to the target, enter directly off the swing on the candle 2 / C3 closure, with the stop below (not at) 50% of the candle, or wait for a further continuation.
quote: "When the CISD level is too far away, doesn't make sense in terms of RR, you can use candle 2 closure, C3 closure, to enter directly off a swing."

rule: IC-CISD: in candle 3 the wick forms from a short-term opposing trend; the series of down-closed candles into the POI, then a close over it, is the intra-candle change in state of delivery and gives the invalidation.
quote: "For price to make a wick, it has to have a short-term trend in the opposite direction."

rule: After C2 closure + SMT + CISD, find a POI to trade away from for the wick: first the FVG; if no continuation forms there (no close over), the sweep of the low (or T-spot) becomes the POI.
quote: "Did we form a continuation here? No, right? We never closed over this level. ... What are we then looking for? The sweep of this low."

rule: 'One shot, one kill' means trading the weekly/daily range from the reversal and holding for multiple days.
quote: "I just view this as Trading weekly slash daily range."

rule: SMT plus a lower-timeframe CISD is no reason to trade without an actual directional bias.
quote: "You need to have some sort of actual bias."

rule: Protected swing = sweep of a low or reach into a gap, followed by a CISD; it replaces waiting for ICT's intermediate-term low to form.
quote: "why don't I just change it to, okay, we have to sweep out a low or reach into a gap. And then we just have a CISD. Oh, protected swings."

rule: Find the root cause of your struggle (tilt, oversizing, revenge trading, not following a model), then change or quit.
quote: "So you either quit or you make change."

rule: Your real risk on a prop account is the fee you paid; treat funded accounts the same as evals.
quote: "It's still the fact that you paid 60 bucks, that's your max risk."

rule: Avoid entries below the 3-minute timeframe; use the 1-minute only when the situation requires it.
quote: "I really don't really like using the one-minute, but it is what it is in some scenarios."

rule: Skip a continuation entry that doesn't offer at least 2R.
quote: "It's, like, not very great RR. Doesn't even give 2R."

rule: Existing exposure matters: already holding swing longs, he didn't want to add another long at the open.
quote: "I'm currently still in my longs from Friday, so I'm not like overly... Wanting to get into a long because I already have that long exposure."

rule: When strength switches mid-move among NQ/ES/YM, ES (the middle one) is usually the cleaner one, but keep the original strongest asset as the reversal reference.
quote: "This strength switched, so NQ got stronger now. YM's weaker. Usually that means ES is going to be the one that's a bit cleaner."

rule: Indicator update: update the script from the three-dot menu, right-click or the purple dot; saved indicator templates do not update themselves and must be re-saved.
quote: "if you have templates up here like I do, right, that's not going to update itself, right? You need to go ahead and go back and make new templates"

rule: Default behaviour: the indicator prints nothing until the candle closure; on the closure the PSP shows and the SMT is marked when it forms.
quote: "default settings, it's gonna not print anything until the candle closure."

rule: Protected swings (new): a protected swing forms on a closure through; it is printed on the next candle's open, drawn as a dot plus a line, and new ones keep forming as price continues (trailing stop use).
quote: "Protected swings will form on the closure through. So on this candle here, that closes through, right? Once we get a closure through that, so on this next candle open, it will print that, right? And it's labeled with a dot."

rule: Protected swings never repaint: when one is taken out it is turned gray (kept for review) and a new line forms.
quote: "The protected swings don't repaint, right? I don't repaint things because I find it dishonest, right?"

rule: History setting = how many past models stay on the chart; 0 shows only the most recent. He keeps 0 when actively trading, 1 in his template; panel default shows 4.
quote: "History is just going to show you how many models show up on your chart at one time"

rule: Fractal setting: Automatic picks the HTF from the chart timeframe (1H chart -> daily, 15m -> 4H, 5m -> 1H); a fixed pair (e.g. daily-hourly) stays the same on any chart timeframe; Custom lets you choose any pair.
quote: "So default, it's automatic. So that means if I'm right here on the hourly, it's going to use the daily, right?"

rule: Bias filter: Neutral shows bullish and bearish models; Bullish/Bearish show only that side; Auto Bias 1 only shows setups aligned with the model one fractal up (5m/H1 aligned with H4-15m), Auto Bias 2 two fractals up (daily-H1).
quote: "If you have auto bias 1 on the 5-minute, it's only going to align when the 4-hour's in line. If you have auto bias 2, it's going to go up two timeframes instead of one."

rule: HTF candles: count (default 4, he uses 4 because his model needs it; minimum 4), size small/medium/large or hide; offset shifts them right so two copies can sit side by side.
quote: "Default, I use four, because that's how I use it in my model."

rule: To overlay two HTF sets: copy/paste the indicator, lock the copy to the daily with offset 17 and turn off its model (C2/C3/C4) so only candles show.
quote: "I can offset it. I use 17, and I can lock it to the daily."

rule: HTF drawing options: HTF open line, vertical lines separating HTF periods, H/L lines of previous candles (he keeps off), previous EQ shown on the previous HTF candle and/or the chart (drawings type: chart, HTF candles, both).
quote: "previous EQ, you know how I use EQ so it'll show it on the previous higher time frame candle as well as On the lower time frame"

rule: HTF candle labels show weekday names on daily candles or the time/period open on lower ones; custom time zone available if not EST.
quote: "we have Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, if you go to a lower time frame, going to say, you know, what time frame those candles are"

rule: Early C2 CISD (off by default): shows the CISD before the candle closes as a dotted line; on the closure the model confirms and turns solid. With it on, continuations also show dotted before the closure.
quote: "If you do want to see that marked out prior to, you can just turn on early CISD."

rule: He leaves early C2 off by default because learners should not trade C2 (more complex), but he personally turns it on.
quote: "I have that off by default because people learning my model, I don't really want you trading C2. It's more complex."

rule: Model style settings: bullish CISD line, bearish CISD line, candle EQ, candle 1 sweep with C1 sweep display (HTF candles only, chart, or both), TTFM label size, T-spot colours.
quote: "C1 sweep, we had a lot of people asking to see the C1 on a higher timeframe candle, but not the lower."

rule: Protected swing settings: enable, style (solid/dashed/dotted), width, bullish/bearish colours; the same width setting controls continuation line thickness.
quote: "Now, protected swings, this is one of the new settings. This is where you can choose the width of the protected swings and what you want it to look like and the color of it"

rule: SMT settings: display on chart, HTF candles or both; labels and size; correlated pairs Automatic (for NQ: ES and YM, shown in the table) or Custom with an optional second pair and an Inverse flag for inversely correlated pairs (e.g. dollar vs euro); SMT line style.
quote: "SMT, I'll use ES and YM for NQ. If you don't want to use the pairs I selected, you can turn off automatic and turn it to custom."

rule: PSP (new): enable and choose candle 1, candle 2 or both; on the chart only 'C2+PSP' is labelled; to see which candle is the PSP look at the HTF candles.
quote: "it will only display C2 plus a PSP if you want to see what the PSP is. You have to look on the higher term from candles here"

rule: PSP definition: the HTF candle closes bearish on one asset and bullish on its correlated asset; SMT is a divergence between the assets.
quote: "SMT is a divergence between the assets."

rule: Session filter: restrict printed setups to a session (e.g. New York only) so nothing prints while you are asleep.
quote: "Turn on a filter and filter it only for New York session. You won't see anything else in your chart but setups that occur in New York session."

rule: Calculation bars sets how many bars back the script calculates; lower it if slow. He uses about 2,000.
quote: "Calculation bars is how many bars it calculates back."

rule: A setup prints only if it qualifies as a fractal setup: candle closure plus a change in state of delivery (CISD).
quote: "If it doesn't have both of those, it's not going to."

rule: Continuations are printed only for a limited time after the model; a continuation that forms too late into the move, or does not meet the demands, is not marked.
quote: "this one forms too late into the move because I mark them out specifically."

rule: Continuation labels are shown only for continuations that form in a fair value gap.
quote: "we just label the ones that are in a fair value gap, right?"

rule: T-spot box: the area where he wants the daily candle's wick to form (bearish gray box for a high, green box for a bullish wick low to be held) before price trades away.
quote: "when this shows up and I have this gray box, I'm looking for the wick of the daily candle to essentially try to form somewhere in this area"

rule: SMT naming: reversal SMT forms with the reversal (indicator shows it on the CISD); continuation SMT forms later in the move (prints live once the correlated asset takes the level); both = double SMT.
quote: "That will be a reversal SMT because it's an SMT formed with the reversal."

rule: Standard-deviation projections: off by default (he keeps them off); can be drawn from wicks or bodies.
quote: "I prefer to just have them off on my indicator."

rule: Alerts: enable alerts and pick types in the inputs; create the alert while on the entry timeframe of the pair (hourly chart for daily closures, 15m for 4H) and add it to the whole watchlist.
quote: "instead of doing it one by one, you can create an alert on the watch list."

rule: The indicator gives no signals, stops or targets and has no win rate; it marks his model mechanically, and a printed model is not automatically one to take.
quote: "There is, in fact, no win rate for the indicator."

rule: The indicator is kept deliberately clean: no C1-C4 labels on chart/HTF candles and no HTF FVGs.
quote: "I don't want a billion things on my charts, right?"

rule: C1 is not marked by the indicator; it is just the liquidity for candle 2's reversal.
quote: "it doesn't mark out C1. C1 is just the liquidity for the reversal of candle 2."

rule: Learners should trade only C3/C4 after a valid model prints; trading C2 comes later.
quote: "Trade CD3, CD4, after valid model prints."

rule: He prefers the confirmed continuation over an early CISD and takes early CISD only when bias is very strong.
quote: "I'll sometimes take an early CISD in the case that my bias is that strong."

rule: A doji / poor daily closure gives little bias; wait for the NY session intraday profile, or wait another day.
quote: "So usually that means I don't really have much bias going into the day, because it could really do whatever it wants."

rule: When price sits between protected swings on both sides, let the day form (watch Asia/London) before choosing a side.
quote: "you have a protected swing on this side you have a protected swing on the side we're in the middle so this is where you just kind of need to let the day form"

rule: At a liquidity target / POI, judge reversal vs continuation from the reaction: running out the opposite high versus forming a continuation, retracement or consolidation.
quote: "So what's our reaction at the low? Do we go run out this high? Or do we form a continuation or a retracement or consolidation?"

rule: Timeframe pairings: 30s entries pair with 10m (not 3m); 15s with 5m; automatic pairs are 1H-D, 15m-4H, 5m-1H; custom pairs such as 7H-15m are possible.
quote: "I would do just 5-minute, 15-second is what I would use. So if you're doing 30-second. I would probably use 10-minute."

rule: Session-dependent pairing (typed on screen): before 9:30 focus on the H4/M15 model with M15 entries; after 9:30 use the H4 chart with LTF fractals H1-M5 or M30-M3. Daily/H1 for bias.
quote: "Something like that is how I would do it if you want to master a 4-hour candle."

rule: After an intraday reversal, either trade the 4H swing on the 15m (London) or wait for NY and trade an hourly swing on the 5m.
quote: "Or we could wait for the New York session, look to trade an hourly swing somewhere in there on the 5-minute."

rule: A 4H/15m trader focused on NY C3 continuations will have many no-trade days; that is normal for a mechanical system.
quote: "it's not every day that you get a 15-minute entry, right?"

rule: Even intraday entries need structure/context on a higher timeframe; it is not pattern trading.
quote: "You need the context. You're not just pattern trading it."

rule: Use the normal daily open (18:00, data-feed open), not true day open or midnight; use the Sunday weekly open for the weekly profile, where a reversal after an expansion generally trades back toward the weekly open.
quote: "If it reverses here, then generally your weekly profile is to trade back towards the weekly open."

rule: He prefers continuation trades; reversals only when bias is very strong.
quote: "I don't really trade the reversals. I'll trade reversals in the case that it's very strong on my bias."

rule: He prefers the New York session for most instruments, including gold.
quote: "I prefer New York for most things"

rule: On stocks, turn protected swings off (messy); prefer higher timeframes there.
quote: "It's going to be a bit messy with the protected swings, honestly."

rule: Once a bias is set, do not flip it just because the previous day high was taken.
quote: "just stop changing your bias once previous day highs taken."

rule: On evaluations he would risk more, trading money for time; a 1:1 R approach needs a higher win rate.
quote: "You just have to have a higher win rate."

rule: When the indices diverge, short the weakest asset and do not trade the lagging (strongest) one against your bias.
quote: "I don't trade the lagging asset. What does that mean? If I'm bearish and YM is the strongest, I'm not touching YM."

rule: For a high-quality expansion you ideally want the strongest asset to reverse together with the weakest.
quote: "ideally you'd want to see the strongest asset reverse within the weakest one to actually go expand."

rule: To avoid chasing, ask before every entry: am I entering near the higher-timeframe open? Entering at the low of an expansion candle is where most losses come from.
quote: "the easiest thing to keep you out of trades that you're chasing is ask this question, am I entering near the higher timeframe open?"

rule: Continuations are easier because a new candle opens and you enter around its opening price.
quote: "That's why a lot of times the continuation is easier where you have a new candle open and then you're entering around that opening price, right?"

rule: If you are trading candle 3, it is not a reversal candle, and you are far from the opening price, usually wait for the new candle open.
quote: "you are trading candle 3, and it's not a reversal candle. You're not around the opening price. So a lot of times, that's when you like to wait for the new candle open."

rule: On Mondays, if he trades, he wants to enter close to the 09:30 open because that's when volatility comes in.
quote: "generally on a Monday, I like to, if I'm going to trade it, I like to be closer to the open, you know, because that's when the volatility will come in."

rule: Stop goes exactly at the protected swing with no extra buffer; if it is taken out, the trade is invalidated.
quote: "I'm just putting my stop loss at the protected swing. I'm not giving it extra room, because if it gets taken out, that's my invalidation."

rule: A higher-timeframe candle with no wick is an unestablished low; treat it as liquidity, not as a low you can trust.
quote: "I mean, it's just an unestablished low."

rule: When there are no lows (or highs) you can trust, trade it as a range: a sweep of the range high targets the range low.
quote: "So with that, I'm trading this as a range, we sweep the range high, we go here, right, and then you expect that."

rule: Don't short below lows (at the bottom of a move); short up high before the lows are run.
quote: "I'm not interested really almost ever trying to short below lows like this, because that's where I would take losses"

rule: After expansion, expansion, expansion, wait for the next higher-timeframe open or a new continuation before re-entering.
quote: "So now if you do want to look short, when does it make sense? 9.45, right? Waiting for that next higher timeframe open. Or we've had expansion, expansion, expansion. My model would say wait for a new continuation."

rule: A target can come from another asset: take profit on NQ when ES hits its target.
quote: "you can take profit on one asset because the other asset hits a target too, right?"

rule: Time-based exits: expansion candles on the 4H, 1H and 30m all end at 10:00, so 10:00 is an exit time.
quote: "What do we have on the 4-hour? Expansion candle. What do we have on the hourly? Expansion candle. What do we have on the 30? Expansion candle. You know, all of these things end at 10 a.m. So that's a time-based exit."

rule: The move he prefers each day is 09:30-10:00 (or 08:00-09:00 / 09:00-10:00); later moves are choppier once the day has expanded.
quote: "I prefer the 9.30 to 10 move, because go to that most days, or an 8 to 9, right?"

rule: Use average daily range as context for targets: with ADR ~500-600 and ~300 done after multi-day expansion and a gap, he did not expect the previous day low without more context.
quote: "What are we thinking here on an average daily range? You know, we've had some larger ranges, but 500, 600 points, let's say, right? We're at 300."

rule: To extend a short to the previous day low he needs the intraday low to fail and a new 4H candle that opens and makes its high first.
quote: "this low needs to not hold, and then you need to have a new 4-hour candle that open high first, right?"

rule: A CISD is a closure through the series of opposite-closing candles; mechanically you wait for that closure.
quote: "Our CISD would be a closure through these candles, right? So mechanically, you have to wait for that."

rule: A C2 and C3 closure without a CISD is not a setup.
quote: "Candle 2 closure, there's a candle 3, right, candle 3 closure, but it never has a CISD. So there's nothing there on gold."

rule: Intra-candle CISD entry: the HTF candle opens, makes its high first, sweeps a POI, then closes below - that swing is protected; enter there, stop on the swing, 2R or hold if the day's context supports it.
quote: "This is an intracandle change in the state of delivery. So if you're going to do that, entry would be there, my stop would be there. You can look for 2R."

rule: Whether to hold beyond 2R depends on the day's context (here a trade down to the lows offered ~10R).
quote: "Well, what's the context of the day? The context of the day is a trade down to these lows. So if you really wanted to, there's your 10R trade, right?"

rule: A protected swing is valid on the closure through the swept POI and only prints on the open of the next candle.
quote: "what's the point of interest it sweeps out it's valid on this closure through it's gonna print on the open of the next candle"

rule: A daily reversal candle that closes back in the bias direction sets up a next-day continuation that should respect the upper half of that day's range (for a bullish read).
quote: "It should form a continuation in respect to the upper half of today's range, and then continue higher."

rule: EQ measurement: on a large-bodied expansion candle measure high to low; on a candle with a large wick measure the wick.
quote: "If you have a large candle body, expansion candle, measure it from high to very low. If you have a candle with a larger wick, measure the wick."

rule: Beginner timeframe stack: daily and H1 for bias, H4 to M15 for entry.
quote: "Most people that are just starting out, I say use the daily and H1 for bias, and then I use the H4 for M15 for entry."

rule: On FX (e.g. EUR) he does not go below the 15m chart; on stocks he mostly enters on the daily (daily-hourly or monthly-daily).
quote: "If I'm trading, like, anything like Euro, something like that, I'm not really going lower than a 15-minute."

rule: He lets Monday print and does the weekly read on Tuesday; he has no view on tomorrow until today closes.
quote: "I usually let Monday print, then I do that on Tuesday."

rule: He doesn't predict how far price goes; he watches the closures.
quote: "I don't try to predict how far it will go. I'm just going to watch the closures, right?"

rule: Avoid consolidating markets; trade something that is trending. Learning when to avoid the market helps a lot.
quote: "you guys gotta learn when to avoid the market. It's gonna help you a lot, right?"
