rule: If a market (e.g. gasoline at all-time highs) is consolidating, it is often better to wait for the new month and for a swing to form.
quote: "I mean, you gotta see a swing form in something. A lot of times this is better waiting for the new month, if it's gonna consolidate."

rule: When late in a move, the alternative is the middle asset (ES): short it before it runs its low, refined on a lower timeframe.
quote: "You'd go to the one that's in the middle."

rule: When a range sweeps one side and then fails to form a continuation, expect the other range extreme to be taken.
quote: "When we failed the form of continuation, what happens? We go take out this range low."

rule: C2/C3 closures are the easiest way to get daily bias, but not the only way he uses.
quote: "That's the easiest way for people to get daily bias, C2 and C3 closures. Is that always what I do? No, because there's more advanced ways to do things."

rule: Limit vs market entries is a process choice; missing a limit fill is part of the game. He market-enters.
quote: "If you use limits to enter and you get missed, that's just part of the game. I personally like to market enter, so that's how I do it."

rule: Once the day has made its full daily range there is nothing left to do unless you are already in.
quote: "Bro, we just went the whole daily range. Like, unless we are like, dying, like, there's nothing really to do anymore. Unless you're short already"

rule: Vertical lines separating the HTF candles are essential to see the individual structure inside each higher-timeframe candle; he runs 4 HTF candles.
quote: "Vertical lines, that just shows me about vertical lines. That's really important to me because it allows me to see the individual structure inside the higher time frame candles."

rule: He keeps the indicator bias on Neutral to see both sides; set it to one side only if you're one-directional for the day.
quote: "I like it at neutral so I can see both sides, but if you're going into a day and you're like, I'm only bearish, you can just put it on bearish, right?"

rule: Only trade when there is a clear daily bias or clean profile and a model that aligns with it; hunting a sweep plus IFVG every day leads to overtrading.
quote: "If you're just going into every day, like, hey, I'm going to go look for a sweep in IFVG, probably going to have you over trading"

rule: On divergent index days, trade the strongest index (usually YM) when bullish and the weakest (NQ, or ES as a laggard) when bearish.
quote: "So if we are bullish, what do we want to generally focus on? Usually YM, Or ES as a lagging. Or if we're bearish, we want to focus on NQ or ES."

rule: When one index trends up and another down, avoid the middle asset (ES); it will chop.
quote: "So usually on days like this, I really want to avoid ES because it's going to be choppy, right?"

rule: Once the previous day low has been taken, the protected swing below it no longer counts as protected; look to the next higher-timeframe target (here the previous month's low).
quote: "I don't really consider this one protected anymore because we took the previous day low."

rule: Ignore an SMT that forms where price has not hit a relevant level; a bullish SMT at the previous day low means nothing if price never reached the relevant level.
quote: "why I didn't really care about the SMT on previous day low in this reaction? Because it failed to actually hit anything relevant."

rule: For a bullish reversal day he needs a consolidation, an open near the previous day low and a hit on the relevant level before looking to the other side.
quote: "For me to trade this to the upside, I need more of a specific framework where I have some sort of consolidation here. We open up right near the previous day low. We hit the relevant level."

rule: A reversal against the daily from a candle with a large wick only targets the open, so it isn't worth trading against a bearish monthly/daily context.
quote: "There is no reason for me to try to trade this reversal day. It has a larger wick, which means I'd only be targeting the open."

rule: Zoom out for the target: the previous day low may be a target, but use the higher-timeframe draw (previous month's low) when the monthly and daily align.
quote: "You have previous day low as a target, yes. But you have to have the context of zoom out. What do we have? Previous month's lows right there."

rule: You need a high to trade away from; with bearish closures it gives you your invalidation.
quote: "The high I can trade away from. That gives me an invalidation when you have bearish closures."

rule: Expect the expansion at 9:30; if the pre-open high is taken before or at 9:30/10:00, the bearish idea is wrong and price is consolidating.
quote: "If we take out this high, it's not going to happen at 9.30 or 10. Because if this high gets taken out, I'm wrong and it's just consolidating or doing something that can do it later."

rule: A 4H SMT at the high of the previous 4H range (marked with vertical lines), with a bearish daily, frames a 9:30 expansion lower.
quote: "I know this is the previous four-hour range, so the high in here, we have an SMT in here. So I go, if price is going to go and expand, when is it going to do that? 9.30, right?"

rule: An expansion candle has a small wick and a large body and closes into its extreme, so you can hold to its close: 9:45 for the 15m, 10:00 for the 30m/1H/4H.
quote: "So a bearish expansion candle, after it forms its wick, generally closes into the low of the candle. If it closes in the low, What does that mean? It means you can hold till the end of the candle"

rule: Exits in order: the price target, then the 9:45 time exit, then the 10:00 time exit.
quote: "Let me look at this. Here's one exit. Here's another exit. Here's the last exit. You're getting pretty good exits."

rule: Macros are fake (arbitrary ranges around HTF candle opens); time entries and exits by the opens and closes of higher-timeframe candles instead.
quote: "Because you're just choosing arbitrary ranges around the open of new higher timeframe candles, right?"

rule: Don't enter at the end of a 15m candle (e.g. 9:50); wait for the new candle to open.
quote: "I don't want to be entering right at the end of this 15-minute candle. Why would I enter at 950 here? I want to wait for the new candle open."

rule: A shallow swing that barely forms a sweep (nearly equal highs) is not a trustworthy protected swing; you need a real reach or swing to trade away from.
quote: "It's so shallow, barely even forms a sweep. It's kind of hard to trust that, right? It's almost like equal highs. If we want to trade away from something, we usually want to see at least some sort of reach, some sort of swing we can trust."

rule: Don't enter below the lows when most of an expansion is done; if already in, trail the stop to each new protected swing.
quote: "You can trail it to these new protected swings, right, as we create new protected swings. But for me, I don't like to enter below the lows already most of the way through an expansion, right?"

rule: Once the 9:30-10:00 trend is over, the short-term trend is done until a new swing forms to trade away from.
quote: "It's just in terms of short-term trend, that's over until you get a new swing to trade away from."

rule: A low only becomes protected when the early-CISD candle closes over the level; if it doesn't close over, the low isn't protected.
quote: "since we have the early CISD, it will show us that this is forming a protected swing if it closes over this in the next 15 seconds... So it didn't close over, so no protected swing yet. So that low is not protected."

rule: His intraday trading window is about 8:00 to 10:30 NY; he mostly ignores what happens outside it.
quote: "If you go to 8 to 10.30 each day, mark that out, that's the move I like to catch."

rule: If price fails to form a continuation, it is likely to make a new low; he prefers it to sweep the high first so a CISD forms the other way and leaves a lower high.
quote: "Fail to form a continuation. If we fail to form a continuation, then we're likely to go to make a new low."

rule: A CISD needs a new low (or high) made by a series of candles, then price closing back over that series; no new low means no CISD.
quote: "It never made a new low. Where is the low? Here is the low. Where is a series of candles that made that? Bryce has to close over that to have a CISD."

rule: He doesn't use EQ from the wick to the close, and doesn't use OTE.
quote: "I don't use the EQ from the wick to the close."

rule: If the bias is right but entries keep getting stopped before price reaches the target, go up one entry timeframe (H1-M5 becomes H1-M15).
quote: "Normally, this means you just need to go up one time frame. It's in my time frame alignment video."

rule: Confirm a 4H high or low with a 15-minute CISD.
quote: "Use a 15-minute change in the state of delivery."

rule: Positional swing trades use daily and hourly, not weekly and 4H.
quote: "I don't use the weekly and 4-hour for positional trading. I use the daily and hourly"

rule: Use all timeframes: everything below the daily sits inside it. Refine from 4H to 1H to 15m when the 4H shows direction but little to frame.
quote: "any time frame under the daily time frame, it's inside of it."

rule: Daily bias comes from the daily chart: highs and lows, candle closures, phases of price, and where you want price to go.
quote: "I use the daily chart. I just use highs and lows and the candle closures, phases of price, basically just where do I want to see price go?"

rule: A level on a correlated index (here ES) can serve as an exit for the instrument you are trading (NQ).
quote: "You could watch this level on ES. Once it hits it, that can provide a potential exit for NQ."

rule: Judge remaining room from the daily range by eye, not ATR: about 200 points inside the day means it can go much further; today was about 400-600.
quote: "If we're like at 200 points range inside the day, you know, that's what I was talking, like when we're inside previous day low or something like that, it's like we can go a lot further."

rule: A small daily wick still counts as a wick; a sweep would be nicer, but by the New York session it matters little.
quote: "It still has a wick. It's small. But it still has one. Would it have been better if it swept out? Sure. But we're in New York all the way over here."

rule: Asia and London highs and lows matter as structure inside the daily idea, on the way to the relevant level; correlated assets can change which one you expect to run.
quote: "So of course, I care about the structure, the highs and lows inside this area, right?"

rule: Intraday entries: once an intraday reversal has formed to trade away from, align the entry with the fractal model.
quote: "once you have an intraday reversal to trade away from, then you're just looking to align it with a fractal model."

rule: The simplest version of his model: trade candle 3 after a candle 2 closure.
quote: "Basically, it's going to say trade candle three after a candle two closure."

rule: Don't trade below the lows once an instrument has already expanded for the day; wait for a new day with a new candle and a new expansion.
quote: "I'm not personally a fan of trying to trade below the lows, right? I'd rather wait for a new day where I have new candle, new expansion"

rule: When you are not in a position, stop watching the chart; wait for the daily close.
quote: "if I'm out of a position not swinging it, I just don't look. Just wait until it closes the daily candle."

rule: On the 15m after an expansion, an index that has not made a new low while yours has (SMT) marks a potential bottom; expect the trailed protected swing to be hit.
quote: "YM is, you can see, prints, so that means YM hasn't made a low on this 15-minute candle. This one has. So potentially a short, a bottom here, and we just hit that protected swing"

rule: Watch the strongest index around the open: a brief pump in the weak index can come from the strong one weakening, and you want that pump to reject without taking the high.
quote: "this move higher caused by YM, you know, having that bearish move at the time. I was wanting to see that reject, right? Because I don't want to see this high taken if we're going to have this bearish move."

rule: In FX, pair a strong currency against a weak one (e.g. bullish USD against the weakest currency); never pair two bearish currencies.
quote: "Because if you did, you would not pair AUD and JPY together. AUD, JPY. Because you have two bearish currencies."

rule: Prop-eval risk per trade = drawdown amount / number of consecutive losses you are willing to take (1-3 aggressive, 5-7 middle, 15-20 conservative).
quote: "2500 divided by seven, maybe. It gives me seven trades before I blow it up. What is that? Something like 350, somewhere in there. There you go. And that's how much I risk."

rule: Judge performance over 100+ trades, not 1-3.
quote: "stop thinking in terms of one, two, three trades and start thinking in terms of 100 trades or more"

rule: Fear of taking a trade is fear of outcome; accept that the next trade can't be predicted.
quote: "So your whole fear is fear of outcome, which means fear of loss."

rule: Trading less often tends to improve results; you don't need to trade every day.
quote: "You don't need to trade a ton to make money."

rule: He doesn't consider fundamentals for intraday trading.
quote: "Do I consider fundamentals? Not in intraday trading, no."

rule: The TTFM indicator only marks SMT where his model looks for it (a reversal SMT and a continuation SMT), not discretionary SMTs.
quote: "So it looks for a reversal SMT and a continuation SMT within my model. It's not going to mark out random SMTs."

rule: When indices decouple (one strongly up, another down), one of them is 'lying' and must come back into alignment; identify which (usually NQ or YM) from the day's relative % change.
quote: "when the market is decoupled, you know, YM was going very bullish, right, and the other two were not, something has to come back into alignment, usually that's NQ or YM"

rule: After the daily EQ is disrespected (daily-bias invalidation), the next draw is the previous day's low/high.
quote: "if you look at my invalidation video, we've disrespected the EQ. The only other thing would be previous state low, right?"

rule: Trade the middle asset, never the lagging one: when the weakest index takes out its target and keeps going, look for the next-weakest (middle) index to catch up to its own daily target.
quote: "I never trade the lagging, only the middle. So I never in this scenario would go trade NQ back here. Personally, I'd only trade a yes."

rule: If the weakest asset continues through its previous-day low, expect the next weakest to reach for its own; as long as the weakest doesn't reverse, don't expect the follower to reverse off its low.
quote: "if YM continues through its previous day low, that means the next weakest asset, oh, yes, could reach for that, right?"

rule: This index-catch-up correlation trade really only works around 9:30-10:00 NY.
quote: "And this really only kind of works right at 9.30, 10."

rule: Targets are almost always daily highs and lows; mark every untaken daily low/high as targets.
quote: "Targets. I almost always use daily highs and lows as targets."

rule: Always focus on the daily: whether price has reached the daily draw/key level decides whether you need a fresh CISD before acting.
quote: "So that's why I'm saying always focus on the daily, right?"

rule: With no daily profile (chop between protected swings, SMT at both PDH and PDL), have no bias and assume consolidation: range highs and lows get swept and price returns inside.
quote: "So I have a lack of bias, right? So I have no real direction. I'm just going to assume that price is going to consolidate"

rule: In consolidation, prefer not to anticipate breakouts; price either sweeps and returns into the range, or sweeps then forms a continuation and breaks out; once it isn't staying in the range, the consolidation read is wrong.
quote: "When price is consolidating, I prefer not to anticipate breakouts"

rule: Don't trade a lower-timeframe fractal setup inside the pre-open range; 9:30 volatility will whipsaw and usually runs both sides of the range.
quote: "9.30 is probably going to whipsaw, right?"

rule: When you lack the setup you want, don't drop to very low timeframes; watch on the hourly so you don't start reading meaning into noise.
quote: "if I kind of lack what I want to see and I go too low, I'm going to start looking at price action and thinking something of it."

rule: A mechanically valid C3/CISD continuation is not a trade without higher-timeframe backing and agreement with the day's context.
quote: "Mechanically a valid C3 within my system. You have the CISD continuation that's formed. Cool. It's not my trade because I don't have the backing from the higher time frame."

rule: A bullish reversal candle in line with the trend tends to return to its opening price for the liquidity around it (used for the 4H in a 15m-4H profile).
quote: "if this is a bullish reversal candle in line with this trend higher, it returns back to its opening price for the liquidity around it."

rule: After a daily closure, the next day needs to respect the low/area for the trend to continue; dumping too deep and not respecting it means the daily profile is poor and there is no bias.
quote: "We need kind of low to respect that. And then we can go trend higher. What do we get? We immediately dump like way too deep."

rule: The daily is the one timeframe where a POI before the closure is not required (ideal, not required) if other context exists, e.g. the monthly candle turning and an aggressive closure.
quote: "So the daily is this one specific timeframe that I don't require a point of interest."

rule: IC-CISD: let the HTF candle open, let a continuation (protected swing) form the wick of candle 3; once it closes, enter in the bias direction with the stop on that wick.
quote: "ICCISD is basically the CISD or continuation, a protected swing that forms the wick of the higher time frame candle in candle 3."

rule: Pre-open/London pairings: H4-M15 or Daily-H1; in London he prefers H4-M15. NY window is 8:00-~11:00.
quote: "If you're trading pre-open or London, what do I like? H4, M15, or daily H1, personally?"

rule: Use the daily open, not the midnight open, because the daily candle is what is being traded.
quote: "I just use the daily open because I'm trying to trade the daily candle."

rule: Don't short (or chase) once price is already below the lows/targets with a full daily range made.
quote: "We're already below the lows of the targets. This is not where it makes sense to be looking short, right?"

rule: Avoid trading an asset that has trended far in one direction and left many failure swings; take the cleaner correlated asset instead.
quote: "when it's trended so far down and you have all these failure swings, I'm not a huge fan of trading that right here. I'd rather take ES"

rule: If a target was already hit (e.g. gold took the PDL/overnight low), expect retracement/consolidation rather than continuation, even with a valid C4 continuation read.
quote: "we've already taken out this intraday low, previous day low, right? So this is an area where we can get some sort of retracement or consolidation."

rule: Mechanically, frame a daily reversal as candle 2 by requiring a sweep of the previous day's low (high); a very shallow sweep is sketchy.
quote: "normally, mechanically, I'd look for a sweep of the previous day's low to frame the reversal as a candle to higher."

rule: For gap targets, use only the portion of the gap with no volume, not the whole gap.
quote: "Why am I not using this full gap? I'm just using the gap where there is no volume whatsoever."

rule: No trading on FOMC after the release; low expectations on FOMC days; wait for the next day.
quote: "I never trade after FOMC. I just wait for the next day."

rule: Chart ETFs/index options on the futures (ES for SPY, NQ for QQQ) because the strategy uses overnight data.
quote: "I use overnight data a lot in my strategy, so I'm not going to use SPY."

rule: In live trading wait for the candle to close exactly as in backtesting; anticipating with a non-closed candle is the most common cause of live underperformance.
quote: "You wait for closures in backtesting in live market. You try to use a non-closed candle to anticipate."

rule: One trade a day maximum (not minimum) for traders who tilt after a loss; 1-2 trades a week is his normal frequency.
quote: "One trade a day max. This doesn't mean not the same as minimum."

rule: Taking profit early changes the system's math: a 2R system breaks even at ~34% win rate, cutting to 1:1 requires 50%.
quote: "Let's say you have a 2R system. Oh, wow, I can't spell. System. There you go. You need, what, a 34% win rate to break even."

rule: Trail runners using daily swings or reactions at previous hourly swings, moving to new continuations; for tighter trailing use a lower-timeframe protected swing (e.g. 3m); start trailing when momentum slows.
quote: "you can just watch reactions at these previously-hour swing points, and then trail to new continuations."

rule: View pullbacks in a winning trade as the chance to trail the stop to the new swing, not as a threat.
quote: "Stop viewing this pullback as something bad. View it as, oh, when it goes here and does this, now I can trail my stop loss to here."

rule: When wrong, own it and review what you saw but didn't act on; the market is always right.
quote: "So when you're wrong, don't just try to say, oh, I'm never wrong and have your ego get in the way."

rule: Psychology: don't tilt, don't revenge trade, don't oversize; 'when you think about doing something stupid, don't do it'; use a max daily loss.
quote: "Don't tilt. Don't revenge trade. Don't oversize. Don't do dumb stuff."

rule: Have a target and plan before entering; he gives no signals so traders develop that skill.
quote: "So I can't tell you a target. That's something you need to figure out for yourself."

rule: At a new monthly open, start by reading how the previous monthly candle closed on every instrument, indices first.
quote: "So, new monthly open, right? So we want to take a look at how this monthly candle closed on everything, right? So we're going to start with indices."

rule: Use the strongest index for the continuation target (YM to previous month's high) and watch for a reversal at that target.
quote: "most likely I'll probably be watching YM reach for previous month's high due to the fact that it's opening up over the area we need it of respect"

rule: At a protected swing near the open of the next HTF candle, expect only a small wick through; if it is disrespected, price runs it out before it can go back the other way.
quote: "we have a protected swing right near the open of this next higher time frame candle, so this is usually where we want to see a small wick to go lower, or if we're going to disrespect that, then we go and run that out, and then we could go back higher."

rule: Mark a consolidation monthly candle high-to-low; the side with the larger wick shows where it points, and failure-swing lows are targets.
quote: "It has a larger wick showing us that it's more pointing down, right? And we have these lows. Failure swings you can see on the monthly candle."

rule: After a large expansion, expect consolidation.
quote: "So obviously large expansion, large expansion usually gets some sort of consolidation."

rule: Avoid doing much on the first day of a new month.
quote: "I don't like to do too much on the first day of the month just because you can get some weirder things occurring."

rule: Protected swings on both sides with mixed bullish/bearish candles means chop: no trade.
quote: "You can see we have protected swings on this side. We have protected swings on that side. It's just a chop fest right now."

rule: Read the weekly profile on the daily chart; you do not need the weekly chart to see previous week's high/low.
quote: "I just use the weekly profile. I'm not making my bias off the weekly candle most of the time."

rule: Trade expansions; after multiple expansion days and an intraday consolidation profile, wait for expansion conditions instead of trading.
quote: "This is not really an area I'd want to be trading at all. I like to trade expansions. I just wait for expansions conditions to form."

rule: The first week of the month (at a pivotal monthly level) decides the monthly direction; by the second week you should have a direction.
quote: "If we are going to form a continuation and go higher, we're going to probably do that this week. If we're going to fail and reverse and go back a lower, we're probably going to do that this week."

rule: A daily close back inside a swept prior-month low would make a candle 2; without that close (and without a CISD) there is no reversal framework.
quote: "I would have really preferred this daily candle could have done it if we would have closed back and reclaimed this previous month's low, so I closed back inside of it. That would have given us a candle too."

rule: Only trade Mondays when Friday was a reversal day.
quote: "The only time I'll look to trade Mondays is when we have a reversal day on Friday."

rule: Do not anticipate oil over weekends; it usually gaps.
quote: "I don't like to anticipate oil over the weekends. You usually get some sort of gap."

rule: Size the daily target with average daily range from the open: a gap-up open uses up range, so the far HTF target becomes unrealistic and the previous day's low becomes the day's target.
quote: "If we open up with a gap up like that, our 80 points become a lot harder to reach, right? Not even to this low. So if we have that gap up, what then becomes our target?"

rule: A gap at the open destroys the expectation for price to really expand that day.
quote: "Kind of destroys the expectation for price to really expand. It's a lot different if it opens up without a gap."

rule: Clusters of failure swings are usually what gets run out (stop-outs before the move).
quote: "The only thing I don't like is I have a lot of failure syncs. That's usually when it gets ran out."

rule: Getting stopped out and taking the re-entry/secondary entry is a valid part of trading toward a daily target.
quote: "Maybe you get stopped out right there trying to trade it, or you get the re-entry, or the secondary entry, right? It can technically be valid to get stopped out taking an entry there"

rule: The trade logic is always derived from the daily chart; lower timeframes only execute it.
quote: "So, but you see how the logic is always derived from the daily chart for me, right?"

rule: Do not take a long when the daily (after three expansion days, a gap up and a PDH sweep) never supports it, whatever the LTF shows.
quote: "Within my model, this daily candle does not ever support the move higher."

rule: A tiny consolidation candle is not part of the CISD series; use the actual structural point, and a close below a consolidation candle is not a CISD.
quote: "I'm not a fan of this little tiny blue green candle. Being the series of the candles because to me I'm looking for the actual structural point, right?"

rule: After a daily open sweeps the previous day high following expansion and trades lower, target the previous day's EQ; a 15m continuation can frame it.
quote: "Opens, sweeps the previous day high after expansion. Trading lower. Where could you look for this to go back to? Previous day's EQ, right?"

rule: Higher-timeframe candles matter, not kill zones.
quote: "I don't really care that much about kill zones. I just care about higher time from candles."

rule: If you keep blowing accounts: consistent position size, one trade a day max, learn to lose.
quote: "How do you fix this? Consistent position size, one trade a day max. He probably struggles to learn to lose"

rule: Set and forget: 2R or -1R; do not trail or move the stop to soothe fear of green going red.
quote: "My fix idea. 2R or minus 1R. Set and forget. Learn to feel the emotions."

rule: Exiting early does not 'book profit'; it raises the win rate you need to break even.
quote: "I just view it as, oh, now I have to win 16% more to break even, right?"

rule: You cannot be emotionless; feel the emotions without acting on them.
quote: "You just have to feel your emotions without acting on them."

rule: Have a defined model and a checklist; if all requirements are met, place the trade; treat trading as data collection.
quote: "make a checklist if everything Meets the requirements. Place the trade. Stop overthinking it. You got to start treating trading like data collection"

rule: Higher timeframe means fewer setups; risk per trade should rise as setup count falls (more setups, less risk each).
quote: "If I'm trading more setups, I want to risk less because I have more. I'm basically spreading my risk out over a number of trades. If I have less setups, I risk more."

rule: Daily swing setups come 6-8 times a year and get much more risk than intraday trades or scalps.
quote: "So for instance, when I take a daily swing, I'm risking a lot more money than an intraday trade or a scalp."

rule: Moving up a timeframe removes losers; a flat period is better than a losing period.
quote: "But it's like, they're flat periods, yeah, but do you want to have a flat period or do you want to have a losing period?"

rule: With no clear bias, do not drop to the 1m to find a trade; zoom out instead of going lower.
quote: "If I don't understand what's going on, I don't go lower. I zoom out, right?"

rule: For a continuation, the candle's wick should form at the point of interest and the candle should close over; once it closes over, that swing is protected.
quote: "Ideally, you'd want to see what? The wick of this candle form, where? Point of interest, right? Then you want to see this close over. When this closes over, this swing's protected."

rule: Trading candle 3 with an intra-candle CISD is the highest win-rate part of his strategy.
quote: "For your win rate, trade candle 3 with an IC, CISD. That is the highest win rate part of my strategy."

rule: To raise win rate, lose less: find what losses share, usually wrong/lacking bias or entering too early; practice bias on the daily, and move one timeframe up for early entries.
quote: "Most likely what they have, these are the main ones I see is bias is wrong slash lack of bias or too early on entries."

rule: When markets/assets disagree and you don't know what's happening, wait patiently rather than zooming in to force a trade.
quote: "Option one, zoom in super low and force a trade. Option two, be patient and wait."

rule: His whole concept set: highs and lows, FVG, CISD, EQ (50%), plus open-high-low-close logic.
quote: "What do I use? Highs and lows, fair value gap, CISD, and then EQ, I guess. 50% FIB. So we'll just say 50% FIB. And then the rest is just open, high, low, close logic."

rule: A HTF CISD can be used as a point of interest only when it makes sense in context (mechanical rules in his POI video).
quote: "So this, sure, it can make sense, but it has to make sense in the context."

rule: Reverse engineer price before backtesting.
quote: "I think you should reverse engineer before you ever backtest."

rule: Trade the framework, not the pattern: a non-ideal candle 2 closure is acceptable when the HTF framework and model are there; an ideal one is only preferred.
quote: "If there's a proper framework and there's a model, I don't really care if it's ideal or not. Would I prefer it? Yeah."

rule: Manage a swing position by watching daily closures only.
quote: "In terms of managing my position, I'm just watching how we close daily closures. That's really it."

rule: PSP and SMT only matter when there is a valid fractal model; they are not confluence on their own.
quote: "I only look for these things when I have a valid fractal model."

rule: Size risk from drawdown, not account size: dollar risk is about drawdown / 10-15 so you survive the 5-7+ loss streaks you will hit.
quote: "Take your drawdown divided by maybe 10 to 15. That's your dollar risk."

rule: Any R:R is fine if you know the break-even win rate: about 51% at 1:1, about 34% at 2R.
quote: "When you go to 1-to-1R, you have to win 51% of trades. When you're at 2R, what do you have to win? 34% of trades."

rule: Price does not have to fill a gap/hit the far level; a 1.5R target is fine.
quote: "Personally, I don't necessarily say you have to fill that. You don't need to go hit this level. 1.5R is fine."

rule: He prefers 2R-4R so that winning 3-4 of 10 trades is still profitable.
quote: "I'm more in the area of wanting to be a 2R, 3R, 4R, because I like the mental barrier it puts up where, hey, I can win three out of ten trades and I'll be okay."

rule: He does not use breaker blocks.
quote: "I don't use breakers, right?"

rule: If the entry is unclear, you can wait for the open of the new higher-timeframe candle.
quote: "Or you can wait for the open and new higher time from candle if you want."

rule: Take partials only if the remaining position still meets the model's requirement; half off at 1R on a 2R trade makes it ~1.5R and needs ~43% win rate.
quote: "I only take partials when it still meets my requirement for a model because partials ruin a win rate."

rule: Do not add to an existing long or hedge when price is low in the range near the EQ.
quote: "The only thing that would be on my mind is hedging my position. Which, it was already too low into the range and around the EQ, so I'm not hedging right there."

rule: On the LTF, a close over forms a new protected swing and price should continue in that direction.
quote: "Remember, I said this closes over, this forms a new protected swing, and it should continue higher."

rule: A bearish day in a bearish model that just took the previous day low does not support longs.
quote: "It's a bearish day in a bearish model, and we just took out previous day low. This doesn't support expansion higher."

rule: When relative strength flips on lower timeframes, trade the asset that is stronger on the lower timeframe and still aligned with the HTF.
quote: "usually you want to be on the one on the lower timeframe that's also aligned, right?"

rule: Set the intraday target from the daily range: look at how far recent daily candles moved (e.g. ~600 NQ points) and target the liquidity that range reaches.
quote: "I just looked at the previous daily candles. This one went like 600 points. That one went like 600 or so points."

rule: Enter in the middle of the candle or near its opening price, not after the candle has already made its expected range; this is what keeps you from chasing.
quote: "You want to be entering in the middle of the candle or near the opening price, not after the candle's already made its range."

rule: Do not take continuation trades once the daily range has been made.
quote: "I don't trade continuations like that at the daily range"

rule: After a pre-open run-up, he prefers a sweep back in (manipulation of the consolidation low into a gap) off the open rather than trading the open off SMT/CISD alone.
quote: "Personally, I'm not a fan of doing that once we've already had this expansion. Usually I prefer some sort of sweep back in."

rule: If price does not meet your entry requirement, skip the entry but keep the bias and the target; a missed setup is not a reversal signal.
quote: "Just because I wanted something, right, and it didn't do it, doesn't mean that I'm like, oh, I'm bearish now. No."

rule: Expansion candles (4H, 1H, 30m) usually only change direction at 10:00 NY; occasionally 9:45.
quote: "Usually 10. It can happen 9.45 too, right? But most of the time it's 10."

rule: Do not trade the strongest index at the high of its 4H candle; wait for 10:00.
quote: "I have no interest in trying to trade YM at the high of this 4-hour candle. You'd have to wait for 10 a.m."

rule: Do not predict a candle before it closes; base anticipation on closures (daily closures for tomorrow, the 9:45/10:00 closure intraday).
quote: "Guys, you gotta stop trying to predict things before the candle closures, right?"

rule: Anticipation for tomorrow comes only from today's daily closure.
quote: "What do I base my anticipation off? Daily closures."

rule: In a consolidation, the bullish framework needs the consolidation low run into a gap where lows rest, then a reaction there; if that level fails, there is no bullish case.
quote: "Then you watch the reaction at this level because this is the only spot for me to be bullish from. If this fails, it's not bullish."

rule: Skip assets that are in a higher-timeframe consolidation or lack daily direction (gold, silver today).
quote: "It's a consolidation to me on the higher time frame, so I'm not touching it."

rule: Among NQ/ES/YM, the middle asset (often ES) is the default to trade; you can switch at the open based on relative strength.
quote: "I would favor ES in terms of trading, correct? Because it's kind of more in the middle while this is the strongest asset, but you can switch at the open."

rule: If you cannot decide what to trade, just trade ES.
quote: "ES is most of the time in the middle, so if you're really struggling with that, just focus on ES."

rule: Do not trade an asset that has already done its expansion while the others are still expanding.
quote: "Because YM's already expanded too far. It already did its expansion, right? Consolidating while these are doing their expansion now."

rule: A lower-timeframe reversal formation against the 4H candle is a fade of all timeframes; use it as a clue for the correlated assets, not as a trade.
quote: "Sure, it's an ideal formation, but you're fading the 4-hour candle, you're fading all the other timeframes."

rule: The POI for the strongest index to reverse is the other indices reaching their targets.
quote: "What's the point of interest for YM to reverse? The other assets hitting a target."

rule: His model prefers price in a premium for continuation higher (it does not require a discount entry in a bullish trend).
quote: "We are in a premium now. Yeah, my model actually prefers premiums or stuff to go higher."

rule: On a bullish day he uses the previous day's EQ: the daily wick should form in the upper part of the previous day's range; the previous month's EQ in the same area adds confluence, plus the intraday profile aligning.
quote: "I'm using the EQ of this previous day. I want to see the wick form in the upper part of it. We also have the previous month's EQ there."

rule: Daily bullish bias read: previous month's lows run out, an engulfing daily candle and an uptrend.
quote: "We run out previous month's lows, we have a nice engulfing candle, and we're trending higher."

rule: Intraday reversal profile = a low taken out, then a 4H candle closure plus an hourly change in state of delivery; treat that low as the low of the day and expect it to hold.
quote: "That would be, what, a 4-hour candle closure, plus an hourly change in the state of delivery."

rule: POIs are gaps and highs/lows (plus CISD); he does not use breakers and rarely uses HTF order blocks.
quote: "So I don't use breakers. I rarely use higher timeframe OBs. I use the CISD, but most of the time I prefer what I talk about in here, which is gaps and highs and lows."

rule: Do not pick a distant HTF gap and trade from it blindly; trade what price is doing now and only reference POIs.
quote: "I trade what is happening over here. Do I reference points of interest over here? Yes"

rule: His model is not 'find POI, find reaction, entry model'; bias comes mechanically from candle closures and EQ, then the intraday profile.
quote: "most models out there just do this. They're like, find a POI, find reaction, entry model. I'm not like that."

rule: If you are right on bias but get stopped before the move, move up one timeframe for entry; do not just widen the stop.
quote: "Move up one time frame for entry. There you go. Make your stop loss bigger? Nah."

rule: Stops go where the model mechanically places them (the low); moving them wider after losses kills R:R and forces resizing.
quote: "this is where I mechanically would put my stop loss on this low, but since I've been taking losses, I'm just gonna do that. Like, now you're just killing your risk to reward"

rule: Do not add intraday risk in the same direction as an open swing; prefer intraday trades against the swing as a hedge.
quote: "I prefer trading short intraday against my long swings because then I'm hedging my position, if that makes sense, instead of doubling down on it"

rule: At all-time highs (no liquidity to target), take profit with time-based exits, a trailing stop or the average daily range.
quote: "Time-based exits, trailing your stop losses, average daily range, all of that."

rule: Only CPI, FOMC and NFP matter as news.
quote: "I only focus on three things. DPI, FOMC, and FP. That's it."

rule: Top-down: for intraday trading nothing above the daily matters; for swings look at monthly, 3-month, even yearly.
quote: "If I'm trading intraday, I really don't care about much more than the daily chart. If I'm taking swing trades, I'll look higher"

rule: He reads the weekly expansion candle but does not lean on it, since the daily already shows it.
quote: "And I said, well, weekly bullish expansion candle. I don't really care too much for that because I can see it from the daily chart."

rule: If London forms the reversal/low, hold into New York because New York expands; only an Asia-reversal / London-continuation trade might be closed before New York.
quote: "If you're trading at Asia reversal, New York or London continuation, then yeah, you might close before New York. But if you're trading this kind of London reversal or London formula low, New York is what expands."

rule: Chart only the mini contracts; ignore what micros do.
quote: "I do all my charting on the minis, no matter what."

rule: He does not use kill zones, seasonal tendencies, Asia/Monday range standard deviations, or index-oil correlation.
quote: "I don't use kill zones."

rule: When waiting on a level, give it ~30 minutes to react on the working timeframe; do not drop to the 1-minute to call every move.
quote: "you literally just have to sit here for 30 minutes or so and see how it reacts. But most people will be like, oh, going to the one-minute."

rule: A candle 2 sequence that continues into candles 3, 4, 5 without expansion is a consolidation; then wait for a manipulation of its low.
quote: "but then now we have candle 2, 3, 4, And this is 5, it's a consolidation."

rule: If backtests win but live trading doesn't, the problem is execution (fear of loss, ego, tilt, oversizing), not strategy.
quote: "So your strategy has nothing to do with strategy. It has the fact that you technically are not following your strategy because you're just skipping things out of fear."

rule: Choose the discomfort of sitting in a trade without breaking rules over the discomfort of breaking rules and blowing accounts; change or quit.
quote: "Do you want the discomfort of not following rules, breaking them, blowing up accounts? Or do you want the discomfort of sitting in a trade, feeling the emotions, not breaking your rules, right?"

rule: Once a swing is on, don't watch it; if you're not exiting at current price, P&L checks change nothing.
quote: "When I put on a trade, I really just don't look at it for the most part."

rule: A swing trade is held for a run, not two days of movement.
quote: "if I'm in a swing trade, I'm not looking for two days of movement. Like for instance, this one. I'm not just looking for two days of movement. I'm looking for a run."

rule: The ideal formation is a fractal concept usable on any timeframe.
quote: "The ideal formation is a fractal concept you can use whenever you want."

rule: Read the daily through phases of price. After several days of expansion into an important level with the daily closing at its low, expect the next day to open, form a small-wick reversal and trade back into the range.
quote: "We've had one, two, three days of expansion into an important level, right? And where are we closing? We're closing right at the low of the day, right? So that allows us to open up. Form a reversal with a small wick"

rule: On a C2 daily reversal, the first target is the EQ and the second is the previous day high.
quote: "on my C2 daily candle, what's our target on this? First target's the EQ, second target, previous day high."

rule: Compare how far each correlated index is from the target; the one closest to it (ES here) is the one to trade.
quote: "ES is a lot closer to hitting previous day high than ES, or I mean than NQ. YM's already over the high."

rule: Normally NQ and YM sit at opposite ends with ES in the middle. When ES is strongest and NQ and YM trade weak together, the correlation is off: wait for it to sort itself out.
quote: "Right now it's a little weird because ES is strongest and NQ and YM are both kind of weakest or trading together. See that? I don't really like days when they do that so we'll just wait."

rule: Use the VIX (or the daily chart itself) to set daily range expectations. With the VIX at the low of its range, expect a smaller daily range.
quote: "you can use the VIX to help with your expectations on range"

rule: If most of the daily range has already been made, a late continuation is less attractive.
quote: "The only thing is we've already made most of a daily range."

rule: Don't drop to the 1-minute without a reason. If you aren't looking for a trade, there's nothing to see there.
quote: "The big lesson is stop trying to go to the 1-minute when you have no idea why you should be on the 1-minute."

rule: Don't short against a set of highs that haven't been swept. To short off highs he needs SMT, i.e. a correlated asset taking out its high.
quote: "to frame something off these highs, I would need some sort of SMT, which is why I was saying I would need NQ to take out this high, because personally I would not short against all these highs right here"

rule: Don't long at the highs. A long needs an early-morning retracement and then a continuation.
quote: "I don't like to long at the highs, so really it would have to be some sort of AM or early morning retracement and then a continuation."

rule: Macros are not real. Trade the opens and closes of higher-timeframe candles; 9:30 matters because it's the stock market open.
quote: "I don't believe in a time macro. I don't believe that's a thing. I really care about Open and closes of higher timeframe candles."

rule: Don't enter at the end of a higher-timeframe candle after its range is made. Wait for the new candle to open and form its wick; entering in the first ~10 minutes of a new higher-timeframe candle is logical. A positional entry is the exception and enters at the open.
quote: "you don't want to enter right before the open of a new candle, generally speaking, unless it's a positional entry. At that point, you enter the open."

rule: The indicator dots are protected swings, and the trend stays valid until the protected swing is taken.
quote: "So, like, technically this trend is still valid because we haven't taken this out"

rule: When the manipulation leg is very large and the CISD level is far away, don't wait for the CISD; use a higher-timeframe candle closure (e.g. 4H) or a new continuation. Mechanically, though, the trend hasn't shifted until price closes through the CISD level.
quote: "You just have to realize, like, technically, mechanically within my model, the trend hasn't shifted until the closure through this level, right? But you can do that."

rule: Only the real FOMC (rate decision, statement, projections) brings volatility. FOMC minutes don't matter.
quote: "I care about the actual FOMC, not the minutes."

rule: If no continuation forms inside the POI/gap, the alternative path is the intraday profile sweeping the lows, a closure through, a new continuation, then trade it.
quote: "So you have to wait for the intraday profile, sweep out the lows, there's your closure through, there's a continuation, you can trade it to the upside."

rule: Without a sweep of the high there's no SMT, and without SMT he has no way to trade the downside against a bullish daily profile.
quote: "We didn't have a sweep of that high to really tell me like, okay, we have an SMT to be able to trade the downside. So there's no way to really trade the downside."

rule: A POI plus displacement is not his model.
quote: "I personally don't just look for a point of interest and then displacement. That's not what my model does."

rule: A very aggressive move lower that leaves the highs unswept is usually fake; he expects it to go higher.
quote: "Now, normally when you see something like this, I usually think a very aggressive move lower, leaving that is usually fake, and then I want to see it go higher."

rule: If C3 sweeps the C2 extreme, the old C2 is void and the sweeping candle becomes the new C2. Wait for its closure.
quote: "What does C3 do? It sweeps it out. This is not C2 anymore. This is now C2."

rule: The model always needs a swing to trade away from. If none has formed, wait for one.
quote: "What's the common theme within my model? I need a swing to trade away from."

rule: A daily CISD against the trend isn't enough on its own. He wants a continuation to form before he gets interested in that direction.
quote: "Once we form a continuation, that's when my eyes are more interested on the downside."

rule: For gold longs out of a range, wait for silver to run the range low (gold holding = SMT) before buying.
quote: "I would not personally look to buy gold until silver runs out this low"

rule: When C3 heads into an opposing imbalance, judge the phases of price at that level and how strong your bias is. Candles that don't reverse at the level suggest continuation through it.
quote: "So it really is how strong is your bias and then also the phases of the price at that level, right?"

rule: A structural SMT (between a swing and a key level such as the PDL, outside the model's swing point) can be used before the model closes. The in-model SMT is only looked for after the C2/C3 closure.
quote: "This is like a structural SMT. So yeah, I can look at this before the model closes."

rule: SMT is confirmed by a change in the state of delivery (CISD).
quote: "I confirm SMT with a change in the state of delivery."

rule: With SMT between correlated assets, trade the weakest one for shorts (and the strongest for longs).
quote: "But I'm probably going to trade whatever one's weakest if I'm looking short."

rule: SMT and PSP are confirmations, not the model.
quote: "SMT is great confirmation. ESP, great confirmation. It doesn't make the whole model, though."

rule: An ideal candle 3 closure also creates a protected swing; on the lower timeframe it needs the sweep and the close below the level, which also closes the higher timeframe. No closure means no C3.
quote: "If we get this closure, then you technically have an ideal candle 3 closure on the 5-minute."

rule: He prefers the higher-timeframe candle to close, not just the lower timeframe.
quote: "I'm not a huge fan of when it closes the lower time frame and not the higher time frame."

rule: Check where the R target lands. If 2R sits below the intraday lows, you must anticipate the day expanding there for the trade to make sense.
quote: "So if you're trading this one, looks like this, 2R would be there. Really, you have to be like, Anticipating the day to go to here, for that to make sense."

rule: Taking profit early raises the win rate you need. 2R needs about 34% to break even, 1R needs 50%.
quote: "let's say you're taking 2R, what win rate do you need to be breakeven? 34%. If you start taking all your profits and you end up trading at 1R, now instead of needing 34% win rate, Now you need 50% win rate."

rule: Every entry needs higher-timeframe logic. Without it, only a new continuation or an invalidation of the opposing structure justifies a counter trade.
quote: "There's no higher timeframe logic to taking this along here, right?"

rule: Higher-timeframe bias is the confluence that stops you pattern-trading the model and explains when C3 delivers versus reverses.
quote: "Very simple. Higher timeframe bias. That's it. If you align the model with a higher timeframe bias, you don't expect it to react like that."

rule: When correlated indices disagree (one bullish, one bearish, one in the middle), ask which one is lying. If you can't tell, the profile is chop: don't trade it.
quote: "Which one's lying, right? ... To me, this daily profile's chop, so I'm not going to touch it."

rule: Trading C2 is inherently a reversal trade and fails more often than trading the next day's continuation (C3).
quote: "This is trying to trade C2, right? So it's inherently you're trying to trade a reversal. So it's more likely to fail than if this would have closed up here, and then you could trade the continuation the following day."

rule: A CISD is the order block that changes the trend. After it, OBs or protected swings in the new direction are just continuations, not CISDs.
quote: "CISD is the order block that changes the trend, right?"

rule: Auto bias 1 shows a model only if the next timeframe pair up also has a valid model (H1-M5 needs H4-M15). Auto bias 2 needs a valid model two pairs up (daily-H1).
quote: "So if you have the M5 chart with auto-bias 1, you have to have not only an hourly and 5-minute fractal model, but you also have to have a 4-hour and 15-minute fractal model."

rule: Trade only when the market is one-sided, i.e. you can frame it in one direction only. A reversal day that frames both ways is confusing; C3 daily candles are one-sided, so learners should focus on them.
quote: "There's a reason why I say for most people, especially if you're learning, to just focus on C3 daily candles."

rule: Even an ideal C3 closure is less attractive if it has already expanded and taken the intraday low; it's better with a smaller candle and a better daily profile.
quote: "So for me, it's already expanded, took out the intraday low. It's not really that ideal."

rule: Don't take a trade after price has already trended to and hit the target.
quote: "Why would I try to short after we already just trended all the way down, and then after we hit our target?"

rule: Don't trade a seek & destroy / chop daily profile with broken correlation; an uneventful day is a watch-and-answer-questions day.
quote: "The daily profile isn't the best. More of a seek and destroy, right?"

rule: A 1H close above the daily C2 EQ against a bearish bias is a soft invalidation. It isn't mechanical: keep the idea but expect less expansion and cut targets to the daily open, intraday lows, sometimes the PDL.
quote: "You're looking to adjust your targets to the current daily open, intraday lows, sometimes previous day low. So it's not a mechanical thing where it closes over this."

rule: In a ranging profile, enter at the edge of the range as a reversal trade.
quote: "It is more of one of these profiles, though, so you really have to enter the edge of the range. You kind of have to reversal trade this"

rule: The cleanest daily profile: open, sweep (or reach into an FVG), a V-shape reversal, then continuation after continuation.
quote: "Guys, if you can have a daily profile that opens up and looks like this, that's like the cleanest thing you can get."

rule: For long-term positions, buy below the yearly open at a logical spot after the yearly candle forms its wick. In a trend, don't wait for a deep discount.
quote: "I'm always trying to buy below the yearly open. Below the yearly open at a logical spot after it's formed a wick."

rule: Swing trading: daily chart with entry on the daily or an aligned hourly; monthly-daily model refined to the H4/H1. Day trading daily-H4-M15 gives roughly 0-1 trades a day.
quote: "I just use the daily chart, and then I either enter on the daily or enter On the hourly chart aligned with that."

rule: Define your model and your session window: he trades the NY morning only (sometimes Asia swings), never the PM session. Watch charts only when a setup exists.
quote: "I know I don't trade PM session, so it's really just the morning, and that's it."

rule: Taking losses: take it, feel it, don't do dumb stuff after it. Otherwise quit.
quote: "Take a loss, feel it, don't do dumb stuff."

rule: Learn the model by marking up charts on a 'quiz' template with the indicator's fractals hidden, then compare with the indicator.
quote: "Now what you can do is practice marking it up."

rule: A close through the daily EQ is a soft invalidation, not a bias switch: it means the wick is too large to expect expansion, so keep the bias and cut targets to the daily open / liquidity around the open / intraday lows.
quote: "A closure through the EQ does not equal switch bias. It can mean the invalidation of the bias when it's paired with other things along with the daily profile."

rule: Bias for the day comes from the daily chart plus the daily profile; an overnight grind up with no trusted low of day is a retracement for a New York reversal, so do not be bullish off it.
quote: "But when we just grind up, I'm viewing this as a retracement for New York to reverse."

rule: On a reversal candle (large wick, small body) expect price to close near its open; targets are the opening price and the liquidity around the open, and range expectations are small.
quote: "Reversal candle, that's what today is. A large wick and a small body, you see that? A large opposing run. Price is likely to close near its open."

rule: On an inside-type day the only reference points are previous day high, previous day low and the EQ.
quote: "Yeah, so on a day like this, really your reference points are previous day high, previous day low, EQ."

rule: Pick the weakest index for continuation shorts (or the middle one); never trade the lagging/strongest asset.
quote: "I never trade the very lagging asset."

rule: If a setup lacks the sweep it needs mechanically, SMT with the other indices lets you still treat the candle as a candle 2 / reversal candle.
quote: "But because of the SMT, you can still treat this like a candle too, as a reversal candle."

rule: For a late continuation after the first target, the weakest asset needs SMT: a stronger asset (YM/ES) must run its previous high first; he dislikes these because he prefers to be in before the expansion.
quote: "I'm not a personal fan of these trades because I like to be in before the expansion, not kind of a later continuation of it, but that's the only option there for me."

rule: Short into the target, not after it is hit; once the target is hit, the move is either done (consolidation) or needs a fresh reason to continue.
quote: "I'm not a huge fan of trying to short after I hit a target, right? I want to short into the target."

rule: When choosing the downside target, take the consolidation low (the easy low) rather than a V-shaped protected low, which is harder to reach.
quote: "Because to me, this is more of a V shape. Like I said, it's harder to get to this low. This is the easy low to get to."

rule: After an expansion into a level, expect a new phase of price: consolidation or a retracement into a gap, which should hold for a continuation.
quote: "What can we look for after expansion into a level? A new phase of price. You want to see a consolidation or retracement. Where would you want to see a retracement? Into a gap."

rule: Small wick on the reversal candle supports expansion; a large wick makes it a reversal candle and you wait for the expansion. For continuation, the candle should hold/respect the EQ, then the expansion candle must close below the level.
quote: "If it has a large wick, right, let's say it would have gone all the way up here, what does that mean? It means that it's a reversal candle, you wait for the expansion. Since it had the small wick, and this is why I wanted to show it quickly, it has a small wick, it supports expansion lower."

rule: The model is fractal: the same C2/EQ logic applies on the 1m as on the daily, and on any asset.
quote: "Guys, you got to think it's all fractal. If you saw this on a daily chart, you'd say, oh, this should respect the EQ and go lower."

rule: If you keep getting stopped out before the move, move up one timeframe for entries (5m to 15m); if you have an invalidation to place a stop on, take the trade.
quote: "Move up one time frame. If you're on the five-minute, you're always getting stopped out. Just go to the 15-minute for entries."

rule: For overnight (London) setups use the 15m for entries because lower timeframes are sloppy; enter on the 15m closure through, stop on the protected swing, target the range EQ or range high.
quote: "I'm just a big fan of if I'm going to be trading overnight session. I just use the 15-minute because it's kind of sloppy."

rule: Timeframe pairings: Daily-1H fractal if you work a 9-5, 4H-15m when free; with 4H-15m you only miss moves if you don't trade C2 in New York.
quote: "If you have to work a 9 to 5, the daily and hourly fractal, I think that's a very solid plan. And then if you're off work, trading the 4-hour and 15, I think that's very solid as well."

rule: A trade needs three things aligned: daily bias, structure, and the daily profile; a swept-and-reclaimed hourly low is not enough without a bullish daily profile.
quote: "All right, I need to have daily bias that lines up. I need to have the structure that lines up and the daily profile."

rule: TGIF profile requirements: Monday/Tuesday high, expansion through Thursday (multiple days of expansion, not expansion-pause-expansion), hits the weekly objective; still needs aligned LTF price action, ideally a sweep of the previous day low with SMT, then trade back into the range.
quote: "Normally, I like to see a sweep of the previous day low, then trading that back in."

rule: Pre-open trades only with bias, an aligned daily profile, and an invalidation he trusts will not be swept by 09:30 volatility.
quote: "The only way I will do a pre-open trade is if I have bias, daily profile aligns, and then I have an invalidation. I trust to not be swept out by vol at 9.30."

rule: Do not fade strong trends/breakouts (e.g. gold); wait for a swing low and trade with the trend.
quote: "Stop trying to fade this. Just trade the trend. Wait for a swing low and trade it higher."

rule: Beginners should use a strict take profit and stop loss with no management; management adds decisions and usually costs R.
quote: "So people early on, I usually say, just have a strict pick profit and stop loss because they mess up the management."

rule: Learning order: swing-point numbering (candle 1-4), candle 2 closure, then wick size for reversals and OHLC.
quote: "So candle 1, candle 2, candle 3, candle 4, and then learn what candle 2 closure is. That's really all you need to start, but you're going to want to focus on learning quick size for reversals and open high, low, close."

rule: EQ placement depends on the candle's wick (large vs small wick).
quote: "It's depending if it has a wick, a large wick, or a small wick."

rule: He uses premium/discount the opposite way to ICT (in expansions he does not want price to retrace up to a discount).
quote: "I don't use discount and premium like ICT teaches it. I use it the opposite way."

rule: Protected swings fail and get re-swept (then price continues with trend) usually after significant liquidity has been taken.
quote: "It is when we have taken out some sort of significant liquidity."

rule: Consolidation = a high and a low that price stays within for a period of time; a range's targets are its EQ and its extremes.
quote: "it's a high and a low that price stays within for a period of time."

rule: Tools in the model: fair value gaps, highs, lows and order blocks only (no OTE, GEX, IFVG-as-strategy, double purge, quarter SMT).
quote: "I use fair value gaps, highs, lows, and order blocks. That's it."

rule: Yellow-folder news like 09:45 PMI is ignored.
quote: "I just don't really care about yellow folder news at 945, personally."

rule: Your HTF opinion only matters at the timeframe you hold trades: a monthly bearish view is irrelevant to a 3m trade held 30 minutes, relevant to a 4H entry.
quote: "If you're trading the four-hour as an entry, sure, then that starts to matter. It depends where your intraday timeframe is"

rule: His NY-open routine: get to the chart (~09:25), look at the daily and daily profile for about three minutes.
quote: "Get to chart. Look at it for maybe three minutes. That's it."

rule: At 10:00 all timeframes print new candles; re-assess whether the move is done or whether a continuation (with a tradeable swing) exists.
quote: "So now we have what, guys? We have 10 a.m. So what does that mean? New candles, right?"

rule: After a reversal you need either a sweep to go the other way or a breakout and retest, evaluated after the candle closes.
quote: "we either need a sweep to go the other way, or we need a breakout and a retest. But that's after this candle closes"

rule: Stop studying once you know the model; most failure is oversizing/tilt, not missing information.
quote: "But guys, you don't need to learn anything else. You need to simply stop doing dumb stuff."

rule: Read relative strength first: watch the strongest asset for a reversal, because when the strongest reverses the weaker ones usually follow.
quote: "So I'm kind of looking towards the strongest asset, see if it forms a reversal because then usually the weakest ones will, right?"

rule: If price has failed to close over a key level after an expansion, expect a retracement/reversal phase. Even for longs, want the nearby low run first ('to go higher, I still want it to go lower first').
quote: "Like if I want it to go higher, I still want it to go lower first."

rule: A close over the level is what forms the protected swing; until that close, don't treat the move as aligned.
quote: "can we close over this level on NASDAQ? Because if we do, we can form a protected swing here and then potentially have a move back towards this gap the other side of the range."

rule: Higher-timeframe bullish signals (4H CISD, weekly sweep) don't make the lower timeframe aligned bullish while price can't close over the daily level.
quote: "Just because you're bullish on the higher timeframes doesn't mean that this is aligned bullish yet."

rule: Don't trade away from failure swings; he doesn't want to short below lined-up highs unless the strongest asset sweeps them.
quote: "I don't want to trade away from failure swings. You can make a case for it in here, but guys, real time, I want that sweep, right?"

rule: To short, the strongest asset must sweep/reverse off its level. That gives the SMT, and then you trade the weaker/middle asset in continuation. If the move is too far away, skip it.
quote: "If I'm wanting to trade short here, I want to see the strongest asset reverse off this level, right? Because then that shows me a high could be put in on the strongest one. So then I can have some sort of SMT and then I can trade this one, right? While this is continuing. A lot of times if it's too far away, I avoid it."

rule: He will not trade away from a high unless the strongest asset sweeps it out; this is a fixed personal rule from experience.
quote: "Like I'm not going to trade away from this high like this unless it sweeps it out with the strongest asset, right? So I just need that to occur."

rule: When strength keeps flipping between NQ and YM off the open, focus on the middle asset (usually ES).
quote: "When the strengths are kind of jumping around, see? Weaker. Now this one's stronger holding up. A lot of times I like to look at the middle asset because these are going to be flipping around."

rule: Strength can switch off the open (weakest becomes strongest); don't act on a 30-second reaction. Give it a few minutes.
quote: "Gotta give it a few minutes. Don't just try to use a 30-second reaction."

rule: A reversal off the low needs at least a 5m CISD (3m is also fine).
quote: "So if it is going to reverse there, now NQ is the strongest, what would you need at least? 5-minute CISD. Use 5 or this 3-minute. Doesn't really matter."

rule: Plan with if-then statements: if price fails to manipulate it goes to one target; if it reacts, take the other path.
quote: "you can have an if-then statement. If it fails to manipulate, it goes there. If it reacts, then you can have this one."

rule: On a bullish reversal, the upper 50% of the reversal range must hold.
quote: "What area do we want to see hold, right? If we're looking at this, we want to see the upper 50% of this, right?"

rule: Refining an HTF POI on the lower timeframe: for the area to hold, it must form a 1m (or 3m) swing there, i.e. a 1m continuation. Otherwise the idea fails.
quote: "If this is going to hold, what does it need to do? It needs to form a one-minute swing in this area, so a one-minute continuation. Does that make sense? Otherwise, this fails."

rule: After a bearish expansion candle closes near its low, he prefers the next candle to take the previous candle's low first and then react bullishly. Not mandatory, but preferred. Upper wick first is more bearish.
quote: "So this next candle, you usually want to see it go lower first. Take out the previous candle's low. And then you have a bullish reaction. So this is like refinement. Of a higher time frame point of interest into the lower time frame. Technically it doesn't have to take the low, I just prefer that, right?"

rule: A deep opposing run into the POI makes the setup less ideal; you want a shallow opposing run.
quote: "You see how this is a deep opposing run? You want to see like a very shallow opposing run."

rule: Waiting for a continuation instead of trading the reversal keeps you out of failed reversals. If it works you can catch it later; on this day reversals would have cost two stop losses.
quote: "You see how trying to wait for this continuation protects you from what I would say is probably going to be a failed reversal trade. If it goes and works, then we can catch it later on. But this is why I wait for continuation."

rule: With only a 5m closure, you want a new continuation that also gives the 15m closure; otherwise you're better off waiting for the 15m.
quote: "Normally in a scenario like this, if you have a five-minute closure, you want to see a new continuation form that also gives you that 15-minute closure, right? Or you're just better off waiting for the 15-minute."

rule: In chop you usually want one asset to run out a low to reset the chop (a range deviation) before anything is framed.
quote: "Normally when you see chop like this, now we have this as the weakest asset, that is the strongest asset. Normally we want one of these assets to run out of low because then that kind of resets the chop rate. Now we have a range deviation."

rule: When price fails to do what your model needs (a reversal with no continuation, repeatedly), don't trade, and don't flip to trading the invalidation off a small SMT.
quote: "It failed to do what I wanted it to do. Now it made a new low, right? It's just not doing what I want it to do. If that's the case, I just don't trade it."

rule: After a failed setup turns into a new range/deviation, wait for a higher-timeframe candle closure. Near the open you can use lower timeframes.
quote: "I'm just going to wait for a higher time from candle closure at this point. When you're around the open, you can go a little bit lower."

rule: Even after a reversal with SMT on the middle asset, only a continuation sets up a trade.
quote: "So even with this reversal, what did we learn on the previous reversals? We want to see, can we form a continuation? Only at that point would something even be set up to try to trade this to the upside."

rule: If price is already at the level you wanted closed over, there is little range left to expect.
quote: "My whole idea is, do we close over this level? Well, if we're already at that level, how much more range do I expect, really?"

rule: When the daily bias is weak, demand better lower-timeframe structure: a V-shape reversal, a continuation, or expansion. Not overlapping chop.
quote: "It has to be aligned, right? Like right now, I don't have a very great daily bias. Like I don't really have much of a bias for today. That means I would demand better, lower timeframe structure."

rule: Something forming on the chart doesn't make it ideal to trade; the structure has to align too.
quote: "Just because we have stuff that is forming doesn't mean that it's still ideal to trade. You need the structure to align with it as well."

rule: On a bullish daily profile (opens low, trades higher), a reversal short from the highs only targets a return to the daily open, so it isn't worth trusting unless it is specific (a sweep of the strongest asset's high).
quote: "So even if this is bearish, right, I just kind of am expecting price to go back into the range, back towards its daily open, right?"

rule: Use YM mainly as a relative-strength and levels gauge. Trade it only in the direction of your bias.
quote: "You can, it's just when it's in the direction of your bias. I a lot of times just use YM as a relative strength and kind of a levels thing."

rule: Top-down for a 3m entry: 30m setup timeframe, bias from H4/daily.
quote: "If you want to enter on the 3-minute, probably want to use the 30-minute, and then you want to have some sort of bias from H4 daily."

rule: The daily profile can be tracked on any timeframe; it is still the daily candle.
quote: "You can watch any time frame. Doesn't matter. Still the daily candle."

rule: ADR is a rope: judge how much range and time was used to form the wick. A quick, small wick leaves range to expand; a wick that used most of the range and time leaves little for New York.
quote: "how much range and time did we use to form this wick? Right here we form this wick quick, so we can use our range to expand. Right? Versus on a day like this, how much range and time did we use to form the wick? We used all this range and all this time until the wick is formed. Then we have less rope or time to expand."

rule: Kill zones don't matter. Trade once the higher-timeframe wick has formed (the daily wick and an intraday H4/H1 wick) and you have a spot for invalidation.
quote: "I don't really care about kill zones. I care more about did the higher timeframe form its WIC, and do I have a spot for an invalidation, right?"

rule: A failure swing is a set of lined-up highs (or lows) not yet taken out. It is structure, not a candle pattern like a Strat 'failed 2'.
quote: "What a failure swing is, is simply, it's just the structure. So for you, you would call it like a pivot machine gun, right? It's just... All of those highs that are lined up."

rule: On trailing/intraday-trailing drawdown accounts, risk small per trade and use more accounts for leverage.
quote: "So it's more about risking less and using more accounts if you want to get leverage."

rule: Prefer an R:R where about 40% wins is breakeven. Higher R:R means more losses and a lower win rate.
quote: "I'd prefer something where if you're right 40% of the time, you're breakeven."

rule: If you trade reversals at all, demand more confirmation (e.g. double SMT); he mostly doesn't trade them.
quote: "I don't really trade reversals. So, would I require a double SMT? I mean, if I'm trading a reversal, I want to have more confirmation of that."

rule: Don't chase: once the daily candle has hit its low/target and is far from the daily open, don't keep shorting.
quote: "Why would you be trying to take a short trade after we already had the reversal into here?"

rule: If NQ fails to close over the level, expect downside this week toward the monthly open. A month closing like that is a reversal month, treated like a candle 2.
quote: "That's telling me that further downside for this week back towards the monthly open. And then that's kind of a reversal month, right? Even though it's not a swing, it is more of a reversal month if we close like that. So I'd treat it like a candle too"

rule: Learn the model with a 'quiz' indicator template: mark C2 closures, CISDs and EQs by hand with the indicator off, then switch on the full template to check.
quote: "And then all you do is practice marking stuff up. So you're going to say, okay, here's a candle 2 closure. Where's the CISD? Mark those up. Where is the EQ of this?"

rule: Volume isn't part of his read; range used is.
quote: "I don't personally look at the volume of the day. I just look at the range, right?"

rule: Without an A+ setup (no bias, no targets), get off and wait for the next day; anything else is reactionary.
quote: "Like, if I'm looking for an A-plus setup, I would get off and wait for tomorrow."

rule: Trade one model and get good at it instead of collecting many ICT concepts; core skill is reading swing points.
quote: "I just trade in one model. Get good at it."

rule: The TTFM indicator prints the T-spot only on the third and fourth candle, not later.
quote: "But it's going to print the T-spot here in the third and fourth candle. It's not going to print it after that."

rule: The indicator's gray boxes mark where a wick counts as 'small' (a candle has limited range, so it needs a small wick to expand).
quote: "The gray boxes are where I determine what is a small wick, all of that."

rule: Seasonality and the calendar month don't matter to him; he reads the daily charts.
quote: "I don't really care about the month, to be honest. I just use daily charts."

rule: Taking the long on NQ when the target is ES's high gives poor R:R because NQ is already up there; trade the asset with room to the target.
quote: "To me, if I'm looking for this as a target, there's not much risk to reward there, right? And it's kind of already up there."

rule: A double inside day (neither the previous day's high nor low taken) is consolidation by definition; expect price to hover around the EQ and the opening price.
quote: "We have not taken out either side of the range. So this is just by definition consolidation. So normally we're just going to be right around the EQ and the opening price."

rule: On a consolidation day the only ways to trade are range deviations or very low timeframe fractal models.
quote: "No, the only way you would trade today is like either really low timeframe fractal models or you're trading just range deviations."

rule: In a consolidating market expect a deviation (out of the range and back in), not a breakout.
quote: "But if price is consolidating, you don't expect it to break out. You expect it to deviate, make a deviation, go outside the range, and then come back in."

rule: On range days take profit move by move; holding for a big target gives it all back.
quote: "You're not really holding, because if you get long here off the open, like some people did, and then they never took profit, they Didn't make any money."

rule: Without a bias, a target and an invalidation there is no trade; on chop days with no expectation of expansion he stays away.
quote: "It's a pretty chopped day. So I don't have the expectations for expansion. That's usually when I stay away."
