rule: Correlated indices cannot all go different ways: when NQ/ES/YM diverge, ask which one is lying; either the weak one reverses and the strong continues, or the strong reverses and the weak continues.
quote: "So it either means YM needs to reverse, and then NQ continues higher, ES goes higher, or NQ needs to reverse, And then YM continues lower"

rule: When price is one point from your TP and reversing, exit; holding risks the whole move for one point.
quote: "Once you get up to here, and you're this close to your TP, now you're risking one point for all of that."

rule: On range days expect price to oscillate back and forth inside the range.
quote: "To me, on days like this, I'm just expecting price to oscillate, just go back and forth in the range"

rule: In a range, look for the weakest asset to run into its failure swings.
quote: "I'm just looking for the weakest asset to go into these failure swings."

rule: The PM session usually has little volatility because most of the intraday range is already made; he does not trade it.
quote: "I find the volatility is gone. Most of the time, the intraday movement has been fulfilled, let's say. Most of the range has been there."

rule: If the New York open confuses you, don't trade before it; let it open.
quote: "If you are confused with the New York Open, then don't trade prior to the New York Open. Let it open."

rule: Look at higher timeframes before lower timeframes so LTF price does not override your bias.
quote: "Stop going down to the lower timeframes before you look at the higher timeframes first."

rule: In a short from a protected swing, move to break even (or trail) once price runs into the lows, so a reversal after sweeping a low doesn't take the trade back.
quote: "you wouldn't want to let it reverse on you after sweeping out of a low. So for instance, if you were short somewhere in here, you know, like, let's say, off this protected swing, 2-hour, or if you're reaching for that, you should go break even once it runs down into these lows, or at least trail."

rule: He has no fixed daily timeframes (used the 1H today); for profiling he uses 1H, 4H, 30m or 15m, and the read is the same whichever you use.
quote: "It doesn't matter if you use a 15-minute timeframe and watch all the price form like this for a bearish day, or if you see a 1-hour chart that's more like this, or if you have a 4-hour candles that are like that"

rule: He does not trade through NFP, CPI or FOMC; for other news-driven volatility (tweets) the stop loss is the protection.
quote: "There's always volatility in the markets, that's why you use a stop loss. I do not trade through NFP, CPI, or FOMC."

rule: No pattern trading: every trade needs discretion and higher timeframe analysis.
quote: "No, you have to have discretion. You have to have hard time frame analysis. Otherwise, people would just trade bots."

rule: Blowing accounts is a management problem (tilt and sizing), not a strategy problem; overcome it by simply not revenge trading or sizing up after a loss.
quote: "If you blew five accounts today, that's not a strategy issue. That is a management issue and going on tilts and sizing."

rule: There is always a fractal model on some timeframe pair; a 15-second model means a 5-minute swing point executed on the 15-second chart.
quote: "If you want to trade the 15-second model, that would be a 5-minute swing point, 15 seconds."

rule: The daily chart is the start of all bias, even when trading off the 30-minute.
quote: "The daily chart is the start of all of my bias. So just because I'm using a 30-minute chart doesn't mean I'm only going to go up to the 4-hour. No, I always personally start at the daily chart."

rule: A new higher-timeframe candle opening after a target is hit can start a new phase/direction before any continuation.
quote: "There's a gap right here in price, but we have a new higher time from candle now, so we can get some sort of new direction, new phase of price before if we get a continuation into the highs."

rule: Long accumulation leads to a big expansion: a big manipulation, then a big distribution (AMD).
quote: "whenever you have moves like this that accumulate for long periods of time, you get big expansion out of it, a big manipulation, then you'll get a big distribution."

rule: Price still at the weekly open midweek means there has been no displacement.
quote: "So it's Wednesday and three days ago we opened up for the week and we are still currently almost at that price. So that tells you that we haven't had much displacement."

rule: Keep charts clean: let the indicator draw structure and mark only the line you expect price to go to.
quote: "I just let my indicator chart stuff up for me, and I don't really have to mark up anything besides a line that I'm looking for price to go to."

rule: Gold tends to pull back to daily gaps and move away from them; wait for hourly displacement out of the daily gap before targeting the high above.
quote: "if we can get a nice push up from here, probably tomorrow or maybe tonight in Asia, we could look to target this high up here"

rule: On a consolidation day, once price hits a target expect it to come back into the range.
quote: "Well, it's a consolidation day, so normally we hit a target, come back into the range."

rule: He keeps the indicator on Neutral bias so it prints both bullish and bearish setups and he decides; auto-bias reads the higher timeframes and filters to one side.
quote: "But I leave it in neutral personally because I want to see all the swings and make my own decisions."

rule: Once the 5-minute swing forms, a 15-second close beyond the level is the continuation entry (5m-15s model).
quote: "Technically, this has formed a model. If it closes below here, it's a continuation."

rule: He dislikes perfectly equal highs at the swing of a short (liquidity sitting there).
quote: "The only thing that sketches me out is the fact that that just makes, I hate perfectly equal highs like that."

rule: For a short, price must not close back over the previous candle's level; that close is a bullish CISD.
quote: "So if we're looking for Nick to be bearish, he doesn't want to see price close over this level. That's what creates a bullish change in the state of delivery off of this previous candle slow."

rule: Wait for the higher-timeframe (5m) candle to close in your direction before the lower-timeframe model is valid.
quote: "Wait for a five-minute closure. Bruh. You're silly for this. You got to wait until the five minutes is actually bullish."

rule: After an expanded leg that is about to hit the low, don't chase continuation entries; let it take the low, watch the reaction, and trade the next 5m candle's wick into the 5m gap.
quote: "It's likely to hit this low. Just let it hit the low, then watch the reaction, try to trade the wick of the next five-minute candle into the five-minute gap, you know?"

rule: A sweep of a high back through the previous range, with three drives and failure swings below, is the clean reversal for a range day.
quote: "That's like a three drives pattern, and then you see all the failure swings below. Like, that's just... That's too easy."

rule: A higher-timeframe gap (15m imbalance) is a target/front-run level: set the alert there and front-run stops/targets ahead of it.
quote: "I still have my alert set at 263 level, which is that 15-minute imbalance, okay? Yeah, it's always good to front run with your stop on the hard time from imbalance. Yeah, 100%."

rule: Reversal trades have a much lower win rate than continuations, so he doesn't normally trade them (speaker possibly Nick).
quote: "I don't normally trade reversals like this because your win rate's going to be like 20, 30, 40% less than it normally is."

rule: A higher-timeframe reversal candle usually does not expand until the next higher-timeframe candle opens.
quote: "We have 20 seconds until I think we can start expanding lower. Because we have a 5-minute reversal candle. Usually that's going to wait normally to expand until the open of a new..."

rule: A reversal must expand quickly; the longer price hangs at the entry, the more likely the stop gets hit.
quote: "You want to see this continue pretty quick. Otherwise, the longer it stays here, the more likely you are to get stopped out in this case for NQ."

rule: After a range breakout, a close back inside the range is AMD and signals the other direction; a valid breakout retests or continues.
quote: "if we break out of this range, you don't want to see us close back in the range. You want to see us retest or get a continuation. If we close back in this range, AMD accumulation, manipulation, going higher."

rule: Don't overhaul your approach after a loss; adjust slightly and keep going (Call of Duty analogy).
quote: "you don't go back to the main menu, quit, get a whole new guy, get a whole new gun, all this, add a new attachment."

rule: Fixed-R risk with 2R targets lets a 0-for-2 start come back to break even after one win.
quote: "Yeah, see, this is why risk management is so important. I was 0 for 2, I hit this back, and now we're break even"

rule: Scale out at 2R (60% off) and hold runners to 3R.
quote: "I'm holding runners. I took up 60% of my position. I'm going to hold another two runners."

rule: In consolidating markets, go with where liquidity was taken and trade the opposite way (highs taken with SMT, so expect a protected high and lower prices).
quote: "The main reason for that is in these consolidating markets, the markets we've had for the past month, you have to kind of go with where was liquidity taken and then trade the opposite way."

rule: A bearish read needs the stronger asset's high taken with SMT and a close through its series of up-close candles (CISD); on a bearish day the 7 a.m. high should not be taken out.
quote: "So my bias for today is that because ES took out this high, we have SMT right there, right on this high, and then we can take a look at the stronger asset. It has closed through the series of up close candles."

rule: When correlated indices diverge, wait for the weakest asset to form a reversal (a 5m closure through); that times the strongest asset's trend leg because all of them then align.
quote: "You want to wait for the weakest one to form a reversal, because if the weakest one forms a reversal, that's usually when this one starts to trend, right? Because that's when they all align in one direction."

rule: On the NY open, confirm a weakest-asset reversal with a 5-minute closure over the level before expecting the stronger assets to continue.
quote: "We want to see a five-minute closure over. If the weakest asset is reversing, then usually that means the stronger assets can also continue."

rule: When the indices diverge, one of them is lying. When relative strength keeps switching, focus on the middle asset (ES) and see whether it respects the area and forms a continuation.
quote: "But what are we going to usually do when that's kind of bouncing around? We're going to focus on ES here. I'm just going to see if ES can respect this area and form any sort of continuation."

rule: If price does not respect a gap (FVG) it was expected to reject from, that usually means continuation through it.
quote: "Yes, not respecting that gap. Usually that means we're going to get a continuation higher."

rule: Without a strong bias, do nothing: sit on your hands. A choppy, divergent open can be a 'wait for 10 a.m.' day.
quote: "I don't have the strongest bias, so there's nothing for me to really do but sit on my hands, personally."

rule: Equal highs that sit below a previous high are failure swings: expect them to be run toward the previous high, and do not put your stop just above them.
quote: "Now, these are still failure swings to this previous high, right? So basically where Nick has a stop loss."

rule: An aggressive V-shape off a low becomes a higher-timeframe (4H) wick and is bullish toward the previous highs.
quote: "I mean, obviously, to me, this is an aggressive V-shape. If you go to a higher timeframe, it's going to be a higher timeframe wick, right? If you get up high enough, right? 4-hour wick. But to me, this is bullish to reach to these previous highs, right?"

rule: Consolidation is mechanically when price fails to take out a previous range (an inside day). Typically avoid it; if you must trade, ask whether PDH or PDL is the more likely draw and make that your bias.
quote: "How do you mechanically define a consolidation? Price fails to take out a previous range."

rule: A close back over the daily open (with a W bottom) invalidates a bearish intraday idea and flips the lean bullish toward PDH.
quote: "I was bearish initially. That's gotten invalid for me is if we can get a closure over a daily open and here we kind of have this little Double V shape here. W bottom, whatever you want to call it."

rule: After a strong expansion that ends with a fresh HTF candle 2 closure (e.g. the 10:00 4H), expect a new phase of price (retracement or consolidation) before any continuation to the next draw.
quote: "This is when you can get some sort of new phase of price because we have expanded pretty far."

rule: There is no way to frame shorts when price fails to sweep an important level (e.g. the previous 4H high). The trend (higher highs/higher lows) stays bullish until price reaches above that high or shows bearish price action.
quote: "So like I said yesterday, there's no way for me to frame shorts when we fail to sweep out an important level, right? So to me, this remains a bullish trend."

rule: The daily EQ should be respected when the candle has a small wick and is going to expand. If the EQ is not respected and the candle shows a large wick, don't expect much range that day.
quote: "I use the EQ, right? So if we have the EQ here. That's generally where we want to see be respected if we have a small wick where we're going to expand. What do we notice? That is not respected. It has a large wick."

rule: He usually does not fade the daily candle.
quote: "Usually, I don't like to fade the daily candle, but now it has been faded. That is a large wick, which doesn't really support too much expansion, right? So I'm not expecting a lot of range today."

rule: A small SMT (one index sweeping a 4H high) is not a reversal signal by itself; you need a CISD with it. The only reversal framing would be a 15m swing with a 1m CISD on the weaker asset. He passes because he is a continuation trader.
quote: "So like I said, yes, there is technically SMT here, but is there any SMT or any CISD to go with that, right?"

rule: He trades continuations, not reversals, because continuations have a higher win rate. He does not try to catch highs or lows.
quote: "Guys, like I said, I'm not a reversal trader. I don't try to catch these types of reversals. I'm the continuation trader."

rule: Watch the phases of price at a level. If price does not form a reversal off the lows (a failure to manipulate), look for continuation through them.
quote: "We want to see the phases of price around these levels. If we don't form a reversal off these lows, then we can look for a continuation. That's a failure to manipulate."

rule: When the weakest index continues through a low (fails to manipulate it), the other indices usually follow to their equivalent lows.
quote: "You can see YM failing to manipulate this previous low, usually. Then the other assets follow to that, right?"

rule: Low-timeframe continuation sequence: the retrace is stopped by a gap, then a candle 2 closure forms a new protected swing, and the trade is the continuation.
quote: "What do we see? We try to go back higher. This gap stops price. We have a candle to closure. We form a new protected swing continuation, right?"

rule: A new protected swing is set after SMT takes out the previous one.
quote: "So, new protected swing after we form SMT, taking out the previous one."

rule: Don't trust a reversal that forms off a failure swing. The relevant swing (e.g. previous day lows) must be taken first, and a low with good distance beyond it is the target.
quote: "So for me, I don't personally trust the reversal here because it's making a failure swing, right? Go watch my relevant swings video."

rule: You cannot frame trades away from an untaken liquidity target (no gold longs before the previous low is run); the POI is that low into the daily gap.
quote: "For me, I can't frame gold higher. Until we run out this low. So this will be my point of interest on gold. Just that previous low into this gap, the daily gap."

rule: Once the HTF target is hit, drop the old bias. The new direction is technically a reversal, so he does not trade it.
quote: "Like I said with gold, gold hit that target, right? So now I'm not bearish anymore. It's bullish, but I'm not going to trade this away because that's a reversal. I don't try to catch the highs or lows."

rule: Always start on the daily chart and keep your targets there.
quote: "Anyways, now we have hit the daily level, and that's why I always start on the daily chart and have my targets there and understanding."

rule: If a big first hour is almost fully retraced in the next hour (e.g. the 9 a.m. move retraced at 10 a.m.), expect chop. In a range, the market just takes highs and lows and fades them.
quote: "The hourly chart from 9 a.m. was pretty big, and then we almost retraced that whole move we did, in fact, on the 10 a.m., so it would make sense for the—as much as I don't want it to happen, it would make sense for us to chop around a little bit."

rule: With no sweep of a higher-timeframe level, use the intraday profile or wait for the next day.
quote: "How do you approach days when there is no sweep on the higher timeframe level? You have to use the intraday profile or you just wait for the next day."

rule: Without a candle 2 closure, derive bias from a candle 3 closure, the OHLC daily profile, the intra-candle profile or the phases of price.
quote: "If we don't get a candle 2 closure, how do we get bias? Candle 3 closure, you can use... Open high-low close, the daily profile or intra-candle profile. You can use the phases of price, all of that."

rule: Use SMT only as confluence after you have a valid model or reason to look in a direction; never hunt highs and lows to support an idea.
quote: "You first need to have an actual valid model or a reason to be looking in a direction. Then look for SMT as a confluence to that. Stop just randomly looking for highs and lows to try to support your idea. That's where everyone goes wrong."

rule: A CISD is not required on both correlated assets to take a trade.
quote: "Is it necessary to see CISD in both assets while taking a trade? No, you don't need to."

rule: A relative-strength 'switch' is not required for a setup.
quote: "No, you don't need a strength switch for a setup."

rule: Don't pattern-trade the indicator: a pattern has to align with something (the higher-timeframe bias).
quote: "No. You have to align with something. If you're just gonna, like, take pattern trades, it's not gonna work."

rule: He uses the daily open, not the midnight (00:00) open.
quote: "No, I don't use midnight open personally. I just use the daily open."

rule: Position size: trading more than one or two minis on a 50K funded account is not how profitable traders operate.
quote: "People that trade more than a mini or two minis on a 50K funded account, like, you're just not profitable."

rule: A doji monthly candle (oil) suggests the month closes around or near its opening price.
quote: "Kind of a doji, so I'm just looking for it to close around or near its opening price."

rule: Into month end, don't fade a trend. A continuation shows as opening low first, forming a wick, then trading through the level; a reversal comes off the previous month's high.
quote: "Bitcoin into the month end, right, to me, don't try to fade this trend, let it close and then see if we can, what, we want to see if we're going to get a continuation, right, we open low first, form some sort of wick, and then trade through this level, be able to manipulate it. If we're going to reverse, what do we do? We reverse off the previous month's high."

rule: TTFM indicator: turn on 'show early C2'; otherwise the C2/CISD prints only at the close of the higher-timeframe candle. All other settings are default.
quote: "If you don't have early CISD turned on in the settings, right here, show early C2. Then it's not going to print this until the close of the higher timeframe candle."

rule: A range high taken with significant distance to the previous highs is where a reaction can come. (Speaker attribution uncertain, TTrades or Nick.)
quote: "Price takes out this range high, right? Why is this relevant? It is relevant because we have a distance that is significant to these previous highs. So this is where we can get some sort of reaction, right?"

rule: A daily candle-2 closure is not enough for a reversal; price must also close over the series of candles that made the swept low (a timely CISD, ideally V-shaped).
quote: "If you've watched my videos, that's not the only requirement. What is the other requirement? We need to see The low, find the series of candles that made that low. Did price close over that low?"

rule: If the change in state of delivery takes too long to form, treat the area as a consolidation range; when it finally closes over, it is a sweep of the range high to go to the other side (consolidation, expansion, opposite).
quote: "We're spending so long trying to form this change in the state of delivery that it's not a change in the state of delivery anymore for me. It is now a consolidation range."

rule: In a consolidation the low you'd 'protect' becomes the target once the high is run late; don't trust it.
quote: "If it takes so long to form this continuation, by the time it closes over, I'm not trusting that low. That low is now the target for this move lower."

rule: It is hard to frame a reversal away from equal lows (on a correlated index); equal lows are a draw.
quote: "ES basically at these lows, right? So for me, it's really hard to frame away from equal lows"

rule: SMT is a confirmation to a setup, not a setup; remove it and the setup should still stand.
quote: "SMT is a confirmation to a setup. So if you have really garbage structure and a really garbage setup, slapping SMT on the thing is not going to help it."

rule: For an intraday reversal, prefer SMT off the external range high, not off an internal equal high.
quote: "I guess we have YM SMT now, but I want SMT off the external range high."

rule: When price makes a deep opposing run before the setup, expansion is less likely and you want an additional SMT before trusting it.
quote: "Usually when price has a deep opposing run like this, what does it mean? It means that it's less likely to expand, but also you want to see another SMT"

rule: Equal highs right at the intraday swing you would short from are a red flag; liquidity remains above.
quote: "The fact that we just have an equal high right here. That's not ideal."

rule: If the open sweeps a high and that is to become the higher-timeframe wick, it must form a continuation; no continuation means no trade.
quote: "So if that's going to remain, AKA forms the higher timeframe wick, what does it need to do? It needs to form a continuation."

rule: Trade the expansion, not after it: short before the expansion, and stop trading once price has hit your target and moved.
quote: "I trade expansions. I don't trade after the expansions. That's how you get caught in consolidations."

rule: Don't drop to lower timeframes when price is choppy after the move; that is how you force losses.
quote: "when things are choppy, I don't go to the lower timeframe because, in my opinion, that's how you force losses"

rule: Don't short below lows.
quote: "I'm not a huge fan of trying to trade short below lows. That's not something I do."

rule: On a C2 reversal day, enter early in the candle, near the open and before the ADR is made; don't enter after price has gone through EQ and run the lows.
quote: "Where do we want to enter early into candle generally before ADR created near the open? Those are the ideal things for a reversal day."

rule: Good structure alone isn't a reason to trade; you need higher-timeframe framework and to know where you are in the daily range.
quote: "You can't just have only structure. You need a higher timeframe framework in reasoning, right?"

rule: If the bias day has already hit its target pre-open, expect little off the open.
quote: "we have a bearish day and we just hit a target, so. Probably not too much off the open because it could go either way."

rule: Take a partial when the ADR is reached and a correlated index has already hit your target (divergence).
quote: "we're already at our daily range. That's the whole reason I took a partial right here. And because if you look, ES already took out this low."

rule: Place the swing stop above the EQ when the protected high gives under 2R; on a reversal day price should not trade above EQ (a tap is allowed).
quote: "if we're going to have a reversal, On this day, I don't want to see it go above the EQ anyways, right? So I just put it above the EQ."

rule: For a C2-C3 continuation, price should not come back above 50% of the move; once your entry is beyond that, you can be at break-even.
quote: "if we get a good closure today, I don't want to see price come above 50% of this, right? Because you've got to think, if we're going to have a candle 2, candle 3 continuation"

rule: Don't predict tomorrow's bias before today's daily candle closes.
quote: "So don't try to predict things until you have the daily closure."

rule: Simplest way to trade the model: find candle 2 or candle 3 closures and trade the continuation day, or the invalidation of a weak continuation day.
quote: "look for candle 2 or candle 3 closures and trade the continuation day or the invalidation of the continuation day."

rule: If a correlated index takes the low and forms a protected swing instead of reversing (failure to manipulate), expect the other indices to continue lower too.
quote: "Because ES formed a protected swing after taking out this low. So this is a failure to form a reversal, failure to manipulate, and we're continuing lower, which usually means what? The other assets are gonna continue lower as well."

rule: A higher-timeframe C2 (e.g. weekly) needs an intra-candle CISD on the lower timeframe before it is tradable; a C2 alone doesn't mean it will rip.
quote: "There's no inter candle change in the state of delivery. There's nothing to do to trade that higher."

rule: A bullish CISD by itself doesn't mean a low has formed; it needs confirmation.
quote: "even if you have the bullish CISD here, it doesn't mean it's going to form a low. You have to confirm it."

rule: A swing that fails to respect its level (took the range-high target, then failed) flips the read to the other side.
quote: "So to me, yes, it can be bullish, but it failed to respect it. So then what? It's bearish."

rule: A low hit with no separation from the prior swing is not a relevant target/swing to frame from.
quote: "Is that relevant? No, because there's no separation to this one."

rule: Using a low as a target while short is different from framing a long off a failure swing; only the first makes sense.
quote: "There's a big difference between being short in something and using this as a target, right, versus using this to try to frame to the upside with a failure swing."

rule: Intraday rule list: have a bias, let the wick form (on the closure through), align/enter with the lower-timeframe fractal model.
quote: "My rules are very simple. Have a bias. Let the wick form align with lower timeframe fractal model. That's all I do, intraday-wise, right?"

rule: The fractal model needs a higher-timeframe bias first; 4H-15m is one of the best pairings.
quote: "I think the 4-hour and 15-minute fractal model is one of the best timeframes for the fractal model, but you need to have a higher timeframe bias."

rule: His stack: daily bias, H1 or H4 setup, M15/M5/M3 entries; daily + H1 for new swing traders; no weekly, no 1m.
quote: "I use daily and under that I use H1 or H4. And then if I'm taking a lower time frame entry, it'll be M15, M5, M3 generally."

rule: Use three higher-timeframe candles as the lookback for draw on liquidity.
quote: "I use three higher time from candles, and that gives you your best lookback in terms of drawn liquidity."

rule: Don't trade through or hold intraday into FOMC, CPI or NFP; other news (PMI) is ignored.
quote: "FOMC, NFP, CPI, those are volatile news events that I tend to not trade through or hold something intraday."

rule: Use ADR (range only, not gaps) to judge how much of the day's range is done.
quote: "if price gaps up, I'm caring more about the actual range of the candle, not the gap, so I would still use the ADR."

rule: Once in a trade, accept the stop and don't manage it based on adverse moves that don't hit it.
quote: "I've already accepted the fact that if price goes up here, I lose money. And if it goes this way, I made money. That's it. There's nothing to do. That's what the stop loss is for."

rule: Live, wait for candle closures and don't micromanage trades, as in backtesting.
quote: "stop messing with your trades, wait for your closures."

rule: For options swings, buy about four times the expected time to the move, slightly OTM/near the money, while premiums are cheap; no short-dated options for swings.
quote: "I'm giving myself four times the amount of time I think it'll take."

rule: Risk more on swing trades than on intraday setups.
quote: "when I'm taking swing trades, I risk more than if I'm trading intraday setup here."

rule: Keep the TTFM indicator bias on neutral to see both sides (setting it to one side is optional).
quote: "I personally just like to have it on neutral because I like to see both sides of things."

rule: Inside a consolidation you can trade to the other side of the range, but a structurally ideal C2 closure inside it has no backing.
quote: "Even on the 4-hour, we are running out a consolidation high. It's a little bit different when it's in this consolidation. You can trade to the other side of the range."

rule: Routine on a done day: watch the open, manage positions, set alerts, leave.
quote: "Normally it's like I watch the open, manage anything if I need, and then I set alerts and I go do other things."

rule: After multiple days of expansion into a low that is a HTF target, do not short at that low; look for a retracement or reversal back into the range.
quote: "So we have expansion into a low that is a target. We don't want to short below this low, right? We want to be looking for a retracement or a reversal."

rule: He prefers shorting up in the range, not at the low after the target has been taken.
quote: "I'm a fan of shorting up in the range not at the low after we take out the target"

rule: On a reversal day the target is reduced: depending on wick size, back toward the daily open / previous EQ; have lower expectations.
quote: "Depending on the wick size, your target's back towards the daily open to the previous EQ."

rule: A larger wick on the reversal day means less expansion; compare assets (NQ larger wick vs YM smaller wick) to see which gets more.
quote: "it's a reversal day with a larger wick on NQ, smaller wick on YM. You can see which one gets more expansion."

rule: His favorite reversal days open right near the previous day low, make a small wick, and then expand.
quote: "usually my favorite reversal days are closer to this, but open right near the previous day low, small wick, and then it just expands, right?"

rule: Bullish framing off the open: the weakest asset should sweep the level / trade into the gap while stronger assets hold, creating SMT; without that sweep it is hard to frame longs.
quote: "normally you want the weakest asset. In this case, that is NQ. To trade into this gap or essentially below this low."

rule: If the weakest asset reverses at the level, expect continuation from the stronger assets.
quote: "If the weakest asset forms a reversal, And what do we expect out of the other assets? A continuation."

rule: SMT is helpful but not required; no SMT off the previous day low is fine.
quote: "There's no SMT off the previous day low. That's fine. I don't require it."

rule: When the current 4H candle has already made its range, wait for the next 4H candle (10:00) before looking for entries.
quote: "The 4-hour candle's already kind of made a good range, so that's why I'm saying it's better to wait till 10 a.m."

rule: Do not enter at the end of a higher-timeframe candle.
quote: "I'm not entering at the end of this higher time frame candle, so that's not me."

rule: A reversal idea needs a continuation to confirm it.
quote: "This is a reversal. I would need some sort of continuation to tell me that."

rule: For a bullish hourly from a bearish prior hour, the next hour must sweep then continue higher (form a reversal candle); if the wick runs too far toward the lows the idea is no longer bullish.
quote: "And if it goes too low, makes too large of a wick, then we're getting towards these lows and it's not bullish anymore."

rule: Consecutive monthly inside bars = consolidation; favor reversion back into the range over breakouts.
quote: "We're just inside bar, inside bar, so it's more consolidation, so I favor a reversion back into the range over breakouts."

rule: Daily profile open-low-first into a target plus an hourly CISD -> assume the 7am low holds; bias bullish.
quote: "the daily profile open low first we have an hourly CISD so I'm going under the indication that 7am low can hold"

rule: Ideal C2: the prior candle closes weak below the level, then the next candle opens and sweeps into it, giving a 15m C2 reversal with a CISD inside.
quote: "I prefer if this actually closes below here, get like a week close, and then the next candle opens, sweeps into it. That would be ideal"

rule: A bearish-bodied candle 2 is not ideal but he still watches it if it marks out the swing.
quote: "This isn't the most ideal candle 2 because it's still a bearish candle, but we'll see if it marks it out."

rule: Expected swing-point area for the C3 wick: 0.5 of the C2 wick (indicator marks it) with a CISD.
quote: "This is using 0.5 of the wick. You can see my indicator marks out 0.5 of this wick. And we have a change in the state of delivery."

rule: A bullish candle should open, make its low first, then trade higher; trade the body after the wick forms ('let the wick form').
quote: "All right, so we let this wick form, and then we look to trade the body higher."

rule: Entering the sweep is a reversal trade; he prefers continuation entries after the closure.
quote: "Some people like to enter that, you know, essentially, that sweep. You know, you can do that as a reversal trade. I prefer more of a continuation"

rule: A swing low becomes protected only after a close over the series of down-closed candles that made it; you may anticipate it on a strong reaction.
quote: "It doesn't automatically make it a protected swing until you get the closure over the series of down closed candles that made that low, right?"

rule: Expansion candles should close near their highs.
quote: "Because expansion candles, we want to see it close near the highs, create a protected swing on the 15-minute, right?"

rule: An early entry inside the 15m candle requires that candle to close over the level to confirm the low; if it doesn't, scratch the trade.
quote: "So I don't need to wait for that, I just want to see that 15-minute candle close over it."

rule: Mechanical first target = the swing high that made the swing low you are trading away from.
quote: "Because this is the swing low we're trading away from. That's the swing high that made it. So this is short-term target for this 15-minute expansion."

rule: Break-even: fine when a return to your entry would mean the expansion has failed (entry below the EQ / deep in the reversal); not when your entry sits at a level price can validly retest.
quote: "Any sort of entry in here or below this EQ can be break-even because we don't want to see price trade into there."

rule: After the first target, a bearish CISD off the highs warns the continuation idea may be wrong; failure to form a bearish CISD is a trend-continuation sign.
quote: "Grace failing to form a bearish change in the state of delivery, which is usually a good kind of a trend continuation"

rule: A very shallow sweep that leaves equal lows is less ideal; he wants a cleaner sweep.
quote: "very shallow sweep. Normally you want a little more of a sweep there, I don't really like that."

rule: 4H-15m is his favorite pairing; on a reversal day with little expected expansion he refines to 15m-1m for R:R, and around the NY open a 3m setup may not form in time.
quote: "The 4-hour and 15 is my favorite, right? Because I find that's the easiest."

rule: For multi-day swings off a daily reversal, enter on the hourly chart.
quote: "when I'm looking to trade or swing multiple days, I'm just taking an entry on the hourly chart."

rule: Bias comes from the daily candle closure; look for continuations in that direction; ideally daily and 4H agree.
quote: "I usually look at the daily candle closure and we'll look for continuations in that direction."

rule: Have one idea, supported by the daily candle and daily profile, and trade it only through the fractal model; if it fails, accept being wrong.
quote: "This is the only way I can frame something because my logic is based off the daily candle, the daily profile, and then my fractal model."

rule: A V-shape reversal out of the objectives after the open signals bullish.
quote: "We open, we go into these objectives, and we have a nice V-shape reversal here. That just tells me it's bullish."

rule: Once his targets are hit (the morning expansion), he is done for the day.
quote: "For me, that's the morning expansion. That's the move. Nothing else left to do."

rule: A big HTF order block at a high makes that high harder to reach; prefer the nearer failure swings as target.
quote: "We have pretty easy failure swings here, so it's like I would just say that's our target on ES."

rule: When correlated assets diverge, use one to frame the other.
quote: "I actually prefer when the assets trade like this because I can Use one asset to frame the other"

rule: Waiting for the HTF candle open removes stress; nothing to do until 10 a.m.
quote: "Because you have to wait till the higher timeframe candle's open. There's nothing to do"

rule: Execute your own trades; copying a streamer won't make you grow.
quote: "You're also never going to grow as a trader if you go sit in a stream and copy someone."

rule: If there is no frame after the 9:30 open on an instrument (gold here), don't trade it.
quote: "Yeah, there's no way I would have traded gold after 9.30, so nothing there for me."

rule: Demand the sweep of the weakest asset; otherwise you are trading away from failure swings.
quote: "that's like what I would demand out of a move. Otherwise you're trading away from failure swings."

rule: On a large-wick (larger opposing run) day do not expect expansion; targets come in a fixed order: daily open, then intraday highs/lows, then previous day high/low; once those are hit the idea is done.
quote: "You have targets on a large wick day, it's always going to be this, daily open, intraday lows, previous day high or previous day low. It's always in that order."

rule: A consolidation (range high taken, equal lows below) points to the range lows next; the move needs volatility, so expect it at 9:30, often after a retest of the level.
quote: "My point here is we've taken out the range high, and then we have equal lows, right? So I want to see it go to the range lows. So when would that occur? You need volatility, so 930."

rule: Use the index closest to a relevant higher-timeframe level as the tell: a shallow wick and reversal there means the others likely reverse (maybe with SMT); trading straight through with no reaction means the others follow lower.
quote: "Now, how YM reacts at this previous low It tells us what the other assets are going to do."

rule: After a relevant level is hit with a large overnight (London) expansion, the only New York framing is back into the range; he avoids trading reversal days whose large wick fights the daily range.
quote: "once we hit a relevant level and we have a large overnight expansion move, the only way to frame something in the New York session for me is back into the range, right?"

rule: Location: do not short below the daily lows / previous day low after the expansion is already done.
quote: "but i'm not trying to short down here below the lows does that make sense it's like a location thing"

rule: A small-wick reversal on the daily supports expansion; with enough daily range left, target the previous day high.
quote: "Gold, I'm still bullish, right, to previous day high. And the reason for that is we have a small wick reversal. It supports expansion."

rule: A swing that forms with SMT against a correlated asset can be read as a candle 2 (candle 2 with SMT) and traded away from the low of the day.
quote: "Why could I consider this a candle 2? Because if you look at correlated assets, it's a candle 2."

rule: If London consolidates after the expansion, do not trade New York out of the consolidation in the bias direction; wait for a sweep of the consolidation's opposite extreme, then a 15m/3m reaction and CISD, and enter before the highs are taken.
quote: "So if you want to trade New York, you're not trying to trade higher from this consolidation. You want to sweep up the low to go to the 15-minute chart."

rule: If you missed the entry and price is already expanding, wait for a new swing to form before looking for the next entry.
quote: "Except if you don't have an entry prior to this, this is expansion, I would want to see a new swing, right?"

rule: When the daily profile and the lower-timeframe structure conflict, it is a not-mess-with-it day: wait for the 10:00 candle to form.
quote: "This is a bearish daily profile. This is bullish structure. So you can really fade it either way here. A lot of times this is when it's better to wait for 10 a.m., you know?"

rule: If at the New York open you don't have a clear idea, wait for 10:00.
quote: "this is what I mean is when New York Open, you don't really have an idea, just wait for 10am."

rule: Leading/lagging means strongest/weakest by looking at the candles. If bullish, frame longs on the strongest (leading) asset and wait for the weakest (lagging) asset to sweep its low and reverse; if bearish, the strongest asset reversing frames shorts and the roles flip.
quote: "So if you were bullish, what one is leading? This one's leading. NQ, because it's the strongest. YM is the lagging."

rule: Relative strength decides which index to trade: with the same entry time, the strongest asset trends while a middle/weak asset goes nowhere.
quote: "We took one at 9.30 here. We've trended. That's why like relative strength is so important."

rule: If the weakest asset never reverses and keeps trending, expect the strongest asset's continuation to fail and chop; read the three indices as one bunch.
quote: "If it doesn't, it just continues to trend lower. What does that mean? Oh, it means that this might just fail and chop around, right? So I use all the assets together."

rule: If a lagging asset has not yet run its low, you cannot frame the low higher on the other assets; expect short-term movement toward that low first.
quote: "We failed to run out that low, so there's no way to frame that low higher on ES. You need YM to run out here."

rule: Use only the mini contracts (NQ/ES/YM) for SMT, not the micros; silver can be used for gold.
quote: "I'm literally just gonna use the minis for everything."

rule: Improve your higher-timeframe read by obsessing over the daily chart and how the daily candle forms; know where you want the daily to go and why.
quote: "Obsess about the daily chart. Obsess about how the daily candle forms. That's it."

rule: Identify the protected low where price must form a low to continue in the bias direction; let the daily wick form there, then trade away from it.
quote: "Is this a protected low? This is where we have to form a low if we're going to continue higher at all."

rule: Do not fade the daily profile; if you do (e.g. trading a retracement against a bearish open-high daily), lower your expectations to the daily open and maybe the intraday highs, not a trend day.
quote: "That's why you don't want to fade the daily profile. If you fade it, you have to have lower expectations."

rule: The trades that line up best have a daily candle supporting them; that's how trend days happen, and aligning with the higher timeframe gives faster moves.
quote: "All I'm saying is when I have trades that line up super well, you're going to have a daily candle that's basically supporting it, which is nice and green. That's how you get those trend days."

rule: A good reversal day profile: London makes failure swings into the level, then New York speeds to the objective; a profile that goes too high first is not an ideal reversal.
quote: "When I have a very good reversal, we don't really go higher first like this so much. It's like maybe this and you have a bunch of failure swings and then New York looks like that."

rule: For a wick to form on the strong asset, you want the weak asset to make an expansion candle with a small wick reversing off its previous low (a re-sweep).
quote: "we still want to see this have an expansion candle. Which would mean a small wick reversing off this previous low."

rule: A lower-timeframe CISD can be a close back over the higher-timeframe candle's opening price, flipping that candle's colour (here a 3m close over the 4H open).
quote: "You'd want to see the three-minute form in SMT. Or not an SMT, my bad, CISD. So close over that level, which is just the opening price of the four-hour candle."

rule: After a failed continuation and a new low, don't trust a close over the old level; require a new continuation.
quote: "Like, there's no way, even if we went closed over here, I would trust that I would need a new continuation."

rule: The model is mechanical: a close over a level with the conditions met is the entry; it rests on price only reversing from a swing point, so a swing point appears whichever way you are wrong.
quote: "That's because my model's built off the fact that price only reverses when it has a swing point."

rule: His trade window is roughly the first two hours of New York (through ~11:00); he does not trade London.
quote: "You have a trade window like the first two hours of New York."

rule: If a 4H candle has already expanded, wait for the next 4H candle (10:00) to form its wick before entering.
quote: "But I think it's pretty much expanded, so you need to wait to 10 a.m. because this 4-hour candle's already kind of gone."

rule: A 10:00 low that respects the EQ of the range supports continuation toward the previous day high.
quote: "Forming some sort of new low, 10 a.m., respecting the EQ. That's the red line's the EQ. I eyeballed it so I was off a little."

rule: Fundamentals and news don't change intraday entries; just don't trade during the Fed announcement and don't hold intraday positions through CPI/NFP (only daily-chart positions).
quote: "Obviously, don't trade right during the Fed announcement of it."

rule: Liquidity is just swing highs and swing lows; focus on the important ones such as previous day high/low. A partially filled FVG can simply be treated as the low and its liquidity.
quote: "Liquidity is quite simple. It's a swing high or a swing low."

rule: Put on size only with a clear bias; otherwise only scalps or smaller formations.
quote: "I prefer to put on size when I have a clear bias, yeah."

rule: He doesn't take setups below 2R; an average RR under 2 is not his model.
quote: "I don't really trade less than 2R on things."

rule: After a win streak, take one trade and get off the charts to avoid tilt.
quote: "Take one trade and get off the charts. You're just setting yourself up to tilt."

rule: Keep the chart simple: highs, lows, fair value gaps and the model; stop adding new concepts when overwhelmed.
quote: "Literally mark out highs, lows, fair value gaps, like my model. That's it."

rule: Use prop accounts rather than demo once you understand the model: same emotional attachment, capped risk.
quote: "I would say prop firms are a good way to get that emotional aspect of trading with capped risk."

rule: Bias for a market can be derived from the dollar: bearish dollar means bullish foreign currencies.
quote: "So dollar, I'm still bearish on, which means bullish on foreign currencies."

rule: Use relative strength across correlated indices: in a bearish move, trade the weakest asset and use the strongest asset reaching its reaction level (e.g. YM hitting PDL) as the target/timing on the weakest.
quote: "you can use the strongest one to consider a target on the not strongest one. So if we are going to consolidate, right, previous day low would be where we react on the strongest asset, right, which means on the weakest asset, that is when you could then use that as a target for this."

rule: Relative strength can switch intraday: once the weakest asset hits its target it can become the strongest, and the trade moves to the asset that is now weakest (NQ to YM).
quote: "Because here, NQ is the weakest, it hits its target, and then YM becomes the weakest."

rule: Confirm the high (low) of day with either an hourly CISD or a 4H candle (3) closure.
quote: "how do you confirm the high of the day? You use either an hourly change in the state of delivery, which we have here."

rule: An hourly CISD here = a consolidation, a sweep of the consolidation high, then a close through the series of up-close candles that made that high; after it, expect the high to be in.
quote: "We have a consolidation. We sweep out the consolidation high. We close through the series of out-closed candles that made that high, right here."

rule: 4H-15m model: after a 4H candle 3 closure (with SMT at the previous high), enter on the 15m protected swing and target 2R, the previous lows, or until the strongest asset hits its target.
quote: "There's a 4-hour candle closure. It's a 4-hour, 15-minute model. We have a little SMT on this previous high. And what do we have? Protected swing right there. So then you can enter on a protected swing."

rule: Before the 9:30 open trade only on the 15-minute chart or higher; after the open any timeframe is allowed.
quote: "But I would not go below the 15-minute here prior to the open."

rule: If price trades through the previous day low and fails to manipulate it (no reversal), expect a continuation / trend day.
quote: "Here's our previous day low. What do we do? We trade through it. Do we form a reversal here? No, we form a continuation, which means lower, which means, hello, the market is trending."

rule: Do not try to catch lows (or highs) on a trend day; align with the trend instead of fighting the daily candle.
quote: "Don't try to catch lows on a trend day. It doesn't work. Get chopped up. Destroyed."

rule: Trading against the daily candle's direction is fighting the daily candle; on a trending day there is zero reason to trade against it.
quote: "You fight the daily candle if you try to trade this to the upside, right? ... There's zero reason to try too long the market when it is trending on a day like this."

rule: Always start top-down on the daily.
quote: "So always start on the daily, right?"

rule: Only FOMC, NFP and CPI matter: don't trade right before them; ignore other (orange folder) news. Crude inventories (~10:30) matter only for oil.
quote: "FOMC, NFP, CPI. Don't trade right before it. Otherwise I do not care."

rule: Do not trade bank holidays.
quote: "What is your idea for bank holiday days? I don't trade it."

rule: Use higher timeframes for execution instead of dropping to 1m/15s out of fear of missing the move; the higher timeframe won't make you miss it, it stops you being stopped out.
quote: "Get off the 15-minute in 1-minute and use the higher timeframes."

rule: Invalidation trading: if the bias idea fails, the low (high) it relied on is not a swing point, so that low becomes the draw on liquidity.
quote: "If this whole idea is going to fail and it's an invalidation trade, it is invalidating this as a swing point, essentially. So if that's not going to be a swing point, what becomes our draw on liquidity? That low."

rule: For a bullish daily, the daily low is too far for a stop; intraday look for the EQ to hold, and a reach into the only lower-timeframe liquidity point (a swept low below EQ) with a V-shape reversal counts as the intraday CISD.
quote: "Now looking intraday, I want to see the EQ hold. Well, this is a low below the EQ that swept out. So ideally, this would hold going into the day. So the only liquidity point on a lower timeframe would be there, right? So if price reaches into there, I would consider that a change in the state of delivery intraday."

rule: After the first entry, when a new continuation forms, the invalidation moves above (below) entry; the previous day high is a good first target, or be at breakeven from the first entry.
quote: "It hits our previous day high. That's a good first target if you're inside on the lower timeframes, or you should be breakeven from the first entry here."

rule: When a daily idea is unclear after a sweep of PDH, wait for the daily candle to close before re-forming the bias.
quote: "I have no idea until tomorrow. I need to let this daily candle close, right?"

rule: In a range where continuations form slowly and keep failing, stand aside.
quote: "this is just a range. It takes so long to form any sort of continuation here."

rule: Intraday reversal process: wait for a CISD or a 4H candle closure, then drop to the 15m and trade the continuations.
quote: "You either wait for change in the state of delivery, this one you get both at the same time, or 4-hour candle closure. Right there. Candle closure, go to the 15, continuation, continuation."

rule: Phases of price apply on every timeframe (fractal); read them across YM/ES/NQ at the daily level: did each manipulate its low or continue through it?
quote: "You look at the phases of price on every timeframe, guys. Everything you do is fractal, right?"

rule: Practice phases of price by watching price around a previous day high or low.
quote: "Just go find a previous day high or low and watch price around it."

rule: For crypto, use daily swing points: a daily swing point plus a CISD with a candle 2 is a short into the lows.
quote: "Daily swing point, CISD with a candle 2, that's a short into these lows."

rule: He does not use projections (standard-deviation style targets).
quote: "I don't use projections."

rule: If an asset has already expanded for multiple days into its target, expect little more from it (consolidation) while the lagging asset catches up.
quote: "Multiple days of expansion. I'm honestly not expecting a whole lot from it"

rule: If bullish, use the weakest asset reversing to frame longs on the strongest; if bearish, use the strongest asset reversing to frame shorts on the weakest.
quote: "if bullish, use the weakest asset reversing to frame longs the strongest. If bearish, use the strongest asset person to frame shorts on the weakest."

rule: When longing, trade the strongest asset; the weakest is only a timing tool, not the instrument.
quote: "If I'm longing, I want to focus on the strongest, but you can use the weakest to help you time that."

rule: When the strongest and weakest assets move in opposite directions against your idea, expect consolidation; it is a bad sign for an open trade.
quote: "But when these two assets are not aligning, Quite difficult to go anywhere, right? And that's why you see we're just getting consolidation"

rule: One of the diverging assets is 'lying'; if the strong one turns out to be the liar, the move fails / consolidates.
quote: "The way I like to think about strongest and weakest assets is one of them is lying, right?"

rule: Prefer the weakest asset to make another sweep of its low before reversing: it traps early longs/shorts and gives another SMT.
quote: "but I like another sweep, personally. That another sweep just kind of catches anyone else out that is short or early on into the longs, and then it provides another SMT."

rule: Do not long the open when, after taking out a high, there are no swings you expect to hold.
quote: "Can you type a 1 in chat if you understand why you wouldn't want to be longing the open today? Because you have no swings you're expecting to hold after we take out a high."

rule: When protected swings are lined up after price takes something out, price often runs that protected swing before the continuation.
quote: "Usually, this is what happens is when we have some protected swings lined up after taking out something, a lot of times we go run out that protected swing before we actually get the continuation or move higher."

rule: You cannot trade higher from failure swings; a deep run that leaves failure swings makes the low untrustworthy.
quote: "Like the only reason I don't like this is just how deep this ran. That makes so many failure swings."

rule: If the daily did not respect the EQ (a larger opposing run), the day is not set up for expansion: expect only the daily open, intraday liquidity, then maybe the previous day high.
quote: "Did we respect the EQ? No. We have a larger EQ, which means it's not set up for expansion, right?"

rule: A C2 with a large wick limits the target to the daily open / intra-candle highs; expect a retracement and let the following candle do the expansion rather than entering on that C2.
quote: "But generally, when I have a larger target like this, I'm expecting some sort of retracement, and then the following candle to do the expansion, right?"

rule: A large-wick closure does not stop a reversal but reduces targets to daily open, intraday lows, then previous day low.
quote: "Doesn't mean it can't reverse, it just wears your targets. Daily open, intraday lows, and then previous day low."

rule: For a candle-3 continuation the candle should respect the EQ of candle 2; sitting at the EQ needs a better closure.
quote: "If you view it, if we want to see a continuation in candle 3, you want to see it respect the EQ. We're right at that EQ."

rule: After a protected swing forms, continuation higher should respect 50% of that swing range.
quote: "So ideally, if we are going to go higher, what are we going to respect? 50% of this, right?"

rule: Wait for the 15m candle closure, then watch the 1m for a continuation.
quote: "As long as we get a decent closer on the 15-minute here, we'll be able to watch the 1-minute for a continuation."

rule: Waiting for the candle closure keeps you out of dumb positions.
quote: "We are waiting for the closure. Because what does waiting for the closure do? Keeps you from dumb positions in a way."

rule: Trade continuations, not reversals: if your bias is wrong, waiting for clean continuations keeps you out instead of repeatedly getting stopped out.
quote: "you always try to trade the reversal and you're wrong on the bias you're just going to continuously get stopped out"

rule: Have one idea for the day with a defined sequence: run/sweep off the open, a reversal, then seek the continuation.
quote: "The only idea for me today is NASDAQ to the overnight highs. With that, we need a run or a sweep off the open, and then we need some sort of reversal, in which case we can seek a continuation."

rule: If the weakest asset makes a massive run into the low, expect little from it; for a continuation before 10:00 you want a shallow run, not a massive move.
quote: "If we're actually going to get a continuation prior to 10 a.m., then I want to see not a massive move."

rule: A positional entry is a protected swing formed before the new higher-timeframe candle opens; take it only with high confidence in the bias, otherwise let the HTF candle form its wick first.
quote: "So would I try to take a positional entry at 10 a.m.? No. Because I'd want to first just let the 4-hour candle form whatever wick it's going to form."

rule: Price either ranges or expands; after an expansion, wait for the range to form before trading.
quote: "price can't expand forever, so it's going to need to range at some point again."

rule: A run of a consolidation into a gap is a good spot for a reaction; a V-shape there sets up the continuation.
quote: "So if you run out the consolidation into a gap, it's a good spot for a reaction, right?"

rule: An FVG in the upper half of the wick may be reached; that is where the higher low must form.
quote: "So this fair value gap is in the upper half of the wick. So it's fine if price can reach into here. It's just that's where we need to form a higher low, right?"

rule: He does not use the first presented fair value gap.
quote: "I don't use it. That's my thoughts."

rule: If price is going to expand it does not wait 20+ minutes; a long delay is evidence against the continuation.
quote: "It's not going to wait 35 minutes, not 35, 20 minutes to go expand, right? It's just going to go."

rule: Do not trade late in the session after the daily profile has used much of its time and range.
quote: "it's used so much time and range, this doesn't obviously support it, so it's like, I don't know, it could go back up there, I just don't trade that late in this session."

rule: If the early NY idea hasn't played out, wait for the 10:00 candle to close and reevaluate.
quote: "Usually what's gonna happen here is you wait for 10 a.m., kinda reevaluate, right?"

rule: Use the 1m (or 3m) for entries so the risk-to-reward to the HTF target is available; the 15m or 5m usually won't give it.
quote: "Sure, I could sit on the 3-minute even. It's all the same though."

rule: Reversals require swing points, so the model is built on swing points.
quote: "So my whole model is based off of, oh, well, if you can only Reverse with a swing point, why would I not study and build my model around swing points?"

rule: After an overnight reversal off a low with an hourly CISD (intraday reversal profile), expect that low to be the low of the day and look for a higher low or continuation.
quote: "We have an hourly change in the state of delivery. So from my intraday reversal video, I'm expecting this to be the low of the day."

rule: Build daily-bias skill by practicing on the daily chart: daily high/low, previous day's EQ, reactions and the daily profile.
quote: "Practice looking at daily high, daily low, previous day's EQ and how price reacts on it and the daily profile around it."

rule: Start every day on the daily chart.
quote: "I start on the daily chart. That's it. I will always be on the daily, and that's always the plan."

rule: Only avoid trading the day of CPI, NFP and FOMC; the day before FOMC is tradable.
quote: "The only thing I do news-wise is I avoid the day of CPI and NFP and NFP, FOMC, CPI, same day."

rule: Do not long at the highs of a consolidation (e.g. oil).
quote: "But, yeah, I'm not trying to long at the highs. That's not my strategy."

rule: Chart settings: B-ADJ on (back-adjust contract rollovers so futures match the index/ETF), SET (settlement) off to use the actual close.
quote: "I always have set turned off. I want the actual close. I always have B-Adjust turned on because I want to have it adjusted for contractor rollover."

rule: Nothing works 100% of the time; a CISD can fail even with bias aligned, accept being wrong.
quote: "Nothing works all the time. Sure, there can be reasons for certain things, but a lot of times things just don't work."

rule: Judge win rate and profitability over large samples (100 trades, 3-6 months); loss streaks are normal at a 50% win rate.
quote: "No, you just haven't taken 100 trades to actually know what your win rate is."

rule: The goal of a session is to learn something, not to be right or make money every day.
quote: "it's not to be right every day to make money every day. It's to learn something that progresses you every day, right?"

rule: An inside day (daily candle inside the prior candle) is consolidation: range-bound, no real bias, trade it as a reaction game or not at all.
quote: "So inside day, inside day, pretty much just a consolidation, we're in a range."

rule: A bullish daily profile (open low then higher) is less trustworthy when the low didn't sweep anything relevant.
quote: "This is a nice open low, going higher, which is bullish, but it doesn't go into anything relevant. We don't sweep out a low. Can't really trust much there"

rule: To get the strongest asset higher, you need the weakest asset to reverse (forming SMT); wait for that reversal off the open before framing longs.
quote: "What would we need if we want this one to go higher? We need the weakest asset to reverse."

rule: When the weakest asset fails to react at the low it should manipulate, expect it to continue to its previous day low and drag the other indices lower.
quote: "Failing to manipulate means it's likely to go for what? It wants to go towards its previous day low."

rule: Mark the 0.5 (EQ) of the wick and watch for a reaction there, usually on a lower timeframe.
quote: "I want to see where 0.5 of that wick is. Going to mark out that back here. So we'll see, usually on a little lower timeframe"

rule: On a no-bias day, wait for the first 15m candle (9:45) to form before judging the open.
quote: "In days like you don't have a bias, it's just a reaction game. So here we'll probably wait, you know, 9.45 because that gives us a 15-minute candle that's formed"

rule: Keep concepts minimal: highs, lows, fair value gaps, CISD and how candles form.
quote: "What is the only concepts I use? I use highs, lows, fair value gaps, change in the state of delivery, and then it's just understanding how candles form."

rule: With SMT on a high, short the weaker asset, not the strongest one.
quote: "Would we want to trade on the strongest asset short? No, you'd want to trade on this one."

rule: His whole model: have an idea (bias) and find a swing formation that aligns with it.
quote: "Literally, my whole model, guys, is just you have an idea for something, and then you find a swing formation that aligns with that."

rule: Liquidity: look back three days and mark the daily highs and lows (relevant swings); previous day high and low are the most relevant levels; ask which side of that range price will target.
quote: "Go back three days, mark out the highs and the lows, and that's how you frame, right?"

rule: Ignore a CISD that isn't paired with a swing point or that goes against your bias on that asset.
quote: "It's not paired with any sort of swing point, right? I'm not even looking at that."

rule: A CISD does not need volatility, but don't use a CISD within consolidation.
quote: "It doesn't have to be volatile to form a CISD. It's just you don't want to use a CISD within consolidation."

rule: Waiting for a continuation protects you from bad reversal ideas: if price retraces into an FVG but never closes through it, there is no continuation and no trade.
quote: "How do you save yourself from These ideas. You just wait for continuations."

rule: Always know what the daily candle is doing, even when executing on the 1m.
quote: "Even if I'm trading a one-minute time frame, I'm still understanding what the daily candle's doing."

rule: Previous day high/low is liquidity because yesterday's traders put their stops there.
quote: "Where are you going to put your stop loss? Probably on a previous day high or a swing high. So that then becomes the area where liquidity is, right?"

rule: A New York reversal profile (previous day high taken, failure swings) has limited targets when price opened in the middle of the range; don't expect it to go far.
quote: "on a normal New York reversal, you don't, like, you're not trying to target this, the weird middle ground. That's why I'm not looking for it to go crazy far."

rule: No kill zones: if the higher-timeframe wick has formed, an entry at 6:45 is as valid as one at 8:30.
quote: "I'm not going to wait for the kill zone if price forms its wick on the higher timeframe and starts to trade lower, right? Then I can get on side with it."

rule: No model wins every time; expect losses.
quote: "no model works all the time. You're never going to have a 100% win rate."

rule: Use CISD instead of BOS/MSS/CHoCH: find the high, find the series of candles that made it, and a close through it is the shift.
quote: "I always find the high, I find the series of candles, I made the high, close through it, that's it."

rule: Top-down: daily for directional bias, then 4H/1H for structure (FVG, daily EQ, swing points) to find where price should react once the daily wick has formed, then align a fractal model.
quote: "Your goal here is to find an area where you expect price to react after you've already lit the wick form of the daily candle."

rule: Entry sequence: swing point to trade away from, CISD (he doesn't trade the reversal itself), wait for a continuation, enter, stop on the protected swing, target 2R.
quote: "I take an entry, I put my stop loss on the protected swing, my indicator marks it out, and then I can look for 2R."

rule: Have a bias before you trade; without one you are pattern trading.
quote: "Have a bias before you look to trade. Otherwise, you're just simply trying to pattern trade."

rule: The wick has formed when price, at your area and in your bias direction, expands and closes over (bullish) or sweeps the previous level and closes below (bearish); time matters only because it defines the HTF candles (9:30, 9:45, 10:00).
quote: "Right here, price sweeps out the previous, closes below. Do you think the wick has formed? If yes, then you can trade it lower."

rule: Use YM mainly as a relative-strength gauge to trade NQ/ES.
quote: "I use it more as a relative strength indicator to trade the other assets."

rule: He enters continuations on any timeframe; 15m setups positioned 6-8am before the open, and hourly/daily ones, are among his favourites.
quote: "I enter continuations on any time frame. It does not really matter the time frame to me. My favorite trades are honestly the higher time frame ones, like the hourly, daily chart."

rule: MMXM maps onto the fractal model: smart money reversal = swing point, target = the swing low that made the swing high; equivalently, candle 2 closure + CISD targeting the 4H swing low / previous day low.
quote: "Or you can forget all of that, remove all the drawings, and just say, okay, cool, we have a candle to closure or trading this way with a change in the state of delivery, what's our target?"

rule: On a no-bias day with decoupled indices, either path is tradable by reaction (strong asset to its high, weak asset to its low).
quote: "Like I said, it's a reaction game. So it's like you could either trade it into the slow or trade it into the high."

rule: Don't trust a V-shape reversal against your bias; the level it would need to respect if it were genuine decides it, and a closure below that sends price to the actual lows.
quote: "You see this nice V-shape reversal? I don't trust it. So what? This is the area you'd have to respect if it was bullish, right?"

rule: To fade a lower-timeframe bullish CISD, you need an asset to run a high (form a swing point) and then close below or form a lower high; without that lower high there is nothing to do.
quote: "But if price never forms a lower high, there's nothing to do."

rule: Reverse engineer in hindsight rather than bar-replay guessing: for each move ask how you could have got on side, which timeframe shows reversal + continuation, the R:R, whether highs were taken, and the draw on liquidity.
quote: "Could I get on side with this? How could I get on side with this? Go look at all the timeframes."

rule: On a no-bias day you are scalping, not holding for a big expansion; after an opposing run, wait for another lower-timeframe continuation.
quote: "But like I said, guys, today is a day where it's like you don't really have a bias. So it's like, are you scalping? Like you're not trying to hold for a huge expansion."

rule: If time is limited, focus on 9:00-11:00 New York, where most of the open's volatility is.
quote: "If you focus on, let's say, 9 to 11 each day. That's when the most of the volatility in the New York Open price pushes."

rule: Expect markets to stay range-bound before a Fed rate decision.
quote: "I'm expecting stuff to stay range bound prior to FOMC, generally speaking."

rule: He avoids shorting when the setup means trading away from a cluster of failure swings against his upside read.
quote: "I don't really have too much interest in the downside for myself just because I don't want to trade away from all these failure things here."

rule: The easiest daily bias comes from three things only: candle 2 closure, candle 3 closure, and the invalidation of those; unless price consolidates, each either works or fails, and both give a trade.
quote: "if you want the easiest bias, you're just going to focus on a couple things. Handle 2 closure, handle 3 closure, then the invalidation of those. Because whenever you see one, you generally, unless it's going to consolidate, it's going to either work or it's going to fail."

rule: A bullish daily bias is invalidated in two ways: a reversal off the previous-day high, or failing the EQ (closing below EQ and forming a bearish continuation).
quote: "We're either going to reverse off our previous day's high, you can take a look at NQ for that, or we're going to fail the EQ."

rule: When the bias is invalidated you either stand aside or trade it to the opposite previous-day extreme (previous-day low for a failed bullish bias).
quote: "I can either, one, just avoid it and say, all right, cool, my idea is not correct to the upside, or I can say, cool, If the idea is wrong, I can look to trade it to its previous day low. It's always going to be that."

rule: If a C2 setup does not form a continuation, the swing is expected to fail and the draw on liquidity becomes the opposite previous-day extreme.
quote: "So now that it's failed, what is our drawn liquidity? Well, if this swing is going to fail, it means previous day low is the target."

rule: Draw on liquidity: from current price, look left and decide whether price is more likely to reach a level above or below, then trade towards it.
quote: "You are going to look left and you're going to say, is price more likely reaching for some level here or some level here?"

rule: With no bias, take no entries; do not drop to lower timeframes looking for one. Go to the higher timeframes or stay out.
quote: "When you don't have a bias or any idea of what's happening, go to the higher timeframes or stay out of it."

rule: If you don't know what is going on at the open, wait 5 minutes, then 15 minutes, after 9:30; often you get help there.
quote: "If you don't really know what's going on, wait for five minutes after 9.30, wait for 15 minutes after 9.30, and a lot of times you get some help there."

rule: If the current candle has already used much of its range and time, wait for the next 30-minute candle or 9:30 before deciding.
quote: "We've already used a lot of this range and time in this candle, so it's usually better off just waiting until the next 30-minute candle or 9.30 and then making the decision."

rule: Before the open, ask how much range you expect. On an expected expansion day don't trade the 9:30 reversal candle, wait for 10:00; on range-bound days 9:30 often just creates volatility inside the range.
quote: "On a day where you're anticipating expansion, you don't really want to trade this candle. You'd rather just wait for 10 a.m."

rule: After about four consecutive daily expansion days, expect consolidation or a retracement to make a higher low rather than a fifth expansion day.
quote: "Sure, there's times where we get a fifth day when it goes that far, but many times going to have some sort of consolidation or a retracement, right, to make a higher low."

rule: The strongest asset reversing off its previous-day high lets you short the weakest asset; for shorts trade the weaker indices, not the strongest/lagging one.
quote: "But strongest asset reversing off of its previous day high allows you to short the weakest asset, right?"

rule: Don't trade the lagging (strongest) index short; you get chopped up. Trade the one showing the weakness.
quote: "You don't want to trade the very lagging one because, look, you could take a short in here. It works. Take any short in here, you're just getting chopped up."

rule: ES rarely leads (9 out of 10 days NQ is the one that moves first); when ES leads and the others lag he treats the tape as unusual and does nothing.
quote: "Generally ES does not lead. Like 9 out of 10 days, ES does not lead."

rule: A single pattern such as an FVG is not a bias; he does not pattern-trade.
quote: "I don't pattern trade things. So just because we have a fair value gap here doesn't mean my bias is bearish, right?"

rule: A swing is only a TTFM protected swing if the move away from it left a fair value gap; a continuation without an FVG is less trustworthy.
quote: "Why is this not showing a protected swing, right? Shouldn't it? No. There's no fair value gap, right?"

rule: Entry-timeframe candle reading: after a bullish candle in a bearish idea, either wait for that candle to turn into a reversal and trade the next, or let it close higher and wait for the next candle to form the reversal; be patient for the next candle.
quote: "Now this is a bullish candle, so you either have to wait for this candle to reverse and be a reversal and then trade the following, or you have to wait for it to close higher and then for the next candle to form a reversal. So usually when I see a bullish candle, I'm just being patient for the next one."

rule: Wick size on the C2 candle predicts the next candle's expansion: a small wick then trading away means it can expand; too large a wick makes expansion on the next candle less likely.
quote: "If it has a small wick and trades lower, then it's possible for that to expand. If it makes too high of a wick, then it's less likely for that candle to expand as the next one."

rule: C1 is arbitrary, just the candle before C2; C2 is the candle that makes the high/low, C3 follows, then C4. Don't spend effort identifying C1.
quote: "Stop trying to learn what a C1 is. C1 is arbitrary, always just before C2. C2 is always just a high."

rule: Always pair the setup with the daily chart; he does not use a weekly-4H model.
quote: "I don't really use the weekly 4-hour model, so I'm not sure. I always pair stuff with the daily chart."

rule: An hourly idea can be traded on the 5m; if the 5m doesn't give enough R:R to the target without a limit order, drop to the 3m or 1m.
quote: "Obviously, if I'm going to trade an hourly, I can trade a 5-minute. Do I get enough risk to reward to that low? Not really without a limit order, and I don't like to trade a limit against that. But then you have to go to either a 3-minute or a 1-minute."

rule: A 1m SMT is not enough to frame the whole idea.
quote: "I'm not a huge fan of SMT on the 1-minute to frame the whole idea"
