rule: Do not enter in the direction of the target once the daily range is mostly made and price is near the target (e.g. shorting into the previous-day low); only hold runners from earlier entries.
quote: "Well, because look at the daily range. It's pretty much made the daily range. Two previous day low. So unless you're short from in here, holding runners, I would never be entering short into here."

rule: Late continuations far into the move (below the lows / below the previous-day low) are places to trail your stop, not to enter.
quote: "So this is a continuation where I would trail my stop to. This is not a continuation I would personally enter because of the location. You're below these lows, you're below previous day low. It's fine to trail stop there. I don't like to enter breakouts like that."

rule: Location in the dealing range matters: a short entered low in the dealing range is not ideal (poor R:R, failure swings before the first target).
quote: "Not super ideal because you're quite low in the range, right, in the dealing range."

rule: He doesn't like breakouts that have no swings below them; a breakout before the range high is taken is acceptable.
quote: "I don't mind trading a breakout before the range high is taken. Not a huge fan of breakouts without any swings below."

rule: When price takes a range low, the read is binary: manipulation (sweep the low and go higher) or failure to manipulate (break down lower).
quote: "Do we manipulate this low to go higher? Or do we fail to manipulate the low to break down lower? It is really just two things."

rule: If a C2 high remains, price must invalidate that wick before a short; if it sweeps the high, wait for a new C2.
quote: "So then the whole idea is if this high is going to remain, right, it may or may not, then it would have to invalidate this kind of wick here. If it goes and sweeps out the new high, then you kind of have to just wait for a new C2."

rule: On an expansion day you can generally hold to the close; otherwise take profit at the correlated draw (e.g. pound/euro shorts held until DXY reaches its daily gap).
quote: "If you're short into Pound or Euro, I prefer Pound, then you can hold until the dollar hits that level. A good profit-taking target or towards the end of the day, then an expansion day, so you can generally hold till the close."

rule: He does not use DXY correlation, CFD charts, Fib projections, CRT or order flow in his analysis; the dollar never vetoes a setup.
quote: "I just don't use it in my analysis at all. If you do, that's great. I just don't."

rule: Think less when trading: hold one clear HTF idea (e.g. NQ into the daily gap then expand to the highs) and trade only that.
quote: "Way too much thought. You have to think less when you trade."

rule: On a consolidating day he expects little from the NY session and only trades expansions/breakouts, not the middle of the range.
quote: "This is not normally the area that I look to trade. I like to trade those expansions or the breakouts, right?"

rule: Pre-open routine: daily relative strength of NQ/ES/YM and previous-day extremes, then other markets, then 15m three-pane indices with projected paths, then wait for 9:30.
quote: "So let's go to the daily. So YM's the weakest and Q the strongest. It's pretty obvious to see on the daily chart, right?"

rule: After multiple days of expansion into all-time highs, don't look for intraday longs over the previous highs.
quote: "It is a bullish day. It's not super interesting to be longing intraday over the previous highs."

rule: Failure swings up on the hourly after an expansion are not a bullish daily profile; expect consolidation or a reversal (9:30 manipulation, then lower).
quote: "normally on a day like this, you either consolidate or you have a reversal. That's why I'm favoring the downside inside the daily profile, because we just have failure sinks. Usually you have 9.30, some sort of manipulation, and they move lower."

rule: Relative strength: for a move higher, the weakest index should reverse off its low and frame the move; for a move lower, the strongest index usually forms the reversal.
quote: "If we're going to go higher, what would we want to frame? We'd want to see YM reverse off of this low. And frame something, right? The weakest asset framing a move higher. If we're going to go lower, then it's most likely NQ forming a reversal off of this."

rule: When indices diverge at the open, one is 'lying'; you cannot know which in advance, so wait for 5m (or 15m) closures. If both are lying, expect consolidation.
quote: "How do you know which one's lying? You don't know. You just kind of wait for closures to tell you"

rule: Do not trade before the open. Bullish entries come around the higher-timeframe open; bearish entries come on the wick of the next candle (the 10:00 candle).
quote: "There's no way to trade this prior to the Open because where are we at, right? If we were bullish, we want to be entering around the higher timeframe Open, which is that. If we're bearish, we want to be entering, this is a large wick on the next candle, which is 10 a.m."

rule: If the 9:30 move does not get a continuation, the session is chop; wait for 10:00.
quote: "If 9.30 move doesn't get a continuation, it's chopped. Wait for 10 a.m. That's like a little lesson."

rule: If you don't know what is going on after the open, wait longer: 5 minutes, then the first 15, then 10:00.
quote: "Just wait five minutes. If you still don't, wait first 15. If you still don't, wait for 10am. You know what I mean? Like, if you don't know what's going on, just wait longer."

rule: Entry timeframe depends on the clock: before 9:30 use M15 or higher for entries; after 9:30 any timeframe (his typed note; the transcript is garbled).
quote: "Entry prior to 9.30. Use M15 or greater after 9.30. Well, I just typed a win key phase. Any time frame."

rule: If the bias-direction move forms no gap on your entry timeframe, step down one timeframe at a time (5m, then 3m, then lower) until a gap appears, rather than putting the stop above the whole higher-timeframe swing.
quote: "But we know there's no gap here, and I wouldn't want to put a stop all the way up there. So you go to the three-minute, which is your next lower time frame. ... Something where there's no gap, right? So then I have to go down one more time frame, and then you have a gap, right?"

rule: No gap on the 5m during a move means a lower-timeframe gap exists and the move is a continuation; for the trend to continue, the high that started it must hold.
quote: "if we don't really form a gap here, it means there should be a lower time frame gap. It's just going to be a continuation. ... So ideally, if this trend is going to continue, that high should remain."

rule: The 4H-15m model is preferred because lower timeframes chop people up even when their direction is right.
quote: "So the reason I say 4-hour and 15 a lot of times is because it can help people not get chopped up."

rule: Keep your bias through intraday chop; don't flip it because the market isn't moving or because of what others say.
quote: "I'm not gonna sit here and be like, oh, never mind, guys. I thought we were gonna go higher right here. Like, that's not what I said. So, I stick with my bias."

rule: A daily doji does not support expansion; when the bias-timeframe candle is a doji, wait for it to close and trade the next day.
quote: "the daily candle doesn't necessarily support expansion lore, right? It is by definition what I would consider to be a doji candle. So if I want to trade it back to the open, I'd rather wait for it to close and then look to trade it tomorrow."

rule: A counter or scalp trade back into a range must be refined inside the T-spot, and its target is the HTF gap where candles don't overlap (refined to the 1H gap).
quote: "But if you scalp gold back into the range, you really are going to have to refine it down in here, in this T-spot here. ... this is kind of the target on the move for today. Because you can see the higher time frame gap where these candles don't overlap with these ones."

rule: EQ is the mechanical test for whether a wick is small enough for expansion: retracing beyond it does not kill the bias, but price will likely only return to the daily open or the intraday highs rather than expand.
quote: "The EQ is what we use to mechanically determine what is a small enough wick for expansion. ... If price goes all the way down here, it's not that it can't be bullish, but it's not going to expand, right? It's likely to just return back to its daily open or its intraday highs."

rule: Candle numbering: C2 is always the swing high/low, C1 is the candle before it, C3 follows C2, C4 follows C3.
quote: "So candle 2 is always going to be the low or the high of a swing point. Candle 1 is arbitrary. It's just prior to that. Candle 3 always follows candle 2. And candle 4 always follows candle 3."

rule: Only trade swing points formed by a candle 2 closure or a candle 3 closure at a point of interest. Example: a C2 that sweeps a high in a gap and closes back below.
quote: "A swing point I'm interested in has to be a candle 2 closure or a candle 3 closure at a point of interest."

rule: Pick the stronger of two correlated pairs off the lows using the higher-timeframe candles (e.g. pound over euro when dollar-bearish).
quote: "In my opinion, pound has more strength off these lows than euro. So look at the higher time from candles as well. That's why I would rather focus on pound versus euro."

rule: Gold SMT uses the gold FX crosses (XAUEUR/XAUGBP) intraday; gold vs silver is preferred on the higher timeframe.
quote: "I do use forex pairs for that. Gold, euro, gold, pound. For some divergences. But you can also compare it with gold and silver. But I prefer gold and silver on the higher timeframe."

rule: When the move happened overnight and indices already expanded over highs, NY is often not worth trading; he logs off early.
quote: "It could do it today, but not very interesting on indices for New York due to the overnight expansion."

rule: Trading all-time highs needs no special method; trade them the same way as any other price.
quote: "It's the exact same if you were trading two weeks ago. You guys overthink all-time highs so much."

rule: A range that keeps sweeping its lows and highs is consolidation; he expects it to be swept out in the bias direction.
quote: "I'm just viewing this as a whole kind of consolidation, which gets swept out to go lower."

rule: Before treating a daily low run as a reversal, wait for the close: a bearish close or a failure to manipulate the low points to the next low, while a reversal leaves failure swings and range trading.
quote: "Oil, running out this low, we'll see how it closes, if it closes bearish or fails to manipulate this low, we can look into this low."

rule: Follow your rules or quit; trading outside your plan (e.g. an instrument you promised not to trade) is the psychology problem.
quote: "Well, the simple fix to that is either follow your rules or give up and quit."

rule: After several days of expansion into a high, a large opposing day frames a new phase of price; plan the next day from closure through the area (continuation), reversal off it, or reaction at the previous-day low.
quote: "Multiple days of expansion, three. So then that is framing a new phase of price, right?"

rule: Do not pattern trade the model: a lower-timeframe bullish pattern against your higher-timeframe bias is not a bullish signal; wait until all timeframes align.
quote: "That's why you don't want to pattern trade the model, right? If you pattern trade it, it would say that it's bullish, right? Like if you're just pattern trading, it says it's bullish. It's not."

rule: On a bullish day do not short the reversal early; wait until all timeframes align, then stop on/above the high and target the previous-day low.
quote: "Do we want to trade short on this day? No, because it's a bullish day. We want to wait until all the timeframes align. So then you can trade it."

rule: In the overnight session he never goes below the 15m; an hourly CISD confirms the high, stop at least on the bodies.
quote: "When I trade overnight session, guys, I don't ever go into the lower timeframes here. The lowest I go is 15-minute."

rule: Entry timeframe by session: Asia H1 (M15 allowed), London M15 or above, New York before 9:30 M15 or above, New York after 9:30 any timeframe.
quote: "New York, free 9.30, M15 or above. New York after 9.30? Anything."

rule: Overnight expansions continue until a volatility event can change them: 8:30 high-impact news, 9:30 or 10:00; a reversal low would form at those times.
quote: "Overnight's expansions are going to continue until you have some sort of volatility that could change that, right? Which is normally 8.30 if you have high impact news. Or 9.30 or 10."

rule: Do not trade away from (fade) an overextended overnight move without a higher-timeframe swing-point SMT; a lower-timeframe SMT alone is not enough for him.
quote: "There's no higher time frame swing point SMT, nothing to really do that. You could make a case for this lower time frame SMT right here, but it's just not my style of trading."

rule: A higher-timeframe bias holds until price reaches its objective or closes through the level (change in the state of delivery); an opposing SMT or a good daily candle alone does not flip it.
quote: "Would have been different if gold would have closed over this level, because then it's forming a change in the state of delivery. Until it does that, this is still bearish to me."

rule: When all three indices are rotating around the open, expect consolidation (often ES) and wait a few minutes.
quote: "So usually what happens here, guys, is if they're all moving around, we get some sort of consolidation on ES. Best to wait five minutes."

rule: Have lower expectations for the open after a big overnight expansion; favor a mean reversion back into the range over continuation, but only if price confirms it.
quote: "We have such an overnight expansion, guys, that generally I'm not expecting too much after this, right? I would more favor trading back into the range as a retracement or like a mean reversion than a continuation, right?"

rule: A valid continuation is not enough: skip it if there is little range to the target or the stop cannot be positioned; take it only when the open/structure leaves room to the target.
quote: "Is this a valid continuation? Yes, right? Because it has SMT paired with that. It's just, does that give you any range, right? If you're taking this on the closure? No, right? Like there's no range on it."

rule: Use higher-timeframe candle closes as time-based exits: a 15m expansion candle can run until 9:45, a 30m one until 10:00; after the close a new phase or direction can start.
quote: "It can continue until 9.45, because this is a 15-minute expansion candle. Or it could continue until 10, because it will also be a 30-minute expansion candle."

rule: An idea with nothing on the chart aligning with it is worthless; switch the idea when price does not confirm it.
quote: "You can have the idea. If nothing aligns with it, your idea sucks, right?"

rule: Judge remaining daily range by eye from the last few daily candles, not from an indicator ADR that outliers skew.
quote: "I don't use ADR from an indicator."

rule: To form a reversal low you want one asset to run out a low (SMT) and a sweep with a small wick.
quote: "Some sort of asset run out a low. To form SMT. You need some sort of sweep of a low with a small wick."

rule: Frame trades with the daily candle: do not buy a big bearish daily candle (e.g. at 50% of its wick); buy green candles.
quote: "So when I see a big bearish daily candle, I don't like to buy that. I like to buy candles that are green."

rule: A CISD is valid when a candle closes through the level; how much of the body closes through does not matter.
quote: "It just matters if it closes through."

rule: Do not trust a weak bounce off a low; failure swings tend to be run out one more time before a real reversal.
quote: "I never trust, generally speaking, this type of move up. Just failure swings to get ran out one more time."

rule: Structure mapping always starts on the daily chart.
quote: "You should always start on the daily chart."

rule: With a bearish 4H candle already in place, any opposing move would come at the 10:00 open, not mid-candle; wait for 10:00.
quote: "If we're going to get any sort of movement that opposes this range, it's going to be at 10 a.m., right? Because it wouldn't be now."

rule: Trading against the daily candle after a large opposing move is the hardest style; the easiest is aligning with the daily candle. Only trade against the daily bias if the move has a small wick.
quote: "The only way I want to trade against the daily bias is if it has a small wick."

rule: Good New York reversals typically have a 9:30 manipulation and then a 10:00 continuation.
quote: "If you go look at New York reversals that work well, you have some sort of 9.30 manipulation, and then 10 a.m. gets a continuation."

rule: Use the weakest asset's reversal off its low to time the low on the stronger asset; the same low should then hold on the other assets.
quote: "We want the weakest asset to reverse off if it's low. So we want to see YM forming a reversal here. And then if it does that, help time the low on NQ."

rule: A large wick is defined by the EQ of the candle (the EQ box); if bullish, price should not take out that low.
quote: "You use the EQ. So see this green box? This is technically what is determining a large wick."

rule: Why continuations fail: if price struggles repeatedly to close over the CISD level and the close that finally gets over it sweeps a short-term high, expect failure and a run to the opposite low.
quote: "We're really struggling to close over this CISD level for the intraday reversal. We can't close over it once, twice, finally go, if we close over it here, we're sweeping out the short-term high."

rule: For a valid move off a low you want an actual displacement / a nice expansive candle, not choppy candles.
quote: "We don't want to see, you want to see like a nice expansive candle."

rule: Ideal reversal: the low holds, price sweeps the consolidation low, then a candle 2 forms off the small consolidation candle and expands.
quote: "You want to see price sweep out that low like it did there."

rule: Oil pairing example: anticipate the hourly candle, align a 15m swing point, enter on the 1m on a candle 3 closure; do not use the 5m there because you likely won't get a CISD.
quote: "So we have this anticipation for the hour to go lower. We have a 15-minute swing point. We have a candle 3 closure. We have an entry right there."

rule: You want the wick to form early in the setup candle and to enter around its open; if the wick forms late (most of the candle used), skip it and wait for the next candle's continuation.
quote: "You want to see the wick form early into the candle, and you want to enter around the open, right?"

rule: Waiting for continuations filters out bad setups: if the setup candle was messy, trade the next candle's continuation instead.
quote: "So it's better off you just wait for this next 15-minute candle, because if it does work, cool, now you just trade the continuation. That's why waiting for continuations just help you filter out things a lot."

rule: He trades expansion, not consolidation; days where the move is done before he wakes up are days to stay away.
quote: "I don't trade consolidation, I trade expansion, so it's not, it's not my type of day."

rule: Once the higher-timeframe target is hit after an overnight expansion, trading back into the range means fading your bias; wait for the next day to give new range.
quote: "Do I want to trade it back into the range? Then I'm fading it, and I'm fading my overall bias. I'd rather wait for tomorrow to give me new range."

rule: A candle 2 against the bias does not switch the bias without a CISD.
quote: "So when I see this candle 2, I don't view this as, hey, this is bullish, I'm switching my whole bias. No. We didn't get the CISD, so I'm looking for this to trade lower."

rule: A bearish daily setup needs the EQ to respect; if price uses the EQ as support instead, the day is an invalidation day.
quote: "You want the EQ to respect, right? If you look, does the EQ respect? No, it's then used as support to go higher."

rule: A wrong bias costs nothing if you never positioned on it; wait for the swing point to form before acting.
quote: "We were wrong on the bias, but we didn't position on it, so it doesn't matter."

rule: Once the short-term target is hit you want price to sustain the expansion (small retracement fine); an inversion of the gap or an opposite CISD says the move is done.
quote: "You want to just see this continue."

rule: No interest in shorting at the lows after the daily range is made; the only frame left is back into the range, timed with volatility (8:30 news, 9:30, 10:00).
quote: "So I have no interest shorting at the lows after it's already made its daily range."

rule: If the trigger candle consolidates but protected swings hold, anticipate candle 4 after the consolidation to continue to the target.
quote: "Because there's protected swings in here, you could still anticipate candle 4 following this consolidation to get a continuation to where? We have equal highs right here."

rule: The daily profile and daily candles restrict which direction he may frame; he only takes moves his rules allow.
quote: "Based off the certain profile, based off the daily candles, I can only frame things certain ways."

rule: Overnight highs / failure swings are the first short-term target for an intraday reversal long.
quote: "Those are the overnight highs, the failure swings."

rule: He ignores FOMC minutes; only the FOMC rate decision matters as news.
quote: "I do not care about FOMC minutes, personally. It's red folder, sure. I just don't care about it. I care about Fed rates."

rule: Identify the strongest and weakest of the correlated assets every day; the previous closure tells you, and 9:30 makes it obvious.
quote: "Relative strength, which was strongest, which was weakest. If you can answer that question most days, you're going to keep yourself from a lot of headache, right?"

rule: You can read relative strength from the first one-minute closure after 9:30 (9:31).
quote: "You could literally wait for 9.31 and get the relative strength by just looking at that one-minute closure."

rule: For longs, trade the strongest asset; never long the weakest asset (and short the weakest when bearish).
quote: "If you were going to long, right, you want to trade the strongest asset. You'd be trading this on YM. Don't try to trade the weakest asset."

rule: Being right on direction isn't enough: shorting the strong asset or longing the weak one can still get you killed.
quote: "YM here, you're getting absolutely killed, right? If you long NQ here, you're getting killed."

rule: Unless the market is consolidating, correlated assets trend together; the asset falling behind may be 'lying' and catch up.
quote: "Unless you're going to completely consolidate, correlated assets trend together."

rule: If the strongest asset is going to continue, you want the weakest asset to sweep a low and reverse first, because that creates SMT.
quote: "if YN is going to get a continuation higher, I like to see the weakest asset, spoken about this before, reverse, because what does that do? That then makes SMT."

rule: SMT is not required to take a trade.
quote: "No, you don't need SMT for a trade."

rule: ES generally doesn't lead; NQ or YM leads.
quote: "Generally, ES never leads. One of the others will lead, right?"

rule: Once one asset has printed several expansion candles, it consolidates or retraces while the others catch up; you can trade the laggard's continuation then.
quote: "So now YM's has its multiple expansion candles. This is now where the other can catch up while it consolidates."

rule: A 9:30 expansion usually lasts two candles: to 9:45 if the 15m is an expansion candle, to 10:00 if the 30m stays one; then the new 4H candle brings new ideas.
quote: "Generally, when you get a 9.30 expansion, it goes until two times, 9.45 or 10. Because this 15-minute candle is an expansion candle, so it should continue until 9.45."

rule: Align with the daily candle; don't fade the opposing higher-timeframe candle.
quote: "So like on this, I'm bearish. Why? Because I want to align with the daily candle."

rule: After an expansion, expect a new phase of price (retracement, reversal or consolidation) before a new continuation; Monday after last week's expansion was that new phase.
quote: "Yesterday is what I would say a new phase of price, because I'm not expecting us to just continue to trend the whole time. Need some sort of retracement, reversal, retracement, so we can get a new continuation."

rule: If the profile shows no intraday reversal against your bias, keep the bias.
quote: "There is absolutely nothing here telling me it is bullish. So then I just remain bearish. That's it."

rule: Don't trade from the middle of a move: wait for a new swing to form so there is something to trade away from and a sensible stop.
quote: "So you'd have to wait for the open for something to form to actually look to trade away from."

rule: If you trust the low (or high) of the day, you can trade away from it.
quote: "As long as you trust a low of the day, you can trade away, right?"

rule: Entry sequence: every entry needs a swing point and then a closure through it, which forms the protected swing; the ideal is both happening at once (a C2/C3 closure), but that isn't required.
quote: "To form a protected swing, you have to have a swing point and then a closure through."

rule: A return from a CISD level also creates a protected swing if it happens in a point of interest.
quote: "If it's in a point of interest, yeah."

rule: Prefer CISD over IFVG as the entry.
quote: "CISD is correct."

rule: Continuations are far easier than reversals; wait for a continuation instead of trying to long the low of the day.
quote: "You don't need to trade the reversal. Reversals are hard to trade, guys. Like, continuations are far easier."

rule: In a bearish idea, no lower high means no trade; it just means the trend continues against you.
quote: "If we can't form a lower high, there's no trade, right? Because then this is just saying it's a continuation of that trend."

rule: Wait for the higher-timeframe candle closure first, then a continuation or lower high; that saves you from losses when the idea is wrong.
quote: "We save ourself a potential loss so far. By waiting for what? The higher time from candle closure first, but also a continuation or a lower high."

rule: Trends happen early in an expansion candle; once a candle has used too much time and range, stop trading it and reevaluate at the next candle's open and close.
quote: "if we're going to trend, when is it going to do it? In an expansion candle. Early into the candle forms, it's how it goes. So I'm better off waiting for 10-15"

rule: When a setup needs to work, look for a very aggressive candle back into the range or away from the high; without it the idea will likely chop out.
quote: "you want to see like a very aggressive candle back into the range. Otherwise, The whole idea just may just chop out."

rule: After sweeping a low, the next move should expand away from it: price forms a gap and a new move comes out of that gap, not a reversal.
quote: "normally what you want to see is this form a gap, and then you have a new move out of that, right?"

rule: On a reversal day with a large wick, targets are the daily open, then intraday liquidity, then the previous-day low or high; don't expect an expansion.
quote: "So whenever you have a reversal day with a large wick, your targets are always daily open and then intraday liquidity, right? And then you can look towards previous day low or previous day high if you need to go further."

rule: Once a reversal trade hits its targets, the move is over for you, whatever price does next.
quote: "This move would be over for me, right? This move can do whatever it wants. Because if you're trading this reversal, like we said, those are your targets."

rule: A short after price hits a higher-timeframe target is valid as an intraday reversal, with adjusted (smaller) targets.
quote: "You're adjusting your targets for sure. I mean, it is valid in terms of a short after you hit a higher time from target."

rule: In a consolidation, a range trade needs a sweep of one side while the opposite extreme holds, then a 15m/30m swing, targeting the other side of the range.
quote: "So you'd want to see a sweep of this side of the range, right? And you want to see this high remain."

rule: He trades expansions only; a separate consolidation strategy fades breaks outside a range back into it.
quote: "I prefer to just focus on the expansions personally, but that's how you would do it."

rule: Avoid trading away from failure swings on both sides of a range.
quote: "I don't like to trade away from all these failure swings on each side."

rule: Continuations that form while sweeping a higher-timeframe key level tend to fail.
quote: "When you have the continuation that forms as it's like sweeping out a higher timeframe key level, that's my in your why your continuations fail video."

rule: Scalping model: trade the continuation only when the hourly and the 15m are both continuing in the same direction.
quote: "You want to trade the continuation on the hourly? And on the 15, right, all of that all aligned together, right?"

rule: Earlier in the day the intraday-reversal timeframes are 4H/1H; in New York you can adjust them slightly.
quote: "Earlier in the day, it's 4-hour, 1-hour. As you get into New York, you can adjust things slightly different."

rule: Once you're further into a continuation (e.g. candle 4), separation from the prior reversal level matters less, because price has already shown it can reverse there.
quote: "if we're in candle 4, Christ already showed me it can reverse there. It doesn't really matter as much anymore once you're further in the continuation."

rule: If Asia and London already expanded and price is consolidating, lower your expectations for the NY move.
quote: "if Asia and London expands, I mean, you gotta realize it's pretty, price is consolidating a little. Like, you can't have the largest expectations right away."

rule: Missing the first entry is not the end; later continuation entries are available, and waiting for them also tells you when you're wrong.
quote: "Because a lot of you guys think that if you miss that very first entry, it's over for you. It's not."

rule: If things are confusing, don't force a trade; some days and weeks are unclear, and that's normal.
quote: "If stuff's confusing, you don't have to force a trade onto it, right? You can be patient."

rule: Learn the model's foundation before adding tools like SMT, PSP or correlation.
quote: "It's just stop trying to add things when you don't actually understand the foundation."

rule: A bias you can't position for intraday isn't a trade; catching a move like GU would need a higher-timeframe position with a wider stop.
quote: "The bias is there, but unless I'm positioning on a higher timeframe, putting my stop lower, I'm not catching that intraday, personally."

rule: He watches several assets on synced side-by-side charts (NQ/ES/YM panes) to compare relative strength intraday.
quote: "We'll take a watch on all these assets at once, kind of intraday like that. Helps you see relative strength, relative weakness, all of that, right?"

rule: Going into the day, the previous day high (or low) is the main focus; after it is taken and price reverses, the first reversal target is the EQ.
quote: "previous day high is your main focus, right? So we do take out previous day high, trade lower. If you're going to trade this type of move, your target for your reversal, the first one is EQ."

rule: Don't trust a reversal away from (near-)equal highs; better to wait for the EQ and a closure, then trade back into those highs.
quote: "you just make perfectly equal highs here. So it's almost Better to wait for the EQ, we have a nice closure, and then trade back into those highs."

rule: Avoid trading internal to a consolidation; if forced, after an expansion into a low the consolidation favors a retracement the other way.
quote: "I don't really like to trade internal to these consolidations, but if I had to choose, we'd be going higher because expansion into low, new phase of price, which is consolidation."

rule: When you come into a day with no idea what's going on, that is the day not to trade.
quote: "hey, when do I not trade? Well, when you come into a day and you just have no idea what's going on, that's usually when."

rule: If you don't know the bias, wait; don't drop to lower timeframes to manufacture one.
quote: "If you don't know the bias, wait. Don't do any other stuff. If you don't know the bias, wait. It's quite simple."

rule: A continuation should close over the series of down-close candles immediately or within the next candle; if it takes many candles (eight in the example) it has become a consolidation, the later run of the high is manipulation, and expansion goes the other way.
quote: "Ideally, you'd want to see this go and just go close over here or in the next candle. What does it do? You have candle 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8. It takes eight candles to go close over. So what is this becoming? It then becomes a consolidation, right?"

rule: Continuations fail by running out short-term highs or by taking too long to form.
quote: "which we talk about either running out short-term highs or taking too long to form a continuation, right?"

rule: Once price is internal to the day's range after a target is taken, don't wait for a confirmation far away; set alerts on the range high and range low and decide only when one is reached.
quote: "I would just once again be waiting for this range high or this range low to make any sort of decisions."

rule: Trading a consolidation is lower probability and needs much more confirmation from the intraday profile: daily wick, then 4H candle 2 closure, then a 15m entry targeting the range high.
quote: "Once we form the daily wick, right, you can use a four-hour closure for this, right? Candle 2 closure there. And then you can trade the 15-minute here"

rule: He only trades a consolidation with his model plus the intraday profile to anticipate the wick, never by buying or selling quadrant levels (25%/75%).
quote: "The only way I will trade consolidation is still using my model and then intraday profile. I'd have to use the intraday profile to anticipate the wick and then trading it."

rule: Reversal target ladder for a large wick / large opposing run: daily open first, then intraday lows, then the previous day low.
quote: "this is a large wick. Your target's the daily open, intraday lows. Right, and then previous day low."

rule: Once the first target has been hit, the trade is much less interesting; he calls it a skip day.
quote: "I would be more interested in just this, but it already hit our first target, right? Does it make sense? Yeah, it's a skip day."

rule: Equal lows that have already been slightly swept are harder targets than clean failure swings.
quote: "there are equal lows, but you see how it sweeps it out slightly? That makes it a little bit harder to get to."

rule: Draws on liquidity should ideally be failure swings, not protected swings.
quote: "Ideally, you want to target failure swings, right? Like here, these are failure swings here. They make for a good target for the move down."

rule: If price expands without forming the daily wick, either skip it or enter positionally on candle 3, and only if a protected swing formed right before candle 3 opened (stop on that swing); you want immediate expansion.
quote: "Usually there's two options, right? You have one, don't trade it, you missed it. Two, positional entry."

rule: If it takes a while to form another protected swing after the move, it is becoming a consolidation, not an expansion.
quote: "you don't really want to see another protected swing just like... Take a minute to form, because now this is becoming a big consolidation"

rule: To frame a long after price runs over a previous high you need a new swing to trade away from; without one (and refusing a stop far below), no long is possible in his model.
quote: "is there any way I can frame a long over this high? No, because I don't trust anything and I'm not going to put my stop down here. And so I'd need a new swing."

rule: A previous-day-high raid that leaves failure swings is not inherently trusted as a full reversal move.
quote: "We take out previous day high. This sets up a short. We leave failure swings. So you don't inherently trust that as a full move."

rule: The direction you can frame comes from structure, not preference: if a long cannot be framed, the only idea is a short, but that does not mean shorts are a good trade.
quote: "It's not like, oh, shorts are the answer. It's just based off the structure."

rule: With highs taken and no SMT on the lows, he can only frame downside.
quote: "We've taken out highs. We have no SMT on the lows. So essentially, that's why I can only frame downside."

rule: When correlated indices decouple, deciding which one is lying is much easier with a strong daily bias; otherwise use phases of price and closures.
quote: "we've done this game before, which one's lying? Well, it's a lot easier when you have a strong daily bias."

rule: Leading/lagging asset = relative strength: the weakest asset leads to the downside, the strongest leads to the upside.
quote: "So that means to the downside, YM is leading. NQ is lagging."

rule: Daily bias comes from blending daily candle closures, phases of price, EQ and open-high-low-close.
quote: "You will use daily candle closures, phases of price, EQ, open high-low close, and blend those all together."

rule: Build the market narrative only from the daily chart.
quote: "everything I think is always just from the daily chart. That's it."

rule: Highest-probability setup: daily C3 with 4H C3 and a 15m entry (alternatives H1 with M5, M30); i.e. trade continuations in line with the bias.
quote: "It's really just trading continuations in line with a bias."

rule: Intraday model: daily bias (candle 2 closure), then an hourly CISD paired with a 4H candle 2 closure, then a 15m entry.
quote: "Hourly change in state of delivery, be paired with a 4-hour candle 2 closure, go into the 15-minute, and there you have a short setup. So get a daily bias, look for an intraday reversal,"

rule: In the overnight session never go below the 15m for entries; use hourly or 30m entries, targeting the lows or the ADR.
quote: "Then if you're trading overnight session, I never go below the 15. So hourly 30, hourly entries, continuation lower into the lows or the ADR, whatever you want."

rule: If London already made the move, he doesn't force New York.
quote: "I just don't really care for today because London had the move, right? It already made the move."

rule: A 10:00 continuation off an hourly gap needs either a small wick or a longer wick that forms a 15m swing point.
quote: "I could set up some sort of continuation at 10 a.m., that's the only thing. That would need to be, most likely, Either a small wick to trade higher in that, which then would form a 15-minute swing point, right? Or you have a longer wicked one, sets it up, and then that would also be a 15-minute."

rule: The weekly profile becomes readable later in the week; expansion away from the weekly open + no established low + SMT anticipates a midweek reversal with Thursday/Friday continuation, but if the target is already taken there is nothing left to trade.
quote: "We expand away from the weekly open, no established low, SMT here, right? Then you can anticipate midweek reversal, so Thursday continuation, Friday continuation. Problem is, Thursday took out the low already, so we have no targets for this."

rule: Whether price retraces or reverses is unknown in advance; the closures tell you.
quote: "How can you say when it needs to retrace or is it going to reverse? You don't know."

rule: Don't do dumb stuff: tilt, revenge trading, oversizing and not following the strategy; if you can't stop, quit trading or change.
quote: "Tilt, revenge trading, oversizing, and then not following strategy."

rule: Form your own bias before consuming anyone else's; trading is you vs the market.
quote: "So if you are Taking in other people's biases, stop doing that. Go trade. Don't consume any other content at the same time."

rule: For stocks he uses the daily and monthly fractal model.
quote: "I use the daily and monthly model, daily and monthly fractal model."

rule: The dotted lines drawn on his chart are the EQ.
quote: "Is the EQ the dotted line? Yeah, it's the dotted line."

rule: When the day has no established low (only failure swings, a drift higher that takes out a range high, no close below), read the daily profile as a range high taken to trade lower / back to the daily open, and do not frame longs.
quote: "This daily profile says back to the daily open, right, because, take a look at this, do we establish any sort of low? No, it's all failure swings."

rule: If you can only frame one direction, use relative strength across the correlated indices to choose the instrument: short the one with lower highs / bearish 4H candle 2, long the one with higher lows / bullish 4H candle 2.
quote: "that means if I can only look short I have to determine the relative strength"

rule: Mechanical targets are the previous higher-timeframe candle highs/lows (e.g. previous 4H lows), the daily open and the intraday low, taken in order as target 1, 2, 3.
quote: "Those are mechanical targets. Those are previous higher time frame candles to lows."

rule: After a sweep of a short-term high, a new continuation means failure to manipulate (bullish); no continuation means trade the other way; if you are still bullish, wait for the sweep and then a new continuation.
quote: "If it sweeps out a short-term high, I want to see a continuation, that's that failure to manipulate. Or if it doesn't have anything, you just trade the other way."

rule: Sweeping a high and failing to close back over the level is bearish, not bullish.
quote: "We just swept out this high. We couldn't close over this level. To me, that's bearish. It's not bullish."

rule: On an open-high daily profile the move up is a retracement until the high is taken out; a retest of the daily open is still bearish.
quote: "This is technically a retracement until this high gets taken out. So a retest of the daily open is still bearish."

rule: A reversal off the previous day high is traded back to the EQ of the range; that is why EQ is marked on everything in his indicator.
quote: "There's a reason I have on my indicator EQ marked out on everything. This is the trade there to there."

rule: Scalping-model template: a 1H expansion candle paired with a 15m swing point (execute 15m/1m); e.g. range high taken, trade range high to range low.
quote: "It's an hourly expansion candle paired with a 15-minute swing point with the anticipation that this was a range high over here."

rule: For a scalp off a higher-timeframe expansion you want to be in candle 3 or the beginning of candle 4; otherwise wait for a new phase of price.
quote: "You'd want to be in candle 3 or at the beginning of candle 4. Otherwise, you want to wait for a new phase of rise."

rule: The scalping model ideally uses a C3 or C4, but a C2 is acceptable (today's NQ move was technically a C2 traded on 15m-1m).
quote: "Ideally you want it to be a C3 or a C4, right? Or you can do a C2."

rule: Bias comes from candle closures.
quote: "Well, candle closures are essentially how I come up with any sort of bias, so yeah."

rule: Almost none of his bias or ideas come from low timeframes: the idea comes from the hourly (or higher) and is only executed on 15m/1m.
quote: "Almost none of my bias or ideas come from low timeframes. This one comes from the hourly chart."

rule: For a continuation lower, the next candle should open and respect the gap / EQ area, and the swing high must remain intact.
quote: "So ideally, you'd still want that high to remain if we're going to get a continuation lore, right?"

rule: Before a high-impact event (FOMC), expect little volatility; he does not scalp pre-FOMC, waits for the event for strong biases, and prefers to trade the day after FOMC rather than right after it.
quote: "I tend not to prefer, I'd like to trade the day after FOMC. I'm not a big fan of trading right after FOMC."

rule: Do not gamble on news releases.
quote: "Guys, I don't sit here and gamble on news events."

rule: Check ForexFactory filtered to USD for the week; know the volatility events (FOMC, elections, NFP); crude oil inventories matter for oil even as a yellow folder.
quote: "Those are like the things you have to know that's going on. And you can just do that at forxfactory.com."

rule: Trading makes sense when you have a strong daily bias; scalping a lower-timeframe idea without one is marginal.
quote: "Now imagine you apply this when you have a strong daily bias, that's when trading actually makes sense."

rule: Treat an NY-session reversal as a New York reversal even if London technically made the high, when SMT supports it.
quote: "So that is what you call a New York reversal. I'm treating it like a reversal, even though London technically makes the high."

rule: On a reversal day with a larger wick, expect price to hit the mechanical targets (intraday low) and then come back into range.
quote: "This is a reversal day, larger WIC, right? So with that, I'm expecting price to hit these targets and then come back into range."

rule: Once the mechanical targets for the opening move are hit, the idea is done; he does not sit through the following consolidation.
quote: "So those are the targets hit, right, for this move lower for me."

rule: If 2R does not fit within your targets, either adjust the entry or adjust the stop.
quote: "You can adjust where you're taking entry to get to 2R, or you can adjust your stop loss."

rule: Win rate is not the sole factor: at 1:1 you need over 50% (plus fees); with a 40% win rate, 1:2 is just above breakeven and 1:3 is quite profitable.
quote: "Because at 1-1R, you have to win 50% or more. And then you subtract out fees and stuff like that."

rule: There is no win rate for an indicator or model; results depend on the trader.
quote: "An indicator is not an algo. There's no win rate to it."

rule: Liquidity develops the bias; bias, liquidity, HTF, order flow and structure are used together, not ranked.
quote: "No, guys, liquidity develops your bias. Like, it all goes together."

rule: SMT is overused; ignore it inside consolidation.
quote: "I don't really care too much for it when it's in a consolidation like that. I think people overuse SMT."

rule: Don't pattern-trade FVGs/order blocks you see; only take the move you can frame from the bias (today only the short from the high to the targets).
quote: "I personally don't just like pattern trade stuff. So just because I see a fair value gap in here where I don't really know, I don't really care."

rule: Do not take longs off a low you don't trust (e.g. a low sitting at a gap after the other side was taken); if nothing long can be framed, be bearish only into that low, and only after it is hit consider bullish setups.
quote: "So if I can't frame anything long, my only option here is, oh, I could only be bearish into this low. Because once we hit this low, then you have the potential for something that is bullish."

rule: Swing points are confirmed by a change in the state of delivery (CISD), with intra-candle CISD as a refinement.
quote: "swing points, I confirm them with a change in the state of delivery."

rule: His model is built on swing points; price never reverses without forming a swing point, so the model does not need to change with market regimes.
quote: "My model is built off of swing points."

rule: When a daily level is respected at 0.5 (without a wick), an engulfing close is the candle-3 closure that sets up another continuation to the highs.
quote: "Well, we're respecting 0.5 without wick. So if we engulf here, that would be a candle 3 closure, and then we can get another continuation of the highs."

rule: After a level is disrespected, you usually want it to fail, i.e. expect price to trade through it to the draw on the other side.
quote: "Now that we've disrespected that, you usually want that level to fail, right? So up into there."

rule: A move after a reversal off a POI (gold off PDH) is a new phase of price: either consolidation or retracement.
quote: "Gold, like we were saying, is new phase of price. This is either consolidation or retracement."

rule: Prep order: daily candles and bias first, then wait for 09:30 to print before acting.
quote: "I look at the daily candles, I went through my bias with you guys, then we like went in, we said we're waiting for 930, 930 prints."

rule: Use one model only; focus instruments are gold, oil and indices, mainly indices intraday.
quote: "I focus on gold oil indices, right? Gold oil indices. But mainly just indices most of the time for intro day stuff."

rule: On a major scheduled event day (US elections), after a big new-month expansion, expect consolidation and keep intraday expectations low; the move comes after the event.
quote: "I would think we're gonna consolidate today, mostly, just because of elections, right? I think that's what the market is waiting on, and that can really impact it."

rule: TGIF = trading the counter-trend move from the weekly high back toward the close, after the week formed its low Monday/Tuesday and expanded through Thursday.
quote: "You need expansion through Thursday, and then you're trying to trade that move back in."

rule: Trade candle 3 and candle 4. Entering C3 after the candle has already expanded far without a strong closure is where you get consolidation.
quote: "If you're trying to trade this candle free open after we've already expanded, that's where you get consolidation."

rule: After a reversal and expansion, classify the next move: a reversal off the PDL, a consolidation, or (if it just moves back) a retracement.
quote: "Is this a reversal off previous day low? No. Is this a consolidation? No. This just starts to move higher. So that's a retracement."

rule: Once you have a bias, look for an intraday reversal; a lower-timeframe reversal needs a closure through the swing point to confirm it, otherwise it is a consolidation and the continuation fails.
quote: "We have no reversal, right? Because we don't get a closure through this confirming the swing point, right? And it's a consolidation."

rule: A candle 2 closure that forms after the intraday reversal is a continuation within the higher-timeframe trend and can be entered directly on the 1H (about 2R) without refining lower; refining is optional.
quote: "Now we have a continuation that has formed within this higher timeframe trend. Could you just enter on the hourly here?"

rule: A previous-day-high sweep is easier to trade back to the EQ when it has SMT; without SMT he passes on it.
quote: "It would have been a lot easier to trade, like, if this swept out previous day high, trading back to the EQ. And there's no SMT, so..."

rule: He does not use ICT macros; he respects economic news, not time macros.
quote: "I do not believe in ICT macros. I do not think they are real. I think they are made up. I do believe in economics."

rule: When the indices go opposite directions, you need a higher-timeframe bias or you must watch SMT and how each reacts; ES leading while NQ/YM diverge is unusual and usually means chop.
quote: "You need to have some sort of higher time frame bias, or you need to watch for SMT and see how they react."

rule: The 1H CISD/closure in the NY session can come from the 9am or the 10am hourly candle.
quote: "It's not one or the other, it's either or."

rule: If you don't know what the market is doing, don't trade.
quote: "Don't trade, stay out. Yeah, exactly."

rule: The market cannot reverse without forming a swing point, which is why a swing-point-based model keeps working.
quote: "The market cannot reverse without a swing point. So if market is going lower here, if it's going to reverse higher, it has to form a swing point."

rule: Mastering the daily chart means anticipating whether the day will be bullish or bearish and how the daily candle will form.
quote: "I mean go to the daily chart and really lock in on anticipating if the day is going to be bullish or bearish and then how it forms."

rule: If price opens, leaves failure swings, and trades too far below the EQ, the wick is too large to support expansion or a trend day. Once the profile targets are hit (daily open, intraday liquidity, PDH), stop looking in that direction; the only idea is back into the range.
quote: "Do we respect the EQ to have a potential trend day? No. We trade too low. So now this wick is too big to support expansion or a trend day, right?"

rule: Unswept highs/lows left as failure swings early in the day become targets for later.
quote: "Is there SMT here? No. So these are failure swings. That becomes a target for later."

rule: He uses the hourly and 4H to read the daily profile.
quote: "I'll use the hourly and the 4-hour for the daily profile."

rule: He doesn't trust a shallow sweep; he expects another run of that level, so the shallow sweep would need to fail first.
quote: "I don't really trust a shallow sweep like this, so a lot of times I'll be looking for another run of that, so you would have to basically fail this."

rule: Top-down process: daily bias, then an intraday reversal (a high or low of day to trade away from), then an aligned fractal-model entry.
quote: "Daily bias, intraday reversal, aligned fractal model. That's really what it comes down to."

rule: Failing funded accounts usually comes from tilt/revenge trading, oversizing, breaking strategy or rules, and no risk management; stop those behaviours instead of learning more.
quote: "So whatever you're doing here that you know you're doing is wrong, stop trying to learn your way out of it."

rule: At 2R, breakeven is about a 34% win rate; with fees, about 40% is breakeven-to-profitable. That's why he shows 2R, though he holds longer.
quote: "It's really 34%, but add fees and other things, right? So if you win four out of 10 trades, nice. You're break-even and making money."

rule: Bias comes from daily closures. Don't predict tomorrow's bias before today's daily candle closes.
quote: "Stop trying to predict your bias for tomorrow before today's even over."

rule: Don't trust a PD array (FVG/OB) to hold on a retracement; wait for it to form a protected swing.
quote: "Stop trying to just guess or predict it. Instead, wait for it to form a protected swing."

rule: Avoid trading before FOMC, NFP and CPI and trade after them; other red-folder news doesn't matter.
quote: "I avoid trading prior to FOMC, NFP, CPI, and then I can trade after."

rule: Gold SMT: compare GC with XAUEUR and XAUGBP, plus silver.
quote: "Gold, I'll use gold, gold euro, gold pound, and I'll also use silver with it."

rule: Use only the CISD level (candle body closing through the swing's body), not break of structure (the wick). A remaining wick beyond the body doesn't matter.
quote: "That's the CISD. For break a structure, they use this. I don't care about break a structure at all. I only use the CISD level."

rule: Don't force a trade on the weak asset just because you're bearish. For a reversal, wait for the strongest asset to run into its high, then frame the weakest asset in the reversal direction; otherwise there is no model.
quote: "For me, I would probably want, what, the strongest asset, which is ES, to go into the high to then, if it's going to reverse, frame the weakest asset, YM, lower, right? Otherwise, I just don't have anything."

rule: No kill zones; timing comes only from higher-timeframe candles (hourly and 4H, mainly 4H).
quote: "I don't use kill zones. So if you're asking for the kill zones on the gold, I don't use them. The only thing I use is higher timeframe candles."

rule: He separates a full top-down idea (daily bias + reversal + model) from an intraday-only idea based on the daily profile. On a neutral-bias day he can still take a profile-based counter-trend idea.
quote: "When I look at trading, I have like a full top-down idea, and then I have intraday idea, like based off profile, et cetera, right? Is this a full top-down idea? No."

rule: After price expands into its target (reversal candle with too large a wick), expect a retracement, reversal or consolidation, and trade it counter-trend.
quote: "So after we expand into a target, what am I expecting? Some sort of retracement, reversal, or consolidation. So this is counter trend, right?"

rule: SMT just means one asset's previous candle high/low was taken out and the other's wasn't; don't overthink it.
quote: "SMTs just look for previous candles high or low that didn't get taken out or did."

rule: For a continuation, price needs to either close over the level (strong close) or form a new swing point.
quote: "Ideally, one of two things. We get to close over this level, right, if we're going to just close strong, or we go and we form a new swing point."

rule: On a bullish continuation, the upper 50% of the leg (where the FVG sits) should hold; the weaker asset trading into it can be SMT if it then reverses.
quote: "What do you want to see? 50% of this be held. In the upper 50% there, we have a gap, right, fair value gap."

rule: If most of the higher-timeframe candle is already used, the most ideal setups form at the open of the next higher-timeframe candle: a price area (y-axis) plus a time area (x-axis).
quote: "Usually, when you have used most your candle, which we have, one's the most ideal to look for some sort of setup like this at the open of new higher time frame candles."

rule: Want the protected swing formed by the end of the current 15m candle, then the next candle to open and expand. He prefers waiting for that next candle over entering mid-candle.
quote: "Alright, so if we do go form a protected swing here, right, prior to the open of the next candle, generally then, you want to see this next candle open and just expand higher."

rule: Equal lows under a continuation are a red flag. A sweep of them is only acceptable if it is quick and aggressive both ways; otherwise the stop just sits on equal lows and the setup can't be framed.
quote: "If it's going to sweep, it needs to be really quick. It needs to be like aggressive down and then aggressive right back up."

rule: He can't trade away from failure swings. A swing formed just before the new HTF candle opens is suspect; one formed at the open of the new candle is tradable.
quote: "personally for me, guys, I can't trade away from failures, things like that. If it would have formed at the open of the new candle, I could make a case for it, but when it happens prior to the new candle, a little sus."

rule: A counter-trend move after a reversal candle starts a new phase of price; you don't know yet if it's a retracement, reversal or consolidation, so the first target is the retracement target that both outcomes share.
quote: "So this is a new phase of price move. And you don't know if it's going to be a reversal or a retracement, right? Or a consolidation even."

rule: Fear comes from trying to control the outcome; you control only risk. Expose yourself with tiny risk (e.g. 10% of the allowed drawdown), set and forget, max one trade a day, until losses stop mattering.
quote: "You're just going to risk 150, right? And just place trades, set it and forget it, max one a day."

rule: A stop loss limits losses; it isn't a judgement on your ego. Traders who refuse stops blow up.
quote: "Like the whole point of a stop loss, guys, is not like, oh, you're wrong, right? It's not here to like crap on your ego."

rule: Targets are the obvious swing lows/highs and failure swings; don't overthink them.
quote: "Let's just find the swing lows that are obvious. Don't overthink it."

rule: SMT is required for reversals but not for continuations; with good top-down analysis you don't need it.
quote: "If you have good top-down analysis, you don't need SMT. If you're trading a reversal, Sure, require it. If I'm trading a continuation, sure, I notice things, but I don't require it."

rule: Forex: never go below the 15m; in lower volatility use higher timeframes.
quote: "Forex, I don't go below the 15-minute ever."

rule: In a range with a bullish lean, wait for an actual sweep of the range lows and a move back in. If one index sweeps while the other leaves perfectly equal lows, don't trust it.
quote: "I don't really trust it. I'd want to see an actual sweep, but the only idea here would be sweep of range lows back into the range."

rule: If you don't have a bias, stay out.
quote: "If you don't have any bias, stay out."

rule: He does not use OTE, kill zones, option levels, break of structure or market structure shift; only HTF candles, swing points and CISD.
quote: "I don't personally use OTE."

rule: When bullish, trade and target the strongest asset; when bearish, the weakest asset.
quote: "if you're bullish, right, you want to be looking at the strongest assets for a target. If you're bearish, you want to use the weakest assets for a target."

rule: Read relative strength from where each index's 4H candle is versus its open (above = strong, below = weak).
quote: "Just look at the 4-hour candle, right? What is it doing? It's down here below its open. What is why I'm doing? It's up there. So clearly the strongest, right?"

rule: Relative strength can rotate once one asset hits its target; re-rank after targets are taken.
quote: "ES hits target, allows the strength to switch around. So initially, NQ is the strongest. That switches. It's the weakest now."

rule: An expansion candle (small wick, large body, high/low formed early) closes into its extreme, so the higher-timeframe candle close is a valid target: 9:30 15m candle to 9:45, 30m and 4H to 10:00.
quote: "Why would you target 9.45? This is an expansion candle. Expansion candles close into their highs. So right here, you can just hold it till 9.45."

rule: Expansion candle definition: small wick, large body, closes near its high or low, and forms its high or low early in the candle using very little time or range.
quote: "An expansion candle has a small wick, a large body. Look, it closes near its high or closes near its low, right? Price forms the high or low early into the candle, using very little time or range, leaving enough time for expansion."

rule: With no clear liquidity target (e.g. price already beyond the daily range), use time-based exits at higher-timeframe candle closes/opens; it works on every timeframe (monthly expansion trade exits at month end).
quote: "If you don't know, if you don't have a target for expansion, you use higher timeframe, candles, flows in time, and basically opens."

rule: After the expansion candle closes, partial or exit at its close; you do not know whether it continues, retraces, reverses or consolidates.
quote: "You don't know now, is this going to continue to expand? That would align with the higher timeframes, but this could also retrace or reverse or consolidate."

rule: A candle that disrespects the EQ with a weak close can still be tolerated as a small wick, but once the wick grows too large the targets revert toward the HTF candle's open; wait for the next candle (or a candle-4 continuation) instead of entering.
quote: "We're already kind of disrespecting the EQ because we have a weaker closure here, and we didn't close into the highs. So I'm allowing it to trade a little bit lower and still considering that a small wick."

rule: If the current candle does not support expansion in your direction, do not trade it; wait for the next higher-timeframe candle.
quote: "But you see how this candle doesn't support expansion higher, so there's no reason to try to trade it, right? You're better off waiting for the next candle"

rule: Trade continuations because they require the market to confirm; when the idea is wrong no continuation forms, so you are wrong without taking a loss.
quote: "But there's no entry whatsoever because when you wait for a continuation to form, you're waiting for the market to tell you that it's doing something. When it doesn't do something, that's fine. You just are wrong and you didn't take a loss, right?"

rule: Do not fade a strong expansion / daily range; if the 4H is still aligned, nothing is bearish until that 4H candle closes (10:00).
quote: "Because, like I said, don't try to fade. Just don't trade this. Like, if you already miss this move, either sit out or you're, this is still aligned bullish, right? The 4-hour? There's nothing bearish here. Not in, at least not until 10 a.m."

rule: An SMT reversal idea whose CISD takes too long to form, and that sweeps the low instead, is a consolidation that trades to the other side of the range, not a reversal.
quote: "Even if you're looking to trade this lower with the SMT, look how long we take to form the CISD. We don't, and we sweep out the low. So now this is a consolidation to trade to the other side of the range."

rule: Invalidation trade: if a valid model fails to work, price goes the other way.
quote: "We have a valid model. Does it work? Nope. Does it work? Nope. Okay, cool. If this valid model doesn't work, price goes the other way. That's it."

rule: The model trades candle 3 and 4 (sometimes candle 2); after three candles of expansion expect a new phase of price and do not look for a candle-5 continuation.
quote: "So that's why we look to trade candle 3 and 4 or sometimes candle 2. But after we get three candles or expansion or three candles of movement, we can get a new phase of price."

rule: Do not enter late after a huge range has already been made (entering after ~2,800 points of range and C2-C3-C4 expansion is entering candle 5).
quote: "I personally wouldn't have been really looking long at 10AM for myself, just because we've already expanded, we've had a massive range"

rule: The wick should form inside the higher-timeframe box (T-spot), ideally near the HTF candle's open, which gives low risk and high probability of expansion.
quote: "If the wick forms near the opening price of the higher timeframe candle, it would be a low risk and high probability to expand."

rule: Size risk per trade from the drawdown and the number of consecutive losses you want to survive (7-10), never from the nominal account size.
quote: "Account size does not matter at all. It's arbitrary. Use the drawdown on it."

rule: A wider stop is handled by reducing position size, not by taking more risk.
quote: "You should be adjusting your position size to account for the movement in"

rule: Normally one trade a day maximum.
quote: "In terms of risk management, I just take one trade a day normally max."

rule: If continuation trades keep stopping you out before reaching target, move the entry up one timeframe (e.g. 5m to 15m), because the stop is likely inside a higher-timeframe FVG.
quote: "So if you're on the five-minute, you're always getting stopped out, then it goes to your entry. Most likely there's like a 15-minute fair value gap you always get stopped at in. So just go to the 15-minute chart and enter on that."

rule: With several markets, get the idea from the hourly or 4H first and only then drop to lower timeframes.
quote: "So stop trying to go down to the 5-minute on all your assets you watch instead of waiting for an hourly or 4-hour to give you an idea, then going lower."

rule: Direction comes from the daily chart.
quote: "Go to the daily chart. Everything should be based off the daily chart."

rule: For candle-3 entries he prefers an intra-candle CISD; positional entries on an FVG/OB are an acceptable alternative.
quote: "I personally prefer intra-candle change in the state of delivery, but you can also take positional entries, that type of stuff."

rule: In the scalping model a 5-minute CISD confirming the 1-hour is ideal but not required.
quote: "You don't need it, but it is ideal."

rule: CISD = find the low, find the series of candles that made it, and check for a close over it; a protected swing is one that went into a POI and closed over, so it is expected to hold if price continues.
quote: "Then we check for the change in the state delivery, right? Which is find a low, find a series of candles that made it, did it close over?"

rule: Swing trading uses the daily-hourly pairing; his intraday layout pairs 15m-4H (also 1m-15m on gold, 3m-30m alerts).
quote: "When I'm looking to swing trade, I'm usually using the daily and hourly model."

rule: After a deep retracement that invalidates the EQ, the continuation idea no longer meets the model; it only revives if price invalidates the EQ, forms a higher low and then a continuation.
quote: "There's either that idea or we invalidate the EQ, form of the higher low, and the continuation. We'll probably just hop off of it because there's really not much to do when it gets that deep of a retracement."

rule: When two paths are alive (reversal vs retracement-then-continuation), do nothing and wait for price to show its phase.
quote: "Like, do we form a reversal, right? Or do we kind of retrace to then set up for the continuation that way, you know? I don't really know what's going on, so we just wait."

rule: A sequence of continuations ending in an expansion with its failure swings hit means the move is 'tapped out': expect consolidation, retracement or a new phase of price rather than fading it.
quote: "So gold is pretty much Tapped out for me. If you notice all these failure swings right here, it gets hit."

rule: Equal highs taken by only one correlated asset are not trusted.
quote: "And one asset took it out, but I don't really trust it. We have equal highs right here, right?"

rule: He prefers trend-aligned trades; counter-trend trades and trading the invalidation of bias are not his preference.
quote: "I don't prefer to take counter trend trades, so up to you."

rule: Use futures, not CFDs, so candle closes are identical across platforms.
quote: "Like these are going to close the same on everything because it's futures."

rule: PSP is on his indicator but he does not really use it; at most extra confluence.
quote: "I don't really use PSP. It's just on my indicator. Like, sure, it can give extra confluence, but I don't really use it."

rule: Once indices have expanded 9:30-10:00 and started consolidating, there is nothing left to do unless already in a position and trailing.
quote: "Can it continue higher? Sure. Hopefully it does, but I mean, there's not much to do anymore on it unless you're in a position and you're trailing it."

rule: An asset that has already hit all its targets is the weakest on a bullish day; skip it.
quote: "Russell looks weak. The weakest asset on a bullish day. Because it hit all its targets."

rule: Use ADR by eye (average of recent candles) to judge whether range is left; no ADR indicator.
quote: "To me, looking at kind of the average of the last candles, this looks like a good amount of range, so I wouldn't say there's much left."

rule: Expansion into a low followed by a C2 closure and C3 (expansion into expansion) reads as a reversal by phases of price; a continuation then needs either a consolidation day swept the next day or a day that respects the previous day's range.
quote: "This is expansion amount with expansion, so phases of price-wise, this is saying reversal."

rule: A Friday reversal is what lets you trade a Monday continuation.
quote: "Oil, I also went over Friday reversal. That's when you can trade a Monday continuation."

rule: An unbalanced price range is where a previous high and a previous low do not overlap and price has only ever moved one way through it; it is a continuation target.
quote: "it's just where you have a previous high and a previous low that doesn't overlap. Price in this area here has only ever gone up, it's never gone back lower."

rule: After a reversal off the previous month's low and an expansion with no POI in the way, stay bullish while the current week's (Tuesday) low holds.
quote: "reversal off the previous month's low, expansion, there's no point of interest, so as long as we can hold this Tuesday low, I'll be bullish into these highs."

rule: Do not long the strongest asset until the weakest asset has formed a reversal off its level; that reversal creates the SMT.
quote: "So weakest asset not forming a reversal, which means do not long the strongest asset yet, right?"

rule: If the weakest asset keeps falling, the other indices usually follow and take out their lows too.
quote: "If it continues lower, then usually it means that ES is also going to go take out this low."

rule: Do not predict right around the 9:30 open unless there is 15m structure; after an expansion at the open, wait until 10:00 for it to sort itself out.
quote: "I'm not a huge fan of predicting this right around the open unless there is some sort of 15-minute structure."

rule: Trading against the current 4H candle is fighting every timeframe; prefer the continuation over the reversal.
quote: "You're fighting the 4-hour candle, you're fighting all the timeframes if you're trying to trade this reversal."

rule: Lower-timeframe stops get slipped on news (a -1R can become -3R); only hold through news when the stop is far enough away, e.g. hourly-timeframe trades.
quote: "So that's why it's a big difference from trading news, you know, on a lower timeframe versus will I hold through CPI or news events on an hourly timeframe? Sure, because I'm not going to get slipped"

rule: Do not trade right before red-folder news (CPI, NFP, FOMC); let the release happen, then trade.
quote: "CPI, NFP, FOMC, just don't trade right before it."

rule: Swing/intraweek trades use the same model on daily and hourly: the entry is when the indicator prints the entry-candle CISD.
quote: "So when it prints my indicator, the entry candle change in the state of delivery, there's a trade."

rule: Discipline: max one trade a day, follow your rules and model, no tilt or revenge trading; if you cannot change, quit trading.
quote: "Best way to go about that is max one trade a day."

rule: Daily profile is read mainly on the 4H and hourly.
quote: "For daily profile, I mainly use the 4-hour and hourly."

rule: For an upside idea after a bearish 4H expansion: the 4H candle forms its wick and closes back up as a reversal, then the next 4H respects that wick, forms its lower wick and goes higher.
quote: "So you want to see this 4-hour forming a wick, and then what do you want to see? You want to see the next 4-hour candle respect the wick to form its lower wick and then go higher."

rule: If the 4H/1H/15m candles are bearish and your idea is up, wait for a small green wick on the next candle (e.g. 10:00) instead of fighting them.
quote: "So if you have an upside idea, it's normally best to wait for a small wick that is green to trade it to the upside instead of trying to fight it."

rule: There will be times you don't know what's going on; wait instead of forcing a trade.
quote: "there's going to be times in the market where you just don't know what's going on, and you just have to wait."

rule: Timeframe alignment: identify a low all the timeframes should form, then trade a fractal model in line with them.
quote: "you want to make sure you find a low that all of these should form, right? And then you want to trade a fractal model in line with all of that."

rule: After the weakest asset reverses at 10:00, trade the asset with the most range left to the target (ES here), unless trading a 1m continuation on the stronger one.
quote: "Usually here, it's what, we have a little range left on NQ. Usually the best chance then is yes, because there's more range left."

rule: When holding, read phases of price: if price blasts through you can hold for the other index's target; if it consolidates, the laggard is catching up and the leader usually stalls.
quote: "If we blast through, then you can just hold it, right, till ES reaches for it?"

rule: A large-wick reversal candle has three targets: the opening price, intraday liquidity around the open, and the previous day high/low.
quote: "You have three. You have daily open, intraday liquidity, and you have previous day high, previous day low."

rule: The strongest index often hits a target and consolidates while the weaker one becomes stronger.
quote: "A lot of times your strongest one will hit something, consolidate. Well, then this one gets stronger."

rule: Positional entry is only valid when a protected swing exists before the open of the new higher-timeframe candle.
quote: "positional entry is a tool, but it occurs when you have a protected swing prior to the open of the new higher timeframe candle."

rule: Do not trade the first swing low of a turn; wait for the higher low to form its wick, then trade it.
quote: "So what I do is I don't trade that swing low because people try to trade the swing low there, there, there, there, there to take all the losses. I then wait for a higher low and then I look to take that."

rule: On a C2 closure, to keep trending inside the higher-timeframe candle price must respect the EQ and print an intra-candle CISD (close over) on the entry timeframe; without it there is no setup.
quote: "So if it's going to respect and trade higher in this one-minute candle, it would need to do what? Respect the EQ here."

rule: Markets are fractal: the same model applies on daily/hourly, hourly/5m, 5m/15s.
quote: "So what you do on the daily, it's the same as what you do on the hourly. What you do on the hourly, it's the same as what you do on the 5-minute."

rule: A continuation that takes too long becomes a consolidation; then look for a run of the consolidation low before the move resumes.
quote: "Took too long. Took too long. So it's a consolidation. So what do you want to see? Run of the low. Go higher."

rule: Predict only the next candle, never a chain of candles.
quote: "I try to predict this next one, or if this one closes, the next one, right?"

rule: Order of a lower-timeframe reversal: inversion (IFVG) first, then CISD.
quote: "You want to see the order of reversal, right? We have inversion first, then we have CISD."

rule: If the continuation doesn't come in one go, wait for a new swing point, normally on the 15m, while keeping the target (PDH / overnight highs); don't fade it.
quote: "We're just gonna sit here and wait until we find a new swing point, right? Which is normally 15 minutes."

rule: Taking a closure-over entry while the current candle is bearish is a reversal on a reversal - not ideal.
quote: "This would be a reversal type entry. It's not ideal because, what, this candle is bearish, right? So you'd be trading essentially a reversal and a reversal, not as ideal."

rule: Align with the higher-timeframe candle: don't long away from a failure swing inside a bearish daily candle that has already expanded; only after the low is taken can you trade a retracement back into the range.
