quote: "This is what I mean is I want to align with the higher time frame candle. This is a bearish, right here, bearish daily candle."

rule: You cannot frame a counter-bias trade just because price hits a pattern (e.g. an FVG); you need targets taken and SMT at the extreme.
quote: "Like, guys, I can't just take a pattern and be like, oh, it's hitting a fair value gap. I'm going to short."

rule: A reversal candle usually forms its reversal midway through; if it hasn't by late in the candle, it is too late - wait for the next candle.
quote: "Now we're a bit late into this candle. Usually if it's a reversal candle, it forms it midway through. Now it's too late, so now you just kind of wait for 10.30."

rule: Generally it is better to just sit on the 15m than watch lower timeframes.
quote: "Generally speaking, it's better just sit on the 15-minute"

rule: Ideal entry timing: a V-shape reversal, then the next candle forms its lower wick as a continuation and goes higher.
quote: "We need some sort of V-shape reversal, and then you come into the next candle, have a continuation that forms the lower wick, and then can go higher."

rule: Do not trade deep retracement continuations; a retracement that goes all the way back flips the read to the other side.
quote: "I've learned that you just don't fight the trend and the easiest way to do that is don't trade deep retracements."

rule: Bullish idea with a bearish expansion candle: the reversal must come off the previous low with a small wick; if it goes too deep, wait for the next 15m/30m candle.
quote: "If we are bullish and we have a bearish expansion candle, right? What do we think about? The reversal has to occur off this previous low."

rule: To form a C2 the previous candle's low must be taken and the gap must hold: close, open, reversal, continuation; not much deeper than that area.
quote: "So it'd be price closes there, opens up, reversal, continuation. That's if we're forming a C2."

rule: Late in the candle there are only three acceptable scenarios: immediate expansion over (continuation), sweep the low then go, or sweep with a larger wick and wait for the next candle.
quote: "There's now three options. One, it immediately expands over, forms a continuation. Two, sweeps out the low, then goes. Three, sweeps out the low with a larger wick. Waits for the next candle to go."

rule: When retesting a CISD level he prefers price to form a swing (sweep the previous candle's low) rather than close straight over, because a direct close leaves lower-timeframe failure swings.
quote: "One tip, when we're retesting a CISD level, I'm a big fan of forming a swing here."

rule: After a CISD, 50% of the CISD candle bodies should be respected for a clean trend in that candle.
quote: "Well, if we have a change in the state of delivery, we want to see 50% of the bodies be respected."

rule: Candle 2 reverses, candle 3 must expand; if C3 doesn't expand, you were wrong.
quote: "You want to see candle 3 expand, right? Candle 2 reversal, candle 3 expand. It doesn't do that, which just tells me, hey, you were pretty much wrong."

rule: After a 9:30 expansion, the ideal is a quick-wick continuation at 10:00, not a deep retracement.
quote: "Usually, though, when you have a 9.30 expansion, you want to see just 10 a.m. form a quick wick continuation."

rule: If the candle has used most of its time without the setup, repeat the idea: let it become candle 1 for the next setup.
quote: "We've already used most of the time in this candle, so what would you do? You'd repeat the same idea, right? This is a candle. I'd want to see that become a candle 1"

rule: To short against the day's idea you need the strongest asset to reverse off the highs; the cleanest days let you trade the strongest up into the highs, then the weakest back down.
quote: "If I wanted to train the downside, I would want to see the strongest asset reverse off these highs."

rule: Bias is invalidated only by (1) price invalidating the EQ or (2) a reversal off the previous day high; changing bias needs a reason.
quote: "For me to invalidate my bias, I need to have, what, an invalidation of the EQ, so basically price would have had to invalidate it, right, to trade lower, or a reversal off that previous day high."

rule: Currencies are choppy on low timeframes: trade them on the hourly, never below 15m intraday.
quote: "If I'm trading currencies intraday, I don't go below a 15-minute timeframe, personally."

rule: If you don't trade reversals, a reversal day is a no-trade day: wait for the next day to form something.
quote: "Guys, I don't trade the reversal, so I'm not going to be trading. I don't really care what it does in this day anymore, right?"

rule: After a 4H candle-2 closure from a POI, if the 15m does not close below the swing, expect that 15m high to be taken; the only valid short is a sweep of that high without taking out the C2 high, then a new continuation.
quote: "Now you essentially want to see, this is the only option, a sweep of that high without taking out this high."

rule: Waiting for the sweep/new continuation lets the higher-timeframe candle form its opposing wick (open to high) before it flips and expands.
quote: "Because you're letting the wick form On this higher time frame candle, right, that move up, open high, forms the wick, now it's flipping bearish, and now it can expand lower"

rule: Time-based exit: if you are in the HTF expansion candle, you can hold the trade until the new HTF candle opens (gold 4H: 10:00 ET); the expansion candle usually closes near its extreme, so you exit close to the low without getting the exact low.
quote: "The reason for that is when you have this expansion candle, it generally closes near its lows. So you can hold towards the end of the time period, which is at 10 a.m."

rule: With a time-based exit you capture the body of the higher-timeframe candle; it is Larry Williams' hold-to-the-close applied fractally.
quote: "If you trade an expansion candle and you hold to the close, right? That's what Larry Williams says. Now do it fractally."

rule: Take profit when the target is hit and the timeframe has already expanded (entry high in the dealing range, target the range low) - or hold to the HTF close.
quote: "So this is a great spot to take profit as what? We have already expanded on this time frame. We've already hit our target from the high, right?"

rule: Targets must justify the entry timeframe: a 15m entry needs a farther target than a nearby 1H low; only a refined 1m entry makes that near target worth 3R.
quote: "But if you're trading on a higher timeframe, no, I would not be taking profit right there because it does not give me good enough risk to reward."

rule: Do not trade the weakest/lagging asset; trade the strongest or the middle one. If the strongest asset is not reversing, do not short the weaker one.
quote: "You can trade the middle one or the strongest one. Stop trading the lagging one. That's where you get chopped, right?"

rule: A short in the weaker index needs confirmation that the strongest one (NQ) reaches the gap/level first; otherwise the move is weak.
quote: "NQ is the strongest, so you generally want to see it reach into this gap right here. Otherwise it's just really weak"

rule: If the bias stays the same through a consolidation or a failed continuation, a PM-session reversal sets up an Asia/opening continuation in the bias direction.
quote: "when we consolidate or fail to form a continuation, right, and the bias remains the same, which it does, and we form a reversal in PM, PM session reversal that's for an Asia or an opening setup continuation higher"

rule: Do not fight the higher (monthly) candle: a daily continuation against an unaligned monthly candle and with a gap in the way is at most a scalp.
quote: "And you are fighting the monthly candle, right? So monthly candle is not aligned with that, so it's a little bit harder, generally speaking."

rule: When the market expands right off the New York open there is little to do unless a clean continuation forms off that expansion.
quote: "It's just there's not really much to do around New York session when you have a day like this because we just expand right off the open."

rule: After a deep retracement, do not enter at a poor R:R; wait for the closure through and then a new continuation, and near the end of the HTF candle often wait for the next candle to open.
quote: "And the one main thing here is we're right at the end of this higher timeframe candle, so a lot of times I want to wait for the open of the new one"

rule: A level-sweep reversal needs an aggressive rejection; price that hits the level and just consolidates is not a setup (that aggressive reaction is when inversions make sense).
quote: "You want to see price hit that level, and you want to see it aggressively come off that level, right? That's where inversions can make sense, right?"

rule: For a new 15m candle to be the high and go lower, it must open, take out the previous 15m high, CISD, and go lower; the previous 15m high area must hold or the downside is invalidated.
quote: "So for this candle to open, make a high, and go lower, it'd have to open, take out the previous high, CISD, go lower."

rule: If a reversal takes too long it becomes a reversal candle; a continuation forming at the end of the HTF candle needs the next candle to expand as candle 3 without returning to the high.
quote: "So if we are going to trade lower, we don't want to see this high returned to. We want to see this next candle expand lower as a candle 3."

rule: A continuation is invalid if price closes back over the level or reaches for the high; taking out a protected swing (especially leaving equal lows) means it usually fails and makes a new high.
quote: "We don't want to see it go take out a protected swing, especially leaving equal lows."

rule: A swing point is confirmed when it becomes a protected swing: price closes over the series of opposite-closed candles that made it (wick-only does not count).
quote: "So it needs to close over the series of down closed candles that made it. So once it closes over, Now you have confirmed this low as a protected swing, right?"

rule: No close through the level = no protected swing, so no entry from it.
quote: "price never closed below this level so this is not a protected swing"

rule: Find the swing point first, then look for the CISD; do not hunt random CISDs.
quote: "You look for a swing point first, then you go look for the CISD. Stop just trying to randomly look for CISD."

rule: CISD is always defined by the series of candles, never a single candle, so it stays mechanical.
quote: "That's why I always use the series no matter what. I need it mechanical."

rule: Swing points used for the model come from candle-2 closures and candle-3 closures.
quote: "we have candle 2 closure and we have candle 3 closure so those are the two that would be used"

rule: XC2 = a candle-2 closure that later failed (got taken out); the indicator keeps the label rather than repainting. C2s with equal highs sitting above them are low probability.
quote: "This means it failed."

rule: If your stop keeps getting hit before price goes to target, check for a higher-timeframe FVG at your stop; wait for price to reach into it, then trade away from it.
quote: "Do you have a higher time frame fair value gap at your stop loss? If so, wait for it to reach into that, then look to trade it away."

rule: If limited to one alignment: daily + hourly fractal (daily C3 closure, 1H fractal, 1H IC-CISD); his preferred entry pairing is 4H with 15m.
quote: "I prefer the 4-hour and 15 for entries, right, like this."

rule: The model is daily bias, then an intraday reversal, then an aligned fractal model - normally three or four timeframes.
quote: "Generally speaking, it's daily bias, intraday reversal, aligned fractal model."

rule: On the NQ intraday idea he works 15m closure or 1m continuation (1m-15m model) after the open.
quote: "So the whole idea is 15-minute closure or one-minute continuation, right?"

rule: Use the real HTF candle open/close times (10:00, 9:30 NYSE open) instead of ICT macros; entering in the last minutes of a candle is illogical, the first minutes of a new HTF candle would be logical.
quote: "So use this time level, 10 a.m."

rule: When Friday forms a C2 or a reversal, Monday can be traded; bank holidays can also be clean.
quote: "When Friday forms a C2 or a reversal, you can trade Mondays."

rule: Fundamentals are irrelevant on intraday (15m) charts and only matter for yearly/monthly-scale trades.
quote: "Now, if we're trading the yearly chart with monthly time frame and A daily entry? Sure, I'll probably care about what the economy and stuff is doing."

rule: Trade only what meets your system's requirements; skip markets with choppy intraday structure (CL) and focus on the cleanest asset (gold today).
quote: "Because you have to realize when you have a system, there's just going to be times where you're like, I do not care about this."

rule: Risk management (not blowing up, not going on tilt) is the number-one skill; flipping direction after each stop-out is gambling.
quote: "Probably risk management, not blowing up your account, not going on tilt, probably the number one strategy, number one thing you need."

rule: Follow the trade plan to its target; don't close early out of fear - emotions exist, they just must not drive decisions.
quote: "You can follow your plan and not let your emotions dictate your decisions, right?"

rule: After a large expansion, expect consolidation rather than an immediate breakdown; a consolidation takes its low, then its high, then the low again.
quote: "Probably a little bit of a consolidation. Sometimes it can really break down, but normally it's consolidation."

rule: He prefers continuations over reversals.
quote: "I don't really like reversal trading, so then I want continuations."

rule: He does not scalp choppy intraday structure; prefers trading a trend.
quote: "This is why I don't really scalp. Like, these are annoying to try to trade."

rule: Trade IFVGs together with higher-timeframe candles.
quote: "I explain how to actually trade IFVGs. With higher timeframe candles."

rule: He marks out targets with dotted lines, hand-draws the projected path on each index pane, and uses the position tool to show stop/target/R:R.
quote: "That's why I was saying, I marked that out and then marked that out. Make it dotted."

rule: Draw a dealing range from the entry high to the target low; an entry high in the range means the range low is the target.
quote: "Taking an entry high into the dealing range, now this is your target, right?"

rule: Low resistance liquidity: a high not swept by the next leg before the reversal, so liquidity still rests there.
quote: "it has that high, does not get swept, thus there is more resting liquidity there. This is defined as low resistance liquidity."

rule: High resistance liquidity: the leg sweeps the resting liquidity before reversing; no failure swing.
quote: "high resistance liquidity does not have a failure swing and price sweeps the liquidity before reversing."

rule: LRL is simply a high or low with a failure swing.
quote: "low resistance liquidity is just a high or low with a failure swing"

rule: Before the trading session, mark LRL as the target; price expands through it more easily than through HRL.
quote: "Prior to the session that I am trading, I will look for low resistance liquidity as a target"

rule: For a bearish continuation, want a reach back into premium of the range and a bearish PD array (FVG).
quote: "I want to see price reach back up into a premium of the range."

rule: Failure-swing highs inside the premium can be taken first; then a close back into the range turns the target to sell-side liquidity.
quote: "price went up, took out this high, closing back into the range, I would want to see sell side liquidity taken now."

rule: Among stacked lows, the LRL is the priority target, with further lows beyond as an extension.
quote: "most importantly, this low resistance liquidity resting right in here."

rule: A new low that is not taken out on the retracement is a failure swing (LRL) for the next leg.
quote: "price put in a low and then could not take that low out. So this is our low resistance liquidity or failure swing."

rule: Sequence: FVG reaction, then the LRL below, then the larger draw on liquidity.
quote: "I would expect price to go for the fair value gap and then reach for The low resistance liquidity below and ultimately to our draw on liquidity below."

rule: Consecutive daily candles where no previous day high is broken = a zone of LRL (failure swings on lower timeframes).
quote: "no previous day high was ever taken out for multiple consecutive days."

rule: Once price starts breaking through such a zone, expect it to continue and expand in that direction.
quote: "we expect price, if it starts to break through these highs, to Continue through them and expand in that direction."

rule: A failure to close out of the range after taking PDH turns order flow bearish.
quote: "as we get a failure to close out of the range, we take a previous day high and fall back in and order flow becomes bearish."

rule: A swept low with closes back into the range is HRL, not a failure swing.
quote: "it's not a failure swing, so this becomes high resistance liquidity."

rule: When targeting a HRL low, target the failure swing above it or the CE of its wick instead.
quote: "this is generally when I want to look for the failure swing above it or using the CE of the WIC."

rule: HRL lows are harder to break through than LRL; avoid targeting them directly.
quote: "this is going to be a lot harder to break through than this low resistance liquidity right here."

rule: A move up and back into a consolidation range is the manipulation; expect expansion to the target.
quote: "with this move up and back into the range, this is our manipulation."

rule: Check the 1m for failure swings that make a lower target worth taking even without an old low.
quote: "these are all failure swings, and what does that create? Low resistance liquidity."

rule: Exit at the failure swing / equal lows rather than holding for HRL; it saves time.
quote: "I would rather save myself the time and just exit my position at this failure swing and equal low than holding to reach for that high resistance liquidity."

rule: Once price returns to the HTF POI (FVG / BPR), look for a lower-timeframe entry model there.
quote: "So once we return to this fair value gap, then we are looking for a lower timeframe entry."

rule: If NQ fails to take lows that ES takes, NQ is stronger; trade the stronger index for longs.
quote: "NASDAQ couldn't take these lows, while ES did take these lows, right? So to me, that pointed out that NASDAQ was a little bit stronger."

rule: Long on the 1m displacement candle, risk the low, target nearby highs rather than the farther London highs.
quote: "I looked for NAS long here and risk this low, right? And then I was targeting these highs here. I didn't shoot for London highs"

rule: A lower timeframe model at a higher timeframe POI is the method.
quote: "That is essentially a lower timeframe model at a higher timeframe point of interest."

rule: With bullish bias, expect a move lower into an OTE / FVG first, then watch the lower timeframe.
quote: "So we expect a move lower to then go higher. So we get a move down into an OTE into a fair value gap."

rule: At the POI, wait for displacement or some lower timeframe model before entering.
quote: "You want to wait for displacement or some lower timeframe model."

rule: Draw the OTE fib from where the displacement started to where it ended.
quote: "Now what you want to do is draw out your OTE from where your displacement already started to where it ended."

rule: Look for a PD array (e.g. an order block) in the discount of that displacement range for longs.
quote: "You want to look for some PD array down here in a discount."

rule: A missed entry is no problem: the next displacement range gives another discount entry.
quote: "And now let's say you missed this entry here. Well, you don't need to worry about that because you can look for another entry."

rule: Prefer the retracement entry after internal liquidity below is swept.
quote: "we now also have internal liquidity resting right here. So we want to see a move below there to then go higher."

rule: No displacement below structure after the sweep supports the long.
quote: "You can tell we don't get any displacement below this structure. Now, that would be your long entry, right?"

rule: Repeat the displacement-range / discount entry until the HTF objective (previous highs) is reached.
quote: "And you can just keep doing this until you reach your objective, right?"

rule: Lower timeframes show you when your bias is wrong.
quote: "So this is a good example of how you can know when you're wrong using lower timeframes, right?"

rule: Do not short just because price is above highs; wait for a model.
quote: "I don't just short when we're above those highs. I wait for a model, right?"

rule: A short model needs displacement below structure (break the 1m low with displacement).
quote: "So now we'd have to break below this low with displacement to go lower, right?"

rule: Still inside an OTE with a big FVG below: unless strong displacement breaks the low, expect continuation higher.
quote: "So unless we get a lot of displacement below that low, we're likely to continue higher."

rule: Raid of stops without a close/displacement below and no FVGs means likely continuation higher.
quote: "We can't close or displace below there. No fair value gaps, right? So this is what I mean by rating stops"

rule: A failure to displace lower is a reason to go long.
quote: "I actually longed right in here, right? And that's because failure to displace lower popped up."

rule: 15s scalps against the bias are riskier; he took a small OTE short, left some at break-even.
quote: "what I did was on a 15 second timeframe, it's a little more risky"

rule: Aggressive down then aggressive up (a box / BPR) switched him to bullish.
quote: "aggressive down, aggressive up. Does that remind you of the box or BPR, right? Then we go up. This was what switched me to bullish."

rule: Even with the wrong bias, structure-based entries with partials and break-even limit damage and let you switch bias.
quote: "So you can see, even if you have the wrong bias, you can still get decent entries."

rule: Do not short a pullback on the higher timeframe when there is no lower-timeframe break of structure.
quote: "on 15 second chart, there's no reason to try to short this, right? There's not even a break of structure on the 15 second"

rule: Expect a low to be taken (small broadening formation) before continuation higher.
quote: "But what you have to notice is we're likely to take some sort of low before continuing higher, right?"

rule: Use structure and follow your rules even when your bias is wrong.
quote: "If you get it wrong and you just use structure, follow your rules, you'll still be in some profitable trades"

rule: After a sweep of an old low and an expansion lower, classify the next move: expansion back into the range = reversal, shallow retracement = continuation, or consolidation.
quote: "do we have a shallow retracement which then I would look for a continuation lower"

rule: A V-shaped recovery with aggressive expansion higher is a reversal, setting a bullish bias.
quote: "we get a nice v-shaped recovery with an aggressive expansion higher so I'm viewing this as a reversal"

rule: When bullish and price consolidates, wait for the range low (external low) to be taken before buying.
quote: "if I am bullish and I have a consolidation range I would prefer to see the external low or the low of the range get taken out to then trade higher"

rule: Target the failure swings (equal highs) on the HTF range.
quote: "we have those failure swings on the highs so that would be my target"

rule: On the hourly, an aggressive move up that closes over the series of down-close candles that formed the low makes that low expected to hold before the highs are run.
quote: "we also close over the series of down Clos candles that formed this low"

rule: After that close, price should not trade much below 0.5 of the bodies of the opposing candle (order block).
quote: "with an opposing candle or an order block I don't want to see price trade much lower or to.5 of the bodies of this candle"

rule: If a later down-close candle into an FVG is not closed over, the low stays exposed to being run.
quote: "since we cannot close over that level that leaves this low still exposed to being ran out"

rule: A run of that low while still respecting 0.5 of the opposing candle is expected to form a swing low for the move higher.
quote: "if we run out a low and are still respecting 05 of this opposing candle I can then expect this to form a swing low"

rule: His trade: longs below the swept low, targeting the highs.
quote: "So within my trade I took Longs below this low targeting these highs up here"

rule: A close back over the down-close candle validates the low as protected.
quote: "we get a closure over this down Clos candle so that is then validating this as a protected low"

rule: Bias comes from the daily chart and the phases of price delivery.
quote: "my whole bias was set by using the daily chart and the phases of price delivery"

rule: In a consolidation, wait for the side of the range opposing your bias to be run (lows if bullish, highs if bearish).
quote: "if I'm bullish I want to wait for the lows to be ran out if I am bearish I want to wait for the highs to be ran out"

rule: Then wait for structure on the intermediate timeframe (here 1h) to give validated lows.
quote: "I then wait for some structure to develop on my intermediate time frame or in this case the hourly"

rule: The run of the consolidation low is the manipulation leg of accumulation-manipulation-distribution.
quote: "the manipulation in this accumulation manipulation and distribution"

rule: Displacement is an aggressive move with full-bodied candles, single or multiple.
quote: "Displacement is an aggressive move with full-bodied candles."

rule: The easiest way to spot displacement is the fair value gaps it leaves.
quote: "Is just looking for fair value gaps."

rule: Lower-timeframe displacement legs appear as a single candle on a higher timeframe.
quote: "Now on a higher timeframe, these would result in a single candle."

rule: Follow the latest displacement for order flow until it is invalidated by an opposite aggressive close over the FVG.
quote: "aggressive down comes after, so we're looking lower"

rule: A market structure shift indicates a change of trend, identified by displacement below a previous low (or above a previous high).
quote: "We look for displacement below a previous low, or if it is bullish, above a previous high."

rule: Prefer a stop raid before the shift; it creates a breaker and high resistance liquidity for the stop loss.
quote: "I also prefer to have a stop rate. Prior to this, which also creates a breaker formation and creates high resistance liquidity for a stop loss."

rule: Most important: price must engage a higher-timeframe level before shifting; otherwise no setup.
quote: "The most important thing I look for in a market structure shift is if price engaged a higher timeframe level prior to shifting structure."

rule: A move below the low without aggression is not a break of structure.
quote: "Not really a break of structure for me because we did not aggressively move below this low."

rule: A sweep that does not close over the high is a better sweep.
quote: "this is a better sweep for me just because we don't close over that high."

rule: The shift is where price starts closing and aggressively moving below the low with full-bodied candles.
quote: "our structure shift is when we start closing and aggressively moving below this low."

rule: After the MSS, look for a setup: FVG within a breaker, with OTE from a fib of the displacement leg as confluence.
quote: "We have a fair value gap setup right here, as well as a breaker block."

rule: Candle bodies should respect the breaker and FVG after the entry.
quote: "you can see how the bodies respect the breaker block and fair value gap."

rule: After the shift in the London-to-New York session, target London / overnight lows.
quote: "We'd want to see London lows taken."

rule: At a higher-timeframe level, do not think long until displacement closes over the high.
quote: "I would not be thinking long yet until we get this placement over this high."

rule: After the MSS, focus on the displacement range and its premium/discount; want a PD array in discount (longs).
quote: "I am focused on this displacement range. So from here, I can look at our discount and premium."

rule: A daily raid into a daily FVG then a close over the high = daily MSS; then look for a discount PD array.
quote: "If we are going to shift structure, we would need to break this high right here and close over it."

rule: Summary: HTF level engaged, sweep of a high/low, close over structure (MSS), then a setup on that timeframe.
quote: "price to sweep a low or a high before closing over structure, making our market structure shift, and then looking for a setup on that timeframe."

rule: MSS is a change in trend: displacement over or below a swing high or swing low.
quote: "a market structure shift is a change in trend. So it is when we shift from bullish to bearish or from bearish to bullish"

rule: Bearish MSS sequence: swing low formed, liquidity swept, then displacement and a close below the swing low.
quote: "We sweep liquidity, and then we get displacement and a close below this swing low, shifting structure."

rule: CISD is a close and displacement below the opening price of the up-close candle(s) that ran into an important level, validating them as an order block.
quote: "it is focused on the close and displacement below the opening price of this up close or series of up close candles into an important level, validating it as an order block"

rule: CISD happens before (or at the same candle as) the MSS.
quote: "You can see the change in the state of delivery happens prior to the market structure shift."

rule: Bullish CISD: close over the down-close candle; bullish MSS: displacement and close over the swing high.
quote: "If looking for the change in the state of delivery, I want to see price closing over this downclose candle."

rule: After CISD validates the order block, look for a retest of the order block before continuation.
quote: "You can see we retest the order block before moving higher."

rule: After a bearish CISD alone, bias shifts bearish toward the old low even before structure shifts.
quote: "So just using the change in the state of delivery, we have now shifted to bearish and looking for this old low over here."

rule: CISD entry: once the close below the opening price prints, look for a short at the order block retest with stop on the high.
quote: "I will look to take an entry right when it retests the order block, my stop on the high, and then at my target"

rule: If the order block retest gives poor R:R (e.g. 1.1), use an FVG or the order block's 0.5 / mean threshold as the entry instead.
quote: "Find the 0.5 or mean threshold of the order block and use that as an entry as well."

rule: MSS may give no entry if price never retraces after the shift.
quote: "Now with this market structure shift, price never retraces and I would have never gotten an entry."

rule: Benefit of CISD: an earlier entry than MSS.
quote: "The one benefit of using the change in the state of delivery is it can provide an earlier entry to market structure shifts."

rule: Cost of CISD: the earlier entry can be a loser where MSS never confirms and structure stays bullish.
quote: "it may get you into a position that ends up to be a loser, where if I was looking for a market structure shift here, we never got displacement"

rule: Inversions also signal a change in order flow.
quote: "they can also be used to signify a change in order flow"

rule: Three ways order flow changes: inversion (close below bullish FVG), CISD (close below up-close series), MSS (close below swing low).
quote: "the three ways we are looking for order flow to change is an inversion"

rule: For an inversion he waits for a full close through the FVG, not just a close past its 50%.
quote: "you could consider this inversion, but I prefer to wait for a full closure below"

rule: Inversion and CISD occur earlier than MSS and are used to get in before the expansion move.
quote: "And generally that is used to get in prior to the expansion move."

rule: With an MSS, look for a retracement to a premium (short) or discount (long) array for entry.
quote: "When you [with a] market structure shift, you're looking for a retracement to a premium or discount array to get short or long."

rule: Which signal to use depends on what you see best; he prefers order blocks; backtest for yourself.
quote: "I personally prefer to use order blocks, however I know people that use inversions and those that just use market structure shifts as well."

rule: Displacement is a large aggressive move, one or several candles, that closes over structure.
quote: "Displacement is a large aggressive move."

rule: The key displacement candle is the large one that creates a fair value gap.
quote: "my focus goes to this large candle that creates a fair value gap as our displacement candle"

rule: Market structure shift = a sweep, then displacement candle(s) closing beyond structure, shifting trend.
quote: "When we get a sweep, and then that large displacement candle or candles closing below structure, shifting the trend from bullish to bearish."

rule: Liquidity grab = failure to displace over structure (reach over, close back in).
quote: "A liquidity grab, simply put, is a failure to displace over structure."

rule: After a failure to displace on one side, look for strong displacement over the opposite extreme for continuation that way.
quote: "right here we get a strong aggressive move closing over this previous high and we are likely to continue higher"

rule: At an old high/low, expect one of three outcomes: displace out-retrace-continue; displace out-displace back in-reverse; or fail to displace and come back in.
quote: "Those are the three things that I look for when price returns to an old high or low."

rule: If price cannot close/displace out of the range at the old level, expect a return into the range or the opposite side.
quote: "you can see price cannot close or displace out of this range. This leads me to believe that we're going to fall back into the range or head lower"

rule: When a fair value gap is disrespected (traded through), look to the next opposite old low/high as the draw.
quote: "where did my eyes draw to that we've disrespected this fair value gap? This low down here."

rule: Before going the other way, he wants price to return to at least premium (for shorts) or discount (for longs) of the range.
quote: "I want to see price return to at least a premium or a discount of the range if we are going to go lower"

rule: After displacement out, a shallow retrace with no displacement back in means continuation.
quote: "the retracement, very shallow, don't really get any displacement back in, so we're likely to continue lower"

rule: After displacement out, displacement back into the range means reversal toward the other side.
quote: "aggressive out, aggressive back in, likely to reverse here"

rule: Respected order blocks / FVGs (bullish or bearish PD arrays) confirm the side; a respected PD array supports continuation.
quote: "Once again, respecting these bullish PD arrays."

rule: No reversal call until there is displacement back the other way (full-bodied candles).
quote: "now I don't think reversal until we get some sort of displacement back up"

rule: A weak close over an old high is not enough; continuation needs aggressive candles like prior displacement.
quote: "If we are going to continue higher, I want to see aggressive candles like we did here and here."

rule: After a target extreme is reached, the next draw is the opposite old highs/lows, found by looking left.
quote: "So from here, I'd be looking left. What do we have to our left? We have lows right here."

rule: On low timeframes there are too many breaks and failures; trade only in the direction of a directional bias.
quote: "that is why I think it is important to have some sort of directional bias"

rule: Bearish: look for displacement down and failure to displace up to go short; bullish: the mirror.
quote: "I'm looking for displacement down and a failure to displace up to position myself short"

rule: Daily bias: find daily swing highs/lows and check whether price fails to displace or displaces out of that range.
quote: "I find swing points in the market, so a swing high or a swing low, and then I look to see if price fails to displace or displaces out of that range"

rule: On the daily, a closure/displacement out of a swing high range means price continues out of the range.
quote: "We get a closure outside this, or displacement out, and price reaches and continues out of this range."

rule: A wick is a lower-timeframe reversal: an aggressive move during that candle's period that came back.
quote: "Wicks are generally a lower time frame reversal where during a given time period price had an aggressive reaction"

rule: Mark 0.5 of the wick, measured from the body to the low (lower wick) or body to the high (upper wick).
quote: "the main focus for Wix is marking out 0.5 of this Wick from the body to the low or the body to the high"

rule: Bullish: the upper half of a lower wick should support price; bearish: the lower half of an upper wick should cap price.
quote: "I'm going to want to see the upper half of the wick support price higher or the lower half of the wick support price lower"

rule: A respected bullish wick produces next-candle sequence open -> low (inside upper half of wick) -> high -> close; bearish mirror open -> high -> low -> close.
quote: "I'd want to see price trade into this area open form a low then move higher and then close"

rule: If price trades through 50% of the wick, it is likely to trade through the wick extreme (the low for a lower wick).
quote: "if the upper half of this Wick is not respected then it is likely to trade to this low"

rule: Setup context: the candle takes out the previous low (high) and closes back into the range, giving a bullish (bearish) next-day bias.
quote: "price takes out the low and closes back into the range"

rule: The close back inside the PDH plus a CISD on the hourly strengthens the bearish case; then require a high formed in the lower half of the wick.
quote: "that is paired with a change in the state of delivery"

rule: Hourly wick into a FVG: on 5m expect open -> low -> high -> close without going below 50% of the wick for expansion.
quote: "I'd want to see an open low high close while not going below 50% of this Wick"

rule: Once the LTF closes over 50% of an upper wick (bearish idea), expect a run of the wick high instead, especially if the previous candle low was already taken.
quote: "it is more likely to reach for this High than go and respect this Wick"

rule: A close over 50% of the wick that also inverts a FVG makes the wick high the likely target; use the inversion as support.
quote: "closing over 50% of this Wick and inverting this fair value Gap"

rule: Wick setups inside a consolidation are lower probability.
quote: "with the context of we're in a consolidation that makes it lower probability"

rule: If price falls through 50% of a lower wick early in the next candle, an expansion candle is unlikely (it would leave too large a wick); expect the low to be taken.
quote: "this would form too large of a wick for an expansion candle"

rule: A good expansion candle lacks a wick on the open side; if it lacks one, price may revisit (form that wick) later.
quote: "we do lack an upper Wick so we may revisit that"

rule: If the LTF closes over the wick 50% against your idea, either skip the reversal or wait for a confirming close back below.
quote: "I'm either not going to try to catch this reversal up here or wait for more confirmation with a close below here"

rule: Entry on the confirming close, stop on the high, target 2R.
quote: "look to enter on the close my stop on this high and then targeting to R"

rule: The 50% rule is not perfect: price can close over it and still expand, or respect it and run the wick late in the candle; add or reduce confirmation based on LTF.
quote: "there are going to be times when price closes over this level and it still expands lower"

rule: Pairing: daily wick -> hourly execution; hourly wick -> 5m execution.
quote: none

rule: Start from an important level: a PD array or buy-side / sell-side liquidity.
quote: "the first thing I start with is an important level, whether this is a PD array or buy side liquidity"

rule: On the lower timeframe, price puts in a swing near the level and then raids it.
quote: "On a lower timeframe, price reaches up and puts in a swing high. Price then reaches up and rates [raids] this high here."

rule: The order block is the up-close candle or series of up-close candles that made the raid (bearish case).
quote: "My eyes go to this up-close candle, or series of up-close candles here."

rule: A close below that up-close candle validates the order block, which should then support price lower; mirror for down-close candles.
quote: "When price closes below this up-close candle, it then validates this order block, and I'm looking for it to support price lower."

rule: Bullish: when price closes over the down-close candle that swept the lows into the level, expect it to support price higher.
quote: "When price closes over this down close candle, I'm looking for it to support price higher."

rule: The opening price of the order block is the reference level for support.
quote: "Now I'm going to be looking at the opening price of this order block."

rule: The candle closing outside (beyond) the order block's opening price on the retest keeps it valid.
quote: "It's important to notice the close is outside the opening price of the order block."

rule: A full-bodied candle into the POI that is later closed through is a preferred order block.
quote: "We get a nice full bodied up close candle into this point of interest. So if we close below it, I would like to see it become an order block."

rule: Overlapping PD arrays (FVG and order block lined up) strengthen the level.
quote: "Now we have overlapping PD arrays as we have a fair value gap and an order block lined up."

rule: After displacement out of the order block, look to the opposite buy-side / sell-side liquidity as the draw.
quote: "Price reaches into this order block, gets displacement out. So now my eyes are drawn to where? These areas of buy side liquidity."

rule: A daily swing low is a valid important level for a 5m reversal.
quote: "we have our daily level or important level here, which is sell-side liquidity from the daily chart here."

rule: He prefers a full-bodied candle into the level; weak displacement off the level is not his preferred look.
quote: "I prefer a nice full-bodied candle down into this low"

rule: A lower-timeframe sweep with a full-bodied candle, then displacement and a close over the high, sets up the order block.
quote: "So I want to see if price can displace and close over this high."

rule: Wicks may pierce the order block on the retest; bodies must respect it.
quote: "You notice the wicks reach into there, the body is still respecting this down close candle."

rule: Sequence: engage an HTF level, displace and close over the series (or single) candle, then it acts as support.
quote: "After engaging with a higher timeframe level, we get displacement and closure over the series, or in this case, the singular down close candle."

rule: On the weekly, up-close candles that swept highs and were then closed below form an order block POI for the lower timeframe.
quote: "these up close candles on the move up that swept the highs before closing back below them is what? An order block."

rule: Ideally the close below the up-close candles also breaks the nearby swing low.
quote: "let's see if we can close below these up close candles and ideally this low here."

rule: Project the manipulation leg; expect 2-2.5 standard deviations, then the 4th.
quote: "Generally, I'd like to see a move towards this 2 to 2.5 standard deviation area, and then eventually to this fourth standard deviation area."

rule: The close below the order block series is treated as the market structure shift.
quote: "So we get that close below, so that's our market structure shift"

rule: A retracement at the first standard deviation can come back to the order block before continuation.
quote: "We just hit our first standard deviation, which is where we got a retracement last time."

rule: Overlapping projections from successive manipulation legs mark the target area.
quote: "you can see how these two standard deviation projections are kind of overlapping."

rule: Reversal = price takes out the previous candle's high or low and closes back inside the previous candle's range; anticipate the following candle to continue in the reversal direction.
quote: "I focus on price taking out its previous candle high or low and then closing back into the range"

rule: Continuation = price takes out the previous candle's high/low and closes outside it; anticipate the next candle to continue that way.
quote: "with a continuation I am anticipating price not to reverse as it took out its previous candle low and closed outside"

rule: When two reads conflict (e.g. swing high swept but candle closed above the prior candle's high), wait for another candle before taking a bias.
quote: "one of those is telling us bearish while the other is telling us bullish so with this I will wait for another candle"

rule: A bearish candle that does not close beyond the prior candle's high/low does not set a new bias.
quote: "with this candle we do have a nice bearish candle but we have not closed over our previous high or low"

rule: After about 3 candles of expansion in one direction, expect a new phase (retracement, consolidation or reversal).
quote: "we have had 3 days of expansion lower which generally indicates we can enter a new phase of price being retracement consolidation or reversal"

rule: An inside bar gives no information; let another candle form.
quote: "here we have an inside bar it does not give us any more information so we let another candle form"

rule: A reversal is stronger when the candle reaches into a POI (FVG) and closes its body beyond the opposing candle (order block) while closing back inside the prior range.
quote: "on this candle we reach into a point of Interest with this fair value Gap we're also closing the body below this opposing candle or this order block"

rule: Blend the model with the phases of price delivery; do not mechanically short every sweep of a high inside a bullish trend.
quote: "that is why is important to blend with the phases of price delivery right as we go through an expansion I can then anticipate a new phase"

rule: A sweep of a low in a bullish trend (trading to the other side of the range) works better than shorting the top of the range.
quote: "if I was always trying to short the top of this range in a bullish trend it's not going to work as well as a sweep of a low in a bullish Trend"

rule: When the candle closes over the prior day high but not over the swing point, a strong close tips the bias in its direction.
quote: "if I had to choose I would be bullish because of this strong closure in candle"

rule: Confirm the daily bias on the lower timeframe with a CISD from the high (or low) that made the reversal.
quote: "I would Mark out this change in the state of delivery here from the high and that gives me my confirmation to this bias"

rule: A series of candles reaching into an opposing candle then closing beyond it forms a propulsion block; he wants price to respect its lower half (for shorts).
quote: "this is now a propulsion block and I would like to see price respect the lower half of this"

rule: Simple execution: enter at the open (or when the open high forms), stop on the invalidation high, target 2R.
quote: "if I was to just enter at the open put my stop on that high and then Target 2 R"

rule: He waits for higher-timeframe candle closures for direction rather than trading intraday volatility.
quote: "that's why I personally wait for the closures of the higher time frame candle to give me direction"

rule: Expansion into consolidation: look for a manipulation against the expected direction to get on side; if no manipulation comes, price may just continue.
quote: "we have expansion into a consolidation so I would look to see if we can have some sort of manipulation lower to get on side with a move higher"

rule: A candle that fails to close outside the prior range after expansion is read as a retracement (continuation pending), and is a place to add to the position.
quote: "if this closes bullish I'm anticipating this to be a retracement to continue higher and not a reversal"

rule: The model is fractal: the same daily rules apply on the hourly (and lower) chart.
quote: "similar to my fractal model that I teach this is a fractal concept so it can be used on all time frames"

rule: Daily profile mirrors the weekly profile: if the day trades higher off the open without forming a low, expect a return to the daily open or the lows.
quote: "it's the same with the intraday profile or the daily profile looking to trade back to our daily open or the lows"

rule: On 5m, the CISD level is the series that made the high; enter when price closes through it, stop on the high, target 2R.
quote: "I would use this as my change in the state of delivery as this is the series or the move that made the high"

rule: Nothing works 100% of the time; a mechanical reversal read can fail once before the move.
quote: "it already has failed once and that is because nothing always works 100% of the time"

rule: Model components: skip Mondays, New York session only, execute on the 15m, economic calendar as roadmap, trade the day after the HTF level hits.
quote: "This model includes skipping Mondays, focusing on the New York session only, executing on the 15 minute chart, using the economic calendar as your roadmap"

rule: Trade the day after your anticipated higher-timeframe level is hit.
quote: "and trading the day after your anticipated higher timeframe levels hit."

rule: On the daily, mark the HTF level price should react from and the draw on liquidity (e.g. a daily FVG on each side).
quote: "we have this daily fair value gap as our draw on liquidity, as noted here, and then we have a daily fair value gap above."

rule: After a good reaction off the daily level on day N, look for day N+1 to continue toward the draw.
quote: "after we get a nice reaction off of this daily level, I'm looking for Wednesday to continue lower, taking the sell side liquidity"

rule: On the hourly, mark the arrays formed by the reaction (hourly breaker, hourly FVG) for the next day's retrace.
quote: "As we reach into Wednesday, price retraces back up into this hourly breaker, hourly fair value gap here, and moves away."

rule: 15m execution: in New York, price reaches into a 15m FVG (its consequent encroachment) before delivering to the target.
quote: "we have a 15-minute fair value gap here, price reaches up, Into the consequent encroachment of this before delivering to the weekly open"

rule: Restatement: skip Monday, wait for the HTF level, then next day look for the New York 15m setup.
quote: "skipping Monday, looking for when price reaches into that higher timeframe level, looking the next day for the New York session 15 minutes set up to deliver price."

rule: A daily close that tests and respects a daily OB sets up next-day shorts in New York.
quote: "Thursday comes up, tests the daily level with this closure, it's respecting it, so going into Friday expecting to find short setups during the New York session."

rule: Note SMT at the highs in the hourly FVG plus sell stops below as the draw.
quote: "the important thing to note is the SMT at the highs here in this hourly fair value gap, as well as the sell stops resting below"

rule: A news wick through the FVG is fine if bodies respect it.
quote: "With the news, getting this wick up, however, the bodies are respecting this fair value gap, displacement down,"

rule: Equal highs on the daily are a future target; bullish structure means expect a bullish week.
quote: "we just put in equal highs. So that would be a target for the future. We have bullish structure. And so I'm expecting this week to be bullish."

rule: On a bullish week expect open, low, high, close.
quote: "Now on a bullish week, I'd want to see an open, low, high, close."

rule: Stacked lows and a candle with no wick are targets.
quote: "We have some nice lows stacked right there, as well as a candle with no wick, which I like to target."

rule: Monday taking the previous day (Friday) high and closing back into the range sets up a next-day move toward the draw.
quote: "Monday took previous day's high, or Friday's high, closed back into the range. A next day move towards my draw on liquidity down here."

rule: When the 15m candle closes and leaves an FVG inside the hourly FVG, want price to reach into it at the open, then move to the draw.
quote: "ideally, I'd like to see during open price reach up into here, and then make a move towards our drawn liquidity down here."

rule: When the draw is hit and the daily closes back into the range, expect expansion the other way toward the opposite liquidity.
quote: "We came back in and closed back into the range. So now what can we expect for Wednesday, Thursday, or until we reach this high? We can expect expansion up"

rule: Run of the previous week high and close back into range: expect the next day to reach for lows.
quote: "we took buy side liquidity and closed back into the range. So with this, we can expect next day to reach for lows."

rule: If no New York setup appears, move to the next day and look for continuation.
quote: "Tuesday we do get a move down, but no setup for New York session, so I'm going to look for Wednesday to have a continuation lower"

rule: Mark midnight open on the hourly; a raid above midnight open then displacement down leaves the 15m FVG entry.
quote: "when we went above midnight open, we displaced down, and we have a fair value gap right here, price respects."

rule: An inside bar that does not reach the HTF PD array is not the trigger; wait for the day that reaches it.
quote: "You can see we stay inside bar and do not reach our higher timeframe PD array. Tuesday, we do end up reaching into that PD array"

rule: If the first 15m entry is missed, look for others (old high used as resistance).
quote: "However, if we miss this one, we can still look for other entries."

rule: Bullish week variant: open, low put in, then expansion higher into old highs and Friday's high before the high and close.
quote: "if I'm expecting a bullish week, I'd want to see an open low put in before expansion higher up into these highs and as well as Friday's high"

rule: Classic Tuesday low week: after Tuesday respects the OB mean threshold, Wednesday should expand to Friday's high.
quote: "So if we're going to get expansion in a classic Tuesday low a week, I'd want to see Wednesday expand towards Friday's high"

rule: No bodies closing below midnight open on the retest supports the long.
quote: "And if you notice how no bodies close below midnight here."

rule: Write a weekly plan on Sunday/Monday night from the economic calendar, the HTF (weekly/daily) draw on liquidity and the expected weekly candle direction.
quote: "in that plan I asked myself what are we reaching for on the higher time frame charts such as the weekly and the daily"

rule: Monday is no-trade or very low risk; Monday with no news is a low-probability day ("false moves of the week").
quote: "a lot of times I don't trade uh Mondays and if I do it's very low risk"

rule: A day with no news is low probability, but index futures still get 9:30 open volatility, so an A+ setup can still be taken.
quote: "one thing about New York session and trading Futures is you always got 9:30 open"

rule: Wednesday and Thursday are usually the best days because most of the weekly range is set then; after a Wed/Thu trade, skip Friday or trade it with light risk.
quote: "majority of the weekly range is being set within those two days sometimes on Friday"

rule: Trade Friday only if the HTF draw on liquidity for the week has not been met.
quote: "if the higher time frame draw on the quity for the week hasn't been met then I'll trade Friday"

rule: Cross-check ES, YM, NQ with DXY and bonds: bonds correlate with indices, DXY is inverse to indices and bonds; bonds are extra confluence, not required.
quote: "bonds correlate with indices and dxy are inversely correlated with indices and bonds"

rule: Trapped order flow (price between an unclosed-through HTF FVG above and below, e.g. weekly or daily FVG plus breaker) is a low-probability condition; do not trade, wait for a close above or below.
quote: "this is a low probability condition and this also goes with indecision on daily bias"

rule: SMT means nothing without displacement in the expected order-flow direction.
quote: "smt smt means no nothing at all if there's no displacement"

rule: Inside a consolidation, trade its range extremes: buy the lows, sell the highs.
quote: "how do you trade Within consolidations you want to trade the highs and lows of it"

rule: Trade only the NY AM killzone 9:00-11:30; if not in a trade by 11:00 stop, if in a trade hold to about 11:30-12:00.
quote: "I am a New York am Killzone Trader so my times are from 9: to 11:30"

rule: During the session watch only 1h/4h until price tags a clear POI (high/low, FVG, volume imbalance, sometimes NWOG on Monday) in line with daily bias or draw on liquidity.
quote: "I'm watching the 1 hour or the 4our chart waiting for price to tag a clear point of interest"

rule: Mark at most one or two POIs pre-session and ignore levels against your bias.
quote: "it could just be one or two things sometimes it's no more than two things"

rule: If no POI is tagged, do not drop to 5m or 15m at all (prevents impulsive trades).
quote: "if price doesn't tag that point of Interest or another throughout the session no need to drop to a 5 minute or 15-minute chart"

rule: Pair timeframes: 1h POI -> 5m execution (main), 4h POI -> 15m execution (rare), and for 1m execution require both a 4h POI and a 15m displacement/FVG.
quote: "you should have two intermediate time frames to kind of work with"

rule: After the POI tag, wait for a short-term stop run (preferably of a consolidation or Asia range high/low, market-maker-model style).
quote: "then from there I'm waiting for some sort of shortterm stop run"

rule: Low-probability sessions: Monday without news, day before CPI/NFP, NY AM before a 2pm FOMC, London taking both Asia high and low aggressively, Powell speech, HTF level already met before the session (common on Fridays).
quote: "if the London session is overextended and takes both highs and lows of the Asia range aggressively probably going be a low probability session"

rule: First/last day of month or quarter: still tradable but be more selective and risk less (manipulation, power of three).
quote: "it just means that I need to be more selective with my setup and I need to maybe risk less"

rule: Execute on the stronger pair when long / weaker when short; limit order at the top or bottom of the breaker.
quote: "I'm setting my limits at the top or the bottom of the break breaker"

rule: Stop at the top/bottom of the FVG candle or of the breaker; rarely at the swing low because it hurts R:R.
quote: "I rarely ever set it at the swing low because that just screws up the risk of reward"

rule: Take 80% off at 2R and the rest at 3R (sometimes all at 2R; occasionally move to breakeven after 2R and hold a runner to e.g. equal highs).
quote: "80% off at 2 to one and then the rest off at 3 to one"

rule: Do not change bias because of the day's profile; stick to the higher timeframe.
quote: "I don't change my bias based off like what the daily profile did"

rule: Use limit orders at the M5/M1 retest because price moves too fast for market entries.
quote: "by the M5 I try to set limits as as much as I can"

rule: Trade against the weekly plan only after a clear daily shift with a clear draw, e.g. an HTF (daily/weekly/4h) PD array invalidated.
quote: "as long as we had a clear shift on The Daily and the draw on the quity is is clear"

rule: Daily bias = obvious market-structure shifts + intermarket (indices, dollar, bonds) + clear displacement; with no displacement, wait for price to tip its hand.
quote: "I look for just obvious shifts in Market structure I combine IPA dollar bonds"

rule: Take 0-3 trades per week; after two winners stop for the week.
quote: "for me it's between zero to three per week"

rule: Journal every trade (chart markup, feelings before/during/after, what went well/badly) and write post-session thoughts after every session, traded or not.
quote: "for post session thoughts I do this like after every session no matter whether or not I took a trade"

rule: External range liquidity (ERL) = old highs and lows; internal range liquidity (IRL) = fair value gaps.
quote: "external range liquidity is just old highs and lows and internal range liquidity is fair value gaps"

rule: Price only does two things: draws to old highs/lows, and rebalances imbalances.
quote: "price only does these two things. It draws to old highs and lows, and it rebalances and imbalance"

rule: When IRL is tagged, expect price to draw to ERL next, and vice versa (ERL taken → draw to IRL).
quote: "if internal range liquidity is tagged, that is an indication for price to then draw to external range liquidity"

rule: Apply the ERL/IRL relationship on monthly, weekly, daily and 4H to form daily bias.
quote: "use this understanding of price on the monthly, the weekly, the daily, and the four hour, and that's going to be your key to finding your daily bias"

rule: Build bias by looking for market structure shifts off higher-timeframe key levels; a key level is an ERL or IRL.
quote: "you want to look for market structure shifts off of higher timeframe key levels"

rule: Timeframe pairs (key level → shift timeframe): monthly→daily, weekly→4H, daily→1H, 4H→M15, 1H→M5, M15→M1.
quote: "four hour to the M15, hourly to the M5, and M15 to the M1"

rule: Look for SMT divergence when price runs a higher-timeframe key level; it is the extra confluence for the shift.
quote: "that will be your extra confluence booster when you're looking for that correlated timeframe to identify a market structure shift"

rule: Bullish shift = a close above a swing high after the key level reaction; then wait for a retrace into a breaker block or FVG to enter.
quote: "We wait for price to retrace into that either breaker block or we can look for a fair value gap"

rule: Fractal: the lower-timeframe swing high that gets closed through is itself ERL, so next expect a retrace into a lower-timeframe IRL FVG.
quote: "price running a one hour swing high, that swing high is external range liquidity"

rule: An IRL FVG that lines up with a breaker block, plus SMT at the higher-timeframe low, is a high-probability entry.
quote: "if that internal range hourly fair value gap lines up with a breaker block, that would be labeled to me as a high probability entry"

rule: In the buy model the draw is a higher-timeframe IRL FVG lying in premium of the range from the swing low that took the ERL to the last energetic swing high.
quote: "the fair value gap or the internal range liquidity pool to be lying in premium of the range from swing low"

rule: Order blocks / up-close candles "on the sell side of the curve" act as mitigation blocks where PD arrays form (reaccumulation).
quote: "Up close candles on the sell side of the curve, they're used as mitigations."

rule: A close above the last down-close candle that took the liquidity is the change in state of delivery and marks a bullish order block.
quote: "we had price close above the last down close candle that took out the liquidity. This would be our change in state of delivery here"

rule: Entry may be the LTF FVG itself, or (more confirmation) the order block formed by the last down-close candle that tagged the gap and was re-tagged.
quote: "This would be labeled as a five minute bullish order block. So you have two means of entry"

rule: Execute after candles close above swing highs off the IRL/ERL reaction; stop rests at the low that tagged the internal or external range.
quote: "have your stop loss resting at the low that tag the internal range or the external range"

rule: For longs, measure premium/discount on the energetic swing and buy only when price drops into discount into the LTF FVG.
quote: "I'm looking at price to drop into discount on the range after we had our energetic move"

rule: For indices, do not execute before the 9:30 equities open.
quote: "I can't execute on this primarily because this is consistent to my rules prior to the equities open"

rule: Advanced market structure entry: long-term low → short-term low → intermediate-term low; the short-term low to the right of the intermediate-term low is the preferred entry (mirror for shorts).
quote: "to the right of that intermediate term low will be your preferred entry short term low to your anticipated draw on liquidity"

rule: On the higher-timeframe key level, wicks through are fine; candle bodies not closing beyond it confirm the level holds.
quote: "The wick is just doing the damage and the body is telling us the story."

rule: Targets: the next ERL / swing high, or 2-2.5 standard deviations of the swing, giving about 1:2-1:2.5 R.
quote: "take profit at two to two and a half standard deviations"

rule: Weekly bias timing: if the weekly IRL is already tagged and the draw is close, expect Monday (not Tuesday/Wednesday) to give the entry.
quote: "I can anticipate already that Monday will most likely be able to give us that opportunity for entry"

rule: The model is identical on every pair; only the timeframes change.
quote: "Everything is the same. It's just, you should be lining up your timeframes properly"

rule: A bullish candle (unless its low equals the open) must move below the open to put in its low before going higher.
quote: "It's going to have to move below the open to put in a low before going higher."

rule: For an expected bullish candle, buy below or near the open, expecting expansion up to the high and then the close.
quote: "I can look for opportunities to buy below the open or near the open, expecting this expansion up"

rule: For an expected bearish candle (OHLC), expect a high above the open and sell between that high and the open.
quote: "This is where I want to look for selling opportunities between this high and around this opening price"

rule: Whether the candle is expected bullish or bearish depends on the draw on liquidity.
quote: "This is dependent on my draw on liquidity or where I think price is likely to reach for."

rule: Weekly: bearish week wants a high first (OHLC); bullish week wants a low first (OLHC).
quote: "If we are expecting a bearish week, we would want to see a high put in."

rule: Use midnight opening price as the open of the daily candle on intraday charts; sell above/around it for a bearish day.
quote: "I am going to be using midnight opening price as the open for this daily candle"

rule: After a 4H down-close candle with a draw above, expect the next 4H candle to be OLHC; trade it on the 5m.
quote: "after this down close candle, I'm looking for an open, low, high close of the next four hour candle"

rule: Once the low is in, the candle's opening price should support price (no closes below it) before expansion.
quote: "that opening price is supporting the candles and nothing is closing below it. I'm expecting a move higher"

rule: Read the candle as AMD: consolidation at the open = accumulation, run beyond the open = manipulation, run to the opposite extreme = distribution.
quote: "Another way to think about this is in terms of accumulation, manipulation, and distribution."

rule: Fib retracement levels: 0, 0.5, 0.62, 0.705, 0.79, 1.
quote: "I am going to be using the 0, 0.5, 0.62, 0.705, 0.79, and the 1"

rule: 0.5 is the discount/premium split; the OTE zone is 0.62-0.79 with 0.705 as midpoint.
quote: "we have our OTE or optimal trade entry zone with our 0.62."

rule: Draw the fib from swing high to swing low (bearish); for bullish from low to high, dragging the anchor as the range extends until a swing high forms.
quote: "I drag my Fibonacci retracement from the swing high,"

rule: After a swing range forms, wait for a retrace into the OTE and look there for an entry or a lower-timeframe entry model toward opposite liquidity.
quote: "I'm looking for an entry or a lower timeframe entry model to go lower or to reach for sell side liquidity resting below"

rule: Align the OTE with PD arrays to the left (FVG, up/down-close candles); overlap = multiple confluences.
quote: "I look to my left and see if there's any PD arrays that line up."

rule: If an order block's opening price is not in the OTE, use its mean threshold (50% of the body) as the confluence.
quote: "This is when I would use the mean threshold of this order block, or 50% of the body."

rule: Order block validation: a large down-close candle sweeps lows, then price displaces and closes over it.
quote: "we have a large down close candle sweeping these lows before we displace and close over this candle here."

rule: Use the PD arrays that catch your eye; he does not stack every possible one (e.g. a respected volume imbalance).
quote: "For me, I focus on which PD arrays catch my eye"

rule: A move out of an OTE that forms a new swing creates a new range; re-draw and use an OTE again, especially on a lower timeframe.
quote: "we now have another range. I can mark out that range and then use an OTE again"

rule: When price makes a new extreme, adjust the fib to the new swing before judging the retracement.
quote: "We make a new low, so I adjust my FIB, and then I look for PD arrays in this area."

rule: Ignore OTE touches outside the kill zone.
quote: "However, it's out of kill zone, so I am not watching this."

rule: Bodies respecting the HTF FVG while wicking to the 0.79, then displacement, confirms the short; enter on the LTF FVG / order block.
quote: "hit the .79, body is still respecting the hourly fair value gap, and then we get displacement lower"

rule: Stop on the high of the entry swing; target liquidity built before the session (equal lows, London session lows).
quote: "my stop on this high, and then looking to target these lows that were generated prior to the session or London session lows"

rule: Project the sweep-to-displacement leg; a 2-2.5 standard deviation zone lining up with old liquidity adds target conviction.
quote: "What do we notice about the 2 to 2.5 area here? It's resting just above these failure swings."

rule: Preferred entry is the 0.705; take 0.62 if you really want to be in the position.
quote: "ideally I want to be entering at the .705, but if I really want to be in a position, I'll look to enter at the .62"

rule: For an OTE long, require a close over the highs first, then draw the OTE from that low to the current high and track new highs.
quote: "I want to see price close over these highs here."

rule: Bearish OB: into an important level, sweep buy-side, displace and close below the opening price of the single/series of up-close candles; the retrace into it is resistance.
quote: "We sweep that high and then displace and close below the opening price of this single or series of up close candles into this important level."

rule: Bullish OB: sweep sell-side, displace and close over the opening price of the single/series of down-close candles; price then uses it as support.
quote: "It then sweeps that sell side liquidity before displacing and closing over the opening price of the single or series of down close candles."

rule: A sweep before the closure is not required for an OB, but he always waits for one.
quote: "Now order blocks don't necessarily need a sweep before this closure below"

rule: The pattern only counts off a higher-timeframe PD array or important level; at a random spot it is not an order block.
quote: "If we get this pattern at a random spot in a chart, it doesn't mean anything. That's not an order block."

rule: Enter on the retest of the OB opening price, stop on the swept extreme, target liquidity or 2R.
quote: "looking to enter on a retest of the order block, my stop on this high and looking for 2R."

rule: Check the higher timeframe (1h) for the level the 5m OB reaches into; without it the up-close candles may just be equal highs in a retracement.
quote: "in the absence of a higher time frame level, these up close candles just created equal highs, and this is a retracement to move higher."

rule: Valid OB sequence: reach into an HTF level (e.g. 1h FVG), then sweep, then close over the down-close candle's open; it should also go with the trend.
quote: "this order block reaches into a higher timeframe level or an hourly fair value gap and is going with the trend."

rule: Mean threshold = 50% of the OB measured body low to body high (fib 0.5).
quote: "I'm going to take my 0.5 fib from the body low to body high and mark out 50% of that order block."

rule: If price is respecting the OB, it should not close below (bullish) the mean threshold.
quote: "I don't want to see any closes below the mean threshold or 50% of this order block."

rule: Use the mean threshold as entry when the OB is a large series of candles and its opening price makes the RR poor.
quote: "I will focus on using the mean threshold of an order block when we have a larger series of candles in which the opening price does not make sense for an entry."

rule: He prefers a clear swing low to be swept, not a small one.
quote: "I prefer a nice swing low to be swept"

rule: The OB is the series of down-close candles before the change in the state of delivery.
quote: "This is our order block here, or the series of down close candles before the change in the state of delivery."

rule: On the HTF FVG, bodies respect the level and wicks do the damage.
quote: "you can see how the bodies respect the fair value gap here and the wicks do the damage."

rule: After the smart money reversal, keep looking for continuation entries on OBs on the buy side of the curve.
quote: "I will still be looking for entries after the smart money reversal. And the way I do that is I look for an order block on the buy side of the curve."

rule: Continuation OB important levels: a previous order block, a fair value gap, or a sweep.
quote: "those important levels are a previous order block, a fair value gap, or a sweep."

rule: For a continuation OB from a sweep, the down-close candle that swept the low gets closed over.
quote: "the down close candle that swept this low gets closed over validating it is an order block to continue higher."

rule: For a series, wait for a close over the lowest-body down-close candle.
quote: "if we're looking for the lowest body down close candle, it would be this candle here. I'm waiting for price to close over that candle."

rule: A mean-threshold entry increases RR but risks not getting filled.
quote: "However, with this technique, I also risk the chance of not getting filled on this trade."

rule: A close below an opening price that never reached into an important level does not validate an OB.
quote: "It doesn't validate it as an order block for me because it's missing that important level."

rule: Stop goes on a swing high/low or the other end of the OB; the OB end gives more RR but can be wicked while the trade is still valid.
quote: "Generally I'm looking to place my stop loss on a swing high or low or the other end of the order block."

rule: Continuation entry types: return to an OB, an FVG, or a sweep of a low, toward the draw on liquidity.
quote: "I'm looking for either a return to an order block, a fair value gap, or a sweep of a low."

rule: Missing the first entry is fine; a later OB is a secondary entry.
quote: "even if I don't catch this first initial buy, this order block is a secondary entry to move higher."

rule: Keep the stop at the swing low and move the entry closer to invalidation, not the stop closer to the entry.
quote: "adjust my entry to get closer to my invalidation point, rather than adjust my invalidation to get closer to my entry."

rule: OTE identifies where (which fib levels) price is likely to retrace to.
quote: "Essentially it is when you are looking for a retracement, where and what FIB levels price is likely to retrace to."

rule: Draw the fib on the displacement range that broke structure; expect the retracement around 0.62-0.79, with 0.5 as premium/discount.
quote: "using the 0.62 and 0.79 FIB, as well as the discount and premium with the 0.5 FIB"

rule: An imbalance or POI inside the OTE zone helps.
quote: "it does help if you have some sort of imbalance or point of interest in there."

rule: After a breaker structure, align the FVG with the OTE for confluence.
quote: "draw out your fair value gap as well as your OTE or optimal trade entry. And you can see how those kind of line up and give you confluence."

rule: If the first entry is missed, a lower-timeframe breaker gives a nested OTE with a 5m FVG.
quote: "So you have an optimal trade entry inside of an optimal trade entry."

rule: On a higher timeframe, the OTE of the displacement leg after a smart money reversal is a POI for a lower-timeframe entry.
quote: "So you can use this as a point of interest and then look for a lower time frame entry."

rule: The same fib levels project where a retracement is likely to go, so they can be targets after a short.
quote: "If you got short up here, you can target a discount for these fib levels right here."

rule: He mainly uses OTE fibs on lower-timeframe displacement legs to choose among many small FVGs.
quote: "Where I really like to utilize these fibs are in my lower time frame entries."

rule: Targets come from two things: liquidity and imbalances.
quote: "The two things I use to choose targets is liquidity and imbalances."

rule: After a short from a stop run and LTF structure shift, the nearby lows are the targets because liquidity rests there.
quote: "let's say you got short after we ran these stops up here, shifted structure on a lower timeframe. What are your targets?"

rule: Imbalances (5m FVG, or a 15m FVG) can be targets, especially when they line up with a liquidity run.
quote: "this would be your 15 minute fair value gap right here, which also corresponds with that liquidity run."

rule: A small order block and lower FVGs inside the range are also targets.
quote: "you have this little order block right here, right, target that, as well as this lower level fair value gap here"

rule: Equal lows (or highs) should always be a target.
quote: "Whenever you see equal lows, that should be a target in your mind."

rule: After the obvious equal-lows target, the next targets are further liquidity pools.
