quote: "your obvious target is these equal lows here, which you take out. And then where are your next targets?"

rule: Add to the position on retracements, risking the highs, and target the next lows and imbalances.
quote: "Let's say you add in here, right? Risking the highs."

rule: Counter-trend scalps: target imbalance to imbalance, with the final target the major liquidity.
quote: "This is also a way you can play counter trend scalps."

rule: He would rather see price move up into an FVG before shorting than short a small order block below it.
quote: "I would have wanted to see a move up into this fair value gap"

rule: Using imbalances as targets means exiting a bit earlier but gives more targets than obvious liquidity alone.
quote: "if you look for imbalances as targets as well, you might exit a little bit more early, but it also will give you a few more targets."

rule: A protected swing is a high or low expected to hold as the trend continues.
quote: "A protected swing is a high or low in which I'm expecting to hold as the trend continues."

rule: Type 1 (bullish): a short-term low is run/swept, then price closes through the series of down-close candles that made the low; the low is now protected.
quote: "I want to see a low or a short-term low be ran out or swept and then close through the series of downclo candles that made the low"

rule: The low need not be run only when SMT exists: the correlated asset runs it; use the series of down-close candles that made the failure swing.
quote: "when do we not need to run out the low? Well, that is only if we use SMT."

rule: Type 2: a protected swing formed out of an FVG: price reaches into the FVG, then closes through the opposing candles that made the swing.
quote: "the other type of protected swing is one formed out of a fair value gap"

rule: While price has not closed over the down-close candles into the important level, the move is still bearish.
quote: "Do we close over those two downlosed candles? No. So it is still bearish."

rule: Once a protected swing forms, he can take an entry or seek a continuation in the new trend direction.
quote: "from here I can look to take an entry or seek a continuation as I'm expecting this trend to continue higher"

rule: In a consolidation focus on the external parts of the range; bearish means wait for highs to be run, then trade lower.
quote: "if we are in a consolidation, where do we want to focus? The external parts of the range."

rule: A turtle soup over the previous day high without the close through the opposing candles is not confirmed and can fail.
quote: "we never get that confirmation of the close through the series of downclosed candles that made that high"

rule: The series can be a single candle; once closed through, the trend is considered flipped.
quote: "In this case, it is just one. Yes, we do. So, with this now, we can anticipate this trend to have flipped"

rule: Ignore insignificant small opposing candles inside a whole series when defining the series.
quote: "I would be ignoring this small little candle there"

rule: Look for sweeps on the side against the trend: in a bearish trend (wick intact), sweep a high then close below the up-close candles.
quote: "Why are we looking for a high to be swept out and not a low? Well, we are bearish"

rule: Each new protected swing in a trend is a continuation (or a lower-timeframe reversal); repeat the process after each new sweep.
quote: "each one of these is a continuation of this bearish trend or a lower time frame reversal"

rule: The trend persists until violated; daily closures outside the previous day's range keep it going, and you keep tracking protected swings as sell areas.
quote: "I can continue to just track the protected swings in the market giving me areas that I want to sell"

rule: You can anticipate a protected swing from the HTF narrative and refine it on a lower timeframe, or wait for the HTF closure as confirmation.
quote: "The anticipation of a protected swing versus a protected swing forming."

rule: A lethargic move back into the range after a sweep does not confirm a protected high; wait for the next sweep and closure.
quote: "We get a very lethargic move back into the range here, not confirming this as a protected high."

rule: In a candle for continuation, expect the lower half of that HTF candle to push price lower (bearish case).
quote: "I'm expecting the lower half of this candle to push price lower"

rule: When the series is messy (up, down, back up), use the level of the cleaner leg rather than every candle.
quote: "price went up, down, back up. So I can really just use this level in here"

rule: For a bearish daily continuation, want the retrace high to form in the lower half of the prior bearish daily candle (e.g. an FVG there).
quote: "If expecting a continuation lower, I want to see from the lower half of this."

rule: Wait for a bearish daily closure (sweep of previous candle and close back inside) before dropping to the lower timeframe.
quote: "We sweep out our previous and we close back inside the range. So, with this, I can drop down to the 15-minute chart."

rule: Do not enter with the stop on a distant protected high; wait for a new protected swing closer to price for better R:R.
quote: "do I want to enter with my stop all the way on this high? That doesn't really give good risk-to-reward"

rule: Entry model: sell when the new protected swing confirms, stop on the protected swing high, target 2R (then standard deviation projections).
quote: "this is where I can sell, put my stop on the protected swing high and then look for 2 R"

rule: The protected swing is the invalidation; enter close to it for good risk-to-reward.
quote: "I'm using it as my invalidation. So I want an entry fairly close to my invalidation"

rule: Trade towards failure swings and keep protected swings on your side of the market.
quote: "we want to be trading towards failure swings and we want protected swings on our side of the market"

rule: A down-close candle into a POI that is closed over gives a new protected swing = the continuation / order block at the low-risk buy.
quote: "this would be the continuation or the order block formed at the low-risk buy"

rule: You don't need to catch the reversal; opportunities lie in the continuation once a new protected swing (invalidation) forms.
quote: "You don't have to catch them at the reversal. You can get the continuation"

rule: Long the stronger of two correlated assets and short the weaker one.
quote: "generally I want to be longing the stronger asset and shorting the weaker asset"

rule: Judge relative strength with three tools: SMT, structure (separation) and candle closures.
quote: none

rule: SMT = a difference in structure at the same swing on correlated assets; the asset making the higher low is stronger, the one making the lower low is weaker (mirror for highs).
quote: "the one that makes the higher low is the stronger asset and the one that makes the lower low is the weaker asset"

rule: For longs focus on the stronger asset; for shorts the weaker; avoid the weaker asset for long setups.
quote: none

rule: Without SMT (both make higher lows), compare the separation of each new low from the prior extreme low: more separation = stronger.
quote: "The greater the separation the stronger the asset."

rule: Candle 2 test: at a swept low, the asset whose candle 2 closes bullish back above candle 1's low is stronger than the one that sweeps and cannot close back above.
quote: "we sweep out the low, but we can't close bullish or back above candle 1's low"

rule: Later closures keep the comparison: a bullish candle 4 vs a bearish one, or a candle closing over its previous candle vs a doji closing back inside it, shows strength vs weakness.
quote: none

rule: Only compare correlated assets that should share structure (e.g. ES/NQ, gold futures / gold in other currencies).
quote: none

rule: Mark the same-timeframe swing on both assets; the one that takes it out while the other does not reveals the divergence (NQ lower high = weaker, ES higher high = stronger in the example).
quote: none

rule: Separation also works against a prior high: the asset trading only a few points from the high is stronger than one far below it.
quote: none

rule: The candles that create the CISD or the continuation often reveal relative strength: the asset that closes through the level is the one moving with conviction.
quote: "a lot of times the closures specifically candles that create the change in the state of delivery or continuation will show you that relative strength or weakness"

rule: Not all three signals will be present; one clear signal (here, the CISD closure) can decide.
quote: none

rule: SMTs can exist on several timeframes at once; when they agree they reinforce the same strong/weak reading.
quote: none

rule: Relative strength rotates: during a consolidation the previously weaker asset can show stronger closures, so re-check it continuously.
quote: "strength and weakness is not going to remain consistent all the time"

rule: Use separation (not SMT) when neither asset has yet taken the reference low; measure how close each is propped to it.
quote: "we would use separation if we had this low and it was not yet taken out because then it wouldn't technically be an SMT"

rule: Closure detail: a candle that cannot close below a prior down-close candle, then one that closes back over it, marks the stronger asset (continuation) vs one that does not reach that candle's open.
quote: none

rule: Relative strength is a filter inside a higher-timeframe framework and a strategy; never trade an asset only because it looks stronger.
quote: "this shouldn't be used alone, right? We want to have a higher time frame framework"

rule: Use market structure and market structure shifts to tell a pullback from a reversal.
quote: "We're going to look at market structure and market structure shifts."

rule: 5m is a good trend read, but higher timeframes are less noisy; most people should use or at least check the 15m.
quote: "For most people, I would recommend the 15-minute chart or at least look at the 15-minute chart to get a bigger picture."

rule: A MSS that creates an imbalance shifts the trend.
quote: "After this market structure shift right here creates an imbalance, we are shifting to a bullish trend."

rule: In an uptrend watch for downside MSS (and vice versa); without a structure break it is only a pullback.
quote: "If price does not break structure, it's just a pullback."

rule: Mark the short-term lows in an uptrend and watch whether they get broken.
quote: "Start by marking out these short term lows to see if they get broken."

rule: A 5m break against an intact 15m trend is counter-trend; target the 15m imbalance where longs reload.
quote: "If you are going to trade this counter trend, you want to target this imbalance here to reload longs"

rule: After the 5m turns bearish into the POI, wait for a 5m or 1m bullish MSS there to re-look longs.
quote: "We want to either see a market structure shift on the five minute or one minute to relook longs in this area, this point of interest."

rule: 1m entry: MSS with displacement creates an imbalance; enter long when price returns to it.
quote: "market structure shift, displacement, energetic move up, creates that imbalance, price returns, enter long there."

rule: After a 5m break, expect the imbalance it created to be filled before continuation.
quote: "So you expect to have an imbalance that wants to be filled."

rule: A structure break with no displacement / no FVG is not a MSS.
quote: "It was broken. There's no displacement, right? There's no fair value gap or reach above energetically."

rule: A valid MSS energetically breaks the swing and leaves a fair value gap.
quote: "Energetically breaks above, creates an imbalance, and that would be your fair value gap and market structure shift."

rule: In a 15m uptrend, mark lows and wait for them to be taken with displacement before calling a reversal.
quote: "So you want to mark out these lows. And wait for them to be taken with displacement."

rule: He does not trade the overnight session.
quote: "we reached the overnight session, which I don't really mess with."

rule: Intraday (below the hourly) trade only within kill zones: NY AM 8:30-11:00 for indices, London 2:00-5:00, Eastern time.
quote: "I personally focus on the New York am session for indices so I'm going to focus on 8:30 to 11 for my trading"

rule: Choose your execution timeframe by temperament: impatient lower, patient higher; he executes on 5m because it aligns with the daily profile.
quote: "impatient people want to be on a lower time frame while patient people are generally better suited for a higher time frame"

rule: Master one PD array rather than every concept.
quote: "instead focus on one of these Concepts and master that"

rule: FVG: three-candle pattern where candle 3's high does not overlap candle 1's low (or candle 3's low does not overlap candle 1's high); the gap is a POI.
quote: "it is a three Candlestick pattern in which the high of the third candle does not overlap the low of the first candle"

rule: Inversion: an FVG that is closed over and then used as support (bullish) or resistance (bearish).
quote: "that is when a fair value Gap gets closed over and then is used as support to trade higher or resistance to trade lower"

rule: Order block (his focus): at a POI, take the series of up-close candles into it; when closed below, expect that high to hold and the block to act as resistance.
quote: "I take the series of up closed candles into that point of interest when it is then closed below"

rule: Bearish breaker: high, low, higher high, lower low; mark the down-close candles between that high and low as resistance; bullish mirror uses up-close candles.
quote: "it is where we have a high a low a higher high and a lower low"

rule: OTE: Fib the impulse leg high to low and look for a lower high around the 70.5% retracement to trade back toward the low.
quote: "using the Fibonacci retracements and specifically the 705 area"

rule: Confluence: look for your chosen PD array in discount for lows and premium for highs (0.5 of the range).
quote: "when we use premium in discount or A5 FIB of a range I can then look for either a fair value Gap or an order block"

rule: SMT (correlated assets with different structure: one higher low, one lower low) is his favourite reversal confluence.
quote: "one asset made a higher low while the other one made a lower low"

rule: Order of a reversal: purge of a low / turtle soup, then inversion, then CISD / order block formation, then FVG and/or breaker.
quote: "this is generally how reversals form is we first have a purge of a low or a turtle soup"

rule: Step 1 (purge) is not needed when SMT is present.
quote: "we will not have this if we have smt"

rule: Step 3: CISD / order block formation = close through the series of down-close candles that purged the low.
quote: "once we close through this series of down closed candles that Purge that low"

rule: The further down the sequence, the more confirmation, but the later the entry; you trade confirmation for price.
quote: "the further down this list the more confirmation there is that it has formed a reversal"

rule: He prefers trading continuations, i.e. later in the sequence.
quote: "I personally prefer to trade continuations so later into the move"

rule: A consolidation (failure to displace out of either side) is a range whose high and low are manipulation candidates.
quote: "you can see we have failed to displace out of either side of this range and we are consolidating"

rule: Remove all drawings except your chosen PD array to read reversals clearly.
quote: "go ahead and remove all the other drawings except for that one"

rule: In a bullish daily profile with Asia highs and London consolidation, expect London/equal highs taken, needing a low manipulation or SMT first.
quote: "we want to see either a manipulation of a low or an smt to form and confirm this reversal"

rule: When steps overlap (inversion, CISD, breaker, FVG in one area), they act as confluence; he still focuses on the CISD and the order block's mean threshold.
quote: "what I would be focusing on here is just the change in the state of delivery and then the main threshold of this order block"

rule: In a retracement against expected continuation, wait for either a close below the up-close candles (validating the high) or a sweep of the high, whichever comes first.
quote: "I either want to see a close below these up close candles here to validate this high or for this High to get swept out"

rule: If the breaker is not clean, use the whole leg as the breaker zone.
quote: "this one isn't very clear so generally on this I would just use this whole leg up"

rule: A strategy needs entry criteria, stop placement, and a profit / break-even rule.
quote: "There are three things that I need to know when building a strategy, and that is criteria for entry, stop placement, and where I'm going to take my profit"

rule: Entry criteria: a stop hunt, then an OTE entry.
quote: "So in this model, I decided on a stop hunt and then an OTE entry. This is my criteria for entry."

rule: Stop always at the stop-hunt extreme; first profit or break even after price breaks the low created for the OTE leg.
quote: "I always place my stop at this high and then I take my first profit or move my stop to break even after we break through this low"

rule: OTE is chosen because it gives over 1.5 R:R, which tolerates a lower win rate.
quote: "it creates a risk to reward over 1.5 which allows me to have a lower win rate."

rule: Mark recent highs and lows; those are what the strategy wants taken.
quote: "I'm going to mark out recent highs and lows as that is what I am looking to be taken out in this strategy."

rule: A stop hunt requires an aggressive move out of the range and an aggressive move back in; otherwise disregard.
quote: "I want to see an aggressive move out and then back into the range."

rule: An invalid sweep becomes the new high to watch.
quote: "So this doesn't validate the criteria for my entry, so I disregard it, but I now have a new high to be watching."

rule: OTE entry at the 0.62 of the leg from the stop-hunt high to the current low, tracked as the low extends.
quote: "from this high to the current low, I'm going to be looking for the 0.62 as far as it goes down."

rule: Moving beyond an old low without returning into the range is invalid.
quote: "you can see we move below this low, but we don't move back into the range. So this is invalid"

rule: Bullish version: stop on the swept low, first TP / break even at the high of the leg; full target the highs or premium of the range.
quote: "Well, either these highs up here, or when we reach into a premium of the range"

rule: Defined rules can be coded into an indicator.
quote: "The nice thing about creating a model with defined rules is that it can be coded and turned into an indicator."

rule: Indicator logic: aggressive take of a high, aggressive displacement back in, fib drawn, OTE highlighted, swing high formed in the OTE, then move down.
quote: "the indicator draws a fib and highlights the OTE here and shows when it creates a swing high in that OTE"

rule: No aggressive move back in or no swing formed in the OTE = no trade even if there is a reaction.
quote: "as we couldn't displace below here, there's no aggressive move back in, or swing low put in."

rule: Plot the previous week's high and low.
quote: "we want to plot the previous week's high and low, right?"

rule: Plot the previous day high, low and close.
quote: "we want to plot the previous day high and the previous day low, along with the previous day's close"

rule: At the market open, plot the opening price; these are the only levels used.
quote: "when market opens, you'll plot the opening price. And that is all the levels that you will use."

rule: Watch the five-minute chart and take actionable trades off these levels.
quote: "watch the five minute chart and take actionable trades. Off these levels."

rule: Triggers: candlestick formations, Strat closes above and below a level.
quote: "you can use candlestick formations, the strat closes above and below"

rule: Short entry on a shooter candle that tests the level and closes below it, on the close or the break.
quote: "we have a shooter candle came out, tested our level, closed below it. You could enter, you know, once it closes below it or on the break"

rule: Target previous five-minute candles.
quote: "you would just target these previous five-minute candles"

rule: Long after a break and close above a level.
quote: "once we break above here, close above, you could enter along [a long]"

rule: Leave runners and trail the stop on previous 5m candles.
quote: "Leave your runners on the five-minute, just trail it."

rule: Plot only: previous week high/low, previous day high/low, previous day close, current day open.
quote: "That is previous weeks, high, low, previous days high, low, previous days close, and the current days open."

rule: With levels plotted, watch price action on the 5-minute chart.
quote: "once you have all your levels, you're just going to watch the price action on a five minute chart."

rule: Play with the overall market: no longs while SPX is tanking, no shorts while it rallies.
quote: "If SPX is tanking, you don't want to be going long, right? If it's going long, you don't want to be going short."

rule: Trade with the higher-timeframe trend; counter-trend only for a quick scalp.
quote: "If we're trending down on NVIDIA daily, you're not going to be wanting to go long most of the time unless it's for a quick scalp"

rule: Entry: rejection of a daily level with a close back above, taken on the retest or on the break of that candle.
quote: "We came down, tried to break below this daily level. We rejected it and closed above."

rule: Confirm with a correlated stock (AMD with NVIDIA) and SPX moving the same direction.
quote: "I like to watch AMD as well because they're pretty similar stocks and move similar."

rule: Stop: exit on a 5m close back below the level.
quote: "my stop would be a close below this level, right? So if it closes back below this daily level, I would exit the trade for a loss."

rule: Management: target the opening price, scale out there, move stop to breakeven, then trail behind 5m bars.
quote: "once it hits here, you'd scale out, and you can move your stop to break even, and then you would just trail the five minute bars up"

rule: After a gap up, a bounce off the gap is higher probability than a breakout.
quote: "If we reject this gap and go long, you'd rather take this bounce here than this break, right? It's a higher probability trade."

rule: Consolidation on a daily level and the opening price: trade the break of the inside bar (or a later break-down to avoid chop), stop on a close above the candle.
quote: "you could just take the break of this inside bar"

rule: Use the two-minute chart.
quote: "Two minute chart."

rule: Only play reversals off a level.
quote: "You're only going to play reversals off of a level."

rule: After the reversal off the level, a short-term high or low must be taken, with displacement.
quote: "A short term high or low must be taken after the reversal off that level, and there must be displacement."

rule: Find the imbalance and enter when price returns to it.
quote: "After that, you're going to find an imbalance and enter when price returns to it."

rule: Stop loss at the low of the candle that made the imbalance.
quote: "Your stop loss will be at the low of the candle that made that imbalance"

rule: Target the next high or low, imbalance or level.
quote: "you're going to target the next high or low, imbalance or level"

rule: If the imbalance is too large, use its 0.5 Fib as entry or do not take the trade.
quote: "If imbalance is too large, use the 0.5 FIB or don't take the trade."

rule: A short-term high break without displacement does not qualify.
quote: "breaks short-term high. However, there's no displacement up."

rule: After the first take profit, move the stop to breakeven to be risk free.
quote: "once you take profit here, I prefer to move my stop to break even here, right? Then you're risk free for the rest of the trade."

rule: Using the 0.5 Fib of a large imbalance cuts risk (60 cents to 40 cents in the example).
quote: "if you draw a 0.5 FIB, use that as your entry, you cut down your risk"

rule: The imbalance can be an FVG or an order block.
quote: "Search for the imbalance, that can be fair value gaps or order blocks if you know more about that"

rule: If the trade does not meet your risk requirements, skip it.
quote: "if it doesn't meet your risk requirements, don't trade it"

rule: S&P 500 and NASDAQ normally track each other's market structure.
quote: "Normally the S&P 500 and NASDAQ track each other."

rule: A divergence is when one makes a higher high while the other makes a lower high.
quote: "For example, one is making a higher high, while the other one is making lower highs."

rule: One making a higher low while the other makes a lower low is also a divergence.
quote: "the NASDAQ is making a higher low, while the S&P is making a lower low. This is also a divergence."

rule: Ideally the divergence comes with a liquidity grab at a point of interest.
quote: "Ideally, you would like to see a grab of liquidity."

rule: Higher-timeframe divergences are more reliable; he prefers 15m, uses 1m a lot.
quote: "Higher timeframes are most likely going to be a little more reliable. I prefer the 15 minute chart, but I do use the one minute chart quite a bit."

rule: Trade the index that is diverging.
quote: "Which one do you take the trade on? Well, you want to take the one that is diverging."

rule: Bearish divergence: short the one making the lower high because it is weaker.
quote: "You want to take the lower high because it is weaker."

rule: Bullish divergence: long the stronger one, the one making the higher low.
quote: "Now, if you have a bullish divergence shown here, making lower lows and higher lows, you want to take the one that is stronger."

rule: Method 1: enter on the diverging index and risk the divergence lows/highs; if they are taken the divergence is invalid (that is the stop).
quote: "If these lows or highs are broken or taken, the divergence is invalidated and that will be your stop."

rule: The stop is at the lows because if price takes them it is no longer a divergence.
quote: "You risk the lows because if this, if price was to return and take out these lows, it's not a divergence anymore, right?"

rule: Method 2: after spotting it, look for a 1-5m market structure shift and a return to an FVG.
quote: "Look for a lower timeframe entry on the one through five minute charts. You want to look for a market structure shift and a return to a fair value gap"

rule: Method 2 is safer but may not always present itself.
quote: "This entry is safer, but may not always present itself."

rule: Example: NQ higher lows, wait for structure shift with displacement, 2m FVG entries.
quote: "And you have a two-minute fair value gap here, combining these two, and gave multiple entries there."

rule: SMT is only applied to correlated assets (ES/NQ, EU/GU) that should move in the same direction.
quote: "if we have ES and NQ, they are both correlated or should be moving in the same direction, so we can use those for SMT"

rule: Bullish SMT: one asset makes a low then a higher low while the other makes a low then a lower low.
quote: "So while this one was making a low and a higher low, this one made a low and a lower low. Now that divergence right there is an SMT."

rule: Bearish SMT: one asset makes a higher high while the other makes a lower high at the same time.
quote: "one making a high and a higher high, while another is making a high and a lower high,"

rule: SMT is a confluence to a reversal used to confirm a pre-existing idea or HTF level, not the reason for the reversal.
quote: "it is really a confluence to a reversal. So if I already have a pre-existing idea or a higher timeframe level, I can look for SMT to confirm that reversal."

rule: Once the SMT high forms at the expected reversal, trust that the SMT extreme will not be touched and anticipate the move to the draw.
quote: "trusting that this SMT will confirm the reversal and this high will not be touched"

rule: Ignore SMTs that do not align with a higher-timeframe level or idea; they appear everywhere.
quote: "not all SMTs are important if they don't align with some sort of higher time frame level or idea"

rule: Look for SMTs at session highs/lows, previous-day highs/lows and HTF levels viewed on a lower timeframe.
quote: "spots where I generally look for SMTs are on session highs and lows, previous days high and lows, and at higher time frame levels on a lower time frame"

rule: Do not short immediately on an SMT; structure and everything else must align first.
quote: "Does this mean I'm going to short it right away? No, because SMT is just a confluence."

rule: If the lagging asset later takes the same high, the SMT is cancelled.
quote: "if we take this high on NQ, there is no SMT anymore"

rule: With an HTF POI (e.g. hourly FVG), use a 5m SMT as confirmation to the entry model for the reversal.
quote: "if I have an SMT on the five minute time frame, I'll use that as a confirmation to my entry model for the reversal"

rule: After an SMT, wait for displacement and an actual setup; never blindly enter because of the SMT.
quote: "I don't just blindly long something because of an SMT. I'm going to wait for an actual setup and then use this SMT to confirm it."

rule: With high-impact news (CPI 8:30) pending, wait until after the release to look for the trade.
quote: "I'm going to wait for post CPI to be looking for an opportunity"

rule: High, low, higher high, lower low makes the last down-close candle a breaker block (entry zone).
quote: "if we have a high, low, higher high, lower low, what does this downclose candle become? Well, that is a breaker block."

rule: In volatile/news conditions, place the stop above the high that ran another high (high-resistance liquidity) rather than just above the breaker.
quote: "I'd prefer to have my stop on a high that ran another high, creating high resistance liquidity"

rule: Which asset to trade after an SMT (the one that swept or the one that failed) depends on the HTF setup and relative strength; it is partly personal opinion.
quote: "this depends on the higher timeframe setup and relative strength. It kinda comes down to personal opinion"

rule: On a high-impact news day he prefers the asset that swept liquidity (high-resistance liquidity for the stop).
quote: "In this case with a high news release, I prefer the one that swept liquidity, giving high resistance liquidity."

rule: A bullish continuation should show down-close candles supporting price higher.
quote: "Now if this is going to continue higher, I want to see what? Down close candles support price higher."

rule: Missed entry: drop from the 15m PD array to 1m and use a CISD (close below series of up-close candles) or the FVG for entry.
quote: "close below the series of Up close candles here, changing the state of delivery"

rule: He prefers at least 2R; if the CISD entry gives 1.65R he moves the entry to the FVG to get 2R.
quote: "Now with a 1.65R, I prefer to have 2R, so I'd likely put my entry on this fair value gap here to get me 2R."

rule: Inversely correlated pairs (EURUSD vs DXY): expect mirrored structure; a high on one should pair with a low on the other.
quote: "if we have EURUSD versus the dollar, those are going to be inversely correlated, but we want to see the same structure"

rule: Inverse SMT: one asset makes a higher high while the other makes a higher low instead of a lower low (or lower high with lower low).
quote: "so if we see a high, we want to see a low, but we have a higher high, I'd want to see a lower low, but we have a higher low"

rule: SMT within an FVG: if one asset trades back into an FVG and the other does not, that is an SMT (the FVG edge is a lower-timeframe swing).
quote: "price on ES reaches back into this fair value gap, while on NQ it doesn't. So is this an SMT? Yes."

rule: Reading SMT inside an FVG/PD array is using the smaller-timeframe SMT without dropping timeframes.
quote: "looking for an SMT within a fair value gap or a PD array is just utilizing the smaller timeframes SMT without dropping down to the lower timeframe"

rule: An HTF wick low taken on one asset but not the other is a lower-timeframe SMT visible from the HTF chart.
quote: "You see how on ES, we go and take this low here. On NASDAQ, we do not. That is going to be a lower timeframe SMT."

rule: Projections are used for targets, areas to expect retracements/reversals, and confluence to an existing strategy.
quote: "Standard deviation projections can be used to find targets, areas to expect retracements or reversals, as well as a confluence to an existing strategy."

rule: Fib retracement tool levels: 1, 0, -1, -2, -2.5, -4.
quote: "the settings we have here are 1, 0, negative 1, negative 2, negative 2.5, and negative 4"

rule: Anchor the projection on the manipulation leg: the swing that swept liquidity before the CISD / structure shift.
quote: "that manipulation leg is the swing that swept liquidity before Changing the state of delivery or shifting structure"

rule: In a bearish reversal the manipulation leg is the leg that made the new high before the new low; project it from the high to the low.
quote: "So where is the price leg that made the new high before the new low?"

rule: In a bullish reversal the manipulation leg is the leg that made the new low before the new high; project it from low to high.
quote: "where is the manipulation leg or the leg that made the new low before the new high?"

rule: At -2 to -2.5 standard deviations, look for a retracement or a reversal.
quote: "when price reaches the negative 2 to negative 2.5 standard deviations, I'm looking for either a retracement or a reversal from this area"

rule: If price displaces and closes through -2 to -2.5, target the -4 (max expansion).
quote: "If price displaces and closes through this area, then I'm looking for the max expansion, or the negative 4 standard deviation."

rule: After max expansion (-4), mark premium/discount of the leg and look for a retrace to equilibrium.
quote: "Once hitting max expansion, what I can do is mark out a discount in premium of this leg here, and look for price to retrace to it in equilibrium."

rule: Pair projections with PD arrays (FVG, equal highs, liquidity) lining up with the levels.
quote: "I personally love to use these projections and then see if it lines up with equal highs or a fair value gap or some sort of PD array."

rule: Liquidity resting just before the -2 to -2.5 zone is the "low hanging fruit" first target.
quote: "Because this is just right above the negative 2 to 2.5 standard deviations, I consider this the low hanging fruit."

rule: Project each new manipulation leg too; overlapping levels from different projections add confluence.
quote: "when we get another manipulation leg, such as here, we can also project that out as well and get matching confluences"

rule: Strongest overlap example: one projection's -4 lining up with another's -2 to -2.5.
quote: "when the negative four from one projection lines up with the negative two to negative 2.5 of another projection"

rule: An order block's mean threshold near a projection level is a PD array confluence.
quote: "If we mark out the mean threshold of that, it will be right around the second standard deviation."

rule: For an FVG with equal lows, he looks for the near side of the FVG; also mark its consequent encroachment.
quote: "generally with a fair value gap like this, I'd be looking for the near side here as we have equal lows"

rule: You can mark the consequent encroachment of the -2 to -2.5 zone as a target.
quote: "another thing you can do is mark out the consequent encroachment of these. Standard deviations."

rule: Classic sell week: Tuesday high into a daily FVG, Wednesday expansion lower, expect Thursday to continue lower.
quote: "Anticipating a classic sell week with a Tuesday high, I'm anticipating Thursday to continue lower."

rule: Top-down: find the HTF manipulation leg into the POI on the hourly chart and project it for the overall target.
quote: "Where is the manipulation on this time frame into that daily fair value gap?"

rule: Asia consolidation, London aggressive move out and back into the range = accumulation, manipulation, so anticipate distribution.
quote: "Asia consolidation, London moves aggressively lower, and then back into the range, accumulation, manipulation, so anticipating distribution"

rule: When London is retracing within the weekly profile, expect New York to move into the projection target.
quote: "since London is retracing in terms of the weekly profile, I'm anticipating New York to move lower into this 2 to 2.5 standard deviation area"

rule: London low resting just above -2 SD on the LTF projection is the target (low-hanging fruit).
quote: "what do we have resting just above negative 2 standard deviation? We have our London low."

rule: Entry: retest of the order block after displacement below it, stop on the high, target the London lows.
quote: "the first entry I would be looking for is a retest of this order block here, my stop on this high"

rule: Displacement = large aggressive candles with closes at their high or low.
quote: "displacement is just large aggressive candles with closes in the high or the low"

rule: Displacement only counts when it happens over structure (through a swing high/low).
quote: "Displacement candle, but you want to see it over structure."

rule: A sweep of a low that immediately returns into the range is a lack of displacement, not a structure break.
quote: "you can see we move below immediately back into the range"

rule: Failing to displace below a short-term low after taking a high means price likely goes higher to the next highs.
quote: "We fail to displace even below this short-term low. That means we're likely to go higher to these highs."

rule: Prefer waiting for a higher-timeframe low (not a tiny 1m low) to be broken before calling displacement.
quote: "I prefer to wait for a higher timeframe low to be broken. And there's our displacement down."

rule: Displacement down through structure flips the state from buy side of the curve to sell side of the curve.
quote: "So now we're going from buy side of the curve. To sell side of the curve."

rule: In a bearish leg, each low aggressively broken means continuation lower.
quote: "aggressively broke below it. That means we're going to continue lower."

rule: The lack of displacement on one side leans price toward the other side.
quote: "The lack to do so on each side leans in the other direction."

rule: Failing one side of a range means expect the other side: broadening formation / power of three (consolidation, manipulation, distribution).
quote: "You fail one side of the range, you want to see the other side of the range."

rule: A break through that does not sustain and immediately moves back in is a BPR on the lower timeframe.
quote: "We immediately aggressively move back in. So on a lower timeframe, that's your BPR."

rule: After displacement down, a small FVG that lines up with the breaker can be the short entry.
quote: "This little fair value gap here. It also lines up with that breaker. That could be your short entry."

rule: Price struggling to reach back into the FVG / POI after displacement is a sign of continuation.
quote: "We're struggling to reach into this. That is a good sign that we're likely to go lower, continue lower."

rule: In a bullish leg, take lows that are swept without displacement as long entries.
quote: "you want to see lows taken without displacement, and that can give you entries to get long"

rule: In a bearish leg, failures to displace over highs are short entries.
quote: "when you're on the sell side of the curve, when you fail to displace over highs, This can be your short entries"

rule: Projections are mechanical targets used as confluence to existing liquidity targets.
quote: "They are mechanical targets and I personally use them as a confluence to existing liquidity targets."

rule: Fibonacci settings: 1, 0, -1, -2, -2.5, -4, -4.5 (add others if they work for you).
quote: "we'll want to mark out a 1, 0, 1 [-1], -2, -2.5, -4, and -4.5."

rule: Projections are always drawn within candle 2 at the reversal point.
quote: "it's always going to be within candle 2 at the reversal point."

rule: After the CISD, the manipulation leg is from the extreme to the swing that made it (bullish: the low and the high that made it); anchor at the extreme and drag to that swing.
quote: "once we have a change in the state of delivery, I'm going to look for that low and then I'm going to find the high that made that low"

rule: Normal-size manipulation leg: target -2 to -2.5; if expanding, -4 to -4.5.
quote: "I'm generally looking for price to reach to the -2 or -2.5. if price is going to expand the -4 to4.5."

rule: Pair projection levels with liquidity targets in that area; projections are confluence.
quote: "So I will look for liquidity targets in that area to be paired with"

rule: Large manipulation leg (very large opposing run / CISD): target only the -1; -2 to -2.5 is too much range.
quote: "When I have a large manipulation leg, I'm not looking for price to reach for that -2 to -2.5. That is just too much range."

rule: He prefers projections on the hourly chart for the daily range.
quote: "I personally love to use this on the hourly chart for the daily range."

rule: After the first projection/liquidity target, a good closure of the next HTF candle lets you look for candle 4 continuation (shallow wick into the highs).
quote: "if we get a nice closure on this next week's candle, then we can look for the fourth candle in the swing to trade higher as well."

rule: Projections can be used alone where there is no liquidity (e.g. all-time highs).
quote: "if you do not have liquidity in a certain area, you can use those projections as a target."

rule: When -2 to -2.5 lines up with previous day high and liquidity to the left, that is good confluence.
quote: "the -2 to -2.5 is also lining up with this previous day's high as well as the liquidity to the left."

rule: Lower expectations when the reversal is not clean and the range is small; a huge projection late in the New York session is unreasonable → use -1.
quote: "It's not very reasonable for late into this New York session to anticipate YM to just go 500 to 600 points."

rule: A manipulation leg near half of the range to the target is "large"; then target -1, not -4.
quote: "Our range or our target is right here. And our manipulation leg is almost half of that."

rule: If price does not reverse off the -1 target, look for expansion to the next projections.
quote: "if we're not going to reverse off this high, that's when we can look for price to expand further to our next targets."

rule: Need a CISD before drawing projections after a new candle 2 closure.
quote: "We have yet to form a change in the state of delivery. So we need to wait for that."

rule: The TTrades indicator can draw projections automatically (settings toggle).
quote: "if I use my indicator, I can just go into the settings here and I will turn on the projections."

rule: When -2 to -2.5 sits just before a liquidity point, take profit at the liquidity point rather than holding for the final target.
quote: "I like to take my profit at that liquidity point prior to the final target"

rule: In a consolidation, the -1 is the liquidity point internal to the range; pay attention to it.
quote: "if price is going to remain in a consolidation, this is where I'm going to want to actually pay attention to this negative one target"

rule: The method is AM Trades' version of standard deviation projections.
quote: "This is the way that my friend AMTrades showed me, and so that is what we will be going over."

rule: Setup context: price runs to an HTF PD array, forms a short-term high, moves over it and back into the range, shifting structure bearish.
quote: "I want a short-term high formed, move over that high, and then back into the range, shifting structure bearish."

rule: The manipulation leg is the move that took those highs; draw the fib from high to low over it and project targets.
quote: "I am then looking for this area right here, the move that took those highs as our manipulation leg."

rule: Targets: the 2-2.5 standard deviations, then the 4th.
quote: "Ideally, I'm looking for the 2 to 2.5 standard deviations as a target and then the fourth standard deviation as a target."

rule: Take profit at areas of liquidity that line up with those projection levels.
quote: "Area of liquidity that lines up in those areas to take profit."

rule: After the 4th SD is hit, look for a retracement back into the range if it makes sense (e.g. original consolidation run, no further displacement).
quote: "after price hits this fourth standard deviation is look for a retracement back into the range if it makes sense."

rule: Find the manipulation leg on the lower timeframe (5m) where a short-term high was broken before price came back down and shifted structure.
quote: "where did we make a short term high and price break through that high before coming back down and shifting structure bearish?"

rule: Draw from the high of the manipulation leg to its low and project.
quote: "draw from the high of that to the low of it and use our projection to project out our targets."

rule: If price does not keep displacing at a projection target, it can be an area to expect a reversal.
quote: "if we don't continue to displace down, this is an area where we could expect a reversal."

rule: A short-term low that holds (no close below) at a PD array followed by aggressive displacement defines a bullish manipulation leg.
quote: "Price does not close below here and gets an aggressive displacement move out. So where is our manipulation leg?"

rule: A projection level (2.5) that lines up with a high is confluence that the high will be reached.
quote: "Our 2.5 lines up almost exactly with this high. So that is good confluence to believe that we are likely to reach for this high."

rule: Lower timeframe use: sweep of a short-term low into an HTF POI (4H FVG), displacement back out, confirm with higher highs and higher lows, then project.
quote: "Okay, now we're starting to get higher highs and higher lows. So where is our manipulation leg? Right here."

rule: For a bullish leg, draw the fib from low to high.
quote: "where would we draw our FIV [fib] from this low to this high?"

rule: The manipulation leg is the move that swept the lows (bullish case).
quote: "That's the move that swept these lows."

rule: Expecting a bullish PM session: want a lunch retracement and a dip into the FVG before/at the PM session to go higher.
quote: "I wanted a retracement during lunch, and then before the PM session or right as it starts, I would want a dip down into this fair value gap to go higher."

rule: Target buy-side liquidity or the standard deviation target.
quote: "I could target our buy side liquidity or our standard deviation target."

rule: Relative strength/weakness: comparing two assets, one is more bullish or bearish than the other.
quote: "Relative strength or weakness is when comparing two assets, one is more bearish or bullish than the other."

rule: Judge relative strength from swing points, candle closures and candle size.
quote: "the main things I look for in judging relative strength or weakness is swing points as well as candle closures and the size of the candle"

rule: At a shared swing point, the index that takes it is stronger; the one that does not get close is weaker.
quote: "ES takes out this swing point, NQ does not even get close"

rule: A bigger candle away from the same level marks the weaker (down) or stronger (up) index.
quote: "not a very big candle down, while NQ gets this massive drop"

rule: At an order block, the index that respects the mean threshold and pushes away is in control of that side; the one trading through it is the other.
quote: "price respects the mean threshold of it"

rule: Look for short setups on the relatively weaker index and long setups on the relatively stronger index.
quote: "if I'm looking for short setups, I know that NQ will generally present a cleaner and better short setup, while ES will present a better and cleaner long setup"

rule: SMT (divergence at a swing between correlated assets) can signal a reversal and also show relative strength.
quote: "This divergence can signify not only a reversal, but also can be used to show relative strength."

rule: Chart ES divided by NQ in TradingView: bullish ratio = ES stronger / NQ weaker; bearish ratio = ES weaker / NQ stronger.
quote: "If it is bullish, I know that ES has the relative strength and NQ has the relative weakness."

rule: When price sweeps a low, the index that closes back inside the range / body of the order block is stronger; the one closing outside is weaker.
quote: "we close outside the body of this order block"

rule: Use CE (50%) of a wick or FVG to compare how far each index reaches.
quote: "ES almost reaches that consequent encroachment, while NQ is nowhere close to that"

rule: With a bullish weekly expectation, expect ES stronger/NQ weaker each day, and drop to lower timeframes to short NQ into its HTF level or long ES from its POI.
quote: "Understanding that NQ is relatively weaker to ES, I would be looking for short setups on NQ down into last month's low"

rule: In an FVG, bodies respecting consequent encroachment then displacement away confirms that side.
quote: "NQ reaches up, the bodies respect the consequent encroachment, we put in a up-close candle, displaced lower"

rule: Theory: a reversal on the ES/NQ chart shows a change in correlation and can anticipate a reversal on ES or NQ.
quote: "reversals on the ES and Q comparison chart can be used to show the change in correlation and used to anticipate a reversal on ES or NQ"

rule: An ES/NQ reversal is "an SMT without an SMT" and sometimes leads the actual reversal.
quote: "it's kind of like an SMT without an SMT"

rule: Pairing: daily for bias, 4h for the swing point, 15m for entry.
quote: "the daily for bias and then using the 4 hour for a swing point and the 15-minute time frame for entry"

rule: Daily bias need not be a candle 2 closure, but that is the easiest way to get it.
quote: "this doesn't have to be a candle to closure, but this is specifically the easiest way to get that daily bias"

rule: Daily bias setup: price at a POI (low, high or FVG), then a candle 2 closure inside the FVG or a reversal candle closing back inside the previous candle's range; trade the next day (candle 3) expansion.
quote: "Or for a reversal candle to close back inside its previous candle's range."

rule: Use the 4h for the swing point and the daily profile; let the daily wick form (bullish: open, trade lower first), then trade the body toward the draw.
quote: "our goal is to let the wick of the daily candle form"

rule: Identify the daily wick with a 4h candle 2 or candle 3 closure.
quote: "we are either going to look for a candle 2 or a candle 3 closure where we anticipate that wick 2 form"

rule: A London 4h candle 2 closure with bias -> anticipate 6am and 10am candles to expand; 10am depends on a strong 6am close; trade the third expansion candle only if the draw on liquidity is unmet.
quote: "we'd only look to trade this third expansion candle if the drawn liquidity has yet to be met"

rule: Every candle 2 closure needs a CISD on the lower timeframe.
quote: "when we have a candle 2 closure, what do we need to check for on the lower time frames? A change in the state of delivery"

rule: Inside the candle 3, again let its wick form: want price to open and make a low "we can trust" out of a POI (sweep into FVG, V-shaped reversal, CISD inside the candle).
quote: "Ideally, go make a low or a low we can trust. Where would that be? Out of a point of interest."

rule: You are trading candle 3s across multiple timeframes; the easiest expansions come from candle 3 on daily and 4h together.
quote: "The easiest expansions occur when you trade candle 3 on multiple different time frames."

rule: On the 15m he waits for a continuation rather than trading the reversal or placing a limit, to save the loss if price falls through.
quote: "I would rather just wait for it to react or not react and save myself a loss than to place a limit"

rule: Continuation = after down-close candles into an FVG (and a sweep of a low), a close over them; entry at market on the new open, stop at the protected low, 2R or HTF objectives.
quote: "My entry is at the market of the new open. My stop is at that protected low"

rule: After many days of one-way expansion without a swing (7 days on gold), expect a retracement or reversal.
quote: "we have not had a swing in 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 days. So that is where we can get a retracement or a reversal"

rule: A 4h candle that does not close as a candle 2 means wait for a new high to be taken and a new closure.
quote: "We need to wait for a new high to be taken and a new closure."

rule: After a bearish 4h candle 2, the 15m should respect the lower half of that 4h candle.
quote: "what do we want to see be respected? The lower half of this 4hour candle"

rule: Target the previous day's low/high and get on side before it is taken.
quote: "We could be looking for this previous day's low, right? That is a pretty good target"

rule: The continuation forms when price closes through the series of candles that went into the POI.
quote: "once we get the closure through those, that is when we form the continuation"

rule: Bearish continuation stop: on the high or on the bodies that made the high.
quote: "put our stop either on the high or on the bodies that made the high"

rule: Easiest alignment: daily candle 3 + 4h candle 3 + 15m protected swing; a daily reversal candle is also tradable if you understand wick size.
quote: "the easiest way to do that is to trade a daily candle 3 with a 4hour candle 3 and then a protected swing on the 15-minute chart"

rule: After a weekly expansion candle, price should respect 50% of it to continue; on the daily, should not trade much below 50% of the swing down-close candle.
quote: "we wouldn't really want to see price trade much below 50% of this down candle"

rule: When HTF bullish but the day opens bearish, want the previous day low taken and then price into the highs; a 4h candle that is not bullish is not yet a reversal.
quote: "Now, is this a bullish candle? No. So, I would not consider this a reversal."

rule: If price takes out the low before the CISD inside candle 3 forms, keep the idea while the same area is respected and wait for a new candle 2 closure.
quote: "So now we're not going to change our idea. We're still bullish as we're respecting the same area."

rule: After targets/highs are taken, price often retraces into the range, into a gap or running the previous low that made the high, before continuing.
quote: "if we take out this target here, we're going to come back in and run out a low before trading back higher"

rule: A new protected swing in candle 3 is the new invalidation; enter on the open of candle 4 with the stop on the low.
quote: "So that is giving us a new invalidation. So we can look to trade on the open of candle 4"

rule: Large R:R comes from a lower-timeframe invalidation with a higher-timeframe target (over 8R here), though his default is 2R.
quote: "this is how you get large risk-to-reward trades is when you're taking a lower time frame invalidation and targeting a higher time frame target"

rule: Unless price stays in consolidation, it reaches for PDH, PDL, or both.
quote: "it is going to reach for previous day high or previous day low."

rule: Stay out of consolidations; trending up -> anticipate PDH taken, trending down -> PDL taken.
quote: "if price is trending up, I can anticipate previous day high being taken."

rule: The easiest trend definition: bullish trend keeps taking PDH, bearish trend keeps taking PDL.
quote: "Price will continue to take previous days high over and over again."

rule: PD arrays supporting price higher keep the PDH draw in play.
quote: "we have PD arrays supporting price higher. So I'd anticipate price to keep reaching for previous days high."

rule: If PDL is not taken in a downtrend, a retracement into a FVG can come first; a down-close candle respecting its consequent encroachment resumes the PDL draw.
quote: "we get a down close candle respecting the consequent encroachment of this fair value gap."

rule: Trends are not always clean: retracements and sweeps leave series of up-close candles (order blocks).
quote: "we're going to have a series of up-close candles creating order blocks."

rule: First question on the daily chart: is price more likely to reach PDH or PDL?
quote: "the first question I ask myself, is price more likely to reach previous days high or previous days low?"

rule: Answering that gives the draw on liquidity and target; then frame an entry at a lower-timeframe POI toward it.
quote: "If I can answer this question, I then have a draw on liquidity and a target"

rule: Failure to displace over PDH gives a downward bias toward PDL; failure below PDL gives a bias back into the range.
quote: "when we fail to displace over previous days high, That gives me a downwards bias looking for previous day's low."

rule: A candle displacing below lows means continuation: next day reaches for the new PDL.
quote: "since this candle displays below these lows, I'm anticipating a continuation of the trend"

rule: Look back three days for previous highs and lows.
quote: "The last thing I'm going to touch on is how many days I will look back for previous day's high and low. And for me, that is three days"

rule: Extended prior-day levels add confluence: a deviation below PDL, back into range and retest of PDL before continuing higher (box setup).
quote: "when we deviate below this previous day low, come back into the range, we retest this previous day low before continuing higher"

rule: In live trading he also targets extensions beyond PDH/PDL, not only the level itself.
quote: "when I'm actually watching price I will look for extensions beyond and below previous day high and low."

rule: Taking both PDH and PDL with a bearish close and a reach into a daily FVG -> bias to PDL.
quote: "Here we take previous day high and low, we close bearish, and we also reach into this daily fair value gap."

rule: An up-close candle does not change a bearish idea after a reach into a daily FVG and displacement lower.
quote: "So here we get an up close candle, but my idea hasn't changed."

rule: In bearish structure, a sweep of PDL with a close back inside is not automatically long; want a close below the up-close candle to validate it as an order block.
quote: "with the structure being bearish, I ideally want to see price close below this up close candle."

rule: After lows are run and price closes back inside, expect PDH or a consolidation.
quote: "I'd want to see price reach up to this previous day high or get some sort of consolidation after running these lows."

rule: Having a bias almost every day does not mean an entry every day.
quote: "even though that I had a bias for almost every day here, it does not mean that I will find an entry each and every day."

rule: Consolidation through Asia and London plus a manipulation down into New York = accumulation, manipulation; expect distribution into PDH.
quote: "seeing this as accumulation, manipulation, I'd want to see distribution higher into this previous day high."

rule: Entry: 5m FVG, stop at the low, target PDH (about 2R).
quote: "looking to enter on the fair value gap, I stop in the low, and then targeting this high, I have a risk to reward of just about 2R."

rule: If Asia already took PDH (the target), skip the New York session.
quote: "with that already being taken in the Asia session, I am not interested into the New York session."

rule: 8:30 news can be the manipulation leg; distribution is the opposite of the manipulation, into PDH.
quote: "And that is 830 news, which manipulates down."

rule: Before entering, want a close below the 8:30 opening price and the down-close series, then a retest of the manipulation (box setup).
quote: "Ideally, I'd want to see a close below this 830 opening price and this series of down close candles here."

rule: Even with a clear draw on liquidity, an entry is not always possible.
quote: "even with daily bias or a clear drawn liquidity, it's not always possible to get an entry."

rule: Pick one system and follow it; hopping between models destroys consistency.
quote: "Too many people bounce around from model to model and then cannot find consistency"

rule: Price cannot reverse without a swing point (bullish swing point to turn up, bearish to turn down).
quote: "this model is built off the fact that price cannot reverse without a swing point"

rule: Swing points at a POI plus specific candle closures let you anticipate the expansion candles that follow.
quote: "if we look for these swing points to form at a point of interest and look for certain candle closures, we can anticipate expansion candles"

rule: Daily bias: a daily close outside the previous range = continuation (close above PDH bullish, below PDL bearish).
quote: "If price has a closure outside the range, we're going to be looking for a continuation."

rule: Daily reversal bias: sweep the PDL and close back above it = bullish next day; sweep the PDH and close back below = bearish.
quote: "We have price sweeping out its previous day low and closing back above that low"

rule: Look for the POI inside the previous day's range.
quote: "I'm going to look for that in the previous range of the previous day"

rule: POIs are always an FVG or a low (bullish) / an FVG or a high (bearish).
quote: "points of interest are always going to be either a fair value gap or a low in a bullish scenario"

rule: Wait for price to reach the POI and print a candle 2 or candle 3 closure, with a draw on liquidity (e.g. PDH) identified.
quote: "wait for price to reach into that point of interest and have either a candle 2 or a candle 3 closure"

rule: Timeframe pairing: swing point on 1h -> 5m; on 30m -> 3m.
quote: "if that swing point was on the hourly, I'd be using the 5minut. If it's on the 30 minute, I'd be using the 3minut."

rule: Check the CISD (confirms the swing point) but do not enter on it; wait for another continuation.
quote: "we're not going to enter on that change in the state of delivery. We're going to wait for another continuation."

rule: Continuation order block = sweep of a low into an FVG (POI) and then a close through the series of down-close candles (mirror for shorts).
quote: "we get the close through the series of downclo candles. This is a continuation order block"

rule: Enter on that close, stop on the protected low, target 2R.
quote: "look to enter on that close through my stop on that protected low and then look for 2 R"

rule: Multiple days of expansion without a new swing point -> look for a retracement or reversal.
quote: "when we have multiple days of an expansion without a new swing point, I can be looking for a retracement or a reversal"

rule: After a bearish reversal day, expect the next day's high (wick) to form within the lower half of the previous day's range; catch it with a candle 2/3 closure or wait for a continuation.
quote: "we'd want to look at the lower half of this previous day's range and look for price to form its wick"

rule: After a bearish CISD, the 5m should respect the lower half of the CISD leg for continuation lower; if price trades high into equal highs, do not short.
quote: "We'd want to see the lower half of this change in the state of delivery be respected"

rule: A reversal very close to the high is hard to trust; wait for a V-shaped reversal then a continuation, otherwise it often fails and runs the swing point.
quote: "it's very hard for me to trust this reversal so close to this high"

rule: Price sometimes runs a protected swing or a new short-term high before going lower; wait for the next continuation close.
quote: "this is where we sometimes will run out a protected swing or a new high to then go lower"

rule: Bearish stop: on the body high or the actual high (either works); entry on close or retest.
quote: "Put my stop on the body high or the actual high. Either one works."

rule: Use a lower-timeframe invalidation with HTF targets (PDL, daily FVG) for greater R:R.
quote: "use a lower time frame invalidation and still target those higher time frame objectives"

rule: Do not fade a bullish monthly candle 2 near month end, especially with equal highs above.
quote: "I don't want to fade that month, especially with these equal highs resting above"

rule: The model is fractal: 1M-1D-1h works like 1D-1h-5m; you may enter on the hourly without refining lower.
quote: "sometimes I just prefer to not refine it down too much"

rule: An FVG reach without a close over the down-close candles is not a continuation (it becomes consolidation); wait for a close over.
quote: "Do we close over these down close candles to form a continuation? No."

rule: Prefer the retest over the close right after price took out nearby highs (expect a retracement); stop on full-bodied candles' bodies.
quote: "I'd rather take it on the retest. Why is that? Well, we just took out these highs here."

rule: Repeated failure to form a continuation = a range/consolidation; avoid it until one side is taken, then look for a continuation or order block there.
quote: "When we fail to form a continuation multiple times, this is just becoming a range"

rule: Trading a consolidation after one side is taken is a reversal day, more complex; do not force messy markets, trade only clear examples.
quote: "Don't try to force yourself on the market."

rule: Do not trade the smart money reversal leg itself; wait for the new dealing range and trade the re-accumulation phase that follows.
quote: "we're going to look for setups in the reaccumulation phase not in the smart money reversal"

rule: Frame setups with 4h, 1h and 15m and execute on the 15m.
quote: "we're going to be using the 4H Hour 1 hour and 15 minutes to frame a setup and we're going to enter on the 15 minute"

rule: Alternative pairing: with 4h structure as the range, you may enter on the 1h instead of the 15m.
quote: "you can also enter on the 1 hour time frame if you're using 4our structure"

rule: A high-probability SMR (bullish) requires a higher-timeframe key level in discount plus SMT at that level.
quote: "we want to be looking for a higher time frame key level with smt in discount"

rule: Six-step flow (bullish): HTF key level -> SMT at it -> HTF dealing range premium/discount -> 4h raid into discount key level -> 1h change in state of delivery -> 15m discount entry; mirror for bearish.
quote: none

rule: Order pairing: the market raids sell stops below an old low and then pairs them with buy stops above the range high (and vice versa); this defines the draw.
quote: "order pairing means um the market moves from sell stops"

rule: A displacement away from the raided low that leaves a bullish FVG and disrespects an up-close candle (bearish OB) indicates the buy side of the curve.
quote: "this displacement over here indicates that we are going into buy side of the curve"

rule: On the 1h, mark the opposing (bearish) array; a close through it means you are on the buy side of the curve (mirror for shorts).
quote: "you're going to Mark out a bearish array which should not get violated and when it does get violated"

rule: When a bearish array is violated and a bullish order block forms in the same area, treat it as "all selling into you buying", a strong buy-side confirmation.
quote: "called all selling into you buying"

rule: On the 15m, no PD array is required: once the 1h range is confirmed, buy in discount (sell in premium) of the new range; an FVG is preferred but optional.
quote: "you can just literally Buy in discount"

rule: When executing on the 15m, stay within the New York kill zone.
quote: "if you stick within the correct time right New York Kill Zone"

rule: Stop loss goes below the low that was raided (long); above the dealing range high (short).
quote: "put your stop loss below the low which got rated"

rule: Move to breakeven only after a new range forms (price makes a new leg that takes the prior range high), never earlier.
quote: "don't go break even too early you only go break even once there's a new Range formed"

rule: No kill zone is required when trading off 1h levels; kill zones apply only to 15m trading.
quote: "you don't require a Kill Zone once you trade 1our levels"

rule: Classify the play first: external-to-internal or internal-to-external range liquidity; for a short off an external high, target internal liquidity that sits in discount.
quote: "are we going from external to internal or we're going from internal to external"

rule: In a market maker sell model, wait for the "low-risk sell" to print at the key level before trading; then trade the first distribution leg.
quote: "wait for the low RIS cell to print first"

rule: Mark the New York midnight opening price for daily profiles; a classic sell day manipulates above it, expands lower, retraces in NY without violating the high, then expands lower again.
quote: "you want to see a manipulation above above the New York midnight opening price and then expansion lower"

rule: Forex entries no later than 12:00 (NY); commodities such as US oil may be entered later (example window ~12:00-14:00).
quote: "with Forex I would not enter past 12 p.m."

rule: Preferred 15m trigger: turtle soup (raid) of a short-term high/low inside the bigger range, entered from premium/discount of the new 15m range.
quote: "Turtle souping a high within a bigger range often gives a very strong reaction"

rule: If there is no short-term high to raid, short above the 0.5 (equilibrium) of the range with stop above the dealing range high.
quote: "if there's no short-term high you can just literally short above the 0.5 line"

rule: Hold for higher-timeframe targets even if the in-range RR looks under 2R.
quote: "you will hold for a longer period of time because you're targeting higher time frame levels"

rule: Start top-down analysis on the monthly; on Mondays let the day play out before deciding the week.
quote: "start off on the monthly as always"

rule: If Asia trends in the trade direction already, London becomes less favourable; focus on New York.
quote: "Asia was kind of trending higher this makes London session a little bit more unfavorable"

rule: When price raids external range liquidity in profit, take a partial (half) and move to breakeven.
quote: "this is the perfect example of taking a partial"

rule: Phase reading always starts from an expansion; every new expansion restarts the process.
quote: "We are always going to start with expansion." (01:34)

rule: Expansion followed by retracement is a continuation signature; expect another expansion in the same direction.
quote: "if we are going from expansion into retracement, that is a continuation signature, and we'd want to see expansion from that retracement."

rule: Expansion into consolidation is continuation or reversal depending on whether the range is manipulated (expansion against, met by expansion) or broken out of.
quote: "if we have expansion into consolidation that can be a continuation or a reversal signature depending on if we manipulate or break out of the range."

rule: Expansion met with expansion in the opposite direction is a reversal; after it, look for continuation in the new direction.
quote: "if we go from expansion met with expansion that is a reversal then we are looking for price to continue in that direction after the reversal."

rule: A slow, shallow counter-move that is then closed through (close below the series of up-close candles) is a retracement.
quote: "we get a slow shallow move higher and then we go and close below that series of up close candles. So that is a retracement."

rule: If a few counter candles could be retracement or reversal, let more candles print before deciding.
quote: "That would be either a retracement or a reversal. If I don't know, I can let some more candles print to tell me."

rule: A close over the series of down-close candles into an important level creates a protected low to trade away from.
quote: "once we close over those series of downlosed candles into an important level, we create a protected low that I can trade away from."

rule: Blend the phases with daily bias: bullish wants a manipulation of consolidation lows (or breakout of highs + retracement); bearish wants a manipulation of the highs.
quote: "Because I am bullish, I want to see a manipulation of the lows to trade it higher or a breakout of the highs, a retracement, and then a continuation."

rule: If not in the move before the highs are taken, wait for a continuation signature (retracement with protected swing, or consolidation low manipulation) before entering.
quote: "if I'm not in this move before these highs are taken, I'm going to want to wait for a continuation signature"

rule: In a true expansion, price should not retrace much.
quote: "if we are expanding I don't want to see price retrace that much. I just want to see it go."

rule: Do not flip the daily bias intraday just because a low is taken; the only way to form a reversal is expansion opposite.
quote: "I'm not going to just switch my bias because of this. I'm still bullish as I determined earlier in the day."

rule: A strong candle close is not enough; require a CISD and pair it with the daily OHLC.
quote: "Now we have a nice candle closure here. But there is no change in the state of delivery yet."

rule: Highest-conviction reversal = daily candle closure reversal + CISD + expansion met with expansion, all at once.
quote: "A change in the state of delivery that tells us reversal as well as paired with that expansion met with an expansion"

rule: After a reversal, the long idea is invalidated if a new expansion-met-with-expansion takes out the reversal low.
quote: "When is this invalidated this idea? Well, if we have expansion met with expansion, then this low gets taken out."

rule: After a daily closure outside the range (continuation expected), only accept a retracement or a consolidation low run; a reversal off previous day high invalidates the idea.
quote: "If we frame a reversal off previous day high, that then invalidates it for me. It is not aligned with my bias."

rule: Reversals are expected only at relevant highs/lows, so do not expect reversal mid-range on the way to the target.
quote: "reversals occur at highs and lows that are relevant. So I'm not expecting price to just reverse here."

rule: If price takes a long time to close over the FVG, treat it as consolidation and demand a run of a low before going long.
quote: "I'm demanding a run of a low if I'm trying to get long in here."

rule: No protected swing means no trade; accept missing that move.
quote: "I'm not going to catch this long because it doesn't form a protected swing for me."

rule: Do not trade an intraday reversal until the daily closure also aligns; that wait filters out counter-bias reversals.
quote: "I'm waiting for the daily closure to also align, similar to how we did down here."

rule: In a bearish retracement, price must not trade over EQ; a high must form below it or the idea is invalid.
quote: "I don't want to see price trade over the EQ. So, really, this is the last area that I want to see price form a high in or it's invalid for me."

rule: A retracement that does not form a protected swing is reclassified as consolidation.
quote: "Is this a retracement? Yes. But does it form a protected swing? No. That means it's then a consolidation."

rule: A daily inside bar after an expansion makes it a consolidation; a sweep of the consolidation high targets its low or failure swings below.
quote: "this next day stays inside bar. So, now this is a consolidation."

rule: The 4H chart can profile the day: a 4H candle that sweeps the previous candle and fails to close above it is a candle 2 closure.
quote: "It is sweeping out the previous, failing to close above. So that's a candle 2 closure."

rule: Stop goes on the protected swing / reversal high; minimum target 2R, optionally extended to previous day low(s).
quote: "put my stop on this high and I can look for 2 R at a minimum or I have projection targets"

rule: When the stop on a protected swing gives poor R, he may measure risk from the candle bodies he does not expect price to exceed; 2R is the minimum requirement for a trade.
quote: "We do hit 2 R and we go quite a bit lower, but that is my minimum requirement for a trade."

rule: Trade the expansion phases: wait for the retracement to end, confirmed by HTF closure + CISD.
quote: "I wait for my higher time frame closure to align with that. Then when I have that change in the state of delivery paired with it"

rule: The phases are fractal: 1h can be the HTF and 5m the intraday timeframe.
quote: "It is a fractal concept, so I can use lower time frames."

rule: Shallow retracement that cannot get back into the range plus a bearish closure = continuation lower; a reversal needs expansion met back at the low.
quote: "Now if we get a retracement or a failure to go back into this range that's when we can get a new expansion lower"

rule: The model moves from external liquidity to internal liquidity on a smaller timeframe, paired with an MSS and SMT.
quote: "it is moving from external liquidity to internal liquidity on a smaller timeframe and pairing that with a market structure shift and SMT"

rule: Short: previous day high taken, target a 1h bullish FVG, 15m MSS + SMT, only short above midnight open.
quote: "Looking for a M15 market structure shift and SMT, and then looking to only short above midnight open"

rule: Long: previous day low taken, target a 1h bearish FVG, same MSS + SMT, only long below midnight open.
quote: "it would be previous days low, a one hour bearish fair value gap, and then the same market structure shift and SMT, and then only longing below midnight open"

rule: The model is fractal: daily/1h/15m can move up to weekly/4H/1H or down to lower timeframes.
quote: "I can move that up a timeframe to the weekly four hour and one hour, or I could move it down to the lower timeframes"

rule: Instead of a strict MSS he also accepts an inversion FVG or a change in the state of delivery (close over the last down-close candle).
quote: "although the model says a market structure shift, I will also look for an inversion or a change in the state of delivery"

rule: Choose the stop that still gives a 2R minimum to the hourly FVG target.
quote: "I want to have a 2R minimum, so that is what I would look to do."

rule: Choose the hourly FVG target with premium/discount in mind: prefer the one whose reach lines up with the range's equilibrium.
quote: "considering premium and discount of the range, reaching an equilibrium of the range would be somewhere above the start of this fair value gap"

rule: SMT with a correlated asset at the PDH/PDL raid (gold-silver, NQ-ES, NQ-YM, GBP pair-GBPCAD).
