quote: "Here's our purge of previous day low. And here we actually create an SMT with silver."

rule: Entry can be at the close of the MSS candle (if below midnight open) or on a retracement; retrace may give a better price.
quote: "I'm going to go ahead and just enter right on the close of this market structure shift candle as we're below midnight."

rule: Once price closes over a series of down-close candles (order block), he does not expect that low to be touched again.
quote: "Here we close over the series of downclosed candles, making an order block, so now I wouldn't anticipate this low being touched."

rule: Midnight open is drawn with the "ICT kill zones and pivots" indicator, all off except the midnight opening price.
quote: "the indicator I'm using to mark out midnight open is ICT kill zones and pivots"

rule: You may trade the weaker asset of an SMT pair for shorts; here he stays on NQ.
quote: "I could go look to trade ES or the weaker asset as we have an hourly fair value gap here"

rule: Variation: use the daily open instead of midnight open as the premium/discount filter.
quote: "instead of using midnight open, I use the daily open"

rule: An up-close series into the POI that sweeps liquidity becomes a bearish order block once closed below; stop above the opposing candles.
quote: "So if it gets closed below, that validates as an order block."

rule: Use three timeframes: higher for bias, middle for structure, lower for entry.
quote: "I am focused on three time frames a higher time frame for bias a middle time frame for structure and a lower time frame for entry"

rule: The structure timeframe must align with the bias first: wait for a CISD or market structure shift in the bias direction.
quote: "if my bias is bearish I want to wait for either a change in the state of delivery or a market structure shift"

rule: Once the structure timeframe is aligned, wait for a key level: FVG, high or low, or order block.
quote: "once this is bearish then I want to wait for a key level"

rule: At the key level, wait for the entry timeframe to shift to the bias (order block formation); all three aligned = expansion.
quote: "all three of my time frames from my lower time frame to my structural time frame to my bias are all aligned bearish and that is when expansion occurs"

rule: Pairings: weekly-4H, daily-1h, 4H-15m, 1h-5m, 30m-3m, 15m-1m.
quote: "I pair the weekly with the 4 Hour the daily with the 1 hour the 4 Hour with the 15 the 1 hour with the five"

rule: Bias comes from the structure timeframe's own higher pair (5m entry → 1h structure → daily bias; 1m entry → 15m → 4H).
quote: "I align my bias the same way as I would align my structure"

rule: CISD (shift in trend) = close through the series of up-close candles into the important level.
quote: "I use a change in the state of delivery which is the series of up close candles into that important level"

rule: Once the structure timeframe shifts, either trade the reversal or wait for a continuation entry (new order block after a retracement).
quote: "I could look to trade the reversal if I want now that the time frames are aligned or I could wait for another continuation"

rule: If the entry-timeframe close fails, track the new high and its new series of up-close candles; enter after the close below them.
quote: "we now make a new high with making a new high we now have a new series of up closed candles"

rule: Target 2R on the entry timeframe.
quote: "now I can look to Target 2 R on my entry time frame"

rule: You can also enter on the structure timeframe itself, using it for invalidation, to avoid getting caught up on lower timeframes.
quote: "taking an entry on the 4-Hour time frame and using a 4 hour chart for my invalidation as well"

rule: The goal is all timeframes aligned in one direction; that is when the aggressive expansion move comes.
quote: "the whole goal of catching expansions is to have all of my time frames aligned in One Direction"

rule: Reason for a setup: e.g. three days of expansion into an old high; a reversal would occur off the previous day high.
quote: "here we have 3 days of expansion into an old high"

rule: After the structure CISD, either enter or wait for the New York session or a lower-timeframe POI.
quote: "I could wait for the New York session or a lower time frame point of interest to be hit"

rule: A propulsion block is an order block formed off another order block.
quote: "this is now a propulsion block because it is an order block formed off of another order block"

rule: No entries until the structure timeframe shifts in the bias direction; then align the entry timeframe with it.
quote: "I'm not going to look for entries until my lower time frame or my structure time frame shifts in that direction"

rule: SMT can stand in for a sweep as lower-timeframe confirmation of a reversal (New York reversal with failure swings on the highs, daily profile).
quote: "we don't sweep out this low but we do have an smt"

rule: After the structure reversal, wait for a structure-timeframe POI (e.g. 30m bullish FVG) before dropping to the paired entry timeframe.
quote: "I want to wait for a point of interest to be hit on the 30 minute chart before dropping down to my aligned 3 minute chart"

rule: A consolidation whose high is swept should reach for its low (accumulation, manipulation, distribution).
quote: "if we sweep out the high of the consolidation what should we reach for the low of the consolidation"

rule: The structure CISD's lower half / mean threshold should be respected for continuation.
quote: "looking for the lower half or the mean threshold of that change in the state of delivery I want to see this area of respect to continue lower"

rule: Don't expect a reversal out of a consolidation that still respects 0.5 of the CISD; look for a propulsion block.
quote: "with this consolidation I'm not anticipating price to reverse from a consolidation"

rule: With aligned timeframes, draw runner targets from the structure / bias timeframe (hourly short-term low, daily consolidation low).
quote: "I can also draw targets from my hourly time frame"

rule: Top-down chain: daily chart for bias, a lower timeframe for the point of interest, another lower timeframe for the entry.
quote: "We know we started with the daily chart, and then from there, went to a lower timeframe to get a point of interest."

rule: Daily framing example: swing low, return to fill the daily FVG, then anticipate the move to sell-side liquidity below.
quote: "return to the fair value gap, fill the fair value gap here, and then he anticipates a move towards this sell side liquidity"

rule: Hourly: after the daily POI is reached, structure shifts bearish; the retrace into a breaker plus FVG is the POI.
quote: "we shift structure bearish. From here we get a retracement back up, reach into a breaker block plus the fair value gap"

rule: 5m: after reaching the hourly array, lower high/lower low trend, entry on a 5m FVG fill.
quote: "he takes an entry here on this five minute fair value gap fill, targeting lower prices."

rule: Failure to displace over a swing high suggests downside.
quote: "we fail to displace over this swing high, so that leads me to believe that there may be downside."

rule: Mark previous day high and low and the nearby daily order block (expected to resist if reached).
quote: "the next thing I'm going to mark out is previous day high and low, and I will also mark out this daily order block here."

rule: On the hourly, look for a POI that aligns with the daily bias.
quote: "I'm going to drop down to the hourly chart to see if I have a point of interest that aligns with my bias"

rule: Mark midnight open; note London sweeping highs without displacing above them.
quote: "London sweeps these highs, but can't displace above them, and we start to move lower."

rule: Into New York: move above the daily open, close back in, displace lower; that validates the hourly OB as the POI.
quote: "we get a move above the daily open, we close back in, and then we get displacement lower. Making and validating this order block."

rule: On the 5m, a high, low, higher high, lower low sequence marks the breaker; price should not return to the high.
quote: "What I see here is a high, low, higher high, lower low. So I'm going to mark out this candle here as a breaker block."

rule: Mark a minimum 2R before leaving runners.
quote: "I can mark out my minimum to R before I leave runners."

rule: Use the weekly profile and daily bias together, then drop to lower timeframes for entry.
quote: "I hope in this example, you can see how I use the weekly profile. And daily bias, and then using that daily bias, dropping down to the lower timeframes"

rule: For an up-close daily candle to become an OB, price should close and reach below the previous day low.
quote: "if this up-close candle is going to become an order block, I would like to see it close and reach below previous day low."

rule: Hourly OB confirmed by a close below after reaching below the low; target the previous day low.
quote: "Now I'd want to see this close below. There it closes below. So I'm anticipating this to support price lower to where? Previous day low"

rule: SMT at the high (one index sweeps, the other does not) is important confirmation; it stays valid while the high holds.
quote: "this is actually an SMT from this high down to here, which is important to note."

rule: Entry at the FVG consequent encroachment, stop on the high, target just beyond previous day low for minimum 2R.
quote: "use the consequent encroachment of it, and from here I can look for an entry. With my stop on this high, and my target just below our previous day low"

rule: Role summary: hourly OB = POI, SMT = confirmation, 5m entry targeting previous day low.
quote: "Here we have an hourly order block as our point of interest, SMT is confirmation, and then our five minute entry targeting our previous day low."

rule: If Tuesday made the high of the week, anticipate expansion lower into Wednesday and Thursday.
quote: "Tuesday has made the high week, so I'm anticipating expansion into Wednesday and Thursday."

rule: Price should not reach much higher than the hourly OB that rejected; bullish arrays respected on the way up into it are expected.
quote: "So I would not want to see price reach much higher than this order block here."

rule: Displacement paired with a breaker: on the return into it expect it to hold; minimum 2R, runners to the daily swing low.
quote: "There is displacement paired with a breaker, so if price returns back up into here, I would anticipate it to hold"

rule: Top-down depth depends on the entry timeframe; for 5m/1m/sub-1m entries he does not use monthly or weekly POIs.
quote: "If I am entering on the lower timeframe, such as five-minute, one-minute, and sub-one-minute timeframes, I'm not really gonna look for monthly or weekly points of interest"

rule: For LTF entries, POIs come from the daily, 4h, 1h and sometimes 15m.
quote: "Most of my points of interest lie on the daily, four-hour, one-hour, and sometimes the 15-minute chart."

rule: If entering on the 4h, look out to the weekly and other higher timeframes.
quote: "Going to trade or enter on the four hour timeframe, then I would look out to the weekly or other timeframes."

rule: Start on the daily and work down.
quote: "we will begin on the daily and work our way down"

rule: An order block that price cannot close above is respected.
quote: "we have an order block sitting here, which we respected as we couldn't close above it"

rule: After displacing under lows, check whether price falls back into the range or reaches lower; mark POIs for each case.
quote: "When we displace under lows right here, we want to see if we fall back into the range or reach lower."

rule: Mark daily blocks from the wick to the open; that is the most sensitive part.
quote: "I do include the wick to the open on these, as that is the most sensitive part"

rule: He trades the New York AM session.
quote: "I am going to move us to New York AM session, as that is what I trade"

rule: 4h POI: body to the wick of the series of up-close candles.
quote: "so I will mark out B. Body to the wick of those series of up close candles and that would be my four hour point of interest"

rule: With HTF POIs marked, use 15m / 5m / 1m to enter toward a POI or when price reaches a POI and moves away.
quote: "I will look at lower timeframes from the 15, 5, and 1 minute to look to either gain entries reaching for these points of interest or when we reach into a point of interest and move away from it"

rule: A run below previous lows into an FVG after the open, then aggressive move up, makes him bullish off the opening drive toward the HTF POI.
quote: "So with this idea in mind, I'm bullish off the opening drive move."

rule: If reaching for the 4h block, the 5m FVG should be respected.
quote: "if I'm under the mindset that we are reaching for this four hour block here, I'd want to see this being respected"

rule: If the 1m only offers a late entry, drop to a lower timeframe to enter inside the 1m/5m FVG for lower risk.
quote: "I don't really want to focus on just the one minute timeframe, because the only entry I would get is after closing or retesting these previous lows"

rule: A news spike that fails to close below the area confirms the long toward new highs.
quote: "We get a news event, but if you notice, we cannot close below this area, and then we reach for new highs."

rule: Trade from one POI to another using LTF setups to reduce risk.
quote: "that is how I would take a trade from one point of interest to another using lower timeframe setup to reduce my risk"

rule: At the POI, look for the 2022 model (liquidity run, break of structure, clean FVG), knowing it does not always appear.
quote: "We don't always get the liquidity run, break a structure, clean fair value gap setup."

rule: Use LTF setups within mitigation blocks or 15s FVGs for low-risk entries toward the objective.
quote: "we go to the 15 second timeframe and you can see we have fair value gaps in here, which give low risk entries to reach for the objective"

rule: At a target low: watch for displacement back into the range (higher), failure to displace back in, or continuation lower.
quote: "We want to look for either displacement back into the range, which would lead us higher, failure to displace back into the range, or displacement continuing to the downside."

rule: When the low is invalidated, look for LTF short entries (e.g. return to OTE) toward the daily block's open.
quote: "When this low is invalidated, I can look for Lower timeframe entries, reaching for that daily blocks open."

rule: He does not trade the afternoon session.
quote: "I do not trade the afternoon session."

rule: Order: daily, 4h, 1h, 15m to find the draw on liquidity, then LTF setups for entry.
quote: "I start at my daily timeframe, go to the 4-hour, 1-hour, 15, and once I know where my draw on liquidity is"

rule: Bearish breaker: high, low, higher high, lower low; mark the down-close candles from the high to the low as resistance.
quote: "a breaker block is a Candlestick pattern in which we have a high low higher high and lower Low"

rule: Bullish breaker: low, high, lower low, higher high; the up-close candles before the move to the lower low are support.
quote: "those up closed candles are what I want to see support price higher"

rule: The reversal breaker equals the CISD / shift of trend; the continuation breaker comes after it.
quote: "that is our change in the state of delivery or our shift of trend from bearish to bullish"

rule: A continuation breaker requires a sweep of a low (bullish) first, then a higher high to complete it.
quote: "what do we have to wait for we have to wait for a sweep of a low"

rule: Entry on the close or on the retest of the breaker; stop on the swing low.
quote: "I can look to take an entry on the close on the retest or just get in around here with my stop on the swing low"

rule: The low must be taken, unless SMT is present: then the low is protected and the up-close candles act as the breaker (the other asset formed the true breaker).
quote: "does it always have to take out the low and yes it does unless it is paired with smt"

rule: SMT-based breakers are more discretionary because no true breaker forms.
quote: "this is a little bit more discretionary as it doesn't form a true breaker"

rule: An intermediate-term low forms by sweeping a low or reaching into an FVG; the up-close candle before the FVG reach, once closed over, can be used ("not a breaker", but works).
quote: "many will say it's not a breaker and it really isn't but I do find that it works"

rule: Do not trust a range-low sweep until price trades away with bullish structure (closes over down-close candles).
quote: "I don't personally trust this low until we start to trade away and put in some bullish structure"

rule: Process: find a swing low, let it be run, let a breaker form, then enter.
quote: "I want to First find a swing low wait for the swing low to be ran out then let a breaker form and then look for an entry"

rule: In advanced market structure terms: short-term low swept, then another short-term low forms an intermediate-term low.
quote: "a short-term low a sweep of that and then anticipating another short-term low which forms an intermediate term low"

rule: When wicks are messy, define the breaker by candle bodies.
quote: "with these Wicks kind of everywhere I will focus on the bodies"

rule: Stop either on the swing low or the other side of the breaker.
quote: "my stop either on the low or the other side of the breaker"

rule: Do not trade the breaker at the reversal; let the reversal form and look for the breaker in the continuation.
quote: "I'm not looking for a breaker here I'm just letting this reversal form and I'm looking for a breaker in the continuation"

rule: Do not trust a sweep low into an FVG until a CISD closes through.
quote: "I don't personally trust this type of low until we get a change in the state of delivery"

rule: Expansion into consolidation: wait for a manipulation / purge of the consolidation lows before the long.
quote: "we have expansion into consolidation which case I'd want a manipulation to trade higher or a purge of the lows"

rule: Instead of getting caught in chop, wait for the sweep, then catch the expansion after the manipulation.
quote: "instead of getting caught in this chop just wait for a sweep of a low and then catch the move"

rule: A swing high formed after an expansion → look for continuation lower or an HTF retracement (bearish day).
quote: "if we have formed a swing high after expansion can be looking for a continuation lower or a retracement"

rule: Prefer waiting for bearish closures (sweep of previous candle's high, engulf) before shorting a breaker rather than blindly shorting.
quote: "I don't like to blindly short this"

rule: Targets: 2R or the HTF liquidity (lows/highs to the left, range high).
quote: "then I can look for two r or two [to] these lows to the left here"

rule: Refining to the LTF is optional; the hourly breaker alone would also have worked but took longer.
quote: "that is one way you can either refine it down or just use the current time frame you are on"

rule: 15m is paired with 1m for entries.
quote: "dropping down to the 1 minute time frame is that as our time frame pairing with the 15minute chart"

rule: After a CISD, the mean threshold (50%) should be respected; then it becomes a propulsion block that should also be respected.
quote: "price retraces into that is the mean threshold or 50% of this respected"

rule: Even late in the trend, wait for a continuation rather than picking a high.
quote: "even if I am a little bit late into the trend I'm not trying to to pick a high I'm waiting for a continuation"

rule: He prefers order blocks for continuations as simpler; breakers are an equally valid alternative.
quote: "although I prefer to just use order blocks as I find them more simple and easy you can use breaker blocks"

rule: Missing the reversal entry is not missing the move: a confirmed reversal lets you look for continuation entries.
quote: "if they miss the reversal entry they are left behind and that is simply not true"

rule: Prerequisite: a reversal sequence (purge + CISD) must have formed first.
quote: none

rule: After missing the first entry, let structure form and wait for the higher low (bullish) / lower high (bearish).
quote: "I just need to let some structure form and essentially waiting for that higher low to form"

rule: The continuation stop goes on the new swing low instead of the reversal low, improving RR.
quote: "position myself with my stop on this low instead of the reversal low"

rule: Two valid continuation triggers: a reaction out of a FVG, or a sweep of a low (high for shorts), each followed by a close through the series of opposing candles.
quote: "there are two types of entries I look for when seeking a continuation entry and that is a reaction out of a fair value gap or a sweep of a low"

rule: Exception: without a sweep or FVG tag, an opposing candle still counts if paired with SMT on a correlated asset (one sweeps, the other doesn't).
quote: "the only time price does not need to sweep out a low or reach into a fair value Gap is if we are using correlated assets and have an smt"

rule: When several FVGs could form the high, you need not predict which; let the high form and trade the order block that forms.
quote: "I don't need to know which one forms the high because I'm not looking to trade the high"

rule: Only take the position after the closure through the series of up-close candles (short) / down-close candles (long) into the important level.
quote: none

rule: With SMT, an earlier level (not yet tagging the FVG) may also be considered.
quote: "if this is paired with smt I can also consider this level here"

rule: Continuation entries are higher probability than the reversal entry because the swing is already confirmed; you trade the 1st or 2nd stage of distribution, not the low-risk sell.
quote: "I'm not trying to get the lowrisk sell but instead the first or second stage of distribution"

rule: After a large expansion day, a continuation should come from a shallow (non-aggressive) retracement.
quote: "if this is going to get a continuation we'd want to see a shallow retracement"

rule: Timeframe pairing used: 4h -> 15m; 1h -> 5m; 1D -> 1h.
quote: "since we were using the 4our chart we'll hop down to the 15minute time frame"

rule: Price may dig deeper into the level; wait for the close over the opposing candle regardless.
quote: "that's fine if it digs a little bit deeper just want to wait for the closure over that"

rule: Target 2R or the nearest high/low draw.
quote: "looking for 2 r or that high there"

rule: A retest of a fresh order block that forms another opposing candle into an important level gives another entry; that swing should then hold.
quote: none

rule: When the manipulation move is so large that the standard deviation projections do not make sense inside the range, target the PDL/PDH instead.
quote: "when you have a very large manipulation move and the projections do not make sense within the range"

rule: After a very aggressive displacement, entering at market with stop on the high gives poor RR to the first target; use a retest (limit) entry instead.
quote: "doesn't really make sense for my final Target or my first Target to enter on the market with my stop on the high"

rule: If no FVG tag or swing sweep occurs in the area, there is no mechanical setup; either wait for more structure or be discretionary.
quote: "mechanically speaking there is nothing here for me yet"

rule: A grind away without sweeps or FVG retests is a move he accepts missing.
quote: "this is just a move that I am going to miss"

rule: A close through an opposing candle that did NOT tag a FVG or sweep a swing is not a valid continuation candle.
quote: "some will consider this a continuation candle if we get closure below this now I do not"

rule: Prefer continuation entries taken before short-term targets are taken out.
quote: "I prefer the entries before our short-term targets are taking out"

rule: Trending price respects opposing candles: up-close candles in a downtrend, down-close in an uptrend.
quote: "when price is trending it's going to respect up Clos candles"

rule: Volume imbalances count as an important level when paired with a retest of another opposing candle.
quote: "I will consider are volume and balances as another Gap or an important level"

rule: The concept is fractal; the same continuation logic applies on daily/monthly.
quote: none

rule: Do not take a bullish LTF setup inside an expected bearish HTF candle (and vice versa); stops on such setups get run.
quote: "it doesn't make sense to be looking bullish when I'm anticipating price to continue bearish"

rule: Only trade LTF setups in the direction of the HTF expansion candle; align LTF with HTF and that is when expansion occurs.
quote: "this is aligning my lower time frames with my higher time frames and that is when expansion occurs"

rule: HTF bias example: a swing point that closes below the previous day low -> anticipate expansion lower.
quote: "we have formed a swing point we have closed below previous day low so I can anticipate price to expand lower"

rule: The intermediate (structure) timeframe is used to see a CISD form the HTF wick and to supply POIs for the LTF.
quote: "on an intermediate time frame I'm going to use this for structure"

rule: Roles: daily = bias, hourly = structure/supporting, 5m = entry.
quote: "the daily is where I will derive my bias my hourly will be my structure or my supporting time frame"

rule: A swept swing low becomes high-resistance liquidity; use 0.5 of its wick as support.
quote: "if I have high resistance liquidity as a low I will look to use 05 of the wick"

rule: On the structure timeframe, a CISD (close through the series of opposite-close candles that made the extreme) confirms the HTF wick has formed.
quote: "I'm going to be waiting for a change in the state of delivery here because that is what to me confirms this Wick has formed"

rule: A low that formed a new order block (opposing candles) in the price leg is not expected to be taken out.
quote: "I don't anticipate this low to get taken out because it has formed a new order block"

rule: If there is no FVG/POI in the leg, use a sweep of a previous low on the structure timeframe as the POI to drop down from.
quote: none

rule: Entry on the LTF CISD: enter on the retest or at market on the close, stop on the low, target 2R.
quote: "I could either look to take an entry right here on either a retest or the close at the market price look for two R"

rule: He prefers continuation entries: after the first CISD, wait for a new order block/propulsion block off a sweep of a low, enter at market, stop on the new (now protected) low.
quote: "My Stop on this new low because it is now protected"

rule: Inside an expected HTF expansion candle, let the HTF wick form first, then trade the body (open-high-low-close for bearish).
quote: "if we're going to have an expansion candle it will have small Wicks and a larger body"

rule: On the 4h, wait for price to reach into a POI (here a swept high overlapping an opposing candle) and close back inside the previous bar before looking for a setup.
quote: "I'd want to see price open reach a higher into a point of Interest before having a setup"

rule: Targets come from the structure timeframe: equal lows, previous lows (indicator), which also lined up with indicator standard deviations.
quote: none

rule: Entering on the close of the CISD candle is his preference over waiting for a retest; stop on the high that should hold.
quote: "I can either wait for a retest or just enter on the close which is my preference"

rule: Three timeframes are optional: you can execute on the structure timeframe (hourly) if the risk is manageable.
quote: "I don't need three time frames I cannot go lower if I can manage my risk"

rule: For a bullish day expect open-low-high-close: wait for the low to form (order block), a shallow run is preferred.
quote: "I would want to see price open low high close"

rule: A missed entry is not too late while the HTF target is unmet: wait for a new structure-timeframe setup (retrace into the order block, sweep, closure).
quote: "is it already too late well since I'm looking for price to trade to this highs it is not"

rule: Do not enter when price is too close to obvious lows (expect them to be taken); wait for a close over the leg and trade the next candle as the likely reversal.
quote: "I would not try to take a setup here because we're so close to these lows"

rule: Stop at least beyond the candle bodies or at the low; first target 2R, runners to HTF targets.
quote: "I want my stop at least on the bodies right or the low"

rule: After an expansion into an FVG, expect a new phase: consolidation, retracement or reversal; let a daily candle pass to decide.
quote: "I'm looking for a new phase of price delivery which will either be a consolidation a retracement or a reversal"

rule: Next daily close lower = reversal; close back inside the range = retracement (trade back to the highs).
quote: "if we close lower it's going to be a reversal to trade to these lows if we close back inside the range I'm viewing it as a retracement"

rule: A new propulsion block should hold; do not want a close below its main threshold.
quote: "I don't want to see a close below the main threshold of it"

rule: Refine the LTF entry to a newer order block that reaches into an FVG for better R:R; hold runners to hourly standard deviations or previous highs.
quote: none

rule: Trade expansion candles: a small wick (open near the extreme) supports a one-sided move; a large wick (opposing run, close near the open) does not.
quote: "We want to be trading expansion candles which have small wicks that support expansion."

rule: Candle 3 is traded following a reversal candle 2.
quote: "we want to trade following reversal candles when we are trading candle 3."

rule: If candle 2 has a small wick, trade candle 2 itself when a lower-timeframe CISD supports it.
quote: "if we had a small wick that is when we could look to trade candle 2 when supported by a change in the state of delivery on the lower time frame."

rule: If candle 2 has a large wick, let it close (back inside the previous candle's range) and wait for the open of candle 3 to join the expansion.
quote: "with a large wick like this I'm going to want to let this candle close."

rule: First lower-timeframe check: a CISD from the candle 2 extreme confirms the reversal, then look for continuation in candle 3.
quote: "from this high, do I have a change in the state of delivery? I do. So, now this confirms the reversal"

rule: Ideal candle 3 entry lets the higher-timeframe wick form and trades the body: wait for a continuation order block (open, sweep a high or reach a POI, opposing candle formation).
quote: "ideally, I'm going to want to let the wick form and then trade the body lower."

rule: Large-wick candle 2 already used much of its range; candle 3 covers similar distance in one direction.
quote: "And that is because we've already used a lot of range in candle 2."

rule: Do not trade candle 3 after a candle 2 expansion; that is where a new phase of price catches you.
quote: "We're not really going to want to focus on trading candle 3 when we have a candle 2 expansion"

rule: Continuation entry: if the first close-over fails, wait for a new low to form a new protected swing, then enter on the open of the candle after the close through the series of down-close candles, stop on the protected low, target 2R or projections.
quote: "we failed to close over that level, which means that we want to see a new low made to form a new protected swing."

rule: Prefer continuation days after a reversal day (e.g. Tuesday reversal, Wednesday continuation): continuations are easier to trade.
quote: "I'm going to look to trade that continuation on Wednesday cuz continuations are easier to trade."

rule: Focus on candle 2s that are clean reversal candles; candle 2s that expand a lot lead into retracement, consolidation or reversal.
quote: "Don't try to trade candle twos that expand a ton because that is when you can get caught in a retracement, a consolidation, or a reversal."

rule: An order block that formed before the open of the higher-timeframe candle can serve as the continuation reference: price should trade away without taking its high (stop above, target the low).
quote: "We have a order block that has already formed prior to the open of that higher time frame candle."

rule: Minimum reward is 1:2; if the natural target only gives 1:1, move the limit entry until it gives 1:2 (a positional entry).
quote: "this is a 1 one. I ideally want to get a 1:2. So, then I'm just going to raise it until I have that 1:2."

rule: A candle 2 that expanded is still tradable for candle 3 only if short-term liquidity remains open; if candle 2 already reached the draw, do not trade candle 3.
quote: "If candle 2 would have expanded all the way to this low, that's something I'm not ever really going to trade."

rule: Strong HTF bias on a continuation day allows aggressive LTF entries (LTF reversal); weaker bias means wait for an LTF continuation; when trading HTF candle 2 (reversal day), wait for an LTF continuation.
quote: "If you're always trading a continuation day on the higher time frame and you have a strong bias, then you can get a bit more aggressive on the lower time frames."

rule: Preferred structure: HTF continuation traded with an LTF continuation (continuation on HTF, intermediate and entry timeframe).
quote: "And then I'm trading a higher time frame continuation with a lower time frame continuation. And that is how I prefer to do it."

rule: After price takes a target, want a retracement, a close over, then a continuation; if price shows a reversal instead, stand aside.
quote: "If price shows me that we are going to reverse here, I'm uninterested."

rule: On an expanded-then-consolidated HTF setup (lower expectations), demand an LTF continuation and do not trade the LTF reversal.
quote: "So, with this, I'm going to demand a continuation on the lower time frame."

rule: If candle 3 does not expand, a candle 4 continuation is likely if the idea is right.
quote: "If price isn't expanding in candle 3, that's when we're likely to get a candle 4 continuation if it is right."

rule: A real reversal closes quickly through the level; a slow, failed close is consolidation, so hold the plan.
quote: "If price was going to form that reversal, we'd want to see a quick close below, right?"

rule: Avoid setups where the opposing liquidity sits at almost the same price as the CISD: the CISD arrives as targets are taken.
quote: "our sellside liquidity is at almost the same point as our change in the state of delivery."

rule: After an expansion, expect a phase: retrace into an FVG then continue, consolidate then sweep and continue, or reverse (not interested).
quote: "Do we get a retracement into a fair value gap to then trade it lower? Do we consolidate?"

rule: A CISD counts only through the series of candles that made the extreme; a CISD that takes too long is just consolidation lows being taken and needs more confirmation (SMT + V-shape).
quote: "I'm not considering this a change in the state of delivery because I'm looking for the series of candles that made the high."

rule: With strong HTF bias, an LTF reversal can be taken with a market entry if 2R to the liquidity is available; stop above the LTF swing protected by 0.5 of the CISD order block rather than the high.
quote: "I'm expecting price to hold five [.5] of this order block, right? this change in the state delivery."

rule: HTF continuation paired with an LTF reversal is allowed when the HTF bias is strong.
quote: "if you have a strong bias, you can trade those lower time frame reversals."

rule: For a reversal candle whose wick ran deep (not a small wick), use 0.5 of the whole candle range, not 0.5 of the wick, as the level to respect.
quote: "that's why I'm going to look for 0.5 of this daily candles range because it makes sense with this candle type."

rule: A candle 2 closure right after an expansion is a low-quality condition: demand more confirmation or skip the day.
quote: "this sets up lowquality conditions following an expansion. This is a date where I either want to have more confirmation or avoid entirely."

rule: Use the HTF EQ, HTF order block opening price, its 0.5 and HTF FVGs to define the window where the HTF wick should form.
quote: "really we have this little window in price where we want to see be respected right here."

rule: In Asia or early in the day stay on higher entry timeframes (15m minimum).
quote: "if I'm in Asia or the early parts of the day I'm trying to stay on the higher time frames so at least minimum 15"

rule: Prefer the first continuation in candle 3; later continuations feel like chasing.
quote: "I like to trade that first continuation instead of the further continuations because I feel like I'm chasing."

rule: Internal range liquidity = a fair value gap (bullish or bearish).
quote: "internal range liquidity is just a fair value Gap"

rule: External range liquidity = a swing high or swing low.
quote: "external range liquidity is just a swing high or a swing low"

rule: Price moves internal -> external and external -> internal, alternately.
quote: "we expect price to move from internal to external and external to internal"

rule: After ERL is purged, expect a move back into the range to IRL; a lower high forming at IRL then targets ERL.
quote: none

rule: The oscillation continues until a trend shift or other movement breaks it, then restarts.
quote: "or until we shift Trend or have some other movement which breaks this"

rule: Flow: HTF bias first, then the HTF IRL/ERL criterion, then LTF stop raid and CISD.
quote: "I am then going down to the lower time frame looking for a stop raid a change in the state of delivery"

rule: Target about 2R, and the whole sequence must happen within a kill zone.
quote: "I will be targeting just around a 2R trade and this must all be done within a Kill Zone"

rule: Weekly bias: if the previous week closed over the week before, anticipate a reach for the previous week high.
quote: "previous week closed over the previous"

rule: If price makes a new low before closing over the series, the CISD reference shifts to the new candle(s) that made the new low.
quote: "with making a new low this would not be our change in the state of delivery"

rule: CISD = close over the series (or single) candle that made the low.
quote: "I'm finding the series or singular candle that made the low and then if price closes over it"

rule: CISD level precisely = the opening price of the series of candles that made the low; a close over it confirms.
quote: "I Mark out the opening price in that Series so I would need a close over this to continue higher"

rule: If the swing-low stop does not give 2R, extend the target or move the invalidation.
quote: "to meet that 2 R minimum I'll either have to extend my price Target or move my invalidation"

rule: Tighter invalidation: price should not disrespect 0.5 of the down-close candle body (order block); stop there, like a breaker-block stop.
quote: "I wouldn't really want to see price disrespect .5 of this down Clos candle body"

rule: A sweep of another low then a close over the down-close candle forms a propulsion block.
quote: "that would be the propulsion block"

rule: Do not use a sweep of a low whose break would invalidate the HTF idea (e.g. the daily low expected to hold); use a FVG instead.
quote: "we could sweep out this low but then that would invalidate the idea"

rule: If the down-move has no clean series of down-close candles, treat the whole move (large down-close candle + continuation) as the series for CISD.
quote: "we don't have a clean series of down closed candles so generally what I do here is I just use this whole move"

rule: If the CISD close is too far from the stop for acceptable RR, wait for a retest (limit order) instead of entering on the close.
quote: "in this case I would have to wait for a retest"

rule: Once the LTF ERL (buy-side) is already taken, avoid further longs unless the HTF narrative is strong; next draw may be IRL or the other side of the range.
quote: "if I'm lacking that strong narrative this is going to be something I want to avoid"

rule: A reaction out of the mean threshold (upper half) of the down-close series supports price; entry there with stop below the mean threshold requires a strong bias.
quote: "reaction out of the mean threshold of this series"

rule: In a bullish trend, each higher low forms in IRL (FVG) and targets the next ERL (higher high).
quote: none

rule: Continuation entry after CISD: a retest that validates the new low gives another entry, stop on that low, target 2R.
quote: "I can always wait for a retest and place a limit order"

rule: Two entry options on the hourly CISD: enter with stop below 0.5 of the order block, or wait for a new order block in the next candle.
quote: "I can take an entry with where I would need my stop below 0 five of this"

rule: A new order block requires either a sweep of a low or a reach into a FVG, then a close over the down-close candles.
quote: "I'd want to see if we either sweep out a low or reach into a fair value Gap"

rule: Manage: take 2R, or hold runners toward the ERL.
quote: "I can Target Two r or hold Runners towards our external range liquidity"

rule: Make AMD mechanical with swing points: candle 1 is always accumulation, then watch candle 2.
quote: "The first candle will always be accumulation and then we're going to watch candle 2."

rule: A candle 2 with a small wick can be both manipulation and distribution; a reversal candle 2 (large wick) is manipulation only and candle 3 is the distribution.
quote: "If candle 2 has a small wick, it can be the manipulation as well as the distribution."

rule: The goal is to trade the distribution / expansion (directional) candle.
quote: "the whole goal is to be trading that distribution or the expansion candle, that directional candle"

rule: Let the HTF candle open and form its opposing run (wick); a shallow wick supports expansion.
quote: "as long as this is a shallow wick, it supports expansion"

rule: If candle 2 has a large opposing run against your direction, it does not support expansion in candle 2: let it close and trade candle 3.
quote: "When it has a large opposing run that does not support expansion higher in candle 2."

rule: The HTF wick is considered formed when the LTF shallow opposing run is followed by a CISD that makes a protected low/high; then trade the expansion.
quote: "has a change in the state of delivery which makes this a protected low"

rule: Align with the daily bias, use 4h closures to decide bias and whether price expands now (already reversed) or must reverse then expand.
quote: "we are going to use the 4hour candles to determine a bias using candle closures"

rule: Let the wick form, then trade the body; trying to catch the wick gets you stopped out repeatedly.
quote: "I need to let the wick form and then look to trade the body."

rule: Pair the 4h with the 15m for entries (most straightforward pairing).
quote: "I'm using the 15-minut time frame in this example as it is paired with the 4hour time frame."

rule: After a London (2:00) reversal 4h candle, expect the 6:00-10:00 candle to be the New York continuation (candle 3).
quote: "we're expecting 6:00 a.m. to 10:00 a.m. to make a move higher"

rule: Once a protected swing forms inside the new HTF candle, any entry is valid with stop on that low, targeting the daily objective (previous day high).
quote: "I can really take any entry in here with my stop loss on this low"

rule: A shallow opposing run should appear early in the HTF candle; if price first moves too far the other way, skip the in-candle reversal.
quote: "normally if we're going to have a shallow opposing run, we want to see that early into the higher time frame candle"

rule: A reversal needs expansion met with expansion, plus a CISD.
quote: "we need that expansion met with expansion to confirm a reversal"

rule: If you missed the entry, either let it go or take a continuation entry with a new protected swing as long as the target is open and 2R is available.
quote: "I can look for a continuation entry as long as my target remains open"

rule: A protected swing for continuation: price reaches an important level (FVG) and closes over the down-close candle into it.
quote: "We close over the down close candle into that. That is then a protected swing"

rule: Do not hold an expansion-candle trade beyond the candle's end once the target is hit; expansion candles only have so much range and time.
quote: "expansion candles only have so much range and so much time"

rule: To keep trading the same direction after the target, wait for the next HTF candle open (new candle, new range) and let its wick form again.
quote: "I'm going to want to wait for the open of the new higher time frame candle"

rule: With lower pairings, wait for a LTF fractal model (consolidation high run, then CISD, still respecting EQ) to confirm the 4h wick.
quote: "We're using a lower time frame fractal model to help confirm the wick of that 4hour time frame."

rule: For a 6:00 continuation after a 2:00 reversal (bearish): price should open, make a high while respecting EQ of the previous candle, then trade lower.
quote: "We'd want to see price open, make a high while respecting the EQ of the previous candle, and then traded lower."

rule: Confident entry: stop on a protected swing or at least beyond 50% of the CISD plus EQ, target 2R or seek continuation.
quote: "put my stop on a protected swing or at least above 50% of this change in the state of delivery"

rule: Positional entry: enter at the open of the new HTF candle with stop on the protected swing, target 2R, when you are confident but have no precise POI.
quote: "putting my entry on the open of the new higher time frame candle, putting my stop on the protected swing"

rule: If a 6:00 4h candle forms a reversal (sweeping previous day high), look for 10:00 to continue.
quote: "So if 6 a.m. forms a reversal, we can look for 10:00 a.m. to continue lower."

rule: With a large opposing run, target -1 standard deviation rather than deeper deviations, since the range is already used.
quote: "So, I'll use negative -1 as my target."

rule: Do not fight an expansion candle: wait for it to close and for a reversal candle to form before trading back into the range.
quote: "It makes more sense to wait for this expansion candle to close"

rule: On a very aggressive reversal at the open of a new HTF candle, enter at the open (little retracement expected) and target 2R.
quote: "I'm going to have to enter at the open because with a very aggressive move"

rule: The fractal model's goal is to anticipate one HTF candle's OHLC / OLHC for bias, then use the LTF for entry.
quote: "my whole goal is to anticipate one candle's open high low close or open low high close"

rule: A sweep of the prior candle and a close back inside lets you anticipate the next candle to expand the other way.
quote: "with the sweep of this first candle and the closure back in then I can anticipate this candle to continue lower"

rule: Pair hourly with 5m and wait until both are aligned in the same direction (5m closes through the series of opposite-close candles).
quote: "I will wait until those time frames are aligned in the same direction"

rule: The T-spot is the area where the HTF wick is expected to form; look for LTF entries there, at a PD array / POI.
quote: "the t-spot is the area in which I expect this higher time frame Wick to form"

rule: Inside the T-spot, use a 1m inversion to get on side with risk at the wick, then trade the HTF expansion.
quote: "I will look in that t-spot for a 1 minute inversion which allows me to get on side with my risk on this High"

rule: With a conflicted bias (bullish structure but previous day high taken and reversing), use the daily profile to decide.
quote: "with a conflicted bias we can go ahead and use the daily profile to see what is going on"

rule: Failure swings are generally a good target to trade back to.
quote: "we are just creating failure swings right which generally are a great Target to trade back to"

rule: When the range is already large, do not expect a large wick and further expansion; target liquidity around the daily open instead.
quote: "when we have a large range already we're not really expecting price to form a large Wick"

rule: Do not take the 5m model until the 5m closes through the series of opposite candles that swept the level.
quote: "we have not closed through this series of down Clos candles that swept out the low"

rule: If the HTF candle still lacks a wick when the T-spot prints, expect a retrace into the T-spot to put in the wick before expansion.
quote: "we lack a higher time frame Wick we can then anticipate price to retrace down to put in a higher time frame Wick"

rule: Lock the indicator settings to hourly and 5m so the model stays the same when dropping to 1m.
quote: "have them locked to the hourly and 5 minutes so I can drop down to the lower time frames"

rule: The inversion requires a candle close over the level; wait for it.
quote: "do we have an inversion out of this t-spot well we would need a close over this level"

rule: Prefer the stop at the swing low rather than waiting for another close; target 2R or hold for HTF targets.
quote: "I prefer to put my stop at the swing low right instead of waiting for another close above"

rule: Once the inversion closes, expect the wick to hold, giving invalidation for the whole HTF candle.
quote: "once closed over I'm anticipating this Wick to hold which gives me an invalidation throughout the duration of this higher time frame candle"

rule: Expansion candles usually close at their high or low, so a time-based exit at the HTF close (e.g. 11:00) is valid for runners.
quote: "expansion candles they usually close in the high or the low"

rule: No inversion and no sweep / relevant POI yet means wait.
quote: "we also have not swept out any lows or hit a relevant point of Interest"

rule: Enter on the inversion close or on its retest; prefer the retest when the target is a nearby short-term high (to get 2R).
quote: "I can choose to look for an entry on the close or on the retest"

rule: Repeated failure to displace out of a range (e.g. three drives at the previous day low) marks it as a consolidation; trade from its high/low.
quote: "see how we continue to fail to displace out of this range"

rule: In a consolidation, want a run of a high before trading lower (protected high).
quote: "if we have a consolidation we want to see a run of a high before trading that lower"

rule: SMT (ES takes highs, NQ does not) shows weakness and gives another chance to get on side with an inversion.
quote: "ES was taking these highs while NQ wasn't which shows its weakness"

rule: If the wick/invalidation already formed before the new HTF open (inversion into the open, 0.5 of the 5m range held), enter at the open with stop on that low.
quote: "when I have an invalidation very close to the opening price that's when I can go ahead and look for an entry off the open"

rule: If price trades below that low after the open, it is consolidating, not expanding.
quote: "if it goes open low below this low then it's already just consolidating"

rule: Later entry on a further CISD / order block needs a stop at least on the body and more range for 2R.
quote: "I need my stop at least on the body down here"

rule: The model is fractal: daily/hourly model with a 15m inversion works the same way.
quote: "let's talk about a daily and hourly model and then using a 15-minute inversion"

rule: A large T-spot makes a positional entry poor risk-to-reward; wait for price to come back into it.
quote: "it is a bit large right so this is not something where I want to take a positional entry"

rule: Do not trade if price runs all the way to the target highs before coming back; the target must stay open.
quote: "I wouldn't want to trade this if it trades all the way to the highs and then back in"

rule: Inversions are not pattern trading; take them only in context (toward the target after a sweep).
quote: "this isn't just pattern trading right I don't want to just take this cuz we have inversion forming in here"

rule: An expansion candle has small wicks on both sides and a large body: price trended in one direction during its period.
quote: "An expansion candle has a small wick on each side and a large body."

rule: A reversal candle opens, makes a large opposing run to form its wick, then returns toward its open before closing.
quote: "a reversal candle opens, makes a large opposing run to form its wick and then goes back towards its opening price before closing."

rule: A small wick supports expansion in the new direction; a large wick does not, because the candle has only so much range.
quote: "Small wick supports expansion. Large wick doesn't support expansion."

rule: With a large-wick reversal, expect only a return to the opening price or the current low, followed by a continuation candle (classic C2 to C3).
quote: "here I'm only expecting price to return back to its opening price or its current low."

rule: The ideal candle 2 is a reversal into an expansion candle (small wick); large-wick reversals are tradable with reduced targets.
quote: "Not saying we cannot trade reversal candles with a large wick. we just have to adjust our targets."

rule: Small-wick C2 targets: previous candle's low and standard-deviation projections; large-wick C2 targets: the opening price and current candle's low.
quote: "with an expansion candle, we can target previous candle's lows and standard deviation projections."

rule: Process: mark the previous HTF candle's high, wait for the sweep, then a CISD forming a protected high, then assume the wick has formed and trade the reversal or the following continuation.
quote: "We're going to wait for a sweep of that high, a change in the state of delivery, forming a protected high"

rule: After a large expansion, expect a new phase of price; if the current candle is not yet a reversal candle, look for it to take the previous candle's high and reverse.
quote: "since this isn't a reversal candle, I'm going to be looking for price to take out its previous candle's high"

rule: If the daily C2 wick is large, either target back to the daily open or trade the next day's continuation instead.
quote: "If we have a large wick, then we're better off either looking back towards the daily open or trading the following day for a continuation."

rule: For a daily C2, phases of price on the hourly chart are his favorite pairing; a reversal there reads as expansion into the high met by expansion back.
quote: "we also can use the phases of price on the hourly chart and that's personally my favorite for the daily time frame."

rule: Intraday reversal signature: expansion met with expansion (into the level, then straight back), plus a CISD.
quote: "We have expansion met with expansion, which is what I would consider to be a reversal."

rule: Daily C2 targets include the previous day's EQ and previous-day highs/lows as liquidity.
quote: "We can use the EQ of the previous day for a target or liquidity."

rule: An intraday CISD early in the day gives a small daily wick, leaving time to expand through the day.
quote: "This allows it to form its wick early enough into the day to expand throughout the day."

rule: The fractal model only trades from swing points; with no swing low left on the other side and a high just swept, favor only downside.
quote: "with my fractal model, I'm only looking to trade swing points."

rule: A large intraday wick over the previous day high (no shallow sweep) means you adjust targets to the daily open and session lows, not full expansion.
quote: "Instead of looking for expansion lower, I'm looking for it back into its daily open."

rule: A range is when one candle's range contains all the following days; wait for one side of it to be taken before looking for setups.
quote: "this previous candle's range encompasses all of the other days following it."

rule: Ignore CISDs inside a range that are not at a relevant level.
quote: "I wouldn't be interested in this CISD here. Why? There is no relevant level."

rule: If most of the daily time and range is used (sweep late in NY), do not expect the afternoon to run to the opposite range extreme; aim for an intraday high or the daily open.
quote: "does it really make sense for the afternoon session on oil or gasoline in this case to rip all the way to these highs?"

rule: Confirmation timeframe by session: Asia 1h or 30m; London 1h, 30m or 15m; New York 1h/30m if present, but often drop lower because NY reversals are fast.
quote: "So, in Asia, I'm almost specifically only going to use the hourly or 30 minute."

rule: If waiting for the HTF CISD would put the entry at your target, drop to a lower timeframe (e.g. 5m) for the CISD and a new protected low.
quote: "a lot of times with a New York reversal, it's going to be very quick."

rule: When the overnight (Asia/London) highs are already taken, there is no low-resistance liquidity left; favor the daily open, and risk-to-reward is poor.
quote: "we don't really have any low resistance liquidity to be sitting to be taken out."

rule: A large-wick reversal day is better left alone; trade the following continuation day if it forms a small wick.
quote: "it's better to let this reversal day trade and then look for the continuation day following"

rule: Do not look for longs after the 4th day of expansion.
quote: "within my model I cannot look long after my fourth day."

rule: Losing trades are normal; use the correlated asset: frame the reversal on the weaker asset (SMT) and enter on the pair you trade with the same stop.
quote: "we can see that Euro is weaker. We can also mark out our SMT."

rule: If the day has already made most of its range in one direction (small wick, already expanded), favor trades back into the range, e.g. off the 9-10 am hourly candle high.
quote: "We've already made most of our daily range. So this is when I favor shorts back into the range."

rule: For these late reversals, the final target is the session lows and the daily open; anything beyond is extra.
quote: "We just want to see those session lows and the daily open."

rule: The same C2 framing works on 1h-5m and 4H-15m; the 4H candle also showed a small wick framing off its previous candle.
quote: "let's say I wanted to use the 4hour and 15minute model, right? I'd be waiting for a closure below there."

rule: If you miss the candle-2 reversal, trade the fractal-model continuations in candle 3 and candle 4.
quote: "even if I just don't catch this reversal in candle 2, that's when I can trade my fractal model continuations in candle 3 and candle 4."

rule: Price cannot reverse without forming a swing high (bull to bear) or swing low (bear to bull); this is the base of the model.
quote: "the market cannot reverse without a swing high or a swing low"

rule: After a swing low with a strong bullish candle-3 close, expect a bullish continuation the next day (day 4); mirror for bearish.
quote: "if a swing low forms I can then anticipate a bullish continuation on the following day with a strong closure in day three"

rule: A bullish day-4 continuation should come out of the upper half of candle 3's range; a bearish one out of the lower half.
quote: "with a swing low in a bullish continuation I would be looking for price to continue out of the upper half of candle 3's range"

rule: Expansion does not give deep retracements, so a retrace into the discount of C3 argues against the bullish continuation.
quote: "if price is going to expand I don't want to see a deep retracement into a discount of this range to go higher"

rule: Workflow: the daily bias marks where day 4's wick should form; look for LTF PD arrays there to form the low of day, then trade continuations.
quote: "I'm looking in this area for the wick to form then I look for PD arrays on the lower time frame in here"

rule: Top-down: day 4 gives the bias, a middle timeframe gives structure, a lower timeframe gives the entry.
quote: "I have my fourth day in which I can anticipate a bias I use a middle time frame for a structure and then I use a lower time frame for entry"

rule: Swing low = a low with a higher low on each side.
quote: "you can see we have a low with a higher low on each side which is a swing low"

rule: Mark C3's EQ; the 0.5 must be respected for the bullish continuation.
quote: "I'd want to see the 0 five of this be respected to trade higher"

rule: A competing swing high is overridden when the correlated index (ES) swept its low (SMT) and the close gives a valid daily CISD.
quote: "es swept out this low so we have smt here and with this closure we then have a valid change in the state of delivery here on the daily time frame"

rule: Day-4 bullish plan: open, make the low in the upper half of the previous candle, then trade to the previous day high, the swing point to the left and beyond; invalidation is trading below that low area.
quote: "I'm wanting to see price form its daily Wick above the EQ of the previous candle"

rule: Classify intraday moves with phases of price: expansion not met by expansion back is a retracement or consolidation, so expect another run of the low.
quote: "is this met with expansion forming a reversal no this is a retracement or a consolidation"

rule: A failure to take an LTF low while the correlated asset does (SMT), confirmed by a close through the down-close candles that formed it, makes that low expected to hold.
quote: "we form an smt with es so I can anticipate this low to hold"

rule: Session sequence: a London reversal that holds should lead to a New York continuation.
quote: "I can anticipate this London reversal to hold if we're going to trade higher and then I'll get a New York continuation"

rule: You do not need to know in advance which FVG will hold; wait for LTF price action around the NY drivers.
quote: "do I need to know which one of these is going to react and hold no I do not"

rule: Pair the LTF sweep with a time driver: 8:30 or 9:30 (ET).
quote: "I also want to pair that with a driver when would that be 8:30 or 9:30"

rule: A consolidation before a news driver whose lows get run at 8:30 is ideal; the close through the (single) down-close candle that took the low is the LTF CISD.
quote: "we run out these lows which is ideal if we're having a consolidation prior to a news driver"

rule: Take the trade when the 3m, 30m and daily align; stop at the low, target 2R.
quote: "our 3 minute our 30 minute and our daily is all aligned in One Direction"

rule: The most important concept is aligning all timeframes.
quote: "the most important concept here is aligning all those time frames together"

rule: If the low lacks a higher low on each side yet, it is a candle-3 trade; let one day pass for the swing to confirm before trading day 4.
quote: "this would be trading candle 3 in the swing so I'm going to let one day pass"

rule: Intraday support should come from the upper half of C3 measured body to body as well.
quote: "I want to see the upper half of this from body to body also support"

rule: A sweep of the lows alone is not a bullish LTF reversal; wait for the close through the down-close candles that made the low.
quote: "this is not enough confirmation to say there is a lower time frame reversal that is bullish"

rule: If you miss the first entry, take a continuation entry from a PD array (FVG) with a close through the down-close candle; skip deep areas since expansion does not retrace deeply.
quote: "if price is going to enter an expansion phase it's not going to have deep retracements"

rule: Stop can be on the body low instead of the wick low; target 2R.
quote: "my stop on the body low or the low in this case I'll use the body low look for 2 R"

rule: With no SMT, a low that price cannot aggressively close back through is expected to be taken; an SMT on that low removes the need for the sweep.
quote: "since we cannot aggressively move lower and then close through here I expect this low to get taken out"

rule: The lower timeframe is optional: some enter on the 1h close with stop on the low and 2R.
quote: "Some people prefer to just take entries on the 1 hour"

rule: London reversal, then New York should continue; a NY sweep plus CISD gives a second entry.
quote: "if we have a London reversal I'd want to see a New York continuation"

rule: Everything starts from the daily: if the daily direction is framed, lower timeframes fall in line.
quote: "if I can frame a direction on the daily chart the lower time frames fall into line"

rule: Bearish version: swing high (high with a lower high each side) whose close goes through the up-close candle; day 4 should hold the lower half of C3 (at most a reach into the FVG there).
quote: "I would want to be looking for the lower half of this third candle here to trade lower"

rule: Fractal: use 0.5 of the HTF candle as the line the LTF continuation must respect; put the stop above the FVG that may be retested inside it.
quote: "I can use 0.5 of this candle looking for a continuation lower on the lower time frame"

rule: The concept is fractal, but he prefers it on daily candles.
quote: "it is a fractal concept however I prefer to use it on the daily candles"

rule: For scalping, align with the hourly candle instead of the daily.
quote: "for scalping, we're using much lower time frames. So, we're going to focus on the hourly chart."

rule: Hourly bias comes from an hourly candle 2 or candle 3 closure anticipating an expansion candle next.
quote: "The easiest way to do that is to have a candle 2 closure on the hourly or a candle 3 closure"

rule: Using the hourly bias, find the 15-minute swing point that forms the hourly low (or high) with a candle 2 closure there.
quote: "we are looking for the swing point that forms the hourly low and then looking for a candle to closure there"

rule: Inside the anticipated 15m expansion, use a 15m and 1m fractal model; the 1m continuation forms the wick of the HTF candle.
quote: "we can be waiting for a continuation on the 1 minute time frame to form the wick of the higher time frame candle"

rule: What is traded is the body of the hourly candle, using the 15m and 1m fractal model.
quote: "We are trading the body of the hourly candle using a 15-minute and 1 minute fractal model."

rule: A consolidation is a continuation signature: in an uptrend prefer a sweep of the low to go higher over a sweep of the high to go lower.
quote: "a consolidation is a continuation signature to me"

rule: An hourly sweep opposing the order flow, followed by candle 2 closure, sets up the next candle(s) higher.
quote: "we have an hourly sweep here opposing the order flow. This is where we can look for a move higher in this next candle"

rule: Wait for a valid 15m swing point within the model; he skips a technical candle 4 entry.
quote: "I could trade this technically in candle 4, but I'm going to wait for a valid swing point within my model"

rule: If highs are taken before you get on side, decide reversal vs retracement/consolidation; an aggressive move back in warrants waiting another candle.
quote: "This candle tells me reversal or retracement, right? Very aggressive move back in. I want to give it another candle."

rule: A small hourly wick supports expansion; the 15m swing point is the wick of the hourly candle.
quote: "we have a small wick on the hourly time frame which supports expansion"

rule: 1m execution: after reaching an FVG, wait for the closure over; enter, stop on the low, target 2R.
quote: "this is something I'd be willing to take an entry on. Put my stop on the low and then be looking for 2 R"

rule: For better R:R, an alternative is to wait for a retest of the level, accepting the trade may leave without you.
quote: "If I do not want that risk-to-reward, I could look for a retest"

rule: You need the bias/narrative for the hourly candle to expand before aligning a 15m and 1m fractal model.
quote: "you need the bias or the narrative for this hourly candle to expand"

rule: A 15m candle 3 that coincides with an hourly candle 3 is the alignment to drop to the 1m.
quote: "we have a candle three on the 15-minute also aligning with a candle three on the hourly"

rule: If price leaves without trading into the POI, he misses it rather than chasing below the lows, since a new phase of price can start there.
quote: "this is something that I would miss here"

rule: After short-term lows are taken, judge the phase: a retracement (not a reversal) is a valid continuation to trade toward the HTF target.
quote: "Is this a reversal? No, that is a retracement. So then that is a valid continuation"

rule: Note HTF targets: they justify continuation trades after short-term lows are already taken.
quote: "that's why it's important to notice your higher time frame targets"

rule: Trade the continuation inside the hourly candle 3 or candle 4, found via a 15m swing point.
quote: "I'm looking to trade the continuation inside that candle 3 or inside that candle 4"

rule: At a consolidation high while bullish, a retracement or consolidation is a continuation signature.
quote: "A retracement or a consolidation is a continuation signature."

rule: A bearish-bodied candle 2 closure alone is not trusted; it becomes trusted when candle 3 engulfs, as long as the EQ is respected.
quote: "this alone I would not trust as a candle 2 closure as it is a bearish candle"

rule: A protected swing already formed before a new HTF candle opens, below EQ, allows positioning at the HTF open with 2R.
quote: "I could position at the open of the new higher time frame candle and look for 2 R that way"

rule: Alternative: wait for a continuation within the new HTF candle and enter on the close through or on the retest, stop on the swing, 2R.
quote: "either entering on this close through with your stop there, looking for two R"

rule: Advanced: trading the hourly reversal candle (candle 2) is possible when the 9:30 open, 15m and hourly all support expansion; most traders should not focus on it.
quote: "for the majority of people I would say don't really focus on this example"

rule: At 9:30 watch how the open plays, then check it is supported by the hourly and 15-minute candle.
quote: "our whole goal is to watch how the open plays and then see if that's supported by the hourly candle and the 15-minute candle"

rule: Stop on the protected swing; target 2R or the other side of the consolidation.
quote: "I could put my stop on that protected swing and then looking for 2 R or the other side of the consolidation"

rule: Step one is always a weekly bias: anticipate whether the weekly candle moves higher or lower using liquidity, highs/lows, FVGs and candle closures.
quote: "step one is always going to be getting a weekly bias"

rule: Internal-to-external liquidity with a weekly candle 2 closure makes weekly candle 3 expansion reasonable to anticipate.
quote: "we have internal to external liquidity with a candle 2 closure. It's reasonable to anticipate expansion on this candle 3"

rule: Weekly bias can be as simple as whether price reaches for the previous week's low or high.
quote: "it can be as simple as am I going to reach for previous week's low or previous week's high"

rule: Then wait for a daily swing point (daily candle 2 or candle 3) forming the wick of the daily candle, and trade the expansion in the following candles.
quote: "I'll be looking for a candle 2 or a candle three on the daily chart"

rule: Weekly profile logic: Tuesday forming the low with a candle 2 closure lets Wednesday and Thursday expand; Thursday depends on Wednesday's close.
quote: "Thursday is totally dependent on Wednesday's closure"

rule: The daily candle 2 closure must also show a CISD; then it is valid to look for the fractal model on the next day.
quote: "That means it's valid to look for the fractal model higher in Wednesday."

rule: Get on side as the next day's candle 3 wick forms and hold through that day (even the next) into the draw on liquidity.
quote: "I can hold that through Wednesday, even Thursday into that drawn liquidity above"

rule: The model is fractal: weekly bias -> daily swing -> hourly entry, or monthly -> weekly swing -> 4h entry for longer holds (e.g. crypto).
quote: "you can use the monthly time frame, then a weekly swing point, and then a 4hour entry as well"

rule: No daily swing point in the direction of the weekly bias = no trade yet.
quote: "I'm not going to be able to take a trade here"

rule: Skip an hourly continuation whose stop would be too large.
quote: "this continuation is not something I would personally look to trade because my stop loss is just too big"

rule: Discretionary entry allowed: after a consolidation sweeps into an FVG on the high, a candle 2 closure entry can be taken even without a continuation yet.
quote: "There are times where you can apply your own discretion to the model to look for entries."

rule: Do not trust a later continuation that did not reach into the POI unless there is SMT on another asset.
quote: "I personally wouldn't trust this because it did not reach into here unless we have SMT on another asset"

rule: A weekly high that falls just shy of a relevant swing is treated as a retracement to trade back into those equal highs, not a reversal.
quote: "it doesn't really make sense for me to try to trade a reversal away from this. So I view this as a retracement"

rule: During a bullish expansion, a retracement that reaches deep into the lower FVG turns price bearish; want price to hold the upper half.
quote: "I want to see price remain in the upper half of this"

rule: On the hourly, look for protected swings; a V-shaped reversal (optionally with SMT) is the preferred reversal structure.
quote: "This is what you want to see when you have a reversal structure"

rule: A positional entry is allowed with the stop on the protected swing, targeting the HTF objective if it gives over 2R.
quote: "put my stop on that protected swing and then look for the higher time frame objective"

rule: An intracandle CISD that creates a new protected swing after a sweep is another entry.
quote: "This would be the intracandle change in the state of delivery."

rule: A stop-out with context, bias and structure is a valid loss; accept it.
quote: "It has the context, it has the bias, and it has the structure. It just comes and stops us back out."

rule: A large-wick reversal (not a candle 2 closure) can be traded if price respects the lower half of the wick (bearish case).
quote: "price should respect the lower half of the wick if we want to trade that lower"

rule: After a daily candle expands far and takes the nearby lows, wait for a new phase of price instead of entering in the next candle.
quote: "So, I generally like to wait for a new phase of price."

rule: If the entry timeframe is messy, move up one timeframe (30m->1h, 1h->4h).
quote: "If things are a bit messy, you can move up one time frame."

rule: After a continuation that already moved far, wait for a retracement back into the range to get 2R to the target.
quote: "I would probably want some sort of retracement back into the range"

rule: He prefers trading candle 3 over trading the reversal candles themselves.
quote: "I just prefer to trade that candle three as I find it easier."

rule: A candle 2 closing on its own wick should keep its upper half (0.5) respected for a move higher; if the low is run, the wick grows and less expansion is expected.
quote: "We're either going to respect 0.5 of this wick and trade higher or we're going to run out the low"

rule: Timeframe choice does not matter as long as you have HTF context and know where price should trade away from.
quote: "it really doesn't matter what time frame you choose as long as you have the higher time frame context"

rule: Weekly directly to 4h with a normal fractal model is a valid swing trade; no further alignment needed, just context.
quote: "you can go directly from the weekly to the 4hour and just use a normal fractal model for a swing trade"

rule: If the protected-swing candle has no wick above, wait for a continuation before entering.
quote: "I wouldn't want to take an entry before it does that"

rule: After an expansion, ask which phase comes next: retracement to continue, consolidation, or expansion the other way.
quote: "We'd want to see what the new phase of price is."

rule: Expansion met with expansion in the opposite direction is a reversal.
quote: "So if we have expansion met with expansion, that is a reversal."

rule: In a consolidation, watch the range high and low for the manipulation that decides direction.
quote: "we can watch the high and the low of the range for either a manipulation to trade higher?"

rule: Failure swings / equal highs above a retracement are a good sign for a bullish continuation (liquidity to run).
quote: "we also have those failure swings off the highs or those equal highs, which is a good sign."

rule: If the daily gives no clear closure (not much lower, not outside the range), drop to the lower timeframe for a new phase of price.
quote: "Using the daily chart, there's just not enough information to make a determination"

rule: Read the daily candle's path on the hourly: open-high-low-close reads bearish even if the close is ambiguous.
quote: "And since it did open high, low close, that is telling me it was more of a bearish candle."

rule: A bearish daily continuation wants the daily candle to close weak, into its lows.
quote: "We want to see that daily candle close into the lows."

rule: With a strong close forming opposing candles and a protected high, anticipate a shallow retracement then continuation.
quote: "I can anticipate a shallow retracement to continue lower as we have a protected high right here."

rule: If price fails to close below the level, treat it as consolidation: expect the high taken, then lower.
quote: "If we fail to close below this level, then I could have viewed this as a consolidation, looked for a high to be taken out"

rule: A late-day bullish close weakens a bearish continuation; if still bearish, require more lower-timeframe confirmation.
quote: "So if I'm still bearish, I'm then going to require more confirmation on the lower timeframes to get short."

rule: For a bearish day, price should respect the T-spot / form the upper wick; opening above it is less than ideal.
quote: "I want to see the T-spot respected, or the upper wick, forming here"

rule: A daily close back over 0.5 of the CISD conflicts with a bearish read (no weak closure).
quote: "We're closing over 0.5 of this change in the state of delivery, but we do have that open high"

rule: Without a bullish CISD, price is still bearish even after expansion met with expansion.
quote: "we do not form a bullish change in the state of delivery, so price is still bearish."

rule: Do not short off failure swings; a short needs a protected swing.
quote: "this is not something I would look to short because we do not have a protected swing. We have failure swings."

rule: Failure swings tend to be revisited (taken out) before the move.
