quote: "when we have failure swings, that's when I want to see those levels revisited."

rule: A level is protected only if price closes below it; no close = no protected swing.
quote: "Well, do we close below this level here? And if we zoom in and take a look, we do not."

rule: With no protected swing, two bearish paths: retrace into the FVG and close lower (two opposing-candle sets), or run the highs and form a new protected high.
quote: "price could retrace up into this important level, this fair value gap, trade lower, which then creates two sets of opposing candles"

rule: For a reversal off a high, price should neither consolidate nor retrace; it needs expansion met with expansion (higher-timeframe wick).
quote: "We want to see expansion met with expansion to form a wick on the higher time frame and this reversal."

rule: Once a protected high forms, the current daily wick should remain intact for continuation lower.
quote: "I anticipate this current daily wick to remain intact if we're gonna get a continuation lower."

rule: Targets for continuation are the higher-timeframe lows: previous day low and the prior day's low.
quote: "We have previous day low, mark out here, as well as that previous day's low, right?"

rule: If the hourly retest will not give a swing formation, drop one timeframe (30m) or refine with the 30m-3m fractal pair.
quote: "this is where I could either look to refine this down and trade the fractal 30 minute and 3 minute setup"

rule: Entry on a newly formed protected swing: stop on the high, target 2R; stop can sit nearer if price should not trade above 50% of the opposing candle.
quote: "I don't anticipate price to trade above 50% of this opposing candle here."

rule: Failure to close below the level usually means the high gets taken out (not always).
quote: "But once again, failure to close below this level, usually the high gets taken out."

rule: When the entry cannot reach 2R to the current low, it is still acceptable if the target is the higher-timeframe objectives.
quote: "I can't really get to R to this current low, but that's fine because I'm looking to target those higher time frame objectives"

rule: Avoid price when ideas conflict (wanting the high taken for manipulation but not wanting it taken for continuation).
quote: "So this is usually an area where I will avoid price because I have conflicting ideas."

rule: Do not trade the breakout of a consolidation; wait for a continuation entry after the expansion.
quote: "I'm not going to trade inside of this, trading the breakout. I'm going to wait for what? A continuation entry."

rule: You do not need to know retracement vs reversal immediately; wait for a CISD (reversal) or a close below (continuation).
quote: "Is this retracement or reversal? Now, I don't need to know this yet. I can just wait."

rule: If the close below that would confirm expansion never comes, treat it as consolidation and watch the range high and low.
quote: "If we can't get that closure below to expand, we are doing what? We are now just consolidating"

rule: The trend is over when price stops respecting the candles and takes out the new protected high.
quote: "So you can see this trend is now over as we are not respecting these candles anymore."

rule: FVGs on both sides from an aggressive move down then up = V-shaped reversal; on the higher timeframe it is a reversal candle.
quote: "when you have an aggressive move lower and then back up, that's forming a reversal candle on a higher time frame"

rule: A weekly reversal candle -> expect the following week to trade higher and take the previous high.
quote: "with a reversal candle here, I'm looking for price to trade higher in this following week"

rule: A Monday consolidation after a large Friday expansion is expected.
quote: "We have Monday open up as a consolidation. And that makes sense following a large expansion on Friday."

rule: A reversal day can be framed off the previous day low, but the easier trade is the continuation day after it.
quote: "The easier trade does lie in the continuation."

rule: Tuesday reversed -> look for Wednesday to continue (expansion, retracement into FVG, expansion).
quote: "Tuesday has reversed. So looking for Wednesday to continue in line with this trend"

rule: Confirm the daily reversal on the hourly: find the low, the series of down-close candles that made it, and a close through them.
quote: "I'll look for the series of down close candles that made that low. And did we get a closure through that level?"

rule: On the continuation day, price should respect the upper half (0.5) of the prior daily candle, giving a small shallow wick before expansion.
quote: "I want to see it respect the upper half of this daily candle because I want to see a small shallow wick"

rule: A small reversal off the PDH that leaves failure swings is irrelevant for a bearish view.
quote: "This doesn't make sense for a bearish perspective as we are just leaving these failure swings here."

rule: Treat an untrusted retracement as a consolidation: wait for the range low to be swept into a POI (here an FVG in the upper half of the previous daily candle).
quote: "I want to see the range low be taken out into a point of interest"

rule: Index selection: YM strongest / NQ weakest (or vice versa) with ES in the middle; when YM is strong and you want longs, trade ES over NQ.
quote: "if I'm looking to trade long, I would prefer to trade ES longs over NQ longs"

rule: An aggressive move lower met by an aggressive move higher forms the HTF wick together with a CISD.
quote: "an aggressive move lower met with an aggressive move higher. That's forming this higher time frame wick"

rule: T-spot logic: 0.5 of the HTF wick and 0.5 of the CISD leg should both hold; their overlap is the area price must hold.
quote: "If we are going to form a higher time frame wick here, I want to see.5 of this wick be respected."

rule: Do not enter where you cannot partial before or at the short-term targets with good R:R; wait for a retracement.
quote: "I want to be able to exit or partial off before or at my short-term targets"

rule: Generally let the HTF (9:00) candle close and trade the 10:00 continuation; trading the reversal itself needs strong context.
quote: "generally, I'm going to let this higher time frame candle close and then trade the 10:00 a.m. continuation"

rule: If the continuation on the entry timeframe does not give 2R to the short-term highs, refine down (5m -> 3m -> rarely 1m).
quote: "this is where I will rarely, and in this case, I did refine it down to the 1 minute time frame"

rule: Keep seeking continuations until R:R makes sense; do not extend the target to force R:R, price may reverse at that level.
quote: "I'm just looking to seek continuations until the risk-to-reward makes sense."

rule: After expansion, wait for a retracement (or consolidation then a move lower) to get the next expansion; a retrace into an FVG marks a retracement.
quote: "If we have expansion, I'm looking for a retracement to get a new expansion"

rule: Fractalize the daily logic on the 1m: treat the 1m reversal candle like a daily one, with 0.5 respected and its low not taken.
quote: "I'm going to fractalize what I did on the daily. This is a reversal candle on the 1 minute"

rule: A retest entry is still valid after a missed entry if it gives 2R, because a protected low exists in the continuation.
quote: "as long as it gives 2 R because I have a protected low in a continuation here"

rule: Trade management: partial at 2R, partial at intraday highs, trail the rest.
quote: none

rule: Expansion, consolidation, break: a retest that holds = continue; consolidation, break, then push back lower = reversal, be out.
quote: "If I have a consolidation, a break, and then push lower, I'm viewing that as a reversal that can then trade lower."

rule: Take profit at intraday highs because if the day does not expand, that is where a retracement is expected.
quote: "if we are going to not expand in this day, that's where I'm expecting a retracement"

rule: A bearish monthly candle 2 closure makes him bearish on the month; ask whether price is more likely to reach the previous month's high or low.
quote: "we have a bearish candle 2 closure on the monthly time frame. So that is telling me that I am bearish on this monthly candle."

rule: Being closer to the previous month's low (with equal lows) makes that low the draw.
quote: "considering we are closer to previous month's low. I'm just looking for that previous month's low to taken out"

rule: Expansion into a high met with expansion out is a reversal; a slow move back is a retracement, not a new higher low.
quote: "We have expansion into the high met with expansion out. So blending with those phases of price. This is a reversal."

rule: In a bearish continuation he does not want the last high taken; he wants a new lower high and lower low.
quote: "I want to see a new lower high and a new lower low"

rule: Top-down checklist: HTF draw on liquidity, daily candle 2 closure, then hourly CISD inside that candle 2.
quote: "go down to the hourly chart and confirm that we have a change in the state of delivery in this candle too"

rule: Read the bodies for a V-shaped reversal as extra confirmation of the candle 2 closure.
quote: "if you focus on the bodies here, we have a nice V-shaped reversal to add to that candle to closure"

rule: Bearish dollar implies bullish foreign currencies; scan the currency futures and pick the chart you like.
quote: "Now that I have a bearish bias for dollar, that gives me a bullish bias for foreign currencies."

rule: Pick the asset with the cleanest daily formation: low taken, V-shaped reversal, open into an FVG, ideal candle 2 closure that forms a protected swing.
quote: "the one that caught my eye was Canadian futures, and that is because of how it has this daily formation"

rule: After an ideal daily candle 2 closure with a protected swing, look for candle 3 next day toward the previous month's high and equal highs.
quote: "So now I can look for this next day in candle 3 to trade higher."

rule: The next daily wick should form in the upper half (above 0.5) of the opposing daily candle, i.e. inside the T-spot.
quote: "I want to see the wick of this next candle formed in the upper half of this area"

rule: Next step after bias: look for protected swings (price reaches an FVG and closes over), each giving an invalidation.
quote: "I want to look for protected swings. You can see I have one here as price reaches into a fair value gap and closes over."

rule: If price opens right near an invalidation, a positional entry overnight is acceptable, letting it swing into the next session.
quote: "I have price opening up right near an invalidation. So, I could look to take a positional entry into this overnight"

rule: Stop on the protected low, target the high.
quote: "put my stop on the protected low, and then I was looking for price to trade into this high here"

rule: After three expansion candles, expect a possible new phase of price; check the 30m for consolidation.
quote: "We have three candles of expansion. This is when we can get a new phase of price."

rule: If price is consolidating, set TP at the consolidation high, since taking it can start a reversal.
quote: "if we have a consolidation and price takes the high, that's when we can get a new phase of price and reverse"

rule: Aligning timeframes lets you swing the monthly/daily expansion if you choose; he day-traded only the daily range.
quote: "this is why it's important to align your time frames"

rule: For USDCAD the same idea is inverted (bearish), using the same protected swings and stop.
quote: "Since you are bearish on dollar and it is USD CAD, not CAD USD, it's going to be a bearish setup."

rule: The cleanest structure is not always the strongest mover; GBPUSD expanded more that day while CAD had better structure.
quote: "I actually did not choose the strongest asset that day."

rule: Target opposing equal highs / failure swings as the draw on liquidity for the scalp.
quote: "we have equal highs at the highs which is the draw on liquidity for me on this trade"

rule: The primary trigger is SMT at the previous-day low across the indices.
quote: "But the main reason is the previous day low SMT."

rule: Rank index strength by three checks: location of price relative to structure, SMT, and candle type.
quote: "where is the location of price currently relative to structure the SMT as well as just candles."

rule: The index closest to (or through) its previous-day low is the weakest.
quote: "NQ is the closest to its previous day low. So that shows me it has weakness."

rule: A bullish-closing reversal candle is weaker than a bullish expansion candle when ranking assets.
quote: "It's not expansion, right? It's a reversal candle."

rule: Longs go on the strongest asset and shorts on the weakest by default.
quote: "it tells me that NQ is the weakest asset and YM is the strongest asset."

rule: Do not short an asset with failure swings above it from the open; wait for a manipulation first.
quote: "for me, there's no way to trade NQ here with all these failure swings on the high."

rule: If the weakest index reverses off its previous-day low, look to long the stronger assets.
quote: "if NQ is going to reverse off of its previous day low, then I'd be looking to long the stronger assets,"

rule: Skip the strongest asset when it has already expanded over its highs (no draw left / consolidation expected).
quote: "Would I want to trade the strongest asset? No, because it has already expanded and it's over highs."

rule: In that case trade the middle asset, the next strongest, which still has liquidity above.
quote: "and then I can look to take the middle asset because that's the next strongest asset."

rule: When the setup depends on another index's reversal, let that index's 15m candle (here the 9:30 candle) close before acting on the traded index.
quote: "I'm letting NQ close its candle here. So letting NQ show that we have a reversal means that I need to let ES also have a reversal here."

rule: Align the 15m/1m model with the hourly: an hourly candle with a small wick reversing off the previous hour supports expansion.
quote: "And this 1-hour candle has a small wick reversing off of its previous hour, which supports expansion higher."

rule: If the only protected low is far away, do not enter with a wide stop; wait for a new low to form.
quote: "No, I'm not going to. I'm going to let a new low form."

rule: On the 1m, when the correlated index takes a low and the traded one does not (SMT), use the traded index's series of down-close candles as the opposing candle and enter on a close back over it.
quote: "And so then now I can look for this series of downcloed candles here as an opposing candle if it is closed back over."

rule: Get in before the failure swings above are taken and target those highs.
quote: "I want to be in before these failure swings are taken and target those highs."

rule: Scalp stop: tight, below the bodies of the entry swing.
quote: "I had my stop pretty tight below the bodies and then I was looking for these highs."

rule: Partial at 2R, more at the intermediate highs, hold the majority for the final high.
quote: "I took some off at 2 R. And then I was holding for these highs."

rule: If the target limit is not filled at the touch, exit manually rather than give back most of the position for a tick or two.
quote: "I'm not going to give up most of my position for a tick or two."

rule: Runners: stop at breakeven, then trail to each new protected swing (sweep + close over).
quote: "So then I move my stop to right here. That is a new protected swing."

rule: Scalping pairing: 1h for context/bias (a candle that supports expansion), 15m swing point, 1m entry; analogous to 1D bias / 4H closure / 15m entry.
quote: "I'm going to use the hourly time frame for context or my bias or a candle that supports expansion and then using the 15-minute as a swing point and 1 minute as entry."

rule: An FVG is a three-candle pattern where candle 1's low does not overlap candle 3's high, or candle 1's high does not overlap candle 3's low.
quote: "A fair value gap is a three candlestick pattern where the first candle low does not overlap with the third candle's high"

rule: If candle 1 and candle 3 wick ranges overlap, there is no FVG.
quote: "you can see that there is overlap between the first candle's high and the third candle's low, meaning there is no fair value gap here"

rule: Consecutive overlapping candle triples can each form their own FVG.
quote: "Now if you notice, do we have another one? Yes, because this candle's low does not overlap with this candle's high."

rule: SIBI (sell-side imbalance, buy-side inefficiency) is a bearish FVG.
quote: "A SIBI is a sell-side imbalance, buy-side inefficiency."

rule: BISI (buy-side imbalance, sell-side inefficiency) is a bullish FVG.
quote: "A BISI is a buy-side imbalance, sell-side inefficiency."

rule: Three reference points inside an FVG: its start, its consequent encroachment (50%), and the full fill.
quote: "The first being the start of the fair value gap. The second being the consequent encroachment, or the 50% of the fair value gap."

rule: Respect at the start: price reaches into the FVG, closes back out, and continues.
quote: "price can either reach up into this fair value gap, close out, and continue lower"

rule: Respect at the CE: prefer a candle close outside the FVG, but he is flexible as long as the CE holds.
quote: "I would like to see a candle close outside of it, but as long as it's respecting the consequent encroachment, I'm pretty flexible with that"

rule: If price fills the whole FVG, he prefers a close back outside the CE.
quote: "It can also reach up, fill the fair value gap, and with this, I prefer to see price close outside the consequent encroachment"

rule: Invalidation is by close: closing over the CE or outside the FVG means price is not respecting it, and often will not reverse.
quote: "When we start to close over the consequent encroachment or outside of the fair value gap, price is not respecting that."

rule: A full close through the FVG invalidates it.
quote: "price did not respect this SIVI [SIBI] at all and closed right through it. This is when I will invalidate a fair value gap"

rule: Even a respected bullish FVG: he would like price to reach discount of the range before continuing.
quote: "if we take a discount and premium of this range, I would like to have it reach a little bit lower to reach a discount of the range"

rule: FVG inversion: when price closes through a failed FVG, it can act as support/resistance on return.
quote: "when a fair value gap fails, Or price closes through it, this fair value gap can then be used as support or resistance"

rule: Inversion need not be back to back or overlapping; it can occur later, after consolidation.
quote: "this doesn't need to occur back to back or these fair value gaps don't have to overlap. This can occur later on. After a period of consolidation."

rule: First clue of a failing FVG is a close beyond its CE.
quote: "our first clue is that This closed below the consequent encroachment."

rule: An FVG can be respected repeatedly (closes back out) while sell-side liquidity is taken, until a close over it inverts it.
quote: "takes sell side liquidity again, comes back up, still respects it. We open up and right here we close over this SIBI."

rule: An inverted FVG's CE can be the support level on return.
quote: "You can see how the consequent encroachment was used as support."

rule: Volume imbalance: gap between the close and open of two candles where trading still occurred across it (wicks overlap).
quote: "A volume imbalance is a gap between the closing and opening price of two candles."

rule: Gap: complete absence of trading between two candles.
quote: "a gap has a complete absence of trading between two candles, while a volume imbalance had trading or overlap between the high and the low"

rule: Learn swing highs/lows and liquidity before market structure.
quote: "it's important to understand what swing highs and swing lows are and understanding liquidity."

rule: Price trends up only by making higher highs and higher lows.
quote: "if price is going to move higher or trend upwards, we're going to have to make higher highs and higher lows."

rule: A downtrend is the mirror: lower highs and lower lows.
quote: "Relative to this high, we create a lower high, a lower low, lower high, lower low"

rule: Bear-to-bull shift: last lower low fails to displace lower, displacement makes a higher high, then the higher low is the low risk buy.
quote: "We can't displace lower. Now we get displacement creating what? A higher high. Now we get our low risk buy or our higher low."

rule: Bull-to-bear shift: lower high, then displace and close below the lower low = market structure shift / break.
quote: "When we put in a lower high and then displace and close below this lower low, creating another lower low and then a lower high, we are shifting to bearish trend."

rule: Always know the higher-timeframe trend when reading lower-timeframe structure.
quote: "you have to understand the higher timeframe trend when you're looking at the lower timeframes."

rule: A lower-timeframe bearish displacement inside a higher-timeframe uptrend is often only a retracement; shorting it gets stopped out.
quote: "A lot of times what happens is people will try to catch this first short here"

rule: Trade with the higher-timeframe trend rather than trying to catch every top or bottom.
quote: "It's a lot easier to frame an idea right here to continue with the trend than it is to catch every top or every bottom."

rule: In an uptrend, after a higher high, the next expected step is a higher low relative to the prior low, then a close over the high.
quote: "if we're going to continue the trend up, I want to see closure over this high or making a higher high."

rule: A higher high exists on the close beyond the old high even before its swing high has formed.
quote: "we have a higher high, even if we have not formed a swing high yet"

rule: Minor highs/lows inside a leg get swept, but the trend is judged relative to the defining swing.
quote: "those get swept out before we go, but you can see, relative to this high here, it is still a lower high."

rule: Higher high / higher low without displacement is consolidation, not a trend change.
quote: "But is there any displacement here? No, it's really just kind of consolidation."

rule: Focus on the closing candle over the previous high as the structure signal.
quote: "Another little higher low, but mostly focused on the close here, making a higher high."

rule: Prefer the new higher low to form in discount (lower high in premium).
quote: "Ideally, I like to see discount, right? This is when I like to use discount and premium."

rule: The trend stays bullish as long as the relevant swing low is not broken.
quote: "So this is still bullish to me, right? Because we never broke this low down here."

rule: To confirm a bull-to-bear shift after breaking the low: lower high, then a close below / break of the low.
quote: "I want to see a close below or break of this low."

rule: Prefer the lower high to form in a premium array.
quote: "I'm not as interested in this because of premium and discount, right? I'd like to see a premium array."

rule: Swing highs/lows and displacement (or lack of it) around them give the clues to direction and shifts.
quote: "just focusing on swing highs and swing lows and the displacement around them, or the lack of displacement around them, can give you clues"

rule: The shift level is the low that made the new high (not a higher high with no swing broken).
quote: "this is the low that made the new high before price came and broke it"

rule: At the break, check discount: if it is just a sweep in discount, no lower high forms and price makes a higher high.
quote: "Do we reject from here, continue lower, shift the trend, or is this just a sweep to continue higher"

rule: Go short to old lows only after displacement and a close below the shift low.
quote: "once we displace and close below this low, that is when I'm looking short, right, to old lows."

rule: A lower-timeframe shift into a higher-timeframe PD array (e.g. hourly FVG) fails; trade toward the higher-timeframe target.
quote: "this lower time frame shift in structure, is actually just a retracement to a higher time frame PD array"

rule: When a short-term high is broken, you want displacement above it.
quote: "if we're looking at these short-term highs here, when we break these, you want to see displacement above that"

rule: Displacement is an energetic move through the short-term high.
quote: "You want to see an energetic move up, right?"

rule: Judge displacement by the range of the breaking candles (here four) and the distance travelled past the short-term high.
quote: "if you just take these four candles when we broke this high here, you have a range about like that"

rule: Compare breaks over the same time: the displacing one has a larger range and covers more distance beyond the high.
quote: "in the same amount of time, right? We have a larger range and more distance covered or broken through more price."

rule: Once displacement is seen, look for the FVG setup.
quote: "So once you see that, that is when you look for your fair value gap setup"

rule: Buy only in the discount of the displacement range (from the low to the displacement high).
quote: "the most important part is that you are buying at a discount of the displacement range"

rule: Liquidity is where stops sit, found at the most obvious highs and lows.
quote: "All liquidity is is where people's stops are sitting. That can be found at the most obvious highs and lows."

rule: Buy-side liquidity rests above highs (shorts' stops); sell-side rests below lows (longs' stops).
quote: "Anyone who got short will put their stops up here to buy back their position. So this is where your buy side liquidity is."

rule: After a pool is taken, look for the setup in the opposite direction.
quote: "Once those are taken, that's when you look for your setup."

rule: A cluster of equal highs holds liquidity and becomes the target; once taken, look for the short.
quote: "There is liquidity in this area. And once it is taken, then you look for the short setup."

rule: Inside a range, stops sit at the nearest internal swing behind an entry, not at the far range extreme.
quote: "Are they going to put their stops all the way down here? Probably not. They're going to put it right here."

rule: Price does not have to run the whole range; running internal stops is enough to start looking for a setup.
quote: "you don't always have to run the whole range of stops, right?"

rule: After the stop run, drop to the 1m and wait for the 2022 mentorship setup rather than buying the sweep directly.
quote: "Could you just buy this right here? Yes, but that's also more risky."

rule: Setup: short-term high broken with displacement, then an FVG entry inside the discount of the displacement range (Fib).
quote: "We put in a short-term high here, right there, right? We run that, get some displacement over it, and then we have a fair value gap"

rule: Entry must be in a discount of the displacement range (for longs).
quote: "Drawing a FIB from our displacement range, right? You are entering in a discount here. So that is a valid setup."

rule: Untaken relative equal highs and lows become targets for later.
quote: "What happens when we put in relative equal highs and relative equal lows? They become targets for later."

rule: A bullish swing point is a candle whose low has a higher low on both its left and its right.
quote: "A bullish swing point is a candle that has a low and then a higher low to its right and to its left"

rule: A bearish swing point is a candle whose high has a lower high on both its left and its right.
quote: "a bearish swing point has a high and then a lower high to its left and right"

rule: A swing with older highs still beyond it (to its left) is not relevant; walk out to the extreme of the cluster and use that as the relevant swing.
quote: "we go find the extreme and that is our relevant swing high"

rule: Only relevant swing highs/lows are places to look for reactions or reversals; watch whether price manipulates or breaks out there.
quote: "relevant swing highs and relevant swing lows are where we can look for reactions or reversals in the market"

rule: A low formed very close to the previous low lacks valid separation and is not a relevant swing; do not trust a reversal from it until the nearby low is taken.
quote: "that is not enough separation to consider this a relevant swing"

rule: When price reacts at a relevant high/low, look for a candle 2 or candle 3 closure, using the wick or EQ as the level candle 3 should respect.
quote: "I'm going to be looking for a candle 2 or candle 3 closure"

rule: Swings count as relevant only inside a lookback of three higher-timeframe candles, the current one included; the same count applies on every timeframe.
quote: "it's always going to be that same look back period of three higher time frame candles, including the current one"

rule: To tell a breakout from a manipulation at a relevant swing, classify what price does there: retracement, reversal or consolidation.
quote: "Do we get a retracement, a reversal, or a consolidation?"

rule: Do not trade away from a low that has equal or stacked lows just below it; wait for the relevant (extreme) low to be taken out.
quote: "I don't trust trading away from these lows below me. So I need to wait for this relevant low to get taken out."

rule: Once price trades into a relevant swing, look for the fractal model there (a candle 2 closure in his example).
quote: "This is where I want to look for a fractal model"

rule: Targets from a relevant-swing reversal are the other side of the range or the failure swings.
quote: "Back to the other side of the range or to those failure swings."

rule: If the opposite-side swing is a failure swing (too close to another), only take the direction toward the relevant swing (here: shorts only).
quote: "So, I would only be interested in the short side."

rule: Keep updating relevant swings as price moves: a new retracement creates a new relevant low or high.
quote: "Now when we get this retracement this becomes a relevant low right and you continue to track those."

rule: Failure swings are stacked highs/lows (stacked liquidity) and are the target; the stop-loss side should have high-resistance liquidity, with no failure swings.
quote: "we want to have high resistance liquidity or no failure swings on our stop-loss side of the market"

rule: A fair value gap counts as a high on a lower timeframe; do not trade away from it while a nearby high is left untaken.
quote: "this is a fair value gap which is a high on a lower time frame"

rule: A relevant low that is close to the previous low is "sketchy"; wait until price closes through and confirms before trading away from it.
quote: "I wouldn't want to trade away from that until when? After we close through and confirm this low."

rule: Before price reaches the relevant high, treat a pullback as a retracement and do not anticipate a reversal unless there is SMT.
quote: "would I anticipate a reversal to form here? No. Not without SMT."

rule: When bullish, the relevant low below should hold during the retracement.
quote: "do we want to see us reach for this relevant low? Not if we're bullish"

rule: Combine with the fractal model by favoring relevant swings that are also higher-timeframe highs/lows (monthly highs/lows on the daily chart).
quote: "I'm going to be focusing on those relevant highs and lows that are a higher time frame higher low [high or low]"

rule: On the daily chart the lookback is three months; on the hourly chart it is three days.
quote: "if I go to an hourly chart here, how far am I going to look back? Well, I'm going to look back 3 days"

rule: Older swings beyond the three-candle lookback can still be watched, but the three-candle window gives the best reactions.
quote: "Generally speaking, that's what's going to give the best reactions."

rule: Look for the model only at relevant swings, not at arbitrary highs or lows.
quote: "relevant swings are where I look for my model to form in the market. I don't want to just look at random highs or lows"

rule: A swing that is technically a failure swing can still be relevant if it has large separation from the next swing.
quote: "Yes, it's a failure swing technically, but look at the separation it has between this low."

rule: Valid separation has no mechanical threshold; he judges it by experience.
quote: "I don't have a mechanical reason to say, hey, this is valid separation. That just comes with experience"

rule: An ideal continuation is a reach into a POI (FVG or a swept low) followed by an aggressive V-shaped recovery that closes through the series of opposing (down-close for longs) candles.
quote: "ideally we want to see a nice aggressive V-shaped reversal"

rule: That aggressive close through the opening price of the opposing candles is what shows intent and lets you trust the continuation.
quote: "This aggressive recovery or swift price action through the opening price shows us that price has the intent to move higher."

rule: When price does not V-recover and drifts sideways, it is forming a consolidation, and a later close over the level is a manipulation of that range, not a valid CISD.
quote: "this closure through which you think is validating this low is actually a manipulation of this consolidation range"

rule: Fix for reason 1: after a slow closure, wait for the next candle to show either a new continuation (breakout) or a failure back across the range; if it fails, trade the swing off the manipulated opposite extreme.
quote: "So step one is to wait to see this next candle and how it reacts."

rule: Reason 2: be cautious when the continuation's closure also takes out range highs or a short-term target; wait for an extra continuation after the sweep.
quote: "the continuation forms at the same time that we are taking out highs in a range or a short-term target is taken"

rule: Reason 3: once a higher-timeframe target (e.g. previous day's high with failure swings) is hit, do not chase new continuations, because a new phase of price can form.
quote: "when we hit a higher time frame target, that is when we can form a new phase of price"

rule: A valid closure through the opposing candles protects the swing low; while price has not taken the prior high, further expansion is expected, and if it does take a high he wants a closure through that high.
quote: "If we have price when it takes out a high, we want to see a closure through that high."

rule: A CISD can be measured off a single opposing candle when there is only one.
quote: "I use a singular candle in this case because there's not more than one candle."

rule: If price cannot close back through the opposing candles after reaching the POI, the retracement is reclassified as a consolidation and the range high/low become the new POIs.
quote: "This is now turning into a consolidation in which this isn't a retracement anymore."

rule: Two ways to trade a consolidation: a breakout confirmed by a continuation, or a new manipulation (sweep) of a range extreme.
quote: "We can either trade the breakout with a continuation or wait for a new manipulation."

rule: Ignore continuations/closures that form inside a consolidation; they are internal and give poor structure.
quote: "That's just internal to the range and you're trading a consolidation. You want to avoid that."

rule: Speed: the closure through should take 1, 2, maybe 3 candles; longer usually means it is taking too long (e.g. 2 candles down, 6 up without reclaiming = not V-shaped).
quote: "Now, I prefer 1 2 maybe three. If it takes longer than that, a lot of times it's just taking too long."

rule: A pullback that does not reach a POI does not qualify as a continuation for him, even with an SMT on a correlated asset.
quote: "I would consider personally no because we don't reach into a point of interest"

rule: Do not trade a breakout of a consolidation until a continuation forms off the breakout.
quote: "we're not going to trade the breakout unless we have a continuation."

rule: Aggressive entry: enter on the closure through, stop at the swing; you can always demand more confirmation (another continuation).
quote: "I could just take an entry like this right on the closure through my stop there."

rule: When choosing which opposing candle(s) to measure the CISD from, ignore a candle that does not form a swing.
quote: "when we have this candle that doesn't form a swing, generally I ignore it."

rule: When the closure takes significant liquidity (buyside/sellside), that is exactly where the opposite setup forms, so wait for a continuation before entering.
quote: "if a bearish setup is going to form, this is where a bearish setup will form"

rule: Sweeps of short-term highs/lows are often the manipulation that builds the higher-timeframe wick.
quote: "that is a lot of time the manipulation that forms the higher time frame wicks."

rule: A strong closure that also clears all nearby highs gives poor risk-to-reward off the protected swing; give it one more candle.
quote: "this doesn't really give me the best risk-to-reward on a protected swing."

rule: Whether to wait for a second continuation after short-term highs are taken depends on bias strength and how aggressive you want your entries.
quote: "depending on how strong your bias is and how aggressive you want to be with entries, many times I wait for another continuation to form."

rule: If the retracement leg was large, allow a few more candles for the reclaim and still call it V-shaped.
quote: "this is quite a move up. So, we can allow for a few more candles and this is still a V-shaped reversal."

rule: An inversion (IFVG) can stand in for the CISD when the candle range is extremely large.
quote: "you can also use inversions as a form of the change in the state of delivery when you have an extremely large candle range."

rule: Choppy price at the end of a trend is a consolidation: look for a manipulation, not continuations.
quote: "This is where it's starting to get a bit choppy, right? And it makes sense at the end of a trend."

rule: In the fractal model, wait for the HTF candle close; if the HTF candle has already expanded, let the next HTF candle form its wick and trade away from it.
quote: "I want to let the next candle form form its wick and then trade it away."

rule: Example management: enter on the closure through, stop on the low, target 2R.
quote: "put my stop on the low, and then look for 2 R."

rule: Core takeaway: frame entries while the higher-timeframe wick is forming instead of hunting random continuations.
quote: "Frame your entries when it is forming the higher time frame wick."

rule: Do not look for continuations after an HTF objective is hit or after multiple (1-3) candles of HTF expansion.
quote: "I don't look for continuations after we've already hit a higher time frame objective or had multiple candles of expansion."

rule: An expansion candle has small wicks and a large body; its opposing run is shallow and made early, then price expands and closes near its high/low.
quote: "when we have an expansion candle, it has a small wick on both sides and a large body"

rule: A large opposing run that uses most of the candle's time and range marks a reversal candle, which does not support expansion.
quote: "When we have a large opposing run that does not support expansion. That is a reversal candle."

rule: Prefer to trade expansion candles; check whether the HTF candle's wick size supports expansion before taking a trade.
quote: "Ideally, we want to be trading expansion candles."

rule: Expansion-candle targets: expansion targets, liquidity points, or the average candle range.
quote: "for targeting, I'm going to be looking for expansion targets, liquidity points, or this average candle's range"

rule: When trading a large-wick reversal candle, do not target expansion; target the opening price (daily open) or liquidity/POIs near it.
quote: "Instead of looking for price to expand, we're just looking for it to reverse or return back to its opening price."

rule: Measure the opposing run on the HTF candle of the timeframe pair (e.g. 1h candle when executing on 5m): open to the high (or low) against your bias.
quote: "when I say opposing run, I mean from the opening price to that high or the move opposite my bias"

rule: A shallow opposing run that sweeps the previous candle's high/low is confirmed as the wick only when paired with a CISD.
quote: "If that is paired with a change in the state of delivery, it's then confirming this wick."

rule: If the HTF candle forms a large wick, wait for the next HTF candle (candle 3) to show a small wick and trade that expansion instead.
quote: "I'm just going to wait for a new higher time frame candle that does support expansion"

rule: Trading a large-wick reversal candle lacks the candle-close filter, and price often keeps trending if the read is wrong; he prefers the close as filter.
quote: "we don't really have the filter of the candle close"

rule: Difficulty ranking: (1) easiest = let the large-wick candle close, trade small-wick continuation in candle 3; (2) harder = reversal-to-expansion in the same candle; (3) hardest, usually avoided = trading inside the large-wick reversal.
quote: "the easiest is letting this candle to close"

rule: Reversal-to-expansion in the same candle requires a small opposing run, an LTF CISD, and enough time left in the candle for the range to expand.
quote: "making sure I have enough time for this range to expand lower"

rule: Exception: if trading a daily reversal candle, trade the lower timeframes back towards the daily open.
quote: "if I'm trading a reversal candle on the daily, then I look to trade the lower time frames back towards the daily open"

rule: A sweep of the previous day high without a CISD is not a confirmed wick; do not trade it.
quote: "Without that change in the state of delivery there, we cannot confirm this wick high."

rule: For a daily expansion, the day's high/low should form early New York or before New York so New York can still expand.
quote: "we want to see this high day form early New York or before New York. So, then New York can expand."

rule: Within the fractal model, EQ is the mechanical target for the expansion after a confirmed small-wick reversal.
quote: "my EQ can be the target for that expansion if we're going to expand lower"

rule: When the intraday low is a protected swing, target around the daily open rather than holding for the intraday low; target the intraday low only when it consists of failure swings.
quote: "if I have a protected swing on the intraday low, as we do here, as we talked about, then I'm going to want to target around the daily open"

rule: Do not try to trade a reversal away from the draw on liquidity until those highs/lows are taken out.
quote: "It does not make sense to try to trade short until these highs are taken out."

rule: Consecutive expansion days each show relatively small wicks; small wicks are what support continued expansion.
quote: "small wicks support expansion lower"

rule: He cannot trade away from a failure swing that has not been taken out unless there is SMT.
quote: "I'm not going to be able to trade away from this failure swing here unless we have SMT, and we don't"

rule: Time matters as much as range: a high taken with ~40 minutes left after consolidating is not an expansion setup; let the candle close and use the new candle.
quote: "Does it make sense for price to consolidate here and then with 40 minutes left in the candle, take out the high and then expand? No."

rule: Ideal: the reversal off the previous candle's high happens right at the start of the new HTF candle.
quote: "we reach into that high right at the start of the candle which is ideal"

rule: Do not enter late in a candle after a long reversal formation; wait for the new candle open (he says this is why macros don't make sense).
quote: "Does it make sense to enter this late into a candle? No. And that's why macros don't even make sense"

rule: The fractal model only looks for candle 3 and candle 4 entries because after that price can shift into a new phase.
quote: "that's why my fractal model only looks for candle 3 and four, because after that, you can get caught in a new phase of price"

rule: If the CISD close needed to confirm a reversal would itself reach the move's target, skip it and wait for another run or the next candle.
quote: "we would need to close through here. That doesn't make sense cuz that would be almost a target for this move lower"

rule: After a large-candle move into a target, the first expectation for a reversal is only back to the daily open or liquidity near it; scalping it is counter-trend.
quote: "my first expectation for this move is just back towards the daily open or the liquidity around it"
